10.x: All three statements are correct. Swaminathan was associated with high-yielding dwarf crops, chaired the National Commission on Farmers and founded MSSRF in Chennai.
10.tq: Combine agricultural contribution, commission and institution facts in a coded statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: Swaminathan developed **high-yielding dwarf wheat and rice** (with **Norman Borlaug**).
Statement 2: he chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (set up **18 November 2004**).
Statement 3: he founded **MSSRF**, **Chennai**.
xa: The commission dealt with **farmer suicides**; its reports = "**Swaminathan report**".
UNEP called him the **"Father of Economic Ecology"**.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in:
10.x: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in 1987.
10.tq: Distinguish the award year from the years of his other honours and institutional activities.
xs: Swaminathan won the **first World Food Prize** in **1987** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It honoured his role as architect of the **Green Revolution** — high-yielding dwarf wheat and rice.
xa: He got the **Bharat Ratna 2024** (posthumous).
⚠ Bharat Ratna order: **Kalam 1997** – **C.N.R. Rao 2014** – **Swaminathan 2024**.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024:
o: during his lifetime for literary contributions
during his lifetime for work in space science
posthumously for his contribution to agriculture
posthumously for work in nuclear physics
10.x: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his contribution to agriculture.
10.tq: Read the qualification carefully and distinguish posthumous recognition from a lifetime award.
xs: Swaminathan got the Bharat Ratna **posthumously** in **2024** for **agriculture** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was the architect of the **Green Revolution**.
xa: First **World Food Prize** (**1987**).
⚠ Other scientist Bharat Ratnas: **Kalam 1997**, **C.N.R. Rao 2014**.

10.s: M.S. Swaminathan was described by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) as the:
10.x: UNEP called M.S. Swaminathan the 'Father of Economic Ecology' (UPPSC 2007). He is the architect of India's Green Revolution. The Blue Revolution is fisheries and the White Revolution is milk (linked to Verghese Kurien), and 'Father of Green Chemistry' is not his title.
10.tq: Swaminathan: UNEP = Father of Economic Ecology; first World Food Prize 1987.
xs: **UNEP** called Swaminathan the **"Father of Economic Ecology"** — so option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC 2007).
He is the architect of India's **Green Revolution**.
xa: He chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (**18 November 2004**).
He founded **MSSRF**, Chennai.

10.s: Which one of the following correctly describes A.P.J. Abdul Kalam’s role in India’s space programme?
o: Founder of the Physical Research Laboratory at Ahmedabad
Project director of SLV-3, which placed Rohini in orbit in 1980
Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission during Aryabhata’s launch
Director of SITE for the transmission of programmes to 2,400 villages
10.x: Abdul Kalam was the project director of SLV-3, which placed the Rohini satellite in orbit in 1980.
10.tq: Match the scientist with the precise project role and reject roles belonging to Sarabhai or other programmes.
xs: Kalam was **project director of SLV-3**, which put **Rohini** in orbit in **1980** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**PRL** was founded by **Sarabhai**; **SITE** (**2,400 villages**) was led by Sarabhai.
xa: Kalam later led the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme** — "**Missile Man of India**".
Key role in **Pokhran-II (1998)**.

10.s: Which of the following missile programmes was led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
10.x: Kalam led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme, associated with missiles such as Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul and Nag.
10.tq: Identify the correct programme from a group of nearby scientific and developmental initiatives.
xs: Kalam led the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its missiles: **Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul, Nag**.
**SITE** was Sarabhai's; the **National Commission on Farmers** was Swaminathan's.
xa: ⚠ "Missile Man" = **Kalam**; "Missile Woman" = **Tessy Thomas** (Agni-IV).
Kalam was the **11th President** (**2002-2007**).

10.s: Which of the following is the correct set of books associated with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: Wings of Fire, Ignited Minds and India 2020
Agriculture Cannot Wait, India 2020 and The History of Indian Agriculture
Wings of Fire, An Equal Music and India 2020
Ignited Minds, The Discovery of India and Wings of Fire
10.x: Wings of Fire, Ignited Minds and India 2020 are associated with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
10.tq: Use a complete-set question and eliminate books associated with agriculture, fiction or other authors.
xs: Kalam wrote **Wings of Fire, Ignited Minds and India 2020** — so option **(1)** is correct.
All three are listed under Kalam, the "**Missile Man of India**" and **11th President**.
xa: Kalam: **Bharat Ratna 1997**.
He flew the **Sukhoi-30 MKI** in **2006** — first President to fly a fighter.

10.s:
Arrange the following events associated with India’s space and nuclear programmes in chronological order:
A. Pokhran-II
B. Launch of Rohini by SLV-3
C. Renaming of Wheeler Island as Abdul Kalam Island
D. Abdul Kalam’s term as President of India begins
10.x: The correct order is SLV-3 placing Rohini in orbit in 1980, Pokhran-II in 1998, the beginning of Kalam’s presidency in 2002 and the renaming in 2015.
10.tq: Place the anchor years first: 1980, 1998, 2002 and 2015.
xs: The correct order is **B, A, D, C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SLV-3/Rohini** (**1980**) → **Pokhran-II** (**1998**) → Kalam's presidency (**2002**) → **Abdul Kalam Island** (**2015**).
xa: Kalam flew the **Sukhoi-30 MKI** in **2006**.
**Pokhran-I** (**1974**) was led by **Raja Ramanna**.

10.s: In 2006, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam became the first President of India to fly in a fighter aircraft. Which aircraft was it?
10.x: In 2006, Kalam, India's 11th President (2002-2007), flew in a Sukhoi-30 MKI and became the first President to fly a fighter (RPSC 2007). The MiG-21, Mirage 2000 and Tejas are other IAF fighters, but none of them is linked to this first.
10.tq: Kalam: 11th President, Sukhoi-30 MKI 2006, Missile Man.
xs: Kalam flew the **Sukhoi-30 MKI** in **2006** — the first President to fly a fighter (RPSC 2007) — so option **(4)** is correct.
He was the **11th President** (**2002-2007**).
xa: Kalam = **first President to fly a fighter jet**.
Kalam: **Bharat Ratna 1997**.

10.s: C.N.R. Rao is primarily associated with:
10.x: C.N.R. Rao is one of the foremost scientists in solid-state and materials chemistry, including structural chemistry.
10.tq: Use the scientist–field association and distinguish chemistry from biological and engineering disciplines.
xs: C.N.R. Rao is one of the world's foremost **solid-state and materials chemists** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Telecommunication = **Ashok Jhunjhunwala**; cereal rusts = **K.C. Mehta**; palaeobotany = **Birbal Sahni**.
xa: C.N.R. Rao — **solid-state and structural chemistry** (UPSC 2006).
**Bharat Ratna 2014**; **Energy Frontiers Award**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about C.N.R. Rao:
1. He received the Bharat Ratna in 2014.
2. He headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.
3. He received the Energy Frontiers Award.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
10.x: All three statements are correct. C.N.R. Rao received the Bharat Ratna in 2014, headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister and received the Energy Frontiers Award.
10.tq: Combine award, advisory and scientific-recognition facts in a complete coded statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
Statement 1: C.N.R. Rao got the **Bharat Ratna 2014**.
Statement 2: he headed the **Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister**.
Statement 3: he won the **Energy Frontiers Award** ("Nobel of energy transition research").
xa: His field: **solid-state and materials chemistry** (five decades).
⚠ Bharat Ratna: **Kalam 1997** – **C.N.R. Rao 2014** – **Swaminathan 2024**.

10.s: Who led Pokhran-I in 1974?
10.x: Raja Ramanna led Pokhran-I in 1974 and was associated with BARC.
10.tq: Match the nuclear test with the scientist who led it, avoiding confusion with Pokhran-II.
xs: **Raja Ramanna** (BARC) led **Pokhran-I (1974)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Anil Kakodkar** was linked to **Pokhran-II**; **U.R. Rao** and **Satish Dhawan** were ISRO chairmen.
xa: ⚠ **Pokhran-I (1974)** = Raja Ramanna; **Pokhran-II** = Anil Kakodkar + Kalam.
Pokhran-II was in **1998**.

10.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anil Kakodkar — Atomic Energy Commission; Advanced Heavy Water Reactor
Tessy Thomas — ISRO; Aryabhata satellite team
U.R. Rao — DRDO; Agni-IV project director
Raja Ramanna — ISRO; drafting committee of NEP 2020
10.x: Anil Kakodkar was associated with the Atomic Energy Commission and the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor. Tessy Thomas was associated with DRDO, U.R. Rao with ISRO and Raja Ramanna with BARC.
10.tq: Use organisation–contribution matching and identify the swapped institutions in the distractors.
xs: **Anil Kakodkar — Atomic Energy Commission; Advanced Heavy Water Reactor** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tessy Thomas** is DRDO (**Agni-IV**); **U.R. Rao** is ISRO (Aryabhata team); **Raja Ramanna** is BARC (Pokhran-I).
**NEP 2020** drafting was chaired by **K. Kasturirangan**.

U.R. Rao (ISRO Chairman **1984-94**) was the first Indian in the **Satellite Hall of Fame**.

10.s: K. Kasturirangan is associated with which of the following roles?
o: Chairman of ISRO and chair of the drafting committee of NEP 2020
Chairman of BARC and leader of Pokhran-I
Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission and developer of the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor
Director of DRDO and project director of Agni-IV
10.x: K. Kasturirangan served as ISRO Chairman from 1994 to 2003 and chaired the drafting committee of NEP 2020.
10.tq: Combine the institutional position and later policy role to distinguish Kasturirangan from other modern scientists.
xs: **K. Kasturirangan** was **ISRO Chairman** (**1994-2003**) and chaired the drafting committee of **NEP 2020** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Pokhran-I = **Raja Ramanna**; AHWR = **Anil Kakodkar**; Agni-IV = **Tessy Thomas**.
xa: His predecessor **U.R. Rao** was ISRO Chairman **1984-94**.
**Satish Dhawan** oversaw the launch of **Aryabhata**.

10.s: Tessy Thomas is popularly known as the “Missile Woman” because she was associated with:
o: The Agni-IV project as its project director
The Rohini satellite as its project director
10.x: Tessy Thomas of DRDO was the project director of Agni-IV and is popularly known as the “Missile Woman.”
10.tq: Match the popular title with the precise project and organisation.
xs: **Tessy Thomas** (DRDO) is the "**Missile Woman**" as **project director of Agni-IV** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Pokhran-I = **Raja Ramanna**; Rohini (SLV-3) = **Kalam**; Aryabhata team = **U.R. Rao**.
xa: ⚠ "Missile Man" = **Kalam** (IGMDP).
Agni is one of the IGMDP missiles: Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul, Nag.

10.s: Satish Dhawan is associated with which of the following developments?
o: The drafting of NEP 2020 and ISRO chairmanship from 1994 to 2003
The leadership of Pokhran-I and BARC
The launch of Aryabhata and renaming of SHAR as Satish Dhawan Space Centre
10.x: Satish Dhawan was associated with the launch of Aryabhata, and SHAR was renamed the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
10.tq: Use the organisation and contribution together to separate Dhawan from other space and defence scientists.
xs: **Satish Dhawan** is linked to the **launch of Aryabhata**, and **SHAR** was renamed the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Agni-IV = **Tessy Thomas**; NEP 2020 = **Kasturirangan**; Pokhran-I = **Raja Ramanna**.
xa: ⚠ **TERLS** was renamed **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre**.
A Parliament debate on ISRO's future invoked **Sarabhai, Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, U.R. Rao and Kalam**.

10.s: Yellapragada SubbaRow, associated with important contributions to biochemistry and medicine, was born at which place?
10.x: Yellapragada SubbaRow was born at Bhimavaram. Guntur district is associated with Yelavarthy Nayudamma.
10.tq: Use the birthplace distinction between the two scientists from Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Yellapragada SubbaRow** was from **Bhimavaram** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Guntur** district is **Yelavarthy Nayudamma**'s; **Florence** hosted the 46th COSPAR Assembly.
xa: SubbaRow: **Fiske-SubbaRow method** (ATP/phosphocreatine in muscle), **folic acid**, **methotrexate**, **aureomycin**, **Hetrazan**.
AP angle: SubbaRow + Nayudamma — both from **coastal Andhra**.

10.s: The Fiske–SubbaRow method is associated with the study of the role of which substances in muscle?
10.x: Yellapragada SubbaRow contributed to understanding the role of ATP and phosphocreatine in muscle through the Fiske–SubbaRow method.
10.tq: Match the named method with its specific scientific contribution rather than with another contribution of the same scientist.
xs: The **Fiske–SubbaRow method** concerns the role of **ATP and phosphocreatine** in muscle — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Folic acid** and **methotrexate**, and **aureomycin** and **Hetrazan**, are SubbaRow's other works, not this method.
xa: **Aureomycin** = first **tetracycline**; **Hetrazan** = **anti-filarial**; **methotrexate** = **anti-cancer**.
SubbaRow was from **Bhimavaram**.

10.s:
Consider the following statements about Yellapragada SubbaRow:
1. He contributed to the synthesis of folic acid.
2. He was associated with the development of the anti-cancer drug methotrexate.

Statement 3 is **wrong**: **digital** computers handle **discrete (binary)** data, as in PCs.

12.s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
12.x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. 12.x: EPROM is erased using ultraviolet light. EEPROM is electrically erasable, while ROM is non-volatile.
12.tq: Use the exact technical distinction among closely related memory terms.
xs: **EPROM — erased by UV** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
**EEPROM** is erased **electrically**; **ROM** is **non-volatile**, not volatile.
xa: ⚠ **EPROM** = UV; **EEPROM** = electrically.
**Flash drives** (pen drive, memory card) are **EEPROM-based** flash.

12.s:
Arrange the following in descending order of access speed:
A. RAM
B. Registers
C. Magnetic tape
D. Cache
12.x: The speed order is registers, cache, RAM and magnetic tape.
12.tq: Arrange items by performance hierarchy, beginning with the fastest.
xs: Descending speed: **Registers > Cache > RAM > Magnetic tape** — so option **(1) B, D, A, C** is correct.
Full order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > optical disc > magnetic tape**.
xa: **Registers** are inside the **CPU**.
**Magnetic tape** is **sequential access**, used for backup and archival.

12.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of a solid-state drive?
o: It uses flash memory and has no moving parts.
It uses a blue-violet laser to read data.
12.x: An SSD uses flash memory, has no moving parts and is generally faster than an HDD.
12.tq: Separate storage devices by their underlying technology.
xs: An **SSD** uses **flash memory** with **no moving parts** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Spinning disks** = **HDD**; **sequential access** = **magnetic tape**; **blue-violet laser** = **Blu-ray**.
xa: SSD is faster than HDD in the speed order.
Flash drives are **EEPROM-based** flash.

12.s: Which storage medium is primarily associated with sequential access and archival backup?
12.x: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access medium commonly used for backup and archival purposes.
12.tq: Match a storage medium with its characteristic use.
xs: **Magnetic tape** is **sequential access**, used for **backup and archival** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **slowest** item in the speed order.
xa: **Blu-ray**: **25 GB** single layer (blue-violet laser).
**SSD**: flash memory, no moving parts.

12.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the approximate single-layer capacity?
1. CD — 700 MB
2. DVD — 4.7 GB
3. Blu-ray — 25 GB
12.x: A single-layer CD stores about 700 MB, a single-layer DVD about 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray disc about 25 GB.
12.tq: Check all numerical pairings before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
**CD** ~**700 MB**; **DVD** **4.7 GB**; **Blu-ray** **25 GB** (single layer).
xa: Blu-ray uses a **blue-violet laser**.
Optical discs are slower than SSD and HDD but faster than magnetic tape.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Operating system — system software
2. Disk cleanup — utility software
3. Word processor — application software
4. Device driver — application software
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
12.x: Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified. A device driver is system software, so pair 4 is false.
12.tq: Spot the wrongly classified software category.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — so option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
**Operating system** = system software; **disk cleanup** = utility; **word processor** = application.
Pair 4 is **wrong**: a **device driver** is **system software**.
xa: Utility software: **antivirus, disk cleanup, backup, compression**.
Language translators (**compiler, interpreter, assembler**) are also system software.

12.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of application software?
12.x: A compiler is a language translator and therefore system software; the other three are application programs.
12.tq: Find the exception by separating system tools from end-user applications.
xs: A **language compiler** is not application software — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a language translator — **system software**.
**Photoshop** (graphics), **Oracle** (database) and **media players** (multimedia) are application software.
xa: Other database examples: **MySQL**, **MS Access**; graphics: **CorelDRAW**.
**Utility software**: antivirus, disk cleanup, backup, compression.

12.s: Which statement best describes open-source software?
o: It is limited to operating systems produced by one company.
Its source code is permanently hidden from users.
It can never be commercially distributed.
Its source code is free to view, modify and share, subject to its licence.
12.x: Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
12.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the precise definition.
xs: Open-source software has **source code free to view, modify, share** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Examples: **GNU, Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox**.
xa: **Richard Stallman** — **GNU** project (**1983**) and the **GPL licence**.
**Linus Torvalds** — **Linux** kernel (**1991**).

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
12.x: Richard Stallman initiated the GNU project in 1983. Linus Torvalds developed the Linux kernel in 1991.
12.tq: Use the person-project-year trap to distinguish related open-source milestones.
xs: **Richard Stallman — GNU project, 1983** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Linux kernel** (**1991**) is **Linus Torvalds**'s; **James Gosling** created **Java**, not the GPL.
xa: Stallman also created the **GPL licence**.
**Android** is **Linux-based**.

12.s:
Which of the following is NOT a normal responsibility of an operating system?
1. Managing hardware
2. Handling processes and memory
3. Managing files and device drivers
4. Manufacturing the motherboard
12.x: An operating system manages hardware resources, processes, memory, files and drivers. Manufacturing a motherboard is not an operating-system function.
12.tq: Find the unrelated function among genuine operating-system responsibilities.
xs: **Manufacturing the motherboard** is not an OS job — so option **(3) 4 only** is correct.
An OS **manages hardware**, handles **processes, memory, file systems, device drivers**, plus security and I/O.
xa: It also provides the **user interface** — **CLI** or **GUI**.
The **motherboard** links components; it is hardware.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about types of operating systems:
1. In a batch operating system, jobs are grouped and run without user interaction.
2. In a time-sharing (multi-user) operating system such as UNIX, many users share CPU time.
3. Real-time operating systems have no fixed response deadlines, so they are unsuitable for missile guidance or air-traffic control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction. Statement 2 is correct: time-sharing OS (e.g. UNIX) lets many users share CPU time. Statement 3 is wrong: real-time OS work to fixed response deadlines and are used precisely for missile guidance, air-traffic control and medical devices. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' and '1 and 3 only' drop statement 2 or add the false 3, and '1, 2 and 3' includes the false statement.
12.tq: Real-time = fixed deadlines (missiles, ATC, medical devices); time-sharing = UNIX.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — so option **(2) 1 and 2 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **batch** OS groups jobs and runs them **without user interaction**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **time-sharing** OS (e.g. **UNIX**) lets many users share CPU time.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **real-time** OS have **fixed response deadlines** — used for missile guidance, air-traffic control, medical devices.
xa: Real-time OS are **hard** or **soft**.
**Distributed / network** OS link many machines.

12.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding mobile operating systems?
o: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google.
Android and iOS are command-line-only systems.
BharOS was developed by a private foreign corporation.
12.x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google, while iOS is associated with Apple. BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.
12.tq: Use the developer-platform-location distinction to reject swapped associations.
xs: **Android** is **Linux-based** and from **Google** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**iOS** is **Apple**'s; **BharOS** was developed at **IIT Madras**.
Mobile OS have **GUI**s, not command-line only.
xa: CLI examples: **MS-DOS**, **UNIX shell**; GUI examples: **Windows**, **macOS**.
**Linux** kernel was written by **Linus Torvalds** (**1991**).

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CLI — icons and windows controlled mainly by a mouse
12.x: MS-DOS is associated with a command-line interface. GUIs use icons, windows and mouse interaction, as in Windows and macOS.
12.tq: Distinguish CLI and GUI by their visible interaction method.
xs: **MS-DOS — command-line interface** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**GUI** uses **icons, windows, mouse** — as in **Windows** and **macOS**.
xa: The **UNIX shell** is another CLI.
The mouse was invented by **Douglas Engelbart**.

12.s: Which programming-language generation uses mnemonics and requires an assembler for conversion?
12.x: Second-generation assembly language uses mnemonics and is converted into machine language by an assembler.
12.tq: Match the language generation with its characteristic translator.
xs: **2GL** (assembly) uses **mnemonics** and needs an **assembler** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**1GL** = machine language (binary 0s and 1s); **3GL** = high-level; **4GL** = **SQL**.
xa: **FORTRAN** was the first HLL (**1957**); **COBOL** is for business.
⚠ **Compiler** = whole program at once; **interpreter** = line by line.

12.s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Assembly language is a fourth-generation database language.
SQL is a first-generation machine language.
FORTRAN was the first high-level language and appeared in 1957.
12.x: FORTRAN is identified as the first high-level language and dates from 1957. SQL is a fourth-generation language used for database queries.
12.tq: Combine the language-generation fact with its historical date.
xs: **FORTRAN** was the **first high-level language** (**1957**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
Assembly is **2GL**; machine language is **binary**; **SQL** is **4GL** (database queries).
xa: **Pseudocode** is the English-like outline, not machine language.
Other 3GLs: **C** (Dennis Ritchie), **C++** (Stroustrup), **Java** (James Gosling), **Python** (Guido van Rossum).

12.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compiler from an interpreter?
o: A compiler translates only comments, whereas an interpreter translates only variables.
An interpreter is used exclusively for assembly language.
A compiler translates the whole program at once, whereas an interpreter translates and runs it line by line.
Both always translate only one line at a time.
12.x: A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
12.tq: Compare paired translators by the unit and timing of translation.
xs: A **compiler** translates the **whole program at once**; an **interpreter** translates and runs **line by line** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Compiled code runs **faster**; interpreters make **debugging easier**.
xa: Assembly language is converted by an **assembler**.
All three are **language translators** (system software).

12.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a flowchart symbol with its function?
12.x: An oval represents start or end; a diamond represents decision, a parallelogram input/output and a rectangle a process.
12.tq: Use the symbol-function pair and reject swapped flowchart meanings.
xs: **Oval — start or end** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Parallelogram** = input/output; **rectangle** = process; **diamond** = decision.
xa: A **flowchart** is the **pictorial** form of an algorithm (APPSC 2019).
**Pseudocode** is an English-like outline.

12.s: The pictorial representation of an algorithm is called a:
12.x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019). Pseudocode is an English-like text outline, a compiler is a language translator, and source code is the written program.
12.tq: Algorithm in pictures = flowchart; in English-like text = pseudocode.
xs: The pictorial form of an algorithm is a **Flowchart** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
**Pseudocode** is an **English-like outline**; a **compiler** is a translator.
xa: An **algorithm** is a **finite step-by-step procedure**.
Flowchart symbols: **oval** = start/end, **diamond** = decision.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its number-system base?
12.x: Binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal have bases 2, 8, 10 and 16 respectively.
12.tq: Check the base rather than the familiar name of the number system.
xs: **Binary — 2** is correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Hexadecimal uses digits **0-9** and **A-F**.

12.s: The hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆ is equal to
12.x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.
12.tq: Convert hexadecimal by applying place value and digit value.
xs: **(FF)16 = 255** — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: **Hexadecimal** is base **16** (digits **0-9**, **A-F**).

12.s:
Consider the following statements about logic gates:
1. NAND and NOR are universal gates.
2. An XOR gate gives output 1 when its inputs are the same.
3. AND, OR and NOT are the basic logic gates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAND and NOR are the universal gates. Statement 2 is wrong: XOR gives 1 when the inputs differ, not when they are the same. Statement 3 is correct: AND, OR and NOT are the basic gates. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and the other two options include the false statement 2.
12.tq: XOR = 'exclusive' = 1 only when inputs differ; universal = NAND, NOR.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **NAND and NOR** are **universal gates**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **XOR** gives 1 when inputs **differ**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **AND, OR, NOT** are the basic gates.
xa: Boolean algebra was given by **George Boole**.
**De Morgan**: (A+B)' = A'.B'.

12.s:
Consider the following Boolean identities:
1. A + A = A
2. A · A′ = 0
3. (A + B)′ = A′ · B′
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: All three are valid Boolean identities; the third is De Morgan's law.
12.tq: Verify each algebraic identity independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three identities are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
**(A+B)' = A'.B'** is **De Morgan**'s law.
xa: Boolean algebra: **George Boole**.
**NAND** and **NOR** are universal gates.

12.s: Word length of a computer refers to the
o: number of bits handled by the CPU at one time
physical length of a memory module
number of characters stored in a file name
number of instructions executed in one minute
12.x: Word length is the number of bits that the CPU can handle at once, such as 32-bit or 64-bit processing.
12.tq: Separate a processing-width term from storage and speed terms.
xs: **Word length** = the **number of bits handled by the CPU at one time** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Typical word lengths: **32-bit** and **64-bit**.
xa: **Clock speed** is measured in **hertz (GHz)**.
**MIPS** = million instructions per second.
**Bandwidth** = data-transfer rate, in **bits per second (bps)**.

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Clock speed — floating-point operations per second
12.x: Bandwidth measures data-transfer rate in bits per second. Clock speed is measured in hertz, MIPS denotes million instructions per second, and word length is measured in bits.
12.tq: Match each performance term with its precise unit or meaning.
xs: **Bandwidth — bits per second** is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Clock speed** is in **hertz (GHz)**, not FLOPS; **MIPS** = million instructions per second, not data-transfer rate.
**Word length** is counted in **bits** (32-bit, 64-bit), not hertz.
xa: **FLOPS** = floating-point operations per second — supercomputer speed.
The **Linpack (HPL)** benchmark gives results in FLOPS.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about computer performance terms:
1. MIPS stands for million instructions per second.
2. Clock speed is measured in bits per second.
3. FLOPS (floating-point operations per second) is used to express supercomputer speed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
12.x: Statement 1 is correct: MIPS = million instructions per second. Statement 2 is wrong: clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz); bits per second is the unit of bandwidth. Statement 3 is correct: FLOPS expresses supercomputer speed. Hence '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 2 include the false unit.
12.tq: Clock = hertz, bandwidth = bps, supercomputer = FLOPS.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — so option **(3) 1 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is **correct**: **MIPS** = **million instructions per second**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: clock speed is in **hertz (GHz)**; bits per second is the unit of **bandwidth**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **FLOPS** expresses **supercomputer** speed.
xa: **Word length** = bits the CPU handles at once.
World's fastest (**ISC 2026**): China's **LineShine**.

12.s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
12.x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
12.tq: Identify the benchmark from its distinctive workload and ranking application.
xs: The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** measures floating-point power on **large dense linear systems** and underlies world supercomputer rankings — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ASCII** and **Unicode** are character codes, and **MIPS** counts instructions — none rank supercomputers.
xa: Results are in **FLOPS**.
**ISC 2026** list: China's **LineShine** replaced US **El Capitan** at the top.

12.s: According to the ISC 2026 ranking referred to here, the world’s fastest supercomputer is
o: El Capitan of the United States
12.x: China’s LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States’ El Capitan.
12.tq: Track the current ranking and the country-replacement relationship carefully.
xs: China's **LineShine** tops the **ISC 2026** list — so option **(1)** is correct.
It replaced the US's **El Capitan**, which held the top spot before.
**Param Shakti** is India's (**IIT Madras**), not Japan's; **PARAM 8000** is not on this list.
xa: Rankings use the **Linpack (HPL)** benchmark in **FLOPS**.
**Param Shakti**: **3.1 petaflops**, C-DAC **RUDRA** servers.

12.s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti at IIT Madras:
1. It was launched by MeitY.
2. It has a capacity of 3.1 petaflops.
3. It uses C-DAC RUDRA servers.
4. It operates with open-source AlmaLinux.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was launched by MeitY, has 3.1 petaflops capacity, uses C-DAC RUDRA servers and runs open-source AlmaLinux.
12.tq: Verify all institutional, numerical and technical attributes before choosing the complete code.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is the answer.
**Param Shakti** at **IIT Madras** was launched by **MeitY** with **3.1 petaflops**.
It runs on **C-DAC RUDRA** servers with open-source **AlmaLinux**.
xa: It was funded under the **National Supercomputing Mission**.
Supercomputer speed is measured in **FLOPS**.

12.s: Param Shakti at IIT Madras was funded under the
12.x: Param Shakti was funded under the National Supercomputing Mission.
12.tq: Identify the correct government mission associated with the named installation.
xs: Param Shakti was funded under the **National Supercomputing Mission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched by **MeitY** at **IIT Madras**.
xa: Capacity **3.1 petaflops**; C-DAC **RUDRA** servers; **AlmaLinux**.
**LineShine** (China) tops the **ISC 2026** list.

12.s:
Which of the following are associated with quantum computing?
1. Superposition
2. Entanglement
3. Cryptography
4. Optimisation
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: Quantum computing uses superposition and entanglement and has applications in cryptography and optimisation. All four statements are correct.
12.tq: Combine the underlying principles with the listed application areas.
xs: All four are linked to quantum computing — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
Quantum computers use **qubits** with **superposition** and **entanglement**.
Uses: ultra-fast calculation, **cryptography**, **optimisation**.
xa: **Q-Day** = when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048**.
That would use **Shor's algorithm (1994)**.

12.s: Q-Day refers to the point at which quantum computers may be capable of
o: breaking RSA-2048 public-key encryption using Shor’s algorithm
converting every file into PDF format
increasing the clock speed of classical processors
12.x: Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.
12.tq: Link the specialised term to its specific security consequence and algorithm.
xs: **Q-Day** is when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048 public-key encryption** using **Shor's algorithm** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Shor's algorithm dates from **1994**.
xa: Quantum computers use **qubits** (superposition, entanglement).
Quantum applications include **cryptography** and **optimisation**.

12.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
12.x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.
12.tq: Start from the sure file-type pair and eliminate the swapped categories.
xs: **MP4 — Video** is correctly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
MP4 = **MPEG-4 Part 14**.
**MP3** is **audio**; **PDF** is a **document**; **MOV** is **video**, not image.
xa: **MP3** = MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3.
Other video formats: **MOV** (QuickTime, Apple), **AVI** (Audio Video Interleave, Microsoft).

12.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
12.x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.
12.tq: Find the altered word in an otherwise familiar acronym expansion.
xs: **PNG — Portable Network Graphics Interface** is NOT correct — so option **(4)** is the answer.
PNG = **Portable Network Graphics** — there is no "Interface".
**GIF** = Graphics Interchange Format; **AVI** = Audio Video Interleave; **MOV** = QuickTime Movie.
xa: **JPEG** = Joint Photographic Experts Group — image, **lossy**.
**PDF** = Portable Document Format (**Adobe**).

12.s:
Consider the following statements regarding ASCII:
1. ASCII is a 7-bit character-encoding scheme.
2. ASCII represents 128 characters.
3. Unicode extends the character-representation capability of ASCII.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
12.x: ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation. All three statements are correct.
12.tq: Check each numerical and relationship statement before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is the answer.
**ASCII** is **7-bit** and represents **128** characters.
**Unicode** extends it.
xa: ASCII = **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**.
A **byte** = **8 bits**; a **nibble** = **4 bits**.

12.s: JPEG is primarily associated with which of the following?
12.x: JPEG, or Joint Photographic Experts Group, is an image format commonly associated with lossy compression.
12.tq: Distinguish the file format’s information type from unrelated compression categories.
xs: **JPEG** is a **lossy** **image** format — so option **(2)** is correct.
JPEG = **Joint Photographic Experts Group**.
xa: Other image formats: **GIF** and **PNG**.
**MP3** is audio; **MP4**, **MOV**, **AVI** are video.

12.s: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is best understood as an umbrella term covering devices and applications used to
o: replace all forms of human communication
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
12.x: ICT covers devices and applications used to access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.
12.tq: Choose the comprehensive definition rather than an exclusive or extreme description.
xs: ICT covers devices and applications to **access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It includes **mobiles, networks, software, internet, satellites**.
xa: ICT aims at human-human, human-machine and **M2M** communication.
Criticisms: **privacy risks**, **digital divide**, job insecurity, over-reliance on technology.

12.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate associated with ICT?
12.x: Privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology are identified concerns. Guaranteed elimination of technological dependence is not such a criticism.
12.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated group of ICT concerns.
xs: **Guaranteed elimination of technological dependence** is not an ICT criticism — so option **(2)** is correct.
The listed concerns are **privacy risks**, **digital divide**, **job insecurity** and **over-reliance on technology** — the opposite of eliminating dependence.
xa: ICT = umbrella term for devices/applications to **access, store, transmit and manipulate** digital information.
Current relevance: **LineShine** tops **ISC 2026**; **Param Shakti** at IIT Madras.

12.s:
ICT aims to facilitate communication among which of the following?
1. Human and human
2. Human and machine
3. Machine and machine
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
12.x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication. Therefore, all three forms are included.
12.tq: Read the communication relationships separately before selecting the combined option.
xs: ICT aims at **human-human, human-machine and machine-machine (M2M)** communication — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
All three channels are named in the notes: **M2M** stands for machine-to-machine.
xa: ICT covers **mobiles, networks, software, internet, satellites**.
⚠ Concerns include the **digital divide** and **privacy risks**.

13.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
13.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
13.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.
xs: **ARPANET** (**1969**) was developed under the **US Department of Defense** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ARPANET is regarded as the **forerunner of the internet**.
**W3C** was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994** — it sets web standards, it did not build ARPANET.
xa: The **WWW** was invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1989** at **CERN**.
India's firsts: **ERNET** (**1986**, academic network) → **VSNL** public internet (**15 August 1995**) → **Satyam Infoway (Sify)**, first private ISP (**1998**).
⚠ Do not confuse the **internet** (ARPANET lineage, 1969) with the **WWW** (Berners-Lee, 1989).

13.s: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in which year?
13.x: Tim Berners-Lee founded the W3C in 1994. The other years correspond to ERNET, the invention of the WWW and the emergence of Satyam Infoway as a private ISP.
13.tq: Discriminate between closely related milestones by their years.
xs: **W3C (World Wide Web Consortium)** was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1986** is **ERNET**, India's academic network.
**1989** is when Berners-Lee invented the **WWW** at **CERN**.
**1998** is the year **Satyam Infoway (Sify)** became the first private ISP.
xa: **W3C** develops and maintains **web standards** so pages work the same across browsers.
**ARPANET** (**1969**, US Department of Defense) was the forerunner of the internet.
**VSNL** launched public internet in India on **15 August 1995**.

13.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the Indian Internet milestones in chronological order?
o: Public internet by VSNL, ERNET, Satyam Infoway
Satyam Infoway, ERNET, public internet by VSNL
ERNET, public internet by VSNL, Satyam Infoway
ERNET, Satyam Infoway, public internet by VSNL
13.x: ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.
13.tq: Use the first, middle and last dates to establish the sequence.
xs: The correct order is **ERNET → VSNL public internet → Satyam Infoway** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**ERNET** began in **1986** as India's academic network.
**VSNL** launched public internet on **15 August 1995**.
**Satyam Infoway (Sify)** became the **first private ISP** in **1998**.
xa: Global milestones: **ARPANET** (**1969**) → **WWW** (**1989**, CERN) → **W3C** (**1994**).
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation.
**NIXI** (**2003**) runs India's internet exchange points and the **.in registry**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network types:
1. A PAN links an individual's personal devices, typically through Bluetooth.
2. A MAN generally covers a city.
3. A firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi is using a MAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: PAN = personal area, e.g. Bluetooth. Statement 2 is correct: MAN covers a city. Statement 3 is wrong: linking LANs in different cities needs a WAN, which spans large areas (the internet is a global WAN) - this was the APPSC 2019 answer. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: Across cities = WAN; within one city = MAN.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: a **PAN** is a personal area network, e.g. **Bluetooth**.
Statement 2 is correct: a **MAN** covers **a city**.
Statement 3 is wrong: linking LANs in **Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi** needs a **WAN** (APPSC **2019**).
xa: A **LAN** covers an office, home or campus.
A **WAN** spans large areas and links LANs — **the internet is a global WAN**.
A **VPN** is an encrypted **"tunnel"** over a public network.

13.s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
13.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
13.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
xs: A **VPN** provides an **encrypted tunnel over a public network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not replace protocols, is not a one-room wireless link and is not a privately owned cable.
xa: Network types by scope: **PAN** (personal, Bluetooth) → **LAN** (office/home/campus) → **MAN** (a city) → **WAN** (large areas).
**The internet is a global WAN**.
**HTTPS** also encrypts browser-server traffic, via **TLS**.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding network topologies:
1. In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable.
2. In a star topology, failure of one node normally isolates the entire network.
3. In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbouring nodes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. In a star topology, failure of one node is generally isolated; failure of the central hub can stop the network.
13.tq: Find the incorrect resilience statement before selecting the code.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: in a **bus** topology all nodes sit on **one backbone cable**.
Statement 2 is wrong: in a **star**, one node failing is **isolated**; only **hub failure** stops all.
Statement 3 is correct: in a **ring**, each node links to **two neighbours**.
xa: A **backbone break** stops the whole bus network; **one break** can disrupt a ring.
**Mesh**: every node linked to every other — **most resilient**, costliest (**n(n-1)/2** links).
**Tree**: a hierarchy of star networks — a branch fails if its parent fails.

13.s: Which topology is characterised by every node being connected to every other node?
13.x: In a mesh topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it highly resilient but costly.
13.tq: Use the complete-connectivity clue.
xs: In a **mesh** topology every node is linked to every other node — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bus** uses one backbone cable; **ring** links each node to two neighbours; **tree** is a hierarchy of stars.
xa: Mesh is the **most resilient** but **costliest**, needing **n(n-1)/2** links.
**Star**: all nodes to a central **hub/switch**; hub failure stops all.
⚠ A **bus** backbone break stops the whole network.

13.s: A tree topology is best described as:
o: A single circular connection of nodes
A topology in which every node has a direct link to every other node
A network using only one backbone cable
13.x: A tree topology combines star networks in a hierarchy. Failure of a parent can affect the branch below it.
13.tq: Match the structural description with the topology name.
xs: A **tree** topology is a **hierarchy of star networks** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A circular link is a **ring**; every node linked to every other is a **mesh**; one backbone cable is a **bus**.
xa: In a tree, a **branch fails if its parent fails**.
**Star**: one node failing is isolated, but **hub failure** stops all.
**Mesh** is most resilient and costliest (**n(n-1)/2** links).

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Device)
a. Hub
b. Switch
c. Router
d. Modem

List-II (Primary role)
i. Routes packets using IP
 ii. Converts digital and analogue signals
 iii. Broadcasts data to all ports
 iv. Forwards frames using MAC addresses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.
13.tq: Start from the sure device-function pairs and complete the code.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hub** broadcasts to all ports (**Physical**, layer 1).
**Switch** forwards frames by **MAC address** (**Data link**, layer **2**).
**Router** routes packets by **IP** (**Network**, layer **3**); **modem** converts **digital ↔ analog**.
xa: A **repeater** regenerates a weak signal (Physical layer); a **bridge** works like a switch (layer 2).
A **gateway** joins networks that use **different protocols** (all/upper layers).
Modem = **Modulator-demodulator**.

13.s: A gateway differs from a router chiefly because a gateway:
o: Operates only as a physical cable
Broadcasts every frame to all ports
13.x: A gateway joins networks that use different protocols and may operate across all or upper OSI layers.
13.tq: Discriminate between two nearby networking devices by their interoperability function.
xs: A **gateway** **joins networks using different protocols** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A **router** connects different networks and routes by **IP** at the **Network** layer (**3**).
Broadcasting every frame to all ports is a **hub**'s job.
xa: A gateway works at **all/upper layers** of the OSI model.
Exam angle: device-to-layer matching — **switch = 2, router = 3**.
**Hub / repeater** sit at the **Physical** layer (**1**).

13.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
13.x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
13.tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.
xs: Top to bottom: **Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) is the bottom-to-top order; options (3) and (4) swap layers.
xa: Layer **7 Application**: **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
Layer **4 Transport**: **TCP, UDP**; layer **3 Network**: **IP**, router.
Layer **2 Data Link**: **MAC addresses**, switch, bridge, NIC; layer **1 Physical**: cables, hub, repeater.

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.
13.tq: Find the device placed at the wrong OSI layer.
xs: **Modem — Transport layer** is wrong: a modem is a **Physical**-layer device — so option **(3)** is correct.
A modem is a **modulator-demodulator** converting **digital ↔ analog** signals.
**Switch** = Data Link (**2**), **router** = Network (**3**), **hub** = Physical (**1**) are all correct.
xa: The **Transport** layer (**4**) carries **TCP** and **UDP**.
A **gateway** joins networks with different protocols (all/upper layers).
A **repeater** regenerates a weak signal at the Physical layer.

13.s:
Match the following OSI layers with their associated functions or protocols:
List-I (Layer)
a. Presentation
b. Session
c. Transport
d. Data Link

List-II (Function or protocol)
i. TCP and UDP
ii. Encryption, compression and formats
 iii. Opens and closes sessions
 iv. MAC addressing and frame forwarding

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.
13.tq: Start with the distinctive TCP/UDP and MAC pairs.
xs: The correct match is **a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Presentation**: encryption, compression, formats (e.g. **JPEG**).
**Session**: opens and closes sessions; **Transport**: **TCP and UDP**.
**Data Link**: framing, **MAC addresses**, error detection; switch, bridge, NIC.
xa: **Application** layer (**7**): **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
**Network** layer (**3**): **IP**; router.
**Physical** layer (**1**): cables, hub, repeater.

13.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the OSI layer?
1. HTTP — Application layer
2. IP — Network layer
3. MAC — Data Link layer
4. Cables — Physical layer
Select the correct answer.
13.x: HTTP is an Application-layer protocol, IP belongs to the Network layer, MAC is associated with the Data Link layer, and cables operate at the Physical layer.
13.tq: Use protocol and device layer matching to validate each statement.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**HTTP** is an **Application**-layer protocol; **IP** belongs to the **Network** layer.
**MAC addresses** are used at the **Data Link** layer; **cables** belong to the **Physical** layer.
xa: Data Link also covers **Ethernet** and **PPP**.
The **Session** layer opens and closes sessions; **Presentation** handles encryption and formats.
A **MAC address** is **48 bits**, burnt into the network card.

13.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its transmission mode?
1. Radio or television broadcast — Simplex
2. Walkie-talkie — Half duplex
3. Telephone conversation — Full duplex
Select the correct answer.
13.x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
13.tq: Compare the direction and simultaneity of communication.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**Simplex** = one way (**radio/TV broadcast**, keyboard).
**Half duplex** = both ways, one at a time (**walkie-talkie**).
**Full duplex** = both at once (**telephone**).
xa: A **keyboard** is another simplex example.
Connection media: **DSL** (telephone copper), **cable** (coaxial TV cable), **fibre** (light pulses).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about Internet connection media:
1. DSL uses telephone copper lines.
2. Cable Internet uses coaxial television cable.
3. Fibre Internet transmits data as light pulses through optical fibre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: DSL uses telephone copper lines, cable Internet uses coaxial TV cable, and fibre Internet uses optical fibre carrying light pulses.
13.tq: Match each technology with its physical transmission medium.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**DSL** uses the **telephone copper line**; **cable** uses **coaxial TV cable**.
**Fibre** carries data as **light pulses** in optical fibre.
xa: **Satellite internet** has **space, ground and user (VSAT)** segments and needs **no terrestrial wire**.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light** — better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
**BharatNet** fibre reaches **2.18 lakh gram panchayats** (ES 2025-26).

13.s: Satellite Internet generally consists of which three segments?
13.x: Satellite Internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and does not require a terrestrial wire connection.
13.tq: Recall the three-part system architecture.
xs: Satellite internet has **space, ground and user (VSAT)** segments — so option **(1)** is correct.
It needs **no terrestrial wire**.
Application/session/transport are **OSI layers**; copper/coaxial/fibre are wired media; router/switch/modem are devices.
xa: Wired media: **DSL** (telephone copper), **cable** (coaxial), **fibre** (light pulses).
AP angle: talks on an **undersea cable landing station** for AP (**29 Jun 2026**).

13.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
13.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
13.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
xs: **HTTP** sets **how messages pass between web browsers and web servers** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Turning domain names into IP addresses is **DNS**.
Downloading e-mail to a device is **POP3**; PAN devices use **Bluetooth**.
xa: **HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**.
HTTP is an **Application** layer (**7**) protocol.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (when and how fast).

13.s: DNS performs which of the following functions?
o: Assigns MAC addresses to network cards
Converts human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses
13.x: DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
13.tq: Identify the service needed when a user knows a name but the network requires an IP address.
xs: **DNS** **converts human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses** — so option **(2)** is correct.
DNS is the **internet's directory** (name → IP address).
MAC addresses are **burnt into the network card**; file transfer is **FTP**.
xa: **ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global **domain name system** and IP allocation.
**DHCP** assigns IP addresses automatically.
Site blocking: ISPs use **DNS poisoning**, **HTTP interception** or **SNI filtering**.

13.s: Which protocol is primarily used for reliable delivery of data in the TCP/IP suite?
13.x: Within TCP/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
13.tq: Separate the transport reliability function of TCP from the addressing and routing function of IP.
xs: **TCP** ensures **reliable delivery** in the TCP/IP suite — so option **(4)** is correct.
**IP** addresses and routes packets; **DNS** turns names into IP addresses; **DHCP** assigns IP addresses.
xa: **TCP/IP** is the basic suite of the internet.
TCP and **UDP** work at the **Transport** layer (**4**); IP at the **Network** layer (**3**).
**IPv4** is **32 bits**; **IPv6** is **128 bits**.

13.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: POP3 — downloading mail to one device, usually deleting it from the server
IMAP — permanently deleting mail from the server after downloading it to one device
13.x: IMAP keeps mail on the server and synchronises it across devices. POP3 generally downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
13.tq: Distinguish the confusable mail protocols by their treatment of messages on the server.
xs: **IMAP — deleting mail after download** is wrong: IMAP **keeps mail on the server**, synced across devices — so option **(4)** is correct.
**POP3** downloads mail to one device and usually deletes it from the server.
**FTP** = file transfer; **SMTP** = **sends** e-mail — both correct.
xa: ⚠ **SMTP** sends; **POP3** downloads and deletes; **IMAP** keeps on server.
**DHCP** assigns IP addresses automatically.
**HTTP** passes messages between browsers and web servers.

13.s: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network?
13.x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically. DNS translates names into IP addresses, while HTTP and TCP perform different communication functions.
13.tq: Identify the protocol by its automatic address-assignment function.
xs: **DHCP** assigns IP addresses **automatically** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**DNS** turns names into IP addresses; **HTTP** transfers webpages; **TCP** ensures reliable delivery.
xa: **IPv4** addresses are **32 bits** in dotted decimal, e.g. **192.168.1.1**.
**IRINN**, run by **NIXI**, handles IP addresses in India.
**IP** addresses and routes packets at the Network layer.

13.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Protocol element)
A. Syntax
B. Semantics
C. Timing

List-II (Meaning)
1. Meaning of each field
2. Format of data
3. When and how fast to send

option_a
13.x: Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.
13.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘syntax–format’ and complete the protocol-element mapping.
xs: **Syntax – format of data, Semantics – meaning of each field, Timing – when and how fast** — so option **(1)** **A-2, B-1, C-3** is correct.
**Syntax** is the format of data; **semantics** is the meaning of each field.
**Timing** is when and how fast to send.
xa: **TCP/IP** is the basic protocol suite of the internet.
⚠ E-mail protocols: **SMTP** sends, **POP3** downloads, **IMAP** keeps on server.
**DHCP** assigns IP addresses automatically.

13.s:
Assertion (A): HTTPS provides greater security for browser-server communication than HTTP.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the traffic between the browser and the server through TLS.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
13.x: Both statements are true, and TLS-based encryption directly explains why HTTPS provides greater security than HTTP.
13.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the security difference between HTTP and HTTPS.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**, which is exactly why it is more secure than **HTTP**.
xa: **HTTP** sets how messages pass between browsers and web servers.
ISPs may block HTTPS sites by **SNI filtering**.
**VPN** = an encrypted tunnel over a public network.

13.s:
Consider the following statements about network addresses:
1. An IPv4 address is 32 bits long and written in dotted decimal, e.g. 192.168.1.1.
2. An IPv6 address is 128 bits long and written as eight groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
3. A MAC address is a 64-bit logical address assigned by DNS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: IPv4 = 32 bits, dotted decimal. Statement 2 is correct: IPv6 = 128 bits, eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons. Statement 3 is wrong: a MAC address is a 48-bit (6-byte, 12 hex digits) physical address burnt into the network card and used at the data link layer; DNS only turns names into IP addresses. Hence '1 and 2 only'; the other options either miss statement 2 or include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 32 / 128 / 48: IPv4 / IPv6 / MAC; MAC is physical, burnt into the card.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **IPv4** = **32 bits**, dotted decimal (e.g. 192.168.1.1).
Statement 2 is correct: **IPv6** = **128 bits**, 8 groups of hexadecimal separated by colons.
Statement 3 is wrong: a **MAC** address is **48 bits**, a **physical** address burnt into the network card.
xa: IPv4 offers **~4.3 billion** addresses.
A MAC address = **6 bytes**, **12 hex digits**; used at the **data link** layer.
**DNS** only turns names into IP addresses.

13.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents IPv4 address classes by their first-octet ranges?
1. Class A — 1 to 126
2. Class B — 128 to 191
3. Class C — 192 to 223
4. Class D — 240 to 255
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively. Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E for experimental use.
13.tq: Check each numerical range against the class boundary, especially the swapped D and E ranges.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Class D** = **224-239** (multicast); **240-255** is **Class E** (experimental).
xa: **127.x.x.x** is the **loopback** range.
Classes are decided by the **first octet**.
IPv4 is **32 bits**; IPv6 is **128 bits**.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
13.x: The 127.x.x.x range is used for loopback. Class D multicast is 224–239, Class E experimental is 240–255, and 192–223 is Class C.
13.tq: Find the correctly matched exception among deliberately interchanged class ranges.
xs: **127.x.x.x — loopback** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**192-223** is **Class C**, not B.
**224-239** is **Class D** (multicast); **240-255** is **Class E** (experimental) — options (3) and (4) swap them.
xa: IPv4 uses dotted decimal, e.g. **192.168.1.1**.
A **MAC** address is **48 bits** (physical).

13.s:
Consider the following statements about wireless standards:
1. Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1 and is a personal area network (PAN) technology.
2. Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11 and uses the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, with 6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E.
3. Wi-Fi Direct needs an existing LAN to link two devices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bluetooth = IEEE 802.15.1, a PAN technology. Statement 2 is correct: Wi-Fi = IEEE 802.11 on 2.4 and 5 GHz (6 GHz in Wi-Fi 6E). Statement 3 is wrong: Wi-Fi Direct links devices with no LAN. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the other options include the false statement 3.
13.tq: 802.15.1 = Bluetooth (PAN), 802.11 = Wi-Fi (WLAN); 'Direct' means no LAN needed.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Bluetooth** = **IEEE 802.15.1**, a **PAN** technology.
Statement 2 is correct: **Wi-Fi** = **IEEE 802.11**, **2.4 GHz and 5 GHz** (6 GHz in **Wi-Fi 6E**).
Statement 3 is wrong: **Wi-Fi Direct** links devices **with no LAN**.
xa: Bluetooth uses the **2.4 GHz ISM band**; microwave ovens and cordless phones share 2.4 GHz.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light** — better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
The **2019** APPSC key gave **Bluetooth 5.1** as the latest version.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bluetooth and Wi-Fi:
1. Bluetooth generally has a short range of about 10 metres for a class 2 device.
2. Wi-Fi generally provides coverage over a longer range, such as a whole building.
3. Bluetooth operates only in the 5 GHz band.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: Bluetooth class 2 devices have a short range of approximately 10 metres, while Wi-Fi generally covers a larger area. Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, not only in 5 GHz.
13.tq: Use range and frequency comparisons to reject the absolute frequency claim.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: Bluetooth range is short — **~10 m** (class 2).
Statement 2 is correct: **Wi-Fi** covers a longer range, a **whole building**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Bluetooth uses the **2.4 GHz ISM band**; Wi-Fi uses 2.4 and 5 GHz.
xa: Bluetooth = **IEEE 802.15.1** (PAN); Wi-Fi = **IEEE 802.11** (wireless LAN).
**Wi-Fi 6E** adds the **6 GHz** band.
Other **2.4 GHz** devices: **microwave ovens**, cordless phones.

13.s: The 2019 APPSC key identified which version as the latest version of Bluetooth?
13.x: The 2019 APPSC key treated Bluetooth 5.1 as the latest version. This is a time-specific reference and should not be confused with later versions.
13.tq: Recognise the dated examination reference rather than applying an unspecified current-version claim.
xs: The **2019 APPSC** key gave **Bluetooth 5.1** as the latest version — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is a **time-specific** exam key; newer versions have come since 5.1.
xa: Bluetooth = **IEEE 802.15.1**, a **PAN** technology on the **2.4 GHz** ISM band.
Class 2 Bluetooth range is about **10 m**.
**Wi-Fi Direct** links devices with no LAN.

13.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the function of HTML tags in a webpage?
o: They define and mark up the structure of text and other content
They assign numerical IP addresses to webpages
13.x: HTML tags mark up and structure the text and other content of webpages. Encryption and indexing are performed by other technologies or services.
13.tq: Distinguish the structural role of HTML from the functions of encryption, addressing and search.
xs: **HTML tags** **mark up the structure of text and other content** of webpages — so option **(1)** is correct.
HTML = **HyperText Markup Language**; a web server keeps information in webpages marked up with HTML tags.
Assigning IP addresses is **DHCP**; indexing is a **search engine**'s job; encryption is **HTTPS/TLS**.
xa: Core front-end technologies: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript**.
**W3C** maintains web standards so pages work the same across browsers.
Exam angle: the **browser** displays webpages; the **server** stores them.

13.s:
Consider the following statements regarding web technologies:
1. A web server stores webpages and sends them when requested.
2. A web browser requests webpages and displays them on the screen.
3. A search engine indexes webpages so that they can be found.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: All three statements are correct. The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
13.tq: Separate the closely related functions of the server, browser and search engine.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3** is correct.
A **web server** stores webpages and **serves** them on request.
A **web browser** fetches and **displays** webpages (Chrome, Firefox); a **search engine** **indexes** them (Google, Bing).
xa: ⚠ Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" = **browser**; "which one stores them" = **server**.
**URL** parts: **protocol** + **domain name** + **path to the file**.
The **surface web** (~**4-5%**) is the part indexed by search engines.

13.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of the principal parts of a URL?
o: Protocol, domain name, path to the file
Protocol, path to the file, domain name
13.x: A URL contains the protocol, such as https://, followed by the domain name and the path to the file.
13.tq: Test the internal order of URL components instead of merely recalling its expansion.
xs: A URL runs **protocol, domain name, path to the file** — so option **(2)** is correct.
e.g. protocol **https://** + domain **www.example.in** + path.
xa: **URL** = **Uniform Resource Locator**.
**DNS** turns the domain name into a numerical **IP address**.
**NIXI** runs India's **.in registry**.

13.s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
13.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
13.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
xs: **W3C** **develops and maintains web standards** so pages work the same across browsers — so option **(1)** is correct.
MAC addresses are **burnt into the network card**; the global domain name system is coordinated by **ICANN**.

13.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its description?
