21.tq: Recognise the complete application cluster rather than an unrelated technology list.
xs: The other listed IoT uses are **smart grids, logistics tracking and smart buildings** (HVAC) — option **(1)**.
Facial recognition (**NAFRS**), **NFTs**, **Li-Fi** and cloud storage are other ICT items, not the notes' IoT use list.
xa: Smart city: **traffic**, **air-quality monitoring**, **waste collection**, public safety.
Smart agriculture: **precision farming**, soil monitoring, livestock, yields.
IoT pillars: **device, data, analytics, connectivity**.

21.s: The four pillars identified for IoT are:
21.x: The four IoT pillars are device, data, analytics and connectivity.
21.tq: Recall the exact components of a named framework.
xs: IoT's four pillars are **device, data, analytics and connectivity** — option **(3)**.
None of the other sets (agriculture, taxation, robotics, legislation) matches.
xa: IoT = devices networked to communicate **without human intervention**.
Three-layer architecture: **perception → network → application**.
**IIoT** = Industrial IoT (production, equipment health).

21.s: The defining feature of the Internet of Things (IoT) is that:
o: Devices are networked to communicate without human intervention
Every device must be operated manually by a human user
Data is transmitted only through LEDs
All devices must be connected through a single blockchain ledger
21.x: IoT devices are networked to communicate with each other without human intervention. Manual operation is the opposite of IoT; data through LEDs describes Li-Fi; a blockchain ledger is DLT, not a defining feature of IoT.
21.tq: IoT = machines talking to machines, no human needed.
xs: IoT = **devices networked to communicate without human intervention** — option **(1)**.
Manual operation is the opposite; data via **LEDs** is **Li-Fi**; a single ledger is **DLT/blockchain**, not IoT.
xa: Pillars: **device, data, analytics, connectivity**.
Exam angle: "What does IoT stand for?" — **Internet of Things** (APPSC **2023**, **2024**).
Layers: **perception** (sensors) → **network** → **application**.

21.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The metaverse is a shared immersive virtual world using AR and VR.
2. Augmented Reality (AR) creates a fully simulated environment.
3. Virtual Reality (VR) creates a fully simulated environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: the metaverse is a shared immersive virtual world built on AR/VR. Statement 2 is wrong: AR overlays digital content on the real world; it does not fully simulate it. Statement 3 is correct: VR is fully simulated. So A, C and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
21.tq: AR adds to reality; VR replaces it.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **metaverse** is a **shared immersive virtual world using AR/VR**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **AR overlays digital content on the real** world; it is not fully simulated.
Statement 3 is correct: **VR is fully simulated** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Web 3.0**: decentralised, blockchain-based internet.
**Edge computing**: data processed near the source → low latency.

21.s: The National Automated Facial Recognition System (NAFRS) is associated with the
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology exclusively
21.x: NAFRS is associated with the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB). Facial-recognition systems also raise privacy concerns.
21.tq: Match the named system with the correct government body.
xs: **NAFRS** (National Automated Facial Recognition System) belongs to the **NCRB** — **National Crime Records Bureau**, option **(1)**.
It raises **privacy concerns** — a listed debate.
xa: **I4C's NCAP** uses AI and big data on **crime trends**.
**AP State Data Lake** cross-links **RCH health with POSHAN** data and housing with **land pattas**.
Criticism: **facial recognition and privacy**; **net neutrality vs slicing**.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about RFID tags:
1. Active tags have their own battery.
2. Active tags generally have a longer range than passive tags.
3. Passive tags are powered by the reader's signal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Active RFID tags contain their own battery and generally offer longer range. Passive tags draw power from the reader's signal.
21.tq: Combine power source and range to distinguish active and passive tags.
xs: All correct: **active tags** have their **own battery** and **longer range**; **passive tags** are **powered by the reader's signal** — option **(4)**.
RFID = tags + readers over **radio waves**.
xa: **NFC** works within a **few centimetres**.
**Li-Fi** = data via **LEDs**.
**IIoT** = Industrial IoT (production, equipment health).

21.s: What is the principal advantage of edge computing over sending all data to a distant cloud first?
o: It replaces all sensors with blockchain tokens.
It ensures that no data is ever processed by a computer.
It processes data near the source, reducing latency and bandwidth use while supporting privacy.
It always requires a central data centre in another country.
21.x: Edge computing processes data near its source, which can reduce latency, save bandwidth and support privacy.
21.tq: Select the option containing the complete operational advantage.
xs: **Edge computing** **processes data near the source**, giving **low latency**, **bandwidth saving** and **privacy** — option **(3)**.
It needs no distant central data centre — that is the opposite of edge.
xa: **Fog computing** sits **between edge and cloud**.
**Reliance** pledged a nationwide **edge network** at the India AI Summit (**2026**).
5G latency can be as low as **1 ms**.

21.s: Fog computing is positioned primarily
o: above the application layer of IoT only
between edge computing and the cloud
21.x: Fog computing occupies an intermediate position between edge devices and cloud computing.
21.tq: Use the spatial relationship in the computing hierarchy.
xs: **Fog computing** sits **between edge computing and the cloud** — option **(3)**.
Not a battery, IoT layer or network generation.
xa: **Edge computing**: data processed near the source → low latency, bandwidth saving, privacy.
**SaaS / PaaS / IaaS**: cloud service models.
IoT layers: **perception → network → application**.

21.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Data Lake is used to cross-link which of the following data combinations for plugging leakages?
o: RCH health with POSHAN data, and housing with land pattas
5G traffic with Wi-Fi 7, and NFTs with bonds
Facial images with AR overlays, and RFID with Li-Fi
SaaS with PaaS, and IaaS with Web 3.0
21.x: The AP State Data Lake cross-links RCH health data with POSHAN data and housing data with land pattas to help plug leakages.
21.tq: Pair the governance datasets with their stated administrative purpose.
xs: The **AP State Data Lake** cross-links **RCH health with POSHAN data** and **housing with land pattas** to **plug leakages** — option **(1)**.
The other options mix unrelated tech terms (5G, NFTs, SaaS).
xa: **I4C's NCAP** uses **AI and big data** on crime trends.
**NAFRS** = **NCRB**; privacy concerns.
**DigiVerify** = AP's blockchain application.

21.s: I4C's NCAP uses artificial intelligence and big data primarily for analysing
21.x: I4C's NCAP uses AI and big data to analyse crime trends.
21.tq: Identify the governance problem addressed by the analytics system.
xs: **I4C's NCAP** uses **AI and big data** on **crime trends** — option **(4)**.
Soil and livestock belong to **smart agriculture** IoT, not NCAP.
xa: **NAFRS** is run by **NCRB**, with privacy concerns.
**AP State Data Lake** plugs leakages by cross-linking datasets.
Reliance pledged a nationwide **edge network** (India AI Summit **2026**).

21.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated feature of blockchain technology?
o: Compulsory control by a single central authority
21.x: Blockchain is characterised by a decentralised distributed ledger, immutability and transparency. Compulsory control by a single central authority is contrary to the stated features.
21.tq: Find the option that reverses the decentralised nature of blockchain.
xs: **Compulsory control by a single central authority** is not a feature — option **(3)**.
Blockchain is a **decentralised distributed ledger**, **immutable**, **transparent**, with **smart contracts**.
xa: Governance uses: **land records**, **digital certificates**, supply chains, **e-Notary** (blockchain e-Sign).
**DLT** = Distributed Ledger Technology.
**DigiVerify** = AP blockchain.

21.s: Tokenization in blockchain applications may represent
o: unique digital assets and real-world assets such as land and bonds
21.x: Tokenization can create NFTs representing unique digital assets and tokens representing real-world assets such as land and bonds.
21.tq: Distinguish the broad asset scope from an extreme only-statement.
xs: **Tokenization** covers **NFTs (unique digital assets)** and **real-world asset tokens** such as **land and bonds** — option **(1)**.
The word "only" makes options (2)–(4) wrong.
xa: **NFT** = Non-Fungible Token — a unique blockchain token.
Blockchain features: decentralised, **immutable**, transparent, **smart contracts**.
**Web 3.0**: decentralised, blockchain-based internet.

21.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a governance use of blockchain?
o: Replacing all public administration with cryptocurrency mining
21.x: Blockchain governance uses include land records, digital certificates and farm insurance, among others. Replacing all public administration with cryptocurrency mining is not a stated use.
21.tq: Reject the extreme and unrelated governance claim.
xs: **Replacing all public administration with cryptocurrency mining** is not a listed use — option **(2)**.
Listed uses include **land records**, **digital certificates** and **farm insurance**.
xa: Others: pharma and agri **supply chains**, **e-Notary**, **e-voting**, health records, **SHG microfinance**.
AP's blockchain application: **DigiVerify**.
Blockchain features: **immutable**, transparent, decentralised.

21.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a blockchain governance application?
21.x: DigiVerify is Andhra Pradesh's blockchain governance application: a permissioned-blockchain platform for tamper-proof certificate verification. The other pairings are wrong: facial recognition (NAFRS) belongs to NCRB, and Wi-Fi 7 manufacturing and 5G network slicing have nothing to do with DigiVerify.
21.tq: Match the named state initiative with its institutional association.
xs: **DigiVerify** is matched with **Andhra Pradesh** — it is the notes' **AP blockchain** governance application, option **(2)**.
Facial recognition (**NAFRS**) belongs to **NCRB**; Wi-Fi 7 manufacturing (**TP-Link**) and **network slicing** have nothing to do with DigiVerify.
xa: Blockchain governance uses include **digital certificates** and **land records**.
**AP State Data Lake** cross-links **RCH** with **POSHAN** data.
AP also hosts a WEF **C4IR centre**, India's **3rd**.

21.s: Which of the following statements about 5G is correct?
o: It can have latency as low as 1 millisecond and supports massive device connectivity.
It necessarily operates only through a 4G core.
It was designed without any requirement of high reliability.
It supports fewer connected devices than earlier generations by definition.
21.x: 5G can provide latency as low as 1 millisecond, massive device connectivity and high reliability. 5G standalone can operate without a 4G core.
21.tq: Prefer the option containing the characteristic features without an absolute restriction.
xs: **5G** offers latency **as low as 1 ms** and **massive device connectivity**, with **high reliability** — option **(1)**.
Options (3) and (4) contradict these listed features; 5G **Standalone** runs **without a 4G core**, so (2) is wrong.
xa: **6G** is expected in the **early 2030s**.
**Network slicing** splits one physical network into virtual networks via **SDN/NFV**.
**IIITDM Kurnool** ranked **1st** in DoT's **100 5G Use Case Labs** evaluation.

21.s: Network slicing in 5G refers to
o: cutting a fibre cable into separate physical networks
splitting one physical network into virtual networks using SDN/NFV
dividing a smartphone screen into multiple displays
21.x: Network slicing creates multiple virtual networks over one physical network using Software-Defined Networking and Network Functions Virtualization.
21.tq: Identify the exact technical meaning rather than a literal interpretation of slicing.
xs: **Network slicing** = **splitting one physical network into virtual networks via SDN/NFV** — option **(3)**.
It is virtual, not a physical cut of fibre, and has nothing to do with tokens or screens.
xa: Use cases: **eMBB**, **URLLC**, **mMTC** (ITU/3GPP).
Debate: **net neutrality vs slicing** (Airtel's **'Priority Postpaid'**).
**5G NR** = 5G New Radio.

21.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with a 5G use-case category?
21.x: The recognised categories are eMBB, URLLC and mMTC. eMBB means enhanced Mobile Broadband, not exclusive Mobile Blockchain.
21.tq: Reject the look-alike expansion of a standard technical abbreviation.
xs: **eMBB — exclusive Mobile Blockchain** is wrong — option **(2)**: eMBB is **enhanced Mobile Broadband**.
**URLLC** and **mMTC** are the other ITU/3GPP **network-slicing** use cases, correctly expanded.
xa: Network slicing splits one physical network via **SDN/NFV**.
5G latency can be as low as **1 ms**.
**5G NR** = 5G New Radio (air interface).

21.s: The ‘Priority Postpaid’ offering of Airtel led to a debate concerning
21.x: Airtel's ‘Priority Postpaid’ offering raised a debate on net neutrality.
21.tq: Match the named telecom offering with the policy issue it raised.
xs: Airtel's **'Priority Postpaid'** raised a **net neutrality** debate (**3 Jun 2026**) — option **(3)**.
It is the **network-slicing vs net neutrality** debate, not privacy or tokenization.
xa: Facial recognition (**NAFRS**) raises a separate **privacy** debate.
**Network slicing**: one physical network split into virtual networks via SDN/NFV.
5G features: latency **as low as 1 ms**, massive connectivity, high reliability.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about 6G:
1. 6G is expected in the early 2030s.
2. The Bharat 6G Alliance was launched in 2023.
3. The Bharat 6G Vision document was released in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: 6G is expected in the early 2030s. Statement 2 is correct: the Bharat 6G Alliance was launched in 2023. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bharat 6G Vision document is also from 2023, not 2025. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
21.tq: Both Bharat 6G Alliance and Vision = 2023; 6G itself = early 2030s.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **6G** is expected in the **early 2030s**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Bharat 6G Alliance** was launched in **2023**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Bharat 6G Vision** document is from **2023**, not 2025 — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Generations: **1G (1980s)** → 5G now.
**IIITDM Kurnool** ranked **1st** in DoT's **100 5G Use Case Labs** (Jan-Jun **2026**).

21.s: Which institution topped the Department of Telecommunications’ 5G laboratories ranking in July 2026?
21.x: IIITDM Kurnool topped the Department of Telecommunications’ 5G labs ranking in July 2026.
21.tq: Use the institution–ranking–month association.
xs: **IIITDM Kurnool** topped DoT's **5G labs ranking** (July **2026**) — option **(3)**.
It ranked **1st** in the **'100 5G Use Case Labs'** evaluation (Jan-Jun **2026**).
xa: AP angle: WEF **C4IR centre in AP**; **AP-Google AI/cloud task force**.
5G latency as low as **1 ms**.
**Bharat 6G Alliance** launched **2023**.

21.s: The debate surrounding network slicing is closely linked with the principle of:
21.x: Network slicing has generated a debate concerning its compatibility with net neutrality.
21.tq: Connect the emerging technical practice with its principal regulatory debate.
xs: The network-slicing debate concerns **net neutrality** — option **(4)**.
It flared over Airtel's **'Priority Postpaid'** (June **2026**).
xa: Network slicing = one physical network split via **SDN/NFV**.
Use cases: **eMBB**, **URLLC**, **mMTC**.
Other debate: **facial recognition and privacy**.

21.s: The Andhra Pradesh–Google task force referred to in the context of emerging ICT focuses on:
o: Nuclear energy and space launch systems
21.x: The Andhra Pradesh–Google AI/cloud task force concerns artificial intelligence and cloud technologies.
21.tq: Use the named partnership to identify its technology domain.
xs: The **AP-Google task force** focuses on **AI and cloud** (June **2026**) — option **(1)**.
It is listed as an **AP angle** with no link to energy, mining or fisheries.
xa: WEF's **C4IR centre in AP** = India's **3rd** after Mumbai and Telangana.
**AP State Data Lake** cross-links datasets to **plug leakages**.
**SaaS / PaaS / IaaS** are cloud service models.

22.s: MCA portal and GSTN are examples of which e-governance model?
22.x: MCA portal and GSTN provide Government-to-Business services, represented by G2B.
22.tq: Use the beneficiary category—businesses—to identify the model.
xs: The **MCA portal** and **GSTN** are **G2B** (Government-to-Business) examples — option **(4)**.
**G2G** = NIC solutions for departments; **G2E** = online HR tools for employees.
xa: **MCA21** (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) is the online company-filing **G2B** MMP.
Four pillars of e-governance: **People, Process, Technology, Resources** (MPPSC **2024**).
Gartner phases: **Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation**.

22.s: NIC solutions for government departments illustrate which e-governance model?
22.x: NIC solutions serving government departments represent Government-to-Government interaction, or G2G.
22.tq: Distinguish inter-governmental services from citizen and employee services.
xs: **NIC solutions for departments** illustrate **G2G** (Government-to-Government) — option **(3)**.
**G2B** = MCA portal, GSTN; **G2E** = online HR tools for employees.
xa: **NIC** was set up in **1976** and is the base of India's digitisation.
NIC built **e-Taal**, a dashboard of e-transaction statistics.
**IVFRT** is run by the Bureau of Immigration **with NIC**.

22.s: Online human-resource tools for government employees are an example of:
22.x: Online HR tools for employees fall under the Government-to-Employee model, or G2E.
22.tq: Identify the model from the internal employee relationship.
xs: **Online HR tools for employees** are **G2E** (Government-to-Employee) — option **(1)**.
**G2B** = MCA portal/GSTN; **G2G** = NIC solutions for departments.
xa: e-Governance pillar of Digital India includes **e-HRMS** and **e-Office**.
Four pillars of e-governance: **People, Process, Technology, Resources**.
Benefits: **lower cost** of government and **more citizen input**.

22.s: Which of the following is a recognised challenge of e-governance?
22.x: Online fraud is a challenge of e-governance; data costs and funding gaps in some States are also identified challenges.
22.tq: Reject absolute claims and select the concrete implementation risk.
xs: **Online fraud** is a listed challenge of e-governance — option **(2)**.
The other challenges are **data costs** and **funding gaps in some states**, so options (3) and (4), which claim these vanish, are wrong.
xa: Benefits: **lower cost** of government + **more citizen input** (UPPSC **2024**); better transparency.
⚠ Trap: e-governance does **not reduce transparency**.
Other debates: **digital divide**, shared devices in rural areas, **data privacy**.

22.s: The four pillars of e-governance are:
22.x: The four pillars of e-governance are People, Process, Technology and Resources (MPPSC 2024). The other options mix in look-alike words such as Policy, Parliament, Police, Telecom, Planning and Regulation that are not among the pillars.
22.tq: Pillars = P-P-T-R: People, Process, Technology, Resources.
xs: The four pillars of e-governance are **People, Process, Technology and Resources** — option **(1)** (MPPSC **2024**).
The other options swap in look-alike words (Policy, Police, Planning).
xa: Gartner phases: **Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation** (MPPSC **2025**).
Models: **G2B** (MCA portal, GSTN), **G2G** (NIC), **G2E** (HR tools).
Challenges: data costs, **online fraud**, funding gaps.

22.s: According to the Gartner model, the correct sequence of the phases of e-governance is:
22.x: Gartner's four phases run Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation (MPPSC 2025). Option A swaps the first two, C swaps the middle two, and D is the reverse order.
22.tq: Gartner: Inform, Interact, Transact, Transform (I-I-T-T).
xs: The **Gartner** phases run **Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation** — option **(2)** (MPPSC **2025**).
Options (1) and (3) swap middle phases; (4) reverses the order.
xa: Pillars: **People, Process, Technology, Resources**.
e-Kranti principle: **"Transformation not translation"**.
Benefits: **lower cost** of government + **more citizen input**.

22.s: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of e-governance?
22.x: E-governance lowers the cost of government, increases citizen input (UPPSC 2024) and improves transparency. It does not reduce transparency, so D is the answer; it is a common trap.
22.tq: Trap: e-governance never 'reduces transparency'.
xs: **Reduced transparency** is not a benefit — option **(4)**; e-governance brings **better transparency**.
Real benefits: **lower cost** of government, **more citizen input** (UPPSC **2024**).
xa: ⚠ Trap: e-governance does **not reduce transparency**.
Challenges: **data costs**, **online fraud**, funding gaps in some states.
Gartner phases end in **Transformation**.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Informatics Centre (NIC):
1. It was set up in 1976.
2. It provides G2G solutions to government departments.
3. It built e-Taal, a dashboard of passport-issuance statistics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: NIC was set up in 1976. Statement 2 is correct: NIC provides G2G solutions. Statement 3 is wrong: e-Taal is a dashboard of e-transaction statistics, not passport statistics. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: e-Taal = e-Transaction Aggregation; NIC = 1976, G2G.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **NIC** was set up in **1976** and provides **G2G solutions**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **e-Taal** is a dashboard of **e-transaction statistics**, not passport issuance — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: NIC is the **base of India's digitisation**.
**IVFRT** is run by the **Bureau of Immigration with NIC**.
**Bhashini** is integrated with NIC tools such as **CollabFiles**.

22.s: The National e-Governance Plan was drafted by DeitY, now MeitY, in association with which body?
22.x: The NeGP was drafted by DeitY, now MeitY, with the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).
22.tq: Test the institutional partnership by distinguishing policy drafting from implementation.
xs: NeGP was drafted by **DeitY (now MeitY)** with **DARPG** — option **(3)**.
**Bureau of Immigration** runs IVFRT; **CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd** implements CSCs.
xa: NeGP was approved on **18 May 2006** with **27 MMPs** and **10 components**.
**DARPG** launched the **NeSDA 2025** portal (Jun **2026**).
**NeGD** is MeitY's programme-management arm.

22.s: NeGD is best described as which of the following?
o: A police organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs
MeitY’s programme-management arm under Digital India Corporation
A judicial body under the eCourts project
22.x: NeGD, or National e-Governance Division, is MeitY’s programme-management arm under Digital India Corporation.
22.tq: Use the organisational-hierarchy clue to distinguish NeGD from an implementing field agency.
xs: **NeGD (National e-Governance Division)** is **MeitY's programme-management arm**, under **Digital India Corporation** — option **(2)**.
Police networking is **CCTNS** (MHA); the judiciary's MMP is **eCourts**.
xa: **MeitY** coordinates **Digital India** with ministries and states.
**CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd** = SPV and implementing agency of CSCs.
**DeitY (now MeitY)** with **DARPG** drafted NeGP.

22.s: CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. functions as which of the following?
o: An SPV and implementing agency of Common Service Centres
The central ministry for corporate affairs
22.x: CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. is the special purpose vehicle and implementing agency of CSCs.
22.tq: Expand the institutional abbreviation through its implementation role.
xs: **CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd** is the **SPV and implementing agency of CSCs** — option **(3)**.
State data centres are **SDCs**; corporate affairs is the **MCA**.
xa: **CSCs** = village ICT kiosks run by local entrepreneurs — NeGP's **front end**.
**5.97 lakh CSCs** (**4.73 lakh** at GP level) under **Public Internet Access** pillar.
**NeGD** = MeitY's programme-management arm.

22.s: According to the APPSC 2017 answer key, which body was associated with the drive to make 100% of Government-to-Citizen (G2C) transactions digital?
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
22.x: The APPSC 2017 key gave NITI Aayog for the drive to make 100% of G2C transactions digital. NIC provides G2G solutions, CSC e-Governance Services is the SPV for CSCs, and DARPG co-drafted NeGP.
22.tq: 100% digital G2C (APPSC 2017) = NITI Aayog.
xs: The **APPSC 2017** key gave **NITI Aayog** for the drive to make **100%** of G2C transactions digital — option **(1)**.
**NIC** provides **G2G** solutions; **DARPG** co-drafted **NeGP**.
xa: APPSC **2017** also asked: mission for electronic delivery of all government services = **e-Kranti**.
**MeitY** coordinates Digital India.
**CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd** implements CSCs.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP):
1. It was approved on 18 May 2006.
2. At approval it had 27 Mission Mode Projects and 10 components.
3. Its MMPs were later expanded to 44.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006. Statement 2 is correct: it began with 27 MMPs and 10 components. Statement 3 is wrong: NeGP was later expanded to 31 MMPs; 44 MMPs belong to e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0). So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: 27 → 31 under NeGP; 44 under e-Kranti.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NeGP was approved on **18 May 2006** with **27 MMPs and 10 components**.
Statement 3 is wrong: NeGP later grew to **31 MMPs**; **44 MMPs** came under **e-Kranti** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Three-tier core: **CSCs** (front end), **SWAN** (network), **SDC** (back end).
**MSDG** (**2011**) serves mobile services.

22.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier core infrastructure of NeGP?
22.x: The three tiers are CSCs at the front end, SWAN as the network, and SDC at the back end.
22.tq: Start from the sure three-tier pairing and eliminate codes that shift the infrastructure roles.
xs: NeGP's three tiers: **Front end — CSCs**, **Network — SWAN**, **Back end — SDC** — option **(1)**.
**NIC** and **MCA21** are not tiers; options (2)–(4) shuffle the components.
xa: **CSCs**: village ICT kiosks run by local entrepreneurs.
**SWAN**: state HQ to block/taluka links.
**SDC**: state data centres hosting applications.

22.s: SWAN, in the NeGP core infrastructure, provides links between:
o: State headquarters and block or taluka offices
22.x: SWAN provides network links from State headquarters to block or taluka levels.
22.tq: Match the network acronym with its administrative connectivity role.
xs: **SWAN** links **state HQ to block/taluka** — option **(4)**.
It is the **network** tier between **CSCs** (front end) and **SDC** (back end).
xa: **SDC** = state data centres hosting applications.
**Meghraj / GI Cloud** is another NeGP piece.
**National Portal** india.gov.in = single window.

22.s: Which of the following is a Central category MMP under NeGP?
22.x: Income Tax is listed among the Central MMPs. Land Records and e-District are State MMPs, while eCourts is an Integrated MMP.
22.tq: Classify the project before comparing it with State and Integrated examples.
xs: **Income Tax** is a **Central** MMP — option **(1)**.
**eCourts** is **Integrated**; **Land Records** and **e-District** are **State** MMPs.
xa: Other Central MMPs: **MCA21**, **Passport**, **UID**, **Pensions**, **Posts**.
Integrated MMPs: **eCourts**, **e-Procurement**, **CSC**, **India Portal**, **e-Biz**.
State MMPs: **Treasuries**, **e-Panchayat**, **CCTNS**.

22.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a State MMP?
22.x: e-Panchayat is a State category MMP. UID and Pensions are Central examples, while India Portal is an Integrated example.
22.tq: Use category-based elimination among the three NeGP MMP groups.
xs: **e-Panchayat** is a **State** MMP — option **(2)**.
**UID** and **Pensions** are **Central** MMPs; **India Portal** is **Integrated**.
xa: Other State MMPs: **Land Records**, **Treasuries**, **e-District**, **CCTNS** (police).
e-Panchayat's **GS NIRNAY** app (**2023**) covers **Gram Sabha decisions**.
Central MMPs: **MCA21**, Passport, Income Tax.

22.s: Which of the following belongs to the Integrated category of NeGP MMPs?
22.x: e-Biz is an Integrated MMP. Posts is Central, while Treasuries and Land Records are State examples.
22.tq: Distinguish an integrated service from central and State departmental projects.
xs: **e-Biz** is an **Integrated** MMP — option **(2)**.
**Posts** is **Central**; **Treasuries** and **Land Records** are **State** MMPs.
xa: Other Integrated MMPs: **eCourts**, **e-Procurement**, **CSC**, **India Portal**.
**e-Procurement** uses online tenders to prevent collusion.
**eCourts** has been in place since **2007**.

22.s:
Consider the following pairs of NeGP components:
1. MSDG (2011) — Mobile services
2. Meghraj — GI Cloud
3. india.gov.in — State Wide Area Network
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
22.x: Pair 1 is correct: MSDG (2011) is for mobile services. Pair 2 is correct: Meghraj is the GI Cloud. Pair 3 is wrong: india.gov.in is the National Portal, a single window; SWAN links State HQ to block/taluka offices. So A misses pair 2, and C and D wrongly include pair 3.
22.tq: Megh = cloud; portal = single window; SWAN = network tier.
xs: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: **MSDG (2011)** = **mobile services**; **Meghraj** = **GI Cloud**.
Pair 3 is wrong: **india.gov.in** is the **National Portal** (single window), not SWAN — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **SWAN** links state HQ to block/taluka.
e-Kranti principles: **cloud by default**, **mobile first**.
NeGP approved **18 May 2006**.

22.s: The eCourts Mission Mode Project has been in place since which year?
22.x: The eCourts integrated Mission Mode Project has been in place since 2007.
22.tq: Use the numerical-year distinction among closely related MMP dates.
xs: The **eCourts** MMP has been in place since **2007** — option **(2)**.
**2009** is **CCTNS**'s start year; NeGP itself dates from **2006**.
xa: It offers **e-filing**, **online cause lists**, **case tracking** (APPSC **2023**).
eCourts is an **integrated** MMP.

22.s: Which of the following is NOT a function associated with the eCourts Mission Mode Project?
22.x: e-Filing, online cause lists and case tracking are associated with eCourts. Online company filing is the function of MCA21.
22.tq: Find the mismatched function by separating judicial services from corporate filing.
xs: **Online company filing** is not an eCourts function — option **(1)**; it belongs to **MCA21** (G2B).
eCourts provides **e-filing**, **online cause lists** and **case tracking**.
xa: eCourts has run since **2007**; **Phase III 2023-27**.
**MCA21** was among the **first NeGP MMPs**.

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the phases of the eCourts Mission Mode Project:
1. Phase I covered 2007–15.
2. Phase II covered 2015–23.
3. Phase III covers 2023–27.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: All three statements correctly state the periods of Phases I, II and III of eCourts.
22.tq: Check each date range independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All correct: eCourts **Phase I 2007-15**, **Phase II 2015-23**, **Phase III 2023-27** — option **(4)**.
The MMP has been in place since **2007**, so Phase I starts that year.
xa: eCourts is an **integrated** MMP offering e-filing, online cause lists, case tracking.
**CCTNS** (MHA) started in **2009**.
**IVFRT** extended to **March 2031** as **IVFRT 3.0**.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about CCTNS:
1. It is a Ministry of Home Affairs project.
2. It was started in 2009.
3. It links courts, tribunals and legal-aid centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: CCTNS is an MHA project started in 2009. Statement 3 is wrong: CCTNS links police stations, State headquarters and central police organisations; linking courts is the domain of eCourts. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: CCTNS = police network (MHA, 2009); eCourts = judiciary.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **CCTNS** is an **MHA** project started in **2009**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it links **police stations, state HQs and central police organisations**, not courts — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: CCTNS is listed as a **State** MMP (police).
⚠ CCTNS = MHA, **2009**; IVFRT = MHA, **2010**; eCourts = **2007**.

22.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. MCA21 is a Ministry of Corporate Affairs project for online company filing (G2B).
2. MCA21 was among the first NeGP Mission Mode Projects.
3. Passport Seva is a Central MMP under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: MCA21 is the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' online company filing (G2B) project. Statement 2 is correct: it was among the first NeGP MMPs. Statement 3 is wrong: Passport Seva is a Central MMP, but under the Ministry of External Affairs, not Home Affairs. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
22.tq: Passport = MEA; CCTNS and IVFRT = MHA.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **MCA21** = **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**, online company filing (**G2B**), among the **first NeGP MMPs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Passport Seva** is under the **Ministry of External Affairs**, not MHA — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Passport Seva is a **Central** MMP.
**MCA portal** and **GSTN** are **G2B** examples.

22.s: The e-Procurement Mission Mode Project seeks to prevent collusion primarily through which mechanism?
22.x: e-Procurement uses online tenders, which are intended to help prevent collusion.
22.tq: Link the stated governance objective with the specific digital mechanism.
xs: **e-Procurement** prevents collusion through **online tenders** — option **(2)**.
Company incorporation is **MCA21**; cause lists are **eCourts**.
xa: e-Procurement is an **Integrated** MMP.
It also sits in the **e-Governance** pillar alongside **e-Office** and **e-HRMS**.
Other Integrated MMPs: **eCourts**, **CSC**, **India Portal**, **e-Biz**.

22.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Passport Seva — Online court cause lists
22.x: e-District is a State MMP providing district-level certificates and services. The other pairs assign functions of different MMPs.
22.tq: Start with the direct service-function pair and eliminate swapped functions.
xs: **e-District** — **district-level certificates and services** is correct — option **(2)**; it is a **State** MMP.
**Passport Seva** issues passports (MEA), not cause lists; **CCTNS** is police networking; **MCA21** is online company filing.
xa: Online cause lists belong to **eCourts** (since **2007**).
**Land Records** is a separate **State** MMP.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about IVFRT:
1. It is a Ministry of Home Affairs project approved in 2010.
2. It is run by CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd with NIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: IVFRT is an MHA project approved in 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: IVFRT is run by the Bureau of Immigration with NIC; CSC e-Governance Services is the implementing agency of Common Service Centres. Hence only 1 is correct; B, C and D are wrong.
22.tq: Immigration project, so the Bureau of Immigration runs it (with NIC).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **IVFRT** is an **MHA** project approved in **2010**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is run by the **Bureau of Immigration** with **NIC**, not CSC SPV — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Extended to **March 2031** as **IVFRT 3.0** (LENS Apr **2026**).
⚠ CCTNS = MHA, **2009**; IVFRT = MHA, **2010**.
**CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd** is the SPV for CSCs.

22.s: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project provides which of the following?
22.x: The e-Panchayat MMP provides core panchayat software under the Panchayati Raj domain.
22.tq: Match the project with its sector-specific administrative function.
xs: The **e-Panchayat** MMP provides **core panchayat software** — option **(3)**, under **Panchayati Raj**.
Company filing is **MCA21**; passports are **Passport Seva**; police networking is **CCTNS**.
xa: Its **GS NIRNAY** app (**2023**) covers **Gram Sabha decisions**.
e-Panchayat is a **State** MMP.
**e-District**: district-level certificates and services.

22.s: The GS NIRNAY application, launched in 2023, is associated with which activity?
22.x: The GS NIRNAY app covers Gram Sabha decisions and is associated with the e-Panchayat initiative.
22.tq: Use the year-and-function combination to distinguish the application from other MMP tools.
xs: **GS NIRNAY** (**2023**) records **Gram Sabha decisions** — option **(4)**.
It belongs to the **e-Panchayat** MMP (Panchayati Raj), which provides **core panchayat software**.
xa: Corporate filing = **MCA21**; passports = **Passport Seva**; court cases = **eCourts**.
e-Panchayat is a **State** MMP.
e-Kranti expanded MMPs to **44**.

22.s: Which ministry coordinates the Digital India programme?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
22.x: The Digital India programme is coordinated by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, or MeitY.
22.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” test to identify the nodal ministry.
xs: **MeitY** (**Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology**) coordinates **Digital India** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025** key).
Central and State ministries are partners, but MeitY is the coordinator.
xa: Launched by PM **Narendra Modi** on **1 July 2015**.
It is an **umbrella programme** ("IT + IT = IT").
**NeGD** is MeitY's programme-management arm.

22.s:
With reference to implementation of Digital India, consider the following statements:
1. It is implemented by the whole government.
2. Public-private partnership is preferred wherever feasible.
3. Its implementation is confined to MeitY alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Digital India is implemented across the whole government, with PPP preferred wherever feasible. It is not confined to MeitY alone.
22.tq: Reject the absolute institutional claim that assigns a whole-of-government programme to one ministry.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Digital India involves **Central and State ministries as partners** under MeitY's coordination.
Statement 2 is correct: **PPP** is preferred **wherever feasible**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is not confined to MeitY — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Digital India is an **umbrella programme** ("IT + IT = IT").
Aim: **knowledge-based economy** + **digitally empowered society**.

22.s: The principal aim of Digital India is to transform India into a:
o: Digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
Centralised administrative state and industrial economy
Fully privatised economy and cashless market
22.x: Digital India aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
22.tq: Identify the precise paired formulation used for the programme’s overarching aim.
xs: Digital India aims at a **digitally empowered society** and a **knowledge-based economy** — option **(1)**.
It is an umbrella IT programme, not a manufacturing-only, centralised or fully privatised plan.
xa: Launched **1 July 2015**; completed **10 years** in **2025**.
Coordinator: **MeitY**.
Three vision areas: **digital infrastructure as a utility**, **governance and services on demand**, **digital empowerment of citizens**.

22.s: Universal digital literacy, documents on the cloud and services in Indian languages are associated with which vision area of Digital India?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
22.x: These measures are components of the vision area called digital empowerment of citizens.
22.tq: Match concrete features to the correct broad vision area.
xs: **Universal digital literacy**, **Indian-language services** and **entitlements on cloud** fall under **digital empowerment of citizens** — option **(3)**.
**Digital infrastructure** = high-speed internet, digital identity, cloud locker; **services on demand** = real-time services, cashless, GIS.
xa: **PMGDISHA** (**2017**): rural digital literacy, one person per household.
**Bhashini** AI language platform tackles the language divide.
Electronics manufacturing is a **pillar**, not a vision area.

22.s: Which one of the following is the fourth pillar of Digital India?
22.x: The fourth pillar is e-Governance: reforming government through technology.
22.tq: Use the numbered pillar sequence to distinguish adjacent pillars.
xs: The **4th** pillar is **e-Governance: reforming government through technology** — option **(1)**.
**Public Internet Access** is **3**, **e-Kranti** is **5**, **Information for All** is **6**.
xa: e-Governance pillar examples: **e-Office**, **e-HRMS**, **e-Procurement**.
Pillars **1** and **2**: **Broadband Highways** and **Universal Access to Mobile**.
Pillar **9**: **Early Harvest Programmes**.

22.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Digital India pillar)
A. Broadband Highways
B. Universal Access to Mobile/Phones
C. Public Internet Access Programme
D. Information for All

List-II (Pillar number)
1. 1
2. 2
3. 3
4. 6

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
22.x: Broadband Highways, Universal Access to Mobile/Phones, Public Internet Access Programme and Information for All are pillars 1, 2, 3 and 6 respectively.
22.tq: Start from the first three sequential pillars and verify the non-adjacent sixth pillar.
xs: **Broadband Highways = 1**, **Universal Access to Mobile = 2**, **Public Internet Access = 3**, **Information for All = 6** — option **(1)**: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.
Pillars **4** and **5** in between are **e-Governance** and **e-Kranti**.
xa: BharatNet: **2,18,347 GPs**, **6.92 lakh km** OFC (Mar **2025**).
**5.97 lakh CSCs** under Public Internet Access.
Information for All = **Open Government Data** platform.

22.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
22.x: Early Harvest Programmes is the ninth pillar, not the seventh. The seventh pillar is Electronics Manufacturing: target net zero imports.
22.tq: Check the pillar number against the official sequence.
xs: **Early Harvest Programmes — Seventh pillar** is wrong — option **(4)**: Early Harvest is pillar **9**; pillar **7** is **Electronics Manufacturing**.
**IT for Jobs** is pillar **8**, **e-Kranti** delivers services electronically, **Information for All** is pillar **6** — all correct.
xa: Early Harvest: quick wins like **biometric attendance**, **Wi-Fi in universities**.
Electronics output **Rs 2.13 lakh cr (2020-21) → Rs 5.25 lakh cr (2024-25)**.
e-Kranti has **44 MMPs**.

22.s: The target of “net zero imports” is associated with which Digital India pillar?
22.x: The seventh pillar, Electronics Manufacturing, carries the target of net zero imports.
22.tq: Match the distinctive policy target to its pillar.
xs: **Net zero imports** is the target of **Electronics Manufacturing** (pillar **7**) — option **(1)**.
Output rose from **Rs 2.13 lakh cr (2020-21)** to **Rs 5.25 lakh cr (2024-25)**.
xa: **IT for Jobs** (pillar **8**): skilling, **BPOs in small towns**.
**Broadband Highways** (pillar **1**): **BharatNet**.
Early Harvest (pillar **9**): biometric attendance, Wi-Fi in universities.

22.s: Which of the following is included among the sub-schemes of Digital India?
22.x: Electronic Governance, National Knowledge Network, Cyber Security and the IndiaAI Mission are included among the stated Digital India sub-schemes.
22.tq: Select the technology-oriented sub-scheme from nearby government programmes.
xs: **IndiaAI Mission** is a Digital India **sub-scheme** — option **(4)**.
Other sub-schemes: **e-Governance**, **NKN**, capacity building, electronics manufacturing and IT/ITeS promotion, **R&D**, **cyber security**.
xa: **NKN** = **National Knowledge Network**.
Digital India is an **umbrella programme** coordinated by **MeitY**.
It completed **10 years** in **2025**.

22.s: Digital India completed ten years in:
22.x: Digital India was launched in 2015 and completed ten years in 2025.
22.tq: Calculate the milestone year from the launch year and confirm the stated figure.
xs: Digital India completed **10 years** in **2025** — option **(3)**.
It was launched on **1 July 2015** by PM **Narendra Modi**.
xa: **UPI** is **10 years** old, with volume up **13,000-fold** (**25 Aug 2026**).
**Aadhaar** reaches **145 crore+** people.
DPI raised the digital economy to **12-14% of GDP**.

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its Digital India pillar?
o: Early Harvest Programmes — long-term university research grants
IT for Jobs — skilling for IT and ITeS jobs
Information for All — Open Government Data platform
22.x: Early Harvest Programmes comprise quick-win projects such as biometric attendance and Wi-Fi in universities; they are not defined as long-term university research grants.
22.tq: Reject the option that swaps a pillar’s quick-win function with an unrelated activity.
xs: **Early Harvest Programmes — long-term university research grants** is wrong — option **(1)**: Early Harvest means **quick-win projects** like **biometric attendance** and **Wi-Fi in universities**.
**IT for Jobs** = IT/ITeS skilling; **e-Governance** = e-Office, e-HRMS, e-Procurement; **Information for All** = Open Government Data — all correct.
xa: Early Harvest is pillar **9**.
IT for Jobs includes **BPOs in small towns**.
⚠ **Not part of Digital India**: issue of **digital currency** (APPSC **2024** key).

22.s: The e-Kranti pillar of Digital India is associated with which of the following?
o: Universal biometric registration of all citizens
Manufacture of electronic goods to achieve net zero imports only
Electronic delivery of services through 44 Mission Mode Projects
Construction of rural roads through 44 projects
22.x: e-Kranti focuses on electronic delivery of services and includes 44 Mission Mode Projects.
22.tq: Identify the function that naturally belongs to the e-Kranti pillar.
xs: **e-Kranti** (pillar **5**) means **electronic delivery of services** through **44 Mission Mode Projects** — option **(3)**.
Net zero imports is **Electronics Manufacturing**; rural roads are not part of Digital India.
xa: e-Kranti = **NeGP 2.0**, approved **2015**.
Vision: **"Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance"**.
Principles: **cloud by default**, **mobile first**, integrated not individual services.

22.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a Digital India vision area?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility — high-speed internet and cloud locker
Governance and services on demand — universal digital literacy only
Digital empowerment of citizens — GIS decision support only
Digital infrastructure as a core utility — cashless transactions only
22.x: High-speed internet, cradle-to-grave digital identity, Common Service Centre access and cloud locker are examples under digital infrastructure as a core utility.
22.tq: Match each example with the correct vision area rather than a neighbouring area.
xs: **Digital infrastructure as a utility** covers **high-speed internet** and **cloud locker** — option **(1)**.
**Digital literacy** belongs to **digital empowerment**; **GIS decision support** and **cashless transactions** belong to **governance and services on demand**, so (2)–(4) mismatch.
xa: Infrastructure area also includes **cradle-to-grave digital identity** and **CSC access**.
Services on demand: **real-time online services**.
**DigiLocker** is India's cloud document wallet.

22.s: The Digital India programme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on:
22.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 (APPSC 2025 key). 15 August 2014 and 25 September 2014 are associated with other announcements (Independence Day speech, Make in India), and 26 January 2016 is not its launch date.
22.tq: Digital India = 1 July 2015; 10 years in 2025.
xs: PM **Narendra Modi** launched **Digital India** on **1 July 2015** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2025** key).
It is an **umbrella programme** coordinated by **MeitY**, aiming at a **knowledge-based economy**.
xa: **e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)** was also approved in **2015**.
Chain: **NeGP 2006 → Digital India 2015 → e-Kranti 2015**.
It completed **10 years** in **2025**.

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the Digital India programme?
22.x: Broadband Highways (pillar 1), e-Kranti (pillar 5) and Information for All (pillar 6) are pillars of Digital India. Issue of digital currency is not part of Digital India (APPSC 2024 key).
22.tq: Digital currency is RBI's domain, not a Digital India pillar.
xs: **Issue of digital currency** is not part of Digital India — option **(3)** (APPSC **2024** key).
**Broadband Highways** (pillar **1**), **e-Kranti** (pillar **5**) and **Information for All** (pillar **6**) are pillars.
xa: Exam angle: "not a pillar" options are usually initiatives (**Aadhaar**, **DigiLocker**, **UPI**) or look-alike names.
Nine pillars end with **Early Harvest Programmes**.
Digital India is coordinated by **MeitY**.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about e-Kranti:
1. It is also known as NeGP 2.0.
2. It was approved in 2015 under Digital India.
3. It comprises 31 Mission Mode Projects.
4. Its vision is 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: e-Kranti is NeGP 2.0, approved in 2015 under Digital India, with the vision 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'. Statement 3 is wrong: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs; 31 is the expanded count of the original NeGP. So A is incomplete, and B and D include the wrong statement 3.
22.tq: NeGP: 27 → 31 MMPs; e-Kranti: 44 MMPs.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **e-Kranti** = **NeGP 2.0**, approved in **2015** under Digital India.
Statement 3 is wrong: it has **44 MMPs**; **31** was NeGP's expanded count.
Statement 4 is correct: vision **"Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance"** — so **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Principles: **transformation not translation**, **cloud by default**, **mobile first**, language localisation.
APPSC **2017**: mission for electronic delivery of all government services = **e-Kranti**.

22.s: e-Kranti constitutes which pillar of Digital India?
22.x: e-Kranti is the fifth pillar of Digital India and concerns electronic delivery of services.
22.tq: Use the pillar-number distinction rather than confusing the initiative with the whole programme.
xs: **e-Kranti** is **Pillar 5** of Digital India — option **(1)**: electronic delivery of services via **44 MMPs**.
Pillar **3** = Public Internet Access, pillar **7** = Electronics Manufacturing, pillar **9** = Early Harvest Programmes.
xa: e-Kranti = **NeGP 2.0**, approved **2015**.
Vision: **"Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance"**.
⚠ **27 MMPs** at NeGP approval → **31** → **44** under e-Kranti.

22.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of e-Kranti?
22.x: The principles include transformation not translation, integrated not individual services, and cloud by default. Paper-first delivery is not an e-Kranti principle.
22.tq: Locate the one option that reverses the digital-first orientation.
xs: **Paper-first delivery** is not an e-Kranti principle — option **(3)**.
Real principles: **transformation not translation**, **integrated not individual services**, **cloud by default**, **mobile first**.
xa: Also: **language localisation** and **process re-engineering in every MMP**.
e-Kranti = **NeGP 2.0**, pillar **5** of Digital India.
APPSC **2017**: mission for electronic delivery of all government services = **e-Kranti**.

22.s:
Which one of the following combinations contains only principles of e-Kranti?
1. Mobile first
2. Language localisation
3. Process re-engineering in every MMP
4. Cloud by default
22.x: Mobile first, language localisation, process re-engineering in every MMP and cloud by default are all stated principles of e-Kranti.
22.tq: Check whether every listed principle belongs to the same framework before selecting the all-inclusive code.
xs: All four — **mobile first**, **language localisation**, **process re-engineering in every MMP**, **cloud by default** — are e-Kranti principles, so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
The list also includes **transformation not translation** and **integrated not individual services**.
xa: e-Kranti = **NeGP 2.0**, approved **2015**, with **44 MMPs**.
Vision: **"Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance"**.
Gartner's last phase is also **Transformation**.

22.s:
Consider the following pairs of initiatives and launch years:
1. MyGov — July 2014
2. UPI and BHIM — 2016
3. UMANG — 2017
4. ONDC — 2020
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
22.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: MyGov came in July 2014, UPI and BHIM in 2016, UMANG in 2017. Pair 4 is wrong: ONDC came in 2022; 2020 was PM eVIDYA. So A is incomplete, and C and D include the wrong pair 4.
22.tq: Ladder: Aadhaar 09, MyGov 14, DigiLocker 15, UPI 16, UMANG 17, eVIDYA 20, ONDC 22.
xs: Pairs 1–3 are correct: **MyGov — Jul 2014**, **UPI and BHIM — 2016**, **UMANG — 2017**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **ONDC** came in **2022**; **2020** was **PM eVIDYA** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Aadhaar (UIDAI)**: **2009**; first numbers Sep **2010**.
**DigiLocker**: Feb **2015**; **Bhashini** also **2022**.
Chronology **Aadhaar → MyGov → PM eVIDYA → ONDC** (APPSC **2024** key).

22.s: DigiLocker was launched in which year?
22.x: DigiLocker was launched in February 2015.
22.tq: Recall the year while avoiding confusion with adjacent digital initiatives.
xs: **DigiLocker** was launched in **Feb 2015** — option **(2)**.
xa: DigiLocker: **10 MB**, extendable to **1 GB**; **CBSE marksheets** from **2015**.
**56.06 crore users**, **970.70 crore documents**.
**BharatNet** (renamed from **NOFN**) also dates from **2015**.

22.s: PM eVIDYA was launched in 2020 primarily in the context of:
22.x: PM eVIDYA was launched in 2020 in response to the educational requirements arising during the pandemic.
22.tq: Link the initiative to its immediate context rather than its technology alone.
xs: **PM eVIDYA** (**2020**) was launched for the **pandemic** — option **(1)**.
**Aadhaar/UIDAI** dates from **2009**, and BharatNet was renamed from NOFN in **2015** — unrelated.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy on Information Technology (NPIT), 2012:
1. It treats ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion.
2. Its objectives include using ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion and governance, with e-literacy for all.
3. It sought to concentrate IT activity further in the six established hubs.

23.x: Statement 1 is correct: NPIT 2012 treats ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion. Statement 2 is correct: its objectives cover ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion, governance and e-literacy for all. Statement 3 is wrong: the six hubs held ~90% of the industry and were near saturation, so NPIT pushed IT into Tier II and Tier III cities. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.

xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **NPIT 2012** treats **ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion**, with ICT in **education, health, skills, financial inclusion, governance** and **e-literacy for all**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the six hubs were **near saturation**, so NPIT pushed IT into **Tier II and Tier III cities** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Six hubs (Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, NCR) held ~**90%** of the industry.
Target: IT-ITES revenue **$100 bn → $300 bn** by **2020**.
Twin goals: ICT **within reach of the whole of India**; India as **Global Hub for IT and ITES by 2020**.

23.s:

2. Making India a Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020

xs: Statements 1 and 2 are NPIT's **twin goals**: full power of ICT **within reach of the whole of India**, and India as **Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020**.
Statement 3 is wrong: NPIT wanted to move IT **beyond** the saturated hubs into **Tier II and Tier III** cities — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Indian IT in **2011-12** = **USD 100 billion** industry, **80%** from exports.
IT exports target: **$69 bn → $200 bn**.
e-literacy target: at least **one e-literate person in every household**.
