23.s: The target for IT-ITES revenue under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was to increase it from US$100 billion in 2012 to:
23.x: The policy target was to raise IT-ITES revenue from US$100 billion in 2012 to US$300 billion by 2020.
23.tq: Match the target year and target value, avoiding confusion with export and electronics figures.
xs: NPIT 2012 targeted IT-ITES revenue rising from **$100 bn (2012)** to **$300 bn by 2020** — option **(1)**.
**$200 bn** was the **IT exports** target; **US$ 400 bn by 2025** was **NPE 2019**'s electronics target; **$190 bn** was NPE's mobile manufacturing value.
In words: **US$300 billion by 2020**, up from **US$100 billion**.
xa: Exam angle: **"$300 bn by 2020"** is the most-asked figure.
⚠ NPIT targets are **by 2020**; NPE 2019 targets are **by 2025**.
Skilled manpower target: **10 million** additional ICT workers.

23.s: The target for IT exports under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was:
o: An increase from US$100 billion to US$300 billion
An increase from US$190 billion to US$110 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$200 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$400 billion
23.x: The IT export target was to increase exports from US$69 billion to US$200 billion by 2020.
23.tq: Distinguish the export baseline and target from the separate IT-ITES revenue figures.
xs: The IT exports target was **$69 bn → $200 bn** — option **(3)**.
**$100 bn → $300 bn** was **IT-ITES revenue**; **US$ 400 bn** is **NPE 2019** electronics; **190/110** are NPE's mobile figures.
In words: an **increase from US$69 billion to US$200 billion** by **2020**.
xa: Both NPIT targets were **by 2020**.
Then, **80%** of IT revenue came from exports.
e-literacy: **one e-literate person in every household**.

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the targets of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012.

List-I (Target)
a. IT-ITES revenue
b. IT exports
c. Skilled manpower
d. E-literacy

List-II (Target by 2020)
i. At least one e-literate person in every household
ii. US$200 billion
iii. 10 million additional skilled ICT workers
iv. US$300 billion

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: IT-ITES revenue was targeted at US$300 billion; IT exports at US$200 billion; skilled manpower at 10 million additional workers; and e-literacy at one e-literate person in every household.
23.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched categories.
xs: **IT-ITES revenue → $300 bn**, **IT exports → $200 bn**, **skilled manpower → 10 million**, **e-literacy → one e-literate person per household** — **a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i**, option **(2)**.
All are NPIT 2012 targets **by 2020**.
xa: Revenue base: **$100 bn (2012)**; exports base: **$69 bn**.
Exam angle: match target figure to category; **$300 bn** is the most-asked.
⚠ NPE 2019 targets (**US$ 400 bn**) are **by 2025**.

23.s: India is regarded as one of the world's largest exporters of IT services. Which one of the following groups consists of Indian IT-service companies associated with this position?
23.x: TCS, Infosys and Wipro are identified as major Indian IT-service companies contributing to India's position as one of the world's largest IT-service exporters.
23.tq: Use the direct company-identification approach and distinguish service exporters from institutions and locations.
xs: **TCS, Infosys and Wipro** are the IT-service exporters cited — option **(2)**.
**Anakapalli** is a place, **NIELIT/C-DAC/MeitY** are government bodies and **NASSCOM** is an industry association.
xa: IT + e-commerce employed **14.67 million** (**2022-23**).
**Infosys** campus at **Visakhapatnam** (~**7,000** jobs).
Digital economy: **12-14% of GDP**, projected **20% by 2029-30**.

23.s: How many persons were employed by the IT and e-commerce sectors in 2022–23?
23.x: The IT and e-commerce sectors employed 14.67 million persons in 2022–23.
23.tq: Identify the exact employment figure and reject nearby numerical distractors.
xs: IT + e-commerce employed **14.67 million** in **2022-23** — option **(3)**.
The other figures are look-alike numbers not given in the notes.
xa: Digital economy: **12-14% of GDP**; projected **20%** by **2029-30**.
Electronics production: **₹13.11 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.
NPIT targeted **10 million** additional skilled ICT workers.

23.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Global Capability Centres (GCCs):
1. They are offshore units operated by multinational corporations for their own functions.
2. Their activities may include engineering, research and development, and analytics.
3. They are the same as outsourcing vendors providing services to unrelated companies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. GCCs perform functions for their parent multinational corporations, whereas outsourcing vendors provide services to other organisations; therefore, statement 3 is false.
23.tq: Test the confusable distinction between captive multinational units and outsourcing vendors.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **GCCs** are **offshore units run by multinationals** for their **own engineering, R&D, analytics**.
Statement 3 is wrong: GCCs are **not outsourcing vendors** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: AP's **IT & GCC Policy (4.0) 2024-29** aims to make AP an IT and GCC powerhouse.
India is among the world's largest IT-service exporters (**TCS, Infosys, Wipro**).
IT + e-commerce employed **14.67 million**.

23.s: India's digital economy, currently about 12-14% of GDP, is projected to reach what share of GDP by 2029-30?
23.x: The digital economy is about 12-14% of GDP now and is projected to reach about 20% by 2029-30. 8% is below the current share, 14% is the current upper bound, and 35% overstates the projection.
23.tq: Digital economy: 12-14% now → 20% by 2029-30.
xs: The digital economy (**12-14% of GDP**) is projected to reach **20% by 2029-30** — option **(3)**.
About **14%** is today's upper figure, not the projection.
xa: IT + e-commerce employed **14.67 million** (**2022-23**).
Electronics = India's **3rd-largest export** item.
Offline population still ~**38%** (Feb **2026**).

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Policy on Electronics (NPE), 2019:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 20 February 2019.
2. It is a policy of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. It replaced the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NPE 2019 is a MeitY policy approved by the Cabinet on 20 February 2019. Statement 3 is wrong: NPE 2019 replaced NPE 2012, not NPIT 2012. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: NPE 2019 replaced NPE 2012 (same series); NPIT 2012 is a separate IT policy.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **NPE 2019** was approved by the **Union Cabinet** on **20 Feb 2019** and is a **MeitY** policy.
Statement 3 is wrong: it replaced **NPE 2012**, not NPIT 2012 — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: NPE 2019 aims at a global hub for **ESDM**, including chipsets.
Target: **US$ 400 bn** electronics manufacturing **by 2025**.
Schemes under NPE (**2020**): **PLI** and **SPECS**.

23.s: The principal aim of the National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was to make India a global hub for:
o: Only software exports without hardware production
23.x: NPE 2019 aimed to establish India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing, including chipsets.
23.tq: Choose the precise official scope rather than a software-only interpretation.
xs: **NPE 2019** aimed to make India a global hub for **ESDM** (Electronics System Design and Manufacturing), **including chipsets** — option **(1)**.
It is a hardware-manufacturing policy, so software-only or app-only options are wrong.
xa: Target: **US$ 400 bn** (~₹**26 lakh crore**) by **2025**.
**1 billion** handsets a year, **600 million** for export.
Replaced **NPE 2012**.

23.s:
Consider the following NPE 2019 targets for 2025:
1. Electronics manufacturing of US$400 billion
2. 1 billion mobile handsets a year, of which 600 million for export
3. Mobile exports of US$190 billion
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statement 1 is correct: US$400 billion (~₹26 lakh crore) electronics manufacturing. Statement 2 is correct: 1 billion handsets a year, 600 million for export. Statement 3 is wrong: US$190 billion is the mobile manufacturing value; mobile exports target is US$110 billion. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: Mobiles: make 190, export 110 (US$ bn).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **US$ 400 bn** electronics manufacturing, and **1 billion** handsets a year with **600 million** for export.
Statement 3 is wrong: **US$ 190 bn** is **mobile manufacturing value**; mobile **exports** are **US$ 110 bn** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: All NPE 2019 targets are **by 2025**.
⚠ NPIT 2012 targets were **by 2020** (**$300 bn**).
NPE aims at an **ESDM** hub.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS):
1. It has an outlay of ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2030-31.
2. It replaces the PLI scheme for Large Scale Electronics.
3. It targets ₹39 lakh crore exports and ₹15 lakh crore production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: MPMS has ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2030-31 and replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics). Statement 3 is wrong: the figures are reversed; targets are ₹39 lakh crore production and ₹15 lakh crore exports. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: Production is always the larger figure than exports.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **MPMS** has **₹62,500 crore** for **FY 2026-27 to 2030-31** and **replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it reverses the figures — **₹39 lakh crore production**, **₹15 lakh crore exports** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Announced **24 Aug 2026**.
**Semicon 2.0** and **MPMS** replace the NPE-era schemes.
Electronics production: **₹13.11 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.

23.s: Electronics production in India is stated to have reached what value in 2025–26?
23.x: Electronics production reached ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26, described as sevenfold growth under PLI.
23.tq: Distinguish the achieved production figure from future scheme targets and policy estimates.
xs: Electronics production reached **₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025-26** — option **(3)**, **sevenfold under PLI**.
**₹39 lakh crore** and **₹15 lakh crore** are MPMS targets; **₹26 lakh crore** is NPE's US$ 400 bn target.
xa: Electronics = India's **3rd-largest export** item.
Reported on **15 Aug 2026**.
**MPMS** outlay: **₹62,500 crore**.

23.s: Electronics is stated to be India’s:
23.x: Electronics is stated to be India’s third-largest export item.
23.tq: Recall the ranking exactly and avoid upgrading a sector’s position to first or second.
xs: Electronics is India's **3rd-largest export** item — option **(1)**.
Production reached **₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025-26**, sevenfold under **PLI**.
xa: NPE 2019 export target: **600 million** handsets a year.
**MPMS** targets **₹15 lakh crore** exports.
India is one of the largest **IT-service** exporters.

23.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Scheme — Description
1. PLI — Large-scale electronics manufacturing
2. SPECS — Promotion of manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors
3. EMC 2.0 — Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters
4. MPMS — National e-Governance Plan Mission Mode Projects
23.x: MPMS is the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme; it is not a scheme for NeGP Mission Mode Projects. The first three pairs are correctly matched with NPE-related schemes.
23.tq: Find the single swapped programme description in a list of familiar schemes.
xs: **MPMS — NeGP Mission Mode Projects** is wrong — **4 only**, option **(1)**: MPMS is the **Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme** (**₹62,500 crore**).
**PLI** = large-scale electronics manufacturing and **SPECS** = components and semiconductors — both correct.
xa: PLI and SPECS were schemes **under NPE (2020)**.
MPMS **replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics)**.
**44** MMPs run under **e-Kranti**.

23.s: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) was launched in December 2021 under the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
23.x: ISM was launched in December 2021 under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
23.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to identify the responsible ministry.
xs: The **India Semiconductor Mission** was launched in **Dec 2021** under **MeitY** — option **(4)**.
MeitY also coordinates Digital India and cyber-security policy.
MeitY = **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology**, which also frames IT and cyber-security policy.
xa: **Semicon 2.0** (Sep **2026**) pillars: Fabs, Packaging, R&D, Talent, Design, Machines/Materials.
**C2S** (**2022**) builds chip-design talent.
**RRP Electronics** semiconductor + OSAT unit in **Sri Sathya Sai district, AP**.

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the pillars of Semicon 2.0 and their support.

List-I (Pillar)
a. CMOS silicon fabs
b. Compound and display fabs
c. Advanced packaging
d. R&D

List-II (Maximum support)
i. 75% of project cost
ii. 35% capital subsidy
iii. 40% capital subsidy
iv. 35% support

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: CMOS silicon fabs receive up to 40% capital subsidy, compound and display fabs 35%, advanced packaging 35%, and R&D up to 75% of project cost.
23.tq: Start with the distinctive 75% R&D pair and then match the two fab subsidy rates.
xs: **CMOS silicon fabs → 40%**, **compound/display fabs → 35%**, **advanced packaging → 35%**, **R&D → 75%** of project cost — **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i**, option **(1)**.
⚠ Compound/display fabs and advanced packaging both get **35%**, but fabs as a **capital subsidy**.
xa: Conventional packaging gets **25%**.
**Talent** pillar: **1,00,000** more engineers and technicians.
Other two pillars: **Design** and **Machines/Materials**.

23.s: Besides Fabs, Packaging and R&D, which of the following are the other two pillars of Semicon 2.0?
23.x: Design and Machines/Materials are the other two pillars in addition to Fabs, Packaging and R&D.
23.tq: Identify the remaining members of a classified list after excluding the familiar pillars.
xs: The other two Semicon 2.0 pillars are **Design** and **Machines/Materials** — option **(4)**.
**Talent** is already a listed pillar alongside **Fabs**, **Packaging**, **R&D**.
xa: Fabs: up to **40%** capital subsidy (CMOS); packaging up to **35%**.
R&D: up to **75%** of project cost.
Talent: **1,00,000** more engineers and technicians.

23.s: RRP Electronics is associated with which of the following semiconductor facilities and locations?
o: Semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district, Andhra Pradesh
First commercial fab at Dholera, Gujarat
23.x: RRP Electronics is associated with a semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh.
23.tq: Discriminate the newer Andhra Pradesh entry from the Gujarat and Assam facilities.
xs: **RRP Electronics** = **semiconductor + OSAT** unit in **Sri Sathya Sai district, AP** — option **(3)** (**11 Apr 2026**).
**Sanand (Gujarat)** ATMP is **Micron**'s; **Jagiroad (Assam)** OSAT is **Tata (TSAT)**'s.
xa: ⚠ **Micron** = Sanand; **Tata** = Jagiroad; **RRP** = Sri Sathya Sai.
Packaging (OSAT/ATMP) support: up to **35%** (advanced).
AP IT/electronics drew **₹18,210 crore+** in one Cabinet round.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chips to Start-up (C2S) programme:
1. It was launched in 2022 to build chip-design talent.
2. It targets 85,000 B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD students over five years.
3. It is implemented by NIELIT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: C2S (2022) builds chip-design talent, targeting 85,000 B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD students over five years. Statement 3 is wrong: C2S is implemented by C-DAC, not NIELIT. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: C2S → C-DAC (both start with C).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **C2S** (**2022**) builds **chip-design talent**, targeting **85,000** B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD over **5 years**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is implemented by **C-DAC**, not NIELIT — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **NIELIT** is a **Deemed-to-be University under MeitY** for IT/electronics training.
C-DAC also built **PARAM** and has a centre at **Amaravati Quantum Valley**.
Semicon 2.0 talent pillar: **1,00,000** engineers and technicians.

23.s: Which of the following semiconductor units is correctly matched with its company and location?
23.x: Tata's (TSAT) OSAT unit is at Jagiroad, Assam. The ATMP unit at Sanand, Gujarat belongs to Micron, not Tata (A), Micron is not at Jagiroad (B), and RRP Electronics is in Sri Sathya Sai district, AP (D).
23.tq: Micron–Sanand (ATMP); Tata–Jagiroad (OSAT); RRP–Sri Sathya Sai (AP).
xs: **OSAT — Tata (TSAT) — Jagiroad, Assam** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Sanand** belongs to **Micron**'s **ATMP**, not Tata; **RRP Electronics** is in **Sri Sathya Sai district, AP**, not Jagiroad.
xa: ⚠ Micron = **Sanand, Gujarat**.
Packaging support: **35%** advanced, **25%** conventional.
ISM launched **Dec 2021** under **MeitY**.

23.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding IT institutions and their roles.

List-I (Institution)
a. MeitY
b. NASSCOM
c. STPI
d. NIC

List-II (Role)
i. Government IT/e-governance network and services
ii. Industry association of IT-BPM firms and partner in IoT CoEs
iii. Policy on IT, electronics, internet and cyber security; coordinates Digital India
iv. Export-oriented IT parks under MeitY and CoEs

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
23.x: MeitY handles policy and Digital India coordination; NASSCOM represents IT-BPM firms and partners in IoT CoEs; STPI runs export-oriented parks and CoEs; NIC provides government IT and e-governance services.
23.tq: Start with the distinctive NIC network role and eliminate codes with swapped institutional functions.
xs: **MeitY → IT/electronics/internet and cyber-security policy, coordinates Digital India**; **NASSCOM → IT-BPM industry association, IoT CoE partner**; **STPI → export-oriented IT parks**; **NIC → government IT network** — **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i**, option **(1)**.
**STPI** = Software Technology Parks of India, under **MeitY**; **NIC** handles government IT/e-governance services.
xa: **C-DAC**: PARAM supercomputers; implements **C2S**.
**NIELIT**: Deemed-to-be University under MeitY.
MeitY-NASSCOM **IoT CoE** is at **Visakhapatnam**.

23.s: Which of the following is a stated role of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)?
o: Licensing all Internet Service Providers exclusively
Formulating policy on IT, electronics, internet except ISP licensing, and cyber security
23.x: MeitY handles policy on IT, electronics, the internet other than ISP licensing, and cyber security, and coordinates Digital India.
23.tq: Watch the explicit exception concerning ISP licensing while identifying the ministry’s policy role.
xs: **MeitY** frames policy on **IT, electronics, internet (other than ISP licensing) and cyber security** — option **(4)**.
ISP licensing is excluded, so (3) is wrong; **PARAM** is built by **C-DAC**; **STPI** runs export-oriented IT parks.
xa: MeitY coordinates **Digital India**.
ISM (**Dec 2021**) and **NPE 2019** are MeitY initiatives.
**NIELIT** is a Deemed-to-be University under MeitY.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about C-DAC:
1. It has an R&D role involving PARAM supercomputers.
2. It implements the Chips to Start-up programme.
3. It has a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: C-DAC’s stated roles include R&D involving PARAM supercomputers, implementation of C2S and a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
23.tq: Combine the institution’s historical R&D role with its current programme and location associations.
xs: All correct: **C-DAC** does R&D on **PARAM supercomputers**, **implements C2S**, and has a centre at **Amaravati Quantum Valley** — option **(4)**.
Founded at **Pune** to build **PARAM**, C-DAC now also runs the **C2S** chip-design programme.
xa: C-DAC was set up at **Pune** in **1988**.
C2S targets **85,000** students over **5 years**.
AP Data Centre Policy adds up to **1 GW**.

23.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with NIELIT?
o: Government e-governance network; national IT services
Industry association of IT-BPM firms; IoT CoEs
Deemed-to-be University under MeitY; IT and electronics training
Export-oriented IT parks; software export promotion
23.x: NIELIT is described as a deemed-to-be University under MeitY and is associated with IT and electronics training.
23.tq: Use the institutional status and training role together to distinguish NIELIT from allied bodies.
xs: **NIELIT** = **Deemed-to-be University under MeitY**; **IT/electronics training** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) is **NIC**, (2) is **NASSCOM**, (4) is **STPI**.
xa: **C-DAC** implements **C2S**.
**MeitY** coordinates Digital India.
STPI also **runs CoEs**.

23.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP IT & Global Capability Centers (GCC) Policy (4.0):
1. It covers the period 2024-29.
2. It came into force on 12 December 2024 for five years.
3. Its aim is to make Andhra Pradesh mainly a semiconductor manufacturing state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the policy covers 2024-29 and came into force on 12 December 2024 for five years. Statement 3 is wrong: its aim is to make AP a global knowledge economy hub and an IT and GCC powerhouse. So A misses statement 2, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
23.tq: AP IT & GCC 4.0: 2024-29, from 12 Dec 2024, knowledge-economy hub.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **AP IT & GCC Policy (4.0)** covers **2024-29** and came into force on **12 Dec 2024** for **five years**.
Statement 3 is wrong: its aim is a **global knowledge economy hub** / **IT and GCC powerhouse** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Workspaces: **IT parks**, **co-working**, **neighbourhood workspaces**.
**AP Data Centre Policy**: up to **1 GW** capacity.
**GCCs** are offshore units of multinationals.

23.s: Which combination correctly identifies the workspaces promoted under the AP IT & Global Capability Centers (GCC) Policy 4.0?
o: IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces
Only large industrial estates and export-processing zones
Data centres, semiconductor fabs and university laboratories only
Quantum campuses, cable landing stations and NIELIT centres
23.x: The policy promotes IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces.
23.tq: Match the policy feature with its complete list rather than with associated infrastructure projects.
xs: Policy 4.0 promotes **IT parks, co-working and neighbourhood workspaces** — option **(1)**.
Data centres fall under the separate **AP Data Centre Policy**; **cable landing station** and **Quantum Valley** are city projects.
xa: Policy in force **12 Dec 2024**, five years (**2024-29**).
Aim: AP as a **global knowledge economy hub**.
**Infosys** campus at Visakhapatnam (~**7,000** jobs).

23.s: The Andhra Pradesh Data Centre Policy provides for adding data-centre capacity of up to:
23.x: The AP Data Centre Policy provides for adding up to 1 GW of data-centre capacity.
23.tq: Convert the stated capacity into the exact quantitative answer and watch the MW–GW scale distinction.
xs: The **AP Data Centre Policy** adds up to **1 GW** of data-centre capacity — option **(1)**.
The other values (**5 GW**, **100 MW**, **500 MW**) are not in the policy.
xa: **Visakhapatnam** hosts **AI data projects** (with Anakapalli) and a **cable landing station**.
**AP IT & GCC Policy (4.0) 2024-29** runs alongside it.
**Amaravati** hosts the **Quantum Valley** (C-DAC).

23.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with Visakhapatnam's information-technology initiatives?
o: Quantum Valley, NIELIT Quantum campus and Acharya Nagarjuna University classes
AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station, and an Infosys campus
NIELIT centre at Sri Venkateswara University and a 1 GW data-centre addition
Only a semiconductor research facility and a neighbourhood workspace
23.x: Visakhapatnam is associated with AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station and an Infosys campus expected to create about 7,000 jobs.
23.tq: Use location-based matching to separate Visakhapatnam initiatives from Tirupati and Amaravati projects.
xs: **Visakhapatnam**: **AI data projects (with Anakapalli)**, a **cable landing station** and an **Infosys campus** — option **(2)**.
**Quantum Valley** is at **Amaravati**, not Visakhapatnam, so option (1) fails.
xa: Infosys campus: ~**7,000** jobs.
MeitY-NASSCOM **IoT CoE** is also at Visakhapatnam.
AP Data Centre Policy: up to **1 GW**.

23.s: The MeitY–NASSCOM IoT Centre of Excellence is associated with which city in Andhra Pradesh?
23.x: The MeitY–NASSCOM IoT Centre of Excellence is listed among the technology initiatives associated with Visakhapatnam.
23.tq: Identify the correct location by separating city-level projects from nearby district-level initiatives.
xs: The **MeitY-NASSCOM IoT CoE** is at **Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)**.
**Amaravati** hosts the **Quantum Valley**; **Anakapalli** pairs with Vizag in AI data projects.
xa: **NASSCOM** = industry association of IT-BPM firms, partner in **IoT CoEs**.
Vizag also has a **cable landing station** and an **Infosys** campus.
**STPI** runs CoEs too.

23.s: The 'Quantum Valley' in Andhra Pradesh, with a C-DAC centre, is being developed at:
23.x: Quantum Valley is at Amaravati, with a C-DAC centre. Visakhapatnam hosts the cable landing station, Infosys campus and IoT CoE; Anakapalli is linked with AI data projects; Tirupati is not named for it.
23.tq: Quantum = Amaravati; IoT CoE & cable landing = Vizag.
xs: **Quantum Valley** (with a **C-DAC** centre) is at **Amaravati** — option **(2)**.
**Visakhapatnam** has the IoT CoE, cable landing station and Infosys campus; **Anakapalli** has AI data projects.
xa: **C-DAC**: PARAM supercomputers, implements **C2S**.
AP Data Centre Policy: up to **1 GW**.
AP IT/electronics drew **₹18,210 crore+** in one Cabinet round.

23.s: Which of the following correctly describes the policy developments identified as replacing the NPE-era schemes?
23.x: Semicon 2.0 (September 2026) and the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, MPMS (August 2026), replace the NPE-era schemes; MPMS replaces the PLI scheme for Large Scale Electronics. GCC 4.0, Quantum Valley, IoT CoE, Digital India and SWAYAM are not replacements for NPE schemes.
23.tq: Discriminate between current policy labels and project or institution names.
xs: **Semicon 2.0** (Sep **2026**) and **MPMS** (Aug **2026**) replace the NPE-era schemes — option **(4)**.
MPMS **replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics)**.
xa: NPE-era schemes (**2020**): **PLI** and **SPECS**.
MPMS outlay: **₹62,500 crore**.
Semicon 2.0 fabs: up to **40%** subsidy.

23.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the criticism and continuing challenges associated with information-technology development:
1. Hub concentration and saturation were issues that NPIT sought to address.
2. Approximately 38% of the population remains offline.
3. These issues indicate that digital access has become universal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
23.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the continuing offline population shows that digital access is not yet universal.
23.tq: Find the false inference created by an extreme conclusion such as universal access.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: **hub concentration and saturation** were what NPIT set out to fix, and ~**38%** remain **offline** (Feb **2026**).
Statement 3 is wrong: a **38%** offline population shows digital access is **not universal** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Six hubs had ~**90%** of the industry in **2011-12**.
NPIT pushed IT into **Tier II and Tier III cities**.

23.s: In one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round, the IT and electronics sectors attracted investment of more than:
23.x: IT and electronics attracted more than ₹18,210 crore in one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round.
23.tq: Identify the exact investment magnitude and reject altered leading digits.
xs: AP's IT and electronics drew **₹18,210 crore+** in one **AP Cabinet** round (Apr **2026**) — option **(2)**.
The other amounts are look-alike figures with digits shuffled.
xa: **RRP Electronics** semiconductor + OSAT unit in **Sri Sathya Sai district**.
**AP IT & GCC Policy (4.0) 2024-29**.
**Infosys** Visakhapatnam campus: ~**7,000** jobs.

24.s: Which of the following correctly represents the four phases of the Gartner model?
24.x: The four Gartner phases are Information, Interaction, Transaction and Transformation, in that order.
24.tq: Recall the exact ordered framework rather than merely identifying its individual terms.
xs: The **Gartner four-phase model** runs **Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation** — option **(1)**.
The other options shuffle or reverse this order.
xa: G2E example: **CEMS** (employee management); G2P example: **DBT** (LPG subsidy, pensions).
m-Governance: **mPassport Seva**, **UMANG**; framework **2012**, **MSDG 2011**.
Open Government Data: **data.gov.in**.

24.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Open Government Data — DBT for LPG subsidy
24.x: G2E is illustrated by CEMS, an employee-management system. G2P is illustrated by DBT, Open Government Data by data.gov.in, and m-Governance by services such as mPassport Seva and UMANG.
24.tq: Match each governance relationship with its specific example.
xs: **G2E — CEMS** (employee management) is correct — option **(1)**.
**data.gov.in** is **Open Government Data**, not G2P; **DBT** is **G2P**, not open data; m-Governance means **mPassport Seva, UMANG**, not the SDC.
xa: G2C / G2B / G2G services run via **SDC + SWAN + CSC**.
m-Governance framework **2012**; **MSDG 2011**.
Gartner phases: **Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation**.

24.s: Which of the following is an example of G2P (Government-to-Person) service?
o: DBT for LPG subsidy and pensions
24.x: Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG subsidies and pensions is an example of G2P service delivery.
24.tq: Infer the relationship from the recipient of the service or benefit.
xs: **G2P** example: **DBT for LPG subsidy and pensions** — option **(1)**.
**mPassport Seva** is **m-Governance**, **data.gov.in** is **Open Government Data**, **CEMS** is **G2E**.
xa: **Jeevan Pramaan** gives pensioners an Aadhaar-based **Digital Life Certificate**.
**UMANG** is the one-app m-Governance platform.
G2C/G2B/G2G services run via **SDC + SWAN + CSC**.

24.s: Which one of the following is associated with m-Governance?
o: Data Lake and Data Lens only
24.x: mPassport Seva and UMANG are examples of m-Governance. The m-Governance framework dates to 2012, while MSDG dates to 2011.
24.tq: Identify the mobile-governance examples and distinguish them from infrastructure platforms.
xs: **m-Governance** examples: **mPassport Seva and UMANG** — option **(3)**.
**Data Lake/Data Lens** are AP's **RTGS** tools; **SWAN/SDC** are core infrastructure; **CEMS** is G2E and **CPGRAMS** a grievance portal.
xa: m-Governance framework: **2012**; **MSDG**: **2011**.
**UMANG**: **8.68 crore users**, **2,339 services** from **240** departments.
**Mana Mitra** (AP) delivers governance over **WhatsApp**.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three vision areas of Digital India mentioned below?
o: Digital infrastructure as a core utility
24.x: The three listed Digital India vision areas are digital infrastructure as a core utility, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.
24.tq: Reject an extreme policy claim that is outside the stated vision areas.
xs: **Universal privatisation of public services** is not a Digital India vision area — option **(1)**.
The three areas are **digital infrastructure as a core utility**, **governance and services on demand**, **digital empowerment of citizens**.
xa: Digital India completed **11 years** (current relevance).
**e-Kranti** is an essential pillar of Digital India with **44 MMPs**.
Role of technology: **enhance citizen engagement** and **improve service delivery** (APPSC **2025**).

24.s: Which of the following best expresses the role of ICT in e-governance?
o: It prevents real-time monitoring of public services.
It enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery.
It replaces all government institutions with private agencies.
It limits citizen participation to physical offices.
24.x: ICT enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery, including through transparency and real-time monitoring.
24.tq: Choose the option that states the positive functional role rather than an absolute consequence.
xs: ICT **enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2025**).
It also brings **transparency** and **real-time monitoring**, so option (1) is the opposite.
xa: ⚠ **Internet shutdowns** disrupt e-services (UPSC).
Gartner model ends in **Transformation**.
First integrated citizen service centres: **e-Seva (2001)**, AP.

24.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was formulated by which of the following combination of organisations?
24.x: The National e-Governance Plan was formulated by DeitY, now MeitY, in association with DARPG.
24.tq: Identify the agencies directly associated with formulation rather than implementation.
xs: **NeGP** was formulated by **DeitY and DARPG** — option **(4)**.
It was approved on **18 May 2006**.
xa: **27 MMPs + 10 components**; split **9 Central, 11 State, 7 Integrated**.
DARPG also organises the **National Conference on e-Governance** (28th at **Visakhapatnam**, **2025**).
**CPGRAMS** is DARPG's grievance portal (**2007**).

24.s:
With reference to the original structure of the National e-Governance Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of 27 Mission Mode Projects and 10 components.
2. The Mission Mode Projects were divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects.
3. The original plan contained 44 Mission Mode Projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: The original NeGP contained 27 MMPs and 10 components, divided into 9 Central, 11 State and 7 Integrated projects. The figure of 44 relates to e-Kranti, not the original plan.
24.tq: Separate the original structure from the later expanded figures.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NeGP had **27 MMPs + 10 components**, split **9 Central, 11 State, 7 Integrated**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **44 MMPs** belong to **e-Kranti**; NeGP later expanded to **31** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Exam angle: "NeGP 2006 identified how many MMPs?" — **27** (APPSC **2025**).
⚠ **27 → 31 → 44** under e-Kranti.
NeGP approved **18 May 2006** (DeitY + DARPG).

24.s: Which one of the following is an Integrated Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan?
24.x: e-Courts is identified as an Integrated MMP. e-Panchayat is an MMP, while IT for Jobs and Early Harvest Programmes are Digital India pillars.
24.tq: Use the category distinction between NeGP MMPs and Digital India pillars.
xs: **e-Courts** is an **Integrated MMP** — option **(2)**.
**e-Panchayat** is another MMP but not listed as Integrated; **IT for Jobs** and **Early Harvest** are Digital India pillars, not MMPs.
xa: Other Integrated MMPs: **e-Procurement**, **National Portal** (india.gov.in).
NeGP's **7 Integrated** MMPs out of **27**.
**CCTNS** (MHA, **2009**) and **IVFRT** (MHA, **2010**) are other MMPs.

24.s: Which of the following most accurately expresses the vision of the National e-Governance Plan?
o: To centralise all government files in the national capital
To make all government services accessible to the common man in his locality through common service delivery outlets
To replace all public authorities with private digital platforms
To restrict government services to mobile applications
24.x: NeGP aimed to make government services accessible locally through common service delivery outlets, with transparency, reliability, efficiency and affordable cost.
24.tq: Choose the option that retains the plan’s locality, access and service-delivery elements.
xs: NeGP's vision: make **all government services accessible to the common man in his locality** through **common service delivery outlets** — option **(2)**.
It also seeks **transparency, reliability and efficiency at affordable cost** — not centralisation or privatisation.
xa: Those outlets are the village-level **CSCs**.
Core infrastructure: **SDC**, **SWAN**, **CSCs**.
NeGP approved **18 May 2006**.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of e-Kranti?
o: Integration of cloud, mobile and geospatial technologies
24.x: e-Kranti is integrated, outcome-oriented, fast and agile; it does not depend exclusively on paper-based files.
24.tq: Identify the option that reverses the digital and integrated character of the programme.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on paper-based files** is not an e-Kranti trait — option **(4)**.
e-Kranti is **integrated (cloud, mobile, geospatial)**, **outcome-oriented**, **fast and agile**.
xa: e-Kranti = **NeGP 2.0**, **44 MMPs**, a **pillar of Digital India**.
AP's **e-Pragati** aims at **"faceless, paperless and cashless"** governance.
**e-Office** offers paperless file management.

24.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: e-Courts — Ministry of Commerce and Industry — 2016
24.x: e-Courts is an Integrated Mission Mode Project under NeGP, not a Ministry of Commerce and Industry programme of 2016, so this pair is wrong. e-Panchayat is an MMP, IVFRT is an MHA MMP of 2010 and CCTNS an MHA MMP of 2009.
24.tq: Find the option that swaps the responsible ministry and adds an unsupported launch detail.
xs: **e-Courts — Ministry of Commerce and Industry — 2016** is wrong — option **(1)**: e-Courts is an **Integrated MMP**; **2016** and Commerce & Industry belong to **GeM**.
**e-Panchayat** is an MMP; **IVFRT** = **MHA, 2010**; **CCTNS** = **MHA, 2009** — all correct.
xa: IVFRT extended till **March 2031** as **IVFRT 3.0**.
**GeM**: online public procurement (**2016**).
Integrated MMPs: e-Courts, **e-Procurement**, **National Portal**.

24.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was approved by the Government of India on:
24.x: NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006. 1 July 2015 is the Digital India launch, 25 March 2015 is PRAGATI's launch, and 2001 is the year AP's e-Seva began; none is NeGP's approval.
24.tq: NeGP = 18 May 2006.
xs: **NeGP** was approved on **18 May 2006** — option **(1)**.
**25 March 2015** is **PRAGATI**'s launch; **2001** is AP's **e-Seva**.
xa: Formulated by **DeitY + DARPG**.
**27 MMPs + 10 components**.
Vision: services to the common man **in his locality**.

24.s: e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) differs from the original NeGP in that it:
o: Has 44 Mission Mode Projects and is a pillar of Digital India
Has 27 Mission Mode Projects and is a stand-alone national plan
Has 31 Mission Mode Projects and replaced Digital India
Has 10 Mission Mode Projects run only by States
24.x: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs and is a pillar of Digital India. 27 MMPs in a stand-alone plan describes the original NeGP 2006; 31 is the later expanded NeGP count; 10 is the number of NeGP components, not e-Kranti MMPs.
24.tq: NeGP 27 (stand-alone) → e-Kranti 44 (Digital India pillar).
xs: **e-Kranti** has **44 MMPs** and is **a pillar of Digital India** — option **(1)**.
**27 MMPs** and **stand-alone national plan** describe the original **NeGP**; **31** was NeGP's expanded count.
xa: e-Kranti features: **cloud, mobile, geospatial** integration; **outcome-oriented**.
NeGP split: **9 Central, 11 State, 7 Integrated**.

24.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as core infrastructure of the National e-Governance Plan?
24.x: State Data Centres, SWAN and village-level Common Service Centres formed the core infrastructure of NeGP. The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund is unrelated to this framework.
24.tq: Find the unrelated institutional component among the three stated infrastructure pillars.
xs: The **National Investment and Infrastructure Fund** is not NeGP core infrastructure — option **(4)**.
Core infrastructure = **SDC**, **SWAN** and village-level **CSCs**.
xa: **SWAN**: converged backbone for data, voice, video.
**SDC**: hosts state e-gov applications and data.
**MeghRaj (GI Cloud)** now provides government cloud hosting.

24.s: Common Service Centres are generally operated by Village Level Entrepreneurs and extend down to the level of:
24.x: CSCs are operated by Village Level Entrepreneurs and reach down to the Gram Panchayat level.
24.tq: Use the delivery-chain endpoint to distinguish grassroots access from higher administrative levels.
xs: **CSCs** are run by **Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs)** and reach down to the **Gram Panchayat** — option **(4)**.
So they are village-level outlets, not municipal, district or state offices.
xa: **5.97 lakh CSCs** functional; **4.73 lakh** at GP level (Apr **2025**).
**400+ services**: government, financial, Aadhaar, welfare, education, telemedicine.
**Seva Se Samriddhi**: MoPR workshop (Guwahati, **2026**) honoured top VLEs.

24.s: Which of the following is NOT among the broad categories of services delivered through Common Service Centres?
24.x: CSCs provide more than 400 services, including government, financial, Aadhaar, welfare, education, telemedicine, travel and utility-bill services. Constitutional amendment drafting is not a listed CSC service.
24.tq: Find the single function outside the established service basket rather than choosing a familiar CSC category.
xs: **Constitutional amendment drafting** is not a CSC service — option **(4)**.
CSCs deliver **400+ services**: government, financial, Aadhaar, welfare, education, **telemedicine**, **travel**, **utility bills**.
xa: Run by **Village Level Entrepreneurs**.
**5.97 lakh** CSCs functional.
**CSC** = **Common Service Centre**, NeGP's village-level front end.

24.s: As of April 2025, which of the following figures correctly represents the number of functional Common Service Centres and those at Gram Panchayat level, respectively?
24.x: There were 5.97 lakh functional CSCs, of which 4.73 lakh were at the Gram Panchayat level as of April 2025.
24.tq: Read the larger total first and distinguish it from the included Gram Panchayat-level subset.
xs: **5.97 lakh** CSCs functional and **4.73 lakh** at GP level (Apr **2025**) — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the two; (1) and (4) give figures not in the notes.
xa: CSCs are run by **VLEs**.
They offer **400+ services**.
CSC-SPV honoured top VLEs at **Seva Se Samriddhi** (**2026**).

24.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its role in NeGP infrastructure?
o: SDC — converged backbone for data, voice and video
CSC — hosts State e-governance applications and data
24.x: Common Service Centres are village-level front-end delivery outlets. SWAN is the converged backbone network, while SDC hosts State e-governance applications and data.
24.tq: Match each infrastructure pillar with its functional layer.
xs: **CSC — village-level front-end delivery outlet** is correct — option **(3)**.
**SWAN** is the **converged backbone** (data, voice, video); **SDC** **hosts state applications and data** — so (1), (2), (4) mismatch.
xa: Together they enable **G2G, G2C, G2B** services.
**MeghRaj (GI Cloud)** provides government cloud hosting.
**SWAN** = State Wide Area Network; **SDC** = State Data Centre.

24.s: Which of the following correctly represents the relationship among G2G, G2C and G2B services and NeGP infrastructure?
o: They are enabled only by CSCs without any network or hosting infrastructure.
They are enabled together by SWAN, SDC and CSC.
They refer exclusively to mobile governance applications.
They are unrelated to State Data Centres.
24.x: SWAN, State Data Centres and Common Service Centres together enable seamless Government-to-Government, Government-to-Citizen and Government-to-Business services.
24.tq: Link each service relationship to the complete infrastructure stack instead of one component alone.
xs: **SWAN, SDC and CSC** together enable seamless **G2G, G2C, G2B** services — option **(2)**.
No single element suffices: network (SWAN), hosting (SDC) and front end (CSC) all play roles.
xa: SDC hosts on **common secure IT infrastructure**.
CSCs are **village-level** outlets.
m-Governance is a separate model (**mPassport Seva**, **UMANG**).

24.s: Government cloud hosting for e-governance applications in India is now provided by:
24.x: MeghRaj, the GI Cloud, now provides government cloud hosting. SWAN is the state backbone network, e-Taal gives e-transaction statistics, and CSCs are village-level front-end outlets.
24.tq: Cloud = MeghRaj (GI Cloud).
xs: **MeghRaj (GI Cloud)** now provides **government cloud hosting** — option **(1)**.
**SWAN** is the network; **e-Taal** gives e-transaction statistics; **CSCs** are delivery outlets.
xa: **SDC** hosts state e-gov applications and data.
e-Kranti integrates **cloud, mobile, geospatial** tech.
**e-Taal** = Electronic Transactions Aggregation and Analysis Layer.

24.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. UMANG provides access to services of central, state and local governments through one mobile application.
2. DigiLocker is primarily a cloud locker for digital documents.
3. e-Sign enables Aadhaar-based signing of electronic documents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All three statements are correct. UMANG is a unified service app, DigiLocker stores documents, and e-Sign facilitates Aadhaar-based electronic signatures.
24.tq: Match each platform with its distinctive core service before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All correct: **UMANG** = one mobile app for **central, state and local-body** services; **DigiLocker** = **cloud locker** for documents; **e-Sign** = **Aadhaar-based signing** of e-documents — option **(4)**.
UMANG covers services like **income tax**, **Aadhaar**, **gas booking**, **Passport Seva** and **PF**; e-Sign authenticates by the holder's **Aadhaar eKYC/OTP**.
xa: UMANG: **8.68 crore users**, **2,339 services** from **240** departments.
DigiLocker: **56.06 crore users**, **970.70 crore documents**.
e-Sign: **110.26 crore** issued, **29.07 crore** by CDAC.

24.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
24.x: e-Pramaan is the national e-Authentication framework. SARATHI concerns driving licences, VAHAN concerns vehicle registration, and Bhavishya is an integrated pensioners’ portal.
24.tq: Check the precise function of each neighbouring transport, pension and authentication platform.
xs: **e-Pramaan — National e-Authentication framework** is correct — option **(2)**.
**SARATHI** = **driving licence**; **VAHAN** = **vehicle registration**; **Bhavishya** = pensioners' portal (the life certificate is **Jeevan Pramaan**).
xa: e-Pramaan was built by **C-DAC**; **SAML-based single sign-on** (APPSC **2023**).
⚠ SARATHI = driving licence; VAHAN = vehicle registration.
Exam angle: "national e-authentication service of DeitY" = **e-Pramaan**.

24.s: Meri Pehchaan is associated with which of the following?
o: A digital life certificate service for pensioners
A national single sign-on service integrating 15,024 services
A national telemedicine service for remote consultations
24.x: Meri Pehchaan is a MeitY single sign-on service, with 15,024 services integrated. Its backend includes Parichay or Jan-Parichay, e-Pramaan and DigiLocker.
24.tq: Use the stated scale and backend relationship to identify the single-sign-on platform.
xs: **Meri Pehchaan (NSSO)** is the **national single sign-on** with **15,024 services** integrated — option **(3)**.
Vehicle registration is **VAHAN**, life certificates **Jeevan Pramaan**, telemedicine **e-Sanjeevani**.
xa: Back end: **Parichay/Jan-Parichay**, **e-Pramaan**, **DigiLocker**.
It is a **MeitY** platform.
NIC Mail also uses **Parichay single sign-on**.

24.s: MyGov, launched in 2014, is primarily a platform for:
24.x: MyGov is a MeitY citizen-engagement platform focused on participation and engagement relating to government policy.
24.tq: Identify the platform by its participatory policy function rather than by a transactional service.
xs: **MyGov** (**2014**) is a **citizen-engagement platform on policy** — option **(3)**.
Vehicle registration = **VAHAN**; health records = **ABDM**; pensions = **Bhavishya**.
In short, MyGov is about **citizen engagement on government policies**, not service delivery.
xa: MyGov is under **MeitY**.
**Jeevan Pramaan** also launched in **2014**.
**CPGRAMS** handles grievances (**2007**).

24.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Platform)
a. UMANG
b. e-Office
c. GeM
d. CPGRAMS
List-II (Ministry or body)
i. DARPG
 ii. MeitY
 iii. Ministry of Commerce and Industry
 iv. MeitY through the NIC platform
24.x: UMANG is under MeitY; e-Office is a MeitY-NIC platform; GeM belongs to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; CPGRAMS is associated with DARPG.
24.tq: Start with CPGRAMS–DARPG and GeM–Commerce, then resolve the two MeitY-related pairs.
xs: **UMANG → MeitY**, **e-Office → MeitY via the NIC platform**, **GeM → Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, **CPGRAMS → DARPG** — **a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i**, option **(1)**.
⚠ Both UMANG and e-Office are MeitY's, but **e-Office** runs on the **NIC platform**.
xa: UMANG: launched **2017**; **2,400+** services by Jul **2026**.
GeM: launched **2016** for online public procurement.
CPGRAMS: launched **2007**, 24x7 grievance redress.
e-Office: paperless file and office management.

24.s: Jeevan Pramaan is associated with:
o: Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners
24.x: Jeevan Pramaan is a MeitY initiative providing Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners.
24.tq: Identify the beneficiary group and authentication method of the pension-related service.
xs: **Jeevan Pramaan** gives **Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners** — option **(2)**.
Procurement = **GeM**; paperless files = **e-Office**; RTI appeals = **RTI Online**.
xa: Launched **2014** (MeitY); **153 lakh** DLCs since **1 Nov 2024**.
**Bhavishya** = integrated pensioners' portal.
**e-Sign** also relies on **Aadhaar eKYC/OTP**.

24.s: PRAGATI, launched on 25 March 2015, is associated with:
o: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs and company registration
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry and public procurement
The Prime Minister’s Office and proactive governance, grievance handling and project monitoring
24.x: PRAGATI is associated with the PMO and stands for Pro-Active Governance And Timely Implementation; it deals with grievances and project monitoring.
24.tq: Use the acronym, launch date and institutional setting together to identify the programme.
xs: **PRAGATI** (**25 March 2015**) is the **PMO**'s **Pro-Active Governance And Timely Implementation** — grievances + project monitoring, option **(4)**.
Company registration = **MCA21**; life certificates = **Jeevan Pramaan**; procurement = **GeM**.
xa: **CPGRAMS** is DARPG's grievance portal.
AP plans a unified **AI governance dashboard** within **90 days**.
**e-Taal 3.0** tracks e-transaction statistics.

24.s: e-Taal 3.0 is related to:
o: Digital signatures based only on paper certificates
24.x: e-Taal 3.0, operated by NIC and MeitY, provides statistics on e-transactions and e-services.
24.tq: Identify the monitoring-and-statistics platform rather than a citizen-service delivery portal.
xs: **e-Taal 3.0** (NIC/MeitY) gives **e-transaction statistics** — option **(4)**.
It shows **4,451+ e-services** and **21,206 crore+** e-transactions (July **2025**).
xa: e-Taal = **Electronic Transactions Aggregation and Analysis Layer**.
Agricultural trading = **e-NAM**; company filings = **MCA21**.
**e-Sign** is **PKI-based**, not paper certificates.

24.s: A citizen who wants to apply online for a new driving licence would use which portal of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways?
24.x: SARATHI handles driving licence applications. VAHAN is for vehicle registration (the classic trap), Bhavishya is the pensioners' portal, and e-Pramaan is the national e-authentication framework.
24.tq: SARATHI = licence (driver); VAHAN = vehicle.
xs: A new **driving licence** is applied for on **SARATHI** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **VAHAN** = **vehicle registration**; **Bhavishya** = pensions; **e-Pramaan** = e-authentication.
xa: Asked in APPSC **2022**.
DigiLocker holds **driving licence and RC** (linked with MoRTH in **Sept 2016**).
Both SARATHI and VAHAN belong to **Road Transport & Highways**.

24.s: Which platform functions as a cloud locker for storing digital documents and was launched in February 2015?
24.x: DigiLocker is MeitY’s cloud-based document locker, launched in February 2015.
24.tq: Use the service-function association to distinguish document storage from authentication and pension services.
xs: **DigiLocker** is the **cloud locker** for documents launched in **Feb 2015** — option **(4)**.
**e-Pramaan** = e-authentication; **Jeevan Pramaan** = life certificates; **Meri Pehchaan** = single sign-on.
xa: **56.06 crore users**, **970.70 crore documents**.
Cloud account per citizen **linked to Aadhaar**.
In AP: **1.277 crore** users, **206** departments.

24.s:
Which of the following statements regarding DigiLocker is correct?
1. It provides each citizen with a cloud account linked to Aadhaar.
2. Driving licences and vehicle Registration Certificates can be included in it.
3. CBSE mark sheets have been available through it since 2015.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
24.x: DigiLocker provides an Aadhaar-linked cloud account, includes driving licences and vehicle RCs, and has provided CBSE mark sheets since 2015.
24.tq: Combine three closely related service features and identify the inclusive coded option.
xs: All correct: a cloud account **linked to Aadhaar**; **driving licence and RC** included (MoRTH, **Sept 2016**); **CBSE mark sheets** from **2015** — option **(4)**.
These features make DigiLocker a **MeitY** cloud locker launched in **Feb 2015**.
xa: DigiLocker documents equal originals under **IT Act 2000** + **2016** Digital Locker Rules.
**56.06 crore users**.
Meri Pehchaan's back end includes **DigiLocker**.

24.s: The linking of driving licences and vehicle Registration Certificates with DigiLocker was undertaken through which ministry in September 2016?
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
24.x: Driving licences and vehicle Registration Certificates were linked with DigiLocker through the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in September 2016.
24.tq: Use the sector-specific ministry to distinguish a transport document service from the digital platform ministry.

**142 crore** numbers generated by **31 Jul 2025**; ~**133.65 crore** live after adjusting for deaths.

25.s: Which of the following is NOT an open API-related Aadhaar service listed among its uses?

25.s:

xa: The first Aadhaar number went to **Ranjana Sonawane** of Tembhli on **29 Sept 2010**.

xs: Aadhaar was launched in **2009** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **2010** is the year of the **first Aadhaar number** (**29 Sept 2010**), and **2016** is the **Aadhaar Act**.
xa: **Aadhaar Act** was amended in **2019**.
**142 crore** numbers generated by **31 Jul 2025**; PIB (Aug 2026): access for "over **145 crore**" people.
Aadhaar = **12-digit** (UIDAI); ABHA = **14-digit**.

25.s:
With reference to UIDAI, consider the following statements:
1. UIDAI became a statutory body under the Aadhaar Act, 2016.
2. UIDAI works under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
3. The Aadhaar Act was amended in 2019.

Statement 2 is correct: UIDAI works under **MeitY**.

xa: The Act covers **enrolment, authentication, targeted delivery** of subsidies, benefits and services.
**Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules 2020** followed.
MeitY's **Policy on Open APIs (2015)** → **API Setu**.

25.s:
The Aadhaar Act primarily covers which of the following functions?
1. Enrolment
2. Authentication
3. Targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services
Select the correct answer using the code below.

25.tq: Test the full statutory scope rather than one isolated function.
xs: The **Aadhaar Act 2016** covers **enrolment, authentication** and **targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services** — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
Under it, **UIDAI** became a **statutory body** working under **MeitY**.
xa: The Act was **amended in 2019**.
**Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules 2020** — e.g. **IBPS** allowed voluntary Aadhaar authentication in **2025**.
DBT uses Aadhaar via the **JAM trinity**.

25.s: Which of the following correctly represents the biometric information captured for Aadhaar?
o: Ten fingerprints, two iris scans and a face photograph
Eight fingerprints, one iris scan and a voice sample
Ten fingerprints, two iris scans and a DNA sample
All biometric traits without any facial photograph
25.x: Aadhaar captures ten fingerprints, two irises and a face photograph.
25.tq: Use the exact numerical combination in a biometric list.
xs: Aadhaar captures **ten fingerprints, two iris scans and a face photograph** — so option **(1)** is correct.
No **voice sample** or **DNA** is collected, and a **face photo** is part of it.
xa: Aadhaar is a **12-digit** random number with **no caste, religion or geography** coding.
**Lifelong, free, one enrolment per person**.

25.s: Which of the following statements regarding open APIs and Aadhaar is correct?
o: API Setu was developed by NPCI exclusively for card payments.
Aadhaar e-KYC can be used only for election-related services.
The Policy on Open APIs was issued by RBI in 2015 and prohibited integration with public services.
MeitY's Policy on Open APIs, 2015, led to API Setu; Aadhaar e-KYC simplified banking and public services.

The policy was **MeitY's**, not RBI's, and it opened APIs for **authentication, e-KYC, e-Sign** — so option (3) is wrong.

xa: **Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance Rules 2020**.
**UIDAI** works under **MeitY** as a statutory body under the **Aadhaar Act 2016**.
**NPCI** runs UPI, IMPS, AePS, NACH, RuPay.

25.s: UPI was launched in April 2016 by:

25.s: Which one of the following best describes the functioning of UPI?
o: It permits cash withdrawals only through Aadhaar-enabled micro-ATMs.

25.tq: Match the digital-payment mechanism with its defining operational feature.
xs: UPI lets **a single application route payments from several bank accounts using a VPA** such as **name@bank** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Cash withdrawal at **micro-ATMs** with Aadhaar is **AePS**, not UPI — option (1) is wrong.
**Wallets (PPIs)** are issued by RBI-authorised banks and non-banks; **RuPay** is NPCI's card network.
xa: UPI was launched in **April 2016** by **NPCI**.

**Bharat QR** = interoperable QR code standard by NPCI with card networks.
**UPI** itself was launched in **April 2016** by NPCI.
