An **external team** joined the PSLV failure probe (**3 Feb 2026**).

40.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with the PSLV-C62 co-passengers?
o: AayulSAT was a navigation satellite, while MOI-1 was a solar coronagraph.
AayulSAT was a weather satellite, while MOI-1 was a lunar lander.
AayulSAT was the first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator, while MOI-1 was an AI image laboratory.
Both AayulSAT and MOI-1 were foreign communication satellites.
40.x: AayulSAT was identified as the first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator and MOI-1 as an AI image laboratory among the PSLV-C62 co-passengers.
40.tq: Match each unusual payload description with its correct satellite name.
xs: **AayulSAT** was the **first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator** and **MOI-1** an **AI image lab** — option **(3)**.
Both were among the **15 co-passengers** lost on **PSLV-C62** (**12 Jan 2026**).
xa: The main payload was DRDO's **400 kg hyperspectral EOS-N1 "Anvesha"**.
PSLV-C62 plans included a **PS4 de-boost** and the Spanish **KID** re-entry capsule.
The failure: **roll-rate disturbance** at the end of the third stage.

40.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a re-entry experiment?
40.x: SRE-1 was associated with PSLV-C7 in 2007. CARE was associated with LVM3 in 2014, and POEM-3 with PSLV-C58 in 2024.
40.tq: Match each experiment with its vehicle and year before considering the distractors.
xs: **SRE-1 — PSLV-C7, 2007** is correct — option **(1)**.
**CARE** flew on **LVM3** in **2014**, not PSLV-C7.
**POEM-3** flew on **C58** (**1 Jan 2024**); **PSLV-C53** (**2022**) carried the first **POEM**.
xa: POEM = the **spent PS4 stage** used as an orbital lab.
PSLV-C62 planned the Spanish **KID** re-entry capsule.

40.s: POEM platforms are best described as:
o: Spent PS4 stages used as orbital laboratories
Reusable crew capsules for ISS missions
Foreign customer satellites launched by PSLV
40.x: POEM platforms use the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.
40.tq: Interpret the platform’s function from its structural origin and orbital use.
xs: POEM platforms are **spent PS4 stages used as orbital labs** — option **(2)**.
They are not ground stations, crew capsules or foreign customer satellites.
xa: Re-entry experiments: **SRE-1** (**PSLV-C7**, **2007**) and **CARE** (**LVM3**, **2014**).
PSLV-C62 planned a **PS4 de-boost**.

40.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Indian satellites used for military communication is correct?
o: GSAT-7, GSAT-7A and GSAT-7B are all operational satellites exclusively used by the Navy.
GSAT-7 is associated with the Navy, GSAT-7A with the IAF, and GSAT-7B has been proposed for the Army.
GSAT-7 is a broadband satellite, GSAT-7A is an ocean satellite, and GSAT-7B is a weather satellite.
GSAT-7 is associated with the IAF, GSAT-7A with the Army, and GSAT-7B is used by the Navy.
40.x: GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A, known as the ‘Angry Bird’, serves the IAF, and GSAT-7B has been proposed for the Army.
40.tq: Use the service-wise association and reject swapped users or unsupported operational status.
xs: **GSAT-7** – **Navy**; **GSAT-7A "Angry Bird"** – **IAF**; **GSAT-7B** – **proposed for the Army** — option **(2)**.
GSAT-7B is only proposed, so option (1) is wrong; options (3) and (4) mix up the users and roles.
xa: Strategic surveillance: **RISAT**, **Cartosat**, **EMISAT** (electronic intelligence), **EOS-N1**.
India has **19** operational communication satellites; **10** moved to **NSIL** in **2022**.
Weather domain: **INSAT-3DS**, **Kalpana-1**.

40.s: Kalpana-1 is best described as which one of the following?
o: India’s first exclusive oceanographic satellite, launched by GSLV in 2002
India’s first navigation satellite, launched by PSLV in 2005
India’s first military communication satellite, launched by GSLV in 2005
India’s first exclusive meteorological satellite, launched by PSLV in 2002
40.x: Kalpana-1 was India’s first exclusive meteorological satellite and was launched by PSLV in 2002.
40.tq: Split the option into mission purpose, launch vehicle and year before selecting the exact combination.
xs: **Kalpana-1** was India's **first exclusive meteorological satellite**, launched by **PSLV** in **2002** — option **(4)**.
It was not oceanographic (that is **Oceansat**), navigation (**NVS/NavIC**) or military communication (**GSAT-7**).
xa: The other weather satellite listed is **INSAT-3DS** (**GSLV-F14**, **2024**, **MoES**).
Science missions: **XPoSat**, **Aditya-L1**.
Aditya-L1 flew on **PSLV-C57** (**2023**).

40.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NVS and NavIC are associated with navigation.
2. XPoSat and Aditya-L1 are associated with scientific studies.
3. Oceansat satellites are primarily military communication satellites.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: NVS/NavIC are navigation systems, while XPoSat and Aditya-L1 are science missions. Statement 3 is false because Oceansat belongs to the ocean-study domain.
40.tq: Find the single domain mismatch and use the coded options to eliminate it.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **NVS / NavIC** = **navigation**.
Statement 2 correct: **XPoSat** and **Aditya-L1** = **science**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Oceansat** belongs to the **ocean** domain; military communication is **GSAT-7/7A**.
xa: Strategic surveillance: **RISAT, Cartosat, EMISAT, EOS-N1**.
Weather: **INSAT-3DS**, **Kalpana-1**.
Aditya-L1 was launched by **PSLV-C57** (**2023**).

40.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the launch event associated with GSLV-F17/EOS-05?
o: It marked the first launch of an Indian navigation satellite after two failures of GSLV.
It ended a two-month launch pause following one PSLV failure.
It ended an eight-month launch pause following two PSLV failures.
It began an eight-month launch pause following two GSLV failures.
40.x: The GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission ended an eight-month launch pause that followed two PSLV failures.
40.tq: Track the launch vehicle, duration of the pause and type and number of earlier failures.
xs: **GSLV-F17/EOS-05** **ended an eight-month launch pause** after **two PSLV failures** — option **(3)** (**5 Sep 2026**).
The failures were **PSLV-C61** (**18 May 2025**) and **PSLV-C62** (**12 Jan 2026**) — not GSLV.
EOS-05 is an imaging satellite, not a navigation satellite.
xa: EOS-05 is a geo-platform "eye in the sky" for **agriculture, environment, disasters**.
An **external team** joined the PSLV failure probe (**3 Feb 2026**).

40.s: With reference to Starlink in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Starlink received a navigation licence from the Department of Telecommunications in 2025, with local terminal manufacturing required within ten years.
Starlink received a GMPCS licence from DRDO in 2026, without any geofencing requirement.
Starlink received a GMPCS licence from the Department of Telecommunications in 2025, subject to geofencing and local terminal manufacturing within five years.
Starlink received a broadcasting licence from ISRO in 2025, with satellite manufacturing to be completed within two years.
40.x: Starlink obtained a GMPCS licence from the Department of Telecommunications in 2025. The new rules require geofencing and local terminal manufacturing within five years.
40.tq: Identify the correct licensing authority and distinguish the paired compliance conditions.
xs: Starlink got a **GMPCS licence** from **DoT** in **2025**, with **geofencing** and **local terminal manufacturing within 5 years** — option **(3)**.
The licence came from **DoT**, not DRDO or ISRO, and is not a navigation or broadcasting licence.
xa: The geofencing and local-manufacturing rules came in **2026**.
**BlueBird Block-2** (**LVM3-M6**) offers **direct-to-smartphone broadband**.
ISRO's commercial arm **NSIL** has launched **141** satellites.

40.s: India's satellite status as reported in the relevant 2026 assessment was:
o: 4,651 satellites in orbit, of which 86 were operational
86 satellites in orbit, of which 27 were operational
27 satellites in orbit, of which 86 were operational
315 satellites in orbit, of which 27 were operational
40.x: India had 86 satellites in orbit, of which 27 were operational.
40.tq: Read the total and subset figures in the correct order.
xs: India had **86 satellites in orbit**, of which **27 were operational** — option **(2)**.
Source: **Indian Space Situational Assessment Report 2025** (**9 Apr 2026**).
**315** is the number of **world launches** in that year, not Indian satellites.
xa: India launched **8** satellites in **2025**.
India has **19** operational **communication** satellites.
**PSLV-C37** holds the record of **104** satellites in one launch.

41.s:
Arrange the following space-shuttle events in chronological order:
A. First flight of Columbia
B. Repair of the Solar Maximum Mission satellite
C. Loss of Challenger
D. Loss of Columbia during re-entry
41.x: The sequence is Columbia’s first flight in 1981, Solar Maximum Mission repair in 1984, Challenger’s loss in 1986, and Columbia’s loss during re-entry in 2003.
41.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle events by year.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Columbia's first flight**: **April 1981 (STS-1)**; **Solar Maximum Mission repair**: **April 1984** (STS-41C).
**Challenger lost**: **1986**; **Columbia lost on re-entry**: **2003**.
xa: Kalpana Chawla was killed in the **Columbia** disaster (**2003**).
The Shuttle programme ended in **2011** with **Atlantis (STS-135)**.
⚠ **Challenger** lost **1986**; **Columbia** lost **2003**.

41.s: The first satellite repaired in orbit was which of the following?
41.x: NASA’s Solar Maximum Mission satellite was repaired by the crew of Space Shuttle Challenger in April 1984 during mission STS-41C.
41.tq: Directly identify the unique satellite associated with the first in-orbit repair.
xs: NASA's **Solar Maximum Mission** was the **first satellite repaired in orbit** — option **(1)**.
It was repaired by the **Challenger** crew in **April 1984** (**STS-41C**).
**Aryabhata** (**1975**) was India's first satellite and **Rohini** (**1980**) went up on **SLV-3** — neither was repaired in orbit.
xa: First Shuttle flight: **Columbia, April 1981 (STS-1)**.
**Challenger** itself was lost in **1986**.
Programme ended in **2011** with **Atlantis**.

41.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India’s early space milestones?
o: SLV-3 was first used for Aryabhata in 1975.
Aryabhata was launched in 1975 using a Soviet rocket.
Aryabhata made India the sixth nation to launch a satellite indigenously.
Rohini was launched in 1975 using a Soviet rocket.
41.x: Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, was launched in 1975 on a Soviet rocket. In 1980, SLV-3 launched Rohini, making India the sixth nation to launch a satellite indigenously.
41.tq: Separate the satellite, launch vehicle and year in two closely related milestones.
xs: **Aryabhata** was launched in **1975** on a **Soviet rocket** — option **(2)**.
**SLV-3** launched **Rohini** in **1980**, not Aryabhata, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
The **6th nation** milestone came with **SLV-3/Rohini (1980)**, not Aryabhata.
xa: Aryabhata was **India's first satellite**.
**Chandrayaan-1** (**2008**) was launched on **PSLV-C11**.
Every mission in this topic launched from **Sriharikota (SDSC SHAR)**, **Tirupati district**.

41.s: India became the sixth nation to launch a satellite indigenously when, in 1980:
41.x: In 1980 SLV-3 launched Rohini, making India the 6th nation with indigenous satellite launch capability. Aryabhata (1975) and APPLE (1981) used foreign rockets, and IRS-P2 on PSLV came only in 1994.
41.tq: 1980 SLV-3/Rohini = India 6th; Aryabhata 1975 = Soviet rocket.
xs: In **1980**, **SLV-3 launched Rohini**, making India the **6th nation** to launch a satellite indigenously — option **(2)**.
**Aryabhata** (**1975**) went up on a **Soviet rocket**, so it was not indigenous.
xa: Aryabhata was India's **first satellite**.
**Mangalyaan** (**2013**, **PSLV-C25**) was India's first interplanetary mission.
**SpaDeX** made India the **4th** country to dock in space (**16 Jan 2025**).

41.s: In a two-body system, the points at which a small object can remain in balance are known as:
41.x: Lagrange points are five points, L1 to L5, in a two-body system where a small object can remain in balance. The Sun–Earth L1 point is about 1.5 million km sunward of Earth.
41.tq: Match the exact scientific term with its defining condition.
xs: These are **Lagrange points** — option **(2)**.
There are **five** (**L1-L5**) in a two-body system.
**Hohmann transfer** is an orbit-transfer method, not a balance point.
xa: Sun-Earth **L1** is ~**1.5 million km** sunward — **Aditya-L1's** station.
Aditya-L1 sits in a **halo orbit** around L1 → continuous view of the Sun, no eclipse.
Escape velocity of Earth: **11.2 km/s**.

41.s: The minimum speed required for an object to escape the gravitational field of Earth is approximately:
41.x: Earth’s escape velocity is approximately 11.2 km/s.
41.tq: Check the decimal place carefully in a standard numerical value.
xs: Earth's escape velocity is **11.2 km/s** — option **(2)**.
It is the **minimum speed** to escape a body's gravity.
xa: **Soft landing** limits for Ch-3: vertical **≤ 2 m/s**, horizontal ≤ **0.5 m/s**, slope ≤ **12 degrees**.
**Hohmann transfer**: fuel-efficient elliptical orbit with **two engine burns**; **MOM** used it.
**Lagrange points**: **five** (L1-L5).

41.s: A Hohmann transfer is best described as:
o: A controlled low-speed touchdown on a planetary surface
A point of gravitational balance in a two-body system
A direct vertical launch requiring continuous engine thrust
A fuel-efficient transfer between two orbits using an elliptical orbit and two engine burns
41.x: A Hohmann transfer uses an elliptical transfer orbit and two engine burns to move between two orbits efficiently. Mangalyaan used this method to reach Mars.
41.tq: Match the operational description with the correct orbital-mechanics term.
xs: A **Hohmann transfer** is a **fuel-efficient elliptical orbit between two orbits** using **two engine burns** — option **(4)**.
**Controlled low-speed touchdown** is a **soft landing**; a **balance point** is a **Lagrange point**.
xa: **Mangalyaan (MOM)** used a Hohmann transfer to reach Mars.
MOM entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014** — on the **first attempt**.
Escape velocity: **11.2 km/s**.

41.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Mission — Launch vehicle
1. Chandrayaan-1 — PSLV-C11
2. Mangalyaan — PSLV-C25
3. AstroSat — PSLV-C30
4. Chandrayaan-2 — GSLV Mk III-M1

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
41.x: All four pairings are correct: Chandrayaan-1 used PSLV-C11, Mangalyaan PSLV-C25, AstroSat PSLV-C30 and Chandrayaan-2 GSLV Mk III-M1.
41.tq: Start with a sure mission-vehicle pair and verify whether each remaining pair belongs to the same launch table.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Chandrayaan-1** – **PSLV-C11** (**22 Oct 2008**); **Mangalyaan** – **PSLV-C25** (**5 Nov 2013**).
**AstroSat** – **PSLV-C30** (**28 Sept 2015**); **Chandrayaan-2** – **GSLV Mk III-M1** (**22 July 2019**).
xa: **Chandrayaan-3** flew on **LVM3-M4** (**14 July 2023**).
⚠ Trap: **GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS** was **2024**, not 2022.

41.s:
Arrange the following missions in chronological order of launch:
A. XPoSat
B. Chandrayaan-3
C. SpaDeX
D. Aditya-L1
41.x: The correct order is Chandrayaan-3 (14 July 2023), Aditya-L1 (2 September 2023), XPoSat (1 January 2024) and SpaDeX (30 December 2024).
41.tq: Use the year first and then distinguish the two missions launched in 2023 by their months.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**Chandrayaan-3**: **14 July 2023**; **Aditya-L1**: **2 Sept 2023**.
xa: APPSC **2023** match order: Ch-2 **Jul 2019** → Ch-3 **Jul 2023** → Aditya-L1 **Sep 2023** → SpaDeX **Dec 2024**.
SpaDeX docked on **16 Jan 2025** → India **4th** to dock in space.
⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated XPoSat **May 2023**.

41.s: The pair GSLV-F14 and INSAT-3DS is associated with which year?
41.x: GSLV-F14 launched INSAT-3DS in February 2024. Therefore, the pairing with 2022 is incorrect.
41.tq: Watch for the famous-year trap in a mission and vehicle combination.
xs: **GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS** belongs to **2024** (Feb **2024**) — option **(3)**.
⚠ "GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS – **2022**" is the known **incorrect** PYQ pair.
xa: Another PYQ pair: **PSLV-C56/DS-SAR** — **July 2023**.
**XPoSat** also flew in **2024** (**1 Jan**, **PSLV-C58**).
**Aditya-L1** flew on **PSLV-C57** in **2023**.

41.s: Which of the following statements regarding LVM3 is correct?
o: Its largest commercial payload in low Earth orbit was Chandrayaan-1.
It launched BlueBird Block-2 for a European government agency.
It was used only for lunar missions and never for commercial launches.
It flew two OneWeb missions carrying a total of 72 satellites.
41.x: LVM3 flew two OneWeb missions carrying 72 satellites in total. The 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2, built for AST SpaceMobile of the United States, was its largest commercial communication satellite in LEO.
41.tq: Reject the absolute statement and distinguish commercial payloads by operator and purpose.
xs: **LVM3** flew **two OneWeb missions** carrying **72 satellites** — option **(4)**.
Its **LVM3-M6** carried the **6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2** for **AST SpaceMobile (US)**, a company, not a European agency.
**Chandrayaan-1** flew on **PSLV-C11**, and LVM3 does fly commercial missions.
xa: BlueBird Block-2 is the **largest commercial communication satellite in LEO** (**2026**).
LVM3 (**LVM3-M4**) also launched **Chandrayaan-3** on **14 July 2023**.
Chandrayaan-2 flew on **GSLV Mk III-M1**.

41.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Mission — Landmark result
1. Chandrayaan-1 — Confirmation of water molecules on the lunar surface
2. Chandrayaan-2 — Soft landing of Vikram in September 2019
3. Chandrayaan-3 — Soft landing at Shiv Shakti Point
4. Mangalyaan — Entry into Mars orbit on the first attempt

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
41.x: Pair 2 is incorrect because Chandrayaan-2's Vikram lander crash-landed in September 2019. The other three pairings are correct.
41.tq: Find the wrong mission-result association by checking the success or failure of the landing.
xs: Only pair 2 is wrong — option **(1) 2 only**.
**Chandrayaan-2's Vikram** did **not** soft-land — it **crash-landed** in **Sep 2019** (**Tiranga point**).
The others are correct: **Ch-1** confirmed **water molecules**; **Ch-3** landed at **Shiv Shakti point**; **Mangalyaan** reached Mars orbit on the **first attempt**.
xa: Ch-2's **orbiter still works** with all payloads active.
Ch-3 soft-landed on **23 Aug 2023**.
MOM entered Mars orbit in **Sep 2014**.

41.s: Aditya-L1 was launched by which launch vehicle?
41.x: Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 in September 2023.
41.tq: Link the scientific mission with its PSLV flight designation.
xs: **Aditya-L1** was launched by **PSLV-C57** — option **(1)** (**2 Sept 2023**).
**LVM3-M4** launched **Chandrayaan-3** (**14 July 2023**), not Aditya-L1.
xa: ⚠ Trap: a prep-app date "**25 January 2024**" is wrong; halo-orbit insertion was **6 January 2024**.
Aditya-L1 is India's **first space-based solar observatory**.
It carries **7 payloads** (**4** remote sensing + **3** in-situ).

41.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chandrayaan-1:
1. It consisted of an orbiter and a Moon Impact Probe.
2. It carried 11 scientific instruments, including NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper.
3. It confirmed the presence of water molecules on the lunar surface.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: All three statements are correct. Chandrayaan-1 comprised an orbiter and MIP, carried 11 instruments including M3, and confirmed water molecules on the lunar surface.
41.tq: Check each statement against the mission's modules, payload count and landmark result.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Chandrayaan-1** = **orbiter + Moon Impact Probe (MIP)**.
It carried **11 instruments**, including NASA's **M3 (Moon Mineralogy Mapper)**.
M3 gave evidence of **water/hydroxyl**; the mission confirmed **water molecules** on the lunar surface.
xa: Instruments came from **India, USA, UK, Germany, Sweden, Bulgaria**; mass **1,380 kg**.
It made **3,400+ orbits**; contact lost **29 Aug 2009** after **312 days**.
Launched **22 Oct 2008** on **PSLV-C11**.

41.s: Which instrument supplied evidence of water or hydroxyl on the Moon in the Chandrayaan-1 mission?
41.x: NASA’s Moon Mineralogy Mapper, or M3, provided evidence of water or hydroxyl on the Moon. The other listed instruments were associated with Mangalyaan.
41.tq: Separate similarly named instruments by their target body and mission.
xs: NASA's **Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3)** gave evidence of **water/hydroxyl** — option **(2)**.
**MENCA**, **Mars Colour Camera** and **Methane Sensor for Mars** are **Mangalyaan** payloads.
xa: Other Ch-1 payloads: **TMC, HySI, LLRI, HEX, CIXS, SIR-2, SARA, Mini-SAR, RADOM**.
Ch-1 carried **11 instruments** from **India, USA, UK, Germany, Sweden and Bulgaria**.
The **MIP** impact site was named **Jawahar Point**.

41.s: Which one of the following is NOT a payload of Chandrayaan-1?
41.x: TMC, Mini-SAR and CIXS were among the Chandrayaan-1 payloads. Lyman Alpha Photometer was one of Mangalyaan’s five payloads.
41.tq: Identify the instrument that belongs to the neighbouring Mars mission.
xs: **Lyman Alpha Photometer** is NOT a Chandrayaan-1 payload — option **(3)**; it is one of **Mangalyaan's 5** payloads.
**Mini-SAR**, **CIXS** and **TMC** are Chandrayaan-1 payloads.
xa: Other Ch-1 payloads: **HySI, LLRI, HEX, SIR-2, SARA, RADOM** and NASA's **M3**.
MOM's other payloads: **Methane Sensor for Mars**, **MENCA**, **Mars Colour Camera**, **TIS**.
Ch-1 confirmed **water molecules** on the Moon.

41.s: India became the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe. Which sequence lists the nations preceding India in this achievement?
41.x: India was the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe, after the USSR, the USA and Japan.
41.tq: Use the stated rank and identify the preceding countries without substituting later lunar powers.
xs: India was **4th** to place its flag on the Moon via an impact probe, after the **USSR, USA and Japan** — option **(1)**.
Chandrayaan-1's **MIP** hit the lunar south polar region on **14 Nov 2008** at **Jawahar Point**.
xa: ⚠ Site names: **Jawahar Point** = Ch-1 MIP; **Tiranga point** = Ch-2 crash; **Shiv Shakti** = Ch-3 landing.
First probe to hit the Moon: **Luna 2** (USSR, **1959**).
NASA's **LCROSS** (**2009**) impacted a polar crater to find water.

41.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal configuration of Chandrayaan-2 at launch?
o: Orbiter, Moon Impact Probe and rover Pragyan
Propulsion Module, lander Vikram and rover Pragyan
Orbiter, lander Vikram and rover Pragyan
Orbiter, lander Vikram and rover Apollo
41.x: Chandrayaan-2 consisted of an orbiter, the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover. The propulsion-module configuration was associated with Chandrayaan-3.
41.tq: Discriminate between closely related mission configurations and retained names.
xs: **Chandrayaan-2** = **orbiter + lander Vikram + rover Pragyan** — option **(3)**.
**Orbiter + MIP** was **Chandrayaan-1**; **Propulsion Module + Vikram + Pragyan** was **Chandrayaan-3**.
xa: Aim: study the **south polar region** (surface, minerals, water ice).
Ch-2 launched **22 July 2019** on **GSLV Mk III-M1**.
Ch-3 kept the names **Vikram** and **Pragyan** (APPSC **2022**).

41.s:
With reference to Chandrayaan-2, consider the following statements:
1. Its objective included studying the lunar south polar region, including surface, minerals and water ice.
2. The Vikram lander successfully completed a soft landing in September 2019.
3. Its orbiter captured the highest-resolution lunar images.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Vikram's soft landing failed in September 2019, although the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter continued operating with its payloads active.
41.tq: Find the single false statement by testing the mission result against the orbiter's continuing contribution.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: Ch-2 aimed to study the **south polar region** (surface, minerals, **water ice**).
Statement 2 wrong: **Vikram's soft landing failed** (Sep **2019**) — it crash-landed at **Tiranga point**.
Statement 3 correct: the **orbiter still works** and gave the **highest-resolution lunar images**.
xa: Ch-2 = **orbiter + Vikram + Pragyan**.
Launched **22 July 2019** on **GSLV Mk III-M1**.
Ch-3's lander **Vikram** soft-landed on **23 Aug 2023**.

41.s: The crash-landing site of the Chandrayaan-2 Vikram lander was named:
41.x: The Chandrayaan-2 crash spot was named Tiranga Point, whereas Chandrayaan-3's landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point.
41.tq: Separate the similarly named landing and impact sites of Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.
xs: Vikram's Chandrayaan-2 crash spot is **Tiranga Point** — option **(3)**.
**Jawahar Point** = Ch-1 **MIP** impact site; **Shiv Shakti** = Ch-3 landing site.
xa: Ch-2's Vikram crash-landed in **Sep 2019**.
Ch-3 soft-landed at **Shiv Shakti point** on **23 Aug 2023**.
Ch-2's orbiter continues to work with all payloads.

41.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Payload — Function
1. ChaSTE — Thermal conductivity and temperature of lunar topsoil
2. ILSA — Seismicity near the landing site
3. Langmuir Probe — Plasma density
4. APXS — Passive laser ranging

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
41.x: ChaSTE, ILSA and the Langmuir Probe perform the functions stated. APXS determines elemental composition; passive laser ranging is performed by the NASA laser retroreflector.
41.tq: Match each payload with its scientific function and identify the swapped-function trap.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**ChaSTE** – topsoil **thermal conductivity and temperature**; **ILSA** – **moonquakes**; **Langmuir Probe (RAMBHA-LP)** – **plasma density**.
Pair 4 wrong: **APXS** (rover) measures **elemental composition**; passive laser ranging is NASA's **LRA**.
xa: **LIBS** (rover) also measures elemental composition.
**SHAPE** on the **Propulsion Module** studies Earth from lunar orbit.
APXS found Shiv Shakti soil **rich in iron + magnesium**, poor in aluminium.

41.s: The SHAPE payload of Chandrayaan-3 was carried by the:
41.x: The Propulsion Module carried the SHAPE payload, which studies Earth from lunar orbit.
41.tq: Ask who carried the payload rather than what the payload studies.
xs: **SHAPE** was carried by the **Propulsion Module** — option **(4)**; it studies **Earth from lunar orbit**.
The Propulsion Module carried the lander-rover to a **100 km** lunar orbit.
xa: Lander payloads: **ChaSTE, ILSA, RAMBHA-LP, LRA (NASA)**.
Rover payloads: **APXS** and **LIBS**.
The **MIP** belonged to **Chandrayaan-1**, not Ch-3.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-3:
1. It consisted of a Propulsion Module, the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan.
2. It was launched by PSLV-C57 from Sriharikota.
3. It soft-landed on 23 August 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Chandrayaan-3 had a Propulsion Module plus lander Vikram and rover Pragyan (names kept from Chandrayaan-2, APPSC 2022), and it soft-landed on 23 Aug 2023. Statement 2 is wrong: it flew on LVM3 (LVM3-M4); PSLV-C57 launched Aditya-L1. So '1 and 3 only'; the other options include statement 2 or drop a true one.
41.tq: Ch-3: Propulsion Module + Vikram + Pragyan, LVM3-M4, 23 Aug 2023.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Propulsion Module + lander Vikram + rover Pragyan**.
Statement 2 wrong: Ch-3 flew on **LVM3 (LVM3-M4)**; **PSLV-C57** launched **Aditya-L1**.
Statement 3 correct: it **soft-landed on 23 Aug 2023**.
xa: Launch date: **14 July 2023** from **SDSC SHAR**.
Total mass **3,900 kg** (lander **1,752 kg** incl. the **26 kg** rover).
Mission life: **one lunar day (~14 Earth days)**.

41.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jawahar Point — impact site of Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe
2. Tiranga Point — Chandrayaan-3 soft-landing site
3. Shiv Shakti Point — Chandrayaan-3 soft landing on 23 August 2023
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
41.x: Pair 1 is correct: the MIP impact site is Jawahar Point. Pair 2 is wrong: Tiranga Point is where Chandrayaan-2's Vikram crash-landed. Pair 3 is correct: Chandrayaan-3 landed at Shiv Shakti Point on 23 Aug 2023. Hence B; A and D accept the false pair 2, C omits pair 1.
41.tq: Ch-1 = Jawahar, Ch-2 crash = Tiranga, Ch-3 = Shiv Shakti.
xs: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Pair 1 correct: **Jawahar Point** = Ch-1 **MIP** impact site.
Pair 2 wrong: **Tiranga Point** is where **Ch-2's** Vikram **crash-landed**.
Pair 3 correct: Ch-3 landed at **Shiv Shakti point** on **23 Aug 2023**.
xa: Shiv Shakti lies ~**600 km** from the South Pole, between craters **Manzinus C** and **Simpelius N**.
**23 August** is **National Space Day**.
MIP hit the Moon on **14 Nov 2008**.

41.s: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon after:
41.x: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, after the United States, Russia and China.
41.tq: Use the stated rank to reconstruct the preceding members of the sequence.
xs: India was the **4th** to soft-land on the Moon, after the **United States, Russia and China** — option **(3)**.
It was also the **1st near the lunar south pole**.
**Japan** came **5th** later, with **SLIM** (**2024**).
xa: Russia's **Luna-25** (**2023**) crashed days before Ch-3 landed.
China's **Chang'e-3** (**2013**) made the first soft landing since **1976**.
Ch-3 landing: **23 Aug 2023**, **Shiv Shakti point**.

41.s:
Assertion (A): 23 August is observed as National Space Day in India.
Reason (R): Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing on the Moon on 23 August 2023.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
41.x: Both statements are true, and the observance of National Space Day is associated with Chandrayaan-3's soft landing on 23 August 2023.
41.tq: Connect a commemorative date with the mission event that gave rise to it.
xs: **Both A and R are true** and R is the **correct explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Chandrayaan-3** soft-landed on **23 August 2023**, and **23 August** is observed as **National Space Day**.
xa: Landing site: **Shiv Shakti point**, ~**600 km** from the South Pole.
India: **4th** to soft-land, **1st** near the lunar south pole.
Pragyan confirmed **sulphur** near the south pole (APPSC **2023**).

41.s: Which element did Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover confirm near the lunar south pole, a finding asked in APPSC 2023?
41.x: Pragyan confirmed sulphur near the south pole; its LIBS also detected Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O. Helium-3, uranium and nitrogen are not among the elements Pragyan confirmed.
41.tq: Pragyan = sulphur near south pole.
xs: **Pragyan** confirmed **sulphur** near the lunar south pole — option **(2)** (APPSC **2023**).
Its **LIBS** also detected **Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O**.
xa: **APXS** found Shiv Shakti soil **rich in iron + magnesium**, **poor in aluminium**.
The soil is chemically similar to lunar meteorite **ALHA 81005** (Jun **2026**).
Pragyan's rover mass: **26 kg**.

41.s: India’s first interplanetary mission, launched on PSLV-C25, was designated as which of the following?
41.x: Mangalyaan was India’s first interplanetary mission and was also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission. It was launched on PSLV-C25.
41.tq: Identify the alternate official name of the mission from its launch vehicle association.
xs: India's first interplanetary mission is the **Mars Orbiter Mission** (Mangalyaan) — option **(3)**.
Launched on **5 Nov 2013** by **PSLV-C25**.
**AstroSat** is a space observatory; **Chandrayaan-1** went to the Moon; **Aditya-L1** studies the Sun.
xa: MOM entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014**, on its **maiden attempt**.
ISRO became the **4th space agency** to orbit Mars.
Designed for **6 months**, it worked about **8 years**.

41.s: Which one of the following achievements is associated with Mangalyaan?
o: India became the first country to return samples from Mars.
India became the first country to soft-land on the Moon.
India became the first country to land a rover on the far side of the Moon.
India became the first country to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt.
41.x: India reached Mars orbit on its maiden attempt through Mangalyaan. It also made India the first Asian nation to orbit Mars.
41.tq: Distinguish an orbital achievement from landing and sample-return achievements.
xs: Mangalyaan made India the **first country to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt** — option **(4)**.
It also made India the **first Asian nation** in Mars orbit.
Soft landing on the Moon was **Chandrayaan-3**, and India was **4th**, not first; the far-side rover was China's **Yutu-2**.
xa: ISRO = **4th space agency** to orbit Mars (after **NASA, Roscosmos, ESA**).
It was the **lowest-cost** Mars mission.
It carried **5 payloads**, including the **Methane Sensor for Mars**.

41.s: ISRO became the fourth space agency to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit after which sequence of agencies?
41.x: ISRO was the fourth space agency to orbit Mars, after NASA, Roscosmos and ESA.
41.tq: Use the stated rank and identify the three agencies preceding it.
xs: ISRO was the **4th** agency to orbit Mars, after **NASA, Roscosmos and ESA** — option **(1)**.
**CNSA** and **JAXA** are not listed as having orbited Mars before ISRO.
xa: MOM orbit insertion: **24 September 2014** (highly elliptical).
India was the **first** to reach Mars orbit on its **maiden attempt**.
Contact was lost in **2022**.

41.s: Which one of the following is NOT a payload carried by Mangalyaan?
41.x: Mangalyaan carried the Methane Sensor for Mars, Mars Colour Camera, MENCA, Lyman Alpha Photometer and Thermal Infrared Imaging Spectrometer. Moon Mineralogy Mapper was a Chandrayaan-1 payload.
41.tq: Find the instrument belonging to a different mission rather than the named mission.
xs: **Moon Mineralogy Mapper** is NOT a Mangalyaan payload — option **(1)**; it was NASA's **M3** on **Chandrayaan-1**.
Mangalyaan's **5 payloads**: **Methane Sensor for Mars**, **Lyman Alpha Photometer**, **MENCA**, **Mars Colour Camera**, **TIS**.
xa: TIS = **Thermal Infrared Imaging Spectrometer**.
MOM was launched on **PSLV-C25** in **2013**.
M3 gave evidence of **water/hydroxyl** on the Moon.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Mangalyaan:
1. It was placed in a highly elliptical Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.
2. Designed for six months, it worked for about eight years.
3. Contact with it was lost in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: contact was lost in 2022, after about eight years. Hence A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
41.tq: MOM: 6-month design, ~8-year life, lost 2022.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: it entered a **highly elliptical Mars orbit** on **24 September 2014**.
Statement 2 correct: designed for **6 months**, it worked about **8 years**.
Statement 3 wrong: contact was lost in **2022**, not 2019.
xa: Launch: **5 Nov 2013**, **PSLV-C25**.
It used a **Hohmann transfer** to reach Mars.
It was the **lowest-cost** Mars mission.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Aditya-L1:
1. It is placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point.
2. The L1 point is about 1.5 million km from Earth.
3. It was launched on 25 January 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1, about 1.5 million km away. Statement 3 is wrong: Aditya-L1 launched on 2 Sep 2023 on PSLV-C57; halo-orbit insertion was 6 Jan 2024 (the 25 Jan 2024 date is a known error). Hence A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
41.tq: Launch 2 Sep 2023 (PSLV-C57); halo insertion 6 Jan 2024.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: Aditya-L1 is in a **halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1**.
Statement 2 correct: L1 is ~**1.5 million km** from Earth.
Statement 3 wrong: it launched on **2 Sep 2023** on **PSLV-C57**; "**25 January 2024**" is a known prep-app error.
xa: Halo-orbit insertion: **6 January 2024** (APPSC **2022** key).
L1 gives a **continuous view of the Sun**, with no occultation/eclipse.
It is India's **first space-based solar observatory**.

41.s: Aditya-L1 reached its halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point on
41.x: Aditya-L1 was inserted into its halo orbit on 6 January 2024. Its launch date was 2 September 2023.
41.tq: Apply the date-separation trap by distinguishing launch from orbit insertion.
xs: Aditya-L1 entered its halo orbit on **6 January 2024** — option **(1)**.
**2 September 2023** is its **launch** date (**PSLV-C57**); **25 January 2024** is a known wrong date.
**1 January 2024** is the launch date of **XPoSat**.
xa: The halo orbit is around **Sun-Earth L1**, ~**1.5 million km** from Earth.
More than **27 TB** of solar data have been released (Jun **2026**).
**7 payloads**: **4** remote sensing + **3** in-situ.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about the payloads of Aditya-L1:
1. It carries seven payloads: four remote-sensing and three in-situ.
2. ASPEX and PAPA are remote-sensing payloads that image the corona.
3. The magnetometer, an in-situ payload, measures the magnetic field.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statement 1 is correct: 7 payloads = 4 remote sensing + 3 in-situ. Statement 2 is wrong: ASPEX and PAPA are in-situ payloads studying solar-wind particles; VELC images the corona. Statement 3 is correct. Hence B; A and D include the false statement 2, C omits statement 1.
41.tq: In-situ = ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometer; corona = VELC.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **7 payloads** = **4 remote sensing + 3 in-situ**.
Statement 2 wrong: **ASPEX** and **PAPA** are **in-situ** payloads studying **solar wind**; **VELC** images the corona.
Statement 3 correct: the **magnetometer** (in-situ) measures the **magnetic field** (Bx, By, Bz).
xa: ASPEX: solar-wind **protons** and heavier ions; PAPA: solar-wind **electrons** and heavier ions.
Remote sensing: **VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS**.
⚠ **VELC** = IIA (corona); **SUIT** = IUCAA (photosphere, chromosphere).

41.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SUIT — Solar-wind electrons and heavier ions
41.x: VELC studies the solar corona through imaging and spectroscopy. SUIT studies the photosphere and chromosphere, ASPEX studies solar-wind protons and heavier ions, and HEL1OS is a hard X-ray spectrometer.
41.tq: Start with the payload whose study area is most directly associated with its name and function.
xs: **VELC — corona imaging and spectroscopy** is correct — option **(1)**.
**SUIT** studies the **photosphere and chromosphere**; **PAPA** (not SUIT) studies solar-wind electrons.
**ASPEX** studies solar-wind **protons** — the **magnetometer** measures the magnetic field; **HEL1OS** is a **hard X-ray** spectrometer.
xa: VELC was built by the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)**.
In the **2025 solar maximum**, VELC made the **first-ever spectroscopic observations of CMEs in visible wavelengths**.
**SoLEXS** is the **soft X-ray** spectrometer.

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Payload)
A. SUIT
B. SoLEXS
C. HEL1OS
D. Magnetometer

List-II (Function)
1. Soft X-ray spectroscopy
2. Magnetic-field measurement
3. Near-ultraviolet imaging of the solar disc
4. Hard X-ray spectroscopy
41.x: SUIT performs near-ultraviolet imaging, SoLEXS performs soft X-ray spectroscopy, HEL1OS performs hard X-ray spectroscopy, and the Magnetometer measures the magnetic field.
41.tq: Begin with the sure X-ray pair and then eliminate codes with reversed payload functions.
xs: **SUIT** – near-UV imaging; **SoLEXS** – soft X-ray; **HEL1OS** – hard X-ray; **Magnetometer** – magnetic field — option **(1) A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2**.
SUIT gives **near-UV full-disc images** of the **photosphere and chromosphere**.
xa: SUIT was built by **IUCAA**; **VELC** by **IIA**.
In-situ payloads: **ASPEX**, **PAPA**, **Magnetometer**.
Aditya-L1 has **7 payloads** in all.

41.s: Which of the following Aditya-L1 payloads was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics?
41.x: The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
41.tq: Test the institution–payload association rather than the scientific function alone.
xs: **VELC** (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) was built by the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)** — option **(3)**.
**SUIT** was built by **IUCAA**; **ASPEX** and **PAPA** are in-situ solar-wind payloads.
xa: VELC does **corona imaging and spectroscopy**.
It recorded the **first-ever spectroscopic observations of CMEs in visible wavelengths** (**2025**, IIA with NASA).
⚠ **VELC** = IIA; **SUIT** = IUCAA.

41.s: During the 2025 solar maximum, VELC recorded the first-ever spectroscopic observations of coronal mass ejections in
41.x: VELC recorded the first-ever spectroscopic observations of coronal mass ejections in visible wavelengths during the 2025 solar maximum.
41.tq: Focus on the exact wavelength rather than the general subject of solar observations.
xs: VELC recorded the first spectroscopic observations of CMEs in **visible wavelengths** — option **(1)** (**2025 solar maximum**).
The work was by **IIA with NASA**.
xa: VELC = **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph**, for **corona** imaging and spectroscopy.
Aditya-L1 has released more than **27 TB** of solar data (Jun **2026**).
X-ray work on Aditya-L1 is done by **SoLEXS** (soft) and **HEL1OS** (hard).

41.s: India's first space-based solar observatory is:
41.x: Aditya-L1 (PSLV-C57, 2 Sep 2023), stationed in a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1, is India's first space-based solar observatory. AstroSat is the first multi-wavelength space observatory, XPoSat the first X-ray polarimetry mission, and Mangalyaan the first interplanetary mission.
41.tq: First solar observatory = Aditya-L1; first multi-wavelength = AstroSat.
xs: **Aditya-L1** is India's **first space-based solar observatory** — option **(3)**.
**AstroSat** is the first **multi-wavelength** space observatory; **XPoSat** the first **polarimetry** mission; **Mangalyaan** the first **interplanetary** mission.
xa: Aditya-L1 launched on **2 Sep 2023** (**PSLV-C57**); halo orbit around **Sun-Earth L1**.
It carries **7 payloads** — **4** remote sensing + **3** in-situ.
L1 is ~**1.5 million km** from Earth.

41.s: AstroSat, launched in 2015 by PSLV-C30, is best described as
o: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory
41.x: AstroSat is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory.
41.tq: Distinguish the first observatory claim of AstroSat from the solar and polarimetry missions.
xs: **AstroSat** (**2015**, **PSLV-C30**) is India's **first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory** — option **(1)**.
The first **X-ray polarimetry** mission is **XPoSat**; the first **solar observatory** is **Aditya-L1**.
xa: AstroSat observes in **visible, ultraviolet and X-ray** bands.
Payloads: **UVIT, LAXPC, SXT, CZTI, SSM**.
Partners: **IUCAA, TIFR, IIA, RRI**.

41.s: Which of the following bands are observed by AstroSat?
41.x: AstroSat observes in the visible, ultraviolet and X-ray bands.
41.tq: Use the complete band combination instead of selecting a partial list.
xs: AstroSat observes in the **visible, ultraviolet and X-ray** bands — option **(3)**.
Microwave/radio and infrared/gamma-ray are not its listed bands.
xa: AstroSat launched on **28 Sept 2015** on **PSLV-C30**.
It is India's **first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory**.
**XPoSat** studies **X-ray polarization** of black holes and neutron stars.

41.s: XPoSat was launched on 1 January 2024 by which launch vehicle?
41.x: XPoSat was launched on 1 January 2024 aboard PSLV-C58.
41.tq: Separate the launch vehicles of AstroSat, Aditya-L1, XPoSat and NISAR.
xs: **XPoSat** was launched on **1 Jan 2024** by **PSLV-C58** — option **(4)**.
**PSLV-C57** launched **Aditya-L1**; **PSLV-C30** launched **AstroSat**; **GSLV-F16** launched **NISAR**.
xa: ⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated XPoSat **May 2023**.
XPoSat is India's **first polarimetry mission** and the **world's second** after NASA's **IXPE**.
Partner: **Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru**.

41.s:
Consider the following statements regarding XPoSat:
1. It is India's first X-ray polarimetry mission.
2. It is the world's second X-ray polarimetry mission after NASA's IXPE.
3. It studies the X-ray polarization of black holes and neutron stars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: All three statements are correct. XPoSat is India's first and the world's second X-ray polarimetry mission, after NASA's IXPE, and studies black holes and neutron stars.
41.tq: Check the national first, global rank and scientific target as three separate facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**XPoSat** is India's **first X-ray polarimetry mission** and the **world's second** after NASA's **IXPE**.
It studies the **X-ray polarization of black holes and neutron stars**.
xa: Launched **1 Jan 2024** on **PSLV-C58**.
Payloads: **POLIX** (by **RRI**) and **XSPECT** (by **URSC**).
⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated it **May 2023**.

41.s: The POLIX payload of XPoSat was developed by
o: Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics
41.x: POLIX was developed by the Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru.
41.tq: Use the payload–institution association and distinguish it from AstroSat's partner institutions.
xs: **POLIX** was built by the **Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru** — option **(3)**.
The other XPoSat payload, **XSPECT**, was built by **URSC** (U. R. Rao Space Centre).
**IUCAA** built Aditya-L1's **SUIT**; **IIA** built **VELC**.
xa: XPoSat launched on **1 Jan 2024** (**PSLV-C58**).
It is the world's **second** X-ray polarimetry mission after **IXPE**.
RRI is also among **AstroSat's** partner institutions.

41.s: The Venus Orbiter Mission, also known as Shukrayaan, is intended to enter orbit around
41.x: Shukrayaan, or the Venus Orbiter Mission, targets Venus. It is not a mission to Saturn.
41.tq: Use the mission name and target association to avoid the Venus–Saturn substitution trap.
xs: The **Venus Orbiter Mission (Shukrayaan)** targets **Venus** orbit — option **(1)**.
It does **not** target Saturn — APPSC-G1 **2022** keyed "none of the above" for that option.
xa: Cost: **₹1,236 crore**, approved by the **Union Cabinet**.
**ESA** is exploring complementary cooperation (**10 Sep 2026**).
Venus and Mars missions are part of the **Space Vision 2047** roadmap.

41.s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-4:
1. It is planned as a lunar sample-return mission.
2. Its landing site has been picked near Mons Mouton, close to the lunar south pole.
3. It is being developed with JAXA as a partner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Chandrayaan-4 is a sample-return mission (regolith and ice) with a site near Mons Mouton. Statement 3 is wrong: the JAXA partnership is Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX; Chandrayaan-4 is an ISRO frontier mission. Hence A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
41.tq: Ch-4 = sample return; Ch-5/LUPEX = with JAXA.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Chandrayaan-4** is a lunar **sample-return** mission (regolith + ice).
Statement 2 correct: **SAC** picked a landing site near **Mons Mouton**, a flat-topped mountain near the south pole.
Statement 3 wrong: the **JAXA** partnership is **Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX**; Chandrayaan-4 is an **ISRO** frontier mission.
xa: Chandrayaan-4's planned timeline is **2027**.
⚠ **Chandrayaan-4** = sample return (ISRO); **Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX** = with JAXA (water ice).
ISRO will focus on **Chandrayaan-4, BAS, Venus and Mars** missions.

41.s: NISAR is correctly described by which of the following statements?
o: It is a NASA–ISRO Earth-observation mission using L- and S-band SAR.
It is an ISRO–JAXA mission for lunar water-ice exploration.
It is a NASA–ISRO mission for X-ray polarimetry.
It is an ESA–ISRO mission for Venus orbit insertion.
41.x: NISAR is a NASA–ISRO Earth-observation mission using L- and S-band synthetic aperture radar to study climate and hazards.
41.tq: Match the agency partnership, observation target and radar bands as a combined identification test.
xs: **NISAR** is a **NASA-ISRO Earth-observation** mission using **L- and S-band SAR** — option **(1)**.
It studies **climate and hazards**.
Lunar water ice with JAXA is **LUPEX**; X-ray polarimetry is **XPoSat**; Venus orbit is **Shukrayaan**.
xa: NISAR was launched in **July 2025** on **GSLV-F16** — now operational, not upcoming.
**Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX** is with **JAXA (Japan)**.
**XPoSat** flew on **1 Jan 2024** (**PSLV-C58**).

41.s: Which of the following correctly represents the targets of the Indian Space Vision 2047?
o: Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2040 and an Indian on the Moon by 2035
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2047 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2030 and an Indian on the Moon by 2035
Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040
41.x: The vision envisages the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and placing an Indian on the Moon by 2040.
41.tq: Close-year discrimination between two linked national targets.
xs: **Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035** and **Indian landing on the Moon by 2040** — option **(4)**.
Options (1)–(3) mix up or misstate these two years.
xa: The roadmap also includes a **Venus mission** and **Mars again**.
**SpaDeX** docking (**16 Jan 2025**) is a step towards BAS.
India targets **50 launches a year** (**25 Aug 2026**).

41.s: ExoMars is primarily associated with the search for signs of life on which celestial body?
41.x: ExoMars is an ESA mission undertaken with Roscosmos involvement to search for signs of life on Mars.
41.tq: Directly identify the target body of a named mission.
xs: **ExoMars** searches for **signs of life on Mars** — option **(2)**.
It is an **ESA** mission (earlier with **Roscosmos**), with the **Rosalind Franklin** Mars rover.
**Europa** is NASA's **Europa Clipper** target; **16 Psyche** is NASA's **Psyche** target.
xa: Europa Clipper launched **Oct 2024**; Psyche launched **Oct 2023**.
India's **Mangalyaan** made it the **first Asian nation** in Mars orbit.
ISRO was the **4th space agency** to orbit Mars (after NASA, Roscosmos, ESA).

41.s:
Consider the following statements about China's Chang'e missions:
1. Chang'e-3 (2013) made the first soft landing on the Moon since 1976.
2. Chang'e-4 (2019) made the first far-side soft landing, with the rover Yutu-2.
3. Chang'e-6 (2024) returned samples from the near side of the Moon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
41.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Chang'e-6 was a far-side sample-return mission. Hence A; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
41.tq: Chang'e-4 = far-side landing; Chang'e-6 = far-side samples.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Chang'e-3 (2013)** made the **first soft landing since 1976**.
Statement 2 correct: **Chang'e-4 (2019)** made the **first far-side soft landing**, with rover **Yutu-2**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Chang'e-6 (2024)** was a **far-side** sample return, not near side.
xa: The Chang'e series belongs to **China (CNSA)**.
China soft-landed on the Moon before India — India was **4th** (after US, Russia, China).
China also runs **SuperView** commercial EO satellites.

41.s: Which one of the following statements about the Artemis missions is correct?
o: Artemis I was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test in 2022.
Artemis II was the first Artemis landing on the Moon.
Artemis III was the first uncrewed SLS-Orion test.
Artemis IV was completed as the first crewed lunar landing in 2024.
41.x: Artemis I was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test conducted in 2022. The stated programme plan places the Artemis III crewed Earth-orbit test in 2027 and the first Artemis landing attempt under Artemis IV in 2028.
41.tq: Trap the interchange of mission numbers and their assigned phases.
xs: **Artemis I** (**2022**) was an **uncrewed SLS-Orion test** — option **(1)**.
**Artemis II** (**2026**) flew the first crewed trip **around** the Moon in **50+** years — it did not land.
**Artemis III** (**2027**) is a crewed **LEO** test; **Artemis IV** (**2028**) is the **first Artemis landing** attempt.
xa: Artemis is NASA's programme to **return humans to the Moon**, restructured in **2026**.
India signed the **Artemis Accords** in **2023**.
Plan as of **16 Aug 2026**: Artemis III in Earth orbit, Artemis IV first landing.

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Mission/vehicle)
a. Europa Clipper
b. Psyche
c. SuperView
 d. Nuri

List-II (Target or purpose)
i. Commercial high-resolution Earth observation
 ii. Jupiter’s moon Europa
 iii. Metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche
 iv. South Korea’s indigenous launch vehicle

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
41.x: Europa Clipper targets Europa, Psyche targets asteroid 16 Psyche, SuperView provides commercial high-resolution Earth observation, and Nuri is South Korea’s indigenous launch vehicle.
41.tq: Begin with the distinctive target 16 Psyche and then complete the remaining pairs.
xs: **Europa Clipper** – Europa; **Psyche** – asteroid **16 Psyche**; **SuperView** – commercial high-res EO; **Nuri** – South Korea's launch vehicle — option **(1) a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv**.
Europa is **Jupiter's moon**; Psyche is a **metal-rich** asteroid.
xa: Europa Clipper launched **Oct 2024**; Psyche launched **Oct 2023**.
**Nuri (KSLV-II)** is the **first indigenous Korean launch vehicle**, reaching orbit in **2022**.
**SuperView** is Chinese.

41.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Moon Impact Probe — NASA’s 2009 polar-crater impactor
SLIM — Japan’s fifth-nation soft landing on the Moon
Luna-25 — Successful first Russian soft landing on the Moon in 2023
LCROSS — First spacecraft to hit the Moon in 1959
41.x: SLIM (2024) made Japan the 5th country to soft-land on the Moon with its 'Moon sniper' precision landing. The others are mismatched: India's MIP was the 2008 impact probe (NASA's LCROSS was the 2009 polar-crater impactor), Luna-25 (2023) crashed before landing, and Luna 2 (USSR, 1959) was the first to hit the Moon.
41.tq: Find the correctly matched mission and reject swapped dates, agencies and achievements.
xs: **SLIM** (**2024**) made **Japan** the **5th** country to soft-land on the Moon — option **(2)**; "**Moon sniper**" precision landing.
India's **MIP** hit the Moon in **2008**; NASA's **2009** polar-crater impactor was **LCROSS**.
**Luna-25** (**2023**) **crashed** before landing; the first to hit the Moon was **Luna 2** (USSR, **1959**).
xa: India was **4th** to soft-land (after US, Russia, China) and **1st** near the south pole.
Luna-25 crashed **days before** Chandrayaan-3 landed.
LCROSS impacted a polar crater **to find water**.

41.s: India signed the Artemis Accords, the NASA-led framework for lunar exploration, in:
41.x: India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023. 2019 (Chandrayaan-2), 2021 and 2025 are not the year of signing.
41.tq: Artemis Accords: India 2023.
xs: India signed the **Artemis Accords** in **2023** — option **(3)**.
**2019** is the year of **Chandrayaan-2**, not the Accords.
xa: **Artemis I** (**2022**) was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test.
**Artemis II** (**2026**) flew the first crewed trip around the Moon in **50+** years.
**Artemis IV** (**2028**) is planned as the first Artemis landing.

41.s:
The ISRO–ESA discussions held in Paris on 10 September 2026 were associated with which of the following initiatives?
1. Venus Orbiter Mission
2. Gaganyaan ground-tracking TIP
3. Chandrayaan-4 sample-return mission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
41.x: The Paris discussions concerned the Venus Orbiter Mission and the Gaganyaan ground-tracking TIP. Chandrayaan-4 was not identified as an agenda item of these discussions.
41.tq: Separate the specifically linked initiatives from the nearby missions mentioned in the wider space programme.
xs: The Paris talks covered the **Venus Orbiter Mission** and the **Gaganyaan ground-tracking TIP** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
**Chandrayaan-4** is an **ISRO** frontier mission and was not on the ISRO-ESA agenda.
xa: The talks were held on **10 Sep 2026**.
Venus Orbiter Mission: **₹1,236 crore**, approved by the Union Cabinet.
ESA is exploring **complementary cooperation** on the Venus mission.

41.s: As India targets a higher launch frequency, the proposed annual launch capacity is approximately:
41.x: India is targeting a capacity of 50 launches a year while focusing on Chandrayaan-4, BAS, and missions to Venus and Mars.
41.tq: Use the exact quantitative target rather than an approximate descriptive option.
xs: India targets **50 launches a year** — option **(1)** (**25 Aug 2026**).
ISRO will focus on **Chandrayaan-4, BAS, Venus and Mars** missions.
xa: Critics say ISRO is being "**weakened**"; the government says it is being **freed** for these missions.
India has launched **more than 400** foreign satellites.
All missions launch from **SDSC SHAR**, **Tirupati district**, AP.

41.s: All the missions discussed in this section were launched from which launch facility?
o: Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota
41.x: The missions were launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR at Sriharikota, located in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh.
41.tq: Identify the launch facility by distinguishing it from satellite centres and missile-test facilities.
xs: All the missions were launched from **Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota** — option **(1)**.
SDSC SHAR is in **Tirupati district, AP**.
xa: **Aditya-L1** (**PSLV-C57**) and **Chandrayaan-3** (**LVM3**) both flew from Sriharikota.
India is the **4th** country to dock in space (**SpaDeX**, **16 Jan 2025**).
India targets **50 launches a year**.

41.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists.

List-I (Mission)
A. Chandrayaan-3
B. Mangalyaan
C. Aditya-L1
D. XPoSat

List-II (Distinction)
1. First Indian solar observatory
2. First Indian polarimetry mission
3. First near-south-pole lunar landing
4. First maiden-attempt Mars orbit

Codes:
41.x: Chandrayaan-3 achieved the first near-south-pole landing; Mangalyaan achieved a Mars orbit on India’s maiden attempt; Aditya-L1 is India’s first solar observatory; and XPoSat is India’s first polarimetry mission.
41.tq: Start with the sure mission–distinction pairs and eliminate codes that reverse the firsts.
xs: **Ch-3** – near-south-pole landing; **Mangalyaan** – maiden-attempt Mars orbit; **Aditya-L1** – solar observatory; **XPoSat** – polarimetry — option **(1) A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**.
Ch-3 soft-landed on **23 Aug 2023** at **Shiv Shakti point**.
xa: Mangalyaan entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014**.
Aditya-L1 sits in a halo orbit around **Sun-Earth L1** (~**1.5 million km**).
XPoSat is the **world's second** X-ray polarimetry mission after **IXPE**.

41.s: Which of the following correctly describes India’s position in Mars exploration?
o: India was the first country to return samples from Mars.
India was the first Asian nation to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit.
India was the second Asian nation to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit.
India was the first country to land a rover on Mars.
41.x: India became the first Asian nation to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit through the Mars Orbiter Mission, also known as Mangalyaan.
41.tq: Distinguish the regional orbital achievement from more advanced landing and sample-return claims.
xs: India was the **first Asian nation** to place a spacecraft in **Mars orbit** — option **(2)**.
This was through **Mangalyaan (MOM)**, which also reached orbit on the **maiden attempt**.
MOM is an **orbiter** — it did not land a rover or return samples.
xa: MOM: launched **2013** on **PSLV-C25**; orbit insertion **24 September 2014**.
ISRO was the **4th space agency** to orbit Mars (after **NASA, Roscosmos, ESA**).
Designed for **6 months**, it worked about **8 years**.

41.s: India’s achievement of becoming the fourth country to dock in space was associated with which mission?
41.x: The SpaDeX mission made India the fourth country to achieve docking in space on 16 January 2025.
41.tq: Match the specific technological achievement with the mission designed for it.
xs: **SpaDeX** made India the **4th** country to dock in space — option **(1)** (**16 Jan 2025**).
**Aditya-L1**, **Mangalyaan** and **Chandrayaan-3** hold other firsts (solar observatory, Mars orbit, near-south-pole landing).
xa: SpaDeX was launched in **Dec 2024**.
Docking supports the **Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035**.
APPSC **2023** order: Ch-2 **Jul 2019** → Ch-3 **Jul 2023** → Aditya-L1 **Sep 2023** → SpaDeX **Dec 2024**.

42.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyaan programme:
1. It was approved in 2018 as India's first human spaceflight programme.
2. It aims to carry a crew of three to a 400 km low Earth orbit for a three-day mission.
3. The Crew Module is planned to return by a runway landing at Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
42.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gaganyaan, India's first human spaceflight programme, was approved in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: crew of 3, 400 km LEO, 3 days. Statement 3 is wrong: the Crew Module splashes down in Indian sea waters. Hence 1 and 2 only (B); A omits the correct statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
42.tq: Remember 2018 / 3 crew / 400 km / 3 days / sea splashdown; any land-recovery claim is the trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Gaganyaan**, India's **first human spaceflight programme**, was approved in **2018**.
Statement 2 is correct: the goal is a **crew of 3** to a **400 km LEO** for a **3-day** mission.
Statement 3 is wrong: the crew returns by **splashdown in Indian sea waters**, not a runway landing.
xa: The aim is to demonstrate human spaceflight to **LEO**.
Gaganyaan would make India the **4th** nation with its own crewed launch, after **USSR/Russia** (**1961**), **USA** and **China**.
**Gagarin** flew the first crewed launch on **Vostok** in **1961**.

42.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Gaganyaan component)

a. Orbital Module
b. Crew Module
c. Service Module

d. Human-rated LVM3

List-II (Function or description)

i. Provides on-orbit support and performs de-orbit manoeuvres
 ii. Injects the Orbital Module into orbit
 iii. Consists of the Crew Module and Service Module joined by a joint
 iv. Provides crew habitat and survives re-entry and splashdown

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
42.x: The Orbital Module consists of the Crew and Service Modules; the Crew Module houses the crew and survives re-entry; the Service Module provides on-orbit support and de-orbits the vehicle; and HLVM3 injects it into orbit.
42.tq: Start from the sure pair linking the launcher with orbital injection.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**Orbital Module (OM)** = **Crew Module + Service Module** joined by a joint.
**Crew Module** = crew habitat that survives re-entry, aero-brakes, uses parachutes and **splashes down in the sea**.
**Service Module** = on-orbit support; fires thrusters to **de-orbit** the OM; **HLVM3** injects the OM into orbit.
xa: After de-orbit, the Service Module **separates and burns up**.
⚠ Gaganyaan OM has **two** parts; **Soyuz** and **Shenzhou** use **three** modules (orbital, descent, service).
HLVM3 is the **human-rated LVM3**, launched from **Sriharikota**.

42.s:
With reference to the Gaganyaan modules, consider the following statements:
1. The Crew Module is double-walled and pressurised.
2. The Service Module fires thrusters to de-orbit the Orbital Module.
3. The Service Module remains attached during the entire splashdown operation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
42.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Service Module separates from the Orbital Module after the de-orbit operation and burns up; therefore, statement 3 is false.
42.tq: Find the false statement by checking the separation stage of the Service Module.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Crew Module** is **double-walled and pressurised**, for **3 crew**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Service Module** fires thrusters to **de-orbit** the Orbital Module.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Service Module then **separates and burns up**; only the Crew Module splashes down.
xa: The Crew Module survives re-entry, **aero-brakes**, then uses **parachutes** before splashdown.
The **Orbital Module** = Crew Module + Service Module joined by a joint.
The **IADT-02** test used a **5.7-tonne** module, equal to the **G1** crew-module mass.

42.s: Which of the following correctly describes the configuration used by Russia's Soyuz and China's Shenzhou spacecraft?
o: A two-module configuration consisting of crew and propulsion modules
A single integrated module without a separate service section
A four-module configuration consisting of orbital, laboratory, service and recovery modules
A three-module configuration consisting of orbital, descent and service modules
42.x: Both Soyuz and Shenzhou use a three-module configuration: orbital, descent and service modules.
42.tq: Compare the named spacecraft by matching their shared module structure.
xs: Russia's **Soyuz** and China's **Shenzhou** use a **three-module configuration** of **orbital, descent and service modules** — option **(4)**.
Gaganyaan's Orbital Module, by contrast, has only **two** parts: **Crew Module** + **Service Module**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Gaganyaan = **two** parts; Soyuz/Shenzhou = **three** modules.
The **USSR/Russia** made the first own crewed launch (**Gagarin**, **Vostok**, **1961**); **USA** and **China** followed.
China's own space station is **Tiangong** (**Tianhe** core + **Wentian** + **Mengtian**).

42.s: Which one of the following is the human-rated launch vehicle for the Gaganyaan mission?
42.x: Gaganyaan will use the human-rated LVM3, also referred to as HLVM3 or HRLV. The earlier GSLV Mk-III structures were redesigned for human rating.
42.tq: Apply the wrong-launcher trap by separating vehicle generations and variants.
xs: Gaganyaan will fly on the **Human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3 / HRLV)** from **Sriharikota** — option **(1)**.
**GSLV Mk-III** structures were redesigned for **human rating** to create it.
xa: The **Vikas** engine for the human-rated **L110** stage was qualified in **3 tests** (**730 s** total).
**LVM3** has had **6 flights**; **LVM3-M6** carried the **6,100 kg** BlueBird Block-2 — its heaviest payload.
Flight sequence: uncrewed **G1 → G2 → G3**, then crewed **H1**.

42.s: Which one of the following represents the present sequence of Gaganyaan missions?
42.x: The planned sequence is two or more uncrewed missions, G1 followed by G2 and G3, before the crewed H1 mission.
42.tq: Identify the uncrewed tests before the first crewed flight.
xs: The sequence is uncrewed **G1 → G2 → G3**, then the crewed **H1** — option **(1)**.
The crewed flight **H1** comes only after the uncrewed test flights, so options placing H1 earlier are wrong.
xa: The robot **Vyommitra** flies on the uncrewed **G1 and G2**.
**H1** is targeted for **Q1 2027** (LENS Sep 2025: "likely beyond **2027**").
The launch vehicle is the **HLVM3** from **Sriharikota**.

42.s: The current target for the first crewed Gaganyaan flight, designated H1, is:
42.x: The current target is H1 during the first quarter of 2027, although later assessments have indicated that it could slip beyond 2027.
42.tq: Distinguish the current target from earlier announced targets and later risk assessments.
xs: The current (**2026**) target for crewed **H1** is the **first quarter of 2027** — option **(4)**.
A LENS assessment of **Sep 2025** said it was "likely beyond **2027**".
xa: The **2018** announcement targeted **December 2021**; later notes said **2023**.
⚠ Trap: always quote a target date with the date of the statement — repeated slippage (**2021 → 2023 → 2027**).
Sequence before H1: uncrewed **G1 → G2 → G3**.

42.s: When Gaganyaan was announced in 2018, the first crewed flight was targeted for:
42.x: The 2018 announcement set December 2021 for the first crewed flight (PYQ 2018); it later slipped to 2023 and now H1 is targeted for Q1 2027. 2019 was never the target, Q1 2027 is the current (2026) target, and August 2025 was IADT-01.
42.tq: Quote dates with the statement year: 2018 -> Dec 2021; now Q1 2027.
xs: The **2018** announcement targeted **December 2021** for the first crewed flight — option **(1)** (PYQ **2018**).
It later slipped to **2023**; **Q1 2027** is the current (2026) target for **H1**.
**August 2025** was the **IADT-01** air-drop test, not a crewed-flight target.
xa: Original target window was **2021-23**; the slippage makes dates unreliable exam facts.
⚠ Quote only milestones that have actually happened, e.g. **TV-D1** (**18 Oct 2023**).
Gaganyaan was **approved in 2018**.

42.s: The TV-D1 test of the Gaganyaan programme was conducted on:
42.x: TV-D1 flew on 18 Oct 2023 and proved the in-flight abort of the Crew Escape System at Mach 1.2. 24 Aug 2025 was IADT-01, 10 Apr 2026 was IADT-02 and 3 Jul 2026 was the SOLVE ground test.
42.tq: Separate the first abort test date from the later integrated air-drop and ground tests.
xs: **TV-D1** flew on **18 October 2023** — option **(1)**.
xa: TV-D1 proved the in-flight abort of the **Crew Escape System** at **Mach 1.2**, with crew module separation and sea recovery.
**CARE** (**18 Dec 2014**, LVM3-X) tested crew module re-entry.
**TV-D2** (abort test-2) is still to come.

42.s: What did the TV-D1 mission demonstrate?
o: Only the docking of two spacecraft in orbit
Deployment of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station
In-flight crew escape at Mach 1.2, crew-module separation and sea recovery
42.x: TV-D1 demonstrated an in-flight abort of the Crew Escape System at Mach 1.2, followed by crew-module separation and sea recovery.
42.tq: Identify the mission by its demonstrated safety sequence and speed.
xs: **TV-D1** demonstrated **in-flight crew escape at Mach 1.2**, **crew-module separation and sea recovery** — option **(3)**.
Docking was shown by **SpaDeX** (**16 Jan 2025**), not TV-D1; **BAS** is not yet deployed (first module **2028**).
xa: TV-D1 flew on **18 Oct 2023**; TV-D1 and all Gaganyaan launches are at **Sriharikota (AP)**.
**TV-D2** is the next abort test, still to come.
**Indian on the Moon by 2040** is only a Space Vision **2047** goal.

42.s:
Match the test with its distinguishing feature:

A. IADT-01
B. IADT-02
C. CARE
D. SOLVE

1. Crew-module re-entry
2. 4.8-tonne dummy module dropped from 3 km
3. Solid-motor ground test for lofting the module to 10–17 km
4. 5.7-tonne module with ten parachutes of four types

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
42.x: IADT-01 involved the 4.8-tonne dummy module, IADT-02 the 5.7-tonne module and ten parachutes, CARE tested re-entry, and SOLVE tested the solid motor.
42.tq: Start with CARE–re-entry and SOLVE–solid motor, then resolve the two air-drop tests.
xs: Correct match: **A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3** — option **(1)**.
**IADT-01** (**24 Aug 2025**): **4.8-tonne** dummy module dropped from **3 km** by an IAF **Chinook**.
**IADT-02** (**10 Apr 2026**): **5.7-tonne** module, **10 parachutes of 4 types**.
**CARE** (**18 Dec 2014**) = crew-module **re-entry**; **SOLVE** (**3 Jul 2026**) = solid-motor ground test to loft the module to **10-17 km**.
xa: SOLVE's solid motor is derived from **PSLV strap-ons**.
IADT-02 was recovered with the **Navy**.
July **2026** qualification tests: **Crew Module Uprighting System** (cold gas), apex cover separation.

42.s: Which of the following statements about Vyommitra is correct?
o: It is the parachute recovery system of the Crew Escape System.
It is an unmanned Chinese space station module.
It is a male humanoid robot planned only for the crewed mission.
It is an AI-enabled female-form half-humanoid robot planned to fly on uncrewed G1 and G2.
42.x: Vyommitra is an AI-enabled, female-form semi-humanoid robot intended to fly on the uncrewed G1 and G2 missions before the crewed flight.
42.tq: Use the robot’s form, artificial intelligence and mission sequence to reject look-alike descriptions.
xs: **Vyommitra** is an **AI-enabled semi-humanoid (female) robot** to fly on uncrewed **G1 and G2** — option **(4)**.
It is not "male" and not only for the crewed mission — it flies **before** the crewed flight.
xa: ⚠ Trap: an **APPSC 2022** statement calling it a "male robot" was false.
Sequence: **G1 → G2 → G3 → H1** (crewed).
Parachute recovery of the **Crew Escape System** was tested by **DRDO**.

42.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the Gaganyaan test sequence?
o: TV-D2 was completed before TV-D1 in the test series.
TV-D2 is the second abort test and is yet to come.
TV-D1 demonstrated an in-flight abort and sea recovery.
DRDO tested the parachute recovery system of the Crew Escape System.
42.x: TV-D2 is the second abort test and was still to come; it had not been completed before TV-D1. DRDO tested the parachute recovery system, while TV-D1 demonstrated abort and sea recovery.
42.tq: Find the reversed sequence in the statement about the two abort tests.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that **TV-D2 was completed before TV-D1** — option **(1)**.
**TV-D2** (abort test-2) is the next test and is **still to come**.
**TV-D1** (**18 Oct 2023**) did prove in-flight abort and **sea recovery**; **DRDO** did test the crew escape parachute recovery.
xa: TV-D1's abort was at **Mach 1.2**.
**IADT-02** (**10 Apr 2026**) used **10 parachutes of 4 types**.
**Drogue parachute tests** (Feb **2026**) used **ribbon parachutes**.

42.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of the four Gaganyatris named in February 2024?
o: Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Pankaj M. Sinha, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
Ajit Krishnan, Pankaj M. Sinha, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Pankaj M. Sinha and Angad Pratap
Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
42.x: The four Gaganyatris named in February 2024 were Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla. Pankaj M. Sinha is not one of them.
42.tq: Eliminate the option containing the non-member of the named group.
xs: The four **Gaganyatris** are **Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla** — option **(4)**.
**Pankaj M. Sinha** is not a Gaganyatri, which rules out options (1), (2) and (3).
xa: They were named in **February 2024**; all are **Indian Air Force test pilots**.
Nair, Krishnan and Pratap were **Group Captains**; Shukla was a **Wing Commander** (later Group Captain).
PYQ: **APPSC-G1 2024** key: I, II, IV, V.

42.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of basic astronaut training for the Gaganyatris?
o: ISRO facility, Bengaluru → NASA → Yuri Gagarin Centre, Russia
Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia → ISRO Astronaut Training Facility, Bengaluru
IAF Institute of Aerospace Medicine, Leh → ESA facility → ISRO facility, Bengaluru
NASA → Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia → Sriharikota
42.x: The basic training sequence included the Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Russia followed by ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility in Bengaluru.
42.tq: Follow the training locations in their stated order rather than selecting a familiar agency.
xs: Basic training went from the **Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia** to **ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility, Bengaluru** — option **(2)**.
Selection came first at the IAF **Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM)**, **Bengaluru** — not Leh.
xa: **Shukla** (prime) + **Nair** (backup) trained in the **US** for **Axiom-4**; **NASA** has also trained the candidates.
Behavioural study: **Mission MITRA** at **Leh**.
**ESA** supports with ground-station tracking (**10 Sep 2026**).

42.s: Which institution conducted the selection and aeromedical testing of the Gaganyaan astronaut candidates?
o: IAF Institute of Aerospace Medicine, Bengaluru
Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre, Russia
42.x: The IAF Institute of Aerospace Medicine in Bengaluru conducted the selection and aeromedical testing of the astronaut candidates.
42.tq: Match the institutional responsibility with the correct agency and location.
xs: The IAF **Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM)**, **Bengaluru** did the selection and **aeromedical testing** — option **(1)**.
**Yuri Gagarin Centre, Russia** gave **basic training**; **HSFC** is in **Bengaluru**, not Sriharikota.
xa: IAM also runs aeromedical training and **Mission MITRA** at **Leh**.
**HSFC** is the new ISRO vertical that leads Gaganyaan.
**DRDO** gives parachutes, life-support and crew-recovery inputs.

42.s: Which of the following statements regarding the specialised training of Shubhanshu Shukla and Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair is correct?
o: Shukla was the prime astronaut and Nair the backup for Axiom-4 training in the United States.
Nair was the prime astronaut and Shukla was not included in the Axiom-4 training.
Shukla was the backup and Nair was the prime astronaut for Axiom-4 training.
