42.s: Which of the following countries had its own crewed space-launch capability before the proposed Gaganyaan mission?
42.x: The USSR/Russia, the United States and China had their own crewed launch capability. Gaganyaan would make India the fourth country in this group.
42.tq: Distinguish existing crewed-launch nations from India’s proposed capability.
xs: **China** already had its own crewed launch capability — option **(4)**.
The order is **USSR/Russia** (1st, **Gagarin**, **Vostok**, **1961**), **USA** (2nd), **China** (3rd).
**India** is not yet in the list — Gaganyaan would make it the **4th**; Canada and Japan are not listed.
xa: Gaganyaan aims at a **crew of 3** to **400 km LEO** for **3 days**.
⚠ Separately, **SpaDeX** (**16 Jan 2025**) made India the **4th** nation to **dock** in space.
Gaganyaan was approved in **2018**.

42.s: The Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) is planned as a:
o: Modular space station in Low Earth Orbit
42.x: BAS is India’s planned modular space station in Low Earth Orbit.
42.tq: Distinguish the station’s location and architecture from other space infrastructure.
xs: **BAS** is India's planned **modular space station in Low Earth Orbit** — option **(3)**.
It was approved by the Union Cabinet in **September 2024**.
xa: First module **BAS-1**: **2028**; full station: **BAS by 2035**.
⚠ A lunar goal is separate: **Indian on the Moon by 2040** (Space Vision **2047**).
Precursors: **SpaDeX**, **Axiom-4**, **Gaganyaan**.

42.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a precursor or supporting mission for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station roadmap?
42.x: SpaDeX, Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan are identified as precursor missions for the BAS roadmap. TV-D1 is a Gaganyaan abort test, not listed as a BAS precursor mission.
42.tq: Separate named precursor missions from an associated but differently classified test.
xs: **TV-D1** is not listed as a BAS precursor — option **(4)**.
The listed precursors are **SpaDeX** (docking), **Axiom-4** (crew experience) and **Gaganyaan** (crew vehicle + technologies).
TV-D1 (**18 Oct 2023**) was a Gaganyaan **Crew Escape System** abort test.
xa: **SpaDeX**: **PSLV-C60**, launched **30 Dec 2024**, docked **16 Jan 2025**.
SpaDeX made India the **4th** nation to dock in space.
BAS-1 is targeted for **2028**.

42.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS):
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024.
2. Its first module, BAS-1, is targeted for 2028.
3. The full station is targeted for completion by 2040.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
42.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Cabinet approved BAS in September 2024 and BAS-1 is targeted for 2028. Statement 3 is wrong: the full station is targeted by 2035; 2040 is the target for an Indian landing on the Moon. So '1 and 2 only'; the other options include statement 3 or drop a true one.
42.tq: BAS: approved Sep 2024, BAS-1 2028, full 2035; Moon 2040.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The Union Cabinet approved **BAS** in **September 2024**; **BAS-1** is targeted for **2028**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the full station is targeted **by 2035**; **2040** is for an **Indian on the Moon**.
xa: The Moon target comes from **Space Vision 2047**.
BAS will be a **modular** station in **LEO**.
**Axiom-4** gave crew experience for the BAS roadmap.

42.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the locations associated with the Gaganyaan programme:
1. TV-D1 was conducted at Sriharikota.
2. Both air-drop tests were conducted at Sriharikota.
3. All Gaganyaan launches are associated with Sriharikota.
4. The proposed Third Launch Pad is located at Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
42.x: TV-D1, both air-drop tests, all Gaganyaan launches and the Third Launch Pad are associated with Sriharikota.
42.tq: Check whether all statements refer to the same launch-site location before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**TV-D1**, both **air-drop tests** and **all Gaganyaan launches** are at **Sriharikota (AP)**.
The **Third Launch Pad** is also at Sriharikota.
xa: **IADT-01** was conducted at **SDSC-SHAR**.
TLP: Cabinet approval **January 2025**, about **₹4,000 crore**, for **NGLV** and human spaceflight.
India's **first private launch pad**, **Dhanush** (Agnikul Cosmos), is also at Sriharikota.

42.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Integrated Air Drop Tests is correct?
o: IADT-01 was the SOLVE solid-motor ground test conducted on 3 July 2026.
IADT-01 was conducted at Leh, whereas IADT-02 was associated with July 2026.
IADT-01 was conducted at SDSC-SHAR, whereas IADT-02 was associated with April 2026.
Both IADT-01 and IADT-02 were conducted in Paris as part of ESA-ISRO talks.
42.x: IADT-01 was conducted at SDSC-SHAR, and IADT-02 was associated with April 2026. The other options confuse locations or different tests.
42.tq: Separate similarly named tests by their individual location and date.
xs: **IADT-01** was conducted at **SDSC-SHAR**, while **IADT-02** was in **April 2026** — option **(3)**.
The **3 July 2026** test was **SOLVE**, a solid-motor ground test — not IADT-01.
xa: **IADT-01** (**24 Aug 2025**): **4.8-tonne** dummy module dropped from **3 km** by IAF **Chinook**.
**IADT-02** (**10 Apr 2026**): **5.7-tonne** module, **10 parachutes of 4 types**, recovered with the Navy.
**ESA** agreed tracking support (**10 Sep 2026**).

42.s: The sequence of projected Gaganyaan launch years that reflects the repeated slippage referred to in programme debates is:
42.x: The sequence cited is 2021, followed by 2023 and then 2027, illustrating repeated slippage.
42.tq: Arrange the successive projected years in chronological order before interpreting the programme trend.
xs: The slippage runs **2021 → 2023 → 2027** — option **(1)**.
The **2018** announcement targeted **December 2021**, later notes **2023**, and now **H1** is targeted for **Q1 2027**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: quote any date with the date of the statement — exam keys differ by year.
LENS (Sep **2025**) said H1 is "likely beyond **2027**".
Quote only milestones that have actually happened.

43.s: GSAT-7A, also known as 'Angry Bird', is primarily associated with which service and capability?
o: Indian Air Force; network-centric warfare and drone operations
43.x: GSAT-7A serves the Indian Air Force and supports network-centric warfare and drone operations.
43.tq: Match the military satellite nickname with its service user and role.
xs: **GSAT-7A** (**2018**), "**Angry Bird**", serves the **Indian Air Force** for **network-centric warfare and drone operations** — option **(4)**.
**GSAT-7** ("Rukmini") is the **Navy**'s; **GSAT-7B** is proposed for the **Army**; **EMISAT** (DRDO) does **ELINT**.
xa: ⚠ **Rukmini** = Navy (GSAT-7); **Angry Bird** = Air Force (GSAT-7A).
**GSAT-7R (CMS-03)** replaces GSAT-7 for the Navy.
**Cartosat** also gives high-resolution border imagery.

43.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5.
2. GSAT-7 provides secure naval communication and maritime surveillance.
3. GSAT-7R, also designated CMS-03, is intended for the Indian Navy.
4. GSAT-7B is associated with the Indian Army.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All four statements are correct. GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7R/CMS-03 is its naval replacement, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
43.tq: Verify each service assignment and operational feature before selecting the full code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**GSAT-7** (**2013**, "Rukmini") was launched by **Ariane-5** for secure **naval communication** and **maritime surveillance**.
**GSAT-7R (CMS-03)** replaces GSAT-7 for the **Indian Navy**; **GSAT-7B** is proposed for the **Indian Army**.
xa: GSAT-7R was launched on **2 Nov 2025** on **LVM3-M5**.
**GSAT-7A** (**2018**, "Angry Bird") = **Indian Air Force**.
**EMISAT** (**2019**, DRDO) = ELINT; launched on **PSLV-C45**.

43.s: GSAT-7R, also designated CMS-03, was launched on which vehicle and date?
43.x: GSAT-7R, or CMS-03, was launched on LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025 as a replacement for GSAT-7 in naval service.
43.tq: Match the replacement satellite with its precise launch vehicle and date.
xs: **GSAT-7R (CMS-03)** was launched on **LVM3-M5** on **2 November 2025** — option **(4)**.
**GSLV-F01** (**20 September 2004**) launched **EDUSAT**; **PSLV-C45** launched **EMISAT**.
xa: GSAT-7R **replaces GSAT-7** for the **Indian Navy**.
GSAT-7 ("Rukmini", **2013**) went up on **Ariane-5**.
**GSAT-7B** for the **Army** is proposed (APPCA **2026**).

43.s: EMISAT is associated with which organisation and function?
43.x: EMISAT is associated with DRDO and performs electronic intelligence (ELINT). It was launched by PSLV-C45 in 2019.
43.tq: Distinguish the defence user organisation from the armed-service satellite operators.
xs: **EMISAT** (**2019**) belongs to **DRDO** and does **electronic intelligence (ELINT)** — option **(4)**.
Drone operations are **GSAT-7A**'s (IAF); maritime communication is **GSAT-7**'s (Navy); classrooms are **EDUSAT**'s.
xa: EMISAT was launched on **PSLV-C45**.
**RISAT-2** series gives the armed forces **radar surveillance** of borders.
⚠ **DSA** = tri-service agency; **DSRO** = its R&D arm.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the RISAT series:
1. RISAT stands for Radar Imaging Satellite and carries a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR).
2. RISAT satellites can image through clouds, but only during daytime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statement 1 is correct: RISAT = Radar Imaging Satellite, carrying SAR. Statement 2 is wrong: SAR images both day and night as well as through clouds (all-weather). Hence 1 only (A); B and C accept the false daytime-only claim, D rejects the correct statement 1.
43.tq: Radar is active sensing: all-weather and day-night; any 'only daytime' limit is the trap.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **RISAT** = **Radar Imaging Satellite**, carrying **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)**.
Statement 2 is wrong: SAR images **day and night** as well as **through clouds** (all-weather).
xa: **RISAT-1** (**2012**) = India's **first fully indigenous** radar imaging satellite, **C-band (5.35 GHz)**.
⚠ **RISAT-2** (**2009**, X-band, Israeli-built) flew **before** RISAT-1.
ISRO has moved to **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.

43.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
43.x: RISAT-2BR1 was launched by PSLV-C48 in December 2019. RISAT-2, RISAT-1 and RISAT-2B were associated with PSLV-C12, PSLV-C19 and PSLV-C46 respectively.
43.tq: Start from the sure launcher-satellite pair.
xs: **RISAT-2BR1 — PSLV-C48** is correct — option **(3)**.
**RISAT-2** flew on **PSLV-C12**, **RISAT-1** on **PSLV-C19**, **RISAT-2B** on **PSLV-C46** — so the other pairs are wrong.
**PSLV-C61** was the failed **EOS-09 (RISAT-1B)** launch.
xa: RISAT-2BR1 (**Dec 2019**) was the **50th flight of PSLV**, with **9** foreign commercial satellites.
It serves **agriculture, forestry and disaster management**.
Exam angle: launcher pairs **RISAT-1/PSLV-C19**, **RISAT-2BR1/PSLV-C48**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RISAT series:
1. RISAT-2 used an X-band radar and was built with Israeli involvement.
2. RISAT-1 carried a C-band SAR operating at 5.35 GHz.
3. RISAT-2B was intended for X-band surveillance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. RISAT-2 used X-band radar, RISAT-1 used C-band SAR at 5.35 GHz, and RISAT-2B was an X-band surveillance satellite.
43.tq: Check each technical specification independently before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**RISAT-2** (**2009**) = **X-band**, **Israeli-built**.
**RISAT-1** (**2012**) = **C-band (5.35 GHz)** SAR; **RISAT-2B** (**May 2019**) = **X-band** surveillance.
xa: ⚠ RISAT-2 flew **before** RISAT-1.
**EOS-09 (RISAT-1B)** = **C-band**, **1,696 kg**, lost on **PSLV-C61**.
**EOS-01** = RISAT-2BR2 (**Nov 2020**, PSLV-C49).

43.s: RISAT-2 was associated with which of the following combinations of purpose and co-passenger?
o: Border surveillance, anti-terror operations and flood monitoring, with ANUSAT as co-passenger
43.x: RISAT-2 supported border surveillance, anti-terror activities and flood monitoring. ANUSAT was its co-passenger.
43.tq: Match the satellite with its operational role and co-passenger.
xs: **RISAT-2** was for **border surveillance, anti-terror operations and floods**, with **ANUSAT** as co-passenger — option **(2)**.
**EMISAT** does ELINT and **EDUSAT** education — not RISAT-2.
xa: RISAT-2 (**2009**) flew on **PSLV-C12**; it is **X-band**, **Israeli-built**.
**ANUSAT** (**Anna University**) = **first satellite built by an Indian university**.
RISAT-2 series is used by the armed forces for border radar surveillance.

43.s: RISAT-2BR1 provided services particularly relevant to which sectors?
o: Deep-space astronomy, navigation and television broadcasting
Manned spaceflight, meteorology and ocean mining
43.x: RISAT-2BR1 provided services for agriculture, forestry and disaster management.
43.tq: Link the satellite’s remote-sensing capability with its stated application sectors.
xs: **RISAT-2BR1** provides services for **agriculture, forestry and disaster management** — option **(4)**.
It was launched in **Dec 2019** on **PSLV-C48**.
xa: It was the **50th flight of PSLV**, with **9 foreign commercial satellites**.
**EOS-01** (RISAT-2BR2) followed in **Nov 2020** on **PSLV-C49**.
RISAT carries **SAR** — imaging day and night, through clouds.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about EOS-09:
1. It was formerly designated RISAT-1B.
2. It carried a C-band SAR and had a mass of 1,696 kg.
3. It was successfully placed in orbit by PSLV-C61.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: EOS-09 was formerly RISAT-1B, carried a C-band SAR and weighed 1,696 kg. The PSLV-C61 mission failed after a pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor, so statement 3 is false.
43.tq: Find the false outcome statement in an otherwise correct technical description.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**EOS-09** was **RISAT-1B**, carrying a **C-band** SAR with mass **1,696 kg**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **PSLV-C61 failed** after a **pressure drop** in the **third-stage** solid motor.
xa: **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1** (**12 Jan 2026**) also failed — a **roll-rate disturbance** at the end of the third stage.
Two consecutive PSLV failures (C61, C62) hit **surveillance satellites**.
ISRO now uses **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.

43.s: In 2019, RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using data from which system?
43.x: RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using NETRA data.
43.tq: Match the space-safety operation with the system that supplied the tracking data.
xs: **RISAT-2B** used **NETRA** data for its **2019** collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite — option **(4)**.
The other systems are not linked to this manoeuvre in the notes.
xa: RISAT-2B (**May 2019**) flew on **PSLV-C46** for **X-band** surveillance.
**RISAT-2BR1** followed in **Dec 2019** on **PSLV-C48**.
RISAT carries **SAR**: all-weather, day-and-night imaging.

43.s: India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite, RISAT-1 (2012), was launched by:
43.x: RISAT-1, carrying a C-band (5.35 GHz) SAR, was launched by PSLV-C19 in 2012. PSLV-C12 carried the X-band RISAT-2 (2009), PSLV-C48 RISAT-2BR1 (2019) and PSLV-C61 failed with EOS-09/RISAT-1B (2025).
43.tq: RISAT-1/PSLV-C19, C-band, first indigenous; RISAT-2/PSLV-C12, X-band, Israeli.
xs: **RISAT-1** (**2012**) was launched by **PSLV-C19** — option **(2)**.
**PSLV-C12** carried **RISAT-2** (**2009**), **PSLV-C48** carried **RISAT-2BR1**, and **PSLV-C61** failed with **EOS-09**.
xa: RISAT-1 carries a **C-band (5.35 GHz)** SAR.
⚠ RISAT-2 (X-band, Israeli-built) flew **before** RISAT-1 (C-band, indigenous).
**EOS-09** was named **RISAT-1B**.

43.s:
With reference to the SBS-3 programme, consider the following statements:
1. It envisages 52 satellites.
2. Of these, 21 satellites are to be developed by ISRO and 31 by private industry.
3. The programme was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security in November 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: SBS-3 comprises 52 satellites, including 21 by ISRO and 31 by private industry. Its approval by the Cabinet Committee on Security was obtained in November 2024.
43.tq: Use the all-inclusive code only after checking each numerical and date-based statement.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**SBS-3** has **52 satellites**: **21 by ISRO**, **31 by private industry**.
It was approved by the **CCS** in **November 2024**, costing **₹25,221.75 crore**.
xa: Cost sharing: **Army, Navy, Air Force 20% each**; **NTRO and ARC 15% each**; **MHA 10%**.
**DSA** ran the first tri-services space exercise **Antariksha Abhyas-2024**.
**DSRO** = DSA's R&D arm.

43.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Defence Space Agency (DSA):
1. It is a tri-service agency.
2. It was established in 2019 at Bengaluru.
3. It conducted the first tri-services space exercise, Antariksha Abhyas-2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: The DSA is a tri-service agency established at Bengaluru in 2019. It conducted the first tri-services space exercise named Antariksha Abhyas-2024.
43.tq: Verify the organisation, location, year and named exercise before selecting the combined code.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **Defence Space Agency (DSA)** is a **tri-service** agency set up in **2019** at **Bengaluru**.
It ran the **first tri-services space exercise "Antariksha Abhyas-2024"**.
xa: ⚠ **DSA** = agency (runs exercises); **DSRO** = its R&D arm.
**SBS-3**: **52 satellites**, CCS approval **November 2024**.
**MHA** bears **10%** of SBS-3 cost.

43.s: The Defence Space Research Organisation (DSRO) primarily functions as:
o: The research and development arm developing space-warfare systems and technologies for the DSA
The launch-control agency for all civilian PSLV missions
The commercial arm for marketing satellite services
The regulatory authority for private communication satellites
43.x: DSRO is the R&D arm associated with the Defence Space Agency and develops space-warfare systems and technologies for it.
43.tq: Identify the correct institutional role by matching the body with its specialised function.
xs: **DSRO** is the **R&D arm** that develops **space-warfare systems and technologies** for the **DSA** — option **(1)**.
It is not a launch, commercial or regulatory body.
xa: **DSA**: tri-service agency (**2019**, **Bengaluru**).
DSA ran **Antariksha Abhyas-2024**.

43.s: Which of the following correctly describes EDUSAT?
o: It was a navigation satellite providing civilian positioning services.
It was India's first satellite dedicated to education and enabled two-way satellite communication with classrooms.
It was India's first radar imaging satellite for border surveillance.
It was a military communication satellite used exclusively by the Navy.
43.x: GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT, was India's first satellite dedicated to education and provided two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
43.tq: Identify the satellite from its distinctive national first and principal purpose.
xs: **EDUSAT (GSAT-3)** was India's **first satellite dedicated to education**, giving **two-way satellite communication to classrooms** — option **(2)**.
India's first indigenous radar satellite was **RISAT-1**; the Navy's satellite is **GSAT-7**.
xa: Launched **20 September 2004** on **GSLV-F01** from **SHAR, Sriharikota**.
Lift-off mass **1,950.5 kg**; geostationary at **74 degrees E**.
Users: schools, colleges, distance-education networks (**virtual classrooms**).

43.s: EDUSAT was launched on which date and launch vehicle?
43.x: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01 from Sriharikota.
43.tq: Match the educational satellite with its exact launch date and vehicle.
xs: **EDUSAT** was launched on **20 September 2004** by **GSLV-F01** — option **(3)**.
**PSLV-C37** (**15 Feb 2017**) was the **104-satellite** record; **LVM3-M5** (**2 Nov 2025**) carried **GSAT-7R**.
xa: EDUSAT = **GSAT-3**; launched from **SHAR, Sriharikota**.
Mass **1,950.5 kg**; geostationary at **74 degrees E**.
⚠ **GSAT-1** was the first GSLV payload (**2001**) — not a student satellite.

43.s: Which satellite was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students?
43.x: WESAT, built by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women in Kerala, was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students.
43.tq: Distinguish the women-student first from the satellite involving 750 girl students.
xs: **WESAT** was the **first Indian satellite fully built by women students** — option **(4)** (PYQ).
It was built by **LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala)**.
**StudSat** = first pico-satellite; **SATYABAMASAT** = greenhouse-gas data; **AzaadiSAT** = girl students, failed.
xa: WESAT flew on **PSLV-C58 POEM-3** (**Jan 2024**) and measures **solar UV**.
⚠ **AzaadiSAT** (**750 girl students**, **SSLV-D1**, failed) vs **WESAT** (women students, flew).
**ANUSAT** = first university satellite.

43.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-1 was a student satellite.
2. GSAT-1 was the first GSLV payload.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: GSAT-1 was not a student satellite; it was the first GSLV payload in 2001. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct.
43.tq: Use the explicit exception to reject a tempting classification.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **GSAT-1** is **not** a student satellite (PYQ).
Statement 2 is correct: GSAT-1 was the **first GSLV payload** (**2001**).
xa: First university satellite: **ANUSAT** (**Anna University**, **2009**).
First pico-satellite: **StudSat** (**2010**).
**EDUSAT** flew on **GSLV-F01** (**2004**).

43.s: Which one of the following was India's first pico-satellite?
43.x: StudSat, developed by a consortium of seven engineering colleges from Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, was India's first pico-satellite.
43.tq: Distinguish the satellite’s class milestone from institutional milestones.
xs: **StudSat** was **India's first pico-satellite** — option **(2)**.
It was built by a **consortium of 7 engineering colleges** (Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh); launched **2010** on **PSLV-C15**.
**Jugnu** (IIT Kanpur) is a **nano-satellite**; **ANUSAT** is the first university satellite; **Kalamsat-V2** first used the **PS4 stage**.
xa: AP angle: the StudSat consortium included colleges from **undivided Andhra Pradesh**.
**Jugnu** and **SRMSAT** shared **PSLV-C18** (**2011**).
All these satellites launched from **Sriharikota**.

43.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Satellite)
A. Jugnu
B. SRMSAT
C. SATYABAMASAT
D. Kalamsat-V2

List-II (Institution)
1. Sathyabama University
2. IIT Kanpur
3. SRM University
4. Space Kidz India

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
43.x: Jugnu was built by IIT Kanpur, SRMSAT by SRM University, SATYABAMASAT by Sathyabama University and Kalamsat-V2 by Space Kidz India.
43.tq: Start with the distinctive institution-satellite pairs and eliminate codes.
xs: Correct match: **A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**Jugnu** = **IIT Kanpur**; **SRMSAT** = **SRM University**; **SATYABAMASAT** = **Sathyabama University**; **Kalamsat-V2** = **Space Kidz India**.
xa: ⚠ Jugnu and SRMSAT = same launcher (**PSLV-C18**, **2011**).
SATYABAMASAT (**2016**, **PSLV-C34**) gave **greenhouse-gas** data.
Kalamsat-V2 flew on **PSLV-C44** (**Jan 2019**).

43.s: Kalamsat-V2 is notable for which of the following?
o: It was India's first satellite built by an Indian university.
It was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite.
It was the first satellite to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest satellite of its kind mentioned here.
It was the first satellite dedicated to education.
43.x: Kalamsat-V2, built by Space Kidz India and launched on PSLV-C44 in January 2019, was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest.
43.tq: Identify the unique first associated with the satellite rather than its builder.
xs: **Kalamsat-V2** was the first to use the **PS4 stage as an orbital platform**, and the **lightest** — option **(3)**.
First university satellite = **ANUSAT**; first indigenous radar satellite = **RISAT-1**; first education satellite = **EDUSAT**.
xa: Built by **Space Kidz India**, Chennai; launched **Jan 2019** on **PSLV-C44**.
Student CubeSats now fly on PSLV **POEM** (the PS4 orbital platform).
Space Kidz India also built **AzaadiSAT** with **750 girl students**.

43.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding AzaadiSAT?
o: It was built by Anna University and became India's first university satellite.
It was built by IIT Kanpur and launched on PSLV-C18.
It was launched on PSLV-C44 and used the PS4 stage as an orbital platform.
It was developed by Space Kidz India with 750 girl students of government schools and failed to reach orbit after launch on SSLV-D1.
43.x: AzaadiSAT was developed by Space Kidz India with 750 girl students of government schools. It was launched on SSLV-D1 in August 2022 but failed to reach orbit.
43.tq: Combine the builder, participants, launcher and mission result.
xs: **AzaadiSAT** was built by **Space Kidz India** with **750 girl students** of government schools and **failed to reach orbit** on **SSLV-D1** — option **(4)**.
**Anna University** built **ANUSAT**; **IIT Kanpur** built **Jugnu** (**PSLV-C18**); **PSLV-C44**/PS4 = **Kalamsat-V2**.
xa: AzaadiSAT launched in **Aug 2022**.
⚠ **AzaadiSAT** (girl students, failed) vs **WESAT** (women students, flew).
WESAT flew on **PSLV-C58 POEM-3** (**Jan 2024**).

43.s: WESAT was developed by which institution and served which principal purpose?
o: LBS Institute of Technology for Women; measurement of solar ultraviolet radiation
Sathyabama University; measurement of greenhouse gases
43.x: WESAT was built by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram, and measured solar UV. It was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students.
43.tq: Match the academic institution with the satellite’s scientific payload purpose.
xs: **WESAT** was built by **LBS Institute of Technology for Women** and measures **solar UV** — option **(2)**.
**Sathyabama University**'s **SATYABAMASAT** measured **greenhouse gases**; **SRM University** built **SRMSAT**.
xa: WESAT = **first Indian satellite fully built by women students** (PYQ).
It flew on **PSLV-C58 POEM-3** (**Jan 2024**).
The institute is in **Thiruvananthapuram (Kerala)**.

43.s: The first satellite built by an Indian university, ANUSAT (2009), was developed by:
o: LBS Institute of Technology for Women
43.x: ANUSAT, launched on PSLV-C12 in 2009, was built by Anna University, Chennai, and is the first satellite built by an Indian university. IIT Kanpur built Jugnu, SRM University built SRMSAT, and the LBS Institute built WESAT.
43.tq: ANUSAT = Anna University = first university satellite.
xs: **ANUSAT** was built by **Anna University, Chennai** — option **(3)**.
**IIT Kanpur** built **Jugnu**, **SRM University** built **SRMSAT**, and the **LBS Institute** built **WESAT**.
xa: ANUSAT flew in **2009** on **PSLV-C12** as co-passenger of **RISAT-2**.
ANUSAT = **first satellite built by an Indian university**.
First pico-satellite: **StudSat** (**2010**).

43.s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO's UNNATI programme:
1. It is a nanosatellite assembly and training programme for participants from developing countries.
2. It was launched in 2019 to mark 50 years of UNISPACE-I.
3. It is a summer programme on space science for Class 9 school students.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: UNNATI (UNispace Nanosatellite Assembly and Training by ISRO) trains developing countries in nanosatellites and was launched in 2019 for 50 years of UNISPACE-I. Statement 3 is wrong: the Class 9 summer programme is YUVIKA. Hence B; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
43.tq: UNNATI = UN + nanosatellites for developing countries; YUVIKA = Yuva (school students).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**UNNATI** (UNispace Nanosatellite Assembly and Training by ISRO) trains **developing countries** in nanosatellites.
It was launched in **2019** to mark **50 years of UNISPACE-I**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **class 9** summer programme is **YUVIKA**.
xa: ⚠ **UNNATI** = foreign/developing-country engineers; **YUVIKA** = Indian school students.
**ATL Space Challenge** = Atal Innovation Mission with **ISRO and CBSE**.
**Space Labs** in **75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools** (Apr **2026**).

43.s: YUVIKA, or Yuva Vigyani Karyakram, is intended for:
o: Class 9 school students and provides exposure to space science
Private companies developing radar imaging payloads
University researchers working on defence satellites
Participants from developing countries receiving nanosatellite training
43.x: YUVIKA is ISRO's summer programme on space science for school students studying in Class 9.
43.tq: Distinguish the school-student programme from the international nanosatellite-training programme.
xs: **YUVIKA** (Yuva Vigyani Karyakram) is ISRO's summer programme on space science for **school students** (**class 9**) — option **(1)**.
Nanosatellite training for **developing countries** is **UNNATI**, not YUVIKA.
xa: UNNATI was launched in **2019** for **50 years of UNISPACE-I**.
**ATL Space Challenge**: **Atal Innovation Mission**, **ISRO** and **CBSE**.
**Space Labs** in **75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools**.

43.s: Which one of the following statements regarding student CubeSats is correct?
o: They can fly on the PSLV POEM, which is the PS4 orbital platform, and also as rideshares.
They are developed only by defence laboratories and not by students.
They fly only as independent payloads and never use an orbital platform.
They are launched exclusively on geostationary launch vehicles.
43.x: Student CubeSats may fly on PSLV POEM, the PS4 orbital platform, or as rideshare payloads. WESAT is an example flown on POEM-3.
43.tq: Reject the exclusive wording and identify the option that preserves both available launch modes.
xs: Student CubeSats fly on PSLV **POEM** (the **PS4 orbital platform**) and as **rideshares** — option **(1)**.
Example: **WESAT** flew on **POEM-3** (**PSLV-C58**).
xa: **Kalamsat-V2** was the first to use the **PS4 stage** as an orbital platform.
**PSLV-C62** (**12 Jan 2026**) carried **15 co-passengers** from start-ups and academic institutions, incl. a **KID re-entry capsule**.
**UNNATI** trains developing countries in nanosatellite assembly.

43.s: The ATL Space Challenge is associated with which institutional combination?
o: Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
UNESCO, ISRO and the Ministry of Defence
Department of Space, UGC and NCERT
43.x: The ATL Space Challenge is an initiative involving the Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE for school students.
43.tq: Use the institutional-combination trap to distinguish the participating bodies from neighbouring agencies.
xs: The **ATL Space Challenge** involves **Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE** for school students — option **(2)**.
The other combinations are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: **YUVIKA** = ISRO summer programme for **class 9** students.
**Space Labs** set up in **75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools** (Apr **2026**).
**UNNATI** = nanosatellite training for developing countries.

43.s: Which country was NOT among the foreign satellite contributors to the PSLV-C37 mission?
43.x: The foreign nanosatellites on PSLV-C37 came from the United States, Israel, Kazakhstan, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the UAE. Japan was not in the listed group.
43.tq: Use the country list and identify the omitted nation.
xs: **Japan** was not a contributor — option **(4)**.
The **101 foreign nanosats from 6 countries** came from the **US, Israel, Kazakhstan, Netherlands, Switzerland, UAE**.
xa: **PSLV-C37** (**15 Feb 2017**) set the record of **104 satellites** in one launch.
It carried **Cartosat-2** series (**714 kg**) + **2 ISRO nanosats**.
Total **1,378 kg** to a **506 km** SSO.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about PSLV-C37:
1. It placed 104 satellites in orbit in a single launch.
2. The mission included 101 foreign nanosatellites from six countries.
3. It carried the Cartosat-2 series and two ISRO nanosatellites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
43.x: All three statements are correct. PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites on 15 February 2017, including Cartosat-2 series, two ISRO nanosatellites and 101 foreign nanosatellites.
43.tq: Check the total and the components of the record-setting launch.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**PSLV-C37** (**15 Feb 2017**) put **104 satellites** in orbit in one launch.
It carried **Cartosat-2** series + **2 ISRO nanosats** + **101 foreign nanosats from 6 countries**.
xa: Total mass **1,378 kg**; orbit **506 km** SSO.
**Over 400 foreign satellites** have flown on Indian rockets (**1 Jan 2026**).
**NSIL**: **141** satellites, incl. **138** international/customer, as of July **2026**.

43.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission anomaly?
o: The mission was launched from Kourou by Ariane-5.
The mission was delayed because of a pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor.
The mission failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage.
The mission achieved a record of 104 satellites in one launch.
43.x: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage. The pressure-drop failure was associated with EOS-09 on PSLV-C61.
43.tq: Separate similar launch failures by identifying the stage and nature of the anomaly.
xs: **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1** **failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage** — option **(3)**.
The **third-stage pressure drop** was the **PSLV-C61 (EOS-09)** failure; the **104-satellite** record was **PSLV-C37**.
xa: C62 flew on **12 Jan 2026** — the **64th PSLV flight**, **105th launch** from Sriharikota.
It was the **9th** dedicated **NSIL** commercial mission.
It carried **15 co-passengers**, incl. a **KID re-entry capsule**.

43.s: EOS-05 is notable as India's first earth-imaging satellite intended for geosynchronous orbit. Its approximate orbital altitude and major applications are respectively:
o: About 2,000 km; television broadcasting and telephone services only
About 800 km; ocean navigation, mining and astronomy only
About 3,600 km; agriculture and deep-space communication only
About 36,000 km; floods, cyclones, fires and security
43.x: EOS-05 is intended for geosynchronous orbit at approximately 36,000 km and supports observation of floods, cyclones, fires and security-related events.
43.tq: Match the orbital regime with the corresponding altitude and application set; reject the altered range and ‘only’ claims.
xs: **EOS-05** sits at about **36,000 km** (**geosynchronous orbit**) and serves **floods, cyclones, fires and security** — option **(4)**.
It is India's **first earth-imaging satellite** for geosynchronous orbit (**7 Sep 2026**).
xa: ISRO has moved to **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.
⚠ **EDUSAT** was also geostationary, at **74 degrees E** — but for education, not imaging.
Two consecutive PSLV failures (**C61**, **C62**) hit surveillance satellites.

43.s: The current relevance associated with EOS-05, reported on 7 September 2026, includes which of the following developments?
o: Two consecutive PSLV failures involving C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026 affected surveillance satellites.
Two consecutive GSLV failures involving C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026 affected communication satellites.
A single PSLV failure in 2024 affected EDUSAT and ANUSAT.
Two consecutive SSLV failures in 2025 affected only academic satellites.
43.x: The reported relevance referred to two consecutive PSLV failures: C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026, which affected surveillance satellites.
43.tq: Track the launch vehicle, mission identifiers and sequence of years together to avoid swapped-vehicle traps.
xs: The relevance includes **two consecutive PSLV failures** — **C61** (**2025**) and **C62** (**Jan 2026**) — that hit **surveillance satellites** — option **(1)**.
These were **PSLV** failures, not GSLV or SSLV.
xa: **C61** lost **EOS-09 (RISAT-1B)** after a third-stage **pressure drop**.
**C62/EOS-N1** failed after a **roll-rate disturbance** at the end of the third stage.
**EOS-05**: first earth-imaging satellite for geosynchronous orbit (~**36,000 km**).

43.s: The StudSat consortium had participation from colleges of:
o: Andhra Pradesh, which was then undivided
Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh only
43.x: The StudSat consortium included colleges from Andhra Pradesh, when the State was undivided.

xs: The **StudSat** consortium included colleges from **Andhra Pradesh (then undivided)** — option **(2)**.
It was a consortium of **7 engineering colleges** from **Karnataka** and Andhra Pradesh.
xa: StudSat = **India's first pico-satellite** (**2010**, **PSLV-C15**).
AP angle: all these student satellites launched from **Sriharikota**.
First university satellite: **ANUSAT** (**Anna University**).

xs: Correct match: **A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1** — option **(1)**.

44.s: Under the revised FDI policy for the space sector, the automatic-route limit for manufacturing satellite components and subsystems is:
44.x: Manufacturing of satellite components and subsystems is permitted up to 100% through the automatic route.
44.tq: Distinguish the component-manufacturing limit from the lower limits for other segments.
xs: Satellite **components and subsystems** manufacturing is allowed up to **100%** on the automatic route — option **(4)**.
**74%** is the limit for satellite manufacturing/operation and data products; **49%** for **launch vehicles and spaceports**.
xa: ⚠ Memory aid: **100 – 74 – 49** = components – satellites/data – launch vehicles/spaceports.
Beyond these limits the **government route** applies.
Overall, FDI up to **100%** is allowed in **non-sensitive** segments.

44.s:
Consider the following statements about foreign direct investment in India’s space sector:
1. Satellite manufacturing, satellite operations and data products have an automatic-route limit of 74%.
2. Launch vehicles and spaceports have an automatic-route limit of 49%.
3. Investment beyond the prescribed automatic-route limits requires the government route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: All three statements are correct. The automatic route permits 74% in satellite manufacturing, operations and data products, 49% in launch vehicles and spaceports, and investment above the applicable limits requires government approval.
44.tq: Combine segment limits with the approval-route condition.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Satellite manufacturing, operation and **data products**: up to **74%** automatic.
**Launch vehicles and spaceports**: up to **49%** automatic; beyond the limits, the **government route** applies.
xa: Components and subsystems: **100%** automatic.
The **June 2020** reforms opened the sector to **NGEs**.
**Indian Space Policy 2023** followed: Cabinet approval **6 April 2023**.

44.s: Under India's revised FDI policy for the space sector, what is the overall ceiling for foreign direct investment in non-sensitive space segments?
44.x: FDI up to 100% is allowed overall in non-sensitive space segments, with segment-wise automatic-route limits of 100%, 74% and 49% and the government route beyond those limits.
44.tq: Non-sensitive = fully open: 100%.
xs: FDI up to **100%** is allowed overall in **non-sensitive** space segments — option **(4)**.
Within it, segment limits on the automatic route are **100%** (components), **74%** (satellites/data) and **49%** (launch vehicles/spaceports).
xa: Beyond the segment limits, the **government route** applies.
⚠ **49%** is the lowest limit — for **launch vehicles and spaceports**.
The **Space Policy 2023** lets NGEs do **end-to-end** space activity.

44.s: The Indian Space Policy 2023 was approved by the Union Cabinet and released by the Department of Space on which of the following dates, respectively?
44.x: The policy was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 April 2023 and released by the Department of Space on 20 April 2023.
44.tq: Use the chronological pairing of the approval and release dates.
xs: The **Indian Space Policy 2023** was **approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 April 2023** and **released by DoS on 20 April 2023** — option **(1)**.
**June 2020** was when the reforms opened the sector to NGEs — not the policy dates.
xa: **IN-SPACe** = independent regulator that promotes, authorises and supervises **NGEs**.
**NSIL** commercialises mature ISRO technology.
**ISRO** focuses on R&D, **deep-space** and **human spaceflight**.

44.s:
With reference to the Indian Space Policy 2023, consider the following statements:
1. IN-SPACe is responsible for authorising and promoting the activities of non-governmental entities.
2. IN-SPACe functions as an independent regulator for non-governmental space activity.
3. IN-SPACe is responsible for commercialising mature ISRO technologies through industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: IN-SPACe authorises, promotes and supervises non-governmental activity and functions as an independent regulator. Commercialisation of mature ISRO technology is the role of NSIL.
44.tq: Separate the regulatory role of IN-SPACe from the commercial role of NSIL.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**IN-SPACe** **promotes, authorises and supervises** NGE activity and is the **independent regulator**.
Statement 3 is wrong: commercialising **mature ISRO technology** is **NSIL**'s role.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **IN-SPACe** is the regulator; **ISRO is not**.
IN-SPACe HQ: **Ahmedabad**; chairman **Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka**.
IN-SPACe gives NGEs access to **DoS facilities**.

44.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding institutional roles under the Indian Space Policy 2023.

List-I (Entity)
a. NSIL
b. Department of Space
c. Non-Governmental Entities

d. ISRO

List-II (Role)
i. Overall policy, international cooperation and treaty compliance
 ii. End-to-end space activities including satellites, launches and services
 iii. Commercialisation of mature ISRO technology
 iv. Advanced research, deep-space activities and human spaceflight

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
44.x: NSIL commercialises mature ISRO technology; the Department of Space handles policy and cooperation; non-governmental entities undertake end-to-end activities; and ISRO focuses on advanced research and strategic missions.
44.tq: Start from the sure pair linking NSIL with commercialisation.
xs: Correct match: **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — option **(1)**.
**NSIL** = commercialises **mature ISRO technology**; **DoS** = overall policy, international cooperation, **treaty compliance**.
**NGEs** = **end-to-end** activity; **ISRO** = advanced R&D, **deep-space** and **human spaceflight**.
xa: **IN-SPACe** = independent regulator for NGEs.
DoS also handles **space diplomacy** and coordination.
ISRO is to move out of making operational/commercial satellites and rockets over time.

44.s: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of the Department of Space under the Indian Space Policy 2023?
o: Independent authorisation of every non-governmental space activity
44.x: IN-SPACe, not the Department of Space, authorises and supervises non-governmental space activity. The Department of Space handles overall policy, cooperation, diplomacy, treaty compliance and coordination.
44.tq: Find the institutional responsibility assigned to a neighbouring authority.
xs: **Independent authorisation of NGE space activity** is not DoS's job — option **(2)**.
That role belongs to **IN-SPACe**, which **promotes, authorises and supervises** NGEs.
**DoS** handles overall **policy**, **international cooperation**, **space diplomacy**, **treaty compliance** and coordination.
xa: IN-SPACe is an **autonomous single-window agency** under DoS (est. **2020**).
**NSIL** is a **CPSE** under DoS.
The policy was released by DoS on **20 April 2023**.

44.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the future role of ISRO under the Indian Space Policy 2023:
1. ISRO is expected to move out of making operational and commercial satellites and rockets over time.
2. The policy assigns ISRO a role in advanced space technology and human spaceflight.
3. The policy seeks to privatise ISRO and reduce it to a regulatory body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
44.x: ISRO is to focus on advanced research, deep space and human spaceflight while gradually moving away from routine operational and commercial production. The stated position is that ISRO will not be privatised or reduced.
44.tq: Reject the extreme-word trap in the statement about privatisation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**ISRO** is to **move out of making operational/commercial satellites and rockets** over time.
It keeps **R&D in advanced space technology**, **deep-space** and **human spaceflight**.
Statement 3 is wrong: IN-SPACe and ISRO said ISRO "**will not be privatised or reduced**" (**7-8 Sep 2026**).
xa: ISRO's **nine** employee associations sought clarity on outsourcing (**Sept 2026**).
⚠ The regulator is **IN-SPACe**, not ISRO.
**NSIL** builds launchers and satellites through industry.

44.s: In September 2026, ISRO employee associations sought clarity primarily regarding which issue?
o: The replacement of all ISRO launch vehicles
The outsourcing of ISRO activities and its future role
44.x: Nine ISRO employee associations sought clarity on outsourcing and ISRO’s future role. IN-SPACe and ISRO stated that ISRO would not be privatised or reduced and that its role was by no means diminishing.
44.tq: Identify the issue directly associated with the institutional controversy.
xs: ISRO's **nine employee associations** sought clarity on **outsourcing** and **ISRO's future role** — option **(4)**.
IN-SPACe and ISRO replied that ISRO "**will not be privatised or reduced**" (**7-8 Sep 2026**).
xa: Under the **2023** policy, ISRO focuses on **R&D**, **deep-space** and **human spaceflight**.
**NGEs** may do **end-to-end** space activity.
IN-SPACe HQ is **Ahmedabad** — no relocation issue is in the notes.

44.s: IN-SPACe was established in 2020 primarily as:
o: a statutory appellate tribunal for space disputes
an autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space
a financial institution for satellite insurance
44.x: IN-SPACe was established in 2020 as an autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space to facilitate non-governmental space activities.
44.tq: Identify the institutional character and parent department before considering its functions.
xs: **IN-SPACe** (**2020**) is an **autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space** — option **(3)**.
It **promotes, authorises and supervises** NGEs and gives them access to **DoS facilities**.
xa: Full name: **Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre**.
HQ **Ahmedabad**; chairman **Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka**.
It runs the **IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme** for space start-ups.

44.s: Which one of the following correctly states the headquarters and chairman of IN-SPACe?
44.x: IN-SPACe is headquartered at Ahmedabad, and Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka is its chairman.
44.tq: Discriminate the regulator’s headquarters and chairman from prominent ISRO locations and office-holders.
xs: **IN-SPACe** is headquartered in **Ahmedabad**, chaired by **Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka** — option **(2)**.
**Bengaluru** is **NSIL**'s HQ, not IN-SPACe's.
xa: ⚠ HQ: **IN-SPACe = Ahmedabad**; **NSIL = Bengaluru**.
IN-SPACe received **834 applications**, processed **499** (**294 satellites**, **103 launch vehicles**).
It authorised the first private launch **Vikram-S** (**2022**).

44.s: Which authority functions as the regulator for non-governmental space activities in India?
44.x: IN-SPACe is the regulator for non-governmental space activities. ISRO is not the regulator, while NSIL and Antrix have commercial roles.
44.tq: Ask which body performs the regulatory function, not which body conducts or commercialises space activity.
xs: **IN-SPACe** is the regulator for NGE space activity — option **(2)**.
⚠ **ISRO is not** the regulator; **NSIL** and **Antrix** are commercial arms.
xa: IN-SPACe = **autonomous single-window agency** under DoS, est. **2020**.
It approved the **PPP EOS constellation** led by **Pixxel**.

44.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Vikram-S — First private launch authorised by IN-SPACe
2. Seed Fund Scheme — Support for space start-ups
3. EOS constellation — Pixxel-led constellation approved by IN-SPACe

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

44.s:
NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is best described as which of the following?

2. The commercial arm of ISRO

44.tq: Separate an organisation’s establishment year from its later status or recognition year.

44.s:
Which of the following activities is associated with NSIL rather than being limited to Antrix Corporation?

1. Technology transfer
2. Launch services
3. Satellite services
4. Ownership and operation of satellites against committed demand

44.s:
Consider the following statements about Antrix Corporation and NSIL:

1. Antrix was set up in September 1992.
2. Antrix became a Miniratna in 2008.
3. NSIL follows a demand-driven model involving ownership of satellites.
4. Antrix’s activities included marketing ISRO products and leasing transponders.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

44.s: Which one of the following statements about India’s space legislation is correct?
o: India currently has no Space Activities Act and the sector operates through policies and guidelines.

xa: The draft proposed **licensing of private space activity**.

44.s: The draft Space Activities Bill first put out by India proposed, among other things:
o: abolition of all private participation in space activity
creation of a separate international liability convention
transfer of space regulation exclusively to Antrix

xs: The draft **Space Activities Bill** (**2017**) proposed **licensing of private space activity** — option **(4)**.
It did not abolish private participation or hand regulation to **Antrix**.
xa: India still has **no Space Activities Act**.
The **Liability Convention** (**1972**) makes the **launching State** liable for damage.
No **sovereign-backed insurance** exists for private ventures (**23 Jun 2026**).

44.s: Vikram-1 is described as India’s first private orbital rocket. Which of the following is correct about it?

45.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes passive remote sensing from active remote sensing?
o: Passive sensors detect naturally available radiation, whereas active sensors transmit their own signal.
Passive sensors operate only at night, whereas active sensors operate only during the day.
Passive sensors emit radar signals, whereas active sensors depend only on sunlight.
Both passive and active sensors depend exclusively on solar radiation.
45.x: Passive remote sensing uses naturally available radiation such as solar radiation, while active systems transmit their own signal. Resourcesat and Oceansat illustrate passive applications, whereas RISAT uses radar.
45.tq: Discriminate paired concepts by their defining operational difference.
xs: **Passive** sensors use naturally available radiation (sunlight), while **active** sensors **transmit their own signal** — option **(1)**.
Passive examples: **Resourcesat**, **Oceansat**; active example: **RISAT** radar.
So passive sensors do not emit radar, and active ones do not depend on sunlight.
xa: Remote sensing gathers information **without physical contact**, from reflected/emitted radiation.
**Microwave (radar/SAR)** bands see through **cloud and darkness**.
⚠ **Active** = own signal (**RISAT**); **passive** = sunlight.

45.s: Microwave or Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing is especially useful during floods because it can:
o: Operate through cloud cover and in darkness
Replace all ground surveys under every condition
Predict the exact time of an earthquake
45.x: Microwave/SAR systems can observe through cloud cover and in darkness, making them useful for flood mapping during cloudy conditions.
45.tq: Use the practical advantage of the technology to solve the stated disaster scenario.
xs: **Microwave/SAR** sees **through cloud cover and in darkness** — option **(1)** — so it maps floods in cloudy weather.
Earthquakes **cannot be predicted** from space, and individual health events like heart attacks cannot be monitored.
xa: Assam's planned flood satellites may carry **SAR** — the State is cloudy half the year (**25 Mar 2026**).
**RISAT/SAR** = flood mapping through cloud.
Bhuvan combines satellites into **flood-inundation maps** and **cyclone warnings**.

45.s:

3. It depends exclusively on visible-light images and cannot use radar observations.

45.tq: Reject the extreme and technically reversed statement while retaining the supported applications.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**NISAR** detects ground movement to the **centimetre** and is used for **land subsidence, earthquakes, glaciers**.
Statement 3 is wrong: NISAR is a radar mission — it has **L- and S-band radar**.
xa: **InSAR** compares the **phase** of two or more radar images to map **ground deformation**.
NISAR's radar is also used for **soil moisture**.
InSAR uses: earthquakes, **land subsidence**, **landslides**, **volcanoes**, **glacier movement**.

45.s: InSAR is primarily used to
o: measure only the colour of vegetation
compare the phase of radar images to map ground deformation
calculate crop production from field surveys alone
45.x: Interferometric SAR compares the phase of two or more radar images of the same area to detect ground deformation.
45.tq: Break the term into interferometric comparison and SAR imaging.
xs: **InSAR** (Interferometric SAR) **compares the phase of radar images** of the same place to **map ground deformation** — option **(2)**.
It is not about vegetation colour, field surveys or fishing advisories.
xa: Uses: **earthquakes**, **land subsidence**, **landslides**, **volcanoes**, **glacier movement**.
PYQ: **APPSC 2024** — statement A correct.
**NISAR** detects ground movement to the **centimetre**.

3. Landslides

xs: All four can be monitored with InSAR — option **(4)**.
InSAR maps ground deformation from **earthquakes**, **land subsidence**, **landslides** and **glacier movement**.
xa: InSAR also tracks **volcanoes**.
It works by comparing the **phase** of **two or more** radar images of the same place.

45.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the usual range and interpretation of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)?
o: It ranges from 0 to 100; higher values indicate barren land.
It ranges from −100 to +100; lower values indicate dense vegetation.
It ranges from 1 to 10; higher values indicate cloud cover.
It ranges from −1 to +1; higher values generally indicate healthy green vegetation.
45.x: NDVI ranges from −1 to +1. High positive values are associated with healthy green vegetation.
45.tq: Use the paired numerical range and interpretation to eliminate reversed meanings.
xs: **NDVI** ranges from **-1 to +1**; high values mean **healthy green vegetation** — option **(4)**.
Formula: **(NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red)** — healthy vegetation reflects strongly in **NIR**.
xa: NDVI = **Normalized Difference Vegetation Index**.

xa: NDVI = **(NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red)**, range **-1 to +1**.

45.s: Why is near-infrared reflectance important in assessing vegetation health through remote sensing?

Near-infrared radiation is emitted only by dry soil.

45.s: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is computed as:
45.x: NDVI = (NIR − Red) / (NIR + Red). Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in near-infrared and absorbs red, so values range from −1 to +1 and high values mean healthy green vegetation. The reversed ratio, the product in the denominator and the green/blue bands are not the NDVI formula.
45.tq: NDVI: NIR minus Red over NIR plus Red; range −1 to +1.
xs: **NDVI = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red)** — option **(1)**.
Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in **NIR**; reversing the ratio or using green/blue bands is not NDVI.
xa: Range **-1 to +1**; high values = **healthy green vegetation**.
NDVI is the most used index for **operational drought assessment** (PYQ).
**VCI**, derived from NDVI, is used for drought declaration.

xs: **Bhoonidhi** = archive and hub for Indian and foreign EO data **since 1988** — option **(1)**.
**MOSDAC** gives **meteorological and oceanographic** data; **VEDAS** visualises EO data; **Bhuvan Panchayat** is for **gram panchayat** planning.
xa: Bhoonidhi is run by **NRSC**; MOSDAC and VEDAS by **SAC**.
Property cards come from **SVAMITVA**.
MGNREGA assets: **Geo-MGNREGA / Yuktdhara**.

45.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Portal or service)
a. Bhuvan Panchayat
b. Yuktdhara
c. SVAMITVA
 d. PM Gati Shakti

 ii. Geospatial support for Gram Panchayat development planning

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

**Bhuvan Panchayat** = **gram panchayat** development planning; **Yuktdhara** = **MGNREGA** assets.
**SVAMITVA** = **drone mapping** of rural properties + **property cards**; **PM Gati Shakti** = **National Master Plan GIS** platform.

45.s: Which organisation developed the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan GIS platform?
45.x: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan GIS platform was built by BISAG-N.

xs: **PM Gati Shakti**'s National Master Plan GIS platform was built by **BISAG-N** — option **(1)**.
**IMD** makes weather apps; **Forest Survey of India** runs the fire alert system; **NRSC** runs **Bhuvan**.
xa: AP integrated **271 GIS layers across 27 departments** into PM Gati Shakti.

**SVAMITVA** = drone mapping with **Survey of India**.

45.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its portal or service?
o: MOSDAC — Meteorological and oceanographic satellite data
Bhoonidhi — Exclusive platform for MGNREGA asset planning
45.x: MOSDAC provides meteorological and oceanographic satellite data. VEDAS visualises Earth-observation data, Bhoonidhi is an Earth-observation data hub, and Srishti concerns watershed monitoring.
45.tq: Use nearby portal names as distractors and verify the exact service association.
xs: **MOSDAC** gives **meteorological and oceanographic satellite data** — option **(1)**.
**VEDAS** visualises EO data; **Bhoonidhi** is the EO data hub; **Srishti** is watershed monitoring.
xa: MOSDAC and VEDAS are both run by **SAC, Ahmedabad**.

Property cards come from **SVAMITVA**.

45.s: The Srishti service is associated with monitoring of:
45.x: Srishti is used for watershed monitoring under the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP).
45.tq: Test a less prominent portal by its specific sectoral application.
xs: **Srishti** is for **watershed monitoring** under **IWMP** — option **(2)**.
Drone property mapping is **SVAMITVA**; ocean data is **MOSDAC**; cyclone warnings come via the **INSAT Disaster Warning System**.
xa: **Yuktdhara** plans and monitors **MGNREGA** assets.
**Bhuvan Panchayat** supports **gram panchayat** planning.
**Resourcesat** data also support **watershed management**.

45.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a Geographic Information System component?
o: Hardware — computer, digitizer, scanner, GPS receiver and plotter
People and methods — satellite images only
45.x: Computers, digitizers, scanners, GPS receivers and plotters are examples of GIS hardware. Software includes GIS packages, data includes spatial and attribute information, and people and methods include analysts and procedures.
45.tq: Classify each item by asking whether it is equipment, software, data or human procedure.
xs: **Hardware — computer, digitizer, scanner, GPS receiver, plotter** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Software** = GIS packages (e.g., **QGIS**); **data** = spatial + **attribute** tables; **people and methods** = analysts and procedures.
xa: **QGIS** is used in **APSAC** workshops.
Each theme (roads, soils, land use, water) is a **layer**.
**Overlay** analysis combines layers.

45.s: Which of the following correctly describes GIS data?
o: Raster data consists only of points, lines and polygons.
Attribute tables are GIS hardware devices.
Spatial data may be vector or raster, and may be linked with attribute tables.
Spatial data consists exclusively of written procedures.
45.x: GIS data includes spatial data such as vector points, lines and polygons and raster satellite images, along with attribute tables.
45.tq: Distinguish spatial representation from hardware and procedural components.
xs: **Spatial data** may be **vector** or **raster**, linked to **attribute** tables — option **(3)**.
**Vector** = points, lines, polygons; **raster** = satellite images — so option (1) mixes them up.
xa: GIS components: **hardware**, **software**, **data**, **people and methods**.
Thematic layers are combined in **overlay** analysis.
A **digitizer** is GIS hardware.

45.s: In a GIS, roads, soils, land use and water are generally represented as
45.x: Each theme, such as roads, soils, land use or water, is represented as a separate GIS layer.
45.tq: Apply the layered representation principle to familiar geographic themes.
xs: Each theme — **roads, soils, land use, water** — is a **separate thematic data layer** — option **(3)**.
**Overlay analysis** combines these layers.
xa: GIS data = **spatial** (vector/raster) + **attribute** tables.
AP's **APSSDI** standardised **74 GIS layers**.
Real-time layers give **situational awareness** for disaster response.

45.s: Overlay analysis in GIS refers to
o: converting all raster data into hardware
measuring only the phase of radar images
combining different data layers for analysis
45.x: Overlay analysis combines multiple thematic layers to derive and analyse relationships between them.
45.tq: Use the meaning of overlay as the combination of thematic layers.
xs: **Overlay analysis** means **combining different data layers** for analysis — option **(4)**.
Sending PFZ messages and measuring radar phase (**InSAR**) are different things.
xa: Each theme (roads, soils, land use, water) = a **layer**.
PM Gati Shakti (AP) integrates **271** layers across **27** departments.
GIS software example: **QGIS**.

45.s: Which of the following is an example of GIS-based situational awareness in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only calculation of the NDVI formula
Real-time flood alerts and mineral-vehicle tracking
45.x: Situational awareness uses real-time layers for disaster response, including flood alerts and mineral-vehicle tracking, as well as shoreline mapping.
45.tq: Identify the real-time operational uses rather than static remote-sensing measures.
xs: GIS **situational awareness** uses real-time layers such as **flood alerts** and **mineral-vehicle tracking** — option **(4)**.
Real-time layers serve **disaster response**, **flood alerts** and **shoreline mapping**.
AP's **APMVTS** fitted **50,000** mineral vehicles with **AIS-140** devices.
xa: AP's **City Flood Alert**: **RTGS with APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar**, piloted in **Vijayawada**.
It gives **48-hour rainfall** and **6-hour flash-flood** warnings.
APSAC shoreline data: **1,053 km** coast — **26%** eroded, **54%** accreting, **20%** stable.

45.s: Which satellite-system combination is correctly matched with its disaster-management application?
o: Cartosat — Detection of human disease spread
45.x: RISAT/SAR can support flood mapping even through cloud cover. INSAT-3DS is used for cyclone tracking, Oceansat for ocean-state information and Cartosat for damage mapping.
45.tq: Start from the sure satellite–application pair and eliminate mismatched uses.
xs: **RISAT/SAR — flood mapping through clouds** is correct — option **(1)**.
**INSAT-3DS** = **cyclone tracks**; **Oceansat** = **ocean state**; **Cartosat** = **damage mapping**.
Heart attacks and disease spread **cannot** be monitored from space.
xa: Bhuvan combines these into **flood-inundation maps and cyclone warnings**.
PYQ: "spread of a disease" (**APPSC 2022**) and "heart attack" (**APPSC 2025**) were the CANNOT answers.
Fire hotspots come from **MODIS** and **VIIRS**.

45.s: Bhuvan combines inputs from RISAT/SAR and INSAT-3DS primarily to provide:
o: Individual medical diagnoses in remote areas
45.x: Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood-related imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.
45.tq: Link the satellite input to the stated decision-support output.
xs: **Bhuvan** combines satellite inputs into **flood-inundation maps and cyclone warnings** — option **(2)**.
**RISAT/SAR** maps floods through cloud; **INSAT-3DS** tracks cyclones.
Earthquakes **cannot be predicted**, and medical diagnoses are not satellite uses.
xa: Bhuvan was launched in **2009** by **NRSC**.
**Cartosat** = damage mapping; **Oceansat** = ocean state.
States must request satellite data from **NRSC** (**25 Mar 2026**).

45.s:
Consider the following statements about fire-hotspot monitoring:
1. Fire hotspots are detected by thermal-infrared sensors such as MODIS (NASA Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP).
2. The hotspot data are received at NRSC's Shadnagar earth station.
3. The data are passed to the India Meteorological Department, which runs the forest-fire alert system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
45.x: Statement 1 is correct: thermal-infrared sensors on MODIS and VIIRS detect fire hotspots. Statement 2 is correct: the data are received at NRSC's Shadnagar earth station. Statement 3 is wrong: the data go to the Forest Survey of India alert system, not IMD. So B (1 and 2 only); A leaves out the correct statement 2; C and D include the wrong statement 3.
45.tq: Hotspot chain: MODIS/VIIRS (thermal IR) -> Shadnagar (NRSC) -> Forest Survey of India.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **thermal-infrared** sensors **MODIS** (NASA Terra/Aqua) and **VIIRS** (Suomi-NPP) detect hotspots.
Statement 2: data are received at **NRSC's Shadnagar** earth station.
Statement 3 is wrong: the data go to the **Forest Survey of India** alert system, not IMD.
xa: These sensors fly on **polar** satellites.
Forest fires (**wildfires**) can be monitored from space.
NRSC is the **nodal agency** for satellite data.

45.s: Which one of the following CANNOT be monitored using satellite remote sensing?
o: Spread of a disease among humans
45.x: Floods, cyclones, drought, forest fires, tsunami inundation, landslides and post-quake ground deformation can all be monitored from space. Individual human-health events cannot: the spread of a disease among humans (APPSC 2022) and a heart attack (APPSC 2025) were the 'cannot be monitored' answers. Forest fires, tsunami inundation and landslides are all monitorable, so they are wrong.
45.tq: 'Cannot be monitored from space' → always the human-health event.
xs: **Spread of a disease among humans** cannot be monitored from space — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2022**).
**Forest fires**, **tsunami inundation of coasts** and **landslides** can all be monitored.
xa: Exam angle: the "CANNOT be monitored" answer is always the **human-health event** — also **heart attack** (**APPSC 2025**).
Also monitorable: floods, cyclones, drought, post-quake **ground deformation**.
⚠ Earthquakes **cannot be predicted**.

45.s:
With reference to the Disaster Management Support Programme of ISRO, consider the following statements:
1. It uses INSAT and IRS systems for warning and damage assessment.
2. It is listed among the applications of INSAT.
3. It supplies satellite imaging and communication support for several disasters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
45.x: The DMS Programme uses INSAT and IRS, is recognised as an INSAT application, and provides satellite imaging and communication support for floods, cyclones, droughts, fires, landslides and earthquakes.
45.tq: Test multiple institutional functions through a coded statement combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **DMS programme** uses **INSAT/IRS** for **warning + damage assessment** and is listed among INSAT applications.
It covers floods, cyclones, droughts, forest fires, landslides, earthquakes (**imaging + communication**).
xa: DMS R&D: **cyclone track and landfall prediction**, earthquake precursors, coastal vulnerability, **landslide early warning**.
**NDEM** = GIS repository for the full disaster cycle.
ISRO led the **International Charter Space and Major Disasters** for **6 months from April 2025**.

45.s: Which of the following is NOT an identified research and development area under ISRO's Disaster Management Support Programme?
45.x: Cyclone prediction, coastal vulnerability and landslide early warning are identified DMS research areas. Manufacture of commercial passenger aircraft is not a DMS research area.

xs: **Manufacture of commercial passenger aircraft** is not a DMS R&D area — option **(3)**.
DMS R&D covers **cyclone track and landfall prediction**, **earthquake precursors**, **coastal vulnerability** and **landslide early warning**.
xa: DMS uses **INSAT/IRS** for warning and damage assessment.
**NDEM** and the **Decision Support Centre** are at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.
The **INSAT Disaster Warning System** links the Cyclone Warning Centre, **Chennai**, to coastal receivers.

45.s:
Consider the following statements about satellite support during disasters in India:
1. The Decision Support Centre and the National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) are both located at NRSC, Hyderabad.
2. The Decision Support Centre acts as a single window for satellite inputs during disasters.
3. States can use satellite data during disasters without requesting it from NRSC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
45.x: Statement 1 is correct: both the Decision Support Centre and NDEM are at NRSC, Hyderabad. Statement 2 is correct: the Decision Support Centre is the single window for satellite inputs. Statement 3 is wrong: States must request satellite data from NRSC. So C (1 and 2 only); A leaves out statement 2; B and D include the wrong statement 3.
45.tq: NRSC Hyderabad = NDEM + Decision Support Centre; States must ask NRSC for data.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: the **Decision Support Centre** and **NDEM** are both at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.
Statement 2: the Decision Support Centre is the **single window** for satellite inputs during disasters.
Statement 3 is wrong: **States must request satellite data from NRSC** (**25 Mar 2026**).
xa: **NDEM** = **National Database for Emergency Management** — a GIS repository for the full disaster cycle.
NRSC gives **disaster support to States**.
**APSDMA-NRSC MoU** (**15 Apr 2026**) to prevent **lightning deaths** in rural AP.

45.s: The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) is best described as:
o: A GIS repository covering the full disaster-management cycle
A database exclusively for census enumeration
A communication network used only for television broadcasting
A satellite launch vehicle tracking system
45.x: NDEM is a GIS repository designed to support the full disaster-management cycle.
45.tq: Expand the official acronym by identifying its functional description.
xs: **NDEM** is a **GIS repository** covering the **full disaster-management cycle** — option **(1)**.
It is based at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.
xa: NDEM = **National Database for Emergency Management**.
The **Decision Support Centre** at NRSC is the single window for satellite inputs.
The **DMS programme** uses **INSAT/IRS**.

45.s: ISRO took the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months beginning in:
45.x: ISRO assumed the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months from April 2025.
45.tq: Test the precise commencement date using closely spaced year options.
xs: ISRO took the **lead role** in the **International Charter Space and Major Disasters** for **6 months from April 2025** — option **(2)**.
The other years are not in the notes.
xa: ISRO's own **DMS programme** uses **INSAT/IRS** for warning + damage assessment.
**NDEM** and the **Decision Support Centre** sit at **NRSC**.
India proposed a **BRICS Space Economy** + stronger BRICS remote-sensing constellation (**25 Jun 2026**).

45.s: Which sequence correctly represents the communication chain in the INSAT Disaster Warning System?
o: Coastal receiver → C-band uplink → Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → S-band downlink
Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → C-band uplink → S-band downlink → coastal receivers
S-band uplink → NRSC, Hyderabad → C-band downlink → inland receivers
Forest Survey of India → optical uplink → INSAT-3DS → ocean receivers
45.x: The system follows the chain: Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai, C-band uplink, S-band downlink and reception by coastal disaster-warning receivers.
45.tq: Follow the first-to-last communication sequence and eliminate reversed links.
xs: The chain is **Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → C-band uplink → S-band downlink → coastal DWS receivers** — option **(2)**.
Uplink is **C-band** and downlink **S-band** — option (3) reverses the bands.
xa: This is the **INSAT Disaster Warning System**.
**INSAT-3DS** tracks cyclones.
**INCOIS**'s **Ocean State Forecast** also gives cyclone tracks.

45.s: Which programme is associated with pre-harvest forecasts of crop acreage and production?
45.x: FASAL provides pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts using space, agro-meteorological and land-based observations.
45.tq: Match the programme with its distinctive agricultural output.
xs: **FASAL** gives **pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts** — option **(1)**.
**Krishi-DSS** = farm-level decision support; **NADAMS** = drought; **CHAMAN** = horticulture.
xa: FASAL = **Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-meteorology and Land-based observations**.
⚠ **FASAL** = crop forecast; **YES-TECH** = yield (**PMFBY**); **CHAMAN** = horticulture; **NADAMS** = drought.
**MNCFC** (**2012**) makes ISRO crop-forecasting methods operational.

45.s: YES-TECH is primarily associated with
o: satellite-based crop-yield estimation for crop insurance under PMFBY
tracking vehicles fitted with AIS-140 devices
monitoring ocean waves and cyclone tracks
45.x: YES-TECH estimates crop yield using satellite technology for crop insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.
45.tq: Distinguish yield estimation from horticulture assessment and maritime monitoring.
xs: **YES-TECH** does **satellite-based crop yield estimation** for crop insurance under **PMFBY** — option **(2)**.
Horticulture mapping is **CHAMAN**; **AIS-140** devices are for vehicle tracking; wave forecasts come from **INCOIS**.
xa: YES-TECH = **Yield Estimation System based on Technology**; it was asked for **rice yield** (APPSC **2023**).
AP: YES-TECH pilots in **Nandyal and Kakinada** (**2025-26**).
**FASAL** gives pre-harvest acreage and production forecasts.

45.s: CHAMAN is concerned with
o: agricultural drought declaration based on rainfall alone
45.x: CHAMAN is used for horticulture area and production assessment, including horticulture area and condition mapping.
45.tq: Use the programme’s horticulture-specific purpose to reject neighbouring agricultural programmes.
xs: **CHAMAN** is for **horticulture area and production assessment** — option **(1)**.
**Jute** acreage is **JCIS**; drought is **NADAMS**; the weather network is **WINDS**.
xa: CHAMAN = **Coordinated Horticulture Assessment and Management using geoiNformatics**; it also does condition mapping.
**NADAMS** uses **vegetation and moisture indices**.
**CROP** framework: Rabi **2024-25** wheat estimate **122.724 MT**.

45.s: Which one of the following platforms is intended for decision support in farm-level planning?
45.x: Krishi-DSS is a decision-support platform intended to assist farm-level planning.
45.tq: Identify the platform whose name and purpose directly indicate decision support.
xs: **Krishi-DSS** is the **decision-support platform for farm-level planning** — option **(2)**.
**FASAL** forecasts crops; **PFZ** advisories locate fish; **NADAMS** monitors drought.
xa: Related tools: **CROPIC** (crop photos) and **WINDS** (weather network).
The **SAC drought geoportal** tracks **rainfall, temperature and soil moisture**.
**JCIS** covers **jute** acreage and crop health.

45.s: The SAC drought geoportal provides information on
o: only crop prices and market arrivals
wave height, sea state and cyclone tracks
45.x: The SAC drought geoportal tracks rainfall, temperature and soil moisture for drought-related assessment.
45.tq: Separate drought-monitoring variables from ocean-state variables.
xs: The **SAC drought geoportal** tracks **rainfall, temperature and soil moisture** — option **(3)**.
**Wave height, sea state, cyclone tracks** come from **INCOIS**'s **Ocean State Forecast**.
xa: **SAC** is in **Ahmedabad** and also runs **MOSDAC** and **VEDAS**.
**NADAMS** = agricultural drought monitoring.
Soil moisture is best measured by **microwave/SAR** sensors.

45.s: Which type of sensor is best suited for measuring soil moisture from space?
o: A plotter attached to a GIS workstation
45.x: Microwave and SAR sensors are particularly suitable for soil-moisture measurement; NISAR uses L-band and S-band radar for such applications.
45.tq: Select the sensor according to its ability to respond to moisture and operate through clouds.
xs: **Soil moisture** is best measured by **microwave/SAR** sensors — option **(4)**.
Example: **NISAR**'s **L- and S-band radar**.
xa: Microwave/SAR also sees **through cloud and darkness**.
**SLUSI** maps soil resources from satellite data.
The **SAC drought geoportal** tracks **soil moisture** with rainfall and temperature.

45.s: Resourcesat-series data are useful for
o: crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming
45.x: Resourcesat data support crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming.
45.tq: Choose the option containing the linked agricultural and land-resource applications.
xs: **Resourcesat** data serve **crop acreage**, **watershed management** and **precision farming** — option **(2)**.
Navigation is **NavIC**; fishermen messaging is **Nabhmitra**; ocean forecasts come from **INCOIS**.
xa: Resourcesat is a **passive** (sunlight) sensor system.
**CROP** framework used **Resourcesat-2A** with **EOS-04** and **EOS-06** for the wheat estimate.
**SLUSI** maps soil resources from satellite data.

2. It makes ISRO's crop-forecasting methods operational.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **MNCFC** was set up in **2012**, not 2005.
Statement 2 is correct: MNCFC **makes ISRO's crop-forecasting methods operational**.
