Prithvi means **Earth**.

48.s: Which one of the following is the IGMDP missile that was never inducted?
48.x: Trishul is the IGMDP missile that was never inducted; its programme was shut in 2008.
48.tq: Use the distinctive exception within the IGMDP missile group.
xs: **Trishul** is the IGMDP missile **never inducted** — option **(3)**.
It was **shut on 27 Feb 2008** after failing operational requirements, with **delays** and **cost overruns**.
**Prithvi**, **Akash** and **Agni** are all in service.
xa: Replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Barak-1** (Navy), **Akash** (Army).
Indigenous successor: **QRSAM**.
⚠ First IGMDP missile = **Prithvi**.

48.s: The user trial of Agni-4 reported in August 2026 was conducted from which location?
48.x: The Agni-4 user trial was conducted at Chandipur on 6 August 2026 (reported 7 August 2026).
48.tq: Chandipur - Odisha's missile test range.
xs: The **Agni-4** routine user trial was at **Chandipur** (**ITR**), on **6 Aug 2026** — option **(3)**.
It was reported on **7 Aug 2026**, under the **Strategic Forces Command**.
**Pokhran** is a field firing range in **Rajasthan**.
xa: **Agni-IV**: about **4,000 km**, two-stage solid, road-mobile.
**Agni-1** test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
Advanced Agni with **MIRV**: **8 May 2026**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a ballistic missile from a cruise missile?
o: A ballistic missile is powered throughout its flight, whereas a cruise missile is powered only during boost phase.
A ballistic missile follows a high parabolic trajectory after boost, whereas a cruise missile remains powered and generally flies at low altitude using aerodynamic lift.
A ballistic missile uses only aerodynamic lift, whereas a cruise missile follows a free-fall arc.
Both ballistic and cruise missiles follow the same powered, low-altitude trajectory.
49.x: A ballistic missile is powered mainly during the boost phase and subsequently follows a high parabolic or free-fall trajectory. A cruise missile is powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift while flying at relatively low altitude.
49.tq: Use the propulsion and flight-path contrast to separate the two missile classes.
xs: A **ballistic missile** is rocket-powered only in the **boost phase**, then follows a **high parabolic path**; a **cruise missile** stays **powered throughout** and flies low using **aerodynamic lift** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two; option (3) wrongly gives lift to the ballistic missile.
Cruise missiles are **air-breathing** and fly at **constant speed** and **low altitude**.
xa: Ballistic examples: **Agni**, **Prithvi**, **Pralay**.
Cruise examples: **BrahMos**, **Nirbhay**.
⚠ **Pralay** is **quasi-ballistic** with **manoeuvrable re-entry**.

49.s: Hypersonic speed is generally defined as speed exceeding
49.x: Hypersonic flight refers to speeds greater than Mach 5.
49.tq: Identify the standard threshold associated with the technical term.
xs: **Hypersonic** means faster than **Mach 5** — option **(2)**.
**BrahMos** at **Mach 2.8-3.0** is only **supersonic**.
xa: **HGV**: rocket-boosted, then **glides at Mach 5+** and manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere.
**HSTDV** flew at **Mach 6+**; **LR-AShM** peaks at **Mach 10**.
Hypersonic examples: **BrahMos-II**, **LR-AShM**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV):
1. It is initially rocket-boosted.
2. It subsequently glides and manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere.
3. Its manoeuvrability makes interception more difficult.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: An HGV is rocket-boosted before gliding and manoeuvring at hypersonic speed in the upper atmosphere. Its manoeuvrability and flight profile make interception difficult.
49.tq: Check whether all three statements describe successive stages and the resulting advantage.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: an **HGV** is first **rocket-boosted**.
Statement 2: it then **glides at Mach 5+** and **manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere**.
Statement 3: this manoeuvring makes it **hard to intercept**.
xa: **LR-AShM** is a **hypersonic glide** anti-ship missile for **Navy coastal batteries**.
LR-AShM averages **Mach 5** via "**skipping**" manoeuvres, peaking at **Mach 10**.
⚠ **FOBS** places a warhead in a **partial low orbit** — different from an HGV.

49.s: Which one of the following statements about the HSTDV is correct?
o: It flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection above 2,000°C.
It flew at speeds below Mach 2 and tested only navigation systems.
It is a submarine-launched missile with a range of 3,500 km.
It is an air-defence interceptor tested only in the endo-atmospheric layer.
49.x: India's HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection at temperatures exceeding 2,000°C.
49.tq: Use the distinctive speed and thermal-performance figures to identify the correct statement.
xs: **HSTDV** flew at **Mach 6+** and validated **scramjet combustion** and **thermal protection above 2,000°C** — option **(1)**.
It is a **Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle**, not an interceptor or a submarine-launched missile.
xa: HSTDV uses an **indigenous scramjet** (supersonic combustion, **no rotating parts**).
A scramjet combustor ran for **over 12 minutes** (**Jan 2026**).
⚠ **HSTDV** = scramjet demonstrator (**Mach 6+**); **LR-AShM** = glide missile (peak **Mach 10**).

49.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a scramjet?
o: A solid-fuel motor designed only for submarine-launched missiles.
A jet engine in which combustion occurs at subsonic speed after the air is completely stopped.
A propulsion system using supersonic combustion and having no rotating parts.
A rocket engine that carries all oxygen required for combustion.
49.x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and does not have rotating compressor or turbine parts. It is distinct from a rocket, which carries its oxidiser.
49.tq: Break the propulsion term into its defining combustion characteristic.
xs: A **scramjet** uses **supersonic combustion** and has **no rotating parts** — option **(3)**.
India's **HSTDV** used an **indigenous scramjet**.
xa: HSTDV flew at **Mach 6+**, with thermal protection above **2,000°C**.
**Jan 2026**: a scramjet combustor ran **over 12 minutes**.
Compare **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet): also uses **atmospheric air** for combustion.

49.s: The first flight-trial of India's long-range hypersonic missile was reported on
49.x: India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on 16 November 2024.
49.tq: Separate closely spaced test dates by linking each date to its specific programme.
xs: India's **first long-range hypersonic missile** had its first flight-trial on **16 November 2024** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **11 Mar 2024** is **Mission Divyastra** (first **MIRV** test on **Agni-V**).
xa: **LR-AShM**: range ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, **two-stage solid motor**.
LR-AShM was shown at the **77th Republic Day Parade**.
AP coast ranges were used for **LRAShM** validation rounds (**Jan 2026**).

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reported flight characteristics of the long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile?
o: It uses skipping manoeuvres, with peak speed around Mach 10 and average speed around Mach 5.
It remains stationary in low orbit before descending vertically at Mach 3.
It flies only in a high parabolic arc, with average speed below Mach 2.
It uses underwater propulsion and approaches the target at subsonic speed.
49.x: The missile is reported to use skipping manoeuvres, with a peak speed of about Mach 10 and an average speed of about Mach 5.
49.tq: Use the peak-versus-average speed distinction to avoid reversing the figures.
xs: The missile uses **skipping manoeuvres**, with **peak Mach 10** and **average Mach 5** — option **(1)**.
This is the **LR-AShM**, a **hypersonic glide anti-ship missile** for **Navy coastal batteries**.
xa: Range: **1,500+ km**; **two-stage solid motor**.
First long-range hypersonic missile trial: **16 Nov 2024**.
⚠ **HSTDV** (**Mach 6+**) is a scramjet demonstrator, not LR-AShM.

49.s: Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology is intended mainly for
49.x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.
49.tq: Match the propulsion system with its stated operational application.
xs: **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet) is meant for **long-range air-to-air missiles** — option **(2)**.
It uses **atmospheric air for combustion** and was demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
xa: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** is being built with an **SFDR** engine, range **350+ km**.
⚠ **BrahMos** uses a **liquid ramjet**; SFDR is a **solid fuel** ramjet.
**Astra Mk-2** uses a **dual-pulse solid motor** (about **200 km**).

49.s: What is the principal feature of a Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) system?
o: Several missiles are permanently linked to one satellite for navigation.
A missile remains in a complete geostationary orbit before re-entry.
One warhead is divided into several non-explosive decoys only.
One missile carries several warheads capable of being directed towards different targets.
49.x: A MIRV allows one missile to carry multiple warheads, each capable of being directed at a different target.
49.tq: Expand the acronym and connect each term to its operational meaning.
xs: A **MIRV** lets **one missile carry several warheads** aimed at **different targets** — option **(4)**.
MIRV = **Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicles**.
xa: First tested on **Agni-V** in **Mission Divyastra** (**11 Mar 2024**).
⚠ **FOBS** is different: a warhead in a **partial low orbit**, approaching from an unexpected direction.
**HGV**: rocket-boosted, glides at **Mach 5+**.

49.s: Which one of the following best explains the Fractional Orbital Bombardment System (FOBS)?
o: A missile remains permanently in a complete orbit and cannot re-enter the atmosphere.
A warhead is placed into a partial orbit and can approach its target from an unexpected direction.
A cruise missile travels only through underwater channels before striking a target.
Several warheads are released from an aircraft without entering orbit.
49.x: In FOBS, the warhead enters a partial low orbit and can descend towards the target from an unexpected or different direction.
49.tq: Distinguish partial orbit from complete orbit and identify the direction-of-approach advantage.
xs: In **FOBS**, a warhead is placed in a **partial low orbit** and approaches from an **unexpected direction** — option **(2)**.
It does not stay in a complete orbit, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: FOBS = **Fractional Orbital Bombardment System**.
⚠ **MIRV** = one missile, several warheads, different targets.
**HGV** manoeuvres in the upper atmosphere at **Mach 5+** — hard to intercept.

49.s: Which one of the following speed classifications is correctly matched?
o: Nirbhay — subsonic; BrahMos — supersonic; BrahMos-II — hypersonic
Nirbhay — supersonic; BrahMos — subsonic; BrahMos-II — ballistic
Nirbhay — hypersonic; BrahMos — subsonic; BrahMos-II — supersonic
Nirbhay — ballistic; BrahMos — hypersonic; BrahMos-II — subsonic
49.x: Nirbhay is subsonic, BrahMos is supersonic, and BrahMos-II is associated with hypersonic technology.
49.tq: Arrange the missiles by speed class without confusing cruise and ballistic categories.
xs: **Nirbhay — subsonic**, **BrahMos — supersonic**, **BrahMos-II — hypersonic** — option **(1)**.
Nirbhay is a **turbojet**-powered subsonic cruise missile; BrahMos flies at **Mach 2.8-3.0** with a **liquid ramjet**.
**BrahMos-II** is planned at **Mach 5** or more (up to **Mach 7**).
xa: ⚠ **Nirbhay** = subsonic, turbojet; **BrahMos** = supersonic, ramjet.
**LR-AShM** is also in the **hypersonic** class.
**BrahMos-NG**: lighter (**about 1.5 t**), about **Mach 3.5**.

49.s: India's first flight test of a missile with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology, Mission Divyastra (11 March 2024), used which missile?
49.x: Mission Divyastra (11 Mar 2024) was the first MIRV test, carried out on Agni-V. Prithvi-II is a short-range ballistic missile, BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile, and K-4 is a submarine-launched missile; none was the Divyastra MIRV platform.
49.tq: Divyastra = Agni-V + MIRV, 11 Mar 2024.
xs: **Mission Divyastra** (**11 Mar 2024**) tested **MIRV** on **Agni-V** — option **(1)**.
**Prithvi** is a ballistic SRBM and **BrahMos** a **supersonic cruise missile** — neither was the MIRV platform.
xa: MIRV = one missile, **several warheads**, **different targets**.
Agni, Prithvi and Pralay are **ballistic** missiles.
⚠ **FOBS** uses a **partial low orbit** — not the same as MIRV.

49.s: The Inter-Governmental Agreement that led to the creation of BrahMos Aerospace was signed in:
49.x: The Inter-Governmental Agreement for BrahMos Aerospace was signed in Moscow in 1998.
49.tq: Use the exact year associated with the agreement rather than the missile’s first test year.
xs: The **Inter-Governmental Agreement** creating BrahMos Aerospace was signed in **Moscow** in **1998** — option **(2)**.
**2001** was the **first successful test** (**12 June 2001**, Chandipur).
xa: BrahMos is an **India-Russia** joint venture (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
Ownership: **DRDO 50.5%** + **NPOM, Russia 49.5%**.
Name: **Brahmaputra + Moskva** rivers.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the ownership pattern of BrahMos Aerospace?
49.x: BrahMos Aerospace is owned by DRDO with a 50.5% share and NPOM of Russia with a 49.5% share.
49.tq: Compare the ownership percentages carefully and distinguish DRDO from ISRO and NPOM from other Russian agencies.
xs: **DRDO 50.5%** and **NPOM, Russia 49.5%** — option **(2)**.
**NPOM** = **NPO Mashinostroyeniya**; the partner is **DRDO**, not ISRO.
xa: The IGA was signed in **Moscow** in **1998**.
⚠ "BrahMos is developed by India and ___" → **Russia** (APPSC G2 **2025**).
First buyer: **Philippines**, **$375 million** deal (**2022**).

49.s: The first successful test of BrahMos was conducted at:
49.x: The first successful test of BrahMos took place at Chandipur in Odisha on 12 June 2001.
49.tq: Separate the first successful test site from later test locations and launch centres.
xs: BrahMos was first successfully tested at **Chandipur, Odisha**, on **12 June 2001** — option **(2)**.
**Balasore** is in **Odisha**, not West Bengal; **Pokhran** is in **Rajasthan**.
xa: **SFDR** was also demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
BrahMos speed: **Mach 2.8-3.0**.
Original range **290 km**, raised to **290-400 km** in extended versions.

49.s: BrahMos is classified as a supersonic cruise missile because its speed is approximately:
49.x: BrahMos has a speed of about Mach 2.8–3.0, placing it in the supersonic category. Mach 5 and above is associated with hypersonic technology.
49.tq: Match the numerical speed range with the correct missile classification.
xs: BrahMos flies at **Mach 2.8-3.0** (~**3,400-3,700 km/h**) — option **(2)**.
That is **supersonic**; **hypersonic** starts above **Mach 5**.
It is one of the **fastest cruise missiles** in the world.
xa: **BrahMos-II**: planned **hypersonic**, up to **Mach 7**.
**BrahMos-NG**: about **Mach 3.5**, lighter (**about 1.5 t** against **2.5 t**).
Warhead: **200-300 kg**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about BrahMos:
1. It uses a solid booster followed by a liquid ramjet.
2. Its navigation combines inertial navigation with satellite navigation.
3. It is launched from a Transport Launch Canister and follows a fire-and-forget principle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. BrahMos uses a solid booster and liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and can be fired from a Transport Launch Canister in fire-and-forget mode.
49.tq: Verify each statement independently by separating propulsion, navigation and launch-control features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: propulsion is a **solid booster** then a **liquid ramjet**.
Statement 2: navigation is **inertial + satellite** (GPS/GLONASS).
Statement 3: it is **fire-and-forget** from a **Transport Launch Canister**.
xa: It cruises at ~**15 km** and dives to **10 m** in the terminal phase.
It has a **low radar cross-section**.
⚠ **Nirbhay** uses a **turbojet**, not a ramjet.

49.s: Which of the following statements regarding the flight profile of BrahMos is correct?
o: It remains above 50 km throughout its flight to avoid radar detection.
It flies only in a ballistic trajectory without a terminal dive.
It cruises at about 15 km and dives to about 10 m during the terminal phase.
It cruises at about 10 m throughout its flight and rises to 15 km at the terminal phase.
49.x: BrahMos cruises at approximately 15 km altitude and descends to about 10 m during the terminal phase. It also has a low radar cross-section.
49.tq: Track the sequence of the flight profile from cruise altitude to terminal altitude.
xs: BrahMos **cruises at about 15 km** and **dives to about 10 m** in the terminal phase — option **(3)**.
It is a **cruise missile**, so it does not follow a ballistic path; option (4) reverses the profile.
xa: BrahMos has a **low radar cross-section**.
Range: **290 km** originally, **290-400 km** in extended-range versions.
First reported combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**).

49.s:
With reference to BrahMos variants, consider the following statements:
1. The base BrahMos can be launched from land, ships, submarines and aircraft.
2. BrahMos-NG is lighter than the base BrahMos and is intended for platforms such as Tejas.
3. BrahMos-II is a planned hypersonic variant capable of speeds above Mach 5.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. The base system has land, ship, submarine and air-launched versions; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms including Tejas; and BrahMos-II is planned as a hypersonic missile.
49.tq: Use the platform and speed clues to distinguish the base, NG and BrahMos-II variants.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: base BrahMos can be launched from **land, ship, submarine and air** (**Su-30MKI**).
Statement 2: **BrahMos-NG** is lighter (**about 1.5 t** against **2.5 t**), for **Tejas**, smaller warships and submarines.
Statement 3: **BrahMos-II** is planned **hypersonic**, above **Mach 5** (up to **Mach 7**).
xa: **P-17A frigates** carry BrahMos.
BrahMos-NG flies at about **Mach 3.5**.
**Land-attack** BrahMos uses **mobile launchers** (Army).

49.s: The extended-range version of BrahMos is associated with a range of approximately:
49.x: Extended-range BrahMos versions have a range of about 400 km or more, with the range described as approximately 450 km after India’s entry into the MTCR in 2016.
49.tq: Distinguish the original range from the later extended-range figure.
xs: Extended-range BrahMos reaches about **400-450 km** — option **(3)**.
The range rose from **290 km** to ~**450 km** after India joined the **MTCR** (**2016**).
**1,500 km** is the range of the **LR-AShM**.
xa: Original BrahMos range: **290 km**.
MTCR covers missiles carrying **500 kg** over **300 km**.
Warhead: **200-300 kg**.

49.s: BrahMos was reportedly used in combat for the first time during:
49.x: The first reported combat use of BrahMos was during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
49.tq: Link the operation name with its reported year and avoid substituting another Indian military operation.
xs: BrahMos was first reportedly used in combat in **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**) — option **(4)**.
The notes do not link the other operations to BrahMos.
xa: **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility, Lucknow** was inaugurated on **11 May 2025**.
First BrahMos export: **Philippines** (**$375 million**, **2022**).
**UAE**: early-stage talks on **BrahMos** and **Akashteer** (**23 Jun 2026**).

49.s: The name 'BrahMos' is derived from which of the following?
o: Brahma and Moscow, the god and the city
The Brahmaputra river and the Mosul region
49.x: BrahMos combines the names of the Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia) rivers, reflecting the India-Russia joint venture. It is not named after a deity and Moscow, not after Mosul, and not after the company names.
49.tq: Brahma(putra) + Mos(kva) = two rivers.
xs: BrahMos = **Brahmaputra + Moskva** rivers — option **(1)**.
The name reflects the **India-Russia** joint venture.
xa: Ownership: **DRDO 50.5%**, **NPOM (NPO Mashinostroyeniya)** **49.5%**.
IGA signed in **Moscow**, **1998**.
First successful test: **12 June 2001**, **Chandipur**.

49.s: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility inaugurated on 11 May 2025 is located at
49.x: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility at Lucknow (in the UP defence corridor) was inaugurated on 11 May 2025, with the first batch flagged off within five months. Hyderabad and Nagpur are other defence-industry centres, and Chandipur is the test range where BrahMos was first tested in 2001.
49.tq: BrahMos unit = Lucknow, UP corridor.
xs: The **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility** is at **Lucknow**, inaugurated **11 May 2025** — option **(2)**.
Its **first batch** was flagged off **within five months**.
**Chandipur** is the test range where BrahMos was **first tested** (**2001**).
xa: First combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**).
First export customer: **Philippines**.
BrahMos-NG is meant for **Tejas**, smaller warships and submarines.

49.s: Nirbhay is best described as India's
49.x: Nirbhay is a subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile, also described as LR-LACM.
49.tq: Separate the missile by speed class, range and mission in one step.
xs: **Nirbhay** is India's **subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile (LR-LACM)** — option **(3)**.
It is not hypersonic, not an interceptor and not air-to-air.
xa: Range ~**1,000 km**; **turbojet** powered.
Navigation: **inertial + GPS/NavIC**.
Successor: **ITCM**, with the **Manik** small turbofan engine.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nirbhay:
1. It has an approximate range of 1,000 km.
2. It is powered by a turbojet.
3. It can carry conventional or nuclear warheads.
4. Its approximate payload is 200–300 kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Nirbhay has an approximate range of 1,000 km, uses a turbojet, can carry conventional or nuclear warheads, and has a payload of about 200–300 kg.
49.tq: Verify range, propulsion, warhead and payload as separate technical attributes.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Nirbhay**: range ~**1,000 km**, **turbojet** powered.
It can carry **conventional or nuclear warheads**, payload ~**200-300 kg**.
xa: It **hugs the terrain** at low altitude to **evade radar**.
⚠ **Nirbhay** = subsonic, turbojet; **BrahMos** = supersonic, ramjet.
The family is now called **LR-LACM** (**Jun 2026**).

49.s: Nirbhay's low-altitude terrain-hugging flight primarily helps it to
49.x: Nirbhay hugs the terrain at low altitude, which helps it evade or reduce radar detection.
49.tq: Connect the flight profile with its tactical purpose.
xs: Nirbhay's **terrain-hugging** low-altitude flight helps it **evade radar** — option **(2)**.
It uses **inertial + GPS/NavIC** navigation, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Nirbhay is **subsonic**, range ~**1,000 km**.
**BrahMos** also dives to **10 m** in its terminal phase, with a **low radar cross-section**.
Critics say long-range missiles (Agni, **Nirbhay LR-LACM**, BrahMos) are **not yet fully integrated** (**30 Jun 2026**).

49.s: The Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM) is regarded as the successor to Nirbhay and uses the indigenous
49.x: ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous Manik small turbofan engine developed by GTRE.
49.tq: Use the successor-engine pairing to distinguish ITCM from other propulsion programmes.
xs: **ITCM** (Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile), the Nirbhay successor, uses the **Manik small turbofan engine** — option **(3)**.
The Manik engine is from **GTRE**.
**SFDR** is for **Astra Mk-3**; the **scramjet** is in **HSTDV**.
xa: The family is now called **Long-Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LR-LACM)** (**Jun 2026**).
Nirbhay itself is **turbojet** powered.

49.s: Astra is best classified as which one of the following?
o: A man-portable anti-tank guided missile with a laser seeker
A short-range surface-to-surface missile with an inertial seeker
A beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile family developed by DRDO with an active radar seeker
A ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile with an infrared seeker
49.x: Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.
49.tq: Identify the weapon by class, developer and seeker type.
xs: **Astra** is a **DRDO** family of **Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missiles (BVRAAM)** with an **active radar seeker** — option **(3)**.
The man-portable ATGM is **MPATGM**; the ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile is Russia's **Zircon**.
xa: **BVR** = engaging beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.
**Astra Mk-1** is on the **Su-30MKI**, planned for **Tejas Mk-1A** and **Rafale**.
**Indonesia** is the first Astra buyer (**Jul 2026**).

49.s: In the context of Astra missiles, BVR refers to the ability to engage targets beyond approximately:
49.x: Beyond Visual Range means engagement beyond 20 nautical miles, approximately 37 km.
49.tq: Convert the stated nautical-mile threshold into its paired kilometre value.
xs: **BVR** means engaging beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)** — option **(2)**.
Astra is a **Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile** family.
xa: **Astra Mk-2**: about **200 km**, **dual-pulse solid motor**.
**Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'**: **SFDR**, **350+ km**.

49.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes Astra Mk-1?
o: About 700–1,900 km range and nuclear capability
80–110 km range, Mach 4.5 speed and altitude up to 20 km
About 200 km range and a dual-pulse solid motor
More than 350 km range and an SFDR engine
49.x: Astra Mk-1 has a range of 80–110 km, a speed of Mach 4.5 and an altitude capability up to 20 km.
49.tq: Match the variant with its distinctive range, speed and altitude figures.
xs: **Astra Mk-1**: **80-110 km** range, **Mach 4.5**, altitude up to **20 km** — option **(2)**.
About **200 km** + dual-pulse motor is **Astra Mk-2**; **350+ km** + SFDR is **Astra Mk-3**.
**700-1,900 km** nuclear-capable is **Shaurya**.
xa: ADA test-fired Astra from an **LCA AF Mk1 prototype** on **12 Mar 2025**.
Astra Mk-1 is the first Astra export, to **Indonesia** (**Jul 2026**).
**VL-SRSAM** for Navy ships is **derived from Astra**.

49.s:
With reference to Astra variants, consider the following statements:
1. Astra Mk-2 uses a dual-pulse solid motor.
2. Astra Mk-2 has a stated range of about 200 km in the latest specification.
3. Astra Mk-3, also called Gandiva, is under development with an SFDR engine and a range exceeding 350 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Astra Mk-2 has a dual-pulse solid motor and an approximately 200 km range in the latest specification. Astra Mk-3 or Gandiva is under development with a solid fuel ducted ramjet engine and a range above 350 km.
49.tq: Separate present specifications from the older range figure and identify the development-stage variant.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Astra Mk-2** has a **dual-pulse solid motor** and about **200 km** range (older notes say **160 km**).
Statement 3: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** is under development with an **SFDR** engine and **350+ km** range.
xa: **SFDR** uses atmospheric air and was demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
BVR = beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.

49.s: Which one of the following missiles is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile designed to home passively on radar emissions?
49.x: Rudram-I is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile. It passively homes on radar emissions to destroy enemy radars and communication sites.
49.tq: Identify the missile from its distinctive operational role.
xs: **Rudram-I** is India's **first indigenous anti-radiation missile** — option **(3)**.
It **homes passively on radar emissions** to **destroy enemy radars and communication sites** (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
**Pralay** is a quasi-ballistic SSM; **QRSAM** and **VSHORADS** are air-defence missiles.
xa: Rudram-I is **air-to-surface**, fired from the **Su-30MKI**, range **100-200 km**.
⚠ Rudram-I attacks **radars**; **Mission Shakti**'s interceptor attacked a **satellite**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about Pralay:
1. It is a quasi-ballistic short-range surface-to-surface missile.
2. It has a stated range of 150–500 km.
3. It uses a conventional warhead and has manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Pralay is a quasi-ballistic short-range tactical surface-to-surface missile with a 150–500 km range, conventional warhead and manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
49.tq: Check each technical characteristic before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Pralay** is a **quasi-ballistic short-range surface-to-surface** (tactical SSM) missile.
Range **150-500 km**, **conventional warhead**, **manoeuvrable re-entry**.
xa: A **salvo** of two Pralay missiles was fired on **31 Dec 2025**.
**Prahaar**: ~**150 km** tactical ballistic missile.
**Shaurya**: hypersonic, **700-1,900 km**, nuclear-capable.

49.s: Which one of the following missiles is a canister-launched, hypersonic, nuclear-capable surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km?
49.x: Shaurya is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.
49.tq: Use the range and launch-mode clues to identify the missile.
xs: **Shaurya** is a **canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface** tactical missile, about **700-1,900 km**, **nuclear-capable** — option **(2)**.
**Prahaar** is ~**150 km**; **Pralay** is **150-500 km** with a conventional warhead.
xa: **Pralay**: quasi-ballistic, **manoeuvrable re-entry**; salvo on **31 Dec 2025**.
**Rudram-I**: first indigenous **anti-radiation** missile.
Hypersonic = faster than **Mach 5**.

49.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: VL-SRSAM — Vertical-launch short-range SAM for Navy ships
QRSAM — Man-portable system against low-altitude threats
49.x: VL-SRSAM is a vertical-launch short-range surface-to-air missile intended for Navy ships and derived from Astra.
49.tq: Start with the platform and role that are most specific.
xs: **VL-SRSAM** — **Vertical-launch short-range SAM** for **Navy ships** is correct — option **(1)**.
**QRSAM** is the **mid-range layer of IADWS** (not man-portable); **VSHORADS** is the **man-portable** one.
**MPATGM** is an **anti-tank** missile, not a SAM.
xa: VL-SRSAM is **derived from Astra**; its weapon control system was tested on a naval ship (**2026**).
**VSHORADS** buy was **DAC-approved** in **Jul 2026**.
**QRSAM** guards against **low-flying aerial threats** (Army).

49.s: QRSAM is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: The mid-range layer of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System
A man-portable system for very short-range air defence
49.x: QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, forms the mid-range layer of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System.
49.tq: Expand the abbreviation and connect it with its system role.
xs: **QRSAM** is the **mid-range layer of IADWS** — option **(2)**.
The man-portable very short-range system is **VSHORADS**; the anti-radiation missile is **Rudram-I**.
xa: QRSAM = **Quick Reaction SAM**, against **low-flying aerial threats**, for the Army.
**VL-SRSAM**: vertical-launch short-range SAM for **Navy ships**.
**MPATGM**: third-generation **fire-and-forget** ATGM.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: MPATGM — Third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile
Prahaar — About 150 km tactical ballistic missile
VSHORADS — Man-portable air-defence system against low-altitude threats
49.x: LRGB Gaurav is a 1,000 kg glide bomb with a range of about 100 km, released from the Su-30MKI. The 120 km guided rocket is Pinaka LRGR-120.
49.tq: Find the swapped identity between two nearby weapon systems.
xs: **LRGB Gaurav — 120 km guided rocket** is wrong — option **(3)**.
**LRGB 'Gaurav'** is a **1,000 kg glide bomb**, ~**100 km**, released from the **Su-30MKI** (**Apr 2025**).
The **120 km** guided rocket is **Pinaka LRGR-120**, first flown **29 Dec 2025**.
xa: **Prahaar**: ~**150 km** tactical ballistic missile.
**MPATGM**: man-portable, third-generation **fire-and-forget**.
**VSHORADS**: man-portable defence against **low-altitude threats**.

49.s:
With reference to MPATGM, consider the following statements:
1. It is man-portable.
2. It is a third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile.
3. Its procurement was approved by the Defence Acquisition Council in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: MPATGM is a man-portable, third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile; its procurement was approved by the DAC in July 2026.
49.tq: Combine a weapon classification with its procurement milestone.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**MPATGM** is **man-portable** and a **third-generation fire-and-forget** ATGM.
Its procurement was **approved by the DAC** in **Jul 2026**, after flight tests.
xa: **VSHORADS** buy was also **DAC-approved** in **Jul 2026**.
**Pralay** salvo of two: **31 Dec 2025**.
**NASM-MR** maiden flight: **14 Jun 2026**.

49.s:
Which of the following statements about the new anti-ship missiles is correct?
1. NASM-SR is India's first indigenous helicopter-launched anti-ship missile.
2. NASM-SR uses an imaging infrared seeker.
3. NASM-MR had its maiden flight on 14 June 2026.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
49.x: NASM-SR is the first indigenous helicopter-launched anti-ship missile and uses an imaging infrared seeker. NASM-MR had its maiden flight on 14 June 2026.
49.tq: Verify the weapon role, seeker type and dated milestone separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**NASM-SR** is India's **first indigenous helicopter-launched anti-ship missile**, with an **IIR seeker**.
**NASM-MR** had its **maiden flight** on **14 Jun 2026**.
xa: **LR-AShM** is the **hypersonic glide** anti-ship missile, ~**1,500 km**.
Multi-layered **BMD + NASM-MR** tests were held in **Jun 2026**.
**Rudram-I** is the first indigenous **anti-radiation** missile.

49.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
A. Rudram
B. Mission Shakti
C. Philippines
D. Indonesia

List-II
1. First Astra buyer
2. Fourth country to demonstrate an ASAT capability
3. First BrahMos buyer
4. First indigenous anti-radiation missile

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
49.x: Rudram is the first indigenous anti-radiation missile; Mission Shakti made India the fourth ASAT nation; the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer; and Indonesia was the first Astra buyer.
49.tq: Start from the sure pair Rudram–first indigenous anti-radiation missile and eliminate codes that disturb it.
xs: **Rudram** = **first indigenous anti-radiation missile**; **Mission Shakti** made India the **fourth ASAT country**.
**Philippines** = **first BrahMos buyer**; **Indonesia** = **first Astra buyer**.
xa: Philippines BrahMos deal: **$375 million** (**2022**), deliveries from **2024**.
Indonesia deal (**Jul 2026**) = **first-ever export** of the Astra family (**Astra Mk-1**).
Mission Shakti: **27 March 2019**, after **USA, Russia and China**.

49.s: Mission Sudarshan Chakra is proposed as a
o: multi-layered air and missile defence network
49.x: Mission Sudarshan Chakra is proposed as a multi-layered network for air and missile defence, with operational maturity targeted by 2035.
49.tq: Identify the programme by its overall strategic role and architecture.
xs: **Mission Sudarshan Chakra** is a proposed **multi-layered air and missile defence network** — option **(3)**.
Its target is **operational maturity by 2035** (**Aug 2026**).
xa: **Project Kusha**: DRDO **long-range** air-defence system.
**Jun 2026**: multi-layered BMD showed India can engage threats **up to ICBM class**.
**QRSAM** is the **mid-range layer of IADWS**.

49.s: Project Kusha refers to a DRDO programme for a
o: hypersonic glide vehicle for space launch
49.x: Project Kusha is DRDO's long-range air-defence system programme.
49.tq: Use the programme's stated defence role to eliminate missile-platform distractors.
xs: **Project Kusha** is DRDO's **long-range air-defence system** — option **(1)**.
It has three interceptors **M1/M2/M3**.
xa: The Defence Minister called it a "**game changer**" (**13 Jun 2026**).
**Kusha LR-SAM** maiden test: **Jul 2026**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the approximate interceptor ranges associated with Project Kusha?
49.x: Project Kusha is associated with three interceptors: M1 of about 150 km, M2 of about 250 km and M3 of about 350–400 km range.
49.tq: Read the progressive range pattern and avoid confusing it with BMD layer altitudes.
xs: These are the three interceptors of **Project Kusha**, DRDO's **long-range** air-defence system.
**15-30 km** is the **AAD** layer and **50-80 km** the **PAD** layer — not Kusha.
xa: The Defence Minister called Kusha a "**game changer**" (**13 Jun 2026**).
**Mission Sudarshan Chakra** targets maturity by **2035**.

49.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (BMD layer)
 a. Phase-I exo-atmospheric
 b. Phase-I endo-atmospheric
 c. Phase-II exo-atmospheric
 d. Phase-II endo-atmospheric
List-II (Interceptor)
 i. AD-1
 ii. AAD/Ashwin
 iii. AD-2
 iv. PAD/Pradyumna
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
49.x: Phase-I exo-atmospheric interception uses PAD/Pradyumna; Phase-I endo-atmospheric interception uses AAD/Ashwin; Phase-II uses AD-1 for exo-atmospheric and AD-2 for endo-atmospheric interception.
49.tq: Start with the familiar PAD-AAD pair and then place the Phase-II interceptors.
xs: **a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
Phase-I **exo** = **PAD / Pradyumna**; Phase-I **endo** = **AAD / Ashwin**.
Phase-II **exo** = **AD-1** (IRBM-class threats); Phase-II **endo** = **AD-2** (under development).
xa: PAD works at **50-80 km**; AAD at **15-30 km**.
⚠ **PAD = Pradyumna = exo**; **AAD = Ashwin = endo**.
Mission Shakti used DRDO's **PDV Mk-II**, from the BMD programme.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two Indian ballistic-missile defence interceptors?
o: PAD is exo-atmospheric at 50–80 km, whereas AAD is endo-atmospheric at 15–30 km.
PAD is endo-atmospheric, whereas AAD is exo-atmospheric.
Both PAD and AAD are anti-tank missiles operating below 10 km.
Both PAD and AAD are surface-to-surface missiles using liquid fuel.
49.x: Prithvi Air Defence or Pradyumna is an exo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 50–80 km altitude, while AAD or Ashwin is an endo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 15–30 km.
49.tq: Discriminate paired systems by atmospheric layer and altitude.
xs: **PAD** is **exo-atmospheric at 50-80 km**; **AAD** is **endo-atmospheric at 15-30 km** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps them; both are BMD **interceptors**, not anti-tank or surface-to-surface missiles.
xa: PAD = **Pradyumna**; AAD = **Ashwin**.
Phase-II: **AD-1** (exo) and **AD-2** (endo, under development).
**14 Jun 2026**: India among few nations able to engage threats **up to ICBM class**.

49.s: Mission Shakti, India’s anti-satellite test, was conducted on:
49.x: India conducted the Mission Shakti anti-satellite test on 27 March 2019.
49.tq: Identify the exact date of the ASAT test rather than the launch date of the target satellite.
xs: **Mission Shakti**, India's **anti-satellite (ASAT)** test, was held on **27 March 2019** — option **(2)**.
It made India the **fourth country** with ASAT capability.
xa: It was a joint mission of **DRDO and ISRO** (APPSC-G1 **2022**).
Interceptor: DRDO **PDV Mk-II**, from the ballistic missile defence programme.
Target: live satellite **Microsat-R** in **LEO** at about **283 km**.
Microsat-R was launched by ISRO's **PSLV-C44** in **Jan 2019**.

49.s: Mission Shakti was a joint mission involving which two Indian organisations?
49.x: Mission Shakti is described as a joint mission of the Defence Research and Development Organisation and the Indian Space Research Organisation.
49.tq: Use the institutional-role clue to distinguish defence research from aerospace manufacturing bodies.
xs: Mission Shakti was a joint mission of **DRDO and ISRO** — option **(1)**.
PYQs (APPSC-G1 **2022**) describe it as a **DRDO-ISRO** programme.
xa: DRDO supplied the **PDV Mk-II** interceptor.
ISRO's **PSLV-C44** had launched the target, **Microsat-R** (a DRDO satellite), in **Jan 2019**.
ASAT = **missile-based system to attack satellites**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the interceptor and its target in Mission Shakti?
49.x: A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.
49.tq: Match the specialised interceptor with the named satellite target instead of a neighbouring missile or satellite programme.
xs: The interceptor was DRDO's **PDV Mk-II** and the target the live satellite **Microsat-R** — option **(4)**.
PDV Mk-II came from the **ballistic missile defence** programme.
**Akash** is a SAM and **Agni-V** a ballistic missile — not the ASAT interceptor.
xa: Microsat-R orbited in **LEO** at about **283 km**.
Microsat-R was a **DRDO satellite** launched by **PSLV-C44** (**Jan 2019**).
⚠ Correct PYQ statement: "destroyed a **live satellite in LEO**".

49.s: At approximately what altitude was the Microsat-R satellite destroyed during Mission Shakti?
49.x: Microsat-R was intercepted in Low Earth Orbit at approximately 283 km, often rounded to about 300 km.
49.tq: Identify the low-LEO altitude and reject geostationary and atmospheric-altitude figures.
xs: **Microsat-R** was destroyed in **Low Earth Orbit** at about **283 km** (~**300 km** in some notes) — option **(4)**.
**80 km** is the top of the **PAD** interception band, far below this orbit.
xa: The low LEO altitude was chosen so the **debris would decay** quickly.
⚠ "Done in the **upper atmosphere** to ensure no debris" is **wrong** (APPSC-G1 **2022**).
Mission Shakti date: **27 March 2019**.

49.s: India became the fourth country to demonstrate an anti-satellite capability. Which of the following shows the three countries that preceded India?
49.x: India became the fourth country with demonstrated ASAT capability after the USA, Russia and China.
49.tq: Use the rank clue to reconstruct the preceding three countries without adding other space powers.
xs: India was the **fourth** ASAT nation, after the **USA, Russia and China** — option **(4)**.
France, Japan, UK and Israel are not named in the notes as ASAT states.
xa: ASAT = **missile-based system to attack satellites**.
India's test: **Mission Shakti**, **27 March 2019**.
Interceptor **PDV Mk-II**; target **Microsat-R**.

49.s: Why was the Mission Shakti interception conducted at a low Low Earth Orbit altitude?
o: To enable the interceptor to operate only in the upper atmosphere
To prevent the satellite from being detected by radar
To ensure that the debris would decay comparatively quickly
To place the debris permanently in geostationary orbit
49.x: The interception was conducted at a low LEO altitude so that the resulting debris would decay relatively quickly. The test was not conducted in the upper atmosphere to guarantee that no debris would be produced.
49.tq: Apply the stated operational rationale and reject the absolute claim that the test created no debris.
xs: The interception was kept at **low LEO altitude** so that **the debris would decay** quickly — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Done in the **upper atmosphere** to ensure no debris" is a **wrong** statement (APPSC-G1 **2022**: I and III correct).
xa: Target altitude: about **283 km** (~**300 km** in some notes).
Target: **Microsat-R**, a **live satellite**.
Joint mission of **DRDO and ISRO**.

49.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
49.x: Spyder is an Israeli system used by the Indian Air Force and replaced Trishul. Iran is associated with Shahab and Fattah, not Spyder.
49.tq: Detect the substituted partner country in a bilateral defence list.
xs: **Spyder — Iran** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**Spyder** is **Israeli**; the **IAF** used it to replace **Trishul**.
Iran's missiles are **Shahab** and **Fattah**.
xa: **Barak-1** (Israel) replaced Trishul for the **Navy**.
**Barak-8 / MRSAM**: DRDO with **Israel Aerospace Industries**, on **P-17A** frigates.
**R-73 Archer** (Russia) is a short-range **air-to-air** missile.

49.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Barak systems is correct?
o: Barak-8 was jointly developed with Russia and deployed only on submarines.
Barak-8 is a man-portable very short-range system.
Barak-1 is an Israeli Navy system that replaced Trishul.
Barak-1 is a Russian short-range air-to-air missile.
49.x: Barak-1 is an Israeli Navy system and replaced Trishul. Barak-8/MRSAM was developed by DRDO with Israel Aerospace Industries and is a medium-range surface-to-air system.
49.tq: Separate the similarly named Barak-1 and Barak-8 systems by partner and role.
xs: **Barak-1** is an **Israeli** Navy system that **replaced Trishul** — option **(3)**.
**Barak-8 / MRSAM** was built by DRDO with **Israel Aerospace Industries** (not Russia), and is a **medium-range SAM**, not man-portable.
The Russian short-range air-to-air missile is **R-73 Archer**.
xa: Barak-8 sits on **P-17A frigates**; its Army version was flight-tested **3-4 Apr 2025**.
**Spyder** (Israel) replaced Trishul for the **IAF**.

49.s: Which one of the following groups contains only missiles associated with Russia?
49.x: BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems. The other groups contain missiles associated with Israel, Iran, North Korea, Pakistan or the United States.
49.tq: Classify each item by partner or country before selecting the complete group.
xs: **BrahMos, R-73 Archer and S-400** are all linked to **Russia** — option **(3)**.
**Barak-1, Spyder, Barak-8** are **Israeli**; **Shahab, Fattah** are **Iranian** and **Hwasong** is **North Korean**.
**Abdali** is **Pakistani** and **Minuteman III** **American**.
xa: **Kinzhal** and **Zircon** are also Russian.
⚠ **Zircon** = ship-launched; **Kinzhal** = air-launched.
BrahMos is a **joint venture**: **DRDO 50.5%**, **NPOM 49.5%**.

49.s: India's first export customer for the BrahMos missile was
49.x: The Philippines became India's first BrahMos export customer through a 2022 deal valued at $375 million.
49.tq: Identify the first customer by distinguishing a completed deal from early-stage talks.
xs: **The Philippines** was India's **first BrahMos export** customer — option **(2)**.
The deal was worth **$375 million** (**2022**), with deliveries from **2024**.
**Indonesia** is the first **Astra** buyer; **UAE** talks are only early-stage.
xa: Indonesia Astra Mk-1 deal (**Jul 2026**) = **first-ever export** of the Astra family.
UAE talks cover **BrahMos** and **Akashteer** (**23 Jun 2026**).
⚠ Philippines = first BrahMos buyer; Indonesia = first Astra buyer.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's missile exports:
1. The Philippines is India's first BrahMos export customer under a 2022 deal, with deliveries from 2024.
2. The Astra Mk-1 deal with Indonesia, signed in July 2026, is the first export of the Astra family.

49.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer (2022 deal, deliveries from 2024). Statement 2 is correct: the Indonesia Astra Mk-1 deal (Jul 2026) is the first Astra-family export. Statement 3 is wrong: with the UAE, BrahMos and Akashteer talks are only at an early stage. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' omits statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
49.tq: Delivered = Philippines (BrahMos); deal signed = Indonesia (Astra); only talks = UAE.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Philippines** — first BrahMos buyer, **2022** deal, deliveries from **2024**.
Statement 2: the **Astra Mk-1** deal with **Indonesia** (**Jul 2026**) is the **first export** of the Astra family.
Statement 3 is wrong: with the **UAE**, BrahMos and Akashteer are only in **early-stage talks**.
xa: Philippines deal value: **$375 million**.
**Akashteer** is an air-defence **control** system.

49.s: Which one of the following missile-country pairs is correctly matched?
49.x: Shahab is an Iranian ballistic missile series. Hwasong is associated with North Korea, Zircon with Russia and Abdali with Pakistan.
49.tq: Use country association to eliminate swapped foreign systems.
xs: **Shahab — Iran** is correct — option **(1)**; Shahab is an Iranian **ballistic missile series**.
**Hwasong** is **North Korean**, **Zircon** is **Russian** and **Abdali** is **Pakistani**.
xa: **Fattah** (Iran): claimed hypersonic missile (**2023**).
**Abdali**: **450 km** SSM, named after **Ahmed Shah Abdali**.
**Minuteman III** (USA): ICBM, the **land leg** of the US triad.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fattah is an Iranian missile claimed to be hypersonic in 2023.
2. Hwasong is a North Korean ICBM/IRBM series.
3. Zircon is a Russian ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct: Fattah is associated with Iran, Hwasong with North Korea, and Zircon with Russia.
49.tq: Test country, missile category and launch mode together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Fattah** — **Iran**, a claimed hypersonic missile (**2023**).
**Hwasong** — **North Korea**, ICBM/IRBM series; **Zircon** — **Russia**, ship-launched hypersonic cruise missile.
xa: ⚠ **Kinzhal** (Russia) is **air-launched**, unlike ship-launched Zircon.
**Shahab** is Iran's ballistic missile series.

49.s: The Minuteman III is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: An American ICBM forming the land leg of the US nuclear triad
49.x: Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.
49.tq: Identify the system from its strategic role rather than its name alone.
xs: **Minuteman III** is an **American ICBM**, the **land leg of the US triad** — option **(2)**.
The **450 km** Pakistani SSM is **Abdali**; the Russian air-launched hypersonic missile is **Kinzhal**; the Iranian claimed hypersonic is **Fattah**.
xa: **Hwasong** is North Korea's ICBM/IRBM series.
**Abdali** (Pakistan) is a **450 km** SSM named after **Ahmed Shah Abdali**.
**Jun 2026**: India's multi-layered BMD showed it can engage threats **up to ICBM class**.

49.s: Which one of the following statements about Kinzhal is correct?
o: It is a Pakistani 450 km surface-to-surface missile.
It is an Iranian ballistic missile series.
It is a North Korean ship-launched cruise missile.
It is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile.
49.x: Kinzhal is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile. Six Kinzhal missiles were reportedly intercepted by Patriot systems in one night over Kyiv in May 2023.
49.tq: Distinguish Kinzhal from the ship-launched Zircon by launch platform.
xs: **Kinzhal** is a **Russian air-launched hypersonic missile** — option **(4)**.
**Patriot** intercepted **six** in one night over **Kyiv** (**May 2023**).
**Abdali** is Pakistani, **Shahab** Iranian; North Korea's series is **Hwasong**.
xa: ⚠ **Zircon** = **ship-launched**; **Kinzhal** = **air-launched** (both Russia).
**Fattah** (Iran) — claimed hypersonic (**2023**).
**S-400** and **R-73 Archer** are also Russian.

49.s: The ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for which of the following purposes?
o: Testing of the Astra export configuration
Demonstration of the first indigenous anti-radiation missile
49.x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.
49.tq: Match the distinctive geographical clue with the specific validation activity rather than with a missile name alone.
xs: AP coast ranges were used for **LRAShM validation rounds** (**Jan 2026**) — option **(2)**.
**LR-AShM** is a **hypersonic glide anti-ship missile** for **Navy coastal batteries**.
xa: LR-AShM: ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, average **Mach 5** via **skipping**.
It was shown at the **77th Republic Day Parade**.
The first indigenous anti-radiation missile is **Rudram-I**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s long-range missile capability:
1. Agni, Nirbhay LR-LACM and BrahMos are identified as long-range systems that are not yet fully integrated.
2. India’s rocket force is still described as a concept rather than an established force.
3. The long-range missile systems are described as fully integrated into an operational rocket force.

49.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reported assessment by changing an incomplete capability into a fully operational one.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **Agni, Nirbhay LR-LACM and BrahMos** are **not yet fully integrated** (**30 Jun 2026**).
Statement 2: the **rocket force** is **still only a concept**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it contradicts both points above.
xa: Another criticism: **hypersonics still maturing**.
**Nirbhay**: subsonic, ~**1,000 km**, **turbojet**.
**Mission Sudarshan Chakra** targets operational maturity by **2035**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's defence 'firsts':
1. Mission Shakti made India the fourth country with anti-satellite capability, after the USA, Russia and China.
2. Indonesia was the first export buyer of BrahMos.
3. The Philippines was the first export buyer of the Astra missile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
49.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mission Shakti (2019) made India the 4th ASAT nation after the USA, Russia and China. Statements 2 and 3 swap the buyers: the Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer, and Indonesia the first Astra buyer (Jul 2026). So '1 only'; the other codes accept one or both swapped statements.
49.tq: Philippines = BrahMos first; Indonesia = Astra first; Shakti = 4th ASAT.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Mission Shakti** made India the **4th ASAT nation** after **USA, Russia and China**.
Statements 2 and 3 swap the buyers: **Philippines** = first **BrahMos** buyer; **Indonesia** = first **Astra** buyer (**Jul 2026**).
xa: Philippines BrahMos deal: **$375 million** (**2022**).

50.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a fission weapon from a fusion (thermonuclear) weapon?

A fusion weapon needs no trigger, while a fission weapon needs a fusion primary to start.
50.x: Fission (atomic) weapons split heavy nuclei (U-235/Pu-239) in a neutron chain reaction, as in Pokhran-I. xs: A **fission** weapon splits heavy nuclei (**U-235 / Pu-239**) in a **chain reaction**; a **fusion** weapon fuses **hydrogen isotopes** with a **fission primary** as trigger — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the two; option (4) reverses the trigger relationship.
xa: Fission example: **Pokhran-I**; fusion was tested in **Pokhran-II**.
