1. The GSI estimated India's coal resources at 389.421 billion tonnes as of 1 April 2024.
2. Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves among the States.
3. The Damodar valley holds about half of India's coal reserves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: GSI put resources at 389.421 BT (1 April 2024) and Jharkhand leads. Statement 3 is wrong: the Damodar valley holds about one-fourth, not half, of India's coal. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses true statement 2, and the other two include false statement 3.
57.tq: 389.421 BT; Jharkhand first; Damodar = one-fourth.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **GSI** put coal resources at **389.421 BT** (**1 Apr 2024**).
Statement 2: **Jharkhand** has the largest reserves.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Damodar** valley holds about **one-fourth**, not half.
xa: Reserves are mainly in **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh**, WB, MP, Telangana, Maharashtra.
⚠ Older notes: about **344 BT** and "**4th largest in the world**".

57.s: India recorded coal production of how much in 2024–25, marking the first year in which production exceeded one billion tonnes?
57.x: India recorded 1,047.50 MT of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.
57.tq: Use the exact production figure and distinguish it from the target and import figures.
xs: Coal output was **1,047.50 MT in 2024-25**, the first year above **1 billion tonnes** — option **(2)**.
xa: Imports fell **7.9%** to **243.62 MT**, saving about **$7.13 billion**.
By Aug 2025 output reached **381.749 MT**.
Coal meets about **55%** of commercial energy needs.

57.s: What was India’s coal production target for 2025–26?
57.x: India’s coal production target for 2025–26 was fixed at 1,157 MT.
57.tq: Separate the future target from the previous year’s actual production.
xs: The **2025-26** target was **1,157 MT** — option **(1)**.
**1,047.50 MT** was the record **2024-25** output.
xa: Output reached **381.749 MT** by **Aug 2025**.
**Coal India Ltd** is the world's largest coal producer.

57.s: Coal accounts for approximately what share of India’s commercial energy needs?
57.x: Coal meets about 55% of India’s commercial energy needs.
57.tq: Distinguish the share in commercial energy needs from the higher share in power generation.
xs: Coal meets about **55%** of India's **commercial energy needs** — option **(3)**.
**About 70%** (some notes **71.4%**) is coal's share of **power generation**, not energy needs.

57.s: Which of the following is the planning arm of Coal India Limited?
57.x: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, abbreviated as CMPDI, functions as Coal India Limited’s planning arm.
57.tq: Test the exact institutional abbreviation rather than the producing subsidiaries.
xs: **CMPDI** is Coal India's **planning arm** — option **(2)**.
**MCL** is a producing subsidiary; **SCCL** is a Telangana-GoI company; **NCDP-2007** was the old linkage regime replaced by **SHAKTI**.
xa: CIL's seven producing subsidiaries: **ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL, MCL**.
**Coal India Ltd** is the world's largest coal producer.

57.s: Which one of the following sets contains all the seven producing subsidiaries of Coal India Limited?
o: ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL
ECL, CMPDI, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and SCCL
BCCL, CCL, MCL, SCCL, NCL, WCL and CMPDI
ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, MCL, SCCL and CMPDI
57.x: The seven producing subsidiaries are ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL. CMPDI is the planning arm and SCCL is not one of these seven subsidiaries.
57.tq: Start with the sure list items and eliminate options containing the planning arm or SCCL.
xs: The seven producing subsidiaries are **ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL** — option **(1)**.
**CMPDI** is the **planning arm**, not a producing subsidiary; **SCCL** is owned **51% Telangana, 49% GoI**.
xa: **Coal India Ltd** is the world's largest coal producer.
**BCGCL** is a **BHEL-CIL** JV for coal gasification (**21 May 2024**).
APGENCO buys washed coal from **MCL**'s **IB Valley Washery**.

57.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
57.x: SCCL is owned 51% by Telangana and 49% by the Government of India.
57.tq: Watch for the reversed ownership percentages and the swapped governments.
xs: **SCCL** is owned **51% by Telangana** and **49% by the Government of India** — option **(1)**.
This follows the **AP Reorganisation Act Schedule**; existing coal linkages continue.
xa: **Singareni** coalfield is in **Telangana**.
APGENCO seeks **better coal from SCCL**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about the SHAKTI coal linkage policy:
1. It was introduced in 2017.
2. It replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
3. Under it, coal linkages are given only through administrative nomination.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: SHAKTI (2017) replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime. Statement 3 is wrong: under SHAKTI, linkages are given through auction or tariff-based bidding, not administrative nomination. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
57.tq: SHAKTI 2017 = auction/tariff-based bidding for linkages.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
**SHAKTI** came in **2017** and replaced the **NCDP-2007** linkage regime.
Statement 3 is wrong: linkages are given through **auction or tariff-based bidding**.
xa: **199 mines** were allocated under the **CMSP Act 2015** and **MMDR Act 1957**.
Revenue-sharing **commercial auctions** began in **2020**.

57.s: Which company is described as the world's largest coal producer?
57.x: Coal India Limited is the world's largest coal producer, working through seven producing subsidiaries with CMPDI as planning arm. SCCL is a Telangana-GoI company, MCL is one of CIL's subsidiaries, and NLC India is mainly a lignite producer.
57.tq: World's largest coal producer = Coal India Ltd.
xs: **Coal India Ltd** is the **world's largest coal producer** — option **(1)**.
**MCL** is one of CIL's seven producing subsidiaries; **SCCL** is a Telangana (**51%**)–GoI (**49%**) company.
xa: Subsidiaries: **ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL, MCL**; **CMPDI** = planning arm.
India produced **1,047.50 MT** in **2024-25**.

57.s: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions in India began in:
57.x: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began in 2020.
57.tq: Place the auction mechanism in time against the nearby years of the CMSP Act, SHAKTI policy and later auction rounds.
xs: Revenue-sharing **commercial coal auctions** began in **2020** — option **(3)**.
**2015** is the **CMSP Act**; **2017** is **SHAKTI**; **2025** saw the **13th round** (**21 Aug 2025**).
xa: After **12 rounds**: **134 mines** sold, peak rated capacity **277.04 MTPA**.
**14th round**: mines to **Reliance Industries + Axis Energy**, first **UCG** clauses (2 May 2026).

57.s: In the 14th round of commercial coal mine auctions, mines went to:
57.x: The 14th round awarded mines to Reliance Industries and Axis Energy.
57.tq: Apply the wrong-owner trap by distinguishing auction awardees from coal-producing public sector entities.
xs: The **14th round** mines went to **Reliance Industries and Axis Energy** — option **(1)**.
Its agreements were the first with **underground coal gasification** clauses (**2 May 2026**).
xa: The **13th round** opened **21 Aug 2025** with **14 mines**.
After **12 rounds**: **134 mines**, **277.04 MTPA** peak capacity.
Commercial auctions (revenue-sharing) began in **2020**.

57.s: The agreements in the 14th round were significant because they were the first agreements to include clauses relating to:
57.x: The 14th-round agreements were the first to include underground coal gasification clauses.
57.tq: Link the special contractual clause with the correct technology rather than with the auction mechanism itself.
xs: 14th-round agreements were the first with **underground coal gasification (UCG)** clauses — option **(4)** (2 May 2026).
**Tariff-based bidding** belongs to the **SHAKTI** linkage policy (**2017**), not these clauses.
xa: **UCG** is an **in-situ** process: air/oxygen + steam injected into coal seams → syngas underground.
UCG uses deep, thin or unmineable coal; risk: **groundwater contamination**.
MoEFCC panel refused to waive the **300 m** minimum depth for UCG pilots.

57.s: A total of 199 coal mines have been allocated under:
o: The CMSP Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957
The Energy Conservation Act and the Electricity Act
57.x: The 199 mines were allocated under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015 and the MMDR Act, 1957.
57.tq: Distinguish the two statutory routes of allocation from the separate linkage policy.
xs: The **199 mines** were allocated under the **CMSP Act 2015** and **MMDR Act 1957** — option **(1)**.
**SHAKTI** (**2017**) deals with **coal linkages**, replacing **NCDP-2007**.
xa: The MMDR amendment made **coking coal** a **Critical and Strategic Mineral** → Centre auctions its leases.
Commercial auctions began **2020**; **134 mines** sold after **12 rounds**.

57.s: Which mineral was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral through an amendment to the MMDR framework, enabling the Centre to auction its leases?
57.x: Coking coal was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral, allowing the Centre to auction its leases.
57.tq: Identify the specific coal variety and avoid substituting the broader category of coal.
xs: **Coking coal** was declared a **Critical and Strategic Mineral** — option **(3)**.
This lets the **Centre** auction its leases under the **MMDR** amendment.
xa: **Jharia** is the largest coking-coal field; coking coal is imported mainly from **Australia**.
Rising **coking-coal imports** are a listed coal-sector problem.
Coking coal is held in **Gondwana** coal.

57.s: Which of the following correctly describes Indian coal?
o: High ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
High ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur
Low ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
Low ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
57.x: Indian coal generally has high ash content, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur content.
57.tq: Track all four quality characteristics without reversing paired properties.
xs: Indian coal: **high ash**, **low calorific value**, **high ash-fusion temperature**, **low sulphur** — option **(2)**.
Ash is **35-45%**; sulphur is only **~0.5%**.
xa: Low **washery** use worsens the quality problem.
APGENCO buys **washed coal** from **MCL's IB Valley Washery** for RTPP and Dr NTTPS.
Experts call for **CFB gasifiers** for high-ash coal.

57.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a problem affecting the Indian coal sector?
o: Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal
57.x: The identified problems include poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports and administrative issues. Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal is not a stated problem.
57.tq: Find the option that reverses the sectoral problem described.
xs: **Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal** is not a problem — option **(1)**; in fact **coking-coal imports are rising**.
Listed problems (BPSC key: all are problems): **poor quality**, **movement bottlenecks**, **low washery use**, **rising coking-coal imports**, **administrative issues**.
xa: Indian coal: **high ash (35-45%)**, low calorific value.
Coking coal comes mainly from **Australia**.

57.s: Disruption of thermal power generation due to rail and logistics delays primarily reflects which problem in the coal sector?
57.x: Rail and logistics delays create movement and evacuation bottlenecks, which can disrupt thermal power generation.
57.tq: Translate the practical situation into the underlying sectoral problem.
xs: Rail/logistics delays reflect **movement and evacuation bottlenecks** — option **(3)**.
These delays often **disrupt thermal power generation**.
xa: Other problems: **poor quality**, **low washery use**, **rising coking-coal imports**, administrative issues.
Coal supplies roughly **70%** of power generation.

57.s: Coking coal is imported mainly from which country, while non-coking coal is obtained mainly from Indonesia and South Africa?
57.x: Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia, whereas non-coking coal comes mainly from Indonesia and South Africa.
57.tq: Keep the source countries of coking and non-coking coal separate.
xs: **Coking coal** comes mainly from **Australia**; **non-coking coal** from **Indonesia and South Africa** — option **(3)**.
Imports fell **7.9%** to **243.62 MT** in 2024-25, saving about **$7.13 billion**.
xa: Coking coal was made a **Critical and Strategic Mineral** under the MMDR amendment.
Gasification-substitutable imports (incl. coking coal) ≈ **₹2.77 lakh crore** in **FY2025**.

57.s: To improve coal quality for its RTPP and Dr NTTPS units, APGENCO buys washed coal from:
57.x: APGENCO buys washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery, posts engineers at mines to stop grade slippage and seeks better coal from SCCL. The other sources are not the ones stated.
57.tq: APGENCO washed coal = MCL IB Valley Washery.
xs: APGENCO buys **washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery** — option **(1)**.
It feeds **RTPP 600 MW** and **Dr NTTPS 500/800 MW** units.
xa: APGENCO also **posts engineers at mines** to stop grade slippage.
It seeks **better coal from SCCL**.
IB Valley (**Deogarh**) is in **Odisha**.

57.s: In coal gasification, coal is converted into syngas by partial oxidation with which of the following at high temperature and pressure?
57.x: Coal is partly oxidised with oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure to produce syngas.
57.tq: Identify the process inputs rather than the products.
xs: In **coal gasification**, coal is partly oxidised with **oxygen and steam** at high temperature and pressure → **syngas** — option **(1)**.
Syngas = **CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2**.
xa: **UCG** does this **in-situ**: air/oxygen + steam injected into coal seams.
Syngas can also run **IGCC** power plants.
**National Coal Gasification Mission**: **100 MT** by **2030**.

57.s: Which one of the following is NOT a constituent of the syngas produced through coal gasification?
57.x: Syngas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide. Ammonia is a product that can be manufactured using syngas, not a stated constituent of syngas.
57.tq: Separate the composition of syngas from products made using syngas.
xs: **Ammonia** is not a constituent of syngas — option **(2)**.
Syngas = **CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2**; ammonia is a **product** made from syngas (for **urea**).
xa: Other products: **SNG, methanol, ethanol, hydrogen, DME, ammonium nitrate**, petrochemicals.
**CBM** ("**sweet gas**") is methane held in coal seams.

57.s:
Which of the following products can be manufactured using coal gasification?
1. Synthetic natural gas
2. Methanol
3. Ammonia for fertilisers
4. Dimethyl ether
Select the correct answer using the code below.
57.x: Coal gasification can produce synthetic natural gas, methanol, ammonia for fertilisers, hydrogen, dimethyl ether, ammonium nitrate and petrochemicals.
57.tq: Use the complete product list to identify the all-inclusive combination.
xs: All four can be made from coal gasification — option **(4)**.
Products: **SNG**, **methanol**, **ammonia for fertilisers (urea)**, **DME**, plus ethanol, hydrogen, ammonium nitrate and petrochemicals.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2025 trap: of ethanol, nitroglycerine and urea, **only two** (ethanol + urea).
**BCGCL** is building a **coal-to-ammonium-nitrate** plant at **Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda**.
**Talcher**: first gasification-based **fertiliser** plant.

57.s: Syngas produced through coal gasification can also be used to operate which of the following power-generation systems?
o: Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle power plants
57.x: Syngas can be used to run Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) power plants.
57.tq: Match the specialised fuel product with its stated power-generation application.
xs: Syngas can run **IGCC (Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle)** power plants — option **(3)**.
Syngas comes from partial oxidation of coal with **oxygen + steam**.
xa: **BHEL** commissioned the first IGCC plant in **1985**.
Syngas = **CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2**.

57.s:
Consider the following substances:
1. Ethanol
2. Nitroglycerine
3. Urea
Which of the substances listed above can be produced through coal gasification?
57.x: Ethanol and urea can be produced through coal gasification. Nitroglycerine is not included among the stated products.
57.tq: Discriminate between direct gasification products and an unrelated chemical.
xs: Only **ethanol and urea** can be made by coal gasification — option **(4)** (UPSC 2025 key: **only two**).
**Nitroglycerine** is not among the gasification products.
xa: Urea comes via **ammonia for fertilisers**.
Other products: **SNG, methanol, hydrogen, DME, ammonium nitrate**.
**Talcher** will host the first gasification-based fertiliser plant (by Dec **2027**).

57.s: The National Coal Gasification Mission aims to gasify how much coal by 2030?
57.x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
57.tq: Recall the mission target and distinguish it from the sub-target under the incentive scheme.
xs: The **National Coal Gasification Mission** aims to gasify **100 million tonnes** of coal by **2030** — option **(1)**.
**75 MT** is what the **₹37,500 crore** surface gasification scheme targets toward that goal.
xa: The Coal Ministry says the target will be met (**26 Apr 2026**).
⚠ EY (Apr 2026): few advanced projects → **100 MT** goal doubtful.
Commercial blocks get a **50%** revenue-share rebate if ≥**10%** of output is gasified.

57.s:
With reference to the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 13 May 2026.
2. Its outlay is ₹37,500 crore.
3. The incentive may be up to 20% of plant and machinery cost.
4. The incentive is capped at ₹5,000 crore per project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All four statements correctly describe the scheme approved on 13 May 2026, including its outlay, incentive rate and project-wise ceiling.
57.tq: Check the date, outlay, percentage and cap as separate components of one scheme.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Approved by the Cabinet on **13 May 2026**, outlay **₹37,500 crore**.
Incentive up to **20% of plant and machinery cost**, capped at **₹5,000 crore per project**.
xa: It targets about **75 MT** toward the **100 MT** goal; coal linkage tenure extended to **30 years**.
Earlier scheme (**2024**): **₹8,500 crore** for public and private projects.
Status (5 Sep 2026): **no bidders** so far.

57.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the status of the ₹37,500-crore coal gasification scheme?
o: Bidding was permanently closed after one unsuccessful round.
All eligible projects had already received the incentive.
The scheme was withdrawn because the mission target had been achieved.
No bidders had turned up, and bid windows were planned every two months.
57.x: No bidders had turned up for the scheme, and bid windows were planned at intervals of two months.
57.tq: Use the current-status detail rather than confusing it with scheme approval or implementation.
xs: **No bidders** turned up and **bid windows** were planned **every two months** — option **(4)** (5 Sep 2026).
The scheme is the **₹37,500 crore** surface coal/lignite gasification scheme (**13 May 2026**).
xa: The **West Asia conflict** pushed gasification up the agenda.
Calls for **CFB gasifiers**, **zero liquid discharge** and **mandatory CCUS**.
Substitutable import bill ≈ **₹2.77 lakh crore** (FY2025).

57.s: Which of the following is the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant identified in the sector?
o: The Talcher fertiliser plant in Odisha
MCL's IB Valley Washery in Odisha
57.x: JSPL's plant at Angul, Odisha, is identified as the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant.
57.tq: Match the project with its distinctive status and location.
xs: **JSPL at Angul (Odisha)** is the **only commercial-scale gasification plant** — option **(1)**.
**BCGCL** (Lakhanpur) and the **Talcher** fertiliser plant are still being built; **IB Valley** is a **washery**.
xa: BCGCL: **BHEL-CIL** JV (**21 May 2024**); **2,500 TPD** coal → **2,000 TPD** ammonium nitrate.
Talcher plant due by **Dec 2027**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about BCGCL:
1. It is a joint venture of BHEL and CIL.
2. It was formed on 21 May 2024.
3. It is building a commercial coal-to-ammonium-nitrate plant at Lakhanpur in Jharsuguda district.
4. The plant is located in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: BCGCL is a BHEL-CIL joint venture formed on 21 May 2024, and it is constructing the plant at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda, Odisha.
57.tq: Verify the organisation, formation date, project and location independently.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**BCGCL** is a **BHEL-CIL** JV formed on **21 May 2024**.
It is building the first commercial **coal-to-ammonium-nitrate** plant at **Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda (Odisha)**.
xa: Capacity: **2,500 TPD** coal in → **2,000 TPD** ammonium nitrate out.
**JSPL Angul** is the only commercial-scale gasification plant today.
**Talcher**: first gasification-based fertiliser plant (by **Dec 2027**).

57.s: To promote coal gasification, commercial coal blocks get what rebate on revenue share, and on what condition?
o: 50% rebate if at least 10% of output goes to gasification
10% rebate if at least 50% of output goes to gasification
20% rebate if at least 5% of output goes to gasification
100% rebate if at least 25% of output goes to gasification
57.x: Commercial blocks get a 50% rebate on revenue share if at least 10% of their output is used for gasification. The other options swap or invent the figures.
57.tq: Gasify >=10% -> 50% revenue-share rebate.
xs: Commercial blocks get a **50% rebate on revenue share** if **≥10%** of output goes to gasification — option **(1)**.
Option (2) simply swaps the two figures.
xa: **₹37,500 crore** scheme: incentive up to **20%** of plant cost, cap **₹5,000 crore** per project.
Mission goal: **100 MT** by **2030**.
14th-round mines carried the first **UCG** clauses.

57.s: The coal gasification incentive scheme of 2024 for public and private projects had an outlay of:
57.x: The 2024 scheme had an outlay of Rs 8,500 crore. Rs 37,500 crore is the May 2026 surface gasification scheme, Rs 5,000 crore its per-project cap, and Rs 2.77 lakh crore the FY2025 import bill of substitutable products.
57.tq: 2024 scheme Rs 8,500 cr; 2026 scheme Rs 37,500 cr.
xs: The **2024** coal gasification incentive scheme had an outlay of **₹8,500 crore** — option **(1)**.
**₹37,500 crore** is the surface coal/lignite gasification scheme (**13 May 2026**); **₹5,000 crore** is its per-project cap.
**₹2.77 lakh crore** is the **FY2025** import bill of gasification-substitutable products.
xa: The 2026 scheme's incentive: up to **20% of plant and machinery cost**; targets about **75 MT**.
Coal linkage tenure for gasification extended to **30 years**.
Mission target: gasify **100 MT** of coal by **2030**.

57.s:
Consider the following statements about coal bed methane (CBM):
1. It is held in coal seams, partly free in joints and partly adsorbed in micropores.
2. It is released by drilling wells and pumping out water.
3. It is called 'sweet gas' because it is rich in heavier hydrocarbons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: CBM is methane held in coal seams (free in joints, adsorbed in micropores) and is released by drilling wells and pumping out water. Statement 3 is wrong: it is called sweet gas because it has few heavier hydrocarbons. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
57.tq: Sweet gas = few heavier hydrocarbons.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **CBM** is methane in coal seams — partly **free in joints**, partly **adsorbed in micropores**.
Statement 2: it is released by **drilling wells + pumping out water**.
Statement 3 is wrong: CBM is "**sweet gas**" because it has **few** heavier hydrocarbons.
xa: ⚠ CBM extracts methane; **UCG** gasifies the coal seam itself in-situ.
Coal gasification syngas = **CO + H2 + CH4 + CO2**.

57.s: Which one of the following correctly describes underground coal gasification?
o: It uses water alone to convert coal into liquid fuel.
It is an in-situ process in which air or oxygen and steam are injected into coal seams to produce syngas underground.
It extracts only methane from micropores without altering the coal seam.
It is an ex-situ process in which coal is transported to a surface furnace.
57.x: UCG is an in-situ process. Air or oxygen and steam are injected into the coal seam to produce syngas underground.
57.tq: Contrast in-situ and ex-situ processes and identify the correct reactants and product.
xs: **UCG** is an **in-situ** process: **air/oxygen + steam** are injected into coal seams to make **syngas underground** — option **(2)**.
Extracting only methane from micropores describes **CBM**, not UCG.
xa: UCG uses **deep, thin or unmineable** coal.
Risk: **groundwater contamination**; MoEFCC panel refused to waive the **300 m** minimum depth for pilots.
The **14th round** agreements were the first with UCG clauses (**2 May 2026**).

57.s:
Consider the following statements about underground coal gasification (UCG):
1. It can use coal that is deep, thin or otherwise unmineable.
2. The MoEFCC expert panel waived the 300 m minimum depth for UCG pilot projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
57.x: Statement 1 is correct: UCG suits deep, thin or unmineable coal. Statement 2 is wrong: the MoEFCC expert panel refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth for UCG pilots. So '1 only' is right; '2 only' and 'Both 1 and 2' include the false statement 2, and 'Neither 1 nor 2' rejects the true statement 1.
57.tq: Panel refused (not granted) the 300 m depth waiver.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **UCG** uses **deep, thin or unmineable** coal.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **MoEFCC** expert panel **refused to waive** the **300 m** minimum depth for UCG pilots.
xa: UCG's main risk is **groundwater contamination**.
UCG injects **air/oxygen + steam** into coal seams → syngas underground.
First UCG clauses: **14th round** mines to **Reliance Industries + Axis Energy**.

57.s: Which of the following is a stated environmental risk of underground coal gasification?
o: Immediate destruction of all surface vegetation
Formation of heavier hydrocarbons in all coal seams
57.x: Groundwater contamination is a recognised risk associated with UCG.
57.tq: Select the specifically stated risk and reject broader unsupported environmental claims.
xs: **Groundwater contamination** is the stated risk of **UCG** — option **(1)**.
That is why the **MoEFCC** panel kept the **300 m** minimum depth for UCG pilots.
xa: UCG is **in-situ**, using **deep, thin or unmineable** coal.
Gasification critics call for **zero liquid discharge** and **mandatory CCUS**.

57.s: Which development pushed coal gasification higher on the policy agenda?
o: The replacement of NCDP-2007 by SHAKTI
The achievement of 1,047.50 MT coal production
57.x: The West Asia conflict increased the policy emphasis on coal gasification.
57.tq: Identify the stated current-affairs trigger rather than a related coal-sector reform.
xs: The **West Asia conflict** pushed coal gasification up the agenda — option **(3)**.
Gasification can substitute imports — **LNG, urea, ammonia, coking coal, methanol, DME** — worth ≈ **₹2.77 lakh crore** in **FY2025**.
xa: Cabinet approved the **₹37,500 crore** gasification scheme on **13 May 2026**.
⚠ It drew **no bids** by **Sep 2026**.

57.s: Why has the 100 MT coal-gasification goal been viewed with doubt?
o: Because few projects have reached an advanced stage
Because all commercial auctions were cancelled
Because UCG uses only shallow coal
Because coal production crossed one billion tonnes in 2024–25
57.x: The 100 MT goal is considered doubtful because few coal-gasification projects have reached an advanced stage.
57.tq: Link the criticism to project maturity rather than to total coal production or auction numbers.
xs: The **100 MT** goal is doubtful because **few projects are at an advanced stage** — option **(1)** (EY, Apr 2026).
The **₹37,500 crore** scheme drew **no bidders** (5 Sep 2026).
xa: Only **JSPL Angul (Odisha)** runs at commercial scale.
The Coal Ministry still says the target will be met (**26 Apr 2026**).
**Talcher** fertiliser plant is due only by **Dec 2027**.

57.s:
Which of the following measures has been recommended in relation to coal gasification?
1. Use of CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal
2. Zero liquid discharge
3. Mandatory CCUS
Which of the statements given above are correct?
57.x: All three have been called for in the debate on coal gasification: CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal, zero liquid discharge and mandatory CCUS.
57.tq: Recognise a complete recommendation set and avoid dropping the environmental safeguards.
xs: All three have been called for — option **(4)**.
**CFB gasifiers** for **high-ash coal**, **zero liquid discharge** and **mandatory CCUS**.
xa: Indian coal has **high ash (35-45%)** — hence CFB gasifiers.
Few projects are advanced → **100 MT** goal doubtful (EY, **Apr 2026**).
UCG risk: **groundwater contamination**.

57.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First coal mine established at Raniganj
B. BHEL commissioned the first IGCC plant
C. Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began
D. The 13th round of commercial coal auctions opened
57.x: The correct sequence is 1774, 1985, 2020 and 21 August 2025: A, B, C, D.
57.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two intermediate milestones by year.
xs: Order: **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Raniganj** first coal mine **1774** → **BHEL** first **IGCC** plant **1985** → revenue-sharing **commercial auctions 2020** → **13th round** opened **21 Aug 2025**.
xa: Raniganj (Sitarampur) is in **West Bengal**.
After **12 rounds**: **134 mines**, **277.04 MTPA**; the 13th round offered **14 mines**.
The **14th round** brought the first **UCG** clauses (**2 May 2026**).

58.s: Which one of the following statements regarding petroleum occurrence is correct?
o: Oil is formed only in Precambrian rocks and occurs chiefly in river valleys.
Oil is formed mainly in the Quaternary period and occurs only in volcanic rocks.
Oil formed in the Tertiary period, and most reserves occur in anticlines and fault traps.
Oil formed in the Jurassic period and is confined exclusively to synclines.
58.x: The Tertiary period is the period of oil formation, and anticlines and fault traps are the principal settings of most reserves.
58.tq: Combine the geological age with the structural-trap concept in the precise option.
xs: Oil formed in the **Tertiary** period, and most reserves lie in **anticlines and fault traps** — option **(3)**.
Commercial oil collects at the **crests of anticlines**, not in synclines or volcanic rocks.
xa: Traps: **anticlines, fault traps, salt domes**.
**Reservoir rock** = porous, permeable sandstone or fissured limestone; **cap rock** seals the trap.
Petroleum = **90-95% hydrocarbons**.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about petroleum geology:
1. Source rock is organic-rich shale in which oil forms.
2. Reservoir rock is an impervious bed that seals the trap.
3. Cap rock is an impervious bed that seals the trap.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: oil forms in organic-rich shale, the source rock. Statement 2 is wrong: reservoir rock is porous and permeable (sandstone or fissured limestone), where oil collects; the impervious seal is the cap rock. Statement 3 is correct. So 1 and 3 only.
58.tq: Source = where oil forms, reservoir = where it is stored (porous), cap = what seals it (impervious).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **source rock** is **organic-rich shale** where oil forms.
Statement 2 is wrong: **reservoir rock** is **porous, permeable sandstone or fissured limestone**.
Statement 3: **cap rock** is the **impervious bed** that seals the trap.
xa: Layering by density (top down): **gas, oil, water**.
Commercial oil sits at **crests of anticlines**.

58.s: Commercial accumulations of petroleum are generally found at the crests of:
58.x: Commercial oil commonly accumulates at the crests of anticlines. Other recognised traps include fault traps and salt domes.
58.tq: Direct recall of the principal structural trap.
xs: Commercial oil is found at the **crests of anticlines** — option **(4)**.
Most reserves lie in **anticlines + fault traps**; **salt domes** are another trap type.
xa: The trap is sealed by an impervious **cap rock**.
Within the trap: **gas on top, then oil, then water**.
Oil formed in the **Tertiary** period.

58.s: In a petroleum reservoir, the usual vertical arrangement from the top downward is:
58.x: Because of differences in density, gas is found above oil, and water is generally below oil.
58.tq: Use density to determine the correct vertical sequence.
xs: From top down: **gas, oil, water** — option **(3)**.
This layering follows **density**: the lightest (gas) rises, the heaviest (water) sinks.
xa: An impervious **cap rock** seals the trap above.
"**Wet gas**" = associated gas (found with oil); "**dry gas**" = non-associated.
Commercial oil sits at the **crests of anticlines**.

58.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: Gas rich in hydrogen sulphide — sour gas
Gas with no hydrocarbons — sour gas
58.x: Gas rich in hydrogen sulphide is called sour gas. Associated gas is termed wet gas, while non-associated gas is termed dry gas.
58.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination among petroleum gas terms.
xs: **Sour gas** is **H2S-rich** gas — option **(3)**.
**Associated gas** is "**wet gas**", not dry; **non-associated gas** is "**dry gas**", not wet.
xa: ⚠ **Wet** = associated; **dry** = non-associated; **sour** = H2S-rich.
**CBM** is called "**sweet gas**" because it has few heavier hydrocarbons.
**Conventional gas** is in permeable sandstone; **unconventional** in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams.

58.s: Petroleum generally consists of approximately what proportion of hydrocarbons?
58.x: Petroleum is composed of approximately 90–95 per cent hydrocarbons.
58.tq: Direct quantitative recall using percentage ranges.
xs: Petroleum is **90-95 per cent hydrocarbons** — option **(4)**.
The hydrocarbons formed in the **Tertiary** period in **organic-rich shale** (source rock).
xa: **PNG** is **85-95% methane** — a confusable range.
**Natural gas** is the **cleanest fossil fuel**.

58.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Basin — State
1. Cambay — Gujarat
2. Krishna-Godavari — Andhra Pradesh
3. Cauvery — Tamil Nadu
4. Rajasthan Basin — Rajasthan
58.x: Cambay is in Gujarat, Krishna-Godavari in Andhra Pradesh, Cauvery in Tamil Nadu and the Barmer-Jaisalmer basin in Rajasthan.
58.tq: Use the state-basin association and eliminate options containing a swapped location.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Cambay** — **Gujarat** (onshore); **Krishna-Godavari** — **Andhra Pradesh** (onshore + offshore).
**Cauvery** — **Tamil Nadu**; **Rajasthan** basin (**Barmer, Jaisalmer**) — Rajasthan.
xa: All four are **Category I** basins (commercial production), along with **Mumbai Offshore**, **Assam Shelf**, **Assam-Arakan**.
**Cambay** has India's **largest shale gas reserves** (APPSC-G1 2017).

58.s:
Consider the following pairs:
Field — Basin
1. Ankleshwar — Cambay Basin
2. Bombay High — Mumbai Offshore Basin
3. Naharkatiya — Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf
4. Kalol — Krishna-Godavari Basin
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
58.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Ankleshwar is in the Cambay Basin (Gujarat), Bombay High in the Mumbai Offshore Basin and Naharkatiya (with Digboi and Moran) in the Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf. Pair 4 is wrong: Kalol, like Ankleshwar, is a Cambay Basin field, not KG. So 'only 1 and 2' leaves out a correct pair, and any option with 4 includes a wrong one.
58.tq: Ankleshwar and Kalol go together (Cambay, Gujarat); KG fields are Ravva and KG-D6.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Ankleshwar** — **Cambay**; **Bombay High** — **Mumbai Offshore**; **Naharkatiya** — **Assam-Arakan / Assam Shelf**.
Pair 4 is wrong: **Kalol** is a **Cambay** field; KG fields are **Ravva** and **KG-D6**.
xa: **Bombay High** was developed after the **1973** oil shock.
Assam fields: **Digboi (1889)**, Naharkatiya, **Moran**.

58.s:
Which of the following fields are associated with the Krishna-Godavari Basin?

1. Ravva
2. KG-D6
3. Narimanam
4. Mangala

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Ravva and KG-D6 are associated with the Krishna-Godavari Basin. Narimanam belongs to the Cauvery Basin and Mangala to the Rajasthan Basin.
58.tq: Separate neighbouring basin fields by matching each field to its basin.
xs: **Ravva and KG-D6** are **Krishna-Godavari** fields — option **(1)**.
**Narimanam** is in the **Cauvery** basin; **Mangala** is in the **Rajasthan** basin.
xa: **Ravva** is offshore, **Cairn-ONGC**; **KG-D6** is **Reliance-BP**.
**APGIC** holds **10%** in a consortium with **ONGC, OIL, NTPC, British Gas** for **four KG-basin blocks**.
The Reliance **East-West pipeline** runs from **Kakinada (AP)** to **Bharuch (Gujarat)**.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
58.x: Moran is associated with the Assam-Arakan or Assam Shelf region, not the Cauvery Basin. Mangala and Dandewala are in Rajasthan, while Trishna is in Tripura.
58.tq: Find the incorrectly paired field and basin by checking the location of each field.
xs: **Moran — Cauvery** is wrong — option **(4)**; Moran is in the **Assam-Arakan / Assam Shelf** with **Digboi** and **Naharkatiya**.
**Trishna** — **Tripura fold belt**, **Mangala** — **Rajasthan**, **Dandewala** — **Jaisalmer** are all correct.
xa: The Cauvery basin's key field is **Narimanam**.
**Trishna** gas project was an **APPSC 2018** key.
**OIL** struck gas in the **Sanu Formation** at Dandewala (**26 May 2026**).

58.s: Trishna gas project is located in
58.x: The Trishna gas project is located in Tripura and is associated with the Tripura Fold Belt.
58.tq: Test the project-to-state association directly.
xs: The **Trishna** gas project is in **Tripura** (**Tripura fold belt**) — option **(3)** (APPSC 2018 key).
The **Tripura fold belt** is not a **Category I** (commercial production) basin.
xa: **Rajasthan**: Mangala and **Dandewala**; **Assam**: Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran; **AP**: Ravva, KG-D6.
The **Indradhanush** NE gas grid (~**1,656 km**) covers the eight NE States.

58.s: Which of the following basins is NOT included among Category I basins in commercial production?
58.x: Category I basins listed as being in commercial production are Cambay, Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery, Assam Shelf, Assam-Arakan and Rajasthan. Tripura Fold Belt is not included in that list.
58.tq: Use the listed-category method and identify the basin outside the specified group.
xs: The **Tripura fold belt** is not a Category I basin — option **(4)**.
**Category I** (commercial production): **Cambay, Mumbai Offshore, KG, Cauvery, Assam Shelf, Assam-Arakan, Rajasthan**.
xa: Tripura fold belt hosts the **Trishna** gas project.
Major gas basins: **Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam, Cambay**.

58.s: In May 2026, Oil India Limited struck gas in the shallower Sanu Formation at Dandewala. The formation belongs to which geological age?
58.x: The Sanu Formation at Dandewala is identified as Tertiary and lower Eocene.
58.tq: Link the dated discovery with the geological-age detail rather than treating the date as the answer.
xs: The **Sanu Formation** at **Dandewala** is **Tertiary, lower Eocene** — option **(4)**.
**OIL** struck gas there on **26 May 2026**, in the **Jaisalmer Basin**.
xa: Oil in India formed in the **Tertiary** period.
The Dandewala find, **Samudra Manthan** and the SPR levy plan were all driven by **West Asia** supply shocks.
Rajasthan basin's main oil field: **Mangala**.

58.s:
Which of the following are identified as major gas basins?

1. Mumbai Offshore
2. Krishna-Godavari
3. Assam
4. Cambay

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay are all identified as major gas basins.
58.tq: Recognise a complete four-item list and reject partial-list distractors.
xs: All four are major gas basins — option **(4)**.
**Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay** (2026).
xa: Gas was first found in **Assam and Maharashtra (1960s)**.
Gas share in energy mix: **~6.7%** → **15% by 2030** target.
Gas import reliance: **~47-51%**.

58.s: Gas was first found in India in the 1960s in which two states?
58.x: The first gas discoveries were in Assam and Maharashtra during the 1960s.
58.tq: Match the decade with the correct pair of states.
xs: Gas was first found in **Assam and Maharashtra** in the **1960s** — option **(3)**.
Oil came earlier: **Digboi (1889)** in Assam.
xa: **Bombay High** (Mumbai Offshore) was developed after the **1973** oil shock.
Major gas basins today: **Mumbai Offshore, KG, Assam, Cambay**.

58.s: India's oil industry began in 1889 at which oil field?
58.x: Digboi (1889) in the Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf basin marks the start of India's oil industry. Ankleshwar is a Cambay Basin field in Gujarat, Bombay High in the Mumbai Offshore Basin was developed after the 1973 oil shock, and Mangala is a Rajasthan Basin field.
58.tq: Digboi, Assam = 1889 = India's first oil field.
xs: India's oil industry began at **Digboi** in **1889** — option **(1)**.
Digboi is in the **Assam-Arakan / Assam Shelf** basin.
**Ankleshwar** is a **Cambay** field; **Bombay High** came after the **1973** oil shock; **Mangala** is in **Rajasthan**.
xa: Other Assam fields: **Naharkatiya, Moran**.
Gas was first found in **Assam and Maharashtra (1960s)**.

58.s: Shale gas and oil are primarily held in
o: permeable sandstone and extracted without stimulation
coal seams and released mainly by pumping water
fine-grained shale and generally require hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling
58.x: Shale hydrocarbons occur in fine-grained shale and require fracking and horizontal drilling. Coal seams hold coal bed methane, while gas hydrates occur as methane-water crystals.
58.tq: Discriminate unconventional resources by their host formation and extraction method.
xs: **Shale gas/oil** is held in **fine-grained shale** and needs **fracking + horizontal drilling** — option **(3)**.
**Coal seams** with pumping of water describe **CBM**; **ice-like crystals in deep-sea sediments** are **gas hydrates**.
xa: **Cambay** basin has the **largest shale gas reserves** (APPSC-G1 2017).
Other shale basins: **KG, Cauvery, Damodar, Assam-Arakan, Indo-Gangetic**.
Unconventional gas needs **costly technology**.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about coal bed methane (CBM) in India:
1. CBM is methane adsorbed in coal seams and is released by pumping out water.
2. The first commercial output of CBM in India came from Jharia.
3. Bokaro and Sohagpur are among the key CBM areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: CBM is held (adsorbed) in coal seams and released by pumping water. Statement 2 is wrong: the first commercial output was at Raniganj, not Jharia (Jharia is only another CBM area). Statement 3 is correct: key CBM areas are Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro and Sohagpur. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
58.tq: CBM first commercial output = Raniganj (also the site of India's first coal mine).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **CBM** is methane **adsorbed in coal seams**, released by **pumping water**.
Statement 2 is wrong: first commercial CBM output came at **Raniganj**, not Jharia.
Statement 3: key CBM areas are **Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro, Sohagpur**.
xa: CBM areas lie in the **Damodar valley** coalfields.
**Gas hydrates**: **KG, Mahanadi, Andaman** offshore.

58.s:
Which of the following locations are associated with gas hydrates?

1. Krishna-Godavari
2. Mahanadi
3. Andaman offshore
4. Damodar Valley

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: Gas hydrates are associated with the Krishna-Godavari, Mahanadi and Andaman offshore areas. Damodar Valley is a major coal bed methane region.
58.tq: Avoid confusing offshore gas-hydrate locations with the coalfield locations of CBM.
xs: Gas hydrates: **KG, Mahanadi and Andaman offshore** — option **(2)**.
They are **ice-like methane-water crystals in deep-sea sediments**.
**Damodar valley** is a **CBM** region, not a gas-hydrate area.
xa: CBM key areas: **Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro, Sohagpur**.
**Shale**: largest reserves in **Cambay**.

58.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes conventional gas from unconventional gas?
o: Conventional gas occurs in impermeable shale only, whereas unconventional gas occurs in permeable sandstone only.
Conventional gas generally occurs in permeable sandstone, whereas unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and requires costly technology.
Both types occur only in coal seams and are extracted by pumping water.
Neither type requires drilling or specialised technology.
58.x: Conventional gas is found in permeable sandstone. Unconventional gas occurs in impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams and generally needs costly extraction technology.
58.tq: Compare the host formations and technological requirements rather than the fuel name alone.
xs: **Conventional gas** is in **permeable sandstone**; **unconventional gas** is in **impermeable sandstone, shale or coal seams** and needs **costly technology** — option **(2)**.
Unconventional types: **shale gas** (fracking + horizontal drilling), **CBM**, **gas hydrates** — so neither "coal seams only" nor "no technology" is right.
xa: **HELP (2016)** gives a **single uniform licence** for conventional + unconventional hydrocarbons.
**Reservoir rock** is porous, permeable sandstone or fissured limestone.

58.s: Which sedimentary basin of India has the largest shale gas reserves?
58.x: The Cambay Basin (Gujarat) has the largest shale gas reserves (APPSC-G1 2017 key). Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and Damodar are other shale basins, with KG still under study, but none holds the largest reserves.
58.tq: Shale gas largest = Cambay; first CBM = Raniganj.
xs: The **Cambay Basin** has India's **largest shale gas reserves** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G1 2017; APPSC 2017 key).
**KG** is under study; **Cauvery** and **Damodar** are other shale basins.
xa: Other shale basins: **Assam-Arakan, Indo-Gangetic**.
Shale needs **fracking + horizontal drilling**.
Cambay fields: **Ankleshwar, Kalol** (Gujarat).

58.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), 2016:
1. It provides a single uniform licence for conventional and unconventional hydrocarbons.
2. It replaced the revenue-sharing contracts of NELP with production-sharing contracts.
3. It gives marketing and pricing freedom.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: HELP gives one licence for all hydrocarbons. Statement 2 is wrong because it is reversed: HELP brought a biddable revenue-sharing contract in place of NELP's production-sharing contracts. Statement 3 is correct: HELP offers open acreage with marketing and pricing freedom. So 1 and 3 only; any option with 2 is wrong.
58.tq: HELP = revenue sharing (new); NELP = production sharing (old).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **HELP (2016)** gives a **single uniform licence** for all hydrocarbons.
Statement 2 is reversed: HELP brought a **biddable revenue-sharing contract** in place of NELP's **production-sharing** contracts.
Statement 3: it gives **marketing and pricing freedom** with **open acreage**.
xa: ⚠ **NELP** = production-sharing; **HELP** = revenue-sharing (APPSC-G1 2017 key).
**OALP** lets companies choose and bid for blocks year-round.

58.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP):
1. Companies may choose the blocks they wish to bid for.
2. Bidding for blocks is permitted throughout the year.
3. The National Data Repository supports identification of blocks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: OALP allows companies to select blocks and bid year-round, using data available through the National Data Repository. The policy is intended to promote domestic exploration and production.
58.tq: Statement elimination using a policy's operational features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Under **OALP**, companies **choose** blocks and **bid year-round**, using the **National Data Repository**.
xa: Its aim: boost **domestic E&P**.
**Samudra Manthan** is open to **OALP block holders**.
OALP works under **HELP (2016)**'s open acreage.

58.s: The Discovered Small Fields policy primarily relates to the auction of small fields held by which entities?
58.x: Under the Discovered Small Fields policy of 2015, small fields held by ONGC and OIL are auctioned to increase domestic output.
58.tq: Direct recall of the concerned public-sector entities.
xs: The **Discovered Small Fields policy** (**2015**) auctions small fields held by **ONGC and OIL** — option **(2)**.
Its aim is to **boost output**.
xa: **HELP** (**2016**): single licence, revenue-sharing.
**OALP**: year-round block bidding via the **National Data Repository**.

58.s:
With reference to Samudra Manthan, consider the following statements:
1. It is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme.
2. Its outlay extends up to 2030-31.
3. It is a 100 per cent Central Sector scheme.
4. It is restricted to blocks held by ONGC alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: Samudra Manthan is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with an outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to 2030-31 and 100 per cent central funding. It is open to OALP block holders, not only ONGC.
58.tq: Find the wrongly restricted statement in a scheme description.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Samudra Manthan** is the **National Offshore Exploration Scheme**, outlay **₹84,084 crore** to **FY 2030-31**, **100% central sector**.
Statement 4 is wrong: it is open to **OALP block holders**, not ONGC alone.
xa: Covers **seismic mapping + risk drilling** (**50%** support, capped at **₹675 crore** per well).
About **60 deep-water wells**; Cabinet approval **3 Aug 2026**.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the exploration activities supported under Samudra Manthan?
o: Coal-bed methane extraction, with support capped at ₹675 lakh per well
Only offshore production, with complete reimbursement of drilling expenditure
Seismic mapping and risk drilling, with 50 per cent support capped at ₹675 crore per well
Refinery modernisation and pipeline construction, with 50 per cent support
58.x: The scheme covers seismic mapping and risk drilling. Risk drilling receives 50 per cent support, capped at ₹675 crore per well, and about 60 deep-water wells are envisaged.
58.tq: Match the scheme's purpose, support rate and ceiling precisely.
xs: Samudra Manthan supports **seismic mapping and risk drilling**, with **50%** support capped at **₹675 crore per well** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) wrongly says **₹675 lakh** and CBM.
xa: About **60 deep-water wells** are envisaged.
Outlay **₹84,084 crore** to FY **2030-31**; **100% central sector**.

58.s: Foreign Direct Investment in many segments of India's petroleum and natural gas sector is permitted up to:
58.x: FDI is permitted up to 100 per cent in many petroleum and natural gas segments. In PSU refining, the limit is 49 per cent without disinvestment.
58.tq: Contrast the general ceiling with the sector-specific exception.
xs: **FDI** is allowed up to **100 per cent** in many segments — option **(4)**.
**49%** applies to **PSU refining** without disinvestment.
xa: **HELP** gives **marketing and pricing freedom**.
India has been a **net exporter of petroleum products** since **2001-02**.

58.s: Regasified LNG can be used for supplying
o: only coal gas to thermal plants
58.x: After regasification, LNG can be supplied for use as piped natural gas and compressed natural gas.
58.tq: Follow the conversion chain from liquefied gas to its end-use forms.
xs: Regasified **LNG** supplies **PNG and CNG** — option **(3)**.
LNG is natural gas cooled **below -160 C**, shrinking its volume **1,000 times**.
xa: ⚠ **LNG** is **lighter than air**; **LPG** is heavier than air.
**CNG** is compressed to **200-250 kg/cm2**.
**PNG** is **85-95% methane**, piped 24x7.

58.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. LPG mainly contains propane and butane.
2. LPG is a by-product of oil refining and gas processing.
3. LPG is heavier than air.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
58.x: LPG mainly consists of propane and butane, is obtained as a by-product of oil refining and gas processing, and is heavier than air.
58.tq: Combine composition, origin and physical-property statements.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**LPG** is **propane + butane**, a **by-product of oil refining and gas processing**, and **heavier than air**.
xa: ⚠ **LNG** is lighter than air.
India has **33 crore** LPG connections; domestic gas could supply **30 crore** via PNG.
New SPR plan: about **six weeks** of LPG; levy **₹1.29/kg** on LPG.

58.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Piped Natural Gas (PNG)?
o: It contains 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied continuously through CGD networks
It contains mainly propane and butane and is stored in cylinders
It is natural gas liquefied below −160°C and transported by tankers
It is a heavy residual fuel supplied only to boilers
58.x: PNG contains approximately 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied through City Gas Distribution networks on a continuous basis.
58.tq: Separate PNG from LPG, LNG and furnace oil using composition and delivery mode.
xs: **PNG** is **85-95% methane**, piped **24x7** through **CGD networks** — option **(1)**.
**Propane + butane** in cylinders is **LPG**; cooled **below -160 C** is **LNG**; heavy residual fuel is **furnace oil**.
xa: **PNGRB** authorises **CGD Geographical Areas**.
AP: **83.61 lakh** PNG connections target by **March 2032**.

58.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Furnace oil — light fuel for household cooking
58.x: Brent is the North Sea crude-price benchmark, while WTI is the United States benchmark. Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel used in boilers.
58.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused crude-price benchmarks.
xs: **Brent** is the **North Sea** benchmark — option **(3)**.
**WTI** is the **US** benchmark, so (1) and (2) swap them; **furnace oil** is a **heavy residual fuel** for industrial boilers, not household cooking.
xa: **LPG** (propane + butane) is the household cooking fuel.
India's import reliance: **88% for crude**.

58.s: India has approximately how many LPG connections?
58.x: India has approximately 33 crore LPG connections. Domestic gas could supply around 30 crore consumers if they switched to PNG.
58.tq: Direct recall of a large sectoral figure.
xs: India has about **33 crore** LPG connections — option **(3)**.
Domestic gas could supply **30 crore** if they switched to **PNG** (PNGRB, Apr 2026).
xa: **LPG** = propane + butane, heavier than air.
AP: **2,98,111** PNG connections by **31 May 2026**; **East Godavari** highest.

58.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Product)
A. LPG
B. CNG
C. Naphtha
D. Furnace oil

List-II (Main use)
1. Petrochemicals and fertilisers
2. Household cooking
3. Industrial boilers and furnaces
4. Vehicles

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
58.x: LPG is mainly used for household cooking, CNG for vehicles, naphtha for petrochemicals and fertilisers, and furnace oil in industrial boilers and furnaces.
58.tq: Start with the sure product-use pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: Correct matching: **A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3** — option **(1)**.
**LPG** → household cooking; **CNG** → vehicles; **naphtha** → petrochemicals, fertilisers; **furnace oil** → industrial boilers and furnaces.
xa: **Petrochemicals** → plastics, synthetic fibres, rubber.
**Gasoline** → cars, two-wheelers.
CNG is compressed to **200-250 kg/cm2**.

58.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Petrochemicals — Plastics, synthetic fibres and rubber
Furnace oil — Industrial boilers and furnaces
58.x: CNG is mainly used in vehicles and produces lower pollutants. Industrial boilers and furnaces mainly use furnace oil in the given classification.
58.tq: Identify the product whose stated use has been swapped with a neighbouring product.
xs: **CNG — industrial boilers and furnaces** is wrong — option **(3)**; CNG is used in **vehicles** with lower pollutants.
Boilers and furnaces use **furnace oil**; **petrochemicals** → plastics, fibres, rubber; **gasoline** → cars, two-wheelers.
xa: **Naphtha** → petrochemicals, fertilisers.
**Natural gas** is the cleanest fossil fuel.

58.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding LNG, CNG and LPG?
o: LNG is natural gas cooled below −160°C; CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains propane and butane.
LNG is propane cooled below −16°C; CNG is compressed to 20–25 kg/cm²; LPG mainly contains methane.
LNG and LPG are identical forms of methane, while CNG is a mixture of propane and butane.
LNG is coal bed methane, whereas LPG is methane frozen in deep-sea sediments.
58.x: LNG is methane-rich natural gas cooled below −160°C, CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm², and LPG mainly consists of propane and butane from refining.
58.tq: Separate the three similar fuel terms using their state, pressure and composition.
xs: **LNG** below **-160 C**; **CNG** at **200-250 kg/cm2**; **LPG** = **propane + butane** — option **(1)**.
LPG is not methane; **PNG** (**85-95% methane**) is.
xa: LNG shrinks gas volume **1,000 times** and is **lighter than air**.
LPG is a by-product of refining and gas processing; **heavier than air**.

58.s: India has been a net exporter of petroleum products since
58.x: India became a net exporter of petroleum products in 2001-02. 1991-92 (the reform year), 2011-12 and 2016-17 are distractors with no link to this milestone. India still imports most of its crude oil; it exports refined products.
58.tq: Net exporter of PRODUCTS (not crude) since 2001-02.
xs: India has been a **net exporter of petroleum products** since **2001-02** — option **(2)**.
It exports refined products even though import reliance is about **88% for crude**.
xa: **FDI**: **100%** in many segments; **49%** in PSU refining.
Crude benchmarks: **Brent** (North Sea), **WTI** (US).

58.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the cleanest fossil fuel?
58.x: Natural gas is the cleanest fossil fuel. Coal is the most polluting. Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel used in boilers. Naphtha is a refinery feedstock for petrochemicals and fertilisers.
58.tq: Cleanest fossil fuel = natural gas.
xs: **Natural gas** is the **cleanest fossil fuel** — option **(2)**.
**Furnace oil** is a heavy residual fuel; **naphtha** is a feedstock for petrochemicals and fertilisers.
xa: Gas share in the energy mix: **~6.7%** → **15% by 2030**.
**CNG** in vehicles gives lower pollutants.
Coal: **CO2 + PM2.5**, heavy water use.

58.s: India's targeted share of gas in the energy mix by 2030 is approximately
58.x: The target is to raise the share of gas in the energy mix from about 6.7 percent to 15 percent by 2030.
58.tq: Distinguish the present approximate share from the future target.
xs: Gas share target: **15 percent** of the energy mix by **2030** — option **(3)**.
**6.7%** is the current share.
xa: Gas imports: **~47-51%**.
~**25 GW** of gas power is **stranded**.
One Nation One Gas Grid: **>32,000 km**, link all States by **2027**.

58.s: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline passes through which states?
o: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
58.x: The HVJ pipeline of GAIL connects Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; Maharashtra is not on this route.
58.tq: Use route sequencing and the excluded-state trap to identify the correct corridor.
xs: **HVJ** runs through **Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh** — option **(2)**.
It is a **GAIL** pipeline and does **not** pass through **Maharashtra** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
xa: **PM Urja Ganga** (JHBDPL): **UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Odisha**.
**East-West** pipeline: **Kakinada** to **Bharuch**.

58.s:
Which of the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga project is correct?

1. It is also known as the Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra pipeline.
2. Its authorised length is 3,546 km.
3. Its running length is 3,272 km.
4. It links the eastern and north-eastern regions to the gas grid.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: All four statements correctly describe Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga, including its JHBDPL identity, authorised and operating lengths, and regional linkage function.
58.tq: Check the project name, both numerical lengths and its stated connectivity before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM Urja Ganga** = **Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra (JHBDPL)**, GAIL.
**3,546 km** authorised, **3,272 km** running; it links the **East and North-East** to the grid.
xa: It includes **Barauni-Guwahati** and **Dhamra-Haldia** sections.
States: **UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Odisha**.

58.s:
Which of the following organisations constitute the joint venture for the Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid?

1. IOCL
2. ONGC
3. GAIL
4. OIL
5. NRL

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The joint venture comprises IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL.
58.tq: Verify the full institutional composition instead of stopping at the first three familiar entities.
xs: All five form the **Indradhanush NE gas grid** JV — option **(4)**.
**IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL**.
xa: Length about **1,656 km** across the **eight NE States**.
**PM Urja Ganga** links the East and North-East to the national grid.

58.s: One Nation One Gas Grid was initiated in
58.x: The One Nation One Gas Grid initiative began in 2014.

58.s:
With reference to the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), consider the following statements:

1. It is a statutory body under the PNGRB Act, 2006.
2. It authorises geographical areas for city gas distribution.
3. It sets pipeline tariffs.
4. It regulates crude oil production.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: PNGRB is a statutory body under the 2006 Act, authorises CGD geographical areas and sets pipeline tariffs. It does not regulate crude oil production among the activities specified here.
58.tq: Apply the authority test: identify the powers expressly assigned to PNGRB and reject the overextended production claim.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
**PNGRB** is a statutory body under the **PNGRB Act 2006** (under MoPNG); it authorises **CGD Geographical Areas** and sets **pipeline tariffs**.
Statement 4 is wrong: PNGRB does **not** regulate **crude or gas production**.
xa: It regulates **refining, storage, distribution, marketing and sale** of products and gas.
⚠ UPSC 2025 trap: PNGRB regulates **only two** of the four listed activities.

58.s:
According to the specified regulatory division, PNGRB regulates which two activities among the following?

1. Production of crude oil
2. Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum
3. Marketing and sale of petroleum products
4. Production of natural gas

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
58.x: The two regulated activities specified are refining, storage and distribution of petroleum, and marketing and sale of petroleum products. Crude oil and natural gas production are not included in these two activities.
58.tq: Separate regulated downstream activities from upstream production activities.
xs: PNGRB regulates **refining, storage and distribution** and **marketing and sale** — items **2 and 3**, option **(2)** (UPSC 2025 key: **only two**).
It does **not** regulate the **production** of crude oil or natural gas.
xa: PNGRB is statutory under the **PNGRB Act 2006**, under **MoPNG**.
It authorises **CGD Geographical Areas** and sets pipeline tariffs.
In AP, PNGRB approved **10 GAs**.

58.s: Oil marketing companies had established how many Energy Stations by 1 August 2025?

58.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Phase I locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
58.x: Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves comprises Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur in Karnataka.
58.tq: Use location-based elimination among closely related energy projects.
xs: SPR Phase I sites: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur (Karnataka)** — option **(2)**.
**Digboi** is an oil field, **Raniganj** and **Talcher** are coalfields, **Neyveli** is lignite and **Barmer** is a Rajasthan field.
xa: Phase I cover: about **9.5 days** of imports vs the **IEA** norm of **90 days**.
Operator: **ISPRL**, under MoPNG through **OIDB**.
New plan (**6 Aug 2026**): **$42 billion** strategic fuel reserve.

58.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR):
1. Phase I reserves cover about 9.5 days of India's imports.
2. The IEA norm for strategic reserve cover is 60 days of imports.
3. The reserves are operated by ISPRL under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas through OIDB.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
58.x: Statement 1 is correct: Phase I (Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur) gives about 9.5 days of import cover. Statement 2 is wrong: the IEA norm is 90 days, not 60. Statement 3 is correct: ISPRL operates the reserves under MoPNG through OIDB. So 1 and 3 only.
58.tq: India about 9.5 days against the IEA norm of 90 days; the gap is the point the exam tests.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Phase I covers about **9.5 days** of imports.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **IEA** norm is **90 days**, not 60.
Statement 3: **ISPRL** runs the reserves under **MoPNG** through **OIDB**.
xa: Phase I sites: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur**.
New **$42 billion** reserve will be the **first beyond crude**.

58.s:
Under the new strategic fuel reserve plan, which of the following combinations is correct?
1. It is planned to hold about two months of crude and LNG.
2. It is planned to hold about six weeks of LPG.
3. It is proposed to be funded partly through levies on LPG and gas.
58.x: The proposed reserve covers about two months of crude and LNG and about six weeks of LPG, with funding through levies on LPG and gas.
58.tq: Use the coverage periods and financing mechanism together to test a policy proposal.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)**.
The **$42 billion** plan (**6 Aug 2026**) holds about **two months** of **crude + LNG** and about **six weeks** of **LPG**.
Funding levies: **₹1.29/kg** on LPG (about **₹18** per cylinder) and **₹1.43/scm** on gas.
xa: It is the **first reserve beyond crude**.
Old Phase I covered only about **9.5 days** of imports.
The SPR levy plan was driven by **West Asia** supply shocks.

58.s:

xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Mission target **100 MT by 2030**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the first gasification fertiliser plant is at **Talcher**, not Angul (by **Dec 2027**).
Statement 3: **JSPL Angul** is the only commercial-scale plant.

**50%** revenue-share rebate if **10%** of output gasified.

58.s:

58.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the stated estimates of India's import dependence?
