Statement 1: in **Sep 2026** the UK recognised CCTS as a qualifying carbon price under its **CBAM** — correct.
Statement 2: the UK CBAM applies from **1 Jan 2027**, not 2026 — wrong.
Statement 3: it covers **aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, iron and steel** — correct.
xa: CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**, notified **2023**.
CCTS is administered by **BEE** and regulated by **CERC**.
It covers **9 heavy industries** with targets for **208 units**.

70.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme as described?
o: Replacement of all PAT-covered sectors by the carbon market
A compliance mechanism involving Carbon Credit Certificates
70.x: CCTS is administered by BEE, regulated by CERC and has a compliance mechanism using Carbon Credit Certificates, so B, C and D are features. It does not replace every PAT sector: as CCTS covers 9 heavy industries, PAT keeps four sectors (thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings).
70.tq: Spot the overbroad replacement claim and compare the two schemes’ coverage.
xs: CCTS does **not replace all PAT-covered sectors** — option **(1)** is the non-feature.
PAT will keep **4 sectors**: **thermal power, railways, DISCOMs, commercial buildings**.
Regulation by **CERC**, administration by **BEE** and a **compliance mechanism** with Carbon Credit Certificates are real CCTS features.
xa: CCTS covers **9 heavy industries**.
PAT = energy-intensity certificates (**ESCerts**); CCTS = emission-intensity certificates (**CCCs**).
Original PAT sectors included **aluminium**, **cement**, **fertilisers**, **chlor-alkali**, **textiles**.

70.s: The compliance mechanism of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme covers:
o: 9 heavy industries with GHG intensity targets for 208 units
4 sectors: thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
70.x: CCTS covers 9 heavy industries, with GHG emission-intensity targets for 208 units. 478 units in 8 sectors was PAT Cycle I; the four sectors are those PAT will retain; 60 clusters in 14 sectors is ADEETIE.
70.tq: CCTS = 9 industries, 208 units; PAT-I = 8 sectors, 478 units
xs: CCTS covers **9 heavy industries**, with GHG intensity targets for **208 units** — option **(2)**.
**478 units in 8 sectors** = PAT Cycle I; the **4 sectors** are those PAT will keep.
**60 MSME clusters in 14 sectors** = **ADEETIE**.
xa: Goal: **45% cut** in GDP emission intensity by **2030** (vs 2005).
Mechanisms: **Compliance** + **Voluntary Offset**.
Legal basis **Section 14AA**; administrator **BEE**; regulator **CERC**.

70.s: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is best described as:
o: a voluntary household scheme for purchasing energy-efficient appliances
a carbon-offset scheme limited to residential buildings
a tax-based scheme for replacing all fossil-fuel plants with nuclear plants
a market mechanism that sets energy-reduction targets for designated consumers
70.x: PAT is a market mechanism under NMEEE that assigns energy-reduction targets to designated consumers.
70.tq: Match the scheme with its operative mechanism and target group.
xs: PAT is a **market mechanism** that sets **energy-reduction targets** for **designated consumers** — option **(4)**.
It is not a household appliance scheme nor limited to residential buildings; it runs under **NMEEE** (NAPCC).
xa: Over-achievers earn **ESCerts**; laggards buy them on **power exchanges** (IEX).
Launched **2012**; Cycle I (**2012-15**): **478** units in **8** sectors.
In AP, PAT covers **59** industries, saving ~**1.16 Mtoe**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) under PAT:
1. Designated consumers that over-achieve their targets can earn ESCerts.
2. Designated consumers that fail to achieve their targets may buy ESCerts.
3. ESCerts are traded on power exchanges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts, under-achievers buy them, and the certificates are traded on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.
70.tq: Track the market mechanism through its three linked stages: earning, buying and trading.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **over-achievers earn ESCerts** — correct.
Statement 2: **under-achievers (laggards) buy** them — correct.
Statement 3: ESCerts trade on **power exchanges** (IEX) — correct.
xa: PAT is a market mechanism under **NMEEE**, launched in **2012**.
⚠ PAT = **ESCerts** (energy intensity); CCTS = **CCCs** (emission intensity).
Later PAT sectors added: **railways, DISCOMs, refineries, commercial buildings**.

70.s: PAT Cycle I, launched for the period 2012–15, covered:
70.x: PAT Cycle I covered 478 units in eight sectors during 2012–15.
70.tq: Separate PAT cycle figures from the later ADEETIE figures and the future residual-sector arrangement.
xs: PAT Cycle I (**2012-15**) covered **478 units in 8 sectors** — option **(2)**.
**60 clusters in 14 sectors** is **ADEETIE**; **4 sectors** is what PAT will retain after CCTS.
xa: PAT now runs in **rolling cycles**.
Original sectors: **thermal power, iron & steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, petrochemicals, chlor-alkali, pulp & paper, textiles**.
CCTS covers **9 heavy industries** with targets for **208 units**.

70.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the original PAT sectors?
70.x: The original PAT sectors included thermal power, chlor-alkali and textiles. Railways was added later and is part of the proposed residual-sector arrangement.
70.tq: Use the time qualifier to distinguish original sectors from sectors added later.
xs: **Railways** was not an original PAT sector — it was **added later** — option **(2)**.
**Chlor-alkali**, **textiles** and **thermal power** were original PAT sectors.
xa: Later additions: **railways, DISCOMs, refineries, commercial buildings**.
After CCTS, PAT keeps only **thermal power, railways, DISCOMs, commercial buildings**.
Cycle I (**2012-15**): **478** units in **8** sectors.

70.s: After the expansion of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), PAT is proposed to retain which four residual sectors?
o: Chlor-alkali, cement, railways and domestic buildings
Iron and steel, petrochemicals, refineries and pulp and paper
Thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
70.x: The proposed four residual PAT sectors are thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings.
70.tq: Use the future-sector list as a direct four-item recall question and reject the older industrial grouping.
xs: PAT will keep **thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings** — option **(4)**.
The reason: **CCTS** now covers **9 heavy industries** like **cement, aluminium, iron & steel**.
xa: Of the four retained, **railways, DISCOMs, commercial buildings** were later additions to PAT.
⚠ PAT = **ESCerts**; CCTS = **Carbon Credit Certificates**.
CCTS administrator **BEE**, regulator **CERC**.

70.s: PAT is associated with which of the following initiatives?
o: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under the National Action Plan on Climate Change
National Solar Mission under the Ministry of Finance
Smart Cities Mission under the Ministry of Power
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture under the National Action Plan on Climate Change
70.x: PAT operates under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE), which is one of the missions under NAPCC.
70.tq: Match the programme with its correct mission and policy framework.
xs: PAT runs under the **National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE)** of the **NAPCC** — option **(1)**.
NMEEE is one of the **8** NAPCC missions; the other options name the wrong mission or ministry.
xa: NAPCC dates from **2008**; PAT launched in **2012**.
PAT sets targets for **Designated Consumers**; trading in **ESCerts**.
BEE runs PAT along with **SEEI**, **S&L**, **ECBC**.

70.s: The Standards and Labelling programme for energy-consuming equipment in India is administered by which organisation under which Ministry?
o: National Productivity Council under the Ministry of Heavy Industries
Energy Efficiency Services Limited under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
70.x: The Standards and Labelling programme is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.
70.tq: Identify the organisation and parent ministry without confusing neighbouring energy institutions.
xs: The **Standards and Labelling** programme is run by **BEE** under the **Ministry of Power** — option **(3)**.
**EESL** implements **UJALA** and **SLNP**; it does not run labelling.
xa: Launched in **2006**; covers **40+ equipment**.
Rating: **1-5 star**; each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy.
From **1 Jan 2026**, labelling became **mandatory** for fridges, TVs, LPG stoves and more.

70.s: The Standards and Labelling programme was launched in which year?
70.x: The Standards and Labelling programme was launched in 2006.
70.tq: Distinguish the programme-launch year from the years associated with the Energy Conservation Act and PAT.
xs: The **Standards and Labelling** programme was launched in **2006** — option **(3)**.
**2001** = EC Act; **2002** = BEE operational; **2012** = PAT launch.
xa: It is run by **BEE** under the **Ministry of Power**.
Covers **40+ equipment**, on a **1-5 star** scale.
Results with PAT and UJALA: **53.6 Mtoe** saved (**FY 2023-24**).

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bureau of Energy Efficiency's Standards and Labelling programme:
1. It covers more than 40 types of equipment.
2. Its rating scale ranges from one star to five stars.
3. Each additional star saves approximately 10–15 per cent energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The programme covers more than 40 equipment categories, uses a one-to-five-star scale and each additional star is associated with approximately 10–15 per cent energy savings.
70.tq: Use the quantitative and scale clues together; all three statements are supported.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: covers **40+ equipment** — correct.
Statement 2: scale is **1-5 star** — correct.
Statement 3: each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy — correct.
xa: Launched **2006** by **BEE** (Ministry of Power).
Voluntary examples: **industrial motors**, **computers**, **microwave ovens**.
From **1 Jan 2026**, makers are **penalised** if actual consumption deviates from the label.

70.s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the mandatory category under the Standards and Labelling programme?
1. Induction hob
2. Solar inverter
3. Computer
4. Domestic LPG stove
70.x: Computers are given as a voluntary example. Induction hobs, solar inverters and domestic LPG stoves are listed as mandatory examples.
70.tq: Find the single item transferred from the voluntary list into the mandatory list.
xs: **Computers** are a **voluntary** example, not mandatory — option **(2) 3 only**.
**Induction hob**, **solar inverter** and **domestic LPG stove** are listed as **mandatory**.
xa: Other voluntary items: **general-purpose industrial motors**, **microwave ovens**.
Other mandatory items: refrigerators, ACs, fans, TVs, geysers, **LED lamps**, distribution transformers, chillers.
Each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy.

70.s:
With effect from 1 January 2026, star labelling became mandatory, having earlier been voluntary, for which of the following groups?
1. Refrigerators and televisions
2. LPG stoves and cooling towers
3. Chillers and deep freezers
4. Distribution transformers and grid-connected solar inverters
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
70.x: From 1 January 2026, mandatory labelling was extended to all the listed categories, which had earlier been voluntary.
70.tq: Check the complete date-linked list; the correct option contains every listed category.
xs: From **1 Jan 2026** labelling became **mandatory** for all four groups — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Covered: **refrigerators, TVs, LPG stoves, cooling towers, chillers, deep freezers, distribution transformers, grid-connected solar inverters**.
xa: Makers are now **penalised** if actual consumption deviates from the label.
The programme is run by **BEE**, launched in **2006**.
It covers **40+ equipment** on a **1-5 star** scale.

70.s: Under the star-labelling changes effective from 1 January 2026, manufacturers may be penalised when:
o: the product receives fewer than three stars irrespective of its actual consumption
actual energy consumption deviates from the declared label rating
a product is sold without an international energy certificate
the product is manufactured outside a designated consumer sector
70.x: Manufacturers may be penalised if the actual energy consumption of a product deviates from the consumption declared through its label.
70.tq: Apply the compliance rule to a manufacturer’s conduct instead of confusing rating level with accuracy of declaration.
xs: Makers are penalised when **actual consumption deviates from the declared label** — option **(2)**.
This came with mandatory labelling from **1 Jan 2026**.
xa: Groups made mandatory: fridges, TVs, **LPG stoves**, cooling towers, chillers, deep freezers, transformers, **solar inverters**.
Each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy.
The programme is run by **BEE** under the **Ministry of Power**.

70.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Code)
a. ECBC
b. ECO Niwas Samhita
c. ECSBC
List-II (Scope or feature)
i. Residential buildings
 ii. New commercial buildings
 iii. Sustainability added to the energy-conservation building framework

Code:
a  b  c
1. i  ii  iii
2. ii  i  iii
3. ii  iii  i
4. iii  i  ii
70.x: ECBC applies to new commercial buildings, ECO Niwas Samhita applies to residential buildings, and ECSBC adds sustainability to the framework.
70.tq: Start with the sure pair: ECO Niwas Samhita is the residential-building code.
xs: Correct match: **ECBC – new commercial (ii)**, **ECO Niwas Samhita – residential (i)**, **ECSBC – sustainability (iii)** — option **(2)**.
ECBC dates from **2007**, ECO Niwas Samhita from **2018**, ECSBC from **2024**.
xa: ECSBC followed the **2022 amendment**, adding sustainability to ECBC.
ECBC buildings use **25-40% less energy**.
AP: ECBC notified in **123 ULBs**, with **1,300** compliant buildings.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about building energy codes:
1. ECBC was introduced in 2007 for new commercial buildings.
2. Buildings complying with ECBC use approximately 25–40 per cent less energy.
3. ECO Niwas Samhita was introduced in 2018 for residential buildings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct: ECBC dates from 2007, applies to new commercial buildings and can reduce energy use by about 25–40 per cent; ECO Niwas Samhita dates from 2018 and covers residential buildings.
70.tq: Combine date, scope and quantitative-effect statements in one coded question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **ECBC (2007)** covers new **commercial** buildings — correct.
Statement 2: ECBC buildings use **25-40% less energy** — correct.
Statement 3: **ECO Niwas Samhita (2018)** is for **residential** buildings — correct.
xa: **ECSBC (2024)** adds **sustainability** to ECBC after the 2022 amendment.
⚠ ECBC = **commercial**; ECO Niwas Samhita = **residential**.
AP model: **Super ECBC building, Sagar Nagar, Visakhapatnam** (Jan 2026).

70.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: ECO Niwas Samhita — new commercial buildings — 2007
ECSBC — sustainability-oriented building code after the 2022 amendment — 2024
70.x: ECSBC is the 2024 sustainability-oriented building code following the 2022 amendment. ECBC concerns new commercial buildings, while ECO Niwas Samhita concerns residential buildings.
70.tq: Check both the scope and year in each pair; the correct pair preserves both dimensions.
xs: **ECSBC** is the **sustainability**-oriented code after the **2022 amendment**, from **2024** — option **(4)**.
**ECO Niwas Samhita** is for **residential** buildings (**2018**), not industrial motors or commercial buildings.
**ECBC** is for new **commercial** buildings (**2007**), not residential.
xa: ECBC buildings use **25-40% less energy**.
AP: ECBC notified in **123 ULBs**; **1,300** compliant buildings.

70.s: The Andhra Pradesh model Super ECBC building referred to in the context of energy-efficient construction is located at:
70.x: The AP model Super ECBC building is located at Sagar Nagar in Visakhapatnam.
70.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the AP example from other possible urban energy-efficiency sites.
xs: AP's model **Super ECBC building** is at **Sagar Nagar, Visakhapatnam** (Jan **2026**) — option **(1)**.
The notes name no such building at Vijayawada, Tirupati or Kurnool.
xa: ECBC is notified in **123 ULBs** of AP, with **1,300** compliant buildings.
**APSECM** (constituted **2012**) is India's first standalone **State Designated Agency** of BEE.
ECBC applies to new **commercial** buildings.

70.s: Which one of the following lamps has the highest efficacy, longest life and no mercury?
70.x: LED lamps have the highest efficacy and longest life among the listed lamps and do not contain mercury.
70.tq: Identify the option carrying the complete energy-efficiency feature set.
xs: The **light-emitting diode (LED) lamp** has the highest efficacy, longest life and **no mercury** — option **(3)**.
**CFL** contains **mercury**; **incandescent** loses most energy as **heat**; **sodium vapour** gives yellow light with poor colour rendering.
xa: LEDs also give off little heat — the energy-saving choice (**PYQ 2025**).
**PYQ 2021**: replacing bright and CFL bulbs with LEDs as LEDs use less energy — **A and R true, R explains A**.
**SLNP** replaced **sodium vapour** street lights with LEDs.

70.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sodium vapour lamp — white light and excellent colour rendering
Incandescent lamp — most energy lost as sound
CFL — contains mercury and has a shorter life than LED
LED — high mercury content and substantial heat production
70.x: CFLs are more efficient than incandescent lamps but contain mercury and have a shorter life than LEDs. Incandescent lamps mainly lose energy as heat, while sodium vapour lamps produce yellow light with poor colour rendering.
70.tq: Use feature-based elimination and watch for swapped lamp characteristics.
xs: **CFL** contains **mercury** and has a **shorter life than LED** — option **(3)**.
Sodium vapour gives **yellow light** with **poor colour rendering**; incandescent loses energy as **heat**, not sound.
**LED** has **no mercury** and little heat.
xa: CFL is better than incandescent but inferior to LED.
Using LED saves energy (**APPSC 2025**).
**UJALA** distributed **36.86 crore** LED bulbs.

70.s: UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme were both launched in:
70.x: Both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme were launched in January 2015.
70.tq: Use the date-pair clue when two programmes were launched together.
xs: **UJALA** and **SLNP** were both launched in **January 2015** — option **(3)**.
**2012** is PAT's launch; **2018** is ECO Niwas Samhita and the Preparedness Index.
xa: Both are implemented by **EESL**.
UJALA = **Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All**.
SLNP replaced **sodium vapour** street lights with LEDs.

70.s: Which organisation implements both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme?
70.x: Both programmes are implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture of public-sector undertakings under the Ministry of Power.
70.tq: Identify the implementing agency, not the supervising ministry or an associated organisation.
xs: **Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)** implements both **UJALA** and **SLNP** — option **(1)**.
EESL is a **JV of Ministry of Power PSUs**; **BEE** is the statutory body running PAT and labelling; **PCRA** gives driving advice and launched **SAKSHAM**.
xa: EESL also runs the **National Efficient Cooking Programme**.
UJALA/SLNP distributed **36.86 crore** LED bulbs and **72.18 lakh** LED tube lights.
**Jul 2026**: an **EESL-APSECM** impact report was released by CS **G. Sai Prasad**.

70.s: The Street Lighting National Programme primarily replaced older street lighting based on which technology with LEDs?
70.x: Under the Street Lighting National Programme, older sodium vapour street lights were replaced by LED lights.
70.tq: Match the programme intervention with the specific older technology.
xs: SLNP replaced **sodium vapour** street lights with LEDs — option **(4)**.
Sodium vapour lamps have high efficacy but **yellow light** and **poor colour rendering**.
xa: SLNP was launched in **January 2015** by **EESL**.
AP: **680 LED streetlights** via the **State Energy Conservation Fund**.
AP has **MoUs with EESL** for LED street lighting.

70.s: Under UJALA, approximately how many LED bulbs have been distributed?
70.x: UJALA distributed about 36.86 crore LED bulbs, along with 72.18 lakh LED tube lights and 23.59 lakh energy-efficient fans. 9.5 crore is the number of PMUY LPG connections.
70.tq: UJALA: 36.86 crore bulbs; 72.18 lakh tubes; 23.59 lakh fans
xs: UJALA distributed **36.86 crore** LED bulbs — option **(3)**.
**72.18 lakh** = LED tube lights; **23.59 lakh** = energy-efficient fans.
xa: UJALA was launched in **January 2015** by **EESL**.
PAT + S&L + UJALA avoided **321.06 MT CO2** annually (FY 2023-24).
⚠ crore (bulbs) vs lakh (tube lights, fans).

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Efficient Cooking Programme:
1. It is run by Energy Efficiency Services Limited.
2. It envisages 20 lakh induction cookstoves.
3. The induction cookstoves are stated to be 25–30 per cent cheaper than traditional cooking.
4. The programme is associated with MECS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All four statements are correct. EESL runs the programme, which covers 20 lakh induction cookstoves, offers a stated 25–30% cost advantage over traditional cooking and is associated with MECS.
70.tq: Verify the agency, quantity, percentage and associated programme as separate components.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
The programme is run by **EESL** — correct.
It covers **20 lakh** induction stoves with a **25-30%** cost advantage — statements 2 and 3 correct.
It is run with **MECS** — correct.
xa: AP's APSECM gave **induction stoves** to Anganwadis.
EESL also implements **UJALA** and **SLNP**.
Cooking tips: lids and **pressure cookers**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fuel-efficiency and conservation initiatives:
1. CAFE norms set average fuel-efficiency targets for M1 cars.
2. The first CAFE norms were notified in 2017.
3. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency enforces the CAFE norms.
4. SAKSHAM is a fuel-conservation drive of the Petroleum Conservation Research Association.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All four statements are correct. CAFE norms concern M1 cars, were first notified in 2017, are enforced by BEE, and SAKSHAM is conducted by PCRA for fuel conservation.
70.tq: Combine regulatory details with the separate agency-led conservation campaign.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**CAFE norms** set average fuel-efficiency targets for **M1 cars**, first notified **2017**, enforced by **BEE** — statements 1-3 correct.
**SAKSHAM** (Sanrakshan Kshamata Mahotsav) is **PCRA**'s fuel-conservation drive — correct.
xa: SAKSHAM **2026** was launched by PCRA at **Chandigarh** (Jun 2026).
PCRA driving advice: correct **tyre pressure**, steady speed, engine off at signals.
**NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first.

70.s: Which of the following sets contains only appropriate energy-conservation practices for lighting and appliances?
o: Replace LEDs with CFLs, avoid switching off appliances and use air conditioners continuously
Use unstarred appliances, leave chargers connected and operate appliances at maximum load
Use LEDs, choose star-rated appliances, switch off idle loads and avoid excessive use of air conditioners
Use incandescent bulbs, keep idle appliances on and increase air-conditioner use
70.x: LEDs, star-rated appliances, switching off idle loads and avoiding excessive air-conditioner use are the stated energy-conservation practices.
70.tq: Select the option in which every practice contributes to reducing energy use.
xs: The right set is: **use LEDs, choose star-rated appliances, switch off idle loads, avoid excessive AC use** — option **(3)**.
The other options keep idle appliances on, use incandescent bulbs or overuse ACs — all waste energy.
xa: **LED** has the highest efficacy, longest life and **no mercury** (**PYQ 2025**).
Each extra **star** on a label saves about **10-15%** energy.
**PYQ 2021** (A-R): replacing bright and CFL bulbs with LEDs because LEDs use less energy — **A and R true, R explains A**.

70.s: Which combination of practices is most suitable for reducing household energy use during cooking?
o: Use oversized burners, leave vessels uncovered and cook without pressure
Keep the flame wider than the vessel and avoid all forms of insulation
Use induction cookstoves, cover vessels with lids and use pressure cookers
Use incandescent heating elements and keep the cooker open throughout
70.x: Induction cooking, using lids and using pressure cookers are recommended practices for improving cooking efficiency.
70.tq: Choose the option containing only efficiency-enhancing practices.
xs: Efficient cooking means **induction cookstoves**, **lids** on vessels and **pressure cookers** — option **(3)**.
Uncovered vessels, oversized flames and open cookers waste fuel.
xa: The **National Efficient Cooking Programme** (EESL) plans **20 lakh** induction stoves.
Induction cooking has a **25-30%** cost advantage over traditional cooking.
AP's **APSECM** gave **induction stoves to Anganwadis**.

70.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the stated fuel-saving driving practices?
o: Keeping the engine running at every traffic signal
Switching off the engine at signals
70.x: Correct tyre pressure, steady speed and switching off the engine at signals are fuel-saving practices. Keeping the engine running at every signal is contrary to the stated advice.
70.tq: Find the reversed driving practice among otherwise practical conservation measures.
xs: **Keeping the engine running at every signal** is not advised — option **(3)**; PCRA says switch the **engine off at signals**.
**Correct tyre pressure** and **steady speed** are PCRA's other fuel-saving tips.
xa: **PCRA** launched **SAKSHAM** (Sanrakshan Kshamata Mahotsav) **2026** at **Chandigarh**.
**CAFE norms** (first notified **2017**, enforced by BEE) set fuel-efficiency targets for **M1 cars**.
India has **~80%** oil import dependence, so fuel saving aids energy security.

70.s: SAKSHAM, expanded as Sanrakshan Kshamata Mahotsav, was launched in 2026 at which place and by which organisation?
o: Hyderabad by Indian Oil Corporation Limited
Chandigarh by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association
New Delhi by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Bengaluru by Energy Efficiency Services Limited
70.x: SAKSHAM 2026 was launched by PCRA at Chandigarh as a fuel-conservation and awareness initiative.
70.tq: Combine the event’s expansion, launching agency and location without swapping related bodies.
xs: **SAKSHAM 2026** was launched by the **Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA)** at **Chandigarh** (Jun 2026) — option **(2)**.
Its aim is **fuel conservation and awareness**; BEE and EESL run other programmes.
xa: PCRA also gives driving advice: **tyre pressure**, steady speed, engine off at signals.
**NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first for energy conservation.
**EESL** runs **UJALA**, **SLNP** and the **National Efficient Cooking Programme**.

70.s: Energy efficiency is linked to sustainability mainly because it:
o: increases the energy intensity of the economy
reduces the need for new energy sources
requires replacing all renewable energy with fossil fuels
has no effect on energy demand
70.x: Using energy efficiently lowers demand, so fewer new energy sources need to be built (APPSC 2025). It lowers energy intensity rather than raising it, does not require fossil fuels, and directly cuts demand.
70.tq: Efficiency = fewer new sources needed (APPSC 2025)
xs: Energy efficiency **reduces the need for new energy sources** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2025**).
It **lowers** energy intensity — BEE's aim is to cut the **energy intensity** of the economy — so option (1) is wrong.
xa: PAT, S&L and UJALA avoid **~321 MT CO2** a year.
It is the **cheapest route** to cut demand and emissions.
Results (**FY 2023-24**): **53.6 Mtoe** saved.

70.s: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index was prepared by which of the following combinations?
o: NITI Aayog with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Energy Efficiency Services Limited
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with NITI Aayog
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
70.x: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index, introduced in 2018, was prepared by NITI Aayog in association with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
70.tq: Use the institution-pair distinction to avoid swapping agencies.
xs: The inaugural **State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index (2018)** was prepared by **NITI Aayog with BEE** — option **(1)**.
**BEE with AEEE** made the framework of the **State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI)** — the trap in option (4).
xa: In the **2018** index, **AP = "Front Runner"** (**APPSC 2018**).
SEEI categories: **Front Runner, Achiever, Contender, Aspirant**.
SEEI is the basis for the **National Energy Conservation Awards**.

70.s:
With reference to the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI), consider the following statements:
1. The framework was developed by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy.
2. The SEEI framework forms the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards.
3. The SEEI uses the categories Front Runner, Achiever, Contender and Aspirant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct. SEEI was developed by BEE with AEEE, is used as the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards, and classifies States into four categories including Front Runner and Aspirant.
70.tq: Check each institutional, functional and classification statement separately.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: SEEI framework is by **BEE with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy (AEEE)** — correct.
Statement 2: SEEI is the basis for the **National Energy Conservation Awards** — correct.
Statement 3: categories are **Front Runner, Achiever, Contender, Aspirant** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Preparedness Index (2018)** = **NITI Aayog with BEE**; SEEI = **BEE with AEEE**.
AP was **Front Runner** in the **2018** index.
**NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding energy conservation awards:
1. Chandigarh ranked first in the National Energy Conservation Award 2025.
2. The 2025 award ranking was given on the basis of the State Energy Efficiency Index.
3. Andhra Pradesh State Energy Conservation Mission won the First Prize in NECA for 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct. Chandigarh ranked first in NECA 2025 on the SEEI basis, while APSECM won the First Prize for 2024–25.
70.tq: Separate the national ranking from the Andhra Pradesh institutional award.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **NECA 2025** — **Chandigarh ranked first** — correct.
Statement 2: **SEEI** is the basis for the **National Energy Conservation Awards** — correct.
Statement 3: **APSECM** has won **First Prize in NECA** (APSES **2024-25**) — correct.
xa: **NECA** was instituted in **1991**; given by **BEE under the Ministry of Power** (not MNRE).
**National Energy Conservation Day** = **14 December**.
**Manohar Lal Khattar** praised AP's efficiency record after a BEE report (Jan **2026**).

70.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. National Energy Conservation Day is observed on 14 December.
2. National Energy Conservation Week is observed from 14 to 20 December.
3. The National Energy Conservation Awards, instituted in 1991, are given annually by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Day is 14 December and the Week is 14-20 December. Statement 3 is wrong: NECA (instituted 1991) is given annually by BEE under the Ministry of Power, not MNRE. Hence '1 only' omits a true statement, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
70.tq: NECA = BEE under Ministry of Power, not MNRE.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **National Energy Conservation Day** = **14 December** — correct.
Statement 2: the Week = **14-20 December** — correct.
Statement 3: **NECA** (instituted **1991**) is given by **BEE under the Ministry of Power**, **not MNRE** — wrong.
xa: **NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first.
AP's **NEC Week 2024** saw the **School Education Department** collaborate in awareness drives.
**APSECM** has won **First Prize in NECA**.

70.s: In the inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index (2018), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
70.x: Andhra Pradesh was rated a Front Runner, the top category, in the inaugural 2018 index prepared by NITI Aayog with BEE (APPSC 2018). Achiever, Contender and Aspirant are the lower categories.
70.tq: AP = Front Runner, 2018 (NITI Aayog + BEE index)
xs: AP was a **"Front Runner"** in the inaugural **2018** Preparedness Index — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2018**).
**Achiever**, **Contender** and **Aspirant** are the lower categories.
xa: The index was prepared by **NITI Aayog with BEE**.
**APSECM** (**2012**) is India's **first standalone State Designated Agency** of BEE.
APSECM has won **First Prize in NECA**.

70.s: During National Energy Conservation Week in Andhra Pradesh in 2024, which department collaborated in the awareness activities?
70.x: The School Education Department collaborated in Andhra Pradesh’s National Energy Conservation Week awareness activities in 2024.
70.tq: Identify the collaborating department rather than the sector-wide beneficiaries of the programme.
xs: The **School Education Department** collaborated in AP's **NEC Week 14-20 Dec 2024** — option **(3)**.
The drives covered awareness across sectors.
xa: **PYQ 2024**: all three statements on AP's role were correct (**APPSC 2024**).
**National Energy Conservation Day** = **14 December**.
AP's **State Energy Conservation Awards-2024** covered thermal plants, textiles, hospitals, **RTC depots**, **ULBs**.

70.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Energy Conservation Mission (APSECM) was constituted in:
70.x: APSECM was constituted in 2012.
70.tq: Use the establishment year, not the year of the State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index.
xs: **APSECM** was constituted in **2012** — option **(3)**.
**2001** = EC Act; **2018** = Preparedness Index (AP Front Runner).
xa: APSECM is **India's first standalone State Designated Agency** of BEE.
It **enforces the EC Act 2001** in AP.
⚠ **2012** is also the year **PAT** was launched.

70.s: Which statement correctly describes APSECM?
o: It is India’s first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE and enforces the Energy Conservation Act in Andhra Pradesh.
It is a tribunal established to adjudicate electricity disputes.
It is a central regulator that administers the national carbon market in every State.
It is a private company responsible only for distributing LED lamps.
70.x: APSECM is India’s first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE and enforces the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, in Andhra Pradesh.
70.tq: Match the agency with its institutional status and enforcement role.
xs: APSECM is **India's first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE** and **enforces the EC Act** in AP — option **(1)**.
The national carbon market is administered by **BEE** and regulated by **CERC**; LED distribution is done by **EESL**.
xa: Constituted in **2012**.
Work: efficient appliances in **112 Anganwadi** schools, **Mangalagiri**; star-rated products for **PMAY** homes.
**Jul 2026**: CS **G. Sai Prasad** released an **EESL-APSECM** impact report.

70.s: APSECM implements energy-efficiency and energy-conservation programmes in coordination with which of the following?
o: The State Industries Department and BEE
Only the Ministry of Finance and RBI
70.x: APSECM works with the State Industries Department and the Bureau of Energy Efficiency while implementing energy-efficiency and energy-conservation programmes.
70.tq: Identify the institutional partners directly connected with the agency’s programme function.
xs: APSECM implements EE&EC programmes with the **State Industries Department** and **BEE** — option **(1)**.
**CERC** is the CCTS regulator, unrelated to APSECM's partners.
xa: APSECM **enforces the EC Act 2001** in AP.
The **15th Executive Committee** of APSECM reviewed **DSM, ECBC, PAT and S&L** (Jan **2026**).
ECBC is notified in **123 ULBs** of AP.

70.s: The first IoT energy pilot associated with APSECM was undertaken at an MSME unit in:
70.x: The IoT energy pilot was first undertaken at an MSME unit in East Godavari and was later extended to all districts with BEE.
70.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the pilot site from the programme’s later statewide extension.
xs: India's first **IoT** pilot at an MSME unit was in **East Godavari** — option **(3)**; it was extended to all districts with **BEE**.
**Mangalagiri** is where **112 Anganwadi** schools got efficient appliances; **Visakhapatnam** has the **Super ECBC** building.
xa: AP MSME energy audits covered **4** clusters: gold ornaments, imitation jewellery, food processing, pharma.
**ADEETIE** (**Jul 2025**) supports MSME efficiency nationally.
**28 W BLDC 5-star fans** were fitted in **16 APSRTC** bus stations.

70.s: Under the Perform, Achieve and Trade programme in Andhra Pradesh, the stated coverage and energy saving were:
o: 59 energy-intensive industries and approximately 1.16 Mtoe saved
208 energy-intensive industries and approximately 1.60 Mtoe saved
123 energy-intensive industries and approximately 0.68 Mtoe saved
16 energy-intensive industries and approximately 1.30 Mtoe saved
70.x: PAT in Andhra Pradesh covered 59 energy-intensive industries and resulted in approximately 1.16 Mtoe of energy savings.
70.tq: Keep the PAT figures separate from CCTS coverage and the number of AP buildings.
xs: PAT in AP covers **59** energy-intensive industries, saving ~**1.16 Mtoe** — option **(1)**.
**208** is CCTS's unit count; **123** is the number of ULBs with ECBC; **16** is APSRTC bus stations.
xa: Nationally, PAT + S&L + UJALA saved **53.6 Mtoe** (**FY 2023-24**).
PAT Cycle I: **478** units in **8** sectors.
ECBC in AP: **1,300** compliant buildings.

70.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four MSME clusters in Andhra Pradesh where energy audits were undertaken?
70.x: The four clusters were gold ornaments, imitation jewellery, food processing and pharmaceuticals. Automobile manufacturing was not listed.
70.tq: Find the substituted sector by checking the complete four-cluster list.
xs: **Automobile manufacturing** is not among the **4** audited clusters — option **(1)**.
The four are **gold ornaments, imitation jewellery, food processing, pharma**.
xa: The first **IoT** pilot was at an MSME unit in **East Godavari**.
**ADEETIE** covers **60 clusters, 14 sectors** nationally.
PAT in AP covers **59** energy-intensive industries.

70.s: Which of the following pairs correctly distinguishes PAT from CCTS?
o: PAT applies only to households, whereas CCTS applies only to agriculture
PAT issues energy-intensity certificates, whereas CCTS issues emission-intensity certificates
PAT issues carbon compliance certificates, whereas CCTS issues energy-intensity certificates
Both PAT and CCTS issue only renewable-energy certificates
70.x: PAT is associated with energy-intensity certificates, called ESCerts, while CCTS is associated with emission-intensity certificates, called CCCs.
70.tq: Discriminate between two similar market mechanisms by their certificate type.
xs: PAT issues **energy-intensity certificates (ESCerts)**; CCTS issues **emission-intensity certificates (CCCs)** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses them; neither scheme is for households or agriculture.
xa: ESCerts are traded on **power exchanges** (IEX).
CCTS covers **9 heavy industries**; PAT will keep **4 sectors**.
CCTS: administrator **BEE**, regulator **CERC**, legal basis **Section 14AA**.

70.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of energy efficiency in India?
o: It eliminates the need for all new energy sources immediately.
It can reduce demand and emissions and strengthen energy security in a country dependent on imports for about 80% of its oil.
It is generally the most expensive route to reduce demand and emissions.
It affects only the building sector and has no relation to energy security.
70.x: Energy efficiency is a relatively inexpensive route to reduce demand and emissions and improves energy security, particularly given India’s approximately 80 per cent oil-import dependence.
70.tq: Apply the significance statement to both emissions reduction and energy security.
xs: Efficiency **reduces demand and emissions** and aids **energy security** with **~80%** oil import dependence — option **(2)**.
It is the **cheapest** route, not the most expensive; it reduces, not eliminates, the need for new sources.
xa: PAT, S&L and UJALA avoid **~321 MT CO2** a year.
Mandatory star labels from **1 Jan 2026**; makers penalised if use deviates from the label.
**UK CBAM** recognised India's CCTS (**Sep 2026**).

70.s:
Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s energy-efficiency initiatives is/are correct?
1. APSECM was a Front Runner in 2018.
2. APSECM received the first prize under NECA.
3. The 15th Executive Committee of APSECM reviewed DSM, ECBC, PAT and Standards and Labelling.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
70.x: All three statements are correct: APSECM was a 2018 Front Runner, received the first NECA prize, and its 15th Executive Committee reviewed DSM, ECBC, PAT and Standards and Labelling.
70.tq: Link the State-specific distinction, award and committee agenda without substituting a national institution.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: AP was a **Front Runner** in the **2018** Preparedness Index — correct.
Statement 2: **APSECM** won **First Prize in NECA** — correct.
Statement 3: the **15th Executive Committee** reviewed **DSM, ECBC, PAT and S&L** (Jan **2026**) — correct.
xa: APSECM = India's **first standalone SDA** of BEE, constituted **2012**.
**EESL-APSECM** impact report released **Jul 2026**.

71.s: How many willing households were electrified under Saubhagya according to the latest reported figure?
71.x: Saubhagya electrified 2.86 crore willing households. An older figure cited 2.82 crore households as of March 2021.
71.tq: Distinguish the updated figure from the older reference figure.
xs: **Saubhagya** electrified **2.86 crore** willing households — option **(3)**.
**2.82 crore** is the older figure (as of **Mar 2021**, UPSC), not the latest.
xa: Saubhagya (**2017**) aimed at **universal household electrification** and claimed **100%**.
Leftovers: **₹6,521 crore** under **RDSS** for **13.65 lakh** households.
**Leisang (Manipur)** was the last village electrified, **28 Apr 2018**.

71.s: Which of the following correctly describes the households covered by the ₹6,521 crore sanctioned under RDSS for Saubhagya leftovers?
o: 9.42 lakh farming households with solar pumps
13.65 lakh households, including specified vulnerable and difficult-area groups
1 crore urban households with rooftop solar
71.x: ₹6,521 crore was sanctioned for 13.65 lakh leftover households, including PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, tribal households under DAJGUA, SC households under PMAJAY and border villages under Vibrant Villages.
71.tq: Match the amount and beneficiary count before checking the special categories.
xs: **₹6,521 crore** under **RDSS** covers **13.65 lakh** leftover households, incl. vulnerable and difficult-area groups — option **(3)**.
Groups: **PVTG** (PM-JANMAN), **tribal** (DAJGUA), **SC** (PMAJAY), **border villages** (Vibrant Villages).
**9.42 lakh** is the PM-KUSUM **B** pump count; **1 crore** households is the PM Surya Ghar target.
xa: Saubhagya electrified **2.86 crore** willing households.
RDSS also funds **prepaid smart meters**.
⚠ PVTG = **PM-JANMAN**; border villages = **Vibrant Villages**.

71.s: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) was launched in which year, and for what purpose?
71.x: Saubhagya was launched in 2017 for universal household electrification. Urban distribution strengthening is IPDS (2014), DISCOM turnaround is UDAY (2015) and farm-pump solarisation is PM-KUSUM (2019).
71.tq: Saubhagya 2017 = every household; IPDS 2014, UDAY 2015, KUSUM 2019
xs: **Saubhagya** was launched in **2017** for **universal household electrification** — option **(3)**.
**IPDS** (Dec **2014**) = urban distribution; **UDAY** (Nov **2015**) = discom turnaround; **PM-KUSUM** (**2019**) = farm solar.
xa: Full name: **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana**.
It electrified **2.86 crore** willing households.
Policy shift: connections (**DDUGJY, Saubhagya**) → discom viability (**UDAY, RDSS**) → prosumers (**PM Surya Ghar**).

71.s: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched in 2016 by the:
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
71.x: PMUY was launched in 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to provide deposit-free LPG connections to poor women.
71.tq: Match the clean-cooking scheme with its administrative ministry.
xs: **PMUY** (**2016**) was launched by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG)** — option **(2)**.
It gives **deposit-free LPG** to **poor women**; **MNRE** runs PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar.
xa: Phase I target: **8 crore** by **2019**; now **9.5 crore+** connections.
Since **Oct 2023**: **₹300** per **14.2 kg** refill, up to **9** refills a year.
⚠ PMUY = **MoPNG**; UDAY = **Ministry of Power**; PM-KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar = **MNRE**.

71.s: What was the Phase I target of PMUY by 2019?
71.x: Phase I of PMUY targeted 8 crore deposit-free LPG connections by 2019; the reported number of connections later exceeded 9.5 crore.
71.tq: Distinguish the original target from the later cumulative achievement.
xs: PMUY Phase I targeted **8 crore** connections by **2019** — option **(2)**.
**9.5 crore+** is the later total of connections, not the Phase I target.
xa: **Ujjwala 2.0**: free first refill and stove; **migrants via self-declaration**.
Cash assistance: **₹1,600** per **14.2 kg** connection.
**Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009)** raised rural LPG distributors from **18%** to **60%**.

71.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with Ujjwala 2.0?
o: Free first refill and stove, self-declaration facility for migrants, and ₹1,600 assistance per 14.2 kg connection
Free electricity up to 300 units and 60% rooftop-solar subsidy
A ₹6,521 crore package for border villages only
71.x: Ujjwala 2.0 provides a free first refill and stove, permits migrants to use self-declaration, and provides cash assistance of ₹1,600 per 14.2 kg connection.
71.tq: Group several features belonging to one phase instead of mixing schemes.
xs: **Ujjwala 2.0** gives a **free first refill and stove**, **self-declaration for migrants** and **₹1,600** per **14.2 kg** connection — option **(2)**.
**30:30:40** sharing is **PM-KUSUM** B/C; **300 units** free and **60%** subsidy is **PM Surya Ghar**; **₹6,521 crore** is RDSS for Saubhagya leftovers.
xa: Refill subsidy since **Oct 2023**: **₹300 × 9** a year.
Older notes: **₹200** per refill, up to **12** a year; **5 kg** double-bottle option.
PMUY is run by **MoPNG** (**2016**).

71.s: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy for PMUY beneficiaries has been:
o: ₹200 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 12 refills a year
₹300 per 5 kg refill without an annual limit
₹1,600 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 5 refills a year
₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 9 refills a year
71.x: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy has been ₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to nine refills a year. Older provisions cited ₹200 and up to 12 refills.
71.tq: Give priority to the latest figure while distinguishing it from the older subsidy arrangement.
xs: Since **Oct 2023**: **₹300** per **14.2 kg** refill, up to **9** refills a year — option **(4)**.
**₹200 × 12** was the older provision; **₹1,600** is cash assistance per **connection**, not per refill.
xa: Ujjwala 2.0 gives a **free first refill and stove**.
PMUY has **9.5 crore+** connections.
Refill problem: households want clean fuel but face **cost and habit** barriers (CEEW's **IRES** survey).

71.s: Which of the following best explains the refill issue faced by many PMUY households?
o: They are prohibited from obtaining LPG refills after the first connection.
They want clean fuel but face cost and habit-related barriers.
They lack any interest in clean fuel and reject LPG completely.
They are supplied only with solar cooking devices.
71.x: Survey findings indicate that households generally want clean fuel but face affordability and established-habit barriers to regular refilling.
71.tq: Select the option that captures both demand for clean fuel and the practical constraint.
xs: PMUY households **want clean fuel** but face **cost and habit barriers** — option **(2)** (CEEW's **IRES** survey).
They are not barred from refills nor uninterested in LPG.
xa: Since **Oct 2023**: targeted subsidy **₹300** per refill, up to **9** a year.
**5 kg** double-bottle and swap options were offered.
**Surya Nutan (2022)**, by **IOCL**, is an indoor solar stove.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding clean-cooking initiatives:
1. The Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009) raised the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%.
2. Surya Nutan, an indoor solar stove launched in 2022, was developed by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009) raised the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%. Statement 2 is wrong: Surya Nutan (2022) was developed by IOCL, not EESL. So '2 only' and 'Both' are wrong, and 'Neither' ignores the true statement 1.
71.tq: Surya Nutan = IOCL (an oil company makes the solar stove).
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1: **Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009)** raised rural LPG distributors' share **18% → 60%** — correct.
Statement 2: **Surya Nutan (2022)** is by **IOCL**, not EESL — wrong.
xa: PMUY (**2016**, MoPNG): deposit-free LPG to poor women.
Ujjwala 2.0 gives **₹1,600** cash assistance per connection.

71.s: UDAY, introduced in November 2015, is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Financial turnaround of state-owned electricity distribution companies
Universal installation of solar pumps in rural areas
Construction of nuclear power plants by state governments
Replacement of LPG with electric cooking appliances
71.x: UDAY, or Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana, was introduced by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 for the financial turnaround of state discoms.
71.tq: Identify the scheme from its ministry, year and core purpose.
xs: **UDAY** (Ministry of Power, **Nov 2015**) is for the **financial turnaround** of state discoms — option **(1)**.
Solar pumps belong to **PM-KUSUM**; LPG to **PMUY**.
xa: States took over **75%** of discom debt (as of **30 Sep 2015**) via state bonds.
Targets by **2018-19**: AT&C losses **15%** and **ACS-ARR gap zero**.
⚠ IPDS = **urban** distribution; UDAY = discom **debt**.

71.s:
Which of the following were targets under UDAY for 2018-19?
1. Reduction of AT&C losses to 15%
2. Elimination of the ACS-ARR gap
3. Reduction of rooftop solar installations to zero

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: UDAY targeted AT&C losses of 15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero by 2018-19. Rooftop solar installations were not a UDAY target.
71.tq: Find the statement belonging to another energy programme.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 were UDAY targets — option **(3) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: AT&C losses to **15%** by **2018-19** — correct.
Statement 2: **ACS-ARR gap to zero** — correct.
Statement 3: rooftop solar was never a UDAY target — wrong.
xa: ⚠ AT&C target: UDAY **15%**; RDSS **12-15%**.
Participating states covered **97%** of outstanding discom debt (**PYQ 2017**).

71.s: The Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), launched in December 2014, primarily aims to strengthen:
o: Rural agricultural feeder separation and village electrification
Urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement
71.x: IPDS strengthens urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement.
71.tq: Distinguish the urban distribution focus of IPDS from the rural focus of DDUGJY.
xs: **IPDS** (Dec **2014**) strengthens **urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement** — option **(3)**.
Village electrification is **Saubhagya**; LPG is **PMUY**; solar pumps are **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: IPDS subsumed **R-APDRP**.
It is credited with **better urban supply**.
⚠ IPDS = **urban** distribution; UDAY = discom **debt**.

71.s: IPDS subsumed which earlier programme?
71.x: The Integrated Power Development Scheme subsumed the Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (R-APDRP).
71.tq: Identify the predecessor by separating urban and rural distribution programmes.
xs: **IPDS** subsumed **R-APDRP** — option **(3)**.
**PM-KUSUM** (**2019**) and **Saubhagya** (**2017**) are separate later schemes.
xa: IPDS was launched in **Dec 2014** for **urban** distribution, metering and IT.
It is credited with **better urban supply**.
**RDSS (2021)** later focused on loss reduction and **prepaid smart metering**.

71.s:
With reference to UDAY, consider the following statements:
1. States took over 75% of DISCOM debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015.
2. Fifty per cent of the debt was taken over in 2015-16 and 25% in 2016-17.
3. The arrangement covered 97% of the total outstanding DISCOM debt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. UDAY provided for State takeover of 75% of DISCOM debt in the two specified instalments, covering 97% of total outstanding debt.
71.tq: Check each numerical statement separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: states took over **75%** of discom debt as of **30 Sep 2015** — correct.
Statement 3: **97%** of total outstanding discom debt covered (**PYQ 2017**) — correct.
xa: Debt was taken over through **state bonds**.
Targets by **2018-19**: AT&C **15%**, ACS-ARR gap **zero**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS):
1. It was approved in 2021.
2. Its approved outlay was ₹3,03,758 crore.
3. Its Gross Budgetary Support was ₹97,631 crore.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: RDSS was approved in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3,03,758 crore, including Gross Budgetary Support of ₹97,631 crore.
71.tq: Test the year, total outlay and budgetary-support figure together.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **RDSS** was launched in **2021** — correct.
Statement 2: outlay **₹3,03,758 crore** — correct.
Statement 3: **GBS ₹97,631 crore** — correct.
xa: Targets: AT&C loss **12-15%** and **ACS-ARR gap zero**.
AP got **₹15,083.14 crore** under RDSS for smart metering and grid modernisation.
RDSS also has **₹6,521 crore** for Saubhagya leftovers.

71.s: The national targets of RDSS include:
o: AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero
AT&C losses of zero and an ACS-ARR gap of 12–15%
AT&C losses of 30% and an ACS-ARR gap of 15%
Only reduction of transmission losses, without an ACS-ARR target
71.x: RDSS aims at pan-India AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero.
71.tq: Avoid reversing the two performance indicators and their target values.
xs: RDSS targets pan-India **AT&C loss 12-15%** and **ACS-ARR gap zero** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the two targets.
xa: ⚠ UDAY aimed at AT&C **15%** by **2018-19**.
Components: **prepaid smart metering**, loss-reduction works.
Outlay **₹3,03,758 crore**.

71.s: Which of the following is a principal intervention under RDSS?
o: Prepaid smart metering and loss-reduction works
Replacement of all agricultural feeders by rooftop solar
Free LPG refills and improved stove design
71.x: RDSS focuses on prepaid smart metering and works for reducing distribution losses.
71.tq: Match the operational intervention with the distribution-sector reform scheme.
xs: RDSS centres on **prepaid smart metering** and **loss-reduction works** — option **(1)**.
Free LPG refills belong to **PMUY**; rooftop solar to **PM Surya Ghar**.
xa: RDSS was launched in **2021**; GBS **₹97,631 crore**.
AP: **₹15,083.14 crore** sanctioned for smart metering and grid modernisation.
Targets: AT&C **12-15%**, ACS-ARR gap **zero**.

71.s: Which component of PM-KUSUM relates to decentralised grid-connected solar or renewable-energy plants on farm or barren land?
71.x: Component A provides for decentralised grid-connected solar or renewable-energy plants on farm or barren land.
71.tq: Match the component letter with its specific intervention.
xs: **Component A** covers decentralised grid-connected solar/RE plants on **farm/barren land** — option **(4)**.
**B** = **standalone solar pumps**; **C** = **solarisation of grid-connected pumps**.
xa: PM-KUSUM **A** reached **667.31 MW** (**30 Nov 2025**).
PM-KUSUM was launched in **2019** by **MNRE**.
It gives daytime irrigation + extra income to over **21.77 lakh** farmers.

71.s: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
71.x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
71.tq: Use the ministry and launch year to separate PM-KUSUM from other rural schemes.
xs: **PM-KUSUM** was launched in **2019** by **MNRE** — option **(4)**.
The **Ministry of Power** runs **UDAY**; MoPNG runs PMUY.
xa: Components: **A** plants on farm land, **B** standalone pumps, **C** solarising grid pumps.
Subsidy for B and C: **30% Centre, 30% State, 40% farmer**.
⚠ PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar are both **MNRE** schemes.

71.s: For Components B and C of PM-KUSUM, the subsidy-sharing pattern is:
71.x: For Components B and C, the Centre contributes 30%, the State 30% and the farmer 40%; a bank loan may also be used by the farmer.
71.tq: Check the three-way percentage split without confusing it with rooftop-solar CFA.
xs: For Components **B and C**: **30% Centre, 30% State, 40% farmer** — option **(3)**.
The farmer's share can come from a **bank loan**.
xa: **B** progress: **9.42 lakh** pumps; **C**: **10.99 lakh** pumps.
AP: solarisation of **2.93 lakh** agricultural pump sets under PM-KUSUM.
⚠ PM Surya Ghar CFA is **60%** for 2 kW, **40%** for extra up to **3 kW**.

71.s: Under PM-KUSUM, Component C relates to:
o: Decentralised grid-connected solar plants on barren land
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
71.x: Component C solarises grid-connected agricultural pumps. Component A covers decentralised grid-connected solar/RE plants on farm or barren land, and Component B covers standalone solar pumps. Urban household rooftop solar comes under PM Surya Ghar, not PM-KUSUM.
71.tq: KUSUM: A = plants, B = standalone pumps, C = solarise grid pumps
xs: **Component C** = **solarisation of grid-connected pumps** — option **(3)**.
**A** = plants on farm/barren land; **B** = **standalone solar pumps**; urban rooftop solar is **PM Surya Ghar**.
xa: Component C progress: **10.99 lakh** pumps.
Subsidy for B/C: **30:30:40** (Centre:State:farmer).
Benefit: **daytime irrigation** + extra income.

71.s: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana was launched in February 2024 by which ministry as a Central Sector Scheme?
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
71.x: The scheme was launched in February 2024 by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy as a Central Sector Scheme.
71.tq: Use the ministry-scheme association as the decisive clue.
xs: **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** was launched in **February 2024** by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** — option **(1)**.
It is a **Central Sector Scheme** for rooftop solar and free power.
xa: Outlay **₹75,021 crore**; target **1 crore households** by **March 2027**.
Free power up to **300 units per month**.
Tag: **world's largest domestic rooftop solar scheme**.

71.s: The approved outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is:
71.x: The outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is ₹75,021 crore.
71.tq: Separate the scheme outlay from the RDSS outlay and grant figures.
xs: PM Surya Ghar outlay = **₹75,021 crore** — option **(3)**.
**₹97,631 crore** is RDSS's **GBS**.
xa: Goals: **30 GW** RTS; **1,000 BU** power and **720 MT CO2** cut over **25** years.
It subsumed the **Phase II Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme (2019)**.
Progress (**2025**): **14.43 lakh** RTS systems, **18.14 lakh** households.

71.s: What is the household target of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana by March 2027?
71.x: The scheme targets rooftop solar installations in 1 crore households by FY 2026-27, that is, March 2027.
71.tq: Match the target number with the stated completion year.
xs: Target: rooftop solar in **1 crore households** by **FY 2026-27** (**March 2027**) — option **(2)**.
**PYQ (UPSC 2025)**: statements on the 1 crore target and MNRE installer training were all correct.
xa: Households become **"prosumers"** with up to **300 units** free a month.
**One Model Solar Village per district**.
AP: **2,27,549** installations done.

71.s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, households may receive free electricity up to:
71.x: The scheme provides for free power of up to 300 units per month, with beneficiary households becoming prosumers.
71.tq: Test the exact monthly ceiling rather than the broader rooftop-solar objective.
xs: Free power up to **300 units per month** — option **(2)**.
**200 units** is AP's own free power for **BPL SC/ST** households — a trap.
xa: Households become **"prosumers"**.
CFA: **60%** for 2 kW; **40%** for extra up to **3 kW**.
Outlay **₹75,021 crore**.

71.s: Under the Central Financial Assistance structure of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which statement is correct?
o: 40% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 60% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
100% of the cost is covered up to 3 kW.
30% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 30% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
60% of the cost is covered for 2 kW and 40% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
71.x: CFA covers 60% of the cost for 2 kW and 40% for the additional capacity up to 3 kW.
71.tq: Avoid reversing the two subsidy percentages and their capacity limits.
xs: CFA = **60%** of cost for **2 kW** and **40%** for extra capacity up to **3 kW** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) reverses the rates; **30%** shares belong to **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: Free power up to **300 units per month**.
Target: **1 crore households**; **30 GW** RTS.
AP SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering**.

71.s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which institutional arrangement is envisaged for districts?
o: One Model Solar Village per district
One solar pump in every village
Two nuclear villages in every district
71.x: The scheme provides for one Model Solar Village per district.
71.tq: Identify the exact unit of implementation and its numerical provision.
xs: PM Surya Ghar provides **one Model Solar Village per district** — option **(1)**.
AP too plans a **model solar village in every district** (Energy Minister **Gottipati Ravi Kumar**).
xa: **City Accelerator Programme (Jun 2025)** helps ULBs and discoms with urban rooftop solar.
Tag: **world's largest domestic rooftop solar scheme**.
Target **1 crore households** by **March 2027**.

71.s: The City Accelerator Programme associated with PM Surya Ghar was launched primarily to provide technical assistance to:
o: Farmers and irrigation departments for solar pumps
ULBs and discoms for urban rooftop solar
LPG distributors for rural refill delivery
Nuclear power corporations for reactor construction
71.x: The City Accelerator Programme, launched in June 2025, provides technical help to urban local bodies and discoms for urban rooftop solar.
71.tq: Match the programme’s beneficiaries with its specific implementation problem.
xs: The **City Accelerator Programme (Jun 2025)** gives technical help to **ULBs and discoms** for **urban rooftop solar** — option **(2)**.
Farm solar pumps come under **PM-KUSUM**, not this programme.
xa: It is part of **PM Surya Ghar** (Feb **2024**, MNRE).
PM Surya Ghar subsumed the **Phase II Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme (2019)**.
AP: **APCPDCL** has **50,114** rooftop units, **180 MW**.

71.s: In Andhra Pradesh, free power up to how many units per month is provided to BPL SC/ST households?
71.x: Free power is provided up to 200 units per month to eligible BPL SC/ST households in Andhra Pradesh.
71.tq: Use the exact numerical limit and eliminate nearby but altered figures.
xs: AP gives free power **up to 200 units/month** to **20.26 lakh** BPL SC/ST households — option **(3)**.
**300 units** is the PM Surya Ghar free-power limit.
xa: AP power subsidy (**FY 2024-25**): **₹10,449.92 crore**.
Concessional tariffs: **BC/MBC professionals, dhobi ghats, handlooms, saloons**.
SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering**.

71.s: Which one of the following groups is NOT specifically included among the beneficiaries of concessional electricity tariffs in Andhra Pradesh?
71.x: Concessional tariffs are mentioned for BC/MBC professionals, dhobi ghats, handlooms and saloons; large-scale automobile factories are not included in this list.
71.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the specified beneficiary group.
xs: **Large-scale automobile factories** are not listed — option **(2)**.
Concessional tariffs go to **BC/MBC professionals, dhobi ghats, handlooms, saloons**.
xa: Free power **up to 200 units/month** for **20.26 lakh** BPL SC/ST households.
AP power subsidy (FY **2024-25**): **₹10,449.92 crore**.

71.s: Free rooftop solar power for SC/ST households in Andhra Pradesh is proposed through:
71.x: The provision of free rooftop solar for SC/ST households is associated with Virtual Net Metering.
71.tq: Discriminate between closely related electricity-metering concepts.
xs: AP's SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering** — option **(2)**.
**Prepaid** smart metering is an **RDSS** component, not this.
xa: AP PM Surya Ghar: **2,27,549** installations.
Discom progress (**Aug 2026**): **SPDCL 47%, CPDCL 35%, EPDCL 32%**.
**APCPDCL**: **50,114** rooftop units, **180 MW**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the rooftop-solar targets announced in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The target is six lakh connections.
2. The target is 6,000 connections in each constituency.
3. A model solar village is proposed in every district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct. The announced targets include six lakh connections, 6,000 connections per constituency and one model solar village in every district.
71.tq: Check whether the numerical target and the geographical targets all belong to the same policy announcement.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **6 lakh** connections — correct.
Statement 2: **6,000 per constituency** — correct.
Statement 3: a **model solar village in every district** — correct.
xa: Targets were announced by Energy Minister **Gottipati Ravi Kumar**.
AP installations so far: **2,27,549**.

71.s: Who announced the targets of six lakh rooftop-solar connections, 6,000 connections per constituency and one model solar village in every district of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission
The Chairperson of the Central Electricity Authority
71.x: Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar announced these rooftop-solar targets for Andhra Pradesh.
71.tq: Identify the responsible authority associated with a specific policy announcement.
xs: AP Energy Minister **Gottipati Ravi Kumar** announced the targets — option **(4)**.
Targets: **6 lakh** connections = **6,000 per constituency**; a model solar village in every district.
xa: AP discom progress (**Aug 2026**): **SPDCL 47%, CPDCL 35%, EPDCL 32%**.
**APCPDCL**: **50,114** rooftop units, **180 MW**.
SC/ST households: **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering**.

71.s: The installed renewable-energy capacity of Andhra Pradesh is 10,639.75 MW. Which component-wise distribution is correct?
71.x: Andhra Pradesh had 10,639.75 MW of renewable-energy capacity, comprising 5,614.52 MW of solar and 4,397.67 MW of wind capacity.
71.tq: Match the component figures with their correct labels before checking the total.
xs: Options (1) and (2) swap solar and wind; option (4) gives wind as the whole total.
xa: PM-KUSUM in AP: solarisation of **2.93 lakh** pump sets.
India's installed capacity **509.74 GW**, RE **49.83%** (Nov **2025**).
⚠ Solar exceeds wind in AP's RE mix.

71.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad evolution of electricity-related policy emphasis in India?
o: Prosumers → quality and discom viability → household connections
Household connections → quality and discom viability → prosumers
Household connections → prosumers → quality and discom viability
71.x: The emphasis moved from providing connections through DDUGJY and Saubhagya, to quality and discom viability through UDAY and RDSS, and subsequently to prosumers through PM Surya Ghar.
71.tq: Arrange the policy stages from basic access to system viability and then consumer participation.
xs: Order: **household connections → quality and discom viability → prosumers** — option **(2)**.
Connections = **DDUGJY, Saubhagya**; viability = **UDAY, RDSS**; prosumers = **PM Surya Ghar**.
xa: Saubhagya (**2017**); UDAY (**Nov 2015**); RDSS (**2021**); PM Surya Ghar (**Feb 2024**).
Criticism: discom finances still weak; slow rooftop uptake and loan access.
**Leisang (Manipur)** was the last village electrified (**28 Apr 2018**).

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the current electricity-sector position:
1. India's installed capacity was 509.74 GW.
2. Renewable energy accounted for 49.83 per cent of installed capacity.
3. These figures relate to November 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: All three statements are correct: installed capacity was 509.74 GW and renewable energy constituted 49.83 per cent in November 2025.
71.tq: Link the quantitative values with the correct reference date instead of considering them in isolation.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: installed capacity **509.74 GW** — correct.
Statement 2: RE share **49.83%** — correct.
Statement 3: figures are of **Nov 2025** — correct.
xa: AP RE capacity: **10,639.75 MW**.
PM Surya Ghar aims at **30 GW** of rooftop solar.

71.s: Which of the following is identified as a continuing criticism of electricity distribution and rooftop-solar expansion?
o: Absence of renewable-energy potential and surplus loan availability
Weak discom finances, slow rooftop uptake and difficulties in accessing loans
Universal adoption of rooftop solar without financing constraints
Complete financial strength of all discoms and excessive rooftop adoption
71.x: The continuing concerns are weak discom finances, slow uptake of rooftop solar and difficulties in accessing loans.
71.tq: Select the option that combines all the stated challenges without reversing their direction.
xs: Continuing criticism: **weak discom finances**, **slow rooftop uptake** and **loan access** — option **(2)**.
The other options claim surplus loans or full discom strength, which the notes contradict.
xa: UDAY (**2015**) and RDSS (**2021**) both targeted discom viability (**ACS-ARR gap zero**).
PM Surya Ghar progress: **14.43 lakh** RTS systems (**2025**) against a **1 crore** target.
RDSS outlay: **₹3,03,758 crore**.

71.s: Which village in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified?
71.x: Leisang in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified.
71.tq: Use the distinctive place-name association to distinguish the first/last fact from nearby locations.
xs: **Leisang (Manipur)** was the last village electrified, on **28 Apr 2018** — option **(1)**.
Imphal, Thoubal and Churachandpur are not mentioned as last villages.
xa: **Saubhagya (2017)** later claimed **100%** household electrification.
Saubhagya electrified **2.86 crore** willing households.
Connections came first via **DDUGJY** and **Saubhagya**.

72.s: The Solar Park Scheme was launched by MNRE on:
72.x: The Solar Park Scheme was launched by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy on 12 December 2014.
72.tq: Direct date recall using nearby scheme milestones as distractors.
xs: MNRE launched the **Solar Park Scheme** on **12 December 2014** — option **(2)**.
**21 Mar 2017** is when its target was raised to **40,000 MW**; **Jul 2022** is the Simhadri floating plant's start.
xa: Original plan: **25 parks / 20,000 MW**, raised to **40,000 MW**; runs till **2025-26**.
CFA: **₹25 lakh/park** for DPR + up to **₹20 lakh/MW** or **30%** of cost.
**Ultra Mega Solar Park** = **500 MW or more** at one location.

72.s: An Ultra Mega Solar Park is defined as a solar park having a capacity of at least:
72.x: An Ultra Mega Solar Park has a capacity of 500 MW or more at one location.
72.tq: Discriminate the official threshold from the higher 1,000 MW figure.
xs: An **Ultra Mega Solar Park** is **500 MW or more** at one location — option **(3)**.
⚠ "**1,000 MW**" is the trap — it is WRONG (**APPSC 2019**).
xa: **Kurnool UMSP (1,000 MW)**, Gani-Sakunala, was once the **world's largest** single-location solar park.
**Ananthapuram-I** (**1,500 MW**) is at **NP Kunta**.
Solar Park Scheme target: **40,000 MW** (raised **21 Mar 2017**).

72.s:
Consider the following statements about floating solar power in India:
1. India has an estimated floating-solar potential of about 102 GW.
2. The existing floating-solar capacity is approximately 0.7 GW.
3. Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh is associated with a 278 MW floating solar project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: India has about 0.7 GW of floating solar capacity against an estimated 102 GW potential, and the 278 MW Omkareshwar project in Madhya Pradesh is the largest identified project.
72.tq: Compare existing capacity, potential and the largest project without reversing units.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: floating solar potential ~**102 GW** — correct.
Statement 2: installed ~**0.7 GW** — correct.
Statement 3: largest = **Omkareshwar** (**278 MW**, Narmada, MP) — correct.
xa: AP: NTPC's **25 MW** floating solar at **Simhadri, Visakhapatnam** (**APPSC 2021**).
⚠ **Simhadri** = floating solar; **Ramagiri** = hybrid park; **Talaricheruvu** = UMSP-II.

72.s: The subsidy mentioned for BC households consuming less than 200 units under the Andhra Pradesh rooftop programme is:
72.x: A subsidy of ₹20,000 is provided for 27.59 lakh BC households using less than 200 units.
72.tq: Direct recall of the subsidy amount with scaled distractors.
xs: **₹20,000** subsidy for **27.59 lakh BC** households using <**200** units (**2025-26**) — option **(3)**.
The other amounts are not given in the notes.
xa: **20.5 lakh SC/ST** households get ~**2 kW** each; Virtual Net Metering for ~**16 lakh** SC/ST (~**₹200/month** lease).
PM Surya Ghar in AP: **1,198.21 MWp** awarded.
Earlier target: **10 lakh** households by **2026-27**.

72.s: The estimated national potential of pumped storage projects is approximately:
72.x: The national pumped-storage potential is estimated at approximately 267 GW.
72.tq: Distinguish total potential from installed and operational components.
xs: National **PSP potential** is **~267 GW** — option **(3)**.
**7 GW** is the installed PSP capacity, not potential.
xa: Split: **58 GW** on-stream + **209 GW** off-stream.
Floating solar potential is **102 GW** against ~**0.7 GW** installed.
India solar capacity: **162.15 GW** (Jun **2026**).

72.s: Which of the following correctly represents the national pumped-storage position?
o: 58 GW on-stream, 209 GW off-stream and approximately 7 GW installed
7 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 209 GW installed
267 GW on-stream, 7 GW off-stream and 58 GW installed
209 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 267 GW installed
72.x: The national potential includes about 58 GW on-stream and 209 GW off-stream components, while installed capacity is approximately 7 GW.
72.tq: Separate potential categories from the installed-capacity figure.
xs: PSP: **58 GW on-stream**, **209 GW off-stream**, ~**7 GW installed** — option **(1)**.
The other options jumble these numbers; total potential is **~267 GW**.
xa: ⚠ Off-stream potential (**209 GW**) far exceeds on-stream (**58 GW**).

72.s: Andhra Pradesh opened 50,000 acres of barren land for solar leases primarily to:
o: replace all wind projects with nuclear projects
restrict private participation in solar generation
72.x: The barren land was opened for solar leases to avoid diversion of farmland for renewable-energy projects.
72.tq: Identify the policy rationale behind land-use decisions.
xs: AP opened **50,000 acres** of barren land for solar leases to **avoid farmland diversion** (Apr **2026**) — option **(1)**.
It is a response to **food-vs-fuel** land conflicts.
xa: **NREDCAP** handles land, clearances and single window for RE.
SAEL **600 MW** Kadapa used **2,400 acres**.
PM-KUSUM in AP targets **2.93 lakh** farm pumps.

72.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW, which one of the following correctly represents the approximate shares of solar and wind energy, respectively?
72.x: Solar energy accounts for approximately 53% and wind energy for approximately 41% of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW.
72.tq: Split the options by comparing the order and approximate shares of the two energy sources.
xs: AP RE mix: **solar ~53%** and **wind ~41%** of **10,639.75 MW** — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses them.
xa: AP's solar is ~**5.6 GW** vs India's **162.15 GW** (Jun **2026**) — a small share.
Major **2025** wind partnership in **Anantapur** (**APPSC 2025**).
Tata **800 MW** hybrid: **400 MW** wind at **Kanekallu**.

72.s: Ananthapuram-I Solar Park, with a capacity of 1,500 MW, is located at which place?
72.x: Ananthapuram-I Solar Park is located at NP Kunta in Ananthapuramu district.
