76.x: The CPCB, originally established under the Water Act, was assigned air-pollution functions, while SPCBs enforce the Act in the States. Statement 3 is false because the same board structure was used.
76.tq: Spot the wrong statement that reverses the institutional relationship between the two Acts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **CPCB** already existed under the **Water Act** and got air functions.
Statement 2: **SPCBs enforce** the Air Act.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **same boards** were given air functions, not a separate set.
xa: The Air Act was **modelled on the Water Act**.
**CPCB (1974)** came before the Air Act.
Both Acts require **prior consent** of the Board to establish/operate a polluting unit.

76.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Act)
a. Water Act, 1974
b. Air Act, 1981
c. Water Cess Act, 1977

d. Air Act amendment, 1987

List-II (Feature)
i. Inclusion of noise in the definition of air pollutant
 ii. Cess on water consumed by specified industries and local authorities
 iii. Standards for discharge of effluents
 iv. Declaration of air pollution control areas and emission standards

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
76.x: The Water Act deals with effluent-discharge standards; the Air Act deals with air-control areas and emissions; the Cess Act funds the Boards; and the 1987 amendment added noise.
76.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a reversed statutory feature.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Water Act** = standards for **discharge of effluents**; **Air Act** = **air pollution control areas** and emission standards.
**Water Cess Act** = cess on water by specified industries and local authorities; **1987 amendment** = **noise** included.
xa: Water Act aim: **wholesomeness of water**; Air Act aim: prevent, control and abate air pollution.
Water Act **Section 33A** and Air Act **Section 31A** give powers of directions.
Cess proceeds → **Consolidated Fund of India**.

76.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is popularly known as an umbrella legislation because it:
o: creates only judicial authorities for environmental disputes
coordinates the Central and State authorities created under the Water and Air Acts
76.x: The Act provides an umbrella framework to coordinate the Central and State authorities established under the Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981.
76.tq: Test the exact institutional meaning of a familiar descriptive term.
xs: EPA is umbrella legislation because it **coordinates the Central and State authorities under the Water and Air Acts** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a framework over the **Water Act 1974** and **Air Act 1981** authorities.
It does not replace State laws or deal only with forests; the specialised tribunal came with the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: **Primary authority**: Central Government.
Enacted after the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Dec 1984)** under **Article 253**.
Notifications under it: **Doon Valley (1989)**, **CRZ (1991)**, **EIA (1994, 2006)**.

76.s: Which one of the following is the primary purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: To regulate only the use of forest land
To protect and improve the environment and control pollution
To levy a cess on municipal water consumption
To establish a specialised environmental tribunal
76.x: The Act provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling pollution.
76.tq: Match the umbrella statute with its broad statutory purpose, not with a related specialised law.
xs: EPA's purpose is to **protect and improve the environment and control pollution** — so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
Forest-land diversion is the **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980**; water cess is the **1977** Act; the tribunal is the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: It implements **Stockholm Conference (1972)** decisions under **Article 253**.
Central powers: **standards**, **location of industries**, **hazardous wastes**, public health.
Section 5: directions including **closure**.

76.s:
Which of the following powers may be exercised by the Central Government under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Laying down emission and discharge standards
2. Regulating the location of industries
3. Managing hazardous wastes
4. Protecting public health
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
76.x: The Central Government’s powers include prescribing emission and discharge standards, regulating industrial locations, managing hazardous wastes and protecting public health.
76.tq: Treat a comprehensive list of statutory powers as correct only after checking every item.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are Central powers under EPA, so option **(4)** is correct.
The Centre lays down emission/discharge **standards**, regulates **location of industries**, manages **hazardous wastes** and protects **public health**.
xa: It can also issue directions including **closure** (**Section 5**).
Standards are set by MoEF&CC with CPCB and published in the **Gazette**; lead in paints capped at **90 ppm**.
**Primary authority** under EPA: Central Government.

76.s: Directions issued by the Central Government under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 may include:
o: appointment of judges to the National Green Tribunal
dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly
76.x: Section 5 empowers the Central Government to issue directions, including directions for closure of an industrial unit.
76.tq: Separate an environmental executive direction from powers belonging to constitutional or judicial authorities.
xs: **Section 5** directions can include **closure of an industrial unit** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The power belongs to the **Central Government**, the primary authority under EPA.
xa: Other Central powers: **standards**, location of industries, **hazardous wastes**, public health.
Water Act **Section 33A** and Air Act **Section 31A** also give powers of directions.
SC (Aug 2025) upheld PCBs' power to impose **environmental compensation** where harm is clear or imminent.

76.s: The National Ganga River Basin Authority, constituted in 2009, is an example of an authority constituted under:
o: Section 5 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
Section 16 of the Water Cess Act, 1977
76.x: The National Ganga River Basin Authority was an authority constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act.
76.tq: Use the section-number and body-name pairing to avoid confusing statutory authorities with constitutional bodies.
xs: The **National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009)** was set up under **Section 3(3) of EPA 1986** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Section 16** of EPA (not the Cess Act) creates the **Environment Protection Fund**.
xa: Another Sec 3(3) authority: **Central Ground Water Authority (1997)**.
Standards under EPA are published in the **Gazette**.
EPA rests on **Article 253**.

76.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted under which constitutional provision, to implement the decisions of which conference?
76.x: EPA 1986 rests on Article 253 (laws to implement international agreements) and gives effect to the Stockholm Conference (1972) decisions. Article 252 is the basis of the Water Act 1974, not EPA. Rio 1992 came after the Act. Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty, not a law-making power.
76.tq: Water Act = Art 252; EPA = Art 253 (Stockholm 1972).
xs: EPA 1986 rests on **Article 253** to implement **Stockholm Conference (1972)** decisions — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Article 252** is the basis of the **Water Act 1974**, not EPA.
xa: Trigger: the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Dec 1984)**.
EPA is **umbrella legislation** over Water Act and Air Act authorities.
**Primary authority**: Central Government.

76.s: The immediate trigger for the enactment of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was the:
76.x: The Act was enacted after the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (December 1984). Chernobyl (April 1986) is not linked to it. The LG Polymers leak (2020) came decades later. The Stockholm Conference is the source of the Article 253 obligation, not the trigger event.
76.tq: Bhopal 1984 = trigger; Stockholm 1972 = treaty basis.
xs: EPA was enacted after the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Dec 1984)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Stockholm Conference (1972)** is the source of the **Article 253** obligation, not the trigger event.
xa: Purpose: **protect and improve the environment** + control pollution (**APPSC 2025**).
Original penalty: up to **5 years** jail or **Rs 1 lakh** fine.
Penalties now decriminalised by the **Jan Vishwas Act 2023**.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the Environment Protection Fund under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986:
1. It is constituted under Section 16 and kept in the Public Account.
2. It holds fines collected under the Air, Water and Environment (Protection) Acts.
3. 75% of the Fund goes to the Centre and 25% to States/UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Fund is under Section 16 in the Public Account. Statement 2 is correct: it holds fines under the Air, Water and EP Acts. Statement 3 is wrong: the split is reversed - 75% to States/UTs and 25% to the Centre. Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: Section 16, Public Account, 75% States / 25% Centre - watch for the reversed split.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: the Fund is under **Section 16**, in the **Public Account**.
Statement 2: it holds **fines under Air, Water and EP Acts**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the split is **75% to States/UTs**, **25% to Centre**.
xa: **EPF Rules, 2026** were notified by **MoEFCC**.
⚠ Water Cess proceeds → **Consolidated Fund of India**; EP Fund → **Public Account**.
Green Credit guidelines: **16 Sep 2025**.

76.s:
Consider the following notifications issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986:
1. Doon Valley (1989): no industry burning more than 24 MT of coal/fuel a day.
2. Revdanda Creek (1989): area declared ecologically fragile and power plants barred.
3. Dhanu Taluka (1991): area declared ecologically fragile and power plants barred.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: Doon Valley (1989) barred industries burning over 24 MT of coal/fuel a day. Statement 2 is wrong: Revdanda Creek (1989) barred industries around the creek; the 'ecologically fragile, no power plants' rule belongs to Dhanu Taluka. Statement 3 is correct. Hence 1 and 3 only.
76.tq: Doon = 24 MT fuel cap; Revdanda = no industries around creek; Dhanu = fragile, no power plants.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Doon Valley (1989)** — no industry burning over **24 MT** coal/fuel a day.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Revdanda Creek (1989)** barred **industries around the creek**.
Statement 3: **Dhanu Taluka (1991)** — ecologically fragile; **no power plants**.
xa: **CRZ (1991)**: regulates coastal stretches; no ash/waste dumping.
**EIA (1994, then 2006)**: prior environmental clearance.
Also under EPA: **Eco-Sensitive Zones**, **Plastic Waste Management Rules**, **Green Credit Rules (2023)**.

76.s: The Coastal Regulation Zone notification issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 primarily:
o: regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping
requires prior clearance for all forest diversion
76.x: The CRZ notification of 1991 regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash and waste dumping in the regulated areas.
76.tq: Connect the environmental zone with its geographical subject and specific restriction.
xs: **CRZ** **regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was notified in **1991** under EPA; CRZ under EPA was confirmed in **Jul 2026**.
Forest diversion is the **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980**; the NGT came by the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: **Dhanu Taluka (1991)**: ecologically fragile; no power plants.
**EIA (1994, then 2006)**: prior environmental clearance.
**Uppada (Kakinada)** faces coastal erosion.

76.s: The Environmental Impact Assessment notification under the Environment (Protection) Act is associated with:
76.x: The EIA notification was issued in 1994 and was subsequently revised in 2006; it provides for prior environmental clearance.
76.tq: Pair the original notification year with its later revision and the clearance requirement.
xs: The **EIA** notification dates from **1994** with its subsequent **revision in 2006** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It requires **prior environmental clearance**.
xa: **Vanashakti v UoI**: SC nullified the **2021 Office Memorandum** allowing retrospective ECs; administrative orders cannot override **EIA Notification 2006**.
Ex post facto EC only via **Article 142** in fit cases (**31 Jul 2026**).
**White** category industries (score **20 or less**) need no consent/EC.

76.s:
Which of the following instruments has been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications
2. Plastic Waste Management Rules
3. Green Credit Rules
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
76.x: Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications, the Plastic Waste Management Rules and the Green Credit Rules are all instruments notified under the Environment (Protection) Act.
76.tq: Test whether the listed instruments belong to the umbrella Act rather than to a specialised statute.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are notified under EPA, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Eco-Sensitive Zones**, **Plastic Waste Management Rules** and **Green Credit Rules (2023)** are all EPA instruments.
xa: Green Credit: voluntary tree planting on **degraded land** earns credits.
Other EPA notifications: **Doon Valley (1989)**, **CRZ (1991)**, **EIA (1994, 2006)**.
**APPCB** implements waste rules (Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid).

76.s: Under the Green Credit Rules, 2023, voluntary tree planting on degraded land can earn:
76.x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 provide Green Credits for voluntary tree planting on degraded land.
76.tq: Match the environmental action with the exact official incentive term.
xs: Voluntary tree planting on degraded land earns **Green Credits** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This is under the **Green Credit Rules (2023)**, notified under EPA.
xa: Green Credit afforestation can be swapped for **compensatory afforestation** under **Van (S&S) Rules 2023**.
Guidelines issued **16 Sep 2025**.
⚠ Water Cess was subsumed with **GST in 2017**.

76.s: What was the original maximum punishment provided under the Environment (Protection) Act for an offence?
o: Only a written warning issued by the Central Government
Up to 5 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence
Life imprisonment and forfeiture of all property
Up to 2 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000, with no continuing penalty
76.x: The original penalty was imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, with an additional Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence.
76.tq: Read the full penalty structure, including the continuing-offence component, rather than only the headline punishment.
xs: EPA's original penalty was **up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh**, with **Rs 5,000 per day** for a continuing offence — so option **(2)** is correct.
These were the figures before the **Jan Vishwas Act 2023** changed the regime.
xa: The **PLI Act 1991** was also decriminalised — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly put these EPA figures under the **Water Act**.
**Water Act** penalties: **1.5 to 6 years'** jail.

76.s: The penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act was decriminalised through the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
76.x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act.
76.tq: Distinguish the original criminal penalty provisions from their later legislative modification.
xs: EPA's penalty regime was decriminalised by the **Jan Vishwas Act, 2023** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **NGT Act 2010** created a specialised tribunal; the **Forest Act 1980** and **Water Cess Act 1977** do not deal with EPA penalties.
xa: The same Act amended the **PLI Act 1991** — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
Water Act minor offences were decriminalised by amendment in **2024**.
Original EPA penalty: up to **5 years** or **Rs 1 lakh**.

76.s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 amended which environmental legislation referred to as the PLI Act, 1991?
76.x: The PLI Act mentioned in this context is the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, which was amended by the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023.
76.tq: Expand the exact abbreviation instead of choosing a look-alike statutory title.
xs: PLI Act 1991 = **Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was amended by the **Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023**.
xa: Offences decriminalised — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
Centre may give **Environmental Relief Fund** money to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration.
Relief for death raised **₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh**.

76.s:
With reference to the amendment of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 by the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, consider the following statements:
1. Offences were decriminalised, with penalties in place of imprisonment.
2. The Centre may give Environmental Relief Fund money to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration.
3. Penalty rates are now fixed in the Act itself rather than in rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: offences were decriminalised (penalty instead of imprisonment). Statement 2 is correct: Environmental Relief Fund money may go to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration. Statement 3 is wrong: rates were shifted to rules. Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: Jan Vishwas = decriminalise + rates moved to rules; relief for death Rs 25,000 -> Rs 5 lakh.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: offences decriminalised — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
Statement 2: **Environmental Relief Fund** money may go to **CPCB/SPCBs** for restoration.
Statement 3 is wrong: **rates were shifted to rules**.
xa: Relief for death raised **₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh**.
The **PLI Act** dates from **1991**.
EPA penalties were also decriminalised by **Jan Vishwas Act 2023**.

76.s: The relief payable in cases involving death was raised to what amount under the Jan Vishwas-related amendment?
76.x: The relief for death was increased from ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh.
76.tq: Distinguish the revised figure from the earlier compensation amount.
xs: Relief for death was raised to **₹5 lakh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It went up from **₹25,000** under the PLI Act amendment.
xa: Amended by **Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023**.
Rates were **shifted to rules**.
**Environmental Relief Fund** money can go to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration.

76.s: The imprisonment term prescribed for offences under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 ranges from:
76.x: The Water Act provides imprisonment of 1.5 to 6 years. 'Up to 5 years' is the original Environment (Protection) Act penalty, often wrongly placed under the Water Act. 6 months to 3 years and 2 to 7 years are not the stated terms.
76.tq: Water Act 1.5-6 years; EPA up to 5 years + Rs 1 lakh.
xs: Water Act imprisonment ranges from **1.5 to 6 years** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ "**Up to 5 years**" is the original **EPA** penalty, which some notes wrongly place under the Water Act.
xa: Water Act **minor offences** were decriminalised by amendment in **2024**.
**Section 33A** of the Water Act: directions and penalties.
EPA original: **Rs 1 lakh** fine, **Rs 5,000/day** for continuing offence.

76.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the institutional status of the CPCB?
o: It is a judicial body constituted under the National Green Tribunal Act.
It is a private regulatory organisation functioning without statutory authority.
It is a constitutional body under the Ministry of Finance.
It is a statutory body under MoEFCC and provides technical services to the Ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
76.x: The CPCB is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and also provides technical services to the Ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
76.tq: Identify the correct institutional status and parent ministry together.
xs: CPCB is a **statutory body under MoEFCC** and gives **technical services** to the Ministry under **EPA 1986** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not judicial, private or a constitutional body; it was created by the **Water Act** (**1974**).
xa: Chairperson nominated by the **Central Government**.
Functions: **co-ordinates SPCBs**; technical assistance, research, training, national monitoring.
NAMP network: **1,646 stations in 603 cities (March 2026)**.

76.s: Who nominates the chairperson of the CPCB and the chairperson of an SPCB, respectively?
76.x: The CPCB chairperson is nominated by the Central Government, while the SPCB chairperson is nominated by the concerned State Government.
76.tq: Compare the appointing authority at the Union and State levels.
xs: The **CPCB** chair is nominated by the **Central Government**, the **SPCB** chair by the **State Government** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the two.
xa: CPCB is a **statutory body** under **MoEFCC**.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs**; SPCBs enforce the Acts.
**APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the Water Act.

76.s: Which one of the following is primarily a function of the CPCB rather than an operational function of an SPCB?
o: Inspecting individual industrial plants within the State
Granting consent to individual industries in the State
Analysing samples collected for State-level enforcement
76.x: Coordination of SPCBs is a CPCB function. Inspection, sample analysis and granting consents to industries are among the operational functions of SPCBs.
76.tq: Separate the coordinating role of the central body from field-level State functions.
xs: **Coordinating SPCBs** is a CPCB function — so option **(4)** is correct.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs** and gives technical assistance, research, training and national monitoring.
Granting **consent** (CTE/CTO) to industries is done by the **SPCB**.
xa: CPCB is the **enforcement body** under the EPA framework (PYQ).
Two-stage consent from SPCB: **Consent to Establish** and **Consent to Operate**.
**APPCB** uses **computerised inspection allocation** — high-risk industries inspected more often.

76.s: For the purpose of environmental enforcement under the Environment (Protection) Act framework, which body is identified as the enforcement body?
76.x: The Central Pollution Control Board is identified as the enforcement body under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
76.tq: Distinguish the pollution enforcement agency from other environment-related attached bodies.
xs: The enforcement body under the EPA framework is the **CPCB** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Central Zoo Authority** (1992) and **FSI** are bodies under MoEFCC with other roles.
xa: CPCB is a **statutory body** giving technical services to MoEFCC under **EPA 1986**.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs**.
**National AQI** launched **2015**.

76.s: Real-time air-quality information from the monitoring network is available through which application?
76.x: Real-time air-quality information is provided through the SAMEER app. SAFAR is a separate air-quality and weather forecasting system.
76.tq: Discriminate between two similarly associated air-quality applications.
xs: Real-time air-quality data comes via the **SAMEER** app — so option **(3)** is correct (**12 Sep 2026**).
It draws on the **NAMP** network of **1,646 stations in 603 cities** (March 2026).
xa: Earlier NAMP figures: **516 cities**, **1,400+ stations**.
**National AQI** launched **2015**.
**NCAP (2019)**: **40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26** in **130 cities**.

76.s: The National Air Quality Index was launched in:
76.x: The National Air Quality Index was launched in 2015.
76.tq: Recall the launch year independently from the later NCAP target year.
xs: The **National AQI** was launched in **2015** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**2019** is the year of **NCAP**, not the AQI.
xa: Real-time data via the **SAMEER** app.
NAMP network: **1,646 stations in 603 cities (March 2026)**.
**NCAP** dates from **2019**.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):
1. It was launched in 2019.
2. It targets a 40% cut in PM10 by 2025-26 compared with 2019-20.
3. It covers 130 cities in 29 States/UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: NCAP dates from 2019. Statement 2 is correct: the target is a 40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26 vs 2019-20. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs (older sources say 131 cities). Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: NCAP: 2019, 40% PM10, 2025-26, 130 cities, 24 States/UTs.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: NCAP dates from **2019**.
Statement 2: target is **40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26** vs **2019-20**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it covers **130 cities in 24 States/UTs** (older notes say **131** cities).
xa: Real-time air data via **SAMEER**; National AQI from **2015**.
NAMP: **1,646 stations in 603 cities**.
The **Air Act 1981** aims to prevent, control and abate air pollution.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of the environment ministry:
1. The Department of Environment was set up in 1980.
2. It became the Ministry of Environment and Forests in 1985.
3. The Ministry was renamed MoEFCC in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: Department of Environment, 1980. Statement 2 is correct: Ministry of Environment and Forests, 1985. Statement 3 is wrong: renaming to MoEFCC came in 2014. Hence 1 and 2 only.
76.tq: 1980 Department -> 1985 Ministry -> 2014 'Climate Change' added.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Department of Environment, 1980**; statement 2: **Ministry of Environment and Forests, 1985**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was renamed **MoEFCC in 2014**.
xa: Bodies under it: **CPCB** (statutory), **Central Zoo Authority (1992)**, **NTCA (2005)**, BSI, ZSI, FSI.
CPCB gives **technical services** to the Ministry under **EPA 1986**.
MoEFCC notified the **EPF Rules, 2026**.

76.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
o: Central Pollution Control Board — statutory body
National Tiger Conservation Authority — established in 2005
Forest Survey of India — body unrelated to the Ministry
Central Zoo Authority — established in 1992 under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972
76.x: Option C is wrong: the Forest Survey of India is one of the bodies under MoEFCC (with BSI, ZSI and NTCA), not unrelated to it. CPCB is a statutory body under the Ministry, NTCA dates from 2005 and the Central Zoo Authority from 1992 under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
76.tq: Find the incorrect association among bodies connected with the Ministry.
xs: **Forest Survey of India — unrelated to the Ministry** is NOT correctly matched — so option **(3)** is correct.
**FSI** is one of the bodies under MoEFCC, along with **BSI, ZSI** and **NTCA**.
**CPCB** is statutory; **NTCA** dates from **2005**; **Central Zoo Authority** from **1992** under **WPA 1972**.
xa: MoEF became **MoEFCC in 2014**.
Department of Environment: **1980**; Ministry of Environment and Forests: **1985**.

76.s: Which of the following set consists entirely of bodies listed under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
76.x: The Botanical Survey of India, Zoological Survey of India and Forest Survey of India are listed among the bodies under MoEFCC.
76.tq: Identify the common institutional parent from a same-sector group.
xs: **BSI, ZSI and FSI** are all bodies under MoEFCC — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes list them with **NTCA**, the **Central Zoo Authority** and **CPCB** as bodies under the Ministry.
xa: **Central Zoo Authority** dates from **1992** (under WPA 1972); **NTCA** from **2005**.
Evolution: Department of Environment **1980** → Ministry **1985** → **MoEFCC 2014**.
CPCB gives technical services to the Ministry under **EPA 1986**.

76.s: Which of the following is a common requirement under both the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: Compulsory registration under the Water Cess Act
Declaration of every industrial site as an air pollution control area
Prior consent of the concerned Board to establish and operate a polluting unit
Prior approval of the National Green Tribunal for every industrial unit
76.x: Both Acts require prior consent of the Pollution Control Board for establishing and operating a unit that may cause pollution.
76.tq: Find the common legal mechanism rather than a feature belonging exclusively to one Act.
xs: Both Acts require **prior consent of the Board to establish and operate a polluting unit** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Industries need this consent **before discharging effluent**.
**Air pollution control areas** are declared by the State Government under the Air Act only; no NGT approval is required for each unit.
xa: Two-stage consent from SPCB: **Consent to Establish (CTE)** before setting up; **Consent to Operate (CTO)** before production.
**Jan 2026** amendment: single integrated application for Air and Water consents + waste authorisations.
**CTO valid until cancelled** (**29 Jan 2026**), instead of periodic renewal.

76.s:
Consider the following statements about the consent mechanism for polluting industries:
1. Consent to Establish (CTE) is needed before setting up the unit.
2. Both CTE and Consent to Operate (CTO) are granted by the Central Pollution Control Board.
3. Consent to Operate (CTO) is needed before production begins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: CTE is the first stage, before setting up. Statement 2 is wrong: both consents are given by the State Pollution Control Board, not the CPCB. Statement 3 is correct: CTO is needed before production. Hence 1 and 3 only.
76.tq: Two-stage consent from the SPCB: CTE before setting up, CTO before production.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: **CTE** is needed **before setting up** the unit.
Statement 2 is wrong: both consents come from the **SPCB**, not the CPCB.
Statement 3: **CTO** is needed **before production**.
xa: Both Water and Air Acts require **prior consent** of the Board.
Since **29 Jan 2026**, **CTO is valid until cancelled**.
**White** category industries need **no consent/EC**.

76.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Category)
 a. Red
 b. Orange
 c. Green
 d. White

List-II (CPCB score)
 i. 21–40
 ii. 20 or less
 iii. 60 and above
 iv. 41–59

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
76.x: Red corresponds to 60 and above, Orange to 41–59, Green to 21–40 and White to 20 or less.
76.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched ranges.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Red = highly polluting (**cement, petrochemicals**); White = practically non-polluting.
**Blue** (new) = essential environmental services, e.g. **Compressed Biogas** (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Basis: **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste** generated (CPCB, Jun 2026).

76.s: Which category is associated with cement and petrochemical industries under the CPCB colour classification?
76.x: Cement and petrochemical industries are examples of highly polluting industries in the Red category.
76.tq: Connect representative industries with the highest pollution category.
xs: **Cement and petrochemicals** are **Red** category — so option **(3)** is correct.
Red = **highly polluting**, CPCB Pollution Index score **60 and above**.
**Orange** = moderately polluting (**41-59**); **Green** = low polluting (**21-40**); **White** = practically non-polluting.
xa: ⚠ **Red ≥ 60**, **White ≤ 20**; Blue = essential environmental services.
Categorisation basis: **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste**.

76.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the White category?
o: CPCB score of 41–59; moderately polluting, with no regulatory oversight
CPCB score of 20 or less; practically non-polluting, with no consent or environmental clearance needed
CPCB score of 21–40; highly polluting, with mandatory annual consent
CPCB score of 60 or above; low polluting, with automatic clearance
76.x: The White category covers industries with a CPCB score of 20 or less and is described as practically non-polluting, requiring no consent or environmental clearance.
76.tq: Check both the numerical range and the regulatory consequence.
xs: **White** = score **20 or less**, **practically non-polluting**, **no consent or EC needed** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**41-59** is **Orange**, **21-40** is **Green**, **60 and above** is **Red** (highly polluting).
xa: **Blue** category (new): essential environmental services such as **Compressed Biogas**.
Consent stages: **CTE** before setting up, **CTO** before production.
Colour basis: emissions, effluents and **hazardous waste** generated.

76.s: A new category introduced for essential environmental services, such as Compressed Biogas, is:
76.x: The Blue category was introduced for essential environmental services, with Compressed Biogas cited as an example.
76.tq: Recall the newly added category by linking it to its representative activity.
xs: The new category for essential environmental services is **Blue** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Example: **Compressed Biogas** (**Economic Survey 2025-26**).
xa: Other categories: **Red (60 and above)**, **Orange (41-59)**, **Green (21-40)**, **White (20 or less)**.
White industries need **no consent/EC**.
Basis: **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste** (CPCB, Jun 2026).

76.s: The colour categorisation of industries by the CPCB is primarily based on the pollution potential arising from:
o: Energy consumption, exports and tax contribution
Land area, workforce and annual turnover
Water availability, raw material cost and product demand
Emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated
76.x: The basis of the colour categories is the pollution potential represented by emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated.
76.tq: Identify the exact regulatory basis instead of choosing general industrial characteristics.
xs: Colour categories are based on **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated** — so option **(4)** is correct (CPCB, **Jun 2026**).
It uses the **CPCB Pollution Index score**, not turnover, land area or tax contribution.
xa: **Red ≥ 60** (cement, petrochemicals); **White ≤ 20** (no consent/EC).
**Blue** = essential environmental services (e.g. Compressed Biogas).
Consents are given by the **SPCB**: CTE and CTO.

76.s: Under the consent reform introduced in January 2026, which of the following is correct?
o: A single application covers Air and Water consents as well as waste authorisations, and CTO remains valid until cancelled.
A single application is available only for mining projects.
Only waste authorisations are covered and CTO is abolished.
Separate applications remain compulsory and CTO expires annually.
76.x: The January 2026 reform provides for a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations, while consent to operate remains valid until cancelled.
76.tq: Apply the reform to a compliance scenario by identifying both its procedural and validity changes.
xs: The **Jan 2026** reform gives **a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations**, and **CTO valid until cancelled** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Earlier, CTO needed **periodic renewal**; the change is dated **29 Jan 2026**.
xa: **CTE** comes before setting up; **CTO** before production.
Both Water and Air Acts require **prior consent** of the Board.
Other current items: **EPF Rules, 2026**; **Vanashakti** ruling (31 Jul 2026).

76.s: Which of the following best describes the statutory role of the AP Pollution Control Board?
o: It implements the Water, Air and Environment Protection Acts and specified waste-management rules in Andhra Pradesh.
It administers only the Wildlife Protection Act in Andhra Pradesh.
It functions exclusively as an appellate judicial tribunal for environmental disputes.
It regulates only municipal drinking-water supply and not industrial pollution.
76.x: The APPCB implements the Water Act, Air Act and Environment (Protection) Act, along with rules relating to hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste.
76.tq: Select the comprehensive but precise description and reject the exclusive-function distractors.
xs: **APPCB implements the Water, Air and EP Acts and waste rules** in AP — so option **(1)** is correct.
Waste rules: **Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid**.
It is a regulator, not a judicial tribunal or a wildlife body.
xa: APPCB was set up in **1976** under the Water Act.
It issues **siting guidelines** for industries and SOPs for **marine outfall monitoring** and hazardous waste.
**Computerised inspection allocation** — high-risk industries inspected more often (APSES 2025-26).

76.s: Which of the following is an additional regulatory activity of the AP Pollution Control Board mentioned in relation to industrial pollution control?
o: Approving Union Budgets for pollution control
76.x: The APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries and also prepares SOPs for marine outfall monitoring and hazardous waste.
76.tq: Identify a practical regulatory function rather than an unrelated governmental power.
xs: APPCB issues **siting guidelines for industries** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It also prepares **SOPs for marine outfall monitoring and hazardous waste**.
xa: APPCB implements **Water, Air and EP Acts** + waste rules.
Ease of Doing Business: **computerised inspection allocation**.
APPCB set up in **1976** (APSES 2024-25).

76.s: Under the computerised inspection-allocation system used for ease of doing business, which industries are inspected more frequently?
o: All industries at exactly the same frequency
76.x: The system allocates inspections based on risk, with high-risk industries inspected more often.
76.tq: Apply the risk-based inspection principle to the practical scenario.
xs: **High-risk industries** are inspected more often — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is APPCB's **computerised inspection allocation** under **Ease of Doing Business** (APSES 2025-26).
xa: **White** category industries are practically non-polluting and need no consent/EC.
**Red** category (score **60 and above**) are highly polluting.
APPCB also issues **siting guidelines** for industries.

76.s: The power of Pollution Control Boards to levy environmental compensation under Section 31A of the Air Act and Section 33A of the Water Act was upheld subject to which limitation?
o: It may be exercised without any connection to actual or imminent harm.
It may be exercised only against government-owned industries.
It may be exercised only when environmental harm is clear or imminent.
It may be exercised only after a criminal conviction.
76.x: The power to levy compensation has been upheld, but its exercise must be connected with clear or imminent environmental harm.
76.tq: Apply the legal power to a fact pattern while checking the limiting condition.
xs: The compensation power applies **only when environmental harm is clear or imminent** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PCBs can impose it under **S.33A Water Act / S.31A Air Act**; upheld by the SC (**Aug 2025**).
xa: **Section 31A** (Air Act): power to give directions.
**Section 33A** (Water Act): directions and penalties.
**Vanashakti v UoI**: ex post facto EC only via **Article 142** in fit cases.

76.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vanashakti v. Union of India case:
1. The Supreme Court held that administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006.
2. The ruling on retrospective environmental clearance was prospective.
3. Ex post facto environmental clearance may be granted in every case merely on payment of a penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
76.x: The Court held that administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006, and its ruling was prospective. Ex post facto clearance is not available in every case merely on payment of a penalty; Article 142 may apply only in fit cases.
76.tq: Find the false absolute statement using the phrase “every case”.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: administrative orders **cannot override EIA Notification 2006**.
Statement 2: the ruling was **prospective**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ex post facto EC only via **Article 142** in **fit cases**.
xa: The SC nullified the **2021 Office Memorandum** allowing retrospective ECs on paying penalties.
Ruling dated **31 Jul 2026**.
**EIA** notification: **1994**, then **2006**.

76.s: The Supreme Court in M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India recognised environmental protection as inherently included in:
76.x: The Court held that environmental protection is inherently included within Corporate Social Responsibility.
76.tq: Associate the case with the precise legal principle rather than a neighbouring constitutional concept.
xs: In **M.K. Ranjitsinh v UoI**, environmental protection was held inherent in **Corporate Social Responsibility** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes record that **CSR inherently includes environmental protection**.
xa: **Vanashakti v UoI**: no retrospective ECs via the **2021 Office Memorandum**.
SC (**Aug 2025**) upheld PCBs' power to impose environmental compensation.
**NGT suo motu** notice to **Rajasthan, MP, UP** over sewage in drinking water.

76.s: The NGT suo motu notice concerning sewage in drinking water was issued to which group of States?
o: Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
76.x: The National Green Tribunal issued the suo motu notice to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh regarding sewage entering drinking water.
76.tq: Recall the exact geographical group attached to the reported action.
xs: The NGT notice went to **Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The issue was **sewage in drinking water** (**15 Jan 2026**).
xa: NGT chairperson: **Prakash Shrivastava**.
The NGT was set up by the **NGT Act 2010** — a specialised environmental tribunal.
NGT Act 2010 is the **latest** in the pollution-law chain.

76.s:
Consider the following statements comparing the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981:
1. The Water Act aims to maintain and restore the wholesomeness of water.
2. The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections, while the Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections.
3. The power to declare pollution control areas is a special feature of the Water Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Water Act aims to maintain and restore wholesomeness of water. Statement 2 is correct: Water Act 8 chapters/64 sections; Air Act 7 chapters/54 sections. Statement 3 is wrong: declaring air pollution control areas is the Air Act's special power; the Water Act's is standards for effluent discharge. Hence 1 and 2 only; 1 only leaves out a true statement.
76.tq: Control areas = Air Act; effluent standards = Water Act.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: Water Act aims to maintain and restore **wholesomeness of water**.
Statement 2: Water Act **8 chapters, 64 sections**; Air Act **7 chapters, 54 sections**.
Statement 3 is wrong: declaring **air pollution control areas** is the **Air Act's** power; the Water Act's is **standards for discharge of effluents**.
xa: ⚠ Water Act = **Article 252**; EPA = **Article 253**.
Air Act amended **1987** — **noise** added.
Both Acts use the same **CPCB and SPCBs**.

76.s: The Central Pollution Control Board is best described as:
o: A constitutional body created under the Environment Protection Act
A judicial body constituted under Article 21
A statutory body under the Water Act, also functioning under the Air Act, 1981
A temporary body established under the EIA Notification, 2006
76.x: The CPCB was established in 1974 as a statutory body under the Water Act and also operates under the Air Act, 1981. It sets standards and monitors air and water.
76.tq: Identify the correct parent statute and distinguish a statutory body from constitutional and temporary bodies.
xs: CPCB is **a statutory body under the Water Act, also functioning under the Air Act, 1981** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was created in **1974** as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution, renamed **CPCB** in **1988**.
It is not constitutional or judicial; the Air Act gave the existing board **air functions**.
xa: CPCB is under **MoEFCC** and gives technical services under **EPA 1986**.
Chair nominated by the **Central Government**.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs**.

76.s: Which legislation added air-pollution-related functions to the CPCB?
76.x: The Air Act, 1981 added air pollution functions to the CPCB, which had originally been constituted under the Water Act.
76.tq: Distinguish the parent legislation from the later legislation that expanded the Board’s functions.
xs: The **Air Act, 1981** gave CPCB its air-pollution functions — so option **(1)** is correct.
CPCB already existed under the **Water Act (1974)**.
xa: ⚠ **CPCB (1974)** came before the Air Act.
Air Act: in force **16 May 1981**; modelled on the Water Act.
The **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980** deals with forest land diversion, not pollution boards.

76.s: Which combination correctly identifies the FIRST and the LATEST laws in India’s pollution-control legislative sequence mentioned below?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
76.x: The Water Act of 1974 is regarded as India’s first pollution-control law, while the National Green Tribunal Act of 2010 is the latest in the stated legislative chain.
76.tq: Use the first-and-last method to identify the chronological extremes.
xs: **Water Act 1974** is the first and **NGT Act 2010** the latest — so option **(2)** is correct.
Chain: **Water 1974 → Water Cess 1977 → Forest 1980 → Air 1981 → EPA 1986 → NGT 2010**.
xa: The Water Act was India's **first pollution law**, passed under **Article 252**.
The NGT is a **specialised environmental tribunal**.
**CPCB (1974)** came before the Air Act.

76.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in which year?
76.x: The APPCB was set up in 1976 under the Water Act.
76.tq: Discriminate between closely related years associated with environmental institutions and laws.
xs: **APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the Water Act — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1974** is the Water Act/CPCB year; **1981** the Air Act; **1986** the EPA.
xa: APPCB enforces **Water, Air, EP Acts** and waste rules (APSES 2024-25).
It issues **siting guidelines** for industries.
**Computerised inspection allocation**: high-risk industries inspected more often.

76.s: Which one of the following preceded the Air Act in the stated institutional sequence of environmental regulation in India?
76.x: The Central Pollution Control Board was established in 1974, before the enactment of the Air Act. The APPCB was established later, in 1976.
76.tq: Identify the institution that came earlier by separating the central and State-level pollution-control bodies.
xs: The **Central Pollution Control Board** preceded the Air Act — so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes: **CPCB (1974) came before the Air Act** (**1981**); the Air Act only added air functions to it.
The **EP Fund** (under EPA **1986**) and the **NGT** (**2010**) came after the Air Act.
xa: ⚠ The notes also say **APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the Water Act — the key names the CPCB from the FIRST/LAST line.
CPCB was renamed from the Central Board by the **1988 amendment**.
Water Act **1974** = India's first pollution-control law.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of EIA in India:
1. The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
2. Before the 1994 notification, environmental clearance was only an administrative decision.
3. The EIA Notification, 2006 replaced the 1994 notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 1994 notification was issued on 27 January under the EPA, clearance had earlier been only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
77.tq: Arrange the legal transition in sequence and verify both the date and the status of clearance before 1994.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1: EIA Notification **1994** was notified on **27 Jan 1994** under **EPA**.
Statement 2: **till 1994**, EC was only an **administrative decision**.
Statement 3: the **EIA Notification 2006** (**14 Sep 2006**) replaced the 1994 notification.
xa: Public hearing was made mandatory by the **1997 amendment**.
Later amendments: **2009** (expanded list), **2013** (thermal power), **2015** (expansion and modernisation).
**Draft 2020** (post-facto, shorter consultation) has **not been finalised**.

77.s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is associated with the National Environmental Policy Act of the:
77.x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.
77.tq: Pair the legislation, country and year precisely.
xs: EIA originated in the **National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)** of the **United States, 1969** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1978** is a date given for India's first use of EIA, not the US origin; **1994** is India's first formal notification.
xa: India began in **1976-77**, when the Planning Commission asked **DST** to examine **river-valley projects**.
⚠ Sources differ on India's start: **1976-77** vs **1978**.
FIRST/LAST: first EIA law **NEPA 1969**; India's first sector appraised — **river-valley projects**.

77.s: In India, the Planning Commission asked the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects during:
77.x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.
77.tq: Distinguish the institutional beginning from the later first-use date.
xs: The Planning Commission asked **DST** to examine river-valley projects in **1976-77** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1969** is the US **NEPA**; **1993-94** and **1978-79** are not the stated start.
xa: ⚠ Some **2026** notes date first use to **1978** (river valley projects).
Next came large public-sector projects needing **Public Investment Board** clearance.
EIA was **codified in 1994**.

77.s: The first use of EIA in India is dated in some accounts to 1978 for:
77.x: The first use of EIA in India is dated to 1978 in connection with river-valley projects.
77.tq: Associate the earliest year with the first project sector.
xs: Some accounts date India's first EIA use to **1978** for **river-valley projects** — so option **(3)** is correct.
River-valley projects were **India's first sector appraised**.
xa: Other notes put the start at **1976-77**, when **DST** examined river-valley projects.
Then large public-sector projects needing **Public Investment Board** clearance.
Amendments later covered **thermal power (2013)** and **mining (2012 / 2018)**.

77.s: After river-valley projects, EIA scrutiny in India extended to large public-sector projects requiring clearance from the:
77.x: Large public-sector projects requiring Public Investment Board clearance became another early area of EIA application.
77.tq: Identify the institutional trigger associated with the early expansion of EIA.
xs: Large public-sector projects needing **Public Investment Board** clearance came next — so option **(3)** is correct.
This followed the first use for **river valley projects** (**1978** in the 2026 notes).
**SEAC** belongs to the **2006** notification and the **NGT** is a later tribunal — neither is the early clearance body.
xa: Till **1994**, EC was only an **administrative decision**.
EIA was codified in **1994** (27 Jan 1994).
Global origin: **NEPA, USA, 1969**.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Tool)
a. Environmental Impact Assessment
b. Life-Cycle Assessment
c. Cumulative Impact Assessment
d. Environmental audit

List-II (Scope)
i. Compliance check of an operating unit after the fact
ii. A product or process across its whole life cycle
iii. A project evaluated before it starts
iv. Combined effect of several projects in one area or basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: EIA concerns a project before it starts; LCA covers a product or process through its life cycle; cumulative impact assessment examines combined effects; and an environmental audit checks an operating unit after the fact.
77.tq: Start from the sure EIA pair and complete the one-to-one matching without repeating a scope.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**EIA** = a specific **project before it starts**; **LCA** = a **product/process across its life**.
**Cumulative Impact Assessment** = combined effect of several projects in one area/basin; **environmental audit** = compliance check of an **operating** unit after the fact.
xa: **SEA** = impacts of **policies, plans and programmes**, upstream of projects.
⚠ EIA = **project**; LCA = **product**; SEA = **policies/plans**; audit = **after** the fact.
The EIA/LCA definitions were asked in **APPSC 2025**.

77.s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
77.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
77.tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.
xs: A new transport policy calls for **Strategic Environmental Assessment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SEA** covers **policies, plans and programmes**, upstream of projects.
**Project-level EIA** studies one project before it starts; **LCA** a product's life cycle; an **audit** checks an operating unit after the fact.
xa: UPSC way-forward: **sector-wide EIAs** (strategic/cumulative) needed.
**Cumulative Impact Assessment**: combined effect of several projects in one basin.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and process technology.

77.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes EIA from LCA?
o: EIA evaluates a product from raw material to disposal, whereas LCA evaluates only a project before construction.
EIA evaluates a project before it starts, whereas LCA evaluates a product or process across its entire life cycle.
EIA is concerned with policies and programmes, whereas LCA is concerned only with public hearings.
Both EIA and LCA are compliance checks conducted only after operations begin.
77.x: EIA focuses on the impacts of a specific project before it starts. LCA considers the impacts of a product or process across its whole life cycle, from raw materials through disposal.
77.tq: Separate the object and time frame of assessment rather than treating the tools as interchangeable.
xs: **EIA evaluates a project before it starts; LCA evaluates a product or process across its life cycle** — so option **(2)** is correct.
LCA runs **cradle to grave** — raw material to disposal; option (1) reverses the two.
**Policies and programmes** belong to **SEA**; after-the-fact checks are an **environmental audit**.
xa: Both definitions were **APPSC 2025** answers.
**Cleaner production** and **green chemistry** shrink impacts at design stage → fewer residual impacts for EIA/LCA.
⚠ SEA = **policies/plans**; audit = **after** the fact.

77.s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
77.x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.
77.tq: Infer the broader assessment level from the phrase sector-wide.
xs: **Sector-wide EIAs** aim to strengthen **strategic and cumulative assessment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the **UPSC way-forward**: sector-wide EIAs (i.e., strategic/cumulative) needed.
xa: **SEA** = policies, plans, programmes; **Cumulative Impact Assessment** = several projects in one area/basin.
Criticism: EIAs by **proponent-paid consultants**; no central baseline data bank.
Suggested fix: an **independent EIA authority**.

77.s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
77.x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Distinguish prevention at source from treatment after pollution is generated.
xs: Cleaner production **cuts waste and pollution at source** through **process change or input substitution** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **preventive** strategy, the opposite of **end-of-pipe treatment**.
xa: **APPCB's** mandate includes encouraging **cleaner production technologies**.
**Green chemistry** designs products/processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
Both shrink impacts **at design stage**.

77.s: Which organisation’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
77.x: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board’s mandate includes encouraging cleaner production technologies.
77.tq: Match the institutional mandate with the correct environmental body.
xs: The **APPCB** mandate includes encouraging **cleaner production technologies** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Cleaner production cuts waste **at source**, versus end-of-pipe treatment.
xa: APPCB conducted the public hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage** (22 May 2026).
Public hearings are conducted by the **SPCB** with the **District Collector** presiding.
**Green chemistry** has **12 principles** (Anastas and Warner, 1998).

77.s: Green chemistry primarily involves designing products and processes that:
o: Reduce or eliminate the use or generation of hazardous substances
Increase the use of hazardous substances for higher efficiency
Transfer all pollution from production to disposal
Avoid consideration of raw materials and solvents
77.x: Green chemistry seeks to design products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances. It addresses environmental impacts at the design stage rather than merely treating pollution later.
77.tq: Choose the preventive design objective instead of an end-of-pipe measure.
xs: Green chemistry designs products/processes that **reduce or eliminate hazardous substances** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It acts at the **design stage**, not by moving pollution to disposal.
xa: **12 principles** by **Anastas and Warner, 1998**.
Examples: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**, **renewable feedstocks**, **design for degradation**.
**Cleaner production** cuts waste at source via process change or input substitution.

77.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Renewable feedstocks are associated with green chemistry.
2. Designing products for degradation is an example of a green chemistry principle.
3. Cleaner production relies exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
4. Both cleaner production and green chemistry seek to reduce impacts at the design stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cleaner production is preventive and seeks process or input changes at the source rather than relying exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
77.tq: Reject the extreme word exclusively and combine the related design-stage principles.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1 and 2: **renewable feedstocks** and **design for degradation** are green chemistry principles.
Statement 3 is wrong: cleaner production is **preventive**, cutting waste **at source**, versus end-of-pipe treatment.
Statement 4: both **shrink impacts at design stage**, so EIA/LCA find fewer residual impacts.
xa: Other principles: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**.
**12 principles**: Anastas and Warner, **1998**.
APPCB encourages **cleaner production technologies**.

77.s: The 12 principles of green chemistry were formulated by:
77.x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).
77.tq: Green chemistry = 12 principles, Anastas and Warner, 1998.
xs: The **12 principles** of green chemistry are by **Anastas and Warner, 1998** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Examples: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**, **renewable feedstocks**, **design for degradation**.
xa: Green chemistry: reduce or eliminate **hazardous substances**.
**Cleaner production**: cut waste **at source** (process change, input substitution).
EIA requires assessment of alternatives in **process technology**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the early stages of EIA:
1. Screening decides whether a project needs EIA and which category it falls in.
2. Scoping identifies the key issues and sets the Terms of Reference.
3. Scoping is the stage at which an expert committee evaluates the final EIA report.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: screening decides need for EIA and category. Statement 2 is correct: scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference. Statement 3 is wrong: evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee is appraisal, not scoping. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Screening = whether/which category; Scoping = ToR; Appraisal = expert committee.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **screening** decides whether a project needs EIA and its **category**.
Statement 2: **scoping** fixes the key issues and **Terms of Reference**.
Statement 3 is wrong: expert evaluation of the EIA report is **appraisal**.
xa: EIA 2006 stages: **Screening → Scoping → Public consultation → Appraisal → Decision**.
⚠ **Category A** has **no screening** — always full EIA.
**Baseline data** = survey of the existing environment.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA process:
1. Baseline data represents a survey of the existing environment.
2. Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives.
3. The Environmental Management Plan forms part of the mitigation planning process.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Baseline environmental conditions are surveyed, alternatives are compared during impact prediction, and mitigation planning includes an Environmental Management Plan.
77.tq: Combine three linked components of the impact-assessment stage.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Baseline data**: existing environment surveyed.
**Impact prediction**: alternatives compared; mitigation plan + **Environmental Management Plan**; risk assessment.
xa: **Monitoring**: EMP implementation is checked.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and **process technology**.
Criticism: **no central baseline data bank**; thin baseline in the **Great Nicobar** EIA.

77.s: Public consultation in the EIA process consists of:
o: A public hearing and written responses
Only written objections submitted to the Ministry
77.x: Public consultation includes both a public hearing and the consideration of written responses.
77.tq: Test the exact components of a formal procedure.
xs: Public consultation = **public hearing + written responses** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a **mandatory two-fold** consultation for scheduled projects.
It comes **before appraisal**, not after clearance.
xa: Conducted by the **SPCB**, **District Collector** presiding.
Notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days**.
Exempt: **defence, national-security and strategic** projects; **B2** projects.

77.s:
Match the stage of EIA with what happens at it:
List-I (Stage)
a. Appraisal
b. Decision
c. Monitoring
List-II (What happens)
i. Environmental clearance granted with conditions or rejected
ii. Expert committee evaluates the EIA report
iii. Implementation of the Environmental Management Plan is checked
Select the correct answer:
77.x: Appraisal is evaluation of the EIA report by the expert committee (a-ii); Decision is EC granted with conditions or rejected (b-i); Monitoring checks EMP implementation (c-iii). Option B swaps appraisal and decision; C and D wrongly link the EMP to appraisal or decision.
77.tq: Appraisal = committee reads report; Decision = grant/reject; Monitoring = EMP.
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-i, c-iii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Appraisal**: expert committee evaluates the EIA report; **decision**: EC granted with conditions or rejected.
**Monitoring**: **EMP** implementation checked.
xa: Category **A** appraised by **EAC**; **B1/B2** by **SEAC**.
Clearance: **MoEFCC** for A; **SEIAA** for B.
Earlier stages: **screening**, **scoping**, baseline data, **public consultation**.

77.s:
Arrange the following stages of EIA in the correct chronological order:
A. Appraisal
B. Screening
C. Decision
D. Scoping
77.x: The sequence is Screening, Scoping, Appraisal and Decision; public consultation occurs before appraisal.
77.tq: Use the first and last stages, then place the intervening steps.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — **Screening → Scoping → Appraisal → Decision** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under EIA 2006, **public consultation** comes between scoping and appraisal.
xa: **Scoping** sets the **Terms of Reference**.
**Monitoring** of EMP follows the decision.
**Category A** skips screening; always full EIA.

77.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
77.x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison between the old and new bases of appraisal.
xs: EIA 2006 shifted focus from **investment size to impact potential** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1994** notification covered industrial projects above **Rs 500 million** — an investment test; option (4) reverses the shift.
xa: EC is compulsory for **39 project categories**.
Safeguards: **air, water, land, biodiversity, wildlife habitat**.
Notified **14 Sep 2006** under **EPA 1986**.

77.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category)
a. Category A
b. Category B
c. Category A clearance
 d. Category B clearance

List-II (Authority)
i. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
 ii. State Expert Appraisal Committee
 iii. Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre
 iv. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
77.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC. Category B projects are appraised by the State EAC and cleared by SEIAA.
77.tq: Separate the appraisal authority from the clearance authority before matching the categories.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Category A**: appraised by central **EAC**, cleared by **MoEFCC**.
**Category B**: appraised by **SEAC**, cleared by **SEIAA**.
xa: ⚠ Only **B2** has no EIA; **B1** needs EIA.
**Category A**: no screening; always full EIA.
Backup bodies (2026): **SAEIA** for SEIAA; **SCEIA** for SEAC.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about the EIA Notification, 1994:
1. Schedule I projects needed clearance from the Ministry of Environment and Forests.
2. Industrial projects above Rs 500 million were covered.
3. Two-stage (site and final) clearance applied to all mining projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as per the 1994 notification. Statement 3 is wrong: two-stage site and final clearance applied to pithead thermal and valley projects, not to all mining projects. So options with 3 are wrong and 2 only leaves out a correct statement.
77.tq: 1994: Schedule I to MoEF, Rs 500 million, two-stage only for pithead thermal and valley projects.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Schedule I** projects needed **MoEF** clearance.
Statement 2: industrial projects above **Rs 500 million** were covered.
Statement 3 is wrong: **two-stage** (site + final) clearance applied to **pithead thermal and valley projects**, not all mining.
xa: Notified **27 Jan 1994** under EPA; also covered **fragile-area** projects.
Public hearing made mandatory by the **1997 amendment**.
Replaced by **EIA Notification 2006**.

77.s: The requirement of mandatory public hearing under the 1994 EIA framework was added through the:
77.x: Mandatory public hearing was added by the 1997 amendment to the 1994 framework.
77.tq: Separate the original notification from a later amendment.
xs: Mandatory public hearing was added by the **1997 amendment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was added to the **1994** EIA framework.
xa: Under **EIA 2006**: notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days**.
**Draft 2020** proposed cutting the notice from **30 to 20 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**, with the **District Collector** presiding.

77.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on:
77.x: The EIA Notification, 2006 was notified on 14 September 2006 and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Use the date-year pairing to reject close distractors.
xs: EIA Notification 2006 was notified on **14 September 2006** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**27 January 1994** is the date of the **1994** notification; **23 July 2026** is the SCEIA amendment.
xa: Issued under **EPA 1986**; replaced the **EIA Notification 1994**.
EC compulsory for **39 project categories**.
Shift from **investment size** to **impact potential**.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance is compulsory for how many project categories?
77.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
77.tq: Direct quantitative recall with nearby numerical distractors.
xs: EC is compulsory for **39 project categories** under EIA 2006 — so option **(2)** is correct.
The 2006 notification also covers safeguards for **air, water, land, biodiversity, wildlife habitat**.
xa: Focus shifted from **investment to impact potential**.
Categories: **A** (EAC → MoEFCC), **B1** and **B2** (SEAC → SEIAA).
Notified **14 Sep 2006**, replacing the **1994** notification.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EIA Notification, 2006:
1. It provides safeguards relating to air, water and land.
2. It includes safeguards for biodiversity and wildlife habitat.
3. It replaced the EIA Notification, 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: The 2006 notification addresses air, water, land, biodiversity and wildlife habitat, and replaced the 1994 notification.
77.tq: Check whether all elements of a regulatory framework belong together.
xs: All three statements — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
EIA 2006 safeguards **air, water, land, biodiversity, wildlife habitat**.
It **replaced the EIA Notification 1994**.
xa: Notified **14 Sep 2006** under EPA 1986.
EC compulsory for **39 project categories**.
Prior EC is **mandatory** under EIA 2006; post-facto approval only as a narrow exception.

77.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes Categories B1 and B2 under the EIA Notification, 2006?
o: B1 projects are cleared by EAC, whereas B2 projects are cleared by MoEFCC.
B1 projects do not require EIA, whereas B2 projects require full EIA.
B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not require EIA.
Both B1 and B2 projects always require full EIA by MoEFCC.
77.x: Category B1 projects require an EIA, while Category B2 projects do not; both are associated with state-level appraisal and clearance arrangements.
77.tq: Discriminate between the closely named B1 and B2 categories.
xs: **B1 projects require EIA, whereas B2 projects do not** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Both are appraised by **SEAC** and cleared by **SEIAA**, not by EAC or MoEFCC.
xa: ⚠ **A** → EAC → MoEFCC; **B1/B2** → SEAC → SEIAA; only **B2** has no EIA.
**B2** projects are also **exempt from public hearing**.
**Draft 2020** proposed moving more projects to **B2/exempt**.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of Category A projects under the 2006 EIA framework?
o: They are appraised by the EAC.
They undergo screening before full EIA is considered.
77.x: Category A projects do not undergo screening; they always require full EIA, are appraised by EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.
77.tq: Find the single reversed feature in a category description.
xs: "Category A undergoes **screening** before full EIA" is wrong — so option **(4)** is correct.
Category **A** has **no screening**; it **always** needs a full EIA.
It is appraised by the **EAC** and cleared by **MoEFCC** — options (1)-(3) are true.
xa: **B1** needs EIA; **B2** has no EIA; both go to **SEAC → SEIAA**.
**Screening** decides whether a project needs EIA and its category.
Jul 2026: Centre may remove **EAC/SEIAA/SEAC** members mid-term for persistent delays.

77.s: Public consultation for scheduled projects under the EIA framework is described as:
o: Optional for all Category A projects
A process conducted only after environmental clearance
A single-stage consultation conducted only through written submissions
77.x: Public consultation is a mandatory two-fold process involving public hearing and written responses for scheduled projects.
77.tq: Recall the procedural structure rather than one component alone.
xs: Public consultation is a **mandatory two-fold process** for scheduled projects — so option **(1)** is correct (Aug 2026).
The two parts: **public hearing + written responses**.
xa: Conducted by the **SPCB**, **District Collector** presiding.
Exempt: **defence and strategic** projects, **B2** projects, units in notified industrial estates.
**Draft 2020** proposed a shorter notice of **20 days**.

77.s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
77.x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.
77.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid swapping institutions.
xs: The **District Collector** presides over the public hearing — so option **(1)** is correct.
The hearing is **conducted by the SPCB** (22 May 2026).
xa: Notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days** (EIA 2006).
APPCB hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage** — HRF called the draft EIA error-ridden.
**SEIAA** and **EAC** clear projects; they do not preside over hearings.

77.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the public-hearing notice must be given at least how many days in advance, and the hearing must be completed within what period?
77.x: The notice period is at least 30 days, and the hearing is to be completed within 45 days.
77.tq: Pair two procedural time limits without reversing their order.
xs: EIA 2006: notice at least **30 days**; hearing completed within **45 days** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**20 days** is the **Draft 2020** proposal, not EIA 2006.
xa: ⚠ Notice **30 days** (EIA 2006) vs **20 days** (Draft 2020); hearing within **45 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**.
Public consultation = hearing + **written responses**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about exemption from public hearing in the EIA process:
1. Defence, national-security and strategic projects are exempt, as their details are kept confidential.
2. B2 projects and units inside notified industrial estates are exempt.
3. Whether a project is 'strategic' is decided by the State Pollution Control Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct exemptions. Statement 3 is wrong: 'strategic' is determined by the Central Government, which is criticised as arbitrary; the SPCB only conducts the hearing. So 1 only is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
77.tq: Exempt: defence/strategic, B2, industrial estates; 'strategic' is the Centre's call.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1: **defence, national-security and strategic** projects are exempt (details kept confidential).
Statement 2: **B2** projects + units inside **notified industrial estates** are exempt.
Statement 3 is wrong: "strategic" is **determined by the Central Government** — criticised as arbitrary.
xa: The SPCB only **conducts** the hearing, with the **District Collector** presiding.
The executive-exemption criticism dates to **2 Jan 2026**.
Criticism also: **hearings exempted**; EIAs by proponent-paid consultants.

77.s: Under the July 2026 amendment, if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide a proposal within 120 days, the proposal may escalate to:
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
77.x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.
77.tq: Link the time limit with the newly designated authority.
xs: After **120 days**, a SEAC proposal escalates to the new **SCEIA** via **PARIVESH** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is the **Jul 2026** amendment (23 Jul 2026), with auto-transfer via PARIVESH.
xa: ⚠ **SAEIA** ↔ SEIAA; **SCEIA** ↔ SEAC.
Category B no longer defaults to the central **EAC** when a state committee lapses.
Backup bodies' tenure: **6 + 6 months** (max 1 year).

77.s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
