Which of the following may be preserved through cryopreservation?
1. Gametes and embryos
2. Seeds and pollen
3. Disease-free meristems and tissues
4. DNA
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
87.x: Cryopreservation can be applied to gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, disease-free meristems, tissues and DNA. Therefore all four statements are correct.
87.tq: Treat the list as a materials question and check whether each biological material is included in the preservation range.
xs: All four can be cryopreserved — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
Listed materials: **gametes, embryos**, **seeds, pollen**, disease-free **meristems**, **tissues**, **DNA**.
xa: Medium: **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
**LaCONES** (CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad) is **India's frozen zoo**.
**Meristem culture** gives **virus-free propagation**.

87.s: The immediate biological effect of storing material in liquid nitrogen during cryopreservation is that it:
o: converts all tissues into permanent fossil material
destroys DNA but preserves only cell walls
increases metabolic activity and accelerates growth
halts metabolic activity while retaining viability
87.x: Liquid nitrogen at cryogenic temperature halts metabolic activity while allowing the preserved material to remain viable for decades or centuries.
87.tq: Infer the purpose of the technology from the relation between temperature, metabolism and viability.
xs: Liquid nitrogen **halts metabolic activity** while keeping the material **viable** — option **(4)**.
Material stays viable for **decades or centuries**.
xa: Temperature: **-196°C** (APPSC 2021 key).
It allows later **IVF** and research.
The **National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank** stores **DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos** of threatened wild animals.

87.s: LaCONES at Hyderabad is best described as which one of the following?
o: A national authority for licensing zoos
India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking
India’s first botanical garden for medicinal plants
A wildlife census office under UNESCO
87.x: LaCONES, the Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species, is associated with CSIR-CCMB at Hyderabad and functions as India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking.
87.tq: Break the institutional description into location, parent organisation and function.
xs: **LaCONES** is **India's frozen zoo**, using **assisted reproduction and DNA banking** — option **(2)**.
It is the **Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species**, at **CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad**.
Zoo recognition is the job of the **Central Zoo Authority**, not LaCONES.
xa: The **National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank** is at **Nehru Zoological Park**.
Cryopreservation uses **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
The **CZA** (set up **1992**) recognises zoos.

87.s:
The National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank at Nehru Zoological Park stores which of the following?
1. DNA and tissues
2. Gametes and embryos
3. Only plant seeds
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
87.x: The bank stores DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos of endangered and threatened wild animals. It is not limited to plant seeds.
87.tq: Reject the exclusive and misplaced storage category in statement 3.
xs: The bank stores **DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos** — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it banks material of **endangered and threatened wild animals**, not only plant seeds.
xa: It is at **Nehru Zoological Park**.
**LaCONES** (CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad) handles **assisted reproduction** and **DNA banking**.
Plant seeds go to gene banks such as **ICAR-NBPGR** and vaults like **Svalbard**.

87.s: The National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank at Hyderabad is located at the:
o: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
87.x: India’s first bank for DNA, tissues and embryos of endangered wild animals is located at Nehru Zoological Park, Hyderabad.
87.tq: Use the specific institutional location to distinguish a wildlife genetic resource bank from plant gene banks.
xs: The **National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank** is at **Nehru Zoological Park** — option **(3)**.
It stores **DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos** of endangered and threatened wild animals.
**NBRI** is a botanical institute in **Lucknow**.
xa: **LaCONES** at **CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad** is India's **frozen zoo**.
Cryopreservation uses **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
Material stays viable for **decades or centuries**.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden — Shibpur, Howrah
National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI — Darjeeling
87.x: The Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, known for the Great Banyan and associated with the Botanical Survey of India, is at Shibpur in Howrah, West Bengal.
87.tq: Use the location of the best-known garden as the sure pair and eliminate shifted locations.
xs: The **Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden** is at **Shibpur, Howrah** — option **(1)**.
**Kew** is in **London**; the **CSIR-NBRI** garden is in **Lucknow**; **Lloyd** is in **Darjeeling**.
xa: The Shibpur garden is known for the **Great Banyan** and belongs to the **BSI**.
The **Government Botanical Garden** is at **Ooty**.
A botanical garden is **ex-situ** — PYQ: "not an in-situ site".

87.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Botanical garden)
a. National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI
b. Lloyd Botanical Garden
c. Government Botanical Garden
d. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

List-II (Location)
i. Ooty
ii. Lucknow
iii. London
iv. Darjeeling
87.x: The National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI is at Lucknow, Lloyd Botanical Garden at Darjeeling, Government Botanical Garden at Ooty and Kew at London.
87.tq: Begin with the international Kew–London pair and then complete the three Indian location matches.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
**CSIR-NBRI** — **Lucknow**; **Lloyd** — **Darjeeling**; **Government Botanical Garden** — **Ooty**; **Kew** — **London**.
xa: NBRI's **Banthara** station holds a **field gene bank**.
**Indian Botanic Garden** (Great Banyan) is at **Shibpur, Howrah**.
**Darjeeling** also hosts the **Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park** (red panda breeding).

87.s: The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, described as the largest botanical garden in the list, is located in:
87.x: The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, is located in London, United Kingdom.
87.tq: Distinguish the international garden from the Indian botanical gardens by location.
xs: **Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew** is in **London, UK** — option **(1)**.
It is called the **"largest botanical garden"**.
**Darjeeling** has Lloyd; **Lucknow** has CSIR-NBRI; **Ooty** has the Government Botanical Garden.
xa: Kew's **Millennium Seed Bank** at **Wakehurst** is the largest store of **wild** plant seeds.
India's **Indian Botanic Garden** is at **Shibpur, Howrah**.
Botanical gardens are **ex-situ** conservation.

87.s: The field gene bank of the National Botanical Research Institute is located at which research station?
87.x: The Banthara research station of NBRI holds a field gene bank.
87.tq: Test the specific sub-location rather than the headquarters of the institution.
xs: NBRI's field gene bank is at its **Banthara** research station — option **(1)**.
**Los Banos** hosts the **International Rice Genebank**; **Chang La** the high-altitude seed vault; **Spitsbergen** the **Svalbard** vault.
xa: NBRI = **National Botanical Research Institute**, **Lucknow** (CSIR).
Field gene banks keep **vegetatively propagated** or **recalcitrant-seed** crops.
Examples: **mango, coconut, banana**.

87.s: Which of the following pairs of zoological parks in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park — Visakhapatnam; Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park — Tirupati
Indira Gandhi Zoological Park — Tirupati; Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park — Visakhapatnam
Indira Gandhi Zoological Park — Kakinada; Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park — Vijayawada
Indira Gandhi Zoological Park — Amaravati; Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park — Nellore
87.x: The Indira Gandhi Zoological Park is at Visakhapatnam and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park is at Tirupati.
87.tq: Match each facility with its exact city before considering the combined option.
xs: **Indira Gandhi ZP — Visakhapatnam**; **Sri Venkateswara ZP — Tirupati** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the two cities.
xa: Both zoos are run by the **Zoo Authority of Andhra Pradesh (ZAAP)**.
They are noted for **animal display**, **conservation breeding** and visitor amenities.
AP has **4 deer parks** and **2 zoos**.

87.s: The Indira Gandhi Zoological Park and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park in Andhra Pradesh are run by which authority?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board only
Central Zoo Authority of India alone
87.x: Both zoological parks are run by the Zoo Authority of Andhra Pradesh.
87.tq: Apply the ‘who administers the facility?’ institutional-authority test.
xs: AP's two zoos are run by the **Zoo Authority of Andhra Pradesh (ZAAP)** — option **(4)**.
The **CZA** only **recognises zoos** nationally; the **NBA** and **APSBB** handle biodiversity rules.
xa: The zoos: **Indira Gandhi ZP, Visakhapatnam** and **SV ZP, Tirupati**.
The **CZA** was set up in **1992** under the **WPA 1972** (**1991** amendment).
The zoos are noted for **conservation breeding**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Zoo Authority (CZA):
1. It is a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, provided for by the 1991 amendment.
2. It was set up in 1992 under the Ministry of AYUSH.
3. It recognises zoos and coordinates planned conservation breeding.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Statement 1 is correct: CZA is statutory under WPA 1972 (1991 amendment). Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up in 1992 under MoEF&CC, not AYUSH (AYUSH runs the NMPB). Statement 3 is correct: it recognises zoos and coordinates conservation breeding. So only '1 and 3 only' fits; every other option includes statement 2 or omits 3.
87.tq: CZA = MoEF&CC (1992); NMPB = AYUSH (2000) - a common swap trap.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **CZA** is a statutory body under the **WPA 1972** (**1991** amendment).
Statement 2 is wrong: it was set up in **1992** under **MoEF&CC**, not AYUSH.
Statement 3: it **recognises zoos** and coordinates **planned conservation breeding**.
xa: ⚠ CZA: **1991** amendment, set up **1992**.
**AYUSH** runs the **National Medicinal Plants Board** (**2000**).
AP's zoos are run by **ZAAP**.

87.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Species)
a. Vultures
b. Great Indian Bustard
c. Red panda

List-II (Conservation-breeding centre)
i. Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
 ii. Sam and Ramdevra centres
 iii. Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
87.x: Vultures are associated with the Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore, the Great Indian Bustard with Sam and Ramdevra in Jaisalmer, and the red panda with Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park.
87.tq: Start from the sure species–centre pair and match the remaining pairs.
xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–ii, c–i** — option **(1)**.
**Vultures** — **Jatayu** Conservation Breeding Centre, **Pinjore**, Haryana (BNHS).
**Great Indian Bustard** — **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer** (with WII); **red panda** — **Padmaja Naidu** Himalayan ZP, **Darjeeling**.
xa: **GIB** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Breeding programmes (2026): **Snow Leopard**, **Asiatic Lion**, **GIB**.
The **CZA** coordinates planned conservation breeding.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Great Indian Bustard:
1. It is also known as Godawan.
2. It is the State bird of Rajasthan.
3. Its population is estimated to be less than 150.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: The Great Indian Bustard is called Godawan, is the State bird of Rajasthan, and has a population estimated at fewer than 150 individuals.
87.tq: Combine three directly related identifying facts and check each statement independently.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Great Indian Bustard** is the **Godawan**, **Rajasthan's state bird**, with a population **<150**.
xa: It is **Critically Endangered**.
A **2024 SC order** mandated **underground power lines** in its habitat.
Breeding centres: **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer**, with **WII**.

87.s: The 2024 Supreme Court order relating to the habitat of the Great Indian Bustard mandated which measure?
o: Conversion of the habitat into a marine reserve
87.x: The 2024 Supreme Court order mandated underground power lines in the Great Indian Bustard’s habitat to reduce threats to the species.
87.tq: Match the judicial order with its precise conservation measure.
xs: The **2024 SC order** mandated **underground power lines** in the GIB's habitat — option **(3)**.
The order did not relocate villages, ban research or create a marine reserve.
xa: The **GIB (Godawan)** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Conservation breeding: **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer**.
It is one of the 2026 breeding programmes, with **Snow Leopard** and **Asiatic Lion**.

87.s: The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), established in 2000, functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
87.x: The NMPB was established in 2000 under the Ministry of AYUSH and promotes the cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.
87.tq: Use the establishment year and ministry pairing to distinguish the board from environmental bodies.
xs: The **National Medicinal Plants Board (2000)** is under the **Ministry of AYUSH** — option **(2)**.
It promotes **cultivation and conservation** of medicinal plants.
⚠ The **CZA** is under **MoEF&CC** — do not confuse.
xa: **Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** is a **CSIR** mission.
**BD Rules 2024** encourage **cultivated** medicinal plants.
NBA/SBB approvals now take **90 days** (**180** for IPR).

87.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission?
o: A CZA programme for breeding endangered mammals
A Supreme Court programme for underground power transmission
An UNESCO programme for recognising biosphere reserves
A CSIR mission for cultivating rare or threatened medicinal plants and developing phytopharmaceutical drugs
87.x: The Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission is associated with CSIR and focuses on rare or threatened medicinal plants and phytopharmaceutical drug development.
87.tq: Distinguish the mission by its agency, plant focus and drug-development objective.
xs: The **Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** is a **CSIR** mission for **cultivating rare/threatened medicinal plants** and **phytopharmaceutical drug development** — option **(4)**.
The **CZA** handles zoos; **UNESCO MAB** recognises BRs; underground power lines come from an **SC** order on the GIB.
xa: The **NMPB** (**2000**) is under the **Ministry of AYUSH**.
**BD Rules 2024** encourage **cultivated** medicinal plants.
**CSIR-NBRI** in **Lucknow** runs the National Botanical Garden.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024:
1. They encourage the use of cultivated medicinal plants.
2. They provide faster approvals by the NBA and SBB in specified cases.
3. The approval period mentioned for IPR-related matters is 180 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: The 2024 Rules encourage cultivated medicinal plants, provide faster NBA/SBB approvals, and mention 90 days generally and 180 days for IPR-related matters.
87.tq: Check each numerical and policy detail rather than relying on the broad subject alone.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **BD Rules 2024** encourage **cultivated** medicinal plants.
They speed up **NBA/SBB** approvals to **90 days**, and **180** days for **IPR**.
xa: They also **decriminalise some provisions**.
The **NMPB** (**2000**, AYUSH) promotes medicinal-plant cultivation.
**CSIR's Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** develops phytopharmaceutical drugs.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Biosphere Reserves, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries:
1. A Biosphere Reserve is associated with UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme, but such recognition does not by itself change the legal status or ownership of land.
2. National Parks are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, through State notification.
3. Wildlife Sanctuaries are established only through UNESCO notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified by the State under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; UNESCO does not notify them.
87.tq: Find the wrong authority in statement 3 and separate UNESCO recognition from statutory notification.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: a **BR** rests on **UNESCO MAB recognition**, with **no change in legal status or ownership**.
Statement 2: **NPs** are notified by the **State** under the **WPA 1972**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **sanctuaries** too are **state-notified under WPA 1972**, not by UNESCO.
xa: BR boundaries are zoned **core-buffer-transition**.
NPs are **clearly demarcated**; sanctuary boundaries are **not strictly specified**.
India has **109 NPs** and **573 WLS**.

87.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of human rights and grazing in the three categories of protected areas?
o: Settlements are prohibited in every zone of a Biosphere Reserve; National Parks permit grazing; Wildlife Sanctuaries permit unrestricted grazing.
National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries provide identical rights, while Biosphere Reserves permit no settlements.
Settlements are allowed in the transition zone of a Biosphere Reserve; National Parks permit no rights or grazing; grazing in a Wildlife Sanctuary is regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
Settlements are allowed throughout National Parks; Biosphere Reserves prohibit all human use; grazing in Wildlife Sanctuaries is regulated by UNESCO.
87.x: Settlements may exist in the transition zone of a Biosphere Reserve. National Parks provide no rights and no grazing, while some rights exist in sanctuaries and grazing is regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden.
87.tq: Compare the authorities and the degree of human-use restriction rather than treating all protected areas alike.
xs: BRs allow **settlements in the transition zone**; NPs allow **no rights, no grazing**; sanctuary grazing is **regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden** — option **(3)**.
NPs and sanctuaries do not give identical rights — sanctuaries allow **some rights**.
xa: NP boundaries change only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A BR does not change **land ownership**.
Sanctuaries regulate human activity but **permit it to an extent**.

87.s: With reference to the boundaries of protected areas, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: National Park — boundaries are not clearly demarcated
Biosphere Reserve — zoned into core, buffer and transition areas
Biosphere Reserve — only a single undivided core zone
Wildlife Sanctuary — boundaries are always strictly specified
87.x: A Biosphere Reserve is organised into core, buffer and transition zones. National Parks are clearly demarcated, whereas sanctuary boundaries are not strictly specified.
87.tq: Match each category with its distinctive boundary characteristic and reject reversed comparisons.
xs: A **BR** is zoned into **core, buffer and transition** areas — option **(2)**.
**NPs** are **clearly demarcated**, so option (1) is wrong.
**Sanctuary** boundaries are **not strictly specified**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: The **core** is usually an NP or sanctuary under the **WPA 1972**.
The **buffer** allows research, education, eco-restoration.
The **transition zone** holds settlements, farming, tourism.

87.s: Which of the following best explains the role of Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in relation to the 30x30 conservation objective?
o: They are restricted to marine areas and cannot include community-managed landscapes.
They include only areas inside National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
They recognise effective conservation areas outside conventional protected areas and can help meet the 30x30 objective.
They replace all Biosphere Reserves recognised under UNESCO's MAB Programme.
87.x: OECMs can cover effectively conserved areas outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands, and thereby support the 30x30 objective.
87.tq: Apply the distinction between formal protected areas and conservation areas outside them.
xs: **OECMs** recognise effective conservation areas **outside the formal PA network** and help meet **30x30** — option **(3)**.
They lie **outside** NPs and sanctuaries, so option (2) is wrong; they do not replace BRs.
APSBB plans them in **sacred groves, greenbelts, wetlands** — not only marine areas.
xa: India's PA share is only **5.32%** — hence the need for OECMs.
OECMs **confer no legal, financial or management authority**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.

87.s: Which one of the following sets correctly identifies the firsts associated with conservation in India?
o: Gulf of Mannar — first OECM; Palk Bay — first National Park; Aravalli Biodiversity Park — first dugong reserve
Gulf of Mannar — first marine Biosphere Reserve; Palk Bay — first dugong reserve; Aravalli Biodiversity Park — first OECM
Palk Bay — first marine Biosphere Reserve; Gulf of Mannar — first dugong reserve; Aravalli Biodiversity Park — first National Park
Anamalai — first marine Biosphere Reserve; Gulf of Mannar — first Hornbill Conservation Centre; Palk Bay — first OECM
87.x: Gulf of Mannar is the first marine Biosphere Reserve, Palk Bay is the first dugong reserve and Aravalli Biodiversity Park is the first OECM.
87.tq: Discriminate among several ‘first’ claims by matching each initiative with its conservation category.
xs: **Gulf of Mannar** — first marine BR; **Palk Bay** — first dugong reserve; **Aravalli Biodiversity Park** — first OECM — option **(2)**.
Other options shuffle these FIRSTs; **Anamalai** is the first **Hornbill Conservation Centre**.
xa: Palk Bay reserve covers **448 sq km**.
First marine **NP**: **Gulf of Kachchh**.
First BR: **Nilgiri** (**1986**); first community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb**.

87.s: Anamalai Tiger Reserve is associated with which of the following conservation firsts?
87.x: Anamalai is associated with India's first Hornbill Conservation Centre.
87.tq: Use the named-site and named-facility association to avoid swapping the conservation firsts.
xs: **Anamalai** is India's **first Hornbill Conservation Centre** (2026) — option **(2)**.
First OECM = **Aravalli Biodiversity Park**; first dugong reserve = **Palk Bay**; first marine BR = **Gulf of Mannar**.
xa: Palk Bay's dugong reserve covers **448 sq km**.
Aravalli Biodiversity Park (**2022**) is a restored mining site.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

87.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major criticism or pressure affecting protected areas?
o: Complete absence of human pressure in protected landscapes
Evictions and conflicts in certain Biosphere Reserves
87.x: Protected areas face human pressure rather than its absence. The stated concerns include inadequate funding and staffing, land grabbers, poachers, miners and eviction-related conflicts.
87.tq: Look for the absolute reversal of the documented criticism.
xs: PAs face **human pressure**, so "**complete absence of human pressure**" is not a criticism — option **(1)**.
Real criticisms: PAs are **small, underfunded, short-staffed**; they face **land-grabbers, poachers, miners**.
**Evictions in Agasthyamalai** and ESZ width versus mining are listed debates.
xa: A **growing share of tigers** now lives **outside reserves**.
Only **5.32%** of India's area is under PAs.
The **SC ordered eviction of encroachers** from Agasthyamalai BR (Jun 2026).

87.s: Ex-situ conservation is particularly important when:
o: The objective is to preserve every interaction within the original ecosystem.
A protected area has no need for seed or gene storage.
A species' natural habitat has been lost or become unsuitable, and its species or genes must be conserved elsewhere.
Only wild landscapes without human intervention are available.
87.x: Ex-situ conservation serves as a fallback when habitats are lost or unsuitable, conserving species or their genetic material outside the natural ecosystem.
87.tq: Distinguish habitat-level in-situ conservation from species- or gene-level ex-situ conservation.
xs: Ex-situ is the **fallback for species with lost habitats** — option **(3)**.
Preserving every ecosystem interaction is the strength of **in-situ**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **Captive breeding** suits species whose **habitat is permanently lost**.
**Gene banks** guard **food security** against climate stress.
Ex-situ limits: needs **space and money**; **cannot save the ecosystem**.

87.s: Which one of the following correctly compares in-situ and ex-situ conservation?
o: In-situ conserves only genes, whereas ex-situ conserves complete ecosystems in nature.
In-situ protects the whole ecosystem, whereas ex-situ primarily conserves the species or its genes outside the natural habitat.
Ex-situ is used only for landscapes, whereas in-situ is used only for laboratories.
Both methods necessarily conserve the whole ecosystem in its original location.
87.x: In-situ conservation protects species along with their ecological setting, while ex-situ conservation focuses mainly on species or genetic material outside the natural habitat.
87.tq: Use the level of conservation—ecosystem versus species or genes—to distinguish the two methods.
xs: **In-situ protects the whole ecosystem**; **ex-situ saves the species or its genes only** — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the roles; option (4) is wrong because ex-situ cannot save the ecosystem.
xa: In-situ is the **most effective** method — it keeps species interactions intact.
Ex-situ = **off-site**: zoos, botanical gardens, seed and gene banks, cryopreservation.
PYQ: "not an in-situ site" = **Botanical Garden**.

87.s: Madhav Gadgil's work is particularly associated with which conservation perspective?
o: Urban management of the Aravalli OECM alone
Exclusive conservation of marine mammals in Palk Bay
Laboratory-based preservation of crop genes in a gene bank
Landscape-level conservation in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
87.x: Madhav Gadgil's work shaped the landscape-level conservation approach in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
87.tq: Match the conservation thinker with the landscape and scale of conservation associated with his work.
xs: **Madhav Gadgil**'s work shaped **landscape-level conservation** in the **Nilgiri BR** — option **(4)**.
He died in **Jan 2026** (reported 9 Jan 2026).
xa: **Nilgiri** was India's **first BR** (**1986**) and spans **TN, Kerala, Karnataka**.
Nilgiri lies within the **Western Ghats WHS**.
It was the first Indian entry in the **WNBR** (**2000**).

87.s: Which statement best reflects the emerging conservation concern regarding tigers and protected areas?
o: All tigers are now confined exclusively to National Parks.
Protected areas have eliminated all threats from miners and poachers.
An increasing share of tigers is living outside formally designated tiger reserves.
Tiger populations outside reserves have become irrelevant to conservation planning.
87.x: A growing share of tigers is reported to live outside reserves, highlighting the need for landscape-level conservation beyond formally protected areas.
87.tq: Reject absolute statements and identify the careful trend statement.
xs: A **growing share of tigers** now lives **outside reserves** (29 Jul 2026) — option **(3)**.
PAs still face **land-grabbers, poachers, miners**, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: India has **58 Tiger Reserves**.
**NSTR** is **India's largest TR by area**.
PAs are **small, underfunded, short-staffed**.

87.s: The proposed OECMs in Andhra Pradesh are intended to include areas such as:
o: Only National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
Sacred groves, wetlands and industrial greenbelts outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
Only marine areas beyond the territorial sea
87.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board plans OECMs outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, wetlands and industrial greenbelts.
87.tq: Apply the outside-formal-reserves requirement to the examples of proposed sites.
xs: **APSBB** plans OECMs in **sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands** outside **reserve forests, NPs and WLS** — option **(3)**.
OECMs lie **outside** the formal PA network, so option (2) is wrong.
The aim is to help meet **30x30** (14 Jun 2026).
xa: OECMs are recognised for **outcomes** and do **not change land ownership**.
**4 criteria**: outside PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
APSBB also plans a **Marine ABS framework**.

88.s: Sri Venkateswara National Park is spread across which districts?
88.x: Sri Venkateswara National Park is located in Annamayya and Tirupati districts.

xa: First reserve: **Corbett**.

IBCA was launched in **April 2023** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):
1. It is a statutory body created through the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
2. It is chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. Under Section 38V(3), each State must prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: NTCA became statutory through the 2006 WPA amendment. Statement 2 is wrong: NTCA is chaired by the Union Environment Minister (the Prime Minister chairs the NBWL). Statement 3 is correct: Section 38V(3) requires a Tiger Conservation Plan for every reserve. Hence 1 and 3 only.
89.tq: PM chairs NBWL; Environment Minister chairs NTCA and the NBWL Standing Committee.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **NTCA** became statutory via the **2006 amendment** to the **WPA 1972**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is **chaired by the Union Environment Minister**.
Statement 3: **Section 38V(3)** requires a **Tiger Conservation Plan** for every reserve.
xa: The **Tiger Task Force** led to the NTCA and the **WCCB**.
The NTCA runs the **All India Tiger Estimation** with **WII** every **4 years**.
**MEE 2022**: **51** TRs assessed, **12** "Excellent", average **78%**.

89.s: The TX2 goal adopted at the Global Tiger Summit was to:
o: double the population of wild tigers by 2022
create two tiger reserves in every State by 2022
increase India’s tiger population twofold by 2010
89.x: TX2 was the goal of doubling the global population of wild tigers by 2022.
89.tq: Decode the named international target by linking the abbreviation with its stated objective.
xs: **TX2** = **double wild tigers by 2022** — option **(1)**.
It was set at the **Global Tiger Summit**, **St Petersburg, November 2010**.
xa: **India met TX2 ahead of schedule**.
The summit also began **International Tiger Day, 29 July**.

89.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Global Tiger Summit of 2010?
1. It was held in St Petersburg in November 2010.
2. It set the TX2 goal.
3. International Tiger Day on 29 July traces its origin to this effort.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: The summit was held in St Petersburg in November 2010, adopted TX2, and is associated with International Tiger Day on 29 July.
89.tq: Combine event location, date, objective and legacy in a coded statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The summit met in **St Petersburg** in **November 2010**, set **TX2**, and began **International Tiger Day, 29 July**.
xa: TX2 = double wild tigers by **2022**; India met it early.
The **Global Tiger Forum** dates from **1993** (HQ **New Delhi**).
Other efforts: **IBCA**, **ITHCP** (led by **IUCN**), **CA|TS**.

89.s: Projects located in tiger corridors require clearance from the:
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
89.x: Projects in tiger corridors require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife.
89.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent wildlife authority.
xs: Projects in tiger corridors need **NBWL Standing Committee** clearance — option **(3)**.
The **NTCA** implements Project Tiger but does not alone clear corridor projects.
xa: A **3rd railway line** threatens the **Satpura-Melghat corridor** (4 Aug 2026).
A **growing share of tigers** disperses **outside reserves**, raising conflict.
The **Global Tiger Forum** is an international body, not a clearance authority.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about tiger reserves in India:
1. There are 58 tiger reserves in 18 States.
2. Their combined area is about 84,488 square kilometres.
3. This area is approximately 2.6 per cent of India’s area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: India has 58 tiger reserves in 18 States, covering about 84,488 sq km, or approximately 2.6% of the country’s area.
89.tq: Test the reserve count, State count and area share as one data set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
India has **58 reserves** in **18 States**, covering **84,488 sq km** — about **2.56%** (~**2.6%**) of its area.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **75,796 sq km**.
At the start (**1973**): **9 reserves**, **18,278 sq km**.
Largest: **NSTR**, about **5,443 sq km** core.

89.s: Which is the largest tiger reserve in India by area?
89.x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh is India's largest tiger reserve, with a core area of about 5,443 sq km. Bandipur, Corbett and Kanha are smaller.
89.tq: Test the largest-reserve comparison using the area-based distinction.
xs: **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)** is **India's largest tiger reserve** — option **(1)**.
Its core area is about **5,443 sq km**, in the **Nallamala** hills of AP.
**Corbett** is the **first** reserve, not the largest.
xa: NSTR anti-poaching camps are rising from **89 to 150** (30 Jul 2026).
AP will receive **4 female tigers** from **Maharashtra** and **MP**.
**Gaur** are being reintroduced in NSTR (Jul 2026).

89.s: Under the Management Effectiveness Evaluation of tiger reserves by 2022, which of the following was reported?
o: 58 reserves evaluated, all rated Excellent and an average score of 100%
51 reserves evaluated, none rated Excellent and an average score of 28%
51 reserves evaluated, 12 rated Excellent and an average score of 78%
12 reserves evaluated, 51 rated Excellent and an average score of 78%
89.x: By 2022, 51 reserves had been evaluated; 12 were rated Excellent, with an average score of 78%.
89.tq: Match the evaluation count, top-category count and average score without reversing them.
xs: **MEE 2022**: **51** reserves assessed, **12** "Excellent", average **78%** — option **(3)**.
Option (4) swaps **51** and **12**.
xa: India has **58 tiger reserves**.
**Section 38V(3)** requires a **Tiger Conservation Plan** for every reserve.
The **NTCA** is chaired by the **Union Environment Minister**.

89.s: CA|TS in the context of tiger conservation stands for:
89.x: CA|TS stands for Conservation Assured Tiger Standards.
89.tq: Expand the conservation accreditation acronym exactly.
xs: **CA|TS** = **Conservation Assured Tiger Standards** — option **(3)**.
It is one of the global tiger efforts, with **IBCA** and **ITHCP**.
xa: **ITHCP** is led by **IUCN**.
The **Global Tiger Forum** (**1993**) is in **New Delhi**.
**TX2** = double wild tigers by **2022**.

89.s: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted at what interval and jointly by which organisations?
o: Every five years by MoEFCC and BNHS
Every three years by WII and Forest Survey of India
Every four years by NTCA and WII
Every two years by NTCA and Zoological Survey of India
89.x: All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years by NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India.
89.tq: Match frequency with the correct institutional partnership.
xs: The **All India Tiger Estimation** is held every **four years** by **NTCA with WII** — option **(3)**.
It uses **camera traps** and the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
xa: The camera-trap survey holds a **Guinness World Record**.
The old **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping + ExtractCompare**.

89.s: All India Tiger Estimation is recognised as the world's largest camera-trap survey. This recognition is associated with which organisation?
89.x: The All India Tiger Estimation's camera-trap survey, run by NTCA with WII, holds a Guinness World Record as the world's largest camera-trap survey.
89.tq: Identify the external recognition body rather than the agency conducting the survey.
xs: The tiger estimation's camera-trap survey holds a **Guinness World Record** — option **(3)**.
It is run by **NTCA with WII** every **4 years**.
xa: **ExtractCompare** software identifies tigers by **stripe pattern**.
**M-STrIPES** = Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status.

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth cycle of All India Tiger Estimation conducted in 2022?
o: 3,925 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925
2,967 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 4,925
89.x: The 2022 estimation recorded 3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925.
89.tq: Distinguish the principal estimate from the upper estimate in paired figures.
xs: **2022 (5th cycle)**: **3,682 tigers**, upper estimate **3,925** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two figures.
xa: Annual growth: **6.1%**.
India holds about **70-75%** of the world's wild tigers.

89.s: The number of tigers estimated in India in 2006 was:
89.x: The 2006 tiger estimate recorded 1,411 tigers.
89.tq: Use the direct numerical-recall pattern for a census benchmark.
xs: India had **1,411** tigers in **2006** — option **(1)**.
xa: The **NTCA** became statutory in **2006**, the same year.
**TX2** aimed to double wild tigers by **2022**; India met it early.
Growth rate: **6.1%** a year.

89.s: India holds approximately what share of the world’s wild tiger population?
89.x: India holds approximately 70–75% of the world’s wild tigers.
89.tq: Use the range rather than confusing it with an exact census figure.
xs: India holds about **70-75% of the world's wild tigers** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes say **70%**, others **75%**.
xa: India also has **60%** of the world's **Asian elephants**.
**58 tiger reserves** cover about **2.56%** of India's area.

89.s: Which technique replaced the old pugmark method in all-India tiger estimation?
o: Camera trapping supported by ExtractCompare software
Counting tiger kills reported by villages
Only satellite imagery without field verification
89.x: The old pugmark technique was replaced by camera trapping and ExtractCompare software, which identifies tigers through stripe patterns.
89.tq: Identify the modern method by contrasting it with the obsolete field technique.
xs: The **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping** with **ExtractCompare** software — option **(1)**.
ExtractCompare identifies tigers by their **stripe pattern**.
xa: The survey uses the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
It is held every **4 years** by **NTCA with WII**.
It holds a **Guinness World Record** as a camera-trap survey.

89.s: M-STrIPES is an acronym for:
o: Mapping System for Terrestrial Protected Regions—Intensive Protection and Ecological Security
Monitoring States for Tiger Recovery—Integrated Population and Ecosystem Studies
Management Strategy for Tiger Reserves—International Protection and Ecological Survey
Monitoring System for Tigers—Intensive Protection and Ecological Status
89.x: M-STrIPES means Monitoring System for Tigers—Intensive Protection and Ecological Status.
89.tq: Expand the official acronym exactly, avoiding look-alike expansions.
xs: **M-STrIPES** = **Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status** — option **(4)**.
It is used in the **All India Tiger Estimation**.
xa: ⚠ **M-STrIPES** = tigers; **MIKE** = elephants (**CITES**).
**ExtractCompare** identifies tigers by stripe pattern.
The estimation runs every **4 years** (**NTCA with WII**).

89.s: Project Elephant was launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme in which month and year?
89.x: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (some sources say 1991-92). '1990' is the trap: APPSC 2022 treated a 1990 launch as the incorrect statement.
89.tq: Use the precise month-year rather than confusing the financial year with the launch year.
xs: **Project Elephant** was launched in **February 1992** as a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Launched in **1990**" is wrong (APPSC **2022**); some notes say **1991-92**.
xa: It covers **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
It also covers the welfare of **captive** elephants.
The elephant became the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010**.

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of Project Elephant?
o: Protection of elephant habitats and corridors
Protection of only captive elephants and not wild elephants
89.x: Project Elephant covers wild elephants, their habitats and corridors, mitigation of conflict, and the welfare of captive elephants. It is not restricted to captive elephants.
89.tq: Find the option narrowed by the extreme word ‘only’.
xs: "**Only captive elephants, not wild ones**" is not an objective — option **(3)**.
Objectives: protect elephants, their **habitats and corridors**; mitigate **man-elephant conflict**; welfare of **captive** elephants.
⚠ The reverse trap — "only wild elephants" — is also wrong (UPPSC **2017**).
xa: Human-elephant conflict causes **over 500 human deaths a year**.
**MIKE** (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) is a **CITES** programme.
Launched **February 1992**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding elephant reserves in India:
1. India has 33 Elephant Reserves.
2. These reserves are distributed across 14 States.
3. They may overlap tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: India has 33 Elephant Reserves in 14 States, and these areas can overlap tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests.
89.tq: Test the complete numerical and institutional description together.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
India has **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
They overlap **tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests** (**WPA 1972**, **Indian Forest Act 1927**).
xa: AP's only elephant reserve: **Rayala** (**Anantapuramu Circle**), including **Koundinya WLS**.
**Brahmagiri-Nilgiri-Eastern Ghats ER** holds one of the world's largest Asian elephant populations.
India has **22,446 elephants** (Apr 2026).

89.s: MIKE, associated with elephant conservation, stands for:
o: Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants
89.x: MIKE stands for Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants and is a CITES programme.
89.tq: Expand the exact acronym and identify the associated international programme.
xs: **MIKE** = **Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants** — option **(1)**.
It is a **CITES** programme.
xa: ⚠ **MIKE** = elephants; **M-STrIPES** = tigers.
**Project Elephant** began in **February 1992**.
India has **60%** of the world's Asian elephants.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about Asian elephants:
1. Only male Asian elephants carry tusks; tuskless males are called makhnas.
2. An elephant herd is usually led by the strongest adult male.
3. The gestation period is about 22 months, the longest of any mammal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: only males have tusks and tuskless males are makhnas. Statement 2 is wrong: the herd is led by a female (matriarch). Statement 3 is correct: gestation is about 22 months, the longest among mammals. Hence 1 and 3 only.
89.tq: Matriarch leads the herd (UPSC 2020 trap).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: only male Asian elephants have **tusks**; tuskless males are **"makhnas"**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the herd is led by a **female (matriarch)** (UPSC 2020).
Statement 3: gestation is about **22 months**, the **longest of any mammal**.
xa: Elephant = **National Heritage Animal** (**2010**).
⚠ Gangetic dolphin = **National Aquatic Animal** (**2009**).
India has **22,446 elephants** (Apr 2026).

89.s: Elephant crop-raiding incidents in Andhra Pradesh are specifically noted from which districts?
89.x: Elephant raids on crops are reported in Chittoor and Anantapur.
89.tq: Separate the district-level fact from the broader State-level conservation information.
xs: Elephant **crop raids** in AP occur in **Chittoor** and **Anantapur** — option **(3)**.
**Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** are known for **Olive Ridley** nesting beaches, not elephants.
xa: **Koundinya WLS** (**Chittoor**) borders **Tamil Nadu** and is AP's **only elephant habitat**.
It lies in the **Rayala Elephant Reserve** (**Anantapuramu Circle**).
**Project HANUMAN** (**3 March 2026**) aims to reduce human-wildlife conflict.

89.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has about 60% of the world’s Asian elephants.
2. Human-elephant conflict causes more than 500 human deaths a year.
3. The count of elephants in the 33 reserves is reported as 29,964 in the older 2017 figure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: India has about 60% of the world’s Asian elephants; conflict causes over 500 human deaths annually; and 29,964 is the older 2017 count for elephants in 33 reserves.
89.tq: Check multiple figures and distinguish a dated count from a current estimate.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
India has **60%** of the world's Asian elephants; conflict kills **over 500** people a year.
**29,964** is the older **2017** figure.
xa: The latest count is **22,446 elephants** (Apr 2026).
India has **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
**MIKE** is a **CITES** programme on illegal elephant killing.

89.s: The count of elephants reported in the April 2026 estimate is:
89.x: The April 2026 estimate reports 22,446 elephants. The figure 29,964 is the older 2017 count cited separately.
89.tq: Distinguish the newer estimate from the older comparison figure.
xs: The April 2026 estimate is **22,446 elephants** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **29,964** is the older **2017** figure.
xa: India has **60%** of the world's Asian elephants.
Compare: **3,682** tigers, **891** lions, **718** snow leopards.
Human-elephant conflict: **over 500** human deaths a year.

89.s: In which year was the elephant declared India's National Heritage Animal?
89.x: The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010. 1992 is the launch of Project Elephant, 2009 is when the Ganges river dolphin became the National Aquatic Animal, and 2020 is the launch of Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
89.tq: Heritage Animal 2010; Aquatic Animal (dolphin) 2009.
xs: The elephant was declared the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010** — option **(3)**.
**1992** = Project Elephant; **2009** = Gangetic dolphin as **National Aquatic Animal**; **2020** = Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
xa: The dolphin was declared on **5 October 2009** — now **National Dolphin Day**.
**Project Elephant** was a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**.
Only male Asian elephants carry **tusks**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Project Cheetah:
1. It involved the translocation of African cheetahs to India.
2. The cheetahs were released at Kuno National Park in Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh.
3. It was intended to restore open forest and grassland ecosystems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. Project Cheetah brought African cheetahs to Kuno National Park and seeks to restore open forest and grassland ecosystems.
89.tq: Combine location, species identity and conservation purpose in a coded statement question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**African cheetahs** were brought to **Kuno NP** (**Sheopur, MP**, on the Kuno river).
The purpose is to restore **open forest and grassland** ecosystems (APPSC-G1 2022).
xa: Batches: **8** from **Namibia** (**17 Sep 2022**); **12** from **South Africa** (**Feb 2023**).
About **30** cheetahs now, with India-born cubs.
Debate: deaths and doubts on **Kuno's carrying capacity**.

89.s: The cheetahs introduced under Project Cheetah are correctly identified as
o: African lions surviving only in Namibia
Asiatic cheetahs sourced from Botswana and Iran
African cheetahs, while the Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran
89.x: The introduced animals are African cheetahs. The critically endangered Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran.
89.tq: Separate the African cheetah from the geographically restricted Asiatic cheetah.
xs: Project Cheetah uses **African cheetahs**; the **Asiatic cheetah** (CR) survives only in **Iran** — option **(4)**.
Sources were **Namibia**, **South Africa** and **Botswana** — not Iran.
The cheetah was declared **extinct in India in 1952**, so none survive in India.
xa: ⚠ One report names "**Nigeria**" — the correct country is **Namibia**.
Release site: **Kuno NP**, **Sheopur, MP**.
**2** **Botswana** females were released into the wild in **May 2026**.

89.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the judicial history of cheetah reintroduction in India is correct?
o: The Supreme Court first ruled on reintroduction in 1973.
The Supreme Court ordered reintroduction only after the 2022 release.
The Supreme Court rejected the reintroduction programme in 2013.
The Supreme Court first ruled on reintroduction in 2012.
89.x: The Supreme Court first ruled on cheetah reintroduction in 2012 and set out the reintroduction programme.
89.tq: Match the institutional action with its correct year.
xs: The SC first ruled on cheetah reintroduction in **2012** — option **(4)**.
**2013** was the SC order to move **Gir lions to Kuno** — not a cheetah rejection.
**1973** is **Project Tiger**; the first release came later, in **2022**.
xa: Gujarat did not carry out the lion order, so **Kuno went to cheetahs**.
**M.K. Ranjitsinh** (**March 2024**) modified the **GIB** power-line order.
First cheetah batch: **8** from **Namibia**, **17 Sep 2022**.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Batch)
A. Eight cheetahs
B. Twelve cheetahs
C. Two female cheetahs

List-II (Source and date)
1. Namibia — 17 September 2022
2. South Africa — February 2023
3. Botswana — May 2026

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
89.x: Eight cheetahs came from Namibia in September 2022, twelve from South Africa in February 2023, and two females were released from Botswana in May 2026.
89.tq: Start from the sure batch-date pair and eliminate mismatched codes.
xs: Correct code: **A-1, B-2, C-3** — option **(1)**.
**8 cheetahs** — **Namibia**, **17 Sep 2022**; **12 cheetahs** — **South Africa**, **Feb 2023**.
**2 females** — **Botswana**, released **May 2026**.
xa: All went to **Kuno NP** (**Sheopur, MP**).
Population: about **30** with India-born cubs.
⚠ "**Nigeria**" in one report is wrong — it is **Namibia**.

89.s: The cheetah, the only large mammal to have gone extinct in India in recent history, was declared extinct in India in:
89.x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. 1947 is Independence, 1972 is the Wildlife (Protection) Act, and 2012 is when the Supreme Court first ruled on its reintroduction.
89.tq: Cheetah extinct 1952; back at Kuno 2022.
xs: The cheetah was declared **extinct in India in 1952** — option **(2)**.
It is the **only large mammal** lost in India in recent history.
**2012** is the SC's first ruling on its reintroduction.
xa: The **Asiatic cheetah** survives only in **Iran**.
**Project Cheetah** aims to restore **open forest and grassland**.
First batch to **Kuno**: **17 Sep 2022**.

89.s: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 primarily to mark
o: the declaration of the cheetah as extinct in India
the first census of Asiatic lions
89.x: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger.
89.tq: Link an organisation's launch with the milestone it commemorated.
xs: **IBCA** was launched in **April 2023** at **Mysuru** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger** — option **(4)**.
Project Tiger began in **1973**.
xa: IBCA is a **treaty-based inter-governmental organisation**.
Secretariat: **New Delhi** — ⚠ **not Geneva**.
First IBCA summit: **New Delhi**, **1-3 June 2026**.

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
89.x: The seven big cats are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Gharial is not a big cat covered by the IBCA.
89.tq: Find the non-member by checking the exact species composition.
xs: The **gharial** is a crocodilian, not a big cat — option **(4)**.
IBCA's **7 big cats**: **tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma**.
xa: IBCA is open to **96 range countries** plus non-range countries.
**37 countries** have consented to join; **Saudi Arabia** was the **26th** member and **Bangladesh** the **27th**.
The gharial was covered by the **Crocodile Project** (**1975**).

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the International Big Cat Alliance:
1. It is a treaty-based inter-governmental organisation.
2. Its Secretariat is in New Delhi.
3. Its headquarters is in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The IBCA Secretariat is in New Delhi; Geneva is not its headquarters.
89.tq: Use a location trap involving a well-known international-city distractor.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: IBCA is a **treaty-based inter-governmental organisation**.
Statement 2: its **Secretariat is in New Delhi**.
Statement 3 is wrong: ⚠ "**HQ in Geneva**" is false.
xa: The India-IBCA agreement was signed **17 April 2025**.
⚠ **Global Tiger Forum** and **IBCA** are both in **New Delhi**; **IUCN** and **WWF** are both in **Gland**.
**China is unlikely to join** (12 May 2026).

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the membership position of the International Big Cat Alliance?
o: It is restricted to seven big-cat range countries.
Only non-range countries can join it.
It was pitched to 96 range and non-range countries, and 37 countries including India had consented to join.
89.x: The IBCA was opened to 96 range and non-range countries, and 37 countries including India had consented to join.
89.tq: Distinguish the countries approached from the countries that consented to join.
xs: IBCA was **pitched to 96 range and non-range countries**, and **37 countries including India** have consented to join — option **(4)**.
It is open to non-range countries too, so options (1) and (2) are wrong; **96** is the pitch, not confirmed members.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024**: statement I true, II false on IBCA membership.
**Saudi Arabia** joined as the **26th** member and **Bangladesh** as the **27th** (Jul 2026).
IBCA covers **7 big cats**: tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma.

89.s: Kuno was initially selected as a second home for which animal before being used for Project Cheetah?
o: Gharials from the National Chambal Sanctuary
89.x: Kuno was initially chosen as a second home for Gir's Asiatic lions. The Supreme Court ordered lion translocation in 2013, but Gujarat did not implement it.
89.tq: Use the earlier conservation purpose of the same site as the discriminator.
xs: **Kuno** was first chosen as a second home for **Gir's Asiatic lions** — option **(1)**.
The SC ordered the translocation in **2013**, but **Gujarat did not carry it out**, so **Kuno went to cheetahs**.
xa: The new proposed lion second home is **Barda WLS** (Gujarat).
⚠ **Kuno** = first chosen for lions; **Barda** = proposed lion second home.
Kuno NP lies in **Sheopur, MP**, on the Kuno river.

89.s: Project Lion, launched in 2020, primarily seeks to conserve:
o: The African lions introduced into Kuno
The mountain lions of the Himalayas
89.x: Project Lion was launched in 2020 to conserve the world's last free-ranging Asiatic lions in Gir through surveillance, research and disease management.
89.tq: Apply the project-species-location triangle.
xs: **Project Lion (2020)** conserves the world's last free-ranging **Asiatic lions of Gir** — option **(4)**.
Tools: **modern surveillance, research, disease management**.
The animals at **Kuno** are **African cheetahs**, not lions.
xa: India has **891 Asiatic lions** (Apr 2026).
The **Asiatic lion** improved from CR to **EN**.
⚠ **Project Lion** and **Project Dolphin** were both launched in **2020**.

89.s: Barda Wildlife Sanctuary has been proposed as a second home for Asiatic lions. The principal criticism of this proposal is that Barda:
o: Is too close to Gir to provide a genuine metapopulation safeguard
Has no forest cover at all
Is exclusively a marine protected area
89.x: Critics argue that Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is too close to Gir to function as an effective separate metapopulation safeguard.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Indian Bustard:

2. It is classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
3. Fewer than 150 birds are left in the wild.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: the GIB (Ardeotis nigriceps) is called Godawan and is Rajasthan's state bird. Statement 2 is wrong: it is Critically Endangered, not Endangered. Statement 3 is correct: fewer than 150 birds remain. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
89.tq: Status trap: GIB is Critically Endangered (CR), not just Endangered.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: the **GIB (Ardeotis nigriceps)** is the **Godawan**, **Rajasthan's state bird**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it is **Critically Endangered (CR)**, not Endangered.
Statement 3: **fewer than 150** birds are left.
xa: Main threat: collisions with **overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones.
Conservation breeding at **Jaisalmer, Rajasthan**.
AP site: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).

89.s: The principal natural range of the Great Indian Bustard is associated with which of the following regions?
89.x: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in the Thar region of Rajasthan, although its range also extends into parts of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
89.tq: Use the core range as the distinguishing geographical fact.
xs: The GIB lives mainly in the **Thar (Rajasthan)** — option **(3)**.
It also occurs in **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra** and **Karnataka**.
xa: In AP: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).
The GIB is **Critically Endangered**, with **fewer than 150** birds.
It is one of MoEFCC's **five new national species projects**.

89.s: The major conservation threat to the Great Indian Bustard in solar and wind-energy zones is:

xs: The GIB's main threat is **collision with overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones — option **(1)**.

xa: The SC ordered GIB-area power lines laid **underground** in **2021**.
**M.K. Ranjitsinh (March 2024)** modified the blanket order and set up an **expert committee**.

89.s: The Great Indian Bustard is included in which of the following conservation initiatives?

89.s: Which one of the following days is observed as National Dolphin Day in India?

89.s: Five slender-billed vultures bred at the BNHS Assam centre were released in an event described as

Option (4) reverses the route.
xa: It stops over in huge numbers at **Doyang reservoir**, **Nagaland**.
**Pangti** = **"Falcon Capital of the World"**.

89.tq: Amur falcon: Nagaland (Doyang, Pangti) stopover, non-stop over the Arabian Sea to southern Africa.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: huge numbers stop at **Doyang reservoir**, **Nagaland**.
Statement 2: **Pangti** is the **"Falcon Capital of the World"**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the non-stop crossing is of the **Arabian Sea**, not the Bay of Bengal.
xa: Route: **SE Russia** and **northern China** → **southern Africa**.

89.s:
Which of the following locations in India have been identified as IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots?

xs: India's **Hope Spots** are **Lakshadweep** and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** — option **(1) 1 and 2 only** (APPSC-G1 2024).
**Gulf of Mannar** is a marine NP/BR and **Palk Bay** a dugong reserve — not Hope Spots.
xa: Hope Spots are named by **IUCN** and **Mission Blue**.
**Palk Bay** = India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** (**2022**).

89.s: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in:
89.x: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu, in 2022.

xs: India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** is in **Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu** (**2022**) — option **(4)**.

Consider the following pairs:

**Coringa** and **Bhitarkanika** are major mangrove sanctuaries.

Match List-I with List-II:

 d. Bhitarkanika    iv. Corals and marine life

89.s:

89.s: The headquarters of the Wildlife Institute of India is located at:
89.x: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is headquartered at Dehradun.
89.tq: Test the location of the institution directly against nearby headquarters.
xs: The **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**, set up in **1982**, is headquartered at **Dehradun** — option **(3)**.
**Gland** is the HQ of **IUCN** and **WWF**; **Mumbai** of **BNHS**; **Noida** of **WTI**.
xa: WII runs the **All India Tiger Estimation** with the **NTCA**, every **four years**.
The **Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre** (Jan 2026) is at **WII Dehradun**, under **Namami Gange**.

89.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the International Big Cat Alliance?

Select the correct answer using the code below:

89.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. NSTR — Tigers
2. Rollapadu — Great Indian Bustard

Select the correct answer using the code below:

xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
**NSTR** = India's largest tiger reserve; **Rollapadu** = **GIB**; **Koundinya** = AP's elephants.
**Coringa WLS** (**Kakinada**) is a **mangrove** site in the **Godavari estuary**, not an Asiatic lion site; lions are in **Gir**.

Increase tiger numbers through captive breeding

Which of the following is a reported concern associated with tiger conservation in and around reserves?

89.s: Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's protected-area profile is correct?

Which of the following recent developments is correctly stated?

Select the correct answer using the code below:
