89.tq: Verify each date-event pair before selecting the combined option.
xs: All three developments are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**BNHS** released **5** captive-bred **slender-billed vultures** in **Assam** (**Aug 2026**) — the world's first.
**Botswana** cheetahs were released at **Kuno** in **May 2026**; the **Nilgiris** vulture release failed when the bird died (30 Jun 2026).
xa: Earlier cheetah batches: **8** from **Namibia** (**17 Sep 2022**); **12** from **South Africa** (**Feb 2023**).
Vultures declined from **diclofenac** (banned **2006**); safe alternative = **meloxicam**.
India's first vulture breeding centre: **Jatayu (Pinjore)**.

90.s:
Arrange the following laws and policies in chronological order of their enactment or adoption:
A. National Forest Policy, 1952
B. Indian Forest Act, 1927
C. Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
D. Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
90.x: The correct sequence is the Indian Forest Act, 1927, National Forest Policy, 1952, Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
90.tq: Use the first and last dates to eliminate sequences before checking the middle entries.
xs: The correct order is **B, A, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Indian Forest Act** came in **1927**, the first post-Independence **National Forest Policy** in **1952**.
The **Wildlife (Protection) Act** followed in **1972** and the **Forest (Conservation) Act** in **1980**.
xa: The **first Indian Forest Act** was drafted in **1865**; the **1878** Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
The **42nd Amendment (1976)** came between WPA and FCA: it inserted **Art. 48A** and **Art. 51A(g)**.
The **National Forest Policy 1988** set a **33%** forest/tree cover target.
⚠ **1865** = first Forest Act; **1878** = three forest categories; **1927** = Act still in force.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Forest Acts:
1. The first Indian Forest Act was drafted in 1865.
2. The Indian Forest Act, 1878 introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
3. The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was repealed after Independence by the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the first Forest Act was drafted in 1865. Statement 2 is correct: the 1878 Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1927 Act is a colonial consolidating law that is still in force. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: 1865 first, 1878 three categories, 1927 consolidating and still in force.
xs: Only statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **first Indian Forest Act** was drafted in **1865** (APPSC 2024 key).
Statement 2 is correct: the **1878** Act introduced **reserved, protected and village forests**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **1927** Act is a colonial consolidating law that is **still in force**.
xa: The **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** came into force on **25 October 1980**; it did not repeal the 1927 Act.
Under the **1927** Act, **Sec. 26** lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.
The **2017 amendment** removed **bamboo grown outside forest areas** from the definition of "tree" in **Sec. 2(7)**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act was enacted in 1960.
2. The Animal Welfare Board of India was set up under this Act in 1962.
3. The Act transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Transfer of forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List was associated with the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
90.tq: Find the statement that assigns a constitutional change to the wrong legislation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act** was enacted in **1960**.
Statement 2: the **Animal Welfare Board of India** was set up under it in **1962**.
Statement 3 is wrong: forests and wildlife went to the **Concurrent List** by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**.
xa: The **Animal Welfare Board** is headquartered at **Ballabhgarh, Haryana**.
Forests became **Entry 17A** and protection of wild animals and birds **Entry 17B** of the Concurrent List.
The **PCA Act 1960** prevents cruelty to animals; the **WPA 1972** protects wild animals, birds and plants.

90.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is significant for forest and wildlife governance because it
o: inserted Articles 48A and 51A(g) and placed forests and wildlife in the Concurrent List
created Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act
90.x: The 42nd Amendment inserted Article 48A, added Article 51A(g), and transferred forests and wildlife to the Concurrent List.
90.tq: Associate a constitutional amendment with its specific Articles and legislative-list change.
xs: The **42nd Amendment** inserted **Articles 48A and 51A(g)** and placed forests and wildlife in the **Concurrent List** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 48A** is a **Directive Principle**; **Art. 51A(g)** is a **Fundamental Duty**.
**Schedule I** belongs to the **WPA 1972**, and the **FCA 1980** is a separate Act of Parliament, not created by an amendment.
The **village forest** category came from the **1878** Indian Forest Act.
xa: Forests = **Entry 17A**; protection of wild animals and birds = **Entry 17B** (moved from the State List).
The amendment was made in **1976**, between the **WPA 1972** and the **FCA 1980**.
⚠ **17A** = forests; **17B** = wild animals and birds; **48A** = DPSP; **51A(g)** = Fundamental Duty.

90.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on
90.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 came into force on 25 October 1980.
90.tq: Test the exact commencement date rather than merely the enactment year.
xs: The **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** came into force on **25 October 1980** — option **(2)**.
Under its **Sec. 2**, **prior Central approval** is needed to de-reserve a forest or use forest land for a non-forest purpose.
xa: The **2023 amendment** renamed it the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980**, w.e.f. **29 Dec 2023**.
The amended Act covers land recorded as forest **on or after 25 Oct 1980**; land converted before **12 Dec 1996** is excluded.
The FCA **checks deforestation** and regulates diversion of forest land; **EPA 1986** is the umbrella pollution law.

90.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the
90.x: The 2023 amendment renamed it the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
90.tq: Distinguish the exact official title from plausible but unofficial alternatives.
xs: The 2023 amendment renamed the FCA as the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** — option **(2)**.
The Act was **renamed, not repealed**, so both names appear in questions; the renaming took effect from **29 Dec 2023**.
xa: **Exemptions** from Central approval: strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC**, eco-tourism, zoos and safaris.
**Compensatory afforestation**: **non-forest land of equal area**, else **twice the area of degraded forest land**, plus **NPV**.
Critics say it takes **"deemed forests"** out of scope, diluting the **Godavarman** ruling.
AP had diverted **27,641.252 ha** of forest under the Adhiniyam up to **31.12.2024**.

90.s:
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 transferred which of the following subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List?
1. Forests
2. Protection of wild animals and birds
3. Public health
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: The 42nd Amendment transferred forests through Entry 17A and protection of wild animals and birds through Entry 17B to the Concurrent List. Public health was not transferred by this amendment.
90.tq: Identify the two related entries and reject the unrelated subject.
xs: **Forests** and **protection of wild animals and birds** were moved — **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
Forests became **Entry 17A** and protection of wild animals and birds **Entry 17B** of the **Concurrent List**.
**Public health** was not part of this transfer.
xa: The same **42nd Amendment (1976)** inserted **Art. 48A** (DPSP) and **Art. 51A(g)** (Fundamental Duty).
The **T.N. Godavarman** case (**1995**) read "forest" as every area recorded as forest in government records.
⚠ **17A** = forests; **17B** = wild animals and birds.

90.s: Which one of the following provisions was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
90.x: Article 48A, directing the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife, was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
90.tq: Use the constitutional-part distinction to separate a DPSP from a Fundamental Duty.
xs: **Article 48A** was inserted into the **Directive Principles** by the **42nd Amendment, 1976** — option **(2)**.
**Article 51A(g)** was also inserted by the same amendment, but it is a **Fundamental Duty**, not a DPSP.
xa: The amendment moved forests (**Entry 17A**) and wild animals and birds (**Entry 17B**) to the **Concurrent List**.
⚠ **48A** = DPSP; **51A(g)** = Fundamental Duty — the classic swap trap.
The **WPA** dates from **1972** and the **FCA** from **1980**, either side of this **1976** amendment.

90.s: Article 51A(g), relating to protection of the natural environment, belongs to which part of the Constitution?
90.x: Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty requiring citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife.
90.tq: Discriminate between the similarly related Articles 48A and 51A(g).
xs: **Article 51A(g)** is a **Fundamental Duty** — option **(3)**.
It was inserted by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** alongside **Art. 48A**, which is a **Directive Principle**.
xa: ⚠ **48A** = DPSP (State's duty); **51A(g)** = Fundamental Duty (citizen's duty).
The same amendment shifted forests (**Entry 17A**) and wild animals and birds (**Entry 17B**) to the **Concurrent List**.
The **T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case (1995)** widened the meaning of "forest" to every recorded forest area.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case:
1. The expression ‘forest’ covers every area recorded as forest in government records.
2. The definition applies irrespective of ownership.
3. The interpretation is confined only to notified national parks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: The Godavarman interpretation covers every area recorded as forest in government records, regardless of ownership. It is not confined to national parks.
90.tq: Find the incorrect limiting statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: "forest" covers **every area recorded as forest in government records**.
Statement 2: it applies **whatever the ownership**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is not confined to national parks.
xa: The case is from **1995**; the **2023 amendment** to the FCA narrows this reading.
Critics say the 2023 amendment takes **"deemed forests"** out of scope and dilutes **Godavarman**.
The amended Act covers only notified forest land or land recorded as forest **on or after 25 Oct 1980**.

90.s: The Supreme Court’s restriction relating to mining provides that mining is barred within what distance of every national park and sanctuary, unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified?
90.x: Mining is barred within 1 kilometre of every national park and sanctuary boundary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
90.tq: Recall the statutory-distance figure and distinguish it from larger possible buffer zones.
xs: The SC bars mining within **1 kilometre** of every national park and sanctuary boundary — option **(2)**.
The bar applies **unless a larger eco-sensitive zone (ESZ)** is notified.
xa: Under the **WPA**, mining is **prohibited inside NPs and sanctuaries** themselves.
India has **1,000+ protected areas** covering **1,75,169.42 sq km**, i.e. **5.32%** of land area.
The **NBWL Standing Committee** clears projects in or near PAs and tiger corridors.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about forest categories under the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. Reserved forests have the strictest protection; felling, grazing and hunting are barred unless expressly permitted.
2. A village forest is a protected forest assigned to a village community.
3. In a protected forest, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: reserved forests are the most strictly protected. Statement 2 is wrong: a village forest is a reserved forest (not a protected forest) assigned to a village community. Statement 3 is correct: in protected forests everything is allowed unless specifically prohibited. Hence 1 and 3 only.
90.tq: Reserved = barred unless permitted; protected = allowed unless prohibited; village = reserved forest given to a village.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **reserved forests** are the strictest — felling, grazing and hunting barred unless expressly permitted.
Statement 2 is wrong: a **village forest** is a **reserved** forest (not a protected forest) assigned to a village community.
Statement 3: in a **protected forest**, activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
xa: Reserved forest = **Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**; village forest = **Ch. III, Sec. 28**; protected forest = **Ch. IV, Sec. 29-34**.
⚠ **Reserved** = barred unless permitted; **Protected** = allowed unless prohibited.
The three categories were first introduced by the **1878** Indian Forest Act.

90.s: Section 26 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 primarily deals with
o: regulation of forests that are not government property
assignment of reserved forests to village communities
acts prohibited in a reserved forest, including punishable trespass
removal of bamboo from non-forest land without a permit
90.x: Section 26 lists prohibited acts in a reserved forest and makes trespass punishable.
90.tq: Match the offence section with its specific prohibited conduct.
xs: **Sec. 26** lists **acts prohibited in a reserved forest** and makes **trespass** punishable — option **(3)**.
Regulating non-government forests is **Sec. 35**; village forests come under **Sec. 28**.
Bamboo removal without permit came from the **2017 amendment** to **Sec. 2(7)**.
xa: Sec. 26 was the **APPSC 2024** key.
Reserved forests (**Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**) are the most strictly protected category.
The 2017 change came as an Ordinance in **2017** and an Act in **2018**.

90.s: Section 35 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 empowers the State to regulate
o: only reserved forests owned by the Union Government
forests that are not government property
wild animals declared vermin under Section 62 of the Wildlife Act
90.x: Section 35 permits the State to regulate forests that are not government property.
90.tq: Identify the correct authority and subject of the statutory power.
xs: **Sec. 35** lets the State regulate **forests that are not government property** — option **(3)**.
**CITES** came into the **WPA** in **2022**, and **vermin** declarations are under **Sec. 62** of the WPA — neither is in the Forest Act.
xa: **Sec. 26** lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.
**Sec. 2(7)** defines "tree"; the **2017 amendment** removed **bamboo grown outside forest areas** from it.
Protected forests fall under **Ch. IV, Sec. 29-34**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927:
1. It was first issued as an Ordinance in 2017 and enacted as an Act in 2018.
2. It removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of 'tree' in Section 2(7).
3. Bamboo grown on private or non-forest land still needs a transit permit to be felled and transported.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ordinance 2017, Act 2018, removing bamboo grown outside forests from 'tree' in Section 2(7). Statement 3 is wrong: such bamboo can now be felled and transported without a permit. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: Bamboo outside forests is no longer a 'tree', so no permit is needed.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: Ordinance in **2017**, Act in **2018**.
Statement 2: **bamboo grown outside forest areas** was removed from "tree" in **Sec. 2(7)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: such bamboo can now be felled and transported **without a permit**.
xa: The 1927 Act was criticised for hurting **forest-dwellers' livelihoods**, pushing reform towards **community rights**.
**Sec. 35** lets the State regulate forests that are not government property.
The **1927** Act is a colonial consolidating law **still in force**.

90.s: Which criticism of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 encouraged later reforms towards community rights?
o: It gave unrestricted ownership of forests to forest-dwellers.
It dealt exclusively with marine biodiversity.
It was viewed as harming the livelihoods of forest-dwellers.
It abolished all State control over forest management.
90.x: The Act has been criticised for harming forest-dwellers’ livelihoods, contributing to reform efforts focused on community rights.
90.tq: Link the criticism to the reform direction without confusing it with the Act’s formal forest categories.
xs: The Act was seen as **harming the livelihoods of forest-dwellers** — option **(3)**.
This criticism pushed reform towards **community rights**.
It never gave forest-dwellers ownership or ended State control: in **reserved forests** the **State controls management**.
xa: The **2017 amendment** freed bamboo on private/non-forest land from the **permit** requirement.
The 1927 Act is a **colonial consolidating law**, still in force.
Critics of the **2023** FCA amendment note it is **silent on FRA** and mandates no **Gram Sabha** consent.

90.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1952, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the prescribed forest-cover targets?
o: Two-thirds of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
One-fourth of the land under forest, including 50% in hills and 33% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 25% in hills and 60% in plains
One-third of the land under forest, including 60% in hills and 25% in plains
90.x: The 1952 policy aimed at one-third of the total land under forest, with 60% forest cover in hills and 25% in plains.
90.tq: Split the overall target from the separate hill and plain targets.
xs: **NFP 1952**: **one-third** of land under forest, **60% in hills** and **25% in plains** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) swaps the hill and plain figures; **two-thirds** is the 1988 target for hills only.
xa: **NFP 1988**: **33%** of geographical area under forest/tree cover; **two-thirds (66%)** in hilly and mountainous regions.
⚠ **1952** hills = **60%**; **1988** hills = **two-thirds (66%)**; national target both ≈ one-third.
NFP **1952** was the first post-Independence forest policy.

90.s:
With reference to the National Forest Policy, 1988, consider the following statements:
1. It envisages forest or tree cover over 33% of the geographical area.
2. It prescribes two-thirds forest or tree cover for hilly and mountainous regions.
3. It requires at least two-thirds of the entire country's land to be under forest.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The two-thirds target applies to hilly and mountainous regions, not to the entire country; hence statement 3 is false.
90.tq: Find the scope of the two-thirds figure before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: NFP 1988 targets **33%** of geographical area under forest/tree cover.
Statement 2: **two-thirds (66%)** is prescribed for **hilly and mountainous regions**.
Statement 3 is wrong: two-thirds applies **only to the hills**, not the whole country (**APPSC 2024**).
xa: NFP **1952** prescribed **60% in hills** and **25% in plains**.
NFP 1988 objectives include checking **soil erosion and desert spread** and a **massive people's movement involving women**.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective associated with the National Forest Policy, 1988?
o: Promoting a massive people's movement involving women
Replacing all natural forests with commercial plantations
Checking soil erosion and desert spread
Meeting the fuelwood, fodder and minor forest produce needs of rural and tribal people
90.x: The policy supports ecological stability, conservation, afforestation, social forestry and local needs. It does not seek to replace all natural forests with commercial plantations.
90.tq: Identify the option that reverses the conservation-oriented objective.
xs: **Replacing all natural forests with commercial plantations** is not an NFP 1988 objective — option **(2)**.
The other three are listed objectives: a **massive people's movement involving women**, checking **soil erosion and desert spread**, and meeting **fuelwood, fodder and minor forest produce** needs.
xa: Other objectives: **ecological stability**, conserving natural heritage, **massive afforestation and social forestry**.
It also calls for **corridors between protected areas** and **fuel-efficient chulhas**.
Target: **33%** forest/tree cover; **two-thirds** in hilly and mountainous regions.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about definitions in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. 'Wildlife' is defined in Section 2(37).
2. 'Animal' is defined in Section 2(1).
3. The definition of 'animal' covers mammals, birds and reptiles but excludes amphibians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 2(37) defines wildlife and Section 2(1) defines animal. Statement 3 is wrong: 'animal' includes amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles and their young, plus eggs of birds and reptiles. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: 2(1) = animal (first word), 2(37) = wildlife; amphibians are included.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **"wildlife"** is defined in **Sec. 2(37)**.
Statement 2: **"animal"** is defined in **Sec. 2(1)**.
Statement 3 is wrong: "animal" covers **amphibians**, birds, mammals, reptiles and their young, plus eggs of birds and reptiles.
xa: The WPA has **66 sections** in **7 chapters**.
**Section 9** prohibits hunting of scheduled animals; **Section 39** makes wild animals **Government property**.
Its purpose is to protect **wild animals, birds and plants** and secure ecological security.

90.s: Under Section 39 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, wild animals, trophies and articles derived from wild animals are treated as:
o: Property of the local body where found
Property of the State Government only
90.x: Section 39 declares wild animals, trophies and articles derived from them to be Government property.
90.tq: Test ownership through the exact statutory authority rather than the place of discovery.
xs: Under **Section 39**, wild animals, trophies and articles are **Government property** — option **(3)**.
Not the property of a local body, only the State, or the landowner.
xa: **Section 9** prohibits hunting of scheduled animals; **Section 11** allows hunting where there is danger to human life or crops.
**Section 12** permits are for education, research, scientific management, incl. **translocation**.
⚠ **Sec. 9** = ban; **Sec. 11** = danger exception; **Sec. 12** = permits; **Sec. 39** = Government property.

90.s: Which of the following amendments to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is NOT included among the amendments identified in the subject matter?
90.x: The identified amendments were made in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022. A 2016 amendment is not included in this sequence.
90.tq: Find the one year outside the recognised amendment sequence.
xs: A **2016 Amendment** is not among the WPA amendments — option **(1)**.
xa: **2002**: Conservation and Community Reserves; **National Board for Wildlife** replaced the Indian Board.
**2006**: **NTCA**, **WCCB** and the **Tiger Conservation Plan** (**Sec. 38V(3)**).
**2022**: schedules cut **6 to 4**, **CITES** brought in; in force **April 2023**.
⚠ The **2017** amendment (bamboo) was to the **Indian Forest Act**, not the WPA.

90.s: Under Section 9 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, hunting of scheduled animals is generally:
o: Permitted throughout the year with a licence
90.x: Section 9 prohibits hunting of scheduled animals, subject to exceptions provided by the Act.
90.tq: Look for the general rule together with its statutory qualification.
xs: **Section 9** **prohibits** hunting of scheduled animals, **subject to specified exceptions** — option **(1)**.
Exceptions: **Section 11** (danger to human life or crops) and **Section 12** (permits for education, research, translocation).
xa: **Sec. 62**: the Centre may declare a wild animal (not in Schedule I) **vermin** for a specified area and period.
**Section 39**: wild animals, trophies and articles are **Government property**.
**Mining** is prohibited inside NPs and sanctuaries.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about exceptions to the hunting ban under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. Section 11 allows action against a wild animal that endangers human life.
2. Section 11 also covers animals causing danger to crops.
3. Permits under Section 12 can be given for education and research but not for translocation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Section 11 covers danger to human life or crops. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 12 permits cover education, research and scientific management, including translocation. Hence 1 and 2 only.
90.tq: Sec 9 bans hunting; Sec 11 = danger to life or crops; Sec 12 = education, research, translocation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2: **Section 11** allows hunting where there is **danger to human life or crops**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Section 12** permits cover education, research, scientific management, **including translocation**.
xa: Maharashtra's **WPA (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill 2026** targets **Sec. 12** to relocate leopards; it needs **President's assent**.
**Section 9** is the basic ban on hunting scheduled animals.
⚠ **Sec. 9** = ban; **Sec. 11** = danger exception; **Sec. 12** = research/translocation permits.

90.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, enacted by Parliament in 1972, is structured into
90.x: The WPA 1972 has 66 sections arranged in 7 chapters. 51/6, 26/5 and 86/9 are made-up structures; the WPA's six original schedules were cut to four in 2022, which is a different count.
90.tq: WPA 1972 = 66 sections, 7 chapters.
xs: The WPA has **66 sections in 7 chapters** — option **(1)**.
It was enacted by Parliament in **1972** to protect **wild animals, birds and plants**.
xa: Its original **6 schedules** were cut to **4** by the **2022** amendment — a different count.
**Sec. 2(37)** defines "wildlife"; **Sec. 2(1)** defines "animal".

90.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act?
o: Conservation Reserve — government-owned buffer or corridor
Community Reserve — exclusively Central Government land
Conservation Reserve — private land managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee
Community Reserve — statutory body for tiger conservation
90.x: Conservation Reserves are government-owned buffers or corridors. Community Reserves concern private or community land and are managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee.
90.tq: Separate the ownership basis of Conservation Reserves from that of Community Reserves.
xs: **Conservation Reserve** = **government-owned buffer or corridor** — option **(1)**.
**Community Reserves** are on **private or community land**, run by a **CRMC** — so options (2) and (3) are wrong.
The statutory tiger body is the **NTCA** (2006 amendment), not a Community Reserve.
xa: Examples of Conservation Reserves: **Tsarap Chu** (HP), **Hesaraghatta** (Karnataka).
The **2022** amendment let **State Governments** declare conservation reserves.
⚠ **Conservation Reserve** = Government land; **Community Reserve** = private/community land.

90.s: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
90.x: The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the National Board for Wildlife.
90.tq: Track the institutional replacement rather than confusing it with bodies created in 2006.
xs: The **2002** amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the **National Board for Wildlife** — option **(2)**.
**NTCA** and **WCCB** came with the **2006** amendment; the **Animal Welfare Board** is under the **PCA Act 1960**.
xa: **NBWL** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**; its **Standing Committee** by the **Union Environment Minister**.
The **State Board for Wildlife** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
The full NBWL met in **2025** after a **13-year** gap; the Standing Committee cleared **over 97%** of diversion proposals.

90.s: The 2022 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act is associated with
o: introduction of the Tiger Conservation Plan requirement under Section 38V(3)
replacement of the Indian Board for Wildlife by the National Board for Wildlife
creation of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
rationalisation of schedules and addition of invasive alien species
90.x: The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules and added invasive alien species. The other options relate to the 2002 or 2006 amendments.
90.tq: Use the amendment timeline to separate later schedule changes from earlier institutional reforms.
xs: The **2022** amendment **rationalised the schedules** and **added invasive alien species** — option **(4)**.
**Sec. 38V(3)** and the **WCCB** came from the **2006** amendment; NBWL replaced the Indian Board in **2002**.
xa: Schedules were cut from **6 to 4** and the separate **vermin schedule deleted**.
**CITES** provisions were brought in (**management and scientific authorities**).
General fines rose to **Rs 1 lakh** (from **Rs 25,000**); in force **April 2023**.

90.s: Section 38V(3), inserted in the Wildlife (Protection) Act by the 2006 amendment, requires
o: a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve
a Community Reserve Management Committee for every community reserve
the Centre to regulate invasive alien species
a Chief Wildlife Warden in every State
90.x: Sec. 38V(3) (2006 amendment) mandates a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve. CRMCs came with the 2002 amendment's community reserves; regulation of invasive alien species and the Chief Wildlife Warden in every State are 2022-amendment changes.
90.tq: 2006 amendment = tiger provisions (NTCA, Sec. 38V Tiger Conservation Plan).
xs: **Sec. 38V(3)** requires a **Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve** — option **(1)**.
**CRMCs** came with the **2002** amendment; invasive species and a **Chief Wildlife Warden** in every State are **2022** changes.
xa: The **2006** amendment also created the **NTCA** and the **WCCB**.
The **NTCA** is chaired by the **Union Environment Minister**.
The **WCCB** was set up on the **Tiger Task Force** recommendation; HQ **New Delhi**.

90.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in:
90.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 came into force in April 2023.
90.tq: Separate the year in the title from the year of commencement.
xs: The **Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022** came into force in **April 2023** — option **(1)**.
The amendment was passed in **2022** and enforced the next year (IYB **2026**).
xa: It cut schedules from **6 to 4** and deleted the separate **vermin schedule**.
It brought **CITES** provisions into the Act and added **invasive alien species**.
Fines: general violations up to **Rs 1 lakh**; specially protected animals minimum **Rs 25,000**.
⚠ **BD (Amendment) Act 2023** came into force on **1 April 2024** — a different date.

90.s: Which international convention’s provisions were specifically brought into the Wildlife (Protection) Act through the 2022 amendment?
90.x: The 2022 amendment incorporated CITES-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
90.tq: Distinguish the wildlife-trade convention from other environmental treaties.
xs: The 2022 amendment brought **CITES** provisions into the WPA — option **(3)**.
It provides for CITES **management and scientific authorities**.
xa: After 2022, **Schedule IV** lists specimens in the **CITES Appendices** (**APPSC-GS 2024**).
⚠ The **CBD** is implemented by the **BD Act 2002**, not the WPA.
The amendment came into force in **April 2023**.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding changes made by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022:
1. The Centre was empowered to regulate invasive alien species.
2. State Governments may declare conservation reserves.
3. Every State is required to have a Chief Wildlife Warden.
4. Captive animals may be voluntarily surrendered without compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: All four statements describe changes associated with the 2022 amendment. Examples of invasive alien species include African catfish and Lantana camara.
90.tq: Test the complete amendment package rather than a single isolated change.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the Centre regulates **invasive alien species** (e.g. **African catfish**, **Lantana camara**).
Statement 2: **State Governments** may declare **conservation reserves**.
Statements 3 and 4: a **Chief Wildlife Warden** in every State; **voluntary surrender** of captive animals without compensation.
xa: Schedules cut **6 to 4**; **CITES** provisions brought in.
Fine for general violations up to **Rs 1 lakh** (from **Rs 25,000**).
In force: **April 2023**.

90.s: Which of the following is an example of an invasive alien species specifically associated with the 2022 wildlife amendment provisions?
90.x: African catfish is an example of an invasive alien species referred to in connection with the amendment. Lantana camara is another example.
90.tq: Separate an invasive alien species from native wildlife species.
xs: **African catfish** is an invasive alien species named with the 2022 provisions — option **(4)**.
The **Asiatic lion** and **rhino** are **Schedule I** species, not invasive aliens.
xa: The other example given is **Lantana camara**.
⚠ Invasive species are regulated under a separate power of the **Centre**, not as **Schedule IV** (which is CITES).
The 2022 amendment came into force in **April 2023**.

90.s: The general penalty for violations under the amended wildlife law was raised to a fine of up to:
90.x: The general maximum fine was raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh. The specially protected animal category has a separate minimum fine provision.
90.tq: Compare the revised penalty with the earlier amount.
xs: General violations now attract a fine of up to **Rs 1 lakh** — option **(3)**.
**Rs 25,000** was the old limit for general violations.
xa: For **specially protected animals**, the minimum fine rose to **Rs 25,000** (from **Rs 10,000**).
Some notes give "up to **Rs 25 lakh** / **Rs 1 crore**".
The amendment came into force in **April 2023**.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the schedules before and after the 2022 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The number of schedules was increased from four to six.
The separate vermin schedule was retained as Schedule IV.
Protected plants were shifted from Schedule VI to Schedule I without any new schedule structure.
The number of schedules was reduced from six to four.
90.x: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four and deleted the separate vermin schedule.
90.tq: Compare the old and new frameworks by focusing first on the numerical change.
xs: The schedules were **reduced from six to four** — option **(4)**.
The separate **vermin schedule was deleted**, not retained.
Protected plants now sit in **Schedule III**, under the new four-schedule structure.
xa: After 2022: **Sch. I** highest protection; **Sch. II** lesser; **Sch. III** protected plants; **Sch. IV** CITES specimens.
Before 2022: **Sch. V** held **vermin** (common crow, fruit bats, rats, mice); **Sch. VI** specified plants.
The **Indian flying fox** moved from vermin (**Schedule V**) to **Schedule II**.

90.s: Which of the following species-category pairs is correctly matched under the post-2022 schedule framework?
o: Indian flying fox — Schedule IV as a CITES specimen
Dugong — Schedule II with lesser protection
Blackbuck — Schedule III as a protected plant
90.x: The Indian flying fox was formerly listed as vermin in Schedule V but is placed in Schedule II after the 2022 framework. Blackbuck and dugong are included in Schedule I.
90.tq: Track the change in status of a familiar species instead of applying the old vermin classification.
xs: **Indian flying fox — Schedule II** — option **(1)**.
It was vermin (**Schedule V**) before 2022; it is not a CITES (**Schedule IV**) entry.
**Dugong** and **Blackbuck** are both **Schedule I**; Schedule III holds plants.
xa: Schedule I also has the **Asiatic lion, tiger, elephant, snow leopard, rhino, Gangetic dolphin** and **GIB**.
The **mugger crocodile** and **rock eagle-owl** are Schedule I.
Maharashtra proposed moving the **leopard** from **Schedule I to II** (**2026**).

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Schedule IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment:
1. It contains specimens listed in the CITES Appendices.
2. It is the schedule for protected plants.
3. It is the schedule for invasive alien species.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
90.x: Schedule IV contains CITES-listed specimens. Protected plants are in Schedule III, while invasive alien species are regulated through a separate power of the Centre.
90.tq: Reject options that swap neighbouring schedule subjects and statutory powers.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Schedule IV** holds specimens listed in the **CITES Appendices**.
Statement 2 is wrong: protected plants are **Schedule III**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **invasive alien species** come under a separate power of the **Centre**.
xa: Schedule IV = CITES species was asked in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
**Sch. I** = highest protection; **Sch. II** = lesser protection.
Before 2022 there were **6** schedules, with **Sch. VI** for specified plants.

90.s: After deletion of the separate vermin schedule, which authority may declare a wild animal not included in Schedule I as vermin?
o: The National Board for Wildlife through a judicial order
The local authority without any restriction on area or period
The Central Government by notification under Section 62
The State Legislature by amendment of Schedule I
90.x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
90.tq: Ask who would perform the statutory power and check its area-and-period limits.
xs: The **Central Government**, by **notification under Section 62**, may declare a non-Schedule I animal **vermin** — option **(3)**.
The declaration is for a **specified area and period**, not unrestricted.
xa: Before 2022, **Sch. V** listed vermin: **common crow, fruit bats, rats, mice**.
The **2022** amendment deleted the separate vermin schedule.
The **Indian flying fox** was vermin and is now **Schedule II**.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of inclusion of an animal in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
o: The species may be hunted freely without restriction during the notified period.
Hunting and trade are generally prohibited except in special cases allowed by the Act.
The species receives the highest statutory protection.
90.x: Schedule I species receive the highest protection; hunting and trade are prohibited except in special cases permitted by the Act. Free hunting is not allowed.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the legal effect of the highest-protection category.
xs: **Free hunting** during a notified period is not a Schedule I consequence — option **(1)**.
Schedule I gives the **highest protection**: hunting and trade prohibited except special cases, with the **heaviest penalties**.
xa: Schedule I species include the **tiger, rhino, Asiatic lion, elephant, dugong, GIB** and **Blackbuck**.
Only animals **not in Schedule I** can be declared vermin under **Sec. 62**.
A **specified plant** cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission.

90.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
1. Mugger crocodile — Schedule I
2. Rock eagle-owl — Schedule I
3. Common crow — Schedule I
4. Blackbuck — Schedule I
90.x: The mugger crocodile, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I. The common crow was included in the former vermin Schedule V, not Schedule I.
90.tq: Separate high-protection species from a former vermin species.
xs: **Mugger crocodile**, **rock eagle-owl** and **blackbuck** are Schedule I — **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(3)**.
The **common crow** was in the old vermin **Schedule V**, not Schedule I.
xa: A mugger crocodile was beaten on the **Tungabhadra** near **Kurnool** (5 Sep 2026).
A Schedule-I **rock eagle-owl** was rescued near **Dharmavaram** and released in **Nelakota RF**.
Other Schedule I species: **Asiatic lion, tiger, elephant, snow leopard, rhino, Gangetic dolphin, dugong, GIB**.

90.s: A specified plant included in the protected-plant schedule cannot ordinarily be
o: cultivated in every circumstance without regulatory permission
observed or photographed in its natural habitat
picked, uprooted or traded without permission
90.x: A specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission. The law regulates these activities rather than prohibiting observation or scientific description.
90.tq: Apply the statutory restriction to the conduct described in the scenario.
xs: A specified plant cannot be **picked, uprooted or traded without permission** — option **(3)**.
The law regulates these acts; it does not bar observing, photographing or describing the plant.
xa: After 2022, protected plants are in **Schedule III**.
Before 2022, **Sch. VI** covered specified plants, with **cultivation and trade regulated**.
The WPA protects **wild animals, birds and plants**.

90.s: Under the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023, central approval is not required for certain strategic projects located within what distance of an international border?
90.x: The amendment provides an exemption from central approval for strategic projects within 100 km of international borders, among other specified exemptions.
90.tq: Use the distance figure as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC** are exempt — option **(3)**.
**50**, **75** and **150 km** are not the limit in the amendment.
xa: Other exemptions: **eco-tourism facilities**, **zoos and safaris** under WPA, minor infrastructure.
Critics fear loss of **tribal land in border States**.
The Act was renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** w.e.f. **29 Dec 2023**.

AP's forest diversion reached **27,641.252 ha** up to **Dec 2024**.

91.s: The Miyawaki method is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Dense, multi-layered mini-forests of native species in urban areas
Conversion of agricultural land into pasture
Seed storage in inaccessible forest areas
91.x: The Miyawaki method creates dense, multi-layered mini-forests using native species, particularly in urban areas.
91.tq: Identify the defining application of the method rather than its associated criticism.
xs: The **Miyawaki method** makes **dense, multi-layered mini-forests of native species in urban areas** — option **(1)**.
It is named after **Akira Miyawaki**, a **Japanese botanist** (**UPSC 2022** key).
Seed storage on inaccessible land relates to **seed balls**; single-species plantations are the monocultures social forestry is criticised for.
xa: **Seed balls**: seeds packed in clay, compost and soil, used on **degraded or inaccessible land**.
**Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam** plans **1,000 micro-forests** by **March 2026**.
⚠ **Extension forestry** = roadside, canal and rail strips; **Miyawaki** = urban mini-forests.

91.s: The term ‘social forestry’ was used by the National Commission on Agriculture in which year?
91.x: The National Commission on Agriculture used the term ‘social forestry’ in 1976.
91.tq: Distinguish the closely placed institutional and programme years.
xs: The **National Commission on Agriculture** used the term "social forestry" in **1976** — option **(2)**.
**1971** is near the **Arabari** JFM experiment (**1971-72**), **1988** is the NFP and **1990** the JFM guidelines.
xa: Components: **farm forestry**, **community forestry**, **extension forestry** and **agroforestry**.
Criticism: it drifted into **commercial monocultures**; fix is **mixed native species**.
India adopted the first **National Agroforestry Policy** in **Feb 2014**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding social forestry:
1. Farm forestry is one of its components.
2. Community forestry is one of its components.
3. Extension forestry includes roadside, canal and rail strips.
4. Agroforestry is excluded from social forestry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Farm forestry, community forestry, extension forestry and agroforestry are components of social forestry. Statement 4 is false because agroforestry is included.
91.tq: Find the excluded component and use the detailed definition of extension forestry.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statements 1 and 2: **farm forestry** and **community forestry** are components.
Statement 3: **extension forestry** covers **roadside, canal and rail strips**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **agroforestry** is also a component.
xa: The term was used by the **National Commission on Agriculture (1976)**.
**Agroforestry** = trees + crops + livestock on the same land.
Social forestry drifted into **commercial monocultures**.

91.s: A major criticism of the implementation of social forestry is that it drifted towards:
o: Mixed native forests under community control
91.x: Social forestry has been criticised for drifting into commercial monocultures. The suggested corrective approach is the use of mixed native species.
91.tq: Test the criticism and its precise policy concern rather than the proposed remedy.
xs: Social forestry drifted into **commercial monocultures** — option **(2)**.
The suggested fix is a shift to **mixed native species**.
Urban multi-layered mini-forests are the **Miyawaki method**, not a criticism.
xa: The term came from the **National Commission on Agriculture (1976)**.
CAMPA money is similarly criticised for **exotic plantations on native grasslands**.
**Extension forestry** covers roadside, canal and rail strips.

91.s: Seed balls, consisting of seeds packed in clay, compost and soil, are particularly used for:
o: Creating commercial monocultures in urban areas
91.x: Seed balls are used to facilitate regeneration on degraded or inaccessible land. They contain seeds packed in clay, compost and soil.
91.tq: Match the technique with its specific field application.
xs: Seed balls are used for **planting degraded or inaccessible land** — option **(3)**.
They are **seeds packed in clay, compost and soil**.
Green Credit exchange and forest-dwellers' consent relate to **CA rules**, not seed balls.
xa: The **Miyawaki method** creates dense **urban mini-forests** of native species.
**Agroforestry** benefits: diversifies farm income, conserves soil, improves fertility, **stores carbon**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Joint Forest Management (JFM):
1. JFM traces its origin to the Arabari experiment in West Bengal (1971-72).
2. The National Forest Policy, 1988 called for people's participation in forest management.
3. The MoEF issued the JFM guidelines on 1 June 1988.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: JFM began with the Arabari experiment in West Bengal in 1971-72. Statement 2 is correct: NFP 1988 called for people's participation. Statement 3 is wrong: the JFM guidelines were issued on 1 June 1990, two years after the policy. Hence 1 and 2 only.
91.tq: Arabari 1971-72, then NFP 1988, then JFM guidelines 1 June 1990.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: JFM traces to the **Arabari experiment in West Bengal (1971-72)**.
Statement 2: **NFP 1988** called for **people's participation**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **JFM guidelines** were issued on **1 June 1990**.
xa: The **National Afforestation Programme** runs through village-level **JFMCs**.
The **Green India Mission** also works through **JFMCs**, VFCs and SHGs under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
⚠ **Arabari** (**1971-72**) = JFM origin; **1990** = JFM guidelines; **2014** = agroforestry policy.

91.s: The National Afforestation Programme is implemented through which village-level institutions?
91.x: The National Afforestation Programme runs through village-level Joint Forest Management Committees.
91.tq: Identify the implementing institution at the correct administrative level.
xs: The **National Afforestation Programme** runs through village-level **Joint Forest Management Committees** — option **(2)**.
**VSS** are used for capacity-building camps in AP, and **FDAs** are federated by AP's State Forest Development Agency — neither is the NAP's village body.
xa: JFM began with the **Arabari experiment** (**1971-72**); guidelines on **1 June 1990**.
The **Green India Mission** is also implemented via **JFMCs**.
In AP, the State FDA federates **22 FDAs** and runs **NAP, GIM and NMPB** schemes.

91.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the State Forest Development Agency in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
It issues Forest Rights Act titles in all ITDA areas.
It federates 22 Joint Forest Management Committees and runs only the Miyawaki programme.
It administers only compensatory afforestation under the Green Credit Programme.
91.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the State Forest Development Agency federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs the NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
91.tq: Test the federation count together with the agency’s programme responsibilities.
xs: AP's State Forest Development Agency **federates 22 Forest Development Agencies** and runs **NAP, GIM and NMPB** schemes — option **(1)**.
It federates **FDAs**, not JFMCs; it does not issue **FRA titles**.
xa: Capacity-building camps are held through **Vana Samrakshana Samithis (VSS)**.
AP schemes: **Great Green Wall of AP**, **Namo Van - Nagar Van**, **School Nursery Scheme**.
**AP CAMPA** prepares an **Annual Plan of Operations** every year.

91.s: In Andhra Pradesh, capacity-building camps associated with forest programmes are held through:
91.x: The State Forest Development Agency conducts capacity-building camps through Vana Samrakshana Samithis.
91.tq: Match the capacity-building activity with the correct local institution.
xs: Capacity-building camps in AP are held through **Vana Samrakshana Samithis (VSS)** — option **(4)**.
**Central PSUs** appear in CA rules (may use **twice the area** of degraded forest land); **land banks** relate to Accredited CA.
xa: AP's State FDA federates **22 FDAs** and runs **NAP, GIM and NMPB** schemes.
AP's **Red Sanders Protection Scheme** covers **5,300.97 sq km**; allotment **₹1,729.83 lakh** (**2025-26**).

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016:
1. It set up both National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds.
2. These funds are non-lapsable public accounts.
3. These funds do not earn interest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act created National and State funds as non-lapsable public accounts. Statement 3 is wrong: the funds are interest-bearing. Hence 1 and 2 only.
91.tq: CAF funds: national + state, non-lapsable, interest-bearing.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **CAF Act 2016** set up **National and State Compensatory Afforestation Funds**.
Statement 2: they are **non-lapsable** public accounts.
Statement 3 is wrong: the funds are **interest-bearing**.
xa: Split: **90%** to State funds, **10%** to the National fund.
The fund held **over ₹66,000 crore** by **2024**, but only **30-35%** was used.
Progress is tracked on the **e-Green Watch** portal.

91.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the two-tier CAMPA arrangement?
o: National CAMPA carries out field work while State CAMPAs frame national policy.
State CAMPAs set national policy and National CAMPA implements village-level works.
National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy, while State CAMPAs carry out the work.
Both National and State CAMPAs are headed by the State Forest Minister and perform identical functions.
91.x: National CAMPA is headed by the Union Environment Minister and sets policy; State CAMPAs undertake implementation.
91.tq: Compare the policy-setting and implementation roles rather than the names alone.
xs: **National CAMPA** is headed by the **Union Environment Minister** and **sets policy**; **State CAMPAs carry out the work** — option **(3)**.
The other options reverse the roles or assign a State Forest Minister.
xa: The tiers come from the **CAF Act, 2016**.
⚠ **90 : 10** = State : National share of funds.
**National CAMPA** funds the **Nagar Van Yojana** and partly the **Green India Mission**.

91.s: The prescribed distribution of CAMPA funds between State funds and the National fund is:
91.x: Ninety per cent is allocated to State funds and ten per cent to the National fund.
91.tq: Keep the direction of the split clear: the larger share goes to the States.
xs: CAMPA funds go **90%** to State funds and **10%** to the National fund — option **(2)**.
The other splits (**75/25**, **60/40**, **50/50**) are not the CAF Act share.
xa: Both funds are **non-lapsable**, **interest-bearing** public accounts under the **CAF Act 2016**.
Only **30-35%** of the **₹66,000 crore**+ fund had been used by **2024**.
State CAMPAs carry out the work; **National CAMPA** sets policy.

91.s: Before a project involving diversion of forest land starts, the agency diverting the land is required to pay:
o: Compensatory afforestation cost and the Net Present Value of the lost forest ecosystem
A wildlife management fee without compensatory afforestation cost
Only the cost of planting new trees
Only the Net Present Value of the lost ecosystem
91.x: The agency must pay for compensatory afforestation as well as the NPV of the lost forest ecosystem before the project begins.
91.tq: Apply the rule to the project-start condition and include both required components.
xs: The agency pays **compensatory afforestation** cost plus the **Net Present Value of the lost forest ecosystem** — option **(1)**.
Both are paid **before** the project starts; neither alone suffices.
xa: CA replaces **"land by land"** and **"trees by trees"** on non-forest land.
Central PSUs or projects without non-forest land may use **twice the area** of degraded forest land.
The money goes to the **Compensatory Afforestation Funds** under the **CAF Act 2016**.

91.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated use of CAMPA funds?
o: Financing unrestricted private urban housing projects
91.x: CAMPA funds may support regeneration, wildlife management, catchment treatment, relocation from protected areas, human-wildlife conflict management and forest-fire prevention. Unrestricted private urban housing is not a stated use.
91.tq: Identify the option outside the listed public forestry and wildlife purposes.
xs: **Unrestricted private urban housing** is not a CAMPA use — option **(4)**.
Listed uses include **forest-fire prevention**, **human-wildlife conflict**, and **artificial and natural regeneration**.
xa: Other uses: **wildlife management**, **catchment treatment**, **relocating villages** out of PAs.
Tracking: **e-Green Watch** portal.
Criticism: CAMPA money funds **exotic plantations on native grasslands**.

91.s: Progress in the utilisation and implementation of CAMPA funds is tracked through the:
91.x: The e-Green Watch portal is used to track CAMPA progress.
91.tq: Distinguish the monitoring portal from similarly named forestry programmes.
xs: CAMPA progress is tracked through the **e-Green Watch portal** — option **(3)**.
**SMAF** is an agroforestry sub-mission, **GROW** a NITI Aayog report and **TOFI** a MoEFCC-USAID programme.
xa: The fund held **over ₹66,000 crore** by **2024**, with only **30-35%** used.
Split: **90%** State, **10%** National.

91.s: With reference to compensatory afforestation, which of the following correctly describes the ‘land by land’ and ‘trees by trees’ principle?
o: It requires only degraded forest land and no non-forest land
It replaces land and trees on non-forest land for compensatory afforestation
It permits only exotic plantations on grasslands
It applies exclusively to urban mini-forests
91.x: Compensatory afforestation replaces ‘land by land’ and ‘trees by trees’ on non-forest land.
91.tq: Break the phrase into its two parallel obligations and identify the correct land category.
xs: "Land by land" and "trees by trees" means CA **replaces land and trees on non-forest land** — option **(2)**.
Degraded forest land (**twice the area**) is only an exception for Central PSUs or where no non-forest land exists.
xa: The diverting agency pays CA + **NPV** **before** the project starts.
**FC Rules 2022** introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation** (land banks).
⚠ Non-forest land, else **twice the area** of degraded forest.

91.s: Under the compensatory afforestation rules, Central Public Sector Undertakings or projects for which no non-forest land is available may use:
o: The same area of non-forest land
Only urban land under the Miyawaki method
Twice the area of degraded forest land
Half the area of degraded forest land
91.x: Central PSUs, and projects where no non-forest land is available, may use twice the area of degraded forest land for compensatory afforestation.
91.tq: Focus on the quantitative exception to the normal land requirement.
xs: They may use **twice the area of degraded forest land** — option **(3)**.
The normal rule is **non-forest land** ("land by land").
xa: CA + **NPV** must be paid **before** the project starts.
**Green Credit** afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**.
⚠ **90 : 10** = State : National CAMPA funds.

91.s:
With reference to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authorities (CAMPA) exist at both the national and state levels.
2. People's participation in compensatory afforestation programmes is mandatory under the Act.
3. By 2024 the fund held over Rs 66,000 crore, but only about 30-35% had been used.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: CAMPA works at both national and state levels. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2016 Act does not make people's participation mandatory (UPSC 2019 trap). Statement 3 is correct: the fund held over Rs 66,000 crore by 2024 with only 30-35% utilised. Hence 1 and 3 only.
91.tq: CAMPA at both levels = correct; 'people's participation mandatory' = wrong (UPSC 2019).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: CAMPA exists at **both national and state levels**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **people's participation** is **not mandatory** under the 2016 Act (**UPSC 2019**).
Statement 3: the fund held **over Rs 66,000 crore** by **2024**, only **30-35%** used.
xa: The funds are **non-lapsable**, **interest-bearing** public accounts.
National CAMPA is headed by the **Union Environment Minister**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about compensatory afforestation (CA):
1. The Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 introduced Accredited Compensatory Afforestation.
2. Under Accredited Compensatory Afforestation, developers may only use plantations raised after the forest land is diverted.
3. Afforestation raised under the Green Credit Programme can be exchanged for CA, as allowed under the Van (S.E.S.) Rules, 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: the FC Rules 2022 introduced Accredited CA. Statement 2 is wrong: it lets developers use plantations raised in advance, which work as land banks. Statement 3 is correct: Green Credit afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023. Hence 1 and 3 only.
91.tq: Accredited CA = plantations raised in advance (land banks).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **FC Rules 2022** introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation**.
Statement 2 is wrong: developers use plantations **raised in advance** (land banks).
Statement 3: **Green Credit** afforestation can be swapped for CA under the **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**.
xa: Green Credit-CA guidelines were issued on **16 Sep 2025**.
FC Rules 2022 also **dropped** the forest-dwellers' **consent** clause.
⚠ **FC Rules 2022** = land banks + dropped consent; **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023** = Green Credit swap.

91.s: Which change in the Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 was disputed by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in its interaction with the MoEFCC?
o: Dropping the clause requiring forest-dwellers’ consent before diversion
91.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the clause requiring the consent of forest-dwellers before diversion, and the NCST disputed this with the MoEFCC.
91.tq: Identify the precise legal change rather than the surrounding forest programmes.
xs: The **NCST** disputed **dropping the clause requiring forest-dwellers' consent before diversion** — option **(2)**.
**JFMCs** date back to JFM (guidelines **1990**), and the **Miyawaki method** is an urban planting technique — neither is in the 2022 Rules.
xa: The same Rules introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation** (land banks).
The **Koya and Kondh** oppose **Polavaram** over land rights and rehabilitation.
Suggested fix: **FRA community titles** to pastoralists.

91.s: Accredited Compensatory Afforestation enables developers to meet their obligations by using:
o: Community titles issued under the Forest Rights Act
Plantations raised in advance, functioning effectively as land banks
Only plantations raised after diversion of forest land
Funds allocated exclusively to VSS camps
91.x: Accredited Compensatory Afforestation permits developers to use plantations raised in advance, effectively creating land banks for meeting obligations.
91.tq: Test the operational meaning of a legal term through a developer scenario.
xs: Developers use **plantations raised in advance**, working as **land banks** — option **(2)**.
It was introduced by the **Forest (Conservation) Rules 2022**.
Option (3) is the opposite: plantations raised after diversion is not the scheme.
xa: **Green Credit** afforestation can also be exchanged for CA (**Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**).
Guidelines on the Green Credit link: **16 Sep 2025**.

91.s: The guidelines for linking afforestation under the Green Credit Programme with compensatory afforestation were issued on:
91.x: The relevant guidelines were issued on 16 September 2025.
91.tq: Use the exact date to separate the guideline from earlier JFM and later rule references.
xs: The guidelines were issued on **16 September 2025** — option **(2)**.
**1 June 1990** is the date of the **JFM guidelines**.
xa: The swap is allowed under the **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**.
**FC Rules 2022** introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation**.

91.s: The Nagar Van Yojana is run by the:
91.x: The National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB) runs the Nagar Van Yojana.
91.tq: Identify the correct implementing body rather than the research institution.
xs: The **Nagar Van Yojana** is run by the **National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB)** — option **(3)**.
**CAFRI** is an agroforestry research institute at **Jhansi**; the **NBA** deals with biodiversity.
xa: Target: **600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas** (**2020-21 to 2026-27**).
Funding: **National CAMPA**.
Progress: **620 projects** in **28** States and **3** UTs, costing **₹654.30 crore**.

91.s: The Nagar Van Yojana targets, between 2020–21 and 2026–27:
91.x: The scheme targets 600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas during 2020–21 to 2026–27.
91.tq: Split the paired targets carefully; the figures are deliberately reversible.
xs: NVY targets **600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas** — option **(2)**.
Some older notes give "**200** urban forests" — not the current target.
xa: Run by **NAEB**, funded by **National CAMPA**.
**620 projects** sanctioned; first instalment **₹458.53 crore** released.
AP runs **Namo Van - Nagar Van**.

91.s: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign commenced on:
91.x: The ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign began on 5 June 2024.
91.tq: Recall the exact launch date of the named campaign.
xs: **Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam** began on **5 June 2024** — option **(2)**.
**5 June 2023** and **1 July 2024** are distractors; the start was **2024**.
xa: **259+ crore** saplings have been planted.
**1,000 micro-forests** are planned by **March 2026**.
**Vanamahotsav** is held in the **first week of July**.

91.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Pradesh — Telangana Ku Haritha Haram
Telangana — Great Green Wall of AP
Andhra Pradesh — Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana
91.x: The Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana is associated with Chhattisgarh. Great Green Wall of AP, Namo Van-Nagar Van and School Nursery Scheme are listed for Andhra Pradesh, while Telangana has Telangana Ku Haritha Haram.
91.tq: Start from the sure State–scheme pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Chhattisgarh — Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Telangana Ku Haritha Haram** is Telangana's; the **Great Green Wall of AP** is Andhra Pradesh's.
xa: The Chhattisgarh scheme dates from **2021**.
AP also runs **Namo Van - Nagar Van** and the **School Nursery Scheme**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Vanamahotsav:
1. It is observed in the first week of July.
2. It was started by K.M. Munshi in 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
91.x: Statement 1 is correct: Vanamahotsav is held in the first week of July. Statement 2 is wrong: K.M. Munshi started it in 1950, not 1960. Hence 1 only; '2 only' and 'both' include the wrong year, and 'neither' rejects the correct statement 1.
91.tq: Vanamahotsav: July, K.M. Munshi, 1950.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Vanamahotsav** is held in the **first week of July**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **K.M. Munshi** started it in **1950**, not 1960.
xa: **Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam** began on **5 June 2024**.
**Akira Miyawaki**, a Japanese botanist, gave his name to the Miyawaki method.

91.s:
The revised 2021–30 framework of the Green India Mission targets which of the following regions or ecosystems?
1. Aravallis
2. Western Ghats
3. Himalayas
4. Mangroves
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
91.x: The revised framework targets the Aravallis, Western Ghats, Himalayas and mangroves.
91.tq: Check whether the list is complete before selecting the coded option.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — option **(4)**.
The revised **2021-30** GIM framework targets **Aravallis**, **Western Ghats**, **Himalayas** and **mangroves**.
xa: GIM is one of the **NAPCC** missions.
A **CAG audit** found forest quality improved on only **0.11 million ha** vs **1.4 million ha** target.
It is funded partly from **National CAMPA**.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the Green India Mission:
1. It is one of the missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
2. It is implemented through Joint Forest Management Committees.
3. It is funded partly from National CAMPA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: The Green India Mission is one of the NAPCC missions, is implemented through JFMCs and receives partial funding from National CAMPA.
91.tq: Combine institutional status, implementation mechanism and funding source.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: GIM is one of the **NAPCC** missions.
Statement 2: it is implemented via **JFMCs**.
Statement 3: it is funded partly from **National CAMPA**.
xa: It also works through VFCs and SHGs under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
Convergence with **CAMPA and MGNREGS** (now **VB-G RAM G**) never happened, per the CAG.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about the institutional implementation of the Green India Mission:
1. It works through JFMCs.
2. It works through VFCs and SHGs.
3. It functions under Gram Sabha oversight.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: The Green India Mission works through JFMCs, VFCs and SHGs under the oversight of the Gram Sabha.
91.tq: Use the inclusive option when all three institutional relationships are correctly stated.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
GIM works through **JFMCs**, **VFCs** and **SHGs**, under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
xa: Revised **2021-30** framework: **Aravallis**, **Western Ghats**, **Himalayas**, **mangroves**.
The **CAG audit** found forest-cover expansion reached only about **4%**.
The **NAP** also runs through village-level **JFMCs**.

91.s: Agroforestry is best described as:
o: Growing trees together with crops and livestock on the same land
Growing crops only beneath naturally occurring forest canopies
Replacing agricultural land entirely with forest species
Growing only commercial tree plantations on degraded land
91.x: Agroforestry integrates trees, crops and livestock on the same land.
91.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a broad description of forestry.
xs: **Agroforestry** is **growing trees together with crops and livestock on the same land** — option **(1)**.
It does not replace farmland with forest, nor is it commercial tree-only plantation.
xa: Benefits: diversifies farm income, conserves soil, improves fertility, **stores carbon**, climate resilience.
The **GROW report** puts ~**8.65%** of India's area under agroforestry.
Funding via the **Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF)** under **PM-RKVY**.

91.s: India became the first country to adopt a National Agroforestry Policy in:
91.x: India adopted the National Agroforestry Policy in February 2014 and was the first country to do so.
91.tq: Distinguish the exact month and year from nearby policy dates.
xs: India adopted the **National Agroforestry Policy** in **February 2014**, the **first country** to do so — option **(2)**.
The policy covers **agroforestry**: trees + crops + livestock on the same land.
xa: **ICAR-CAFRI** is at **Jhansi, UP**.
Agroforestry is funded via **SMAF** under **PM-RKVY**.
⚠ **Arabari** (**1971-72**) = JFM origin; **1990** = JFM guidelines; **2014** = agroforestry policy.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the GROW report:
1. GROW stands for Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry.
2. It was associated with NITI Aayog.
3. It estimated that about 8.65% of India’s geographical area is under agroforestry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: All three statements are correct. The GROW report by NITI Aayog uses the expansion ‘Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry’ and places the agroforestry area at about 8.65% of India’s geographical area.
91.tq: Check the expansion, institution and numerical estimate separately.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**GROW** = **Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry**.
It is a **NITI Aayog** report and puts ~**8.65%** of India's geographical area under agroforestry (**APPSC 2024** key).
xa: **ICAR-CAFRI** is located at **Jhansi, UP**.
India's **National Agroforestry Policy** came in **Feb 2014**.

91.s: The Central Agroforestry Research Institute (ICAR-CAFRI) is located at:
91.x: ICAR-CAFRI is located at Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh.
91.tq: Use the institution-location association.
xs: **ICAR-CAFRI** is at **Jhansi**, Uttar Pradesh — option **(3)**.
It is the **Central Agroforestry Research Institute** of **ICAR**.
xa: The **GROW** report (NITI Aayog) puts ~**8.65%** of area under agroforestry.
Agroforestry funding: **SMAF** under **PM-RKVY**.
India was the **first country** with an agroforestry policy (**2014**).

91.s: The Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) is implemented under:
91.x: Agroforestry receives support through the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry under PM-RKVY.
91.tq: Separate the funding programme from related forestry schemes.
xs: **SMAF** is implemented under **PM-RKVY** — option **(3)**.
**Nagar Van Yojana** is run by **NAEB**, and the **GIM** is an **NAPCC** mission.
xa: The **National Agroforestry Policy** came in **Feb 2014**.
**ICAR-CAFRI** (**Jhansi**) is the agroforestry research institute.
**TOFI** is a **MoEFCC-USAID** programme.

91.s:
With reference to Trees Outside Forests in India (TOFI), consider the following statements:
1. It is a programme of MoEFCC and USAID.
2. It was launched in 2023.
3. It was launched in seven States, including Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: TOFI is an MoEFCC-USAID programme launched in 2023 in seven States, one of which is Andhra Pradesh.
91.tq: Verify the partners, launch year and geographical coverage together.
xs: All three are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**TOFI** is a **MoEFCC-USAID** programme.
It was launched in **2023** in **7** states incl. **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: **Trees Outside Forests in India** links to agroforestry, funded via **SMAF** under **PM-RKVY**.
~**8.65%** of India's area is under agroforestry (**GROW**).

91.s: The Koya and Kondh communities have opposed the Polavaram project primarily over:
o: The location of the Arabari experiment
91.x: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose the Polavaram project over land rights and rehabilitation concerns.
91.tq: Connect the affected communities with the specific tribal-conflict issue.
xs: The **Koya and Kondh** oppose **Polavaram** over **land rights and rehabilitation** — option **(1)**.
It is a **tribal conflict** in the **AP** angle of forest rights.
xa: **FC Rules 2022** dropped the forest-dwellers' **consent** clause, disputed by the **NCST**.
Suggested fix: give **FRA community titles** to pastoralists.
AP's **Red Sanders Protection Scheme** spans **Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona**.

91.s: A CAG audit of the Green India Mission found that forest quality improved on only 0.11 million hectares against a target of:
91.x: The audit found improvement on only 0.11 million hectares against the target of 1.4 million hectares.
91.tq: Compare the achieved area with the target rather than selecting the repeated figure.
xs: The target was **1.4 million hectares**; only **0.11 million ha** improved — option **(1)**.
**0.11 million ha** is what was achieved, not the target.
xa: Forest-cover expansion reached about **4%**.
Convergence with **CAMPA and MGNREGS** (now **VB-G RAM G**) never happened.
GIM is one of the **NAPCC** missions.

91.s: Which of the following convergence arrangements was reported as not having materialised in the implementation of the Green India Mission?
o: Convergence with JFMCs and VFCs under Gram Sabha oversight
Convergence between NAP and GIM from 2021–22
Convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G
Convergence between social forestry and agroforestry
91.x: The audit-related assessment stated that convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G, never happened.
91.tq: Identify the missing convergence arrangement by distinguishing it from institutional linkages that do exist.
xs: Convergence with **CAMPA and MGNREGS, now VB-G RAM G**, never happened — option **(3)**.
GIM does work through **JFMCs**, VFCs and SHGs under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
xa: CAG: forest quality improved on only **0.11 million ha** vs **1.4 million ha** target.
GIM's revised **2021-30** framework targets **Aravallis**, **Western Ghats**, **Himalayas**, **mangroves**.

91.s: Which of the following has been criticised in relation to the use of CAMPA funds?
o: Funding exotic plantations on native grasslands
Funding mixed native species in all historical forest zones
91.x: CAMPA money has been criticised for funding exotic plantations on native grasslands.
91.tq: Find the practice that represents the criticism, not the proposed corrective measures.
xs: CAMPA money has been criticised for **funding exotic plantations on native grasslands** — option **(1)**.
Mixed native species and **FRA community titles** to pastoralists are the suggested **fixes**, not criticisms.
xa: Another fix: limit CAMPA to **historical forest zones**.
Only **30-35%** of the **₹66,000 crore**+ fund was used by **2024**.

91.s: Which document is prepared every year by the Andhra Pradesh CAMPA?
91.x: The Andhra Pradesh CAMPA prepares an Annual Plan of Operations every year.
91.tq: Identify the recurring administrative document associated with the agency.
xs: **AP CAMPA** prepares an **Annual Plan of Operations** every year — option **(4)**.
**State CAMPAs** carry out the work under the **CAF Act 2016**.
xa: CAMPA funds split **90%** to States and **10%** to the National fund.
State CAMPAs **carry out the work**; National CAMPA sets policy.
AP's Red Sanders scheme allotment (**2025-26**): **₹1,729.83 lakh**.

92.s: The atmosphere’s selective behaviour towards radiation is best described as follows:
o: It absorbs all incoming short-wave solar radiation and transmits all outgoing long-wave radiation
It is opaque to both incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation
It permits much of the incoming short-wave solar radiation but is relatively opaque to outgoing terrestrial long-wave infrared radiation
It reflects all solar radiation and absorbs only ultraviolet radiation
92.x: The atmosphere allows much incoming short-wave solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface but absorbs outgoing long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation through greenhouse gases.
92.tq: Apply the short-wave incoming and long-wave outgoing distinction to the atmospheric mechanism.
xs: The atmosphere **permits incoming short-wave solar radiation** but is **opaque to outgoing terrestrial long-wave infrared radiation** — option **(3)**.
It is not opaque to both, nor does it transmit all outgoing radiation — that selectivity is the greenhouse effect.
xa: The surface re-emits **infrared at 8,000-25,000 nm**; CO2 and water vapour absorb strongly at **14,000-25,000 nm**.
GHGs re-radiate **in all directions**, partly back to the surface.
⚠ Transparent to **short-wave** in; opaque to **long-wave infrared** out.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the role of carbon dioxide and water vapour in the greenhouse effect?
o: They absorb incoming visible light and convert it directly into ultraviolet radiation
