The **GCF** was set up in **2010** with HQ at **Songdo**.
The **Adaptation Fund** was set up under the **Kyoto Protocol (2001)**, not the Montreal Protocol.
The **Loss and Damage Fund** was created at **COP27 (2022)**.
xa: The GEF houses the **GBF Fund** (Global Biodiversity Framework Fund).
It finances the **UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm** and **Minamata** conventions.

95.s: The Global Environment Facility finances which of the following groups of conventions and frameworks?
o: Only the CBD and Ramsar Convention
Only the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement
UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention
Kyoto Protocol, CITES and Montreal Protocol exclusively
95.x: The GEF finances the UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention, among others. It also houses the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund.
95.tq: Use the complete institutional portfolio against options that incorrectly restrict the body to one treaty.
xs: The GEF finances the **UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention**, among others — option **(3)**.
It is not limited to one or two conventions.
xa: GEF: founded **1991**; HQ **Washington DC**.
It houses the **GBF Fund** (Global Biodiversity Framework Fund).
**Minamata Convention (2013)** deals with **mercury**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol.
2. It is financed by a share of proceeds from the Clean Development Mechanism.
3. The share of CDM Certified Emission Reductions associated with it is 2 percent.
4. NABARD is India’s National Implementing Entity for the Adaptation Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The Adaptation Fund was established under the Kyoto Protocol, is financed by a 2% share of CDM CER proceeds, and NABARD is India’s National Implementing Entity.
95.tq: Combine origin, financing percentage and national implementation facts in one coded question.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(3)**.
The **Adaptation Fund** was set up under the **Kyoto Protocol**.
It is financed by a **2% share of CDM proceeds (CERs)**.
**NABARD** is India's **National Implementing Entity** for the Adaptation Fund.
xa: The Adaptation Fund was set up in **2001** and has run from **2007**.
NABARD is also a **Direct Access Entity of GCF**.
CDM projects in developing countries earned **Certified Emission Reductions (CERs)**.

95.s: Which of the following correctly describes the chronology of the Adaptation Fund?
o: Set up under Kyoto Protocol in 2001 and running from 2007
Set up at COP27 in 2022 and running from COP28
Set up in 1991 and running from 1992
Set up under the Paris Agreement in 2015 and running from 2016
95.x: The Adaptation Fund was set up under the Kyoto Protocol in 2001 and has been running from 2007.
95.tq: Use the first and last dates to distinguish the Kyoto-era fund from later climate-finance institutions.
xs: The Adaptation Fund was **set up under the Kyoto Protocol in 2001** and has been **running from 2007** — option **(1)**.
**1991** is the founding year of the **GEF**; **COP27 (2022)** created the **Loss and Damage Fund**.
xa: It is financed by a **2%** share of CDM proceeds (CERs).
**NABARD** is India's National Implementing Entity for it.
The Kyoto Protocol entered into force on **16 Feb 2005**.

95.s: The Green Climate Fund, the largest dedicated climate fund, was set up in:
o: 2010, with headquarters at Songdo, Incheon (South Korea)
95.x: The GCF was set up in 2010 by UNFCCC parties and is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon, South Korea. 1991/Washington is the GEF; 2001 is the Adaptation Fund under Kyoto; Bonn hosts the UNFCCC secretariat and Geneva the IPCC secretariat.
95.tq: GCF = 2010, Songdo; GEF = 1991, Washington.
xs: The **GCF** was set up in **2010**, with HQ at **Songdo, Incheon (South Korea)** — option **(1)**.
**1991 / Washington** is the **GEF**; **2001** is the **Adaptation Fund** under Kyoto.
**Bonn** hosts the **UNFCCC** secretariat and **Geneva** the **IPCC** secretariat.
xa: The GCF has a **24-member Board**.
It is the operating entity of the **UNFCCC financial mechanism**.
It was criticised for a **7-year delay** on Nepal's **$49.9 million** GLOF-risk proposal.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was:
o: created at COP27 and made operational at COP28
created at COP21 and made operational at COP22
created in 1991 and made operational in 2001
created under the Montreal Protocol and made operational at COP29
95.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at COP27 and became operational at COP28.
95.tq: Arrange the creation and operationalisation conferences rather than confusing them with the Paris Agreement timeline.
xs: The Loss and Damage Fund was **created at COP27** and **made operational at COP28** — option **(1)**.
**COP21** adopted the Paris Agreement; **1991** is the GEF's founding year.
xa: **COP30 opened the fund to applications**, but capitalisation remains small.
**World Bank** = interim host and trustee until **COP33 (2028)**.
Climate justice: the fund is seen as an **ethical win**.

95.s:
With reference to the Loss and Damage Fund, arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Operationalisation of the Fund
B. Agreement to establish the Fund
C. Opening of the Fund to applications
D. End of the World Bank’s interim-host period
95.x: The Fund was agreed at COP27 in 2022, operationalised at COP28 in 2023, opened to applications at COP30, and the World Bank’s interim role extends until COP33 in 2028.
95.tq: Start with the agreement and then place operationalisation, applications and the terminal year.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Agreed at COP27 (2022)** → **operationalised at COP28 (2023)** → **opened to applications at COP30** → World Bank interim role ends at **COP33 (2028)**.
xa: The **World Bank** is interim host and trustee for **four years**.
The start-up phase runs under the **Barbados Implementation Modalities**.
Board: **26 members** — **14** developing + **12** developed.

95.s: Which institution serves as the interim host and trustee of the Loss and Damage Fund?
95.x: The World Bank is the interim host and trustee of the Fund for four years, until COP33 in 2028.
95.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ institutional trap.
xs: The **World Bank** is the **interim host and trustee** of the Loss and Damage Fund — option **(1)**.
It holds the role for **four years** until **COP33 (2028)**.
xa: The fund's **26-member Board** decides by **consensus**.
Nepal sought aid from the fund after an **Aug 2026** glacial-collapse flood.
The **GCF** is a separate fund with HQ at **Songdo**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the Board of the Loss and Damage Fund:
1. It has 26 members.
2. It consists of 14 members from developing countries and 12 from developed countries.
3. It takes decisions by majority vote only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The Board has 26 members, including 14 from developing countries and 12 from developed countries. It decides by consensus, so statement 3 is incorrect.
95.tq: Locate the wrong decision-making method after verifying the composition.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
The Board has **26 members**: **14 developing + 12 developed**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the Board **decides by consensus**, not majority vote.
xa: ⚠ GCF board **24**; FRLD board **26**.
Interim host and trustee: **World Bank**, until **COP33 (2028)**.
It covers **economic and non-economic** losses.

95.s: The Loss and Damage Fund covers losses arising from:
o: Both economic and non-economic losses from sudden- and slow-onset events
95.x: The Fund covers economic and non-economic losses resulting from both sudden-onset and slow-onset events.
95.tq: Check both dimensions of the coverage instead of accepting an ‘only’ statement.
xs: The fund covers **economic and non-economic losses** from both **sudden- and slow-onset events** — option **(4)**.
It is not limited to one type of event or to insured losses.
xa: Created at **COP27 (2022)**, operationalised at **COP28 (2023)**.
Start-up phase: **Barbados Implementation Modalities**.
**World Bank** is interim host and trustee.

95.s: Which statement correctly describes the start-up phase of the Loss and Damage Fund?
o: It is financed exclusively by the World Bank.
It operates under the Barbados Implementation Modalities, and capitalisation remains small.
It has no application process until COP33.
It operates under the Kyoto Implementation Modalities and is fully capitalised.
95.x: The start-up phase is under the Barbados Implementation Modalities. The Fund was opened to applications at COP30, but its capitalisation remains small.
95.tq: Match the fund with its stated implementation framework and current limitation.
xs: The start-up phase runs under the **Barbados Implementation Modalities**, and **capitalisation remains small** — option **(2)**.
The World Bank is **host and trustee**, not sole financer; and **COP30 already opened the fund to applications**.
xa: The fund was created at **COP27** and operationalised at **COP28**.
The World Bank hosts it until **COP33 (2028)**.
Board: **26 members**, deciding by **consensus**.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the European Green Deal?
o: A voluntary forest declaration adopted at the 2014 UN Climate Summit
A UNFCCC mechanism for financing adaptation in least developed countries
A plan of the European Union to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with Farm to Fork as a component
A scientific assessment programme jointly run by WMO and UNEP
95.x: The European Green Deal is an EU plan for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Farm to Fork strategy is one of its components.
95.tq: Use the exact objective and institutional identity to distinguish the initiative from nearby climate mechanisms.
xs: The **European Green Deal** is the EU plan for **net-zero GHG by 2050**, with **Farm to Fork** as a component — option **(3)**.
The **2014** voluntary forest declaration is the **New York Declaration on Forests**.
The WMO-UNEP body is the **IPCC**, an assessment body.
xa: APPSC **2024** key: statements **1, 2 and 4** correct on the Green Deal.
The EU also runs **CBAM**, a carbon levy on imports.
India's own net-zero target is **2070**.

95.s: Climate Action Tracker is best described as an initiative involving which of the following?
o: The IPCC and the World Meteorological Organization
Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute
95.x: Climate Action Tracker is an independent scientific analysis initiative of Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute.
95.tq: Apply the founder-versus-function distinction to avoid confusing it with intergovernmental bodies.
xs: **Climate Action Tracker** is independent scientific analysis by **Climate Analytics** and the **NewClimate Institute** — option **(3)**.
**UNEP and six countries** launched the **CCAC**; **Spain and Senegal** launched the **International Drought Resilience Alliance**.
xa: **The Climate Group** is a London non-profit (**2003**) that runs **RE100** and **EV100**.
**Climate Neutral Now** is a voluntary UNFCCC secretariat initiative (**2015**).
The **IPCC** was set up by **WMO** and **UNEP** in **1988**.

95.s: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at which event and by which countries?
o: The Rio Earth Summit; India and Brazil
95.x: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at COP27 by Spain and Senegal.
95.tq: Match the initiative with its launch forum and founding countries.
xs: The **International Drought Resilience Alliance** was launched at **COP27** by **Spain and Senegal** — option **(1)**.
COP26 launches include the **Global Methane Pledge** (USA and EU) and **Glasgow Breakthroughs** (UK-led).
xa: The **Global Shield against Climate Risks** was also launched at COP27, by **G7 and V20**.
COP27 also created **loss and damage funding arrangements**.
**AWARe** was COP27's water initiative.

95.s: The principal aim of the Early Warnings for All initiative, commonly abbreviated as EW4All, is to provide universal early-warning coverage by:
95.x: EW4All aims to achieve universal early-warning coverage by 2027.
95.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern and compare the closely spaced distractor years.
xs: **EW4All (Early Warnings for All)** aims at **universal early-warning coverage by 2027** — option **(2)**.
**2030** and **2035** are dates of other goals (e.g. the Methane Pledge, NCQG).
xa: **CCAC** (launched **2012** by **UNEP** and six countries) targets short-lived climate pollutants.
**MARS** is UNEP's methane satellite alert system.
India launched **CDRI** in **2019**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC):
1. It was launched in 2012.
2. UNEP and six countries were involved in its launch.
3. It targets short-lived climate pollutants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The CCAC was launched in 2012 by UNEP and six countries, and it targets short-lived climate pollutants.
95.tq: Verify the date, founding participants and target area as three independent statement components.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **CCAC** was launched in **2012** by **UNEP and six countries** and targets **short-lived climate pollutants**.
xa: The **Global Methane Pledge** (COP26) aims at a **30%** methane cut by **2030** from **2020** levels.
**MARS** = UNEP's methane satellite alert system (COP27).
**Climate Neutral Now** is a voluntary UNFCCC secretariat initiative (**2015**).

95.s: The New York Declaration on Forests is associated with which of the following pairs?
o: 2007 Bali Conference and phase-out of ozone-depleting substances
1992 Rio Summit and compulsory finance by OECD countries
2014 UN Climate Summit and voluntary, non-binding action to halt deforestation
95.x: The New York Declaration on Forests was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit and is voluntary and non-binding, with the objective of halting deforestation. It also formed the basis of the Bonn Challenge target of 350 Mha.
95.tq: Discriminate the declaration by its year, voluntary character and forest objective.
xs: The **New York Declaration on Forests** came from the **2014 UN Climate Summit** and is **voluntary, non-binding** action to **halt deforestation** — option **(4)**.
It is not legally binding and is unrelated to ozone or OECD finance.
xa: It is the basis of the **Bonn Challenge** **350 Mha** target.
India did not sign the **Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use** (COP26).
The **TFFF (US$125 bn)** was launched at **COP30**.

95.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Global Methane Pledge is correct?
o: It was launched at COP28 by India and Japan and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2015 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2020 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP27 by G7 and V20 and targets methane neutrality by 2040.
It was launched at COP26 by Spain and Senegal and addresses drought resilience.
95.x: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and aims to cut methane emissions by 30 per cent from 2020 levels by 2030. India is not a member.
95.tq: Check the launch COP, founders, baseline year and target together; one swapped detail makes an option wrong.
xs: The **Global Methane Pledge** was launched at **COP26** by the **USA and EU** and seeks a **30% cut from 2020 levels by 2030** — option **(2)**.
**G7 and V20** founded the **Global Shield** (COP27); **Spain and Senegal** the **Drought Resilience Alliance** (COP27).
xa: **India is not a member** of the Methane Pledge.
Methane is one of Kyoto's six gases (**CH4**).
UNEP's **MARS** is a methane satellite alert system.

95.s: The sector goals of the Glasgow Breakthroughs include all of the following EXCEPT:
95.x: The Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture. Mercury management is associated with the Minamata Convention, not the Glasgow Breakthroughs.
95.tq: Find the item that belongs to a different environmental treaty or subject.
xs: **Mercury management** is not a Glasgow Breakthrough goal — option **(3)**.
The **Glasgow Breakthroughs** set goals for **power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture**.
Mercury is the subject of the **Minamata Convention (2013)**.
xa: The Glasgow Breakthroughs were launched at **COP26**, led by the **UK** with world leaders.
COP26 also produced the **Glasgow Climate Pact** with coal "**phase-down**" language.
India announced **Panchamrit** at COP26.

95.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Initiative — Founders or leadership
1. International Drought Resilience Alliance — Spain and Senegal
2. Global Methane Pledge — United States and European Union
3. Glasgow Breakthroughs — United Kingdom-led with world leaders
4. Global Shield against Climate Risks — G7 and V20

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
95.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Drought Resilience Alliance and the Global Shield were launched at COP27, and the Global Methane Pledge and the Glasgow Breakthroughs at COP26, with the Glasgow Breakthroughs led by the United Kingdom with world leaders.
95.tq: Match each initiative with its founders before considering the COP at which it was launched.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Drought Resilience Alliance** → **Spain and Senegal** (COP27); **Global Methane Pledge** → **USA and EU** (COP26).
**Glasgow Breakthroughs** → **UK-led** with world leaders (COP26); **Global Shield** → **G7 and V20** (COP27).
xa: ⚠ In **APPSC 2024** both Global Shield statements were keyed **wrong** ("None of the above") — check who founded it and where.
**India is not a member** of the Global Methane Pledge.

95.s: Which one of the following treaties is NOT primarily concerned with reducing greenhouse-gas emissions?
95.x: The Basel Convention concerns the transboundary movement of hazardous waste, not greenhouse-gas reduction. The UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement address greenhouse-gas emissions and climate change.
95.tq: Find the treaty whose environmental objective belongs to hazardous-waste management rather than climate mitigation.
xs: The **Basel Convention** deals with transboundary movement of **hazardous waste**, **not GHGs** — option **(4)**.
The **UNFCCC**, **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and **Paris Agreement (2015)** all aim to **reduce GHG emissions**.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2025** key.
⚠ **Rotterdam** = prior informed consent; **Minamata** = mercury.
The **Montreal Protocol** addresses GHGs only indirectly: CFCs are GHGs and **Kigali** targets HFCs.

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Treaty)
a. Montreal Protocol
b. Basel Convention
c. CBD
 d. Ramsar Convention

List-II (Environmental goal)
i. Wetlands
ii. Biodiversity
iii. Ozone-depleting substances
iv. Transboundary movement of hazardous waste
95.x: The Montreal Protocol addresses ozone-depleting substances, Basel concerns hazardous-waste movement, CBD concerns biodiversity and Ramsar concerns wetlands.
95.tq: Start with the distinctive ozone and wetlands pairs, then complete the remaining matches.
xs: The correct match is **a–iii, b–iv, c–ii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Montreal Protocol (1987)** → ozone-depleting substances; **Basel** → hazardous waste movement.
**CBD (1992, Rio)** → biodiversity; **Ramsar (1971, Iran)** → wetlands.
xa: Montreal's **Kigali Amendment (2016)** phases down **HFCs**.
CBD adopted the **Kunming-Montreal GBF** in **Dec 2022**.
**CITES** (Washington) regulates trade in endangered species; signed **1973**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about CITES:
1. It concerns international trade in endangered species.
2. It is associated with Washington.
3. It was signed in 1973.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three are correct. CITES regulates international trade in endangered species, is known as the Washington Convention and was signed in 1973 (one source's 1963 is wrong).
95.tq: Check all three identifying details before selecting the complete coded option.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**CITES** regulates **trade in endangered species** and is associated with **Washington**.
It was signed in **1973**.
xa: ⚠ One source (APP) says **1963** — the correct year is **1973**.
**Ramsar (1971, Iran)** = wetlands; **CBD (1992, Rio)** = biodiversity.
**Basel** = hazardous waste; **Rotterdam** = prior informed consent; **Minamata** = mercury.

95.s: The Rotterdam Convention is associated with the principle of:
o: Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals
95.x: The Rotterdam Convention establishes the Prior Informed Consent procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides in international trade.
95.tq: Recognise the operational principle attached to the convention rather than its general environmental character.
xs: The **Rotterdam Convention (1998)** sets up **Prior Informed Consent** for **hazardous chemicals/pesticides** — option **(3)**.
Ozone-depleting substances fall under the **Montreal Protocol**.
xa: Rotterdam does **not** address GHGs.
⚠ **Basel** = hazardous waste; **Rotterdam** = prior informed consent; **Minamata** = mercury.
**Minamata Convention** dates from **2013**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Montreal Protocol primarily addresses ozone-depleting substances, although some such substances are also greenhouse gases.
2. The Paris Agreement addresses global warming through nationally determined contributions.
3. The Minamata Convention addresses mercury.
4. The Stockholm Convention addresses persistent organic pollutants.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements are correct. The Montreal Protocol has an indirect greenhouse-gas relevance because CFCs are greenhouse gases, while the other statements correctly identify the subjects of the Paris, Minamata and Stockholm instruments.
95.tq: Separate the principal subject of each treaty from its indirect environmental relevance.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Montreal Protocol (1987)** targets **ozone-depleting substances**; it addresses GHGs **indirectly** as **CFCs are GHGs**.
The **Paris Agreement** limits warming **via NDCs**; the **Minamata Convention** covers **mercury**.
The **Stockholm Convention** (persistent organic pollutants) is among the conventions financed by the **GEF**.
xa: Montreal's **Kigali Amendment (2016)** phases down **HFCs**.
**Basel Convention** = hazardous waste, **not** GHGs (APPSC 2025 key).
The GEF also finances the **UNFCCC, CBD** and **UNCCD**.

95.s: The Kigali Amendment (2016) is an amendment to which treaty, and what does it target?
o: Minamata Convention; mercury in dental amalgam
95.x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs, which is why Montreal indirectly addresses GHGs. Kyoto has no Kigali amendment (CFCs are Montreal's), Basel deals with hazardous waste and Minamata with mercury.
95.tq: Kigali → Montreal → HFC phase-down.
xs: The **Kigali Amendment (2016)** to the **Montreal Protocol** targets the **phase-down of HFCs** — option **(1)**.
Kyoto has no Kigali amendment; **Basel** deals with **hazardous waste** and **Minamata** with **mercury**.
xa: This is why Montreal **indirectly** addresses GHGs: CFCs are GHGs, and Kigali targets HFCs.
**HFCs** are also among the **six Kyoto gases**.
The Montreal Protocol dates from **1987**.

95.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by:
o: UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
UNDP and the International Energy Agency
UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
95.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
95.tq: Apply the institution-founder trap by distinguishing the IPCC’s founding bodies from other environmental organisations.
xs: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **UNEP** and the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)** — option **(4)**.
It is not a UNFCCC or World Bank body; its secretariat is in **Geneva**.
xa: It has **195** member countries.
It won the **2007 Nobel Peace Prize**, shared with **Al Gore**.
The **CCAC** was launched in **2012** by **UNEP** and six countries.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC:
1. It has 195 member countries.
2. It conducts original research independently of published literature.
3. Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
4. It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The IPCC has 195 member countries, its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive, and it shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore. It does not conduct its own original research; it assesses published literature.
95.tq: Find the single false statement among institutional role and recognition facts.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
The IPCC has **195** member countries; its reports are **policy-relevant, not policy-prescriptive**.
It shared the **2007 Nobel Peace Prize** with **Al Gore**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it **conducts no original research** — it **assesses published literature**.
xa: Each report carries a **Summary for Policymakers (SPM)**.
Set up **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**; secretariat **Geneva**.
Besides three WGs it has a **Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories**.

95.s: The secretariat of the IPCC is located in:
95.x: The IPCC secretariat is located in Geneva.
95.tq: Use location discrimination to distinguish the IPCC secretariat from the UNFCCC secretariat in Bonn.
xs: The IPCC secretariat is in **Geneva** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Bonn** hosts the **UNFCCC** secretariat, not the IPCC.
xa: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**.
It has **195** member countries.
The **GEF** HQ is **Washington DC**; the **GCF** HQ is **Songdo**.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an IPCC Working Group with its subject?
o: WG III — impacts, adaptation and vulnerability
95.x: WG I covers the physical science basis, WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and WG III covers mitigation.
95.tq: Use the standard three-way subject mapping and reject the reversed working-group labels.
xs: **WG III** deals with **Mitigation** — option **(3)**.
**WG I** = **physical science basis**; **WG II** = **impacts, adaptation and vulnerability**.
xa: AR6 WG III report: "Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change", released **4 Apr 2022**.
The IPCC also has a **Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories**.

95.s:
Arrange the following IPCC Assessment Reports in chronological order:
A. AR4
B. AR1
C. AR5
D. AR2
95.x: AR1 was published in 1990, AR2 in 1995, AR4 in 2007 and AR5 in 2014. Therefore, the order is B, D, A, C.
95.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest assessment years, then place the middle reports.
xs: The order is **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
xa: **AR3** came in **2001**; the **AR6 Synthesis Report** on **20 Mar 2023**.
AR1 fed into the **UNFCCC**.
**AR7 began in July 2023**.

95.s: The first IPCC Assessment Report, published in 1990, contributed to the development of the:
95.x: AR1 (1990) fed into the UNFCCC of 1992. The Convention was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992. Kyoto (1997), Paris (2015) and Montreal (1987) came later or deal with other issues.
95.tq: Connect the report to its immediate institutional outcome rather than to later climate agreements.
xs: **AR1 (1990)** fed into the **UNFCCC**, adopted in **1992** — option **(3)**.
The UNFCCC was adopted on **9 May 1992** (New York) and opened at the **1992 Rio Earth Summit**.
**Kyoto (1997)** and **Paris (2015)** came later; **Montreal (1987)** deals with ozone.
xa: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**.
UNFCCC entered into force on **21 March 1994**.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the release date of an AR6 Working Group report?
95.x: The AR6 WG I report was released on 9 August 2021. WG II was released on 28 February 2022, WG III on 4 April 2022, and the Synthesis Report on 20 March 2023.
95.tq: Discriminate closely spaced dates by matching each date to the correct report component.
xs: The AR6 **WG I** report was released on **9 August 2021** — option **(1)**.
**WG II** came on **28 Feb 2022**, **WG III** on **4 Apr 2022**, and the **Synthesis Report** on **20 Mar 2023**.
xa: WG I title: "Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis".
The Synthesis Report **closed the AR6 cycle**.
AR6 WG I put the carbon budget at ~**500 GtCO2** from **2020** for a **50%** chance of **1.5°C**.

95.s: Which one of the following best describes the role of an IPCC Summary for Policymakers (SPM)?
o: It is the annual negotiating text adopted by the UNFCCC COP.
It is a legally binding emission-reduction schedule for Annex I Parties.
It accompanies each assessment report and summarises its findings for policymakers.
It presents the IPCC’s independent original laboratory research only.
95.x: Each IPCC assessment report carries a Summary for Policymakers, which presents the assessment findings in a form relevant to policymakers. It is not a legally binding negotiating instrument.
95.tq: Distinguish an assessment communication product from a treaty, negotiating text or original research report.
xs: Each IPCC report **carries a Summary for Policymakers (SPM)** that **summarises its findings** for policymakers — option **(3)**.

xa: The IPCC **assesses** published literature.

SR1.5 and AR6 are the **agreed scientific baseline** for UNFCCC/COP negotiations.

95.s:

95.tq: SR1.5 formula: 45% below 2010 by 2030, net zero ~2050.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **SR1.5** was released in **October 2018**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **45%** cut by **2030** is measured from **2010** levels, not 2005.
Statement 3 is correct: 1.5°C pathways reach **net zero around 2050**.
xa: SR1.5: human activity has already caused ~**1.0°C** warming.
Cuts must be **deep, rapid and sustained**.
Exam angle: fill-in-the-blanks on "**2030-2052**", "**45% by 2030 from 2010**" and "**net zero by 2050**".

95.s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?

xs: **Gradual or limited emission cuts** are not enough for 1.5°C — option **(4)**.

95.s:

GHG emissions are at their **highest in human history**.

**1.5°C** is likely to be crossed in the **early 2030s** without deep cuts.

xs: Without immediate, deep cuts the **1.5°C** threshold is likely crossed in the **early 2030s** — option **(2)**.
This is an **AR6 Synthesis Report** finding.

Surface temperature is already **1.1°C** above pre-industrial.
There is **no plausible path below 1.5°C without overshoot**.

95.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the mitigation pathway described in the AR6 assessment?

SR1.5: CO2 to fall ~**45%** from **2010** levels by **2030**.

The figure comes from **AR6 WG I**.

Emissions must **peak before 2025**.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024** (WMO State of the Global Climate 2025).

95.s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) are best described as

o: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity
only crude oil and natural gas
95.x: CBAM covers imports of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.
95.tq: Recall the complete sector list rather than selecting a partial or unrelated list.
xs: CBAM covers **iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity** — option **(2)**.
It is an **EU carbon levy on imports** in these carbon-intensive sectors.
xa: Transitional phase from **2023**; **definitive phase from 1 January 2026**.
India says it **raises export costs for steel and aluminium**.
CBAM aims to prevent **carbon leakage**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the European Union's CBAM:
1. Its transitional phase began in 2023.
2. Its definitive phase began on 1 January 2026.
3. Its stated aim is to prevent carbon leakage.
4. Firms facing an equivalent domestic carbon price are exempt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements are correct. CBAM entered its transitional phase in 2023, its definitive phase on 1 January 2026, aims to prevent carbon leakage, and exempts firms subject to an equivalent domestic carbon price.
95.tq: Verify the dates, purpose and exemption separately before choosing the complete code.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
CBAM's **transitional phase** began in **2023**; its **definitive phase** on **1 January 2026**.
It aims to prevent **carbon leakage**.
Firms under an **equivalent domestic carbon price** are **exempt**.
xa: Sectors: **iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity**.
India calls CBAM a violation of **CBDR-RC** — **green protectionism**.
BRICS sees it as **sidestepping UNFCCC principles**.

95.s: India has criticised the EU CBAM mainly on the ground that it
o: eliminates all export costs for Indian producers
supports CBDR-RC and strengthens climate equity
violates CBDR-RC and represents green protectionism
applies only to domestic European production
95.x: India argues that CBAM violates the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) and amounts to green protectionism.
95.tq: Distinguish India's criticism from the stated purpose of the EU measure.
xs: India says CBAM **violates CBDR-RC** and is **green protectionism** — option **(3)**.
It **raises export costs** for Indian **steel and aluminium**, rather than eliminating them, and applies to **imports**.
xa: India fears **others may copy it**.
The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting** (New Delhi) called CBAM "**unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist**".
CBDR-RC = **Principle 7** (Rio) = **Article 3.1** (UNFCCC) = **Article 2.2** (Paris).

95.s: The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting held in New Delhi described CBAM as
95.x: The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi, during India's chairmanship, called CBAM unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist.
95.tq: Recall the exact cluster of descriptive terms used in the declaration.
xs: The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting, New Delhi** called CBAM "**unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist**" — option **(3)**.
It was held under **India's chair** on **19 Aug 2026**.
xa: BRICS sees **EU CBAM** as **sidestepping UNFCCC principles**.
CBAM's **definitive phase** began on **1 January 2026**.
The **BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance** came at **Rio, July 2025**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the G20 New Delhi Summit:
1. It was held on 9-10 September 2023.
2. Its Leaders' Declaration adopted a Green Development Pact.
3. The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the BRICS meeting in Rio rather than at this summit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
95.x: Statement 1 is correct: the summit was held on 9-10 September 2023. Statement 2 is correct: the Leaders' Declaration adopted the Green Development Pact. Statement 3 is wrong: the Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit; Rio (July 2025) is linked to the BRICS Framework Declaration on Climate Finance. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.
95.tq: G20 Delhi 2023 = Green Development Pact + Global Biofuels Alliance.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **G20 New Delhi Summit** was held on **9-10 Sept 2023**.
Statement 2 is correct: its Leaders' Declaration adopted the **Green Development Pact**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Global Biofuels Alliance** was launched at the **G20 New Delhi Summit**; **Rio (July 2025)** is the **BRICS** climate-finance declaration.
xa: India hosted the **Voice of Global South Summits** from **January 2023**.
**Mission LiFE** was launched in **October 2022**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Voice of Global South Summits:
1. The summits were hosted by India from January 2023.
2. India has used the platform to argue for the finance and technology needs of developing countries.
3. The summits were established as a mechanism of the European Union's CBAM.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The summits were hosted by India from January 2023 and addressed developing-country finance and technology needs. They were not established as a CBAM mechanism.
95.tq: Reject the unrelated institutional claim and retain the two linked policy statements.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
India has hosted the **Voice of Global South Summits** from **January 2023**.
They voice **developing-country finance and technology needs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **CBAM** is an **EU carbon levy on imports**, which India opposes.
xa: The **G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 Sept 2023)** adopted the **Green Development Pact**.
India **leads Global South positions** in climate talks.

95.s: Mission LiFE, associated with India's climate contribution, primarily seeks to promote:
95.x: Mission LiFE is India's idea-level contribution centred on individual behaviour change.
95.tq: Infer the central objective from the nature of the mission rather than its launch venue.
xs: **Mission LiFE** promotes **individual behaviour change** — option **(3)**.
It is not a treaty or carbon-trading mechanism.
xa: It was **announced at COP26** and **launched October 2022**.
COP26 also saw India announce **Panchamrit**.
India's other institutions: **ISA (2015)** and **CDRI (2019)**.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the chronology of Mission LiFE?
o: Announced at COP26 and launched in October 2022
Announced at COP21 and launched in September 2023
Announced at COP27 and launched in November 2022
Announced at COP28 and launched in October 2023
95.x: Mission LiFE was announced at COP26 and launched in October 2022.
95.tq: Separate the announcement year and the launch year before selecting the sequence.
xs: Mission LiFE was **announced at COP26** and **launched in October 2022** — option **(1)**.
**COP21** gave the **ISA**; **COP28** saw India's **COP33** bid.
xa: Its focus: **individual behaviour change**.
COP26 was held at **Glasgow** in **2021**.
India hosted the **Voice of Global South Summits** from **January 2023**.

95.s: The BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance was associated with which of the following?
95.x: The declaration was associated with the BRICS meeting at Rio in July 2025 and supported Global South demands.
95.tq: Match the declaration with its city and date.
xs: The **BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance** came at **Rio, July 2025** — option **(4)**.
It **backed Global South demands**.
**New Delhi, Sept 2023** was the **G20** summit; **Bonn, June 2026** was **SB64**.
xa: BRICS also **welcomed India's COP33 bid** in **July 2025**.
The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting** (New Delhi, **Aug 2026**) rejected **CBAM**.

95.s: Why are the consensus procedures of the CMP and CMA criticised by some observers?
o: Only developed countries may participate in them.
They operate without any parties or governments.
Consensus gives every party an effective veto.
95.x: Because the CMP and CMA work by consensus, every party can effectively block agreement, leading to the criticism that they resemble 'hop-on, hop-off buses'.
95.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of consensus decision-making.
xs: **Consensus gives every party a veto** — option **(4)**.
Critics call the **CMP/CMA** governance "**hop-on, hop-off buses**".
xa: **CMP** serves the **Kyoto Protocol**; **CMA** serves the **Paris Agreement**.
The **COP** is the supreme body and meets annually.
The Loss and Damage Fund Board also **decides by consensus**.

95.s: Persons displaced by sea-level rise are, as a category, outside the scope of the:
95.x: Climate refugees displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the legal scope of the 1951 Refugee Convention.
95.tq: Distinguish a climate-migration issue from the climate treaties themselves.
xs: Sea-level-rise refugees fall **outside the 1951 Refugee Convention** — option **(4)**.
The notes treat this as a comparative gap in international law.
xa: **Sea-level rise** threatens **Mumbai and Chennai** (AR6).
**AOSIS** small island states press for **1.5°C**.
SROCC: sea level rising from **thermal expansion and ice melt**.

95.s: Nepal's request for Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage assistance after the August 2026 glacial-collapse flood was described as:
o: An early test of the fund
A challenge to the 1951 Refugee Convention
A review of the Paris Agreement's temperature goal
The first activation of the Kyoto Protocol
95.x: Nepal's request after the August 2026 glacial-collapse flood was viewed as an early test of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage.
95.tq: Connect the disaster event with the institutional function being tested.
xs: Nepal's request after the **Aug 2026** glacial-collapse flood was an **early test of the fund** (FRLD) — option **(1)**.
The **Loss and Damage Fund** was created at **COP27** and opened to applications at **COP30**.
xa: The fund covers **economic and non-economic losses** from **sudden and slow-onset** events.
The **GCF** was criticised for a **7-year delay** on Nepal's **$49.9 million** GLOF-risk proposal.
**World Bank** = interim host and trustee until **COP33 (2028)**.

95.s: The unmet climate-finance promise of 100 billion dollars has primarily:
o: Made the Kyoto Protocol legally void
Ended the operation of the UNFCCC
95.x: Failure to meet the 100-billion-dollar promise has contributed to erosion of trust in climate negotiations.
95.tq: Link the financial shortfall with its stated political consequence.
xs: The unmet **$100 bn** promise **eroded trust** — option **(1)**.
**CBAM** is an EU levy, unrelated to this promise.
xa: The **US$100 billion/year** goal was a focus at **COP26**.
It was replaced by the **NCQG**: **US$300 billion/year by 2035**.
Developing countries excluding China got only **~15%** of **US$1.9 trillion** climate finance in **2023**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the scientific basis of UNFCCC and COP negotiations:
1. The agreed scientific baseline supports UNFCCC and COP negotiations.
2. The Paris 1.5°C goal and net-zero-by-2050 benchmarks rest on SR1.5 and AR6.
3. SR1.5 and AR6 are unrelated to climate-policy benchmarks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The agreed scientific baseline informs negotiations, and the 1.5°C and net-zero-by-2050 benchmarks rest on SR1.5 and AR6. Statement 3 is false.
95.tq: Reject the reversed relationship in the third statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**SR1.5 and AR6** are the **agreed scientific baseline** for UNFCCC/COP negotiations.
The Paris **1.5°C** goal and **net-zero-by-2050** rest on them.
Statement 3 is wrong: they are the very basis of these benchmarks.
xa: SR1.5 (**October 2018**): **net zero around 2050**.
AR6 SYR (**20 March 2023**): **1.5°C** likely crossed in the **early 2030s**.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about attribution of extreme weather events:
1. Single-event attribution of every extreme weather event to climate change is questioned.
2. AR6 notes that some local phenomena are difficult to attribute.
3. Attribution of all local phenomena is considered scientifically certain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Single-event attribution is debated, and AR6 notes difficulty in attributing some local phenomena. The claim that all local phenomena are certain to attribute is false.
95.tq: Find the absolute word in the false statement and compare it with the cautious scientific position.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Single-event attribution** of extreme weather is **questioned**.
**AR6** notes some **local phenomena are hard to attribute**.
Statement 3 is wrong: attribution of all local phenomena is not certain.
xa: AR6: human influence has **unequivocally** warmed the climate.
India **2025** extreme weather: **4,419 deaths**; **17.4 million ha** crops damaged.

95.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: International Solar Alliance — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP21, 2015 — France and India
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure — COP26 — Gurugram
95.x: The International Solar Alliance was established at COP21 in 2015 with France and India. CDRI was established in 2019 in New Delhi.
95.tq: Start with the institution's founding event and eliminate swapped dates and locations.
xs: **ISA — COP21, 2015 — France and India** is correct — option **(1)**.
**CDRI** was set up in **2019** in **New Delhi**, not at COP21 or COP26.
The ISA HQ is **Gurugram**, not New Delhi.
xa: ISA is the **first intergovernmental body headquartered in India**.
CDRI was launched at the **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019 (New York)**.
The USA's **January 2026** memorandum ended its participation in the **ISA**.

95.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance is correct?
o: It is headquartered in Paris and was created at COP26.
Its headquarters are at New Delhi, and it was created in 2019.
Its headquarters are at Gurugram, making it the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
It is a BRICS institution headquartered in Rio de Janeiro.
95.x: The International Solar Alliance is headquartered in Gurugram and is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
95.tq: Separate the headquarters fact from the similar CDRI location and date.
xs: The **ISA** is headquartered at **Gurugram** — the **first intergovernmental body headquartered in India** — option **(3)**.
It was created at **COP21, 2015**, with **France**, not at COP26 or in **2019** (that is **CDRI**).
xa: CDRI: **2019**, **New Delhi**.
US exit memorandum covers **UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA and IRENA**.
COP21 (**Paris**) also adopted the **Paris Agreement**.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's position on its net-zero target for 2070?
o: India rejects CBDR and treats the target as an immediate obligation by 2030.
India bases the target exclusively on the 1951 Refugee Convention.
India has abandoned the target because of the CBAM.
India defends the target on the grounds of CBDR and development, although it is criticised as late.
95.x: India's 2070 net-zero target is criticised as late, while India defends it using the principles of common but differentiated responsibilities and development needs.
95.tq: Contrast criticism of the timeline with India's stated justification.
xs: India **defends** its **net zero 2070** on **CBDR** and **development** grounds, though it is **criticised as late** — option **(4)**.
Most developed countries target **2050**.
xa: A large population in poverty needs **growth** and room to industrialise.
India depends on **coal**; it uses clean-coal technology and **CCS/CCUS**.
India's NDC targets **47% by 2035**.

96.s: What was the base year adopted for India's Nationally Determined Contributions relating to the reduction of emissions intensity?
96.x: India's NDC commitments on emissions intensity use 2005 as the base year.
96.tq: Direct recall of the base year.
xs: India's NDC emissions-intensity targets use **2005** as the base year — option **(2)**.
The target year is **2030** (APPSC 2019 asked the base year).
xa: India achieved a **36%** cut by **2020**.

96.s: The Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of India was submitted to the UNFCCC in:
96.x: India submitted its INDC to the UNFCCC in October 2015, before the Paris Climate Change Conference, COP21.
96.tq: Distinguish the submission date and its position relative to COP21.
xs: India submitted its **INDC** to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**, **before COP21** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** is when the **updated NDC** was communicated.
xa: In the INDC, **four of the eight NAPCC missions** focus on adaptation.
INDC targets: **33-35%** intensity cut and about **40%** non-fossil **installed capacity** by 2030.
**MoEFCC** prepares NDCs; the **Union Cabinet** approves them.

96.s:
With reference to India's 2015 INDC, consider the following statements:
1. It targeted about 40% of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
2. It targeted 40% of total electricity generation from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
3. It proposed an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through extra forest and tree cover by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The target concerned installed electric capacity, not 40% of actual power generation; hence statement 2 is false.
96.tq: Separate installed capacity from electricity generation, a frequent comparison trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: about **40%** of cumulative electric power **installed capacity** from non-fossil sources by **2030**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the target is **installed capacity**, not **generation** — a common trap in UPSC notes.
Statement 3 is correct: an additional carbon sink of **2.5-3 billion tonnes CO2e** by 2030.
xa: ⚠ Some notes write "30-35%" and "40% of power generation"; correct = **33-35%** and **installed capacity**.
NDC 3.0 raises the sink to **3.5-4.0 bn t CO2e**; **2.29 bn t** added so far.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's updated NDC:
1. It was communicated in August 2022.
2. It raised the emissions-intensity reduction target for 2030 to 47% below 2005 levels.
3. It added Mission LiFE (sustainable lifestyles) as a qualitative element.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: the updated NDC was communicated in August 2022, formalising the Panchamrit. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022 target is 45%; 47% is the NDC 3.0 target for 2035. Statement 3 is correct: Mission LiFE was added as a qualitative element. Hence 1 and 3 only; options with 2 are wrong.
96.tq: Updated NDC = Aug 2022, 45%, LiFE; 47% belongs to NDC 3.0.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **updated NDC** was communicated in **August 2022**, formalising the **Panchamrit**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the 2022 target is **45%**; **47%** is the **NDC 3.0** target for **2035**.
Statement 3 is correct: it added **Mission LiFE** (sustainable lifestyles) as a qualitative element.
xa: The Aug 2022 intensity target of **45%** was asked in **APPSC 2022**.
The 2022 non-fossil capacity target is **50%**.

96.s: Who prepares India's NDCs and who gives their final approval?
o: NITI Aayog prepares them and Parliament approves them
The UNFCCC prepares them and MoEFCC approves them
MoEFCC prepares them and the Union Cabinet gives final approval
The Ministry of Power prepares them and the President approves them
96.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change prepares India's NDCs, while the Union Cabinet gives final approval.
96.tq: Use the authority-role test to distinguish preparation from approval.
xs: **MoEFCC** prepares India's NDCs and the **Union Cabinet** gives final approval — option **(3)**.
Parliament, the UNFCCC and the President play no such role in the notes.
xa: The Union Cabinet approved **NDC 3.0** in **March 2026**.
The updated NDC was communicated in **August 2022**.
The INDC went to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the adaptation dimension of India's climate commitments:
1. The 2015 INDC stressed adaptation.
2. Four of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change focus on adaptation.
3. The updated NDC removed adaptation from India's climate commitments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Adaptation was not removed; it continued to be an important part of India's climate commitments, making statement 3 false.
96.tq: Find the statement that reverses the continuity of a policy objective.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **2015 INDC** stressed adaptation: **four of the eight NAPCC missions** focus on adaptation.
Statement 3 is wrong: adaptation was never removed — **NDC 3.0** in fact **scales up adaptation** (coasts, agriculture, Himalayan states).
xa: NDC 3.0 also embeds **LiFE** and seeks **new, low-cost climate finance**.
The **NAPCC Dashboard** tracks the national missions (launched **Sept 2026**).

96.s: India's emissions intensity of GDP had fallen by what percentage below the 2005 level by 2020?
96.x: India achieved a 36% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP below the 2005 level by 2020.
96.tq: Direct recall of a progress figure, separated from the 2030 target figures.
xs: India's emissions intensity fell **36%** below **2005** levels by **2020** — option **(3)**.
**33%** is the lower end of the **2015** target; **45%** is the **2022** target for 2030.
xa: Panchamrit pledge 4: cut emissions intensity **45%** from 2005 by **2030**.
BTR1: **over 20%** of 2022 emissions came from industry.

96.s: India crossed 50% of installed electric capacity from non-fossil sources in:
96.x: India crossed the 50% non-fossil share in installed electric capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 target timeline.
96.tq: Distinguish the achievement date from the target year and reporting dates.
xs: Non-fossil share of installed capacity **crossed 50% in June 2025**, **five years early** — option **(3)**.
The **50%** target was set for **2030** in the updated NDC.
xa: Non-fossil capacity was **51.5%** (**262.74 of 509.64 GW**) in **Nov 2025**.
⚠ **Capacity** crossed **50%**, but **generation** is only ~**25%**.
NDC 3.0 raises the capacity target to **60%**.

96.s:
Consider the following statements about India's non-fossil electricity position:
1. More than 50% of installed electric capacity was non-fossil by 2025.
2. About 25% of electricity generated was non-fossil because storage remains limited.
3. The share of non-fossil electricity generation was necessarily equal to its share of installed capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Installed capacity and actual generation are different measures; therefore statement 3 is false.
96.tq: Contrast capacity with generation instead of treating the two percentages as identical.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: non-fossil capacity **crossed 50% in June 2025**.
Statement 2 is correct: only ~**25% of power generated** is non-fossil, due to **storage shortage**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **capacity** and **generation** are different measures — the classic trap.
xa: The **National Generation Adequacy Plan** expects **70%** of **1,121 GW** non-fossil by **2035-36**.
BESS under implementation: **43 GWh** by **2028**.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Commitment)
a. INDC 2015 emissions-intensity reduction
b. Updated NDC 2022 emissions-intensity reduction
c. NDC 3.0 emissions-intensity reduction
d. NDC 3.0 non-fossil installed-capacity share

List-II (Target)
i. 47%
ii. 33–35%
iii. 60%

Codes:
96.x: The 2015 INDC target was 33–35%, the 2022 target was 45%, and NDC 3.0 sets 47% emissions-intensity reduction and 60% non-fossil installed capacity.

xs: The match is **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
NDC 3.0 → **47%** intensity cut and **60%** non-fossil installed capacity.
xa: All targets use the **2005** base year.
NDC 3.0 carbon sink: **3.5-4.0 bn t CO2e**.
Non-fossil capacity targets rose from about **40%** (2015) to **50%** (2022) to **60%**.

96.s: NDC 3.0 for the period 2031–2035 was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
96.x: The Union Cabinet approved NDC 3.0 for 2031–2035 in March 2026.
96.tq: Direct recall of the approval authority and date.
xs: NDC 3.0 (**2031-35**) was approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **March 2026** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** was the updated NDC; **June 2025** is when non-fossil capacity crossed 50%.
xa: It embeds **LiFE** and scales up adaptation.
It was described as "continuity and incremental advance" within India's **equitable share**.

96.s: Which of the following is NOT a qualitative aim associated with India's NDC 3.0?
o: Scaling up adaptation in coasts, agriculture and the Himalayas
Demanding new and low-cost climate finance
Replacing the 2005 base year with 2015 for all NDC calculations
96.x: NDC 3.0 includes Mission LiFE, enhanced adaptation and demands for new, low-cost climate finance. It does not replace the 2005 base year with 2015.
96.tq: Find the unrelated base-year substitution among the genuine qualitative aims.
xs: **Replacing the 2005 base year with 2015** is not an NDC 3.0 aim — option **(3)**.
NDC 3.0 aims: **embedding LiFE**, **scaling up adaptation** (coasts, agriculture, Himalayan states), and **new, low-cost climate finance**.
xa: The base year stays **2005**.
NDC 3.0 was approved in **March 2026**.
India relies mainly on **domestic resources (about 83%)** for climate finance.

96.s: As of 31 December 2025, which of the following correctly described the position of G20 members regarding 2035 NDCs?
o: India was the only G20 member without a 2035 NDC.
India, Argentina and Brazil were the only G20 members without a 2035 NDC.
India and Argentina were the only G20 members without a 2035 NDC.
All G20 members had filed their 2035 NDCs.
96.x: As of 31 December 2025, India and Argentina were the only G20 members that had not submitted a 2035 NDC.

xa: India's NDC 3.0 was approved later, in **March 2026**.
NDC 3.0 targets **47%** intensity cut by **2035**.
MoEFCC prepares the NDC; the **Union Cabinet** approves it.

96.s:

2. 60% non-fossil power capacity

96.s: The five commitments collectively known as 'Panchamrit' were announced by the Prime Minister at Glasgow on:
96.x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced at Glasgow on 1 November 2021 during COP26.
96.tq: Pair the named initiative with its exact announcement date and venue.
