3. It primarily provides free LPG connections to poor households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 and concerns solar pumps and farm solar plants for farmers. Statement 3 describes PM Ujjwala Yojana, not PM-KUSUM.
105.tq: Separate similar clean-energy schemes by their beneficiaries and technology.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statements 1-2 are correct: **PM-KUSUM** (**2019**) promotes **solar pumps and farm solar plants** for farmers.
Statement 3 is wrong: **free LPG connections** is **PM Ujjwala Yojana (2016)**.
xa: **PM E-DRIVE (2024)**: incentives for **electric vehicles and charging**, successor to **FAME**.
UNEP-CCAC "**Hidden Assets**" cites **PMUY** as a model clean-cooking programme.
Every **$1** in integrated action yields about **$15** (Hidden Assets).

105.s: PM E-DRIVE, launched in 2024, is intended to provide incentives for:
o: Solar pumps and agricultural land restoration
105.x: PM E-DRIVE was launched in 2024 to incentivise electric vehicles and charging infrastructure. It is the successor to FAME.
105.tq: Identify the scheme from its transport technology and stated successor relationship.
xs: **PM E-DRIVE (2024)** gives incentives for **electric vehicles and charging infrastructure** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **successor to FAME**.
LPG connections are **PMUY** (**2016**); solar pumps are **PM-KUSUM** (**2019**).
xa: **BS-VI** norms from **1 April 2020**.
Air programmes: **NCAP**, **CAQM**, **GRAP**; NAAQS cover **12 pollutants**.
Clean cooking/heating = South Asia's leading solution to **2035** (UNEP-CCAC).

105.s: The UNEP-CCAC ‘Hidden Assets’ assessment identifies PMUY as a model programme for:
105.x: The assessment cites PMUY as a model clean-cooking programme and identifies clean cooking and heating as South Asia’s leading solution towards 2035.
105.tq: Match the programme with the environmental problem it directly addresses.
xs: UNEP-CCAC "**Hidden Assets**" cites **PMUY** as a model **clean cooking** programme — option **(2)** is correct (13 Sep 2026).
**Clean cooking/heating** = South Asia's leading solution to **2035**.
xa: Every **$1** in integrated action yields about **$15**.
**PMUY** (**2016**): free LPG connections, less indoor smoke.

105.s: Ecomark was originally launched in 1991 by the:
105.x: Ecomark was launched in 1991 by the environment ministry for environment-friendly consumer products.
105.tq: Match the eco-label with its launching authority and year.
xs: **Ecomark** was launched in **1991** by the **environment ministry** (PYQ) — option **(3)** is correct.
The **FEE (Denmark)** runs **Blue Flag**, not Ecomark.
xa: **Ecomark Rules** notified **26 September 2024**, replacing the 1991 scheme.
Categories: soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics, aerosols.

105.s: Which one of the following product groups was NOT covered under the original Ecomark categories?
105.x: The notified Ecomark categories included soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics and aerosols. Drugs and antibiotics were not covered.
105.tq: Find the excluded category from a list containing closely related consumer products.
xs: **Drugs/antibiotics** were **not covered** by Ecomark (PYQ trap) — option **(2)** is the answer.
Covered: **soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics, aerosols**.
xa: Ecomark (**1991**) is for **environment-friendly** consumer products.
**Ecomark Rules 2024** aim to **prevent misleading green claims**.

105.s: The Ecomark Rules notified on 26 September 2024 primarily sought to:
o: Remove consumer information from product labels
Replace all environmental standards with voluntary advertising
Improve accurate labelling and prevent misleading green claims
105.x: The 2024 Ecomark Rules replaced the 1991 scheme and aim to ensure accurate labelling, prevent misleading green claims and support informed purchases.
105.tq: Combine the date with the principal regulatory purpose instead of confusing it with the original launch.
xs: The **Ecomark Rules** (**26 September 2024**) aim at **accurate labelling** and preventing **misleading green claims** — option **(4)** is correct.
They also support **informed purchases** and replaced the **1991** scheme.
xa: **Blue Flag** is the beach eco-label (FEE, Denmark).
**PRAMAAN**: voluntary forest and wood certification.

105.s: PRAMAAN is associated with:
o: Certification of electric vehicle charging stations
Voluntary third-party certification for sustainable forestry and agroforestry
Certification of indoor air quality in hospitals
105.x: PRAMAAN is a voluntary third-party forest and wood certification initiative for sustainable forestry and agroforestry.
105.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed environmental labels by their certified subject.
xs: **PRAMAAN** = **voluntary third-party forest and wood certification** for **sustainable forestry and agroforestry** — option **(3)** is correct.
CCS for cement and EV charging are unrelated.
xa: **Ecomark** (**1991**) — environment-friendly consumer products.
**Blue Flag** — beaches, by **FEE, Denmark**.

105.s: How many Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020?
105.x: Eight Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020.
105.tq: Recall the specific count and year rather than substituting a later status figure.
xs: **8 Indian beaches** were recommended for **Blue Flag** in **2020** (PYQ) — option **(2)** is correct.
6, 10 and 12 are not the stated number.
xa: Blue Flag is awarded by the **Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), Denmark**.
**Ecomark** is India's product eco-label (**1991**).

105.s: The 'Blue Flag' eco-label for beaches is awarded by:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
International Union for Conservation of Nature
105.x: Blue Flag is an international beach eco-label of the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), Denmark. UNEP, MoEFCC and IUCN do not award it; MoEFCC ran Ecomark (1991).
105.tq: Blue Flag = FEE Denmark; 8 Indian beaches in 2020.
xs: **Blue Flag** is awarded by the **Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), Denmark** — option **(1)** is correct.
**MoEFCC** ran **Ecomark (1991)**, not Blue Flag.
xa: **8 Indian beaches** recommended in **2020**.
**PRAMAAN** — forest and wood certification.

105.s: Which of the following functions is associated with the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board?
o: Issuing siting guidelines for industries near habitations, water bodies and fragile areas
Administering the Green Credit Programme nationally
Auditing the accounts of the Environmental Protection Fund
Awarding the Blue Flag eco-label to beaches
105.x: APPCB issues siting guidelines for industries near habitations, water bodies and fragile areas. The other functions belong to different institutions or bodies.
105.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the state pollution regulator’s function.
xs: **APPCB** issues **siting guidelines** for industries near **habitations, water bodies, fragile areas** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **CAG** audits the Environment Fund; **FEE** awards Blue Flag.
xa: APPCB (est. **1976**) has **SOPs** for effluents, marine outfalls, hazardous waste.
**Computerised inspection allocation** by risk (2025-26).

105.s:
Consider the following statements about APPCB’s regulatory arrangements:
1. It has standard operating procedures for effluents, marine outfalls and hazardous waste.
2. It uses computerised inspection allocation based on risk.
3. It permits industrial siting without considering fragile areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
105.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. APPCB’s siting guidelines specifically consider fragile areas, making statement 3 incorrect.
105.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the stated regulatory safeguard.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **SOPs** for **effluents, marine outfalls, hazardous waste** — correct.
Statement 2: **computerised inspection allocation** by risk — correct.
Statement 3: wrong — **siting guidelines** specifically cover **fragile areas**.
xa: APPCB was established in **1976**.
AP imposed a **green tax** on industries (**September 2019**).

105.s: Under the Business Reform Action Plan, Andhra Pradesh streamlined environmental clearances mainly through:
o: Transfer of all clearances to local self-government bodies
Compulsory physical inspection for every application
105.x: Andhra Pradesh streamlined clearances through digitisation and single-window systems under BRAP.
105.tq: Link the administrative reform objective with its practical implementation mechanism.
xs: Under **BRAP**, AP streamlined clearances through **digitisation and single-window systems** (2025-26) — option **(4)** is correct.
Approvals were not abolished or handed to local bodies.
xa: National single window: **PARIVESH 3.0**.
**CTO** valid till cancelled (Jan 2026).

105.s: In September 2019, the Andhra Pradesh government decided to check industrial pollution by:
o: Imposing and collecting a green tax from industrial houses
Banning all industries near water bodies
Launching the Blue Flag programme for beaches
105.x: In September 2019 AP decided to impose and collect a green tax from industrial houses (PYQ). Siting near water bodies is handled by APPCB guidelines, not a blanket ban; APPCB (est. 1976) continues; Blue Flag is an FEE eco-label.
105.tq: AP green tax = Sept 2019.
xs: In **September 2019**, AP decided to **impose and collect a green tax** from industrial houses (PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
**APPCB** (est. **1976**) continues; **Blue Flag** is an **FEE** eco-label.
xa: APPCB issues **siting guidelines** — not a blanket ban near water bodies.
AP angle also includes **BRAP single window**.

105.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised in debates relating to recent environmental regulatory changes?
o: The prohibition of clean fuels and eco-labelling.
The replacement of all Pollution Control Boards by local bodies.
Decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms may weaken deterrence.
The complete abolition of all environmental clearances for industries.
105.x: The debates include concerns that decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms could reduce deterrence. The other alternatives do not represent the stated concerns.
105.tq: Identify the genuine criticism rather than an extreme or absolute claim.
xs: Critics argue **decriminalisation and relaxed green-belt norms** may weaken **deterrence** — option **(3)** is correct.
Another debate: **ex-post facto clearances**.
xa: **Jan Vishwas Act 2023** replaced jail with **monetary penalties**.
Mandatory **33% green belt** replaced by **pollution-potential norms**.

105.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of Andhra Pradesh's environmental initiatives?
o: APPCB — siting guidelines; BRAP — single-window system
APPCB — NAAQS formulation; BRAP — CETP construction
APPCB — Blue Flag certification; BRAP — ozone monitoring
APPCB — Environmental Protection Fund Rules; BRAP — SAAP grants
105.x: APPCB is associated with siting guidelines, while BRAP is associated with a single-window system. The other pairings assign unrelated functions to these bodies or initiatives.
105.tq: Start with the sure institutional-function pair and eliminate swapped responsibilities.
xs: **APPCB — siting guidelines; BRAP — single-window system** is correct — option **(1)**.
**NAAQS**, **Blue Flag**, **Environment Fund Rules** and **SAAP** belong to other bodies or schemes.
xa: AP **green tax** on industries (**Sept 2019**).
APPCB uses **computerised inspection allocation** by risk.

105.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the emerging approach to industrial pollution control?
o: A shift from end-of-pipe control towards prevention through clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits
A policy of replacing compliance monitoring with voluntary disclosure alone
A restriction of pollution control measures to large industries only
A shift from prevention towards exclusive dependence on end-of-pipe treatment
105.x: The emerging approach moves beyond end-of-pipe control towards prevention, including clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits.
105.tq: Identify the correct direction of policy change and its associated instruments.
xs: The approach is a shift from **end-of-pipe control → prevention** through **clean fuels, eco-labels and market credits** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the direction; monitoring is not dropped.
xa: End-of-pipe tools: **ESPs, scrubbers, SCR**.
Prevention examples: **PMUY** clean cooking, **Ecomark**, **CCTS** credits.

106.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes a hazard from a disaster?
o: A hazard and a disaster are identical terms used in disaster management
A hazard refers only to economic loss, whereas a disaster refers only to physical damage
A hazard is always caused by human activity, whereas a disaster is always natural
A hazard is a potentially damaging event, whereas a disaster results when hazard interacts with vulnerability and causes serious harm
106.x: A hazard is a potentially damaging event. It becomes a disaster when it interacts with vulnerability and produces serious adverse consequences.
106.tq: Discriminate between closely related technical terms instead of treating them as synonyms.
xs: A **hazard** is a **potentially damaging event**; it becomes a **disaster** when it **interacts with vulnerability** and causes serious harm — so option **(4)** is correct.
The two terms are not identical: **risk** is the probability of harm from the **hazard-vulnerability interaction**.
A hazard need not be human-made: **natural** hazards arise from **environmental or geological processes**, **man-made** ones from human activity.
xa: **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity** — capacity reduces risk.
**Vulnerability** = susceptibility (**physical, social, economic, environmental**).
**Resilience** = ability to **resist, absorb and recover quickly**.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).

106.s:
Consider the following statements regarding vulnerability:
1. Vulnerability denotes susceptibility to harm.
2. It may have physical, social, economic and environmental dimensions.
3. It is determined exclusively by the intensity of a hazard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Vulnerability is susceptibility to harm and may be physical, social, economic or environmental. It is not determined exclusively by hazard intensity.
106.tq: Find the statement that wrongly narrows a multidimensional concept through the word 'exclusively'.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **vulnerability** means **susceptibility** to harm.
Statement 2 correct: it has **physical, social, economic and environmental** dimensions.
Statement 3 wrong: vulnerability is a separate factor from the **hazard**; risk arises from their **interaction**.
xa: **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.
**Capacity** = strengths/resources to cope; **Resilience** = ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).

106.s: Which one of the following correctly describes capacity in disaster management?
o: The strengths and resources available to cope with hazards
The process of restoring infrastructure after a disaster
The susceptibility of a community to damage
The probability that a hazard will occur
106.x: Capacity comprises the strengths and resources available to individuals, communities and institutions to cope with hazards.
106.tq: Match the exact definition with the appropriate disaster-management term.
xs: **Capacity** means the **strengths and resources available to cope** with hazards — option **(1)**.
**Susceptibility** to damage is **vulnerability**, not capacity.
**Restoring/rebuilding** after a disaster is the **recovery** phase.
xa: **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity** — higher capacity lowers risk.
**Resilience** = ability to **resist, absorb and recover quickly**.
DM cycle: **Mitigation** (pre-disaster), **Response** (during/after), **Recovery** (post-disaster).

106.s: The ability of a community to resist, absorb and recover quickly from the effects of a hazard is called
106.x: Resilience is the ability to resist, absorb and recover quickly from the effects of a hazard.
106.tq: Use the defining action words to identify the technical term.
xs: The ability to **resist, absorb and recover quickly** is **resilience** — option **(3)**.
**Vulnerability** is susceptibility to harm; **mitigation** is the pre-disaster phase (embankments, mangroves, zoning).
xa: **Capacity** = strengths/resources to cope.
**Hazard** = potentially damaging event.
**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.

106.s: In disaster management, disaster risk is commonly expressed by which relationship?
106.x: Risk rises with hazard and vulnerability and falls as coping capacity rises, so Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity. Putting capacity in the numerator (B) or adding/subtracting terms (C) reverses or breaks this logic, and D drops vulnerability entirely.
106.tq: Capacity divides risk; vulnerability multiplies it.
xs: Disaster risk is expressed as **Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity** — option **(1)**.
Risk rises with **hazard** and **vulnerability** and falls as **capacity** (strengths/resources to cope) rises, so capacity belongs in the **denominator**.
The other formulas put capacity in the numerator or drop vulnerability, reversing this logic.
xa: **Risk** = probability of harm from the **hazard-vulnerability interaction**.
**Vulnerability** dimensions: **physical, social, economic, environmental**.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).

106.s: Disaster risk reduction (DRR) works best when it:
o: Concentrates only on post-disaster relief distribution
Addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability
Relies only on rescue by national forces
Focuses solely on rebuilding damaged infrastructure
106.x: DRR is most effective when it tackles the underlying causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024 key). Relief, rescue and rebuilding are response or recovery activities, not the core of risk reduction.
106.tq: DRR = fix root causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024).
xs: **DRR** works best when it **addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2024** key).
**Relief** and **rescue** belong to the **response** phase; **rebuilding** belongs to **recovery** — not the core of risk reduction.
xa: **Mitigation** (pre-disaster): **embankments, mangroves, zoning**.
**Significance:** the **DM Act 2005** moved India from **relief → risk reduction**.
**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.

106.s: Building embankments, planting mangroves and land-use zoning belong to which phase of the disaster management cycle?
106.x: Embankments, mangroves and zoning are pre-disaster mitigation measures. Response covers rescue and relief during or just after the event; recovery covers restoration and rebuilding after it.
106.tq: Mitigation = before; response = during; recovery = after.
xs: **Embankments, mangroves and zoning** are **pre-disaster** measures of **mitigation** — option **(3)**.
**Response** (during/after) covers **rescue and relief**.
**Recovery** (post-disaster) covers **restoration and rebuilding**.
xa: **DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (**APPSC 2024**).
Cyclone mitigation uses **mangroves (Coringa, Krishna)** and **shelter belts**.
Flood mitigation: **embankments, reservoir regulation, flood forecasting**.

106.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as a biological disaster?
106.x: Epidemics, pandemics and pest attacks are biological disasters, so pest attack is correct. Earthquakes are geological, cyclones are weather-related (hydro-meteorological), and nuclear incidents are man-made/industrial disasters.
106.tq: Classify the example rather than the general term.
xs: **Pest attack** is a **biological** disaster — option **(1)**.
**Earthquakes** are **geological**; **nuclear incidents** are **man-made / industrial**.
xa: Biological also includes **epidemics** and **pandemics (COVID-19)**.
Geological: **earthquakes, landslides, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis**.
Climatological: **extreme temperatures, droughts**.
Emerging: **cyber attacks, space weather, AI failures**.

106.s: Which of the following is an emerging hazard identified in addition to conventional natural and technological hazards?
106.x: Cyber attacks, space weather and AI failures are identified as emerging hazards.
106.tq: Pick the item belonging to the emerging-hazard category.
xs: **Cyber attack** is listed as an **emerging** hazard — option **(2)**.
Emerging hazards also include **space weather** and **AI failures**, beyond conventional natural and man-made types.
xa: Man-made / industrial: **chemical and industrial accidents, fires, nuclear incidents**.
Biological: **epidemics, pandemics (COVID-19), pest attacks**.
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure** (**APPSC 2025** key).

106.s:
Consider the following statements about notified disasters eligible for SDRF or NDRF assistance:
1. The number of notified disasters became 14 after August 2026.
2. Heatwave and lightning were added on the advice of the Sixteenth Finance Commission.
3. Man-made calamities are included among the notified disasters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The number rose to 14 after heatwave and lightning were added; no man-made calamity is notified for this purpose.
106.tq: Find the single false statement by checking the eligibility exception.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: notified disasters eligible for **SDRF/NDRF** are **14 since Aug 2026** (earlier **12**).
Statement 2 correct: MHA added **heatwave and lightning** on the **16th Finance Commission's** advice.
Statement 3 wrong: ⚠ **no man-made calamity is notified**.
xa: **Heat wave**: max temp **>=40 C** in plains — now notified.
**Drought** is administered by the Ministry of **Agriculture** (with hailstorm, frost, pest attack).
AP funds (Jul 2026): SDRF/NDRF released **Rs 479.01 crore** in **2026-27** (Rs **277.63 crore** in **2025-26**).

106.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Geological disasters — Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
2. Biological disasters — Epidemics and pest attacks
3. Emerging disasters — Cyber attacks and space weather
4. Man-made disasters — Chemical accidents and nuclear incidents
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
106.x: All four pairs match the classification: geological = earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; biological = epidemics, pest attacks; emerging = cyber attacks, space weather; man-made/industrial = chemical accidents, nuclear incidents. Hence 1, 2, 3 and 4.
106.tq: Match each example with its disaster category before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Geological** = earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; **Biological** = epidemics, pest attacks.
**Emerging** = cyber attacks, space weather; **Man-made** = chemical accidents, nuclear incidents.
xa: Geological also includes **landslides** and **tsunamis**; climatological = **extreme temperatures, droughts**.
Emerging also includes **AI failures**.
**Fire from careless handling of gas cylinders** = **man-made disaster**.
⚠ **No man-made calamity is notified** for SDRF/NDRF.

106.s: A fire caused by careless handling of gas cylinders in a residential building is best classified as a:
106.x: Man-made disasters arise from human activity, negligence or technological failure (APPSC 2025 key), so a fire from careless gas-cylinder handling is man-made. It is not natural (no environmental or geological process), not biological (no pathogen or pest) and not hydrological (no water-related event).
106.tq: Negligence or technology failure = man-made.
xs: A fire from **careless handling of gas cylinders** is a **man-made disaster** — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure**; the notes rule out **natural, biological and hydrological**.
**Natural** disasters arise from **environmental or geological processes**; **biological** ones are epidemics and pest attacks.
xa: Man-made / industrial: **chemical and industrial accidents, fires, nuclear incidents**.
**Bhopal Gas Tragedy, 1984** — a chemical leak, an **anthropogenic** hazard.
⚠ **No man-made calamity is notified** for SDRF/NDRF.

106.s: Chemical accidents are regulated, among other provisions, under which pair of rules?
o: EIA Rules, 2006 and Bio-medical Waste Rules, 2016
Environment Protection Rules, 1986 and Forest Rules, 1992
106.x: Chemical accidents fall under the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules, 1989 and the Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996.
106.tq: Recall the paired legal instruments and their years without confusing them with environmental pollution rules.
xs: Chemical accidents are regulated under the **MSIHC Rules 1989** and the **CAEPPR Rules 1996** — option **(3)**.
The **CAEPPR Rules** set up **Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups**.
xa: **Bhopal Gas Tragedy**: **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** leak, night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Plant of **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
Chemical and industrial accidents are **man-made / industrial** disasters.

106.s: Under the arrangements for chemical accidents, Crisis Groups may be constituted at which levels?
o: Central, State, District and Local levels
106.x: The institutional arrangement for chemical accidents includes Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups.
106.tq: Use the complete administrative-level sequence to avoid dropping the local or district tier.
xs: Crisis Groups for chemical accidents work at **Central, State, District and Local** levels — option **(2)**.
They come under the **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.
xa: **Bhopal Gas Tragedy, 1984**: **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** at **Union Carbide India Ltd**.
Chemical leaks are **anthropogenic / man-made** hazards.
⚠ **No man-made calamity is notified** for SDRF/NDRF.

106.s: The gas that leaked in the Bhopal Gas Tragedy of 1984 was:
106.x: The Bhopal leak was of methyl isocyanate (MIC). Chlorine, carbon monoxide and ammonia are common distractors but were not the gas released at Bhopal.
106.tq: Bhopal = MIC, not chlorine/CO/ammonia.
xs: The Bhopal gas was **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — option **(2)**.
It was **not chlorine, CO or ammonia** — these are the usual distractors.
xa: Date: night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Plant of **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
A chemical leak = **anthropogenic / man-made** hazard.
Chemical accident rules: **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhopal Gas Tragedy:
1. It occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984.
2. The leak took place at the plant of Union Carbide India Ltd.
3. It is classified as a natural hazard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the leak occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984 at Union Carbide India Ltd, Bhopal. Statement 3 is wrong: it was a chemical leak, an anthropogenic (man-made) hazard. So every option with statement 3 is wrong.
106.tq: Bhopal: 2-3 Dec 1984, Union Carbide, man-made.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: it happened on the night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Statement 2 correct: the plant belonged to **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
Statement 3 wrong: it was a **chemical leak**, an **anthropogenic / man-made** hazard.
xa: Gas = **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — not chlorine, CO or ammonia.
Chemical accident rules: **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure**.

106.s:
The mitigation of cyclones and storm surges may include which of the following?
1. IMD warnings
2. Cyclone shelters and evacuation
3. Shelter belts and mangroves
4. Seismic zoning as the primary measure
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves are cyclone-related measures. Seismic zoning is primarily an earthquake mitigation measure.
106.tq: Separate hazard-specific measures from a plausible but unrelated technical measure.
xs: **IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves** are cyclone measures — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 4 wrong: **seismic zoning** is an **earthquake** measure, with safe construction.
xa: Cyclone mangroves: **Coringa, Krishna**.
Tsunami: **INCOI** warning and **Tsunami Ready** villages.
Landslide: **hazard zonation mapping**, early warning.
AP has the **longest coastline on the east coast**.

106.s: Coringa and Krishna are mentioned in the context of
o: mangroves used in cyclone and storm-surge mitigation
106.x: Coringa and Krishna are associated with mangroves that help mitigate cyclones and storm surges.
106.tq: Use location-based recall for a specific mitigation example.
xs: **Coringa and Krishna** are **mangroves** used in **cyclone and storm-surge mitigation** — option **(4)**.
Other cyclone measures: **IMD warning, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts**.
xa: **Seismic zoning** is for earthquakes; **reservoir regulation** is for floods.
**Tsunami Ready**: **24 Odisha villages** recognised, target **100**.
**Mangroves** are a **mitigation** (pre-disaster) measure, like embankments and zoning.

106.s: Which Ministry administers drought-related disaster management along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The Ministry of Agriculture administers drought-related matters along with hailstorm, frost and pest attack.
106.tq: Apply the 'who administers this subject?' authority-identification method.
xs: **Drought** is administered by the **Ministry of Agriculture**, along with **hailstorm, frost and pest attack** — option **(4)**.
**Overall coordination** of DM rests with the **Ministry of Home Affairs**' DM division.
xa: **NTRB** was set up by **MoES**.
Climatological disasters: **extreme temperatures, droughts**.
**Pest attacks** are **biological** disasters.

106.s: Tsunami mitigation and preparedness in India are associated with
o: IMD warnings and shelter belts only
INCOI warnings and Tsunami Ready villages
106.x: Tsunami warning information is associated with INCOI, while Tsunami Ready villages support local preparedness.
106.tq: Distinguish tsunami-specific institutions and preparedness measures from those for other hazards.
xs: Tsunami preparedness rests on **INCOI warnings** and **Tsunami Ready villages** — option **(4)**.
**IMD warnings and shelter belts** are cyclone measures; **embankments and reservoir regulation** are flood measures.
xa: **UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready:** **24 Odisha villages** recognised; target **100 villages**.
**NTRB** set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
Tsunamis are **geological** disasters.

106.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. Flood — embankments and flood forecasting
2. Landslide — hazard zonation mapping and early warning
3. Heat wave — maximum temperature of at least 40°C in plains with a departure of at least 4.5°C
4. Cold wave — minimum temperature of at most 10°C in plains with a departure of at most −4.5°C
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: All four statements are correct. Floods are mitigated through embankments and forecasting; landslides through zonation and warnings; and the stated thresholds define heat-wave and cold-wave conditions in plains.
106.tq: Check each hazard against its specific mitigation measure or quantitative criterion.
xs: All four combinations are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Flood**: embankments, reservoir regulation, flood forecasting; **Landslide**: hazard zonation mapping, early warning.
**Heat wave**: max **>=40 C** (plains), departure **>=4.5 C**; **Cold wave**: min **<=10 C**, departure **<=-4.5 C**.
xa: Heat wave is **now notified** — MHA added **heatwave and lightning**.
**Earthquake**: seismic zoning, safe construction.
**ISRO** supports all hazards through **DMS programme** + **NDEM**.

106.s: The Tsunami Ready recognition programme associated with UNESCO-IOC has recognised how many villages in Odisha?
106.x: Twenty-four Odisha villages have been recognised under the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready programme. The target is 100 villages.
106.tq: Distinguish the achieved number from the larger target number.
xs: **24 Odisha villages** are recognised under **UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready** — option **(3)**.
**100** is the **target**, not the number recognised.
xa: **NTRB** set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
Tsunami warning: **INCOI**.
**ISRO support:** **DMS programme** + **NDEM** (GIS database).

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Tsunami Ready Board (NTRB):
1. It was set up by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. It is chaired by the Director of INCOIS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Both statements are correct: the NTRB was set up by MoES and is chaired by the Director of INCOIS. So 'Both 1 and 2'; '1 only', '2 only' and 'Neither' each reject a true statement.
106.tq: Tsunami warning chain: MoES -> INCOIS.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: the **NTRB** was set up by **MoES**.
Statement 2: it is chaired by the **Director of INCOIS**.
xa: **UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready:** **24 Odisha villages** recognised; target **100**.
Tsunami mitigation: **INCOI** warning and **Tsunami Ready** villages.
**SACHET** (developed by **C-DOT**) is NDMA's **Common Alerting Protocol** system.

106.s: Which of the following supports the management of all hazards through a GIS database and satellite-based disaster management capabilities?
106.x: ISRO's Disaster Management Support programme and the National Database for Emergency Management support all hazards, with NDEM functioning as a GIS database.
106.tq: Match the technological system with its stated cross-hazard function.
xs: **ISRO's DMS programme and NDEM** (a **GIS database**) support all hazards — option **(4)**.
**SACHET** is NDMA's alert system and **NPDRR** a multi-stakeholder body; **Aapda Mitra** trains volunteers; **NTRB** handles tsunami readiness.
xa: **SACHET** was developed by **C-DOT** on the **Common Alerting Protocol**.
**NPDRR** is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
**Tsunami Ready**: **24 Odisha villages**, target **100**.

106.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding international disaster-risk-reduction frameworks:

List-I (Framework)
a. IDNDR
b. Hyogo Framework for Action
c. Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
d. CDRI

List-II (Period or launch year)
i. 2015–2030
ii. 1990–1999
iii. Launched in 2019
iv. 2005–2015

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
106.x: IDNDR covered 1990–1999, Hyogo covered 2005–2015, Sendai covers 2015–2030, and CDRI was launched in 2019.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive CDRI launch year and verify the remaining periods.
xs: Correct match: **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
xa: **Yokohama Strategy** (**1994**) = blueprint from IDNDR.
Sendai was adopted at the **3rd UN WCDRR**, Sendai, and **succeeds Hyogo**.
**CDRI** secretariat: **New Delhi**.
IDNDR prompted India's **DM Cell**.

106.s:
With reference to the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, consider the following statements:
1. It covers the period 2015–2030.
2. It contains four priorities for action.
3. It contains seven global targets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: The Sendai Framework covers 2015–2030 and contains four priorities and seven global targets.
106.tq: Combine the framework’s period with its two key numerical features.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Sendai** covers **2015-2030**, with **4 priorities** and **7 global targets**.
xa: Priorities: understanding risk; strengthening risk governance; investing in DRR; enhancing preparedness + **Build Back Better**.
Adopted at the **3rd UN WCDRR**; **succeeds Hyogo** (**2005-2015**).
⚠ Sendai = **4** priorities, **7** targets — do not swap them.

106.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four priorities of the Sendai Framework?
o: Investing in disaster-risk reduction for resilience
Replacing all community-based systems with centralised response agencies
106.x: The four priorities include understanding risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in risk reduction, and enhancing preparedness for effective response and Build Back Better. Replacing community systems is not a Sendai priority.
106.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the recognised priority set.
xs: **Replacing community-based systems with centralised agencies** is NOT a Sendai priority — option **(4)**.
The **4 priorities**: **understanding risk**, **strengthening risk governance**, **investing in DRR** for resilience, **enhancing preparedness** + **Build Back Better**.
xa: Sendai also has **7 global targets** (cut mortality, economic loss, etc.).
Sendai covers **2015-2030** and **succeeds Hyogo**.
Community role: the **DM Act** gives **PRIs and ULBs** a legal role.

106.s: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) is best described as:
o: A predecessor framework to the Hyogo Framework for Action
A UN treaty body headquartered in Geneva
An India-led infrastructure-resilience coalition with its secretariat in New Delhi
A State-level fund administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs
106.x: CDRI is an India-led coalition focused on infrastructure resilience, and its secretariat is located in New Delhi.
106.tq: Combine the organisation’s identity, leadership and headquarters.
xs: **CDRI** is an **India-led infrastructure-resilience coalition**, secretariat in **New Delhi** — option **(3)**.
It was launched in **2019** — well after **Hyogo** (**2005-2015**), so it is no predecessor.
xa: **Sendai Framework**: **2015-2030**.
**IDNDR** (**1990-1999**) was the first concerted UN effort.
**Yokohama Strategy**: **1994**.

106.s: The Yokohama Strategy is best described as the:
o: blueprint that emerged from the IDNDR process
106.x: The Yokohama Strategy, adopted in 1994, was the blueprint developed from the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
106.tq: Identify the framework’s relationship with IDNDR rather than its date alone.
xs: The **Yokohama Strategy** (**1994**) was the **blueprint from IDNDR** — option **(1)**.
It came long before **Sendai** (**2015-2030**), so it is no successor.
xa: **IDNDR** (**1990-1999**): first concerted UN effort; prompted India's **DM Cell**.
**Hyogo Framework**: **2005-2015**, Hyogo, Japan.
**CDRI**: launched **2019**, secretariat **New Delhi**.

106.s: Which of the following is included among the seven global targets of the Sendai Framework?
o: Reduction of international cooperation in disaster management
106.x: The Sendai global targets include increasing the availability of and access to multi-hazard early-warning systems, along with reducing mortality, affected people, economic loss and infrastructure damage.
106.tq: Identify the positive disaster-risk-reduction target among reversed or unrelated policy statements.
xs: **Multi-hazard early warning** is one of Sendai's **7 global targets** — option **(3)**.
The targets also seek **more** national/local DRR strategies and **international cooperation** — so options reducing these are wrong.
xa: Other targets: cut **mortality**, **affected people**, **economic loss**, **infrastructure damage**.
Sendai has **4 priorities**, incl. "**Build Back Better**".
Sendai: **2015-2030**, 3rd UN WCDRR.

106.s: Which set contains the three post-2015 frameworks identified as shaping India’s disaster-risk reduction approach?
o: Sendai Framework, Sustainable Development Goals and Paris Agreement
Hyogo Framework, Kyoto Protocol and Montreal Protocol
Yokohama Strategy, SDGs and Convention on Biological Diversity
IDNDR, Paris Agreement and Ramsar Convention
106.x: The three post-2015 frameworks are the Sendai Framework, the Sustainable Development Goals for 2015–2030 and the Paris Agreement.
106.tq: Use the post-2015 time filter to eliminate the earlier IDNDR, Yokohama and Hyogo instruments.
xs: The three post-2015 frameworks are **Sendai**, the **SDGs (2015-2030)** and the **Paris Agreement** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **Hyogo** is NOT one — it covered **2005-2015**.
xa: **Sendai** succeeds Hyogo: **4** priorities, **7** targets.
**CDRI** launched **2019**, India-led.

106.s: The first concerted UN effort on disaster reduction, which prompted India to set up a Disaster Management Cell, was the:
o: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction (IDNDR)
106.x: The IDNDR (1990-1999) was the first concerted UN effort and prompted India's DM Cell. Hyogo (2005-15) and Sendai (2015-30) came later, and CDRI is an India-led coalition launched in 2019.
106.tq: IDNDR 1990s -> India's DM Cell.
xs: The first concerted UN effort, which prompted India's **DM Cell**, was the **IDNDR** — option **(3)**.
**Hyogo** (**2005-2015**) and **Sendai** (**2015-2030**) came later; **CDRI** is an India-led coalition launched in **2019**.
xa: **Yokohama Strategy** (**1994**) = blueprint from IDNDR.
Hyogo stressed **resilience of nations and communities**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):
1. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
2. It lays down policies and approves the National Plan.
3. It supports other countries in major disasters and lays down policy for NIDM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
106.x: Statement 1 is wrong: NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister. Statements 2 and 3 are correct functions of NDMA. Hence '2 and 3 only'; every other option includes the false statement 1.
106.tq: NDMA = PM; NPDRR = Home Minister.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 wrong: **NDMA** is **chaired by the PM**, not the Home Minister.
Statements 2, 3 correct: NDMA **lays down policies**, **approves the National Plan**, **supports other countries** and makes policy for **NIDM**.
xa: ⚠ **NPDRR** is the body chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
NDMA also issues **guidelines to ministries/states**.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
**"Resilient India 2047"**: NDMA push for Ministry DM plans.

106.s: The overall coordination of disaster management at the Union level is undertaken through the disaster management division of the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
106.x: The disaster management division of the Ministry of Home Affairs undertakes overall coordination.
106.tq: Identify the responsible ministry rather than the operational force or technical ministry.
xs: **Overall coordination** is done by the DM division of the **Ministry of Home Affairs** — option **(2)**.
**Policy-making** and approving the **National Plan** rest with **NDMA**, chaired by the PM.
xa: **NPDRR** is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
**DG Fire Services, Civil Defence & Home Guards** is under **MHA**.
MHA added **heatwave and lightning** to notified disasters.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about fire services in India:
1. Fire services are a State subject.
2. The Directorate General of Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Fire services have no advisory role in disaster management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: Fire services are a State subject, and the DG Fire Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards under MHA has an advisory role. Statement 3 is false.
106.tq: Spot the false absolute statement and retain the two compatible administrative facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **fire services** are a **State subject**.
Statement 2 correct: **DG Fire Services, Civil Defence & Home Guards** is under **MHA**.
Statement 3 wrong: the DG has an **advisory** role.
xa: **Fires** are **man-made / industrial** disasters.
**MHA** DM division does **overall coordination**.
Gas-cylinder fire = **man-made disaster** (**APPSC 2025**).

106.s: The southern campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
106.x: The southern campus of NIDM was set up at Kondapavuluru in Krishna district, pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
106.tq: Combine the institution, location and district to avoid nearby-place substitutions.
xs: The **NIDM southern campus** is at **Kondapavuluru**, **Krishna district** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2024**).
It was set up under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.
xa: **NDMA** lays down policy for **NIDM**.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
AP: **longest coastline on the east coast**.

106.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority?
o: It is chaired by the Governor and manages only post-disaster compensation.
It is chaired by the Chief Minister and functions as the chief nodal agency for disaster management in the State.
It is chaired by the District Collector and controls the National Disaster Response Force.
It is headed by the Municipal Commissioner and operates only in municipal corporations.
106.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister, serves as the State’s chief nodal agency, runs the State Emergency Operations Centre and supports early warning.
106.tq: Match the authority with its chairperson and operational responsibilities in a state-level scenario.
xs: **APSDMA** is **chaired by the Chief Minister** and is the **chief nodal agency** — option **(2)**.
It runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre** and **early warning** — not limited to compensation.
xa: Governed by **AP DM Rules 2007**.
**NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **NPDRR** by the **Union Home Minister**.
**NIDM southern campus**: **Kondapavuluru**, Krishna district.
AP SDMF/NDMF allotted = **Rs 521.17 crore**.

106.s: The National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR) is chaired by the
106.x: NPDRR is a multi-stakeholder body chaired by the Union Home Minister.
106.tq: Identify the chairperson of the coordinating body rather than its implementing agencies.
xs: **NPDRR** is chaired by the **Union Home Minister** — option **(4)**.
⚠ The **Prime Minister** chairs **NDMA**, not NPDRR.
xa: NPDRR is a **multi-stakeholder** body.
**MHA** DM division: **overall coordination**.
**APSDMA**: chaired by the **Chief Minister**.

106.s: SACHET is best described as
o: an ISRO GIS database for all hazards
an NDMA alert system based on the Common Alerting Protocol and developed by C-DOT
a volunteer-training scheme run by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj
106.x: SACHET is NDMA's Common Alerting Protocol-based alert system, developed by C-DOT.
106.tq: Match the system with its authority, technical protocol and developer.
xs: **SACHET** is NDMA's **Common Alerting Protocol**-based alert system, developed by **C-DOT** — option **(3)**.
**Tsunami Ready** is the UNESCO-IOC programme; **NDEM** is ISRO's **GIS database**; **Aapda Mitra** trains volunteers.
xa: **NTRB**: set up by **MoES**, chaired by Director **INCOI**.
**ISRO** support: **DMS programme** + **NDEM**.
**Social media** is a **complementary**, not replacement, tool.

106.s: The 'Resilient India 2047' push is associated with
o: the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready recognition process
only the Ministry of Agriculture's drought programme
106.x: The 'Resilient India 2047' push is associated with NDMA and Ministry disaster-management plans.
106.tq: Identify the institutional setting of a named policy initiative.
xs: **"Resilient India 2047"** is an **NDMA** push for **Ministry DM plans** — option **(4)**.
It dates to **Jun 2026**.
xa: **NDMA** (chaired by the **PM**) **approves the National Plan** and issues guidelines to ministries/states.
**NPDRR**: chaired by **Union Home Minister**.
**SACHET**: NDMA alert system by **C-DOT**.

106.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies under the disaster-management framework?
o: They are responsible only for international humanitarian assistance
They have a legal role involving local plans, relief and capacity building
They have no legal role and may act only after approval from NDRF
They replace State Disaster Management Authorities in every function
106.x: The Disaster Management Act gives PRIs and ULBs a legal role in local plans, relief and capacity building.
106.tq: Reject extreme institutional claims and identify the defined local-government functions.
xs: The **DM Act** gives **PRIs and ULBs** a **legal role** — **local plans, relief, capacity** — option **(2)**.
So they are neither without a legal role nor a replacement for State authorities.
xa: **National Project for Community-Based DRR in PRIs**: **Rs 507.37 crore**, MoPR + NDMA.
It builds **20 Model GPs** on **6 hazard themes**.
**Aapda Mitra**: NDMA scheme training **community volunteers** as **first responders**.

106.s: Aapda Mitra is primarily associated with
o: maintaining a national GIS database of hazards
training community volunteers as first responders
106.x: Aapda Mitra is an NDMA scheme for training community volunteers to act as first responders.
106.tq: Match a named scheme with its distinctive operational purpose.
xs: **Aapda Mitra** is an **NDMA** scheme **training community volunteers as first responders** — option **(4)**.
Tsunami warnings come from **INCOI**; drought is with **Agriculture**; the GIS database is ISRO's **NDEM**.
xa: The **DM Act** gives **PRIs and ULBs** a legal role.
**20 Model GPs** on **6 hazard themes** under the PRI project.
**Social media** = **complementary** tool.

106.s: Which statement regarding the use of social media in disaster risk reduction is correct?
o: Social media has no role in community-based disaster management
Social media is a complete replacement for official warning systems
Social media can be used only after the recovery phase
Social media is a complementary tool and not a replacement for established systems
106.x: Social media can support communication and community engagement, but it is a complementary tool rather than a replacement for official disaster-management systems.
106.tq: Avoid absolute claims and identify the limited but useful complementary role.
xs: **Social media** is a **complementary** tool, **not a replacement** — option **(4)**.
So it neither replaces official systems nor lacks a role in community DRR.
xa: **SACHET**: NDMA's **Common Alerting Protocol** alert system (**C-DOT**).
**Aapda Mitra** trains community **first responders**.
**PRIs and ULBs** have a legal role under the **DM Act**.

106.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Project for Strengthening Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction in Panchayati Raj Institutions:
1. Its outlay is Rs 507.37 crore.
2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with NDMA.
3. It develops 20 Model Gram Panchayats on six hazard themes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
106.x: All three are correct: the project has an outlay of Rs 507.37 crore, is run by MoPR with NDMA, and creates 20 Model GPs on 6 hazard themes. Each other option leaves out a true statement.
106.tq: CBDRR in PRIs: Rs 507.37 cr, MoPR+NDMA, 20 model GPs.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Outlay **Rs 507.37 crore**; run by **MoPR + NDMA**.
It develops **20 Model GPs** on **6 hazard themes**.
xa: The **DM Act** gives **PRIs and ULBs** a legal role — local plans, relief, capacity.
**Aapda Mitra**: NDMA volunteer **first-responder** training.
**Social media** = **complementary**, not replacement.

106.s: Operation Vanilla was associated with humanitarian assistance to
o: Turkey and Syria after the 2023 earthquake
106.x: Operation Vanilla assisted Madagascar following Cyclone Diane in 2020.
106.tq: Link the operation name to the assisted country and disaster event.
xs: **Operation Vanilla** helped **Madagascar** after **Cyclone Diane, 2020** — option **(1)**.
**Karuna** = Myanmar (**Cyclone Mocha**, **2023**); **Maitri** = Nepal (earthquake, **2015**); **Dost** = Turkey, Syria (earthquake, **2023**).
xa: **Sadbhav**: Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar — **Typhoon Yagi**, **2024**.
**Brahma**: Myanmar — earthquake, **2025**.
**NDMA** also **supports other countries** in major disasters.

106.s:
Match the following HADR operations with the countries assisted:

A. Maitri
B. Dost
C. Karuna
D. Sadbhav

1. Turkey and Syria
2. Nepal
3. Myanmar
4. Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
106.x: Maitri assisted Nepal, Dost assisted Turkey and Syria, Karuna assisted Myanmar, and Sadbhav assisted Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar.
106.tq: Start with the distinctive multi-country pair and eliminate codes that swap neighbouring operations.
xs: The correct code is **A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Maitri** went to **Nepal** (earthquake, **2015**); **Dost** went to **Turkey and Syria** (earthquake, **2023**).
**Karuna** went to **Myanmar** (Cyclone **Mocha**, **2023**); **Sadbhav** went to **Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar** (Typhoon **Yagi**, **2024**).
xa: **Operation Vanilla** helped **Madagascar** after Cyclone **Diane**, **2020**.
**Operation Brahma** helped **Myanmar** after the **2025** earthquake.
⚠ **Myanmar** appears in three operations: **Karuna** (cyclone), **Sadbhav** (typhoon) and **Brahma** (earthquake).
**NDMA** has the role of **supporting other countries** in major disasters.

106.s: Operation Brahma, as listed in the humanitarian assistance context, was associated with
o: the 2024 Typhoon Yagi in Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar
the 2023 earthquake in Turkey and Syria
106.x: Operation Brahma assisted Myanmar following the 2025 earthquake.
106.tq: Use the event-year combination to distinguish operations with the same assisted country.
xs: **Operation Brahma** was India's help to **Myanmar** after the **2025 earthquake** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Typhoon Yagi, 2024** (Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar) was **Operation Sadbhav**.
The **2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake** was **Operation Dost**; **Cyclone Diane, 2020** (Madagascar) was **Operation Vanilla**.
xa: **Operation Maitri** helped **Nepal** after the **2015** earthquake.
**Operation Karuna** helped **Myanmar** after Cyclone **Mocha**, **2023**.
⚠ Do not mix up the two Myanmar quake/cyclone missions: **Brahma** = earthquake, **Karuna** = cyclone.

106.s: Which statement correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's coastline in the stated geographical context?
o: It is the longest coastline in India and lies on the west coast
It is the second-longest coastline in India and the shortest on the east coast
It has no significant exposure to coastal hazards
It is the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast
106.x: Andhra Pradesh now has the third-longest coastline in India and the longest on the east coast. 'Second-longest' is the older figure, AP is on the east (not west) coast, and its long coast makes it highly exposed to cyclones and storm surges.
106.tq: Handle comparative rankings carefully and avoid substituting an older figure for the stated current one.
xs: Andhra Pradesh has the **third-longest coastline in India** and the **longest on the east coast** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**"Second-longest"** is only the **older figure**, and AP lies on the **east coast**, not the west.
A long coast means high exposure: cyclone mitigation uses **cyclone shelters**, evacuation and **mangroves (Coringa, Krishna)**.
xa: The **Godavari floods of July 2026** tested **NDRF/SDRF** and early warning in AP.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** and runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**.
The **NIDM southern campus** is at **Kondapavuluru**, **Krishna district**, under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.

106.s: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 is considered significant because it shifted India's disaster-management approach from
106.x: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 marked a shift from a primarily relief-oriented approach towards risk reduction and more comprehensive disaster management.
106.tq: Test the policy significance through the direction of institutional change.
xs: The **DM Act 2005** moved India from **relief-oriented action towards risk reduction** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Act also gives **PRIs and ULBs** a legal role (local plans, relief, capacity) — the opposite of centralisation.
xa: **NDMA**, chaired by the **PM**, lays down policies and approves the **National Plan**.
**DRR** works best when it **addresses underlying causes of vulnerability** (APPSC **2024**).
The DM cycle: **Mitigation** (pre-disaster), **Response** (during/after), **Recovery** (post-disaster).
**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.

106.s: The amount released by Andhra Pradesh under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26, as compared with Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27, was
106.x: Andhra Pradesh released Rs 277.63 crore under SDRF/NDRF in 2025–26, compared with Rs 479.01 crore in 2026–27.
106.tq: Distinguish successive-year figures from the separate SDMF/NDMF allocation.
xs: AP's SDRF/NDRF release in **2025-26** was **Rs 277.63 crore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It rose to **Rs 479.01 crore** in **2026-27**.
**Rs 521.17 crore** is the **SDMF/NDMF** (mitigation fund) allotment, and **Rs 507.37 crore** is the outlay of the **PRI community-based DRR project**.
xa: Notified disasters eligible for **SDRF/NDRF**: **14 since Aug 2026** (earlier **12**).
MHA added **heatwave and lightning** on the **16th Finance Commission's** advice.
⚠ **No man-made calamity** is a notified disaster.

106.s: The July 2026 Godavari floods primarily tested the effectiveness of
o: NDRF/SDRF operations and early warning systems
106.x: The Godavari floods in July 2026 tested NDRF and SDRF operations along with early-warning mechanisms.
106.tq: Identify the disaster-management capabilities directly engaged by a flood event.
xs: The **July 2026 Godavari floods** tested **NDRF/SDRF operations and early warning systems** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Flood mitigation rests on **embankments**, **reservoir regulation** and **flood forecasting**, not tsunami or earthquake measures.
xa: AP has the **third-longest coastline** in India and the **longest on the east coast**.
AP's SDRF/NDRF release: **Rs 479.01 crore** in **2026-27** against **Rs 277.63 crore** in **2025-26**.
**APSDMA** (chaired by the **Chief Minister**) runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre** and early warning.

106.s: As of July 2026, the amount allotted to Andhra Pradesh under SDMF/NDMF (State/National Disaster Mitigation Fund) was
106.x: Andhra Pradesh was allotted Rs 521.17 crore under SDMF/NDMF. Rs 479.01 crore and Rs 277.63 crore were SDRF/NDRF releases in 2026-27 and 2025-26.
106.tq: Mitigation 521 > Response 479.
xs: AP was allotted **Rs 521.17 crore** under **SDMF/NDMF** (as of **July 2026**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rs 479.01 crore** is the **SDRF/NDRF** release for **2026-27**, and **Rs 277.63 crore** the SDRF/NDRF release for **2025-26**.
xa: ⚠ SDRF/NDRF = **response** funds; SDMF/NDMF = **mitigation** funds.
Mitigation is the **pre-disaster** phase: **embankments, mangroves, zoning**.
The **PRI community-based DRR project** has an outlay of **Rs 507.37 crore** with **20 Model GPs**.

107.s: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 primarily provides the legal framework for which of the following?
107.x: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for dealing with biological disasters and epidemics and was used during COVID-19.
107.tq: Choose the legal instrument according to its subject matter and historical use.
xs: The **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** is the legal framework for **biological disasters and epidemic control** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was the law used during **COVID-19**.
**Genome sequencing** of pathogens is done by the **INSACOG** lab network, not by any Act.
xa: Under it, e.g. **20 states** made **human rabies** notifiable (Jan **2026**).
The **2020 amendment** made violence against health workers **cognizable and non-bailable**.
The **Draft Public Health Bill, 2017** was meant to replace it but was **not enacted**.
Criticism: the Act is **colonial**, with no definition of "**dangerous epidemic disease**" and no rights safeguards.

107.s: Under the Epidemic Diseases Act framework, which of the following is correctly matched?
107.x: Urgent cases must be reported within 24 hours, while routine cases must be reported within three days.
107.tq: Separate the shorter urgent-reporting period from the routine period.
xs: **Urgent cases** must be reported **within 24 hours** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Routine cases** are reported **within 3 days**, so options (2), (3) and (4) mix up the timelines.
xa: Example of notification: **20 states** made **human rabies** notifiable (Jan **2026**).
⚠ **24 hours** is also the IHR deadline to report a possible **PHEIC** to **WHO**.
The Act provides the legal framework for **biological disasters** and was used in **COVID-19**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897:
1. It came as an ordinance in April 2020 and became an Act in September 2020.
2. It made violence against health workers cognizable and non-bailable.
3. It gave State Governments exclusive powers over inspection at ports of entry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: ordinance in April, Act in September 2020. Statement 2 is correct: violence against health workers became cognizable and non-bailable. Statement 3 is wrong: the Centre, not the States, got powers over inspection at ports of entry. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: 2020 amendment: protection of health workers + Centre's port powers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the amendment came as an **ordinance in April** and became an **Act in September 2020**.
Statement 2 correct: violence against health workers became **cognizable and non-bailable**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Centre**, not the States, got powers over **inspection at ports of entry**.
xa: Penalty for violence: **3 months to 5 years** jail + **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine.
Grievous hurt: **6 months to 7 years** + **Rs 1-5 lakh** fine.
PM-ABHIM builds preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about India's COVID-19 response:
1. The national lockdown of March 2020 was ordered under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
2. The lockdown was ordered by NCDC and ICMR.
3. Empowered Groups of the Ministry of Home Affairs ran the pandemic response.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the lockdown was under the DM Act, 2005. Statement 2 is wrong: it was ordered by NDMA and MHA, not NCDC and ICMR. Statement 3 is correct: MHA Empowered Groups ran the response. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
107.tq: Lockdown = DM Act via NDMA + MHA, not the 1897 Act.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **March 2020 national lockdown** was ordered under the **DM Act, 2005**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was ordered by **NDMA + MHA**, not NCDC and ICMR.
Statement 3 correct: **MHA Empowered Groups** ran the pandemic response.
xa: **NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **SDMAs** by the **Chief Ministers**.
**MoHFW** remains the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.
The **MoHFW Disaster Management Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the Draft Public Health Bill, 2017:
1. It was intended to replace the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897.
2. It concerned prevention, control and management of epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters.
3. It has been enacted as a law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: The draft Bill was intended to replace the 1897 Act and covered epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters, but it has not been enacted.
107.tq: Find the false statement by checking the legal status of the draft Bill.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Draft Public Health Bill, 2017** was meant to **replace the 1897 Act**.
Statement 2 correct: its full title covers **Epidemics, Bio-Terrorism and Disasters**.
Statement 3 wrong: it was **not enacted** and is still pending.
xa: The **1897 Act** is criticised as **colonial**, with no definition of "**dangerous epidemic disease**".
The **2020 amendment** to the 1897 Act came as an ordinance in **April** and an Act in **September 2020**.
**IHR (2005)**, in force since **2007**, is a legally binding **WHO** instrument.

107.s: Under the Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act, 2020, violence against health-care workers that does not cause grievous hurt is punishable with:
o: Imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years and a fine of Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh
Imprisonment of 6 months to 7 years and a fine of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh
Imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to Rs 10,000
Imprisonment of 1 to 3 years and a fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh
107.x: Simple violence carries 3 months to 5 years and Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh. B (6 months to 7 years, Rs 1-5 lakh) is the higher penalty for grievous hurt. C and D are not the penalties in the amendment.
107.tq: Violence 3m-5y + 50k-2L; grievous 6m-7y + 1-5L.
xs: Violence without grievous hurt carries **3 months to 5 years** jail and a **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2), **6 months to 7 years** and **Rs 1-5 lakh**, is the higher penalty for **grievous hurt**.
xa: The offence is **cognizable and non-bailable**.
The amendment came as an **ordinance (April)** and an **Act (September 2020)**.
The Centre also got powers over **inspection at ports of entry**.

107.s: Which of the following is the technical arm of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare?
107.x: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) functions as the technical arm of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
107.tq: Distinguish the technical arm from coordinating and surveillance bodies.
xs: The **DGHS** is the **technical arm** of MoHFW — so option **(1)** is correct.
**INSACOG** is a genome-sequencing lab network; **NDMA** is the PM-chaired disaster authority; **MHA Empowered Groups** ran the COVID response.
xa: **MoHFW** is the **nodal ministry for epidemics** (PYQ).
**NCDC** (formerly **NICD**) is the apex surveillance and outbreak-response agency.
**NCDC** runs **IDSP** and the **National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC):
1. It was formerly the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD).
2. It runs the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme and sends Outbreak Investigation Teams.
3. The National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre is run by DGHS, not NCDC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: NCDC was formerly NICD. Statement 2 is correct: it runs IDSP and sends Outbreak Investigation Teams. Statement 3 is wrong: NCDC itself runs the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre; DGHS is MoHFW's technical arm. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: NCDC = surveillance + outbreak response + NPHEOC; DGHS = technical arm.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **NCDC** was formerly **NICD**.
Statement 2 correct: NCDC runs **IDSP** and sends **Outbreak Investigation Teams**.
Statement 3 wrong: **NCDC itself** runs the **National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre**; DGHS is only MoHFW's technical arm.
xa: **IDSP** began in **2004** under **NHM**, with a **Central Surveillance Unit** in Delhi.
Centre asked states to step up **IDSP** surveillance for **Ebola** (23 May **2026**).
AP's **zoonotic disease action plan** is being drawn up with **NCDC**, **US CDC** and **Jhpiego**.

107.s:
With reference to the institutional framework for health emergencies, consider the following statements:
1. NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. State Disaster Management Authorities are chaired by Chief Ministers.
3. NDMA lays down guidelines and coordinates health emergencies under the Disaster Management Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
107.x: All three are correct: NDMA is chaired by the Prime Minister, SDMAs by the Chief Ministers, and NDMA lays down guidelines and coordinates health emergencies under the DM Act, 2005 (e.g. its Biological Disaster Management guidelines of 2008).
107.tq: Verify both the chairpersons and the statutory function before selecting the code.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4) 1, 2 and 3** is correct.
**NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **SDMAs** are chaired by **Chief Ministers**.
NDMA lays down **guidelines** and coordinates health emergencies under the **DM Act**.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **March 2020** lockdown was ordered by **NDMA + MHA** under the **DM Act, 2005**.
**MoHFW** is still the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.

107.s: The Biological Disaster Management guidelines were issued by the National Disaster Management Authority in which year?
107.x: NDMA issued the Biological Disaster Management guidelines in 2008.
107.tq: Separate the guideline year from the years of the DM Act and National Plan.
xs: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**2005** is the **DM Act**; **2016** is India's first **National Disaster Management Plan**; **2020** is the year of the DM Cell and the lockdown.
xa: Epidemics are classed as **biological disasters**.
The **MoHFW Disaster Management Cell** was set up in **Dec 2020** for pandemic planning.
The **NDMP (2016)** aligns with **Sendai (2015-30)**, the SDGs and Paris.

107.s: Which of the following was designated as the nodal unit for pandemic planning in December 2020?
o: National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre
107.x: The Disaster Management Cell of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare became the nodal unit for pandemic planning in December 2020.
107.tq: Identify the exact institutional unit rather than the parent ministry alone.
xs: The **MoHFW Disaster Management Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Central Surveillance Unit** (Delhi) belongs to **IDSP**; the **National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre** is run by **NCDC**.
**MHA Empowered Groups** ran the pandemic response, not pandemic planning.
xa: Under **PM-ABHIM**: **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**.
BHISHM Cubes were deployed during **Operation Sindoor**.
**INSACOG** was also set up in **Dec 2020**.

107.s: Which Ministry is the nodal ministry in India for the management of epidemics (biological disasters)?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
107.x: MoHFW is the nodal ministry for epidemics (PYQ), with DGHS as its technical arm and NCDC as the surveillance agency. MHA coordinates disasters in general, while Science and Technology and Environment ministries are not nodal for epidemics.
107.tq: Epidemic nodal = MoHFW; general DM = MHA.
xs: **MoHFW** is the **nodal ministry for epidemics** (PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**MHA** coordinated the COVID lockdown with **NDMA** under the DM Act, but is not nodal for epidemics.
Within MoHFW, **DGHS** is the **technical arm** and **NCDC** the surveillance agency.
xa: The **MoHFW DM Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
The **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** is the legal framework for biological disasters.

107.s: BHISHM Cubes, deployed during Operation Sindoor, are associated with which programme?
o: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM)
107.x: Under PM-ABHIM, MoHFW's DM Cell has 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes, which were deployed during Operation Sindoor. NDRF, IDSP and Aapda Mitra are separate programmes.
107.tq: BHISHM Cubes (50) + HEOCs (15) = PM-ABHIM.
xs: **BHISHM Cubes** belong to **PM-ABHIM (PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PM-ABHIM provides **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**, deployed during **Operation Sindoor**.
**IDSP** is a surveillance programme (**2004**), not the cubes' parent scheme.
xa: PM-ABHIM: **744 IPHLs**, one in every district.
PM-ABHIM: **631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks** in districts with over **5 lakh** people.
PM-ABHIM: preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

107.s: Distributing vaccines before the occurrence of an epidemic is classified under which phase of the disaster management cycle?
107.x: Pre-outbreak vaccine distribution reduces the potential impact of an epidemic and is therefore a mitigation measure.
107.tq: Classify the measure by asking whether it reduces impact before the event.
xs: **Distributing vaccines before an outbreak** is a **mitigation** measure (PYQ key) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Preparedness** = surveillance, stockpiles, hospital readiness, mock drills.
**Response** = isolation, quarantine, contact tracing; **Recovery** = restoring services, rehabilitation.
xa: Other epidemic mitigation measures: **sanitation** and **vector control**.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
⚠ Vaccines **before** an outbreak = mitigation; treatment **during** it = response.

107.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mitigation — sanitation and vector control
2. Preparedness — hospital readiness and mock drills
3. Response — isolation, quarantine and contact tracing
4. Recovery — rehabilitation and economic relief
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
107.x: All four pairs correctly associate epidemic measures with the mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery phases respectively.
107.tq: Match each measure to the phase in which it is normally undertaken.
xs: All four pairs are correctly matched — so option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4** is correct.
**Mitigation**: sanitation, vector control; **Preparedness**: hospital readiness, mock drills.
**Response**: isolation, quarantine, contact tracing; **Recovery**: rehabilitation, economic relief.
xa: PYQ key: **distributing vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.
**Lockdown** and **treatment** also fall under the **response** phase.
The **NDMP (2016)** covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP):
1. Issued in 2016, it was India's first national disaster management plan.
2. It aligns with the Sendai Framework (2015-30), the SDGs and the Paris Agreement.
3. It deals only with post-disaster response and recovery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 2016 NDMP was India's first. Statement 2 is correct: it aligns with Sendai, the SDGs and Paris. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: NDMP 2016 covers the whole cycle, not just response.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **NDMP (2016)** was **India's first** national plan.
Statement 2 correct: it aligns with **Sendai (2015-30)**, the **SDGs** and **Paris**.
Statement 3 wrong: it covers **prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery**.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **DM Act 2005** is the law under which NDMA operates.
PYQ key: **vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.

107.s: For disaster-management purposes, epidemics are classified as which type of disasters?
107.x: Epidemics are treated as biological disasters in disaster-management planning.
107.tq: Identify the disaster category from the nature of the hazard.
xs: Epidemics are classified as **biological disasters** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Geological** disasters are earthquakes and landslides; **industrial** disasters are chemical accidents.
xa: The **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** provides the legal framework for biological disasters.
NDMA issued **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
**MoHFW** is the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.

107.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IHIP portal — real-time pooling of grassroots surveillance data
U-WIN — genome sequencing of SARS-CoV-2 variants
107.x: The IHIP portal pools grassroots data in real time. U-WIN tracks immunisation, while INSACOG tracks variants through genome sequencing.
107.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate swapped functions.
xs: The **IHIP portal** does **real-time pooling of grassroots surveillance data** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**U-WIN** tracks **immunisation**, not genomes.
**INSACOG** does **genome sequencing** to track variants; the AP **Covid Pharma app** tracked purchases of fever medicines.
xa: **IHIP** began in **2018** in a few states and went **nationwide from Sep 2021**.
**IDSP** began in **2004** under **NHM**.
Reporting categories: **Syndromic (S)**, **Presumptive (P)**, **Laboratory-confirmed (L)**.

107.s:
Consider the following statements about disease surveillance in India:
1. The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) was launched in 2004 under the National Health Mission.
2. IDSP works through a Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi along with State and District Surveillance Units.
3. The Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) was launched nationwide in 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
107.x: Statement 1 is correct: IDSP began in 2004 under NHM. Statement 2 is correct: CSU in Delhi plus State and District units. Statement 3 is wrong: IHIP began in a few states in 2018 and went nationwide only from September 2021. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
107.tq: IHIP: 2018 pilot, nationwide Sep 2021.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **IDSP** was launched in **2004** under **NHM**.
Statement 2 correct: its units are a **Central Surveillance Unit** (Delhi) + State and District Surveillance Units.
Statement 3 wrong: **IHIP** began in a few states in **2018** and went **nationwide only from Sep 2021**.
xa: IDSP is implemented by **MoHFW** and run by **NCDC**.
The **IHIP** portal pools grassroots data in **real time**.
Centre asked states to step up IDSP surveillance for **Ebola** (May **2026**).

107.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three categories of reporting used in disease surveillance?
107.x: Surveillance data are reported through syndromic (S), presumptive (P) and laboratory-confirmed (L) categories.
107.tq: Expand the surveillance abbreviations and distinguish them from site categories.
