Elimination targets: **malaria**, **LF**, **kala-azar**.
AP **Adult BCG drive** (from **16 May 2024**): **27.10 lakh** doses — **leader in India**.

114.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016–2030) aims to achieve which of the following?
o: Elimination of all communicable diseases by 2030
114.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers the period 2016–2030 and aims at a malaria-free India by 2030.
114.tq: Match the programme period with its precise national target.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016-2030)** aims at a **malaria-free India by 2030** — option **(2)** is correct.
It targets malaria only, not dengue or all communicable diseases.
xa: Malaria is an NCVBDC elimination target alongside **LF** and **kala-azar**.
WHO malaria-free in South Asia: **Maldives (2015)**, **Sri Lanka (2016)**.
AP response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Biological control agent)
A. Gambusia
B. Bti
C. Wolbachia
D. Guppy

List-II (Description)
1. Bacterial bio-larvicide
2. Larvivorous fish
3. Bacterium associated with cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking

Codes:
A B C D
(a) 2 1 3 2
(b) 1 2 3 1
(c) 2 3 1 2
(d) 3 1 2 3
114.x: Gambusia and guppy are larvivorous fish; Bti is a bacterial bio-larvicide; Wolbachia is associated with cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking.
114.tq: Start from the sure pair Bti–bacterial bio-larvicide and eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: **Gambusia – larvivorous fish (2)**; **Bti – bacterial bio-larvicide (1)**; **Wolbachia – cytoplasmic incompatibility + pathogen blocking (3)**; **guppy – larvivorous fish (2)** — option **(1)** (2 1 3 2).
**Bti** = **Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis**.
xa: **Wolbachia** works with **no GM or pesticides**.
Wolbachia is in **40-60%** of insect species; harmless to humans.
⚠ It is **not native** to **Aedes aegypti** or **Anopheles**.

114.s:
With reference to Wolbachia, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Gram-negative bacterium found naturally in 40–60% of insects.
2. It is naturally present in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.
3. It can cause cytoplasmic incompatibility in which eggs fail to develop.
4. It can contribute to pathogen blocking.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: Wolbachia is a Gram-negative bacterium found in 40–60% of insects. It causes cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking, but it is naturally absent in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.
114.tq: The false statement reverses the important absence of Wolbachia in the named mosquito genera.
xs: Statements **1, 3 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: **Wolbachia** is a **Gram-negative bacterium** in **40-60%** of insect species.
2 is wrong: it is **absent naturally** in **Aedes aegypti** and **Anopheles**.
3 and 4: it causes **cytoplasmic incompatibility** (eggs fail to hatch) and **pathogen blocking**.
xa: Wolbachia is **harmless to humans**; no GM or pesticides needed.
**Verily 'Debug'** (**2026**) released Wolbachia-carrying males of **Culex quinquefasciatus**.
Other bio-control: **Gambusia**, guppy, **Bti**.

114.s: In the Verily ‘Debug’ approach described for vector suppression, Wolbachia-carrying males were used to suppress which mosquito species?
114.x: The Verily ‘Debug’ approach used Wolbachia-carrying males to suppress Culex quinquefasciatus, a vector associated with West Nile and St Louis encephalitis.
114.tq: Discriminate between closely related mosquito genera by linking the intervention to the exact species.
xs: Verily's **'Debug'** project released Wolbachia-carrying non-biting males of **Culex quinquefasciatus** — option **(2)** is correct.
This Culex is the vector of **West Nile** and **St Louis encephalitis** (and **lymphatic filariasis**).
xa: Done with **no GM, no pesticide** (**2 Jun 2026**).
Wolbachia acts by **cytoplasmic incompatibility** + **pathogen blocking**.
Wolbachia is **not native** to **Aedes aegypti** or **Anopheles**.

114.s: Which of the following pairs of countries was certified malaria-free by WHO in South Asia in 2015 and 2016, respectively?
114.x: Maldives was certified malaria-free in 2015 and Sri Lanka in 2016.
114.tq: Use the year sequence to distinguish two closely associated regional certifications.
xs: WHO certified **Maldives (2015)** and **Sri Lanka (2016)** malaria-free — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the order; **India** is still aiming for malaria-free status by **2030**.
xa: **National Framework for Malaria Elimination**: **2016-2030**.
Malaria, **LF** and **kala-azar** are NCVBDC **elimination targets**.
AP malaria **2025**: **7,119** cases, **8** deaths.

114.s: Under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (now NCVBDC), which diseases are targeted for elimination?
114.x: Of the six diseases covered (malaria, JE, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, LF), the elimination targets are malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar. Dengue, chikungunya and JE are controlled, not targeted for elimination.
114.tq: Elimination trio = malaria, LF, kala-azar.
xs: The elimination targets are **malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Dengue**, **chikungunya** and **JE** are covered but not slated for elimination.
xa: **Malaria and dengue** = **outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive**.
Malaria-free India target: **2030**.
**Kala-azar** vector: **sandfly**; **LF** pathogen: **Wuchereria bancrofti**.

114.s: The Widal test is associated with the diagnosis of which disease?
114.x: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, and the Widal test is associated with its diagnosis.
114.tq: Link the named diagnostic test to its specific water-borne disease.
xs: The **Widal test** is for **typhoid** (**Salmonella Typhi**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Cholera** is caused by **Vibrio cholerae**; **hepatitis A** is viral; **dysentery** by **Shigella**, **E. coli**, **rotavirus**.
xa: Typhoid spreads by the **faeco-oral route**.
Floods spread **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis** and **leptospirosis**.
Cholera toxin → severe **dehydration**; treated with **ORS**.

114.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
114.x: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae. Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, while acute diarrhoea and dysentery may involve Shigella, E. coli and rotavirus.
114.tq: Separate the principal pathogen from pathogens of other faecal-oral diseases.
xs: **Cholera — Vibrio cholerae** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Typhoid** is **Salmonella Typhi**, not Shigella; **hepatitis A** is a **virus**; **dysentery** involves **rotavirus, E. coli, Shigella**.
xa: Cholera toxin → severe **dehydration**; **ORS**.
**Widal test** = typhoid.
Acute diarrhoea/dysentery = **leading child killer**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis A and E can spread through the faecal-oral route.
2. Hepatitis B and C are generally blood-borne rather than water-borne.
3. Tuberculosis is an airborne disease, not a water-borne disease.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: Hepatitis A and E are faecal-oral diseases, hepatitis B and C are blood-borne, and tuberculosis is airborne rather than water-borne.
114.tq: Use the transmission-route contrast to identify all correct statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
1: **Hepatitis A and E** spread by the **faecal-oral** route.
2: **Hepatitis B/C** are **blood-borne**; 3: **TB** is **air-borne** — a common odd-one-out.
xa: Faeco-oral group: **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery, polio**.
TB: **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, **droplet nuclei**, targets the **lungs**.
Hepatitis A and E cause **jaundice**.

114.s: Which one of the following is the correct set of diseases commonly spread through the faecal-oral route by contaminated water or food?
o: Tuberculosis, hepatitis B, malaria, dengue and rabies
Japanese encephalitis, cholera, hepatitis B, scrub typhus and influenza
Cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio
Hepatitis C, sleeping sickness, yellow fever, typhoid and plague
114.x: The faecal-oral group includes cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio.
114.tq: Identify the complete transmission-route group and reject airborne, blood-borne and vector-borne diseases.
xs: The faecal-oral set is **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other sets mix in **air-borne TB**, **blood-borne hepatitis B/C** and **vector-borne** diseases like **malaria, dengue, scrub typhus, sleeping sickness, yellow fever**.
xa: Spread through **contaminated water/food**.
**~5,000 children die daily** worldwide from water- and sanitation-related disease.
Remedies: **Jal Jeevan Mission**, **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **AMRUT**.

114.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
114.x: Nitrate contamination is associated with blue-baby syndrome. Fluorosis is associated with fluoride contamination.
114.tq: Find the swapped chemical-contamination pair.
xs: **Nitrate — fluorosis** is wrong: nitrate causes **blue-baby syndrome**; **fluoride** causes **fluorosis** — option **(3)**.
The rest are correct: **arsenic — blackfoot disease**; **mercury — Minamata**; **cadmium — itai-itai**.
xa: Faeco-oral diseases: cholera, typhoid, **hepatitis A and E**, polio.
**~5,000 children die daily** from preventable water/sanitation disease.
Remedies: **Jal Jeevan Mission**, **Swachh Bharat**, **AMRUT**.

114.s: Approximately how many children die daily worldwide from preventable water- and sanitation-related diseases?
114.x: The stated estimate is approximately 5,000 children every day worldwide.
114.tq: Distinguish the order of magnitude in the quantitative estimate.
xs: About **5,000 children die daily** worldwide from preventable water- and sanitation-related disease — option **(2)** is correct.
**Acute diarrhoea/dysentery** is the **leading child killer**.
xa: Remedies: **Jal Jeevan Mission**, **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **AMRUT**.
AP IDSP (**2025**): water-borne outbreaks **-62.7%**, diarrhoea deaths **-72%**.
Contaminants: **arsenic** → blackfoot; **nitrate** → blue-baby syndrome.

114.s: Which one of the following sets contains diseases whose spread can be associated with floods?
o: Scrub typhus, polio, cancer and asthma
Hepatitis B, AIDS, dengue and influenza
114.x: Floods can spread cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and leptospirosis, in addition to supporting the spread of some vector-borne diseases.
114.tq: Recognise the environmental-disaster cluster of water-related diseases.
xs: Floods spread **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and leptospirosis** — option **(2)** is correct.
Floods also aid **vector-borne disease**; cancer, asthma, AIDS and rabies are not flood-borne.
xa: Climate impact: more **heatwaves, floods, cyclones** and **VBDs**.
Heatwaves → **dehydration**, **heatstroke**, cardiovascular stress.
**3.6 billion+** people live in highly climate-vulnerable areas.

114.s: According to the cited Andhra Pradesh assessment for 2025–26, water-borne outbreaks declined by approximately:
114.x: The reported decline in water-borne outbreaks was 62.7%. The other figures refer to food-borne outbreaks, all outbreaks or diarrhoea deaths.
114.tq: Separate closely related percentages by the indicator to which each belongs.
xs: AP's **water-borne outbreaks fell 62.7%** (IDSP **2025**, APSES **2025-26**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**21%** = food-borne outbreaks; **47%** = all outbreaks; **72%** = diarrhoea deaths.
xa: **ADD cases** fell **9.63%**.
**24-member State task force** on communicable diseases (**7 Jan 2026**), headed by the Health Commissioner.
AP **State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) — workshop at **Vijayawada**.

114.s: Which of the following is a set of measures identified for addressing water and sanitation-related disease risks?
o: Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT
National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme, BCG and ORS
AMRUT, Widal test and Wolbachia release
Swachh Bharat Mission, Widal test and DPT
114.x: Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT are identified as relevant remedies or interventions.
114.tq: Distinguish programmes and remedies from diagnostic tests, vaccines and vector-control methods.
xs: **Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT** are the water and sanitation remedies — option **(1)** is correct.
**Widal** is a typhoid test, **Wolbachia** a vector control, **BCG** a TB vaccine — not sanitation measures.
xa: **~5,000 children die daily** from water/sanitation disease.
Faeco-oral diseases include **cholera**, **typhoid**, **polio**.
Cholera treatment: **ORS**.

114.s: The organ system primarily affected by air pollution is the:
114.x: Air pollution primarily affects the respiratory system, although it is also associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke and lung cancer.
114.tq: Select the principal health system rather than a secondary effect.
xs: Air pollution mainly targets the **respiratory system** (APPSC **2023** PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
It also causes **heart disease**, **stroke** and **lung cancer**.
xa: WHO: **4.2 million** premature deaths from **ambient** air pollution (**2019**).
Triggers: **pollens, spores, bacteria, viruses**.
**DALY = YLL + YLD**.

114.s:
Noise pollution is associated with which of the following health effects?
1. Hearing loss
2. Hypertension
3. Sleep disorders
4. Anxiety
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: Noise pollution is associated with hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety.
114.tq: Check whether all listed effects belong to the same environmental-health category.
xs: Noise pollution causes **hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety** — all four, option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
Options **(1)-(3)** each leave out at least one of these listed effects.
xa: Air pollution mainly targets the **respiratory system**.
WHO: **4.2 million** ambient air pollution deaths (**2019**).
**DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) is WHO's disease-burden metric.

114.s: According to the World Health Organization figure cited for 2019, ambient outdoor air pollution caused approximately how many premature deaths?
114.x: The cited WHO estimate is 4.2 million premature deaths from ambient outdoor air pollution in 2019.
114.tq: Use the scale of the statistic to distinguish millions from thousands and crores.
xs: WHO estimated **4.2 million** premature deaths from **ambient (outdoor)** air pollution in **2019** (APPSC **2023**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The other figures scale it wrongly.
xa: Air pollution's main target: **respiratory system**.
Also heart disease, **stroke**, **lung cancer**.
WHO projects **~2.5 lakh** extra climate-linked deaths a year (**2030-2050**).

114.s: A public-health assessment is examining premature mortality and time lived with disability together. Which measure is most appropriate for this purpose?
114.x: DALY combines years of life lost due to premature death and years lived with disability, making it a disease-burden metric.
114.tq: Identify the metric from the components described in the scenario.
xs: **DALY** combines premature death and disability: **DALY = YLL + YLD** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is **WHO's disease-burden metric**; AQI, BOD and Widal measure other things.
xa: YLL = years of life lost; YLD = years lived with disability.
**NCDs** = **57%+ of deaths**, yet communicable diseases persist.

114.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with respect to climate-sensitive health impacts?
114.x: Floods can trigger outbreaks of cholera and hepatitis. Heatwaves are associated with dehydration, heatstroke and cardiovascular stress, while warming may expand the range of dengue and malaria vectors.
114.tq: Use cause-effect matching and reject the reversed trend.
xs: **Floods — cholera and hepatitis outbreaks** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Heatwaves** cause **dehydration, heatstroke**, cardiovascular stress; **warming expands** (not contracts) vector range; cyclones do not reduce VBDs.
xa: Climate change raises **VBDs** (malaria, dengue, **JE**).
**Dasra** report: **~40%** of Indian districts at high risk.
**3.6 billion+** people in highly climate-vulnerable areas.

114.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Climate change can intensify heatwaves, floods and cyclones.
2. Malaria, dengue and Japanese encephalitis are among the vector-borne diseases affected by climate change.
3. About 3.6 billion people live in highly climate-vulnerable areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: All three statements are correct. Climate change increases the risk of extreme weather events and several vector-borne diseases, and about 3.6 billion people are reported to live in highly vulnerable areas.
114.tq: Check whether all three linked statements describe the same climate-health relationship.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
1: more **heatwaves, floods, cyclones**; 2: **VBDs** like **malaria, dengue, JE**.
3: **3.6 billion+** people in highly climate-vulnerable areas.
xa: WHO projection: **~2.5 lakh** extra deaths a year (**2030-2050**).
**Dasra 'Under the Weather'** (Apr **2026**): **~40%** of districts at high risk.
Warming **expands the range** of dengue and malaria vectors.

114.s: According to the Dasra report ‘Under the Weather’, approximately what proportion of Indian districts are at high risk from extreme weather?
114.x: The Dasra report ‘Under the Weather’ estimated that approximately 40% of Indian districts are at high risk from extreme weather.
114.tq: Distinguish the reported percentage from nearby rounded alternatives.
xs: **Dasra's 'Under the Weather'** report (Apr **2026**) put **~40%** of Indian districts at high risk from extreme weather — option **(3)**.
The report is also cited as dated **10 Apr 2026**.
xa: WHO projection: **~2.5 lakh** extra deaths a year (**2030-2050**) from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea, heat.
**3.6 billion+** people live in highly climate-vulnerable areas.
Heatwaves → **heatstroke**, dehydration, cardiovascular stress.

114.s: The World Health Organization has estimated that climate change may cause approximately how many additional deaths annually during 2030–2050 from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea and heat?
114.x: The estimate is approximately 2.5 lakh additional deaths annually during 2030–2050 from the specified climate-sensitive causes.
114.tq: Split the numerical options by magnitude before selecting the reported estimate.
xs: WHO projects **~2.5 lakh extra deaths a year (2030-2050)** from malnutrition, malaria, diarrhoea and heat — option **(1)** is correct.
The crore and lakh variants in other options inflate the figure.
xa: Climate change brings more **heatwaves, floods, cyclones** and **VBDs**.
**Dasra** report: **~40%** of districts at high risk.
WHO: **4.2 million** air-pollution deaths (**2019**).

114.s:
Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause or facilitating factor of antimicrobial resistance?
1. Overuse or misuse of antibiotics
2. Self-medication
3. Poor sanitation
4. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: Overuse or misuse, self-medication and poor sanitation contribute to AMR. Regulated and scientifically supervised veterinary drug use is not a cause; unregulated veterinary drug use is a concern.
114.tq: Find the carefully reversed statement in an otherwise familiar list of AMR causes.
xs: **Regulated, scientifically supervised veterinary drug use** is not a cause — it is **unregulated** veterinary drugs that drive AMR — option **(3)** (**4 only**).
Causes include **overuse/misuse** of antibiotics in humans and animals, **self-medication** and **poor sanitation**.
xa: Also **poor waste control** and **pharma effluents** → a **One Health** problem.
**National Action Plan on AMR (2017)**: One Health based.
**Biofilms** shield bacteria from antibiotics and immunity.

114.s: What are biofilms in the context of antimicrobial resistance?
o: Microbial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix
Synthetic capsules used to deliver antibiotics
Dead bacterial cells produced after antibiotic treatment
Free-floating viruses that destroy antibiotic molecules
114.x: Biofilms are microbial or bacterial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix, which shields them from antibiotics and, in many cases, from host immunity.
114.tq: Use the exact structural definition rather than a broad association with infection.
xs: **Biofilms** are bacterial communities in a **self-made slimy matrix** — option **(1)** is correct.
The matrix **shields** them from **antibiotics and immunity**.
xa: **WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (2024)**: critical = carbapenem-resistant **Acinetobacter baumannii**, **Enterobacterales**, rifampicin-resistant **TB**.
AMR causes: **overuse/misuse**, self-medication, **pharma effluents**.
**Nafithromycin** — India's first indigenous **macrolide**.

114.s: Nafithromycin, marketed as ‘Miqnaf’, is correctly described as which of the following?
o: India’s first indigenous antiviral for dengue
A fungal vaccine developed for tuberculosis
A carbapenem developed exclusively for hospital-acquired malaria
India’s first indigenous macrolide for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia
114.x: Nafithromycin, or Miqnaf, is India’s first indigenous macrolide antibiotic intended for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
114.tq: Link the drug name with its exact class, origin and therapeutic indication.
xs: **Nafithromycin ("Miqnaf")** is India's **first indigenous macrolide** for **community-acquired bacterial pneumonia** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is an antibiotic — not an antiviral, vaccine or carbapenem.
xa: Launched **20 Nov 2024** by **Dr. Jitendra Singh**.
Developed by **Wockhardt** with **BIRAC** support — ⚠ **NOT Sun Pharma**.
**Red Line campaign (2016)** marks prescription-only antibiotics.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nafithromycin:
1. It was launched on 20 November 2024.
2. It was launched by Dr Jitendra Singh.
3. It was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support.
4. It was developed by Sun Pharma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: Nafithromycin was launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh and was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support. It was not developed by Sun Pharma.
114.tq: The wrong-company trap tests precise attribution of a product’s developer.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Nafithromycin was launched **20 Nov 2024** by **Dr. Jitendra Singh**, developed by **Wockhardt** with **BIRAC** support.
Statement 4 is wrong: ⚠ it is **NOT Sun Pharma**.
xa: Brand name **"Miqnaf"**; a **macrolide** for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
**National Action Plan on AMR**: **2017**.
**Kerala KARSAP (2018)**: first State AMR plan.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's policy response to antimicrobial resistance:
1. The National Action Plan on AMR (2017) is based on the One Health approach.
2. Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State-level AMR action plan.
3. The Red Line campaign (2016) places a red vertical line on the packs of all over-the-counter medicines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: NAP-AMR (2017) is One Health based. Statement 2 is correct: Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State AMR action plan. Statement 3 is wrong: the Red Line (2016) marks prescription-only antibiotics, not all over-the-counter medicines. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses KARSAP, and options with 3 include the false statement.
114.tq: Red Line = prescription-only antibiotics; NAP-AMR 2017, KARSAP 2018, Red Line 2016.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **National Action Plan on AMR (2017)** is **One Health** based — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Kerala's KARSAP (2018)** was the **first State AMR action plan**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Red Line (2016)** marks **prescription-only antibiotics**, not all OTC medicines.
xa: **National One Health Mission** (**PM-STIAC**) tackles **AMR**, rabies, Nipah, avian influenza.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AMR causes include **self-medication** and unregulated veterinary drugs.

114.s:
Which of the following are listed as critical priority bacterial pathogens in the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, 2024?
1. Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii
2. Enterobacterales
3. Rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis
4. Wolbachia
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: The critical-priority group includes carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, Enterobacterales and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis. Wolbachia is not included in this list.
114.tq: Separate antimicrobial priority pathogens from an unrelated biological-control organism.
xs: The critical group of the **WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (2024)** is **carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii**, **Enterobacterales** and **rifampicin-resistant TB** — option **(2)** (**1, 2 and 3 only**).
**Wolbachia** is not a pathogen list entry — it is a harmless bacterium used for **vector control**.
xa: **Biofilms**: bacterial communities in a **self-made slimy matrix** shielding them from antibiotics.
AMR causes: **overuse/misuse** of antibiotics, self-medication, **pharma effluents**.
**Nafithromycin ("Miqnaf")** — India's first indigenous **macrolide**.

114.s:
The central principle of One Health is that which of the following are interconnected?
1. Human health
2. Animal health
3. Environmental health
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: One Health treats human, animal and environmental health as linked and manages them together through coordinated action.
114.tq: Identify the defining three-domain structure of the concept.
xs: **One Health** = **human, animal and environmental health** managed together — all three, option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
Options (1)-(3) each leave out one of the three linked domains.
xa: **Biodiversity loss** raises **zoonotic and pandemic risk**.
Tools: **joint surveillance**, animal vaccination, veterinary drug oversight, linked databases.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.

114.s: Which of the following is a likely public-health consequence of biodiversity loss under the One Health framework?
o: Lower risk of zoonotic spillover and pandemics
114.x: Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic and pandemic risk by disturbing ecological relationships and interactions between humans, animals and pathogens.
114.tq: Apply the ecological component of One Health to an emerging-disease scenario.
xs: Under One Health, **biodiversity loss** leads to **increased zoonotic and pandemic risk** — option **(4)** is correct.
It does not lower spillover, eliminate reservoirs or give immunity.
xa: **One Health** = human, animal and environmental health together.
**National One Health Mission (PM-STIAC)**: used against **rabies, Nipah, avian influenza** and **AMR**.
Tools include **carcass/waste control** and **veterinary drug oversight**.

114.s: The National One Health Mission is associated with which of the following institutions or bodies?
114.x: The National One Health Mission is associated with PM-STIAC and provides institutional multisectoral coordination for One Health actions.
114.tq: Use institutional association to distinguish the mission from unrelated national bodies.
xs: The **National One Health Mission** comes under **PM-STIAC** — option **(3)** is correct.
It provides **institutional multisectoral coordination**; ECI, CPCB and ILO are unrelated.
xa: Used against **rabies**, **Nipah**, **avian influenza** and **AMR**.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AP's **State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) is under One Health.

114.s: The National Institute of One Health is located at:
114.x: The National Institute of One Health is located at Nagpur.
114.tq: Test the location of the specialised institution directly against nearby major-city distractors.
xs: The **National Institute of One Health** is in **Nagpur** — option **(4)** is correct.
New Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad are not named for it.
xa: **National One Health Mission** is under **PM-STIAC**.
**One Health** = human, animal and environmental health together.
**IDSP (2004)** under **MoHFW/NCDC** handles disease surveillance.

114.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP):
1. It was established in 2004.
2. It functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the NCDC.
3. It is concerned with disease surveillance.
4. It is now operated through the IHIP digital platform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: IDSP was established in 2004 under MoHFW/NCDC for disease surveillance and is now implemented through the digital IHIP platform.
114.tq: Accept the complete institutional, chronological and functional description when all statements align.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**IDSP** began in **2004**, under **MoHFW/NCDC**, for **disease surveillance**, now on the **IHIP** digital platform.
xa: **NCDC** leads **surveillance and response**.
AP IDSP (**2025**): water-borne outbreaks **-62.7%**; all outbreaks **-47%**.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897:
1. It was enacted against the bubonic plague in Bombay.
2. It contains four sections.
3. It was amended in 2005 to protect health workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act was enacted against bubonic plague in Bombay. Statement 2 is correct: it has four sections. Statement 3 is wrong: the amendment protecting health workers came in 2020, not 2005. Hence '1 and 2 only'; every other option includes the false statement 3 or drops a true one.
114.tq: 1897 plague in Bombay, 4 sections, amended 2020 (COVID) for health workers.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **Epidemic Diseases Act 1897** was enacted against **bubonic plague** in **Bombay** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **4 sections**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it was **amended in 2020** (not 2005) to protect health workers.
xa: **Plague**: rodents via **rat flea**; pathogen **Yersinia pestis**.
**IDSP (2004)**: disease surveillance under **MoHFW/NCDC**.
**NCDC** leads **surveillance and response**; IDSP now runs on the **IHIP** platform.

114.s: Which of the following combinations correctly identifies diseases against which the National One Health Mission may be used?
o: Rabies, Nipah, avian influenza and antimicrobial resistance
114.x: The National One Health Mission is applicable to rabies, Nipah, avian influenza and AMR, among other linked health threats.
114.tq: Choose the option that spans zoonotic, epidemic and antimicrobial-resistance concerns.
xs: The **National One Health Mission** is used against **rabies, Nipah, avian influenza and AMR** — option **(4)** is correct.
It targets **zoonotic** and **AMR** threats, not only malaria/dengue or NCDs.
xa: Mission body: **PM-STIAC**; institute at **Nagpur**.
AMR is a **One Health problem** (antibiotic misuse in humans and animals).
Zoonoses: **rabies** (dog bite), **Nipah** (fruit bats), **H5N1** (birds/poultry).

114.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases was being prepared under One Health through a workshop involving which set of organisations?
114.x: The Andhra Pradesh workshop involved NCDC, the US CDC and Jhpiego, as part of preparation of a State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases.
114.tq: Identify the exact institutional partnership rather than a generic international-agency combination.
xs: AP's workshop at **Vijayawada** for the **State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) involved **NCDC, US CDC and Jhpiego** — option **(1)**.
WHO, IMF, UNEP, ISRO etc. are not named.
xa: Departments: **Health**, **Animal Husbandry**, **Forest**, **Environment**, **Agriculture**, **Fisheries**.
**24-member State task force** on communicable diseases (**7 Jan 2026**).
Scrub typhus: **941** cases in AP.

114.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Indradhanush:
1. It was launched in December 2014.
2. It aims at more than 90% full immunisation of children and pregnant women.
3. IMI 5.0 was designed mainly to reach adults above 60 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
114.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Mission Indradhanush began in December 2014 with a target of >90% full immunisation of children and pregnant women. Statement 3 is wrong: IMI 5.0 reaches missed and dropped-out children, not the elderly. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses a true statement and the others include statement 3.
114.tq: Indradhanush = children + pregnant women; IMI targets missed/dropped-out children.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Mission Indradhanush** began in **Dec 2014** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
Statement 2 is correct: target **>90% full immunisation** of children and pregnant women.
Statement 3 is wrong: **IMI 5.0** reaches **missed/dropped-out children**, not the elderly.
xa: **U-WIN**: digital portal registering every UIP vaccination.
AP adult **BCG** drive: **27.10 lakh** doses.

114.s: The Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) was introduced in which year?
114.x: The Universal Immunisation Programme was introduced in 1985.
114.tq: Select the programme year from the sequence of major immunisation milestones.
xs: The **Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)** began in **1985** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **12 diseases**.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush**: **Dec 2014**, **>90%** full immunisation target.
**U-WIN** registers every UIP vaccination.
UIP includes **JE** in **endemic districts**.

114.s:
Which of the following diseases are included in the 12-disease basket of the Universal Immunisation Programme?
1. Diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus
2. Polio, measles and rubella
3. Childhood tuberculosis and hepatitis B
4. Hib meningitis/pneumonia, rotavirus diarrhoea, pneumococcal pneumonia and Japanese encephalitis in endemic districts
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
114.x: The UIP list includes all the diseases stated: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, measles, rubella, childhood TB, hepatitis B, Hib disease, rotavirus diarrhoea, pneumococcal pneumonia and JE in endemic districts.
114.tq: Treat the complete disease list as one integrated enumeration and select the inclusive combination.
xs: All four groups are in the **UIP's 12 diseases** — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**Diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, measles, rubella**, **childhood TB**, **hepatitis B**.
**Hib meningitis/pneumonia**, **rotavirus diarrhoea**, **pneumococcal pneumonia**, **JE (endemic districts)**.
xa: UIP began in **1985**.
**IMI 5.0** reaches missed/dropped-out children.
⚠ **Hepatitis B** is **blood-borne**, unlike faeco-oral hepatitis A and E.

114.s: What is the principal function of the U-WIN digital portal?
o: Registering every vaccination provided under UIP
Monitoring only antimicrobial resistance in hospitals
Recording only adult BCG doses in Andhra Pradesh
114.x: U-WIN is a digital portal for registering every vaccination administered under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
114.tq: Match the digital platform with its exact record-keeping function.
xs: **U-WIN** is the digital portal **registering every UIP vaccination** — option **(2)** is correct.
It does not license manufacturers, monitor AMR or record only AP BCG doses.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush** (**Dec 2014**): **>90%** full immunisation.
**IDSP** surveillance now runs on the **IHIP** digital platform.

114.s:
With reference to the adult BCG drive in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It began on 16 May 2024.
2. It involved 27.10 lakh doses.
3. Andhra Pradesh was the leading State in India in this drive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
114.x: The AP adult BCG drive began on 16 May 2024, administered 27.10 lakh doses and placed Andhra Pradesh first in India for this drive.
114.tq: Combine date, numerical scale and comparative rank in a single factual set.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
AP's **adult BCG drive** began **16 May 2024**, gave **27.10 lakh** doses and made AP the **leader in India** (APSES **2024-25**).
xa: **Childhood TB** is one of the **UIP**'s **12** diseases.
TB is **air-borne**, targets the **lungs**.
**24-member State task force** on communicable diseases (**Jan 2026**).

114.s: As reported up to 30 August 2026, which combination is correct for Andhra Pradesh?
114.x: Up to 30 August 2026, Andhra Pradesh recorded 7,895 malaria cases and 1,475 dengue cases. The reported increases were 27.9% for malaria and 4.6% for dengue.
114.tq: Anchor the figures to the stated cut-off date before comparing year-wise data.
xa: 2026 malaria hotspots: **ASR**, **Polavaram**, **Vizianagaram**.
Scrub typhus: **941** cases.
**Agency (tribal) districts** carry most of AP's malaria.

114.s: The 2026 rise in malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh was particularly concentrated in which districts or area?
114.x: The rise in malaria in 2026 was concentrated in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Polavaram and Vizianagaram districts.
114.tq: Use location-based elimination and avoid substituting other district groups.
xs: The **2026** malaria rise was concentrated in **ASR (Alluri Sitharama Raju), Polavaram and Vizianagaram** — option **(1)** is correct.
These are **tribal/agency** districts, not the coastal or Rayalaseema districts in other options.
xa: Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam.
Response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

114.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported 2026 burden of scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh and its concentration?
o: 1,475 cases, rising in all coastal districts
941 cases, rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam
52 cases, rising in ASR and Kurnool
146 cases, rising in Polavaram and Vizianagaram
114.x: Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
114.tq: Match the disease burden figure with the correct geographical concentration.
xs: AP had **941** scrub typhus cases, **rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Scrub typhus vector: **chigger mite**; pathogen **Orientia tsutsugamushi**.
**High-level committees** were set up for scrub typhus.
**Agency districts** carry most of AP's scrub typhus.

114.s: Which of the following measures is most directly associated with the response to vector-borne disease burden in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Indoor residual spraying, LLIN mosquito nets and source reduction
Removal of all livestock from tribal districts
Replacement of mosquito control with vaccination alone
Exclusive use of antibiotics and suspension of surveillance
114.x: The response includes indoor residual spraying, long-lasting insecticidal nets and source reduction. These measures target mosquito vectors and their breeding sites.
114.tq: Apply the control method to the vector-borne disease scenario.
xs: AP's response: **indoor residual spraying (IRS)**, **LLIN mosquito nets** and **source reduction** — option **(1)** is correct.
These target the vectors; removing livestock, vaccination alone or antibiotics are not the measures.
xa: Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) (**23 Apr 2026**).
**24-member State task force** (Jan **2026**).
Bio-control options: **Gambusia**, guppy, **Bti**, **Wolbachia**.

114.s: In January 2026, what institutional measure was reported for communicable disease control in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A 12-member national committee on air pollution
A 24-member State task force on communicable diseases
A district-level committee exclusively for dengue vaccines
A 50-member international task force on malaria
114.x: A 24-member State task force on communicable diseases was constituted in January 2026. High-level committees were also associated with scrub typhus response.
114.tq: Identify the exact body and membership figure instead of a similar administrative arrangement.
xs: In **January 2026** AP set up a **24-member State task force on communicable diseases** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is headed by the **Health Commissioner** (**7 Jan 2026**).
xa: **High-level committees** were formed for **scrub typhus**.
**State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) under One Health.
AP IDSP (**2025**): water-borne outbreaks **-62.7%**.

114.s: Malaria parasites first multiply in the liver and subsequently infect which blood component?
114.x: Malaria parasites first undergo development in the liver and then infect red blood cells.
114.tq: Follow the biological sequence from the initial organ to the blood component.
xs: Malaria parasites hit the **liver**, then **red blood cells (RBCs)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Platelets** are the main target of **dengue**, not malaria.
xa: **Plasmodium** is a **protozoan**; vector **female Anopheles**.
**P. falciparum** is the most lethal (**cerebral malaria**).
**Filariasis** targets the **lymphatic system**.

114.s: Amoebiasis is primarily an infection of the:
o: Lymphatic system caused by filarial worms
Small intestine caused by Ascaris lumbricoides
Large intestine caused by Entamoeba histolytica
114.x: Amoebiasis affects the large intestine and is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
114.tq: Discriminate between similar disease-organ and causative-organism combinations.
xs: **Amoebiasis** infects the **large intestine**, caused by **Entamoeba histolytica** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Ascaris lumbricoides** = **ascariasis** (small intestine); **filariasis** = lymphatic system; **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** = TB (lungs).
xa: **Dengue** targets **platelets** (APPSC **2023**).
**Malaria**: liver, then RBCs.
Water-borne **dysentery** pathogens: **rotavirus**, **E. coli**, **Shigella**.

114.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Malaria — liver followed by red blood cells
114.x: Dengue is associated with platelets. The lymphatic system and elephantiasis are associated with filariasis.
114.tq: Find the deliberately swapped disease-organ association.
xs: **Dengue — lymphatic system — elephantiasis** is wrong: dengue targets **platelets**; lymphatic system/elephantiasis = **filariasis** — option **(1)**.
The rest are correct: **malaria** — liver then RBCs; **ascariasis** — small intestine; **TB** — lungs.
xa: **Amoebiasis**: large intestine (**Entamoeba histolytica**).
Filariasis: **Wuchereria bancrofti**, vector **Culex quinquefasciatus**.
TB spreads by **droplet nuclei**.

114.s: Which of the following best describes India’s epidemiological transition as reflected in the reported health indicators?
o: Life expectancy increased, but non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths while communicable diseases persist.
Life expectancy remained unchanged and non-communicable diseases account for less than 10% of deaths.
Communicable diseases have disappeared because life expectancy increased.
Life expectancy declined while communicable diseases became the only major cause of death.
114.x: Life expectancy increased from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023, yet non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths and communicable diseases continue to persist, creating a double burden.
114.tq: Recognise the double burden by comparing improvements with continuing disease persistence.
xs: **Life expectancy rose**, but **NCDs** cause **>57%** of deaths while **communicable diseases persist** — option **(1)** is correct.
Life expectancy rose **49.7 (1973) → 70.3 (2023)** — so the "unchanged/declined" options are wrong.
xa: This is the **epidemiological transition/double burden** (ES **2025-26**).
Vector-borne and water-borne diseases still persist.
**DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) measures disease burden.

114.s: Which statement about the geographical distribution of malaria and scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The burden is confined to districts with no tribal population.
The agency districts carry most of the State’s malaria and scrub typhus burden.
Agency districts have no significant vector-borne disease burden.
The burden is concentrated exclusively in the major coastal cities.
114.x: The agency or tribal districts carry most of Andhra Pradesh’s malaria and scrub typhus burden, making them a priority for surveillance and control.
114.tq: Use the AP-specific geographical trend and reject absolute location claims.
xs: The **agency (tribal) districts** carry **most of AP's malaria and scrub typhus** — option **(2)** is correct.
So the burden is not confined to non-tribal or coastal areas.
xa: 2026 malaria hotspots: **ASR**, **Polavaram**, **Vizianagaram**.
Scrub typhus rising in **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people.

114.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh in 2025, which of the following is correct?
o: Malaria: 5,268 cases and no deaths; dengue: 6,453 cases and 2 deaths
Malaria: 7,119 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 2,686 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,895 cases and 8 deaths; dengue: 1,475 cases and 5 deaths
Malaria: 7,871 cases and no deaths; dengue: 5,555 cases and 5 deaths
114.x: In 2025, Andhra Pradesh recorded 7,119 malaria cases with 8 deaths and 2,686 dengue cases with 5 deaths in the cited data.
114.tq: Read the paired case-and-death figures together rather than matching cases alone.
xs: In **2025**, AP had **malaria 7,119 cases, 8 deaths** and **dengue 2,686 cases, 5 deaths** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: **AES/JE 2025**: **146** cases, **2** deaths; chikungunya **52** cases.
2023 and 2024 had **0** malaria deaths.
Source: **APSES 2025-26**.

114.s: Which statement correctly describes the 2025 Andhra Pradesh figures for AES/JE and chikungunya?
o: AES/JE: 2 cases and 146 deaths; chikungunya: 52 deaths
AES/JE: 146 cases and 8 deaths; chikungunya: 941 cases
AES/JE: 52 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 146 cases
AES/JE: 146 cases and 2 deaths; chikungunya: 52 cases
114.x: The reported 2025 figures were 146 AES/JE cases with 2 deaths and 52 chikungunya cases.
114.tq: Keep case and death figures separate while matching the two diseases.
xs: AP **2025**: **AES/JE 146 cases and 2 deaths**; **chikungunya 52 cases** — option **(4)** is correct.
Other options swap the figures; **941** is scrub typhus and **8** is malaria deaths.
xa: JE vector: **Culex**; **pigs** amplify it.
Chikungunya: **alphavirus**, spread by **Aedes**.
Malaria **2025**: **7,119** cases, **8** deaths.

114.s: Which of the following correctly represents Andhra Pradesh’s 2024 malaria and dengue figures?
114.x: The 2024 figures were 7,871 malaria cases and 5,555 dengue cases, with zero malaria deaths reported in the cited APSES data.
114.tq: Use the year-number association and reject figures belonging to adjacent years.
xs: AP **2024**: **malaria 7,871**, **dengue 5,555**, with **zero deaths** — option **(4)** is correct.
xa: ⚠ Malaria rose from **5,268** (2023) to **7,871** (2024), while dengue fell from **6,453** to **5,555**.
Source: **APSES 2024-25**.
AP adult **BCG** drive from **16 May 2024**.

114.s: Free long-lasting insecticidal nets were reported to cover approximately how many people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, at a cost of Rs 19.25 crore?
114.x: Free LLINs were reported for approximately 7.80 lakh people in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam, involving an expenditure of Rs 19.25 crore.
114.tq: Separate the beneficiary count from the expenditure figure.
xs: Free **LLINs** covered **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) in **ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam** — option **(3)** is correct.
**19.25** is the cost in crore, not lakh people.
xa: Reported **23 Apr 2026**.
Other measures: **IRS**, source reduction.
**Agency districts** carry most malaria and scrub typhus.

114.s: As of 30 August 2026, Andhra Pradesh reported how many malaria cases, marking a rise of 27.9%?
114.x: AP reported 7,895 malaria cases up to 30 August 2026, a 27.9% rise, concentrated in tribal districts such as ASR, Polavaram and Vizianagaram. 7,119 and 7,871 are the full-year 2025 and 2024 figures; 1,475 is the 2026 dengue count.
114.tq: 2026 malaria 7,895 - up nearly 28%.
xs: AP reported **7,895** malaria cases up to **30 Aug 2026** (**+27.9%**) — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Hotspots: **ASR**, **Polavaram**, **Vizianagaram**.
**National Framework for Malaria Elimination**: malaria-free India by **2030**.

114.s: As per the September 2026 update for Andhra Pradesh, which pairing of 2026 case counts is correct?
114.x: In 2026 (to 30 Aug) AP reported 1,475 dengue cases (+4.6%) and 941 scrub typhus cases. 2,686 and 5,555 were dengue totals for 2025 and 2024.
114.tq: Dengue 1,475 > scrub typhus 941.
xs: In 2026: **dengue 1,475**, **scrub typhus 941** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps them; **2,686** and **5,555** are the dengue totals of **2025** and **2024**.
xa: Scrub typhus rising in **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Dengue mainly hits **platelets**; vector **Aedes aegypti**.

115.s: The term 'triple burden' in public health refers to the simultaneous presence of:
o: Maternal diseases, childhood diseases and old-age diseases
Communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries
115.x: The triple burden combines communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries such as road accidents and trauma.
115.tq: Use the defining components of the term rather than confusing it with the dual burden.
xs: The **triple burden** = **communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries** (road accidents, trauma) — option **(4)** is correct.
It **adds injuries** to the **dual burden** of CDs + NCDs.
xa: **Dual burden**: **rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases** (PYQ).
**Dual burden of malnutrition**: undernutrition + adult **overweight and obesity** (NFHS-6).
**DALY = YLL + YLD**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Non-communicable diseases account for 57% of all deaths in India.
2. Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in India.
3. The share of non-communicable diseases in deaths has declined from 61.8% in 2016 to 37.9% in 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the trend: the recorded share was 37.9% in 1990 and 61.8% in 2016 in the cited study.
115.tq: Check the direction of the numerical trend before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NCDs cause 57% of all deaths** (ES **2025-26**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **cardiovascular diseases** are India's leading cause.
Statement 3 reverses the trend: NCD share **rose** from **37.9% in 1990** to **61.8% in 2016** (Lancet study).
xa: World's single biggest killer: **ischaemic heart disease** (WHO).
Data: **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**.
⚠ Older notes give NCD share as **">60%"**.

115.s: Dual burden of malnutrition means the coexistence of:
o: Undernutrition with adult overweight and obesity
115.x: The dual burden of malnutrition refers to undernutrition existing alongside adult overweight and obesity.
115.tq: Distinguish the nutritional dual burden from the public-health dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases.
xs: **Dual burden of malnutrition** = **undernutrition with adult overweight and obesity** (NFHS-6) — option **(3)** is correct.
It is distinct from the **dual burden of disease** (infectious + NCDs).
xa: NFHS-5 (**2019-21**): **24% of women** and **23% of men** overweight/obese.
**Triple burden** adds **injuries** to CDs + NCDs.
**Obesity** results from **excess energy intake** + low physical activity.

115.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the leading causes of death in India and in the world?
o: Tuberculosis leads in India, while dengue is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cardiovascular diseases lead in India, while ischaemic heart disease is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cancer leads in India, while cardiovascular disease is absent from the global ranking.
Injuries lead in India, while chronic respiratory disease is the single biggest global killer.
115.x: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in India, while WHO estimates identify ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer.
115.tq: Keep the country-level and global-level comparisons separate before matching the two answers.
xs: **Cardiovascular diseases lead in India**, while **ischaemic heart disease** is the **world's single biggest killer** — option **(2)** is correct.
TB, cancer and injuries are not India's leading cause in the notes; dengue is not the global top killer.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths in India (ES **2025-26**).
"**Big four**" NCDs: **cardiovascular**, **cancers**, **chronic respiratory**, **diabetes**.
India's probability of dying from an NCD **rose** (**2001-2019**).

115.s: The India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative is associated with which combination of institutions and study?
o: ICMR, PHFI and IHME; Global Burden of Disease study
WHO, UNICEF and FAO; World Health Survey
NCDC, FSSAI and NITI Aayog; National Family Health Survey
ICMR, ISRO and DRDO; Census of India
115.x: The estimates are produced through the ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative, which forms part of the Global Burden of Disease study.
115.tq: Match the institutional group with the named study rather than with a nearby health survey.
xs: Data come from the **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**, part of the **Global Burden of Disease study** — option **(1)**.
WHO/UNICEF, NCDC/FSSAI/NITI and ISRO/DRDO are not its partners.
xa: **DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) is the burden metric.
**NFHS-5** gives overweight/obesity data.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding non-communicable disease mortality in India:
1. The probability of dying from an NCD rose in India between 2001 and 2019.
2. The rise was especially noted among women over 40 and men over 55.
3. Most countries reduced NCD deaths during the same period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: most countries reduced NCD deaths, whereas India's probability of dying from an NCD rose, particularly in the specified age-sex groups.
115.tq: Compare the general international trend with India's contrasting trend and retain all supported statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
**Most countries cut NCD deaths** in **2001-2019**, but **India's probability of dying from an NCD rose** (Lancet).
The rise was especially among **women over 40** and **men over 55**.
xa: **Cardiovascular diseases** = India's leading cause.
SDG 3: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

115.s: The 'dual burden of disease' in India refers to:
o: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same household
High maternal mortality alongside high infant mortality
Simultaneous rise of injuries and mental illness
115.x: Dual burden (PYQ answer) means persistent communicable diseases such as TB, malaria and dengue coexisting with rising NCDs. Undernutrition with obesity is the dual burden of malnutrition; adding injuries gives the triple burden; the other option is not the term.
115.tq: Dual = CDs + NCDs; triple adds injuries.
xs: The **dual burden of disease** = **rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases** (PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
Persistent CDs (**TB, malaria, dengue**, vector-borne) coexist with rising **NCDs**.
**Undernutrition + obesity** is the **dual burden of malnutrition**; adding **injuries** makes the **triple burden**.
xa: India's path: a **"linear shift"** from infectious diseases to NCDs.
Health systems must shift from **curative care to screening and prevention**.

115.s:
Arrange the following stages of epidemiological transition in the correct chronological order:
A. Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases
B. Age of Pestilence and Famine
C. Age of Receding Pandemics
115.x: Omran's sequence proceeds from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to the Age of Receding Pandemics and then to the Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.
115.tq: Identify the initial high-infection stage and the final NCD-dominant stage, then place the intermediate stage.
xs: **Omran**'s order: **Pestilence and Famine → Receding Pandemics → Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases** (B, C, A) — option **(1)**.
Stage 1: deaths from infections and famine; stage 2: infections fall; stage 3: **NCDs dominate**.
xa: Receding Pandemics: improved **sanitation and vaccination**.
India's path: **"linear shift"** to NCDs.
**NCDs** now cause **57%** of deaths.

115.s: Which stage of epidemiological transition is characterised by declining infectious deaths due to improvements in sanitation and vaccination?
o: Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases
115.x: In the Age of Receding Pandemics, infectious deaths decline as sanitation and vaccination improve.
115.tq: Associate the stage with its defining health pattern rather than its name alone.
xs: In the **Age of Receding Pandemics**, infectious deaths fall as **sanitation and vaccination improve** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Pestilence and Famine** has high infection deaths; **Degenerative and Man-Made** is NCD-dominated; "Nutritional Transition" is not an Omran stage here.
xa: Model by **Omran**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is undergoing a linear shift from infectious diseases to non-communicable diseases.
2. Life expectancy in India rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023.
3. Maternal mortality ratio has fallen by 86% since 1990.
4. Under-five mortality rate has fallen by 78% since 1990.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All four statements correctly describe the epidemiological and mortality transition reported for India.
115.tq: Check each numerical and trend statement independently before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
India shows a **"linear shift"** from infections to NCDs; life expectancy **49.7 (1973) → 70.3 (2023)**.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths.
**Cardiovascular diseases** lead in India.
Omran's third stage: **Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases**.

115.s: Which one of the following is NOT a communicable disease?
115.x: Hypertension is a non-communicable lifestyle-related disease. Chikungunya, typhoid and Nipah are communicable diseases.
115.tq: Classify each option by whether it is caused by a transmissible pathogen.
xs: **Hypertension** is a lifestyle **NCD**, not communicable — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Chikungunya**, **typhoid** and **Nipah** are communicable (pathogen-caused).
xa: Other NCDs: **diabetes, obesity, heart disease, stroke, cancer, COPD**.
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for **hypertension** and **diabetes**.
**Malaria is NOT a lifestyle disease** (PYQ).

115.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of the four major non-communicable disease groups?
o: Cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes
115.x: The four major NCD groups are cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes.
115.tq: Look for a set in which every item belongs to the same classification, not merely one or two items.
xs: The **"big four" NCDs**: **cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other sets mix in communicable diseases like **malaria, typhoid, dengue, TB, cholera, chikungunya, Nipah**.
xa: **Cardiovascular diseases** lead in India.
Risk factors: unhealthy diet, **physical inactivity, tobacco, alcohol**.
**NP-NCD** screens everyone over **30**.

115.s: Meningococcal meningitis is primarily transmitted through:
o: Respiratory droplets from person to person
115.x: Meningococcal meningitis spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets. Vomiting and neck stiffness are among its symptoms.
115.tq: Separate a respiratory-droplet infection from mosquito-borne diseases by identifying the mode of transmission.
xs: **Meningococcal meningitis** spreads **person to person via respiratory droplets**, **not mosquitoes** — option **(3)** is correct.
Symptoms: **vomiting**, **neck stiffness**.
xa: **Aedes** spreads **dengue, chikungunya, Zika**; **Culex** spreads **JE**.
**H1N1** spike in **Aug 2026**.
ICMR wastewater surveillance: **5 to 50** cities.

115.s: Which one of the following is NOT a lifestyle disease?
115.x: Malaria is a communicable disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by mosquitoes, so it is not a lifestyle disease (PYQ). Diabetes, hypertension and obesity are lifestyle-related NCDs.
115.tq: Odd one out: malaria (pathogen-caused).
xs: **Malaria** is a communicable, pathogen-caused disease — **NOT a lifestyle disease** (PYQ) — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Diabetes**, **hypertension** and **obesity** are lifestyle NCDs.
xa: ICMR's malaria initiative: **MERA**.
Main NCD risk factors: diet, **physical inactivity**, **tobacco**, **alcohol**.
**Obesity**: excess energy intake + low physical activity.

115.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the ICMR initiatives associated with tuberculosis and malaria respectively?
o: India TB Research Consortium and MERA
MERA and India TB Research Consortium
NCDC and India TB Research Consortium
115.x: The India TB Research Consortium is associated with tuberculosis, while MERA is the ICMR initiative associated with malaria.
115.tq: Use the disease-specific association and beware of reversing the two initiatives.
xs: ICMR's **India TB Research Consortium** (TB) and **MERA** (malaria) — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses them; **PHEOC** is NCDC's emergency centre, and **NCDC** is not an ICMR initiative.
xa: The **national TB prevalence survey** covers **all states and UTs**.
**ICMR wastewater surveillance** (**2026**) tracks **10** viruses + **AMR**.
**NCDC's PHEOC** activated **13 Jan 2026**.

115.s: A national tuberculosis prevalence survey in India is notable because it covers:
o: All States but not Union Territories
115.x: The national TB prevalence survey covers all States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Watch for restrictive words such as 'only' and distinguish complete national coverage from partial coverage.
xs: The **national TB prevalence survey** covers **all States and UTs** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is not limited to high-burden districts or cities, and includes UTs.
xa: ICMR's TB initiative: **India TB Research Consortium**.
TB is a persistent CD within the **dual burden**.
ICMR's malaria initiative: **MERA**.

115.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Dengue — Aedes mosquito
2. Chikungunya — Aedes mosquito
3. Zika — Aedes mosquito
4. Japanese encephalitis — Culex mosquito
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
115.x: Dengue, chikungunya and Zika are carried by Aedes mosquitoes, whereas Japanese encephalitis is carried by Culex mosquitoes.
115.tq: Start with the repeated Aedes association and verify the contrasting Culex pair.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
**Dengue, chikungunya and Zika** are spread by **Aedes**; **JE** by **Culex**.
xa: **Meningococcal meningitis** spreads by **respiratory droplets**, not mosquitoes.
AP **2025**: dengue **2,686** cases, **5** deaths; AES/JE **146** cases, **2** deaths.
**Malaria is NOT a lifestyle disease**.

115.s: Which one of the following statements regarding infectious disease surveillance in India is correct?
o: NCDC wastewater surveillance covers 10 cities and excludes antimicrobial resistance.
ICMR wastewater surveillance declined from 50 to 5 cities and tracks only one virus.
ICMR wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities and tracks 10 viruses, along with antimicrobial resistance.
The programme tracks only dengue and chikungunya and does not include avian influenza.
115.x: ICMR's wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities, tracks 10 viruses including avian influenza, and also monitors antimicrobial resistance.
115.tq: Check the direction of expansion, the number of cities and the scope of surveillance together.
xs: **ICMR wastewater surveillance** (**2026**) expanded **from 5 to 50 cities**, tracks **10 viruses** incl. **avian influenza**, plus **AMR** — option **(3)**.
It is ICMR's (not NCDC's), it **expanded** (not declined), and it includes **avian influenza**.
xa: **NCDC's PHEOC** activated (**13 Jan 2026**).
**India TB Research Consortium** and **MERA** are other ICMR initiatives.

115.s: Which agency's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre was activated following the two Nipah cases reported in January 2026?
115.x: The NCDC's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, or PHEOC, was activated in response to the reported Nipah cases.
115.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to distinguish the public-health response authority.
xs: **NCDC**'s **Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC)** was activated (**13 Jan 2026**) — option **(4)** is correct.
FSSAI, ICMR and WHO run no PHEOC in the notes.
xa: **Nipah** is a communicable disease.
**H1N1** spike in **Aug 2026**.
**ICMR** runs wastewater surveillance in **50** cities.

115.s: According to NFHS-5 data for 2019–21, which of the following statements is correct regarding overweight or obesity?
o: 24% of women and 23% of men were overweight or obese.
34% of women and 33% of men were overweight or obese.
23% of women and 24% of men were overweight or obese.
14% of women and 13% of men were overweight or obese.
115.x: NFHS-5 reported overweight or obesity among 24% of women and 23% of men for 2019–21.
115.tq: Read the sex-wise figures carefully; the close reversal is the intended trap.
xs: **NFHS-5 (2019-21)**: **24% of women** and **23% of men** overweight/obese — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) swaps the sexes; the other figures are wrong.
xa: **Dual burden of malnutrition**: undernutrition + overweight/obesity (NFHS-6).
**Sedentary lifestyle** and **energy-dense foods** → degenerative diseases (PYQ).
Programmes: **Eat Right India**, **Fit India**.

115.s: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has capped trans fat in fats and oils at:
115.x: FSSAI has capped trans fat in fats and oils at 2%.
115.tq: Use the precise regulatory limit rather than the broader dietary-risk information.
xs: **FSSAI** caps **trans fat** at **≤2%** in fats and oils — option **(2)** is correct.
The cap targets trans fats because excess intake **raises NCD risk** (PYQ).
xa: **Bakery products** are rich in **hydrogenated fats** containing trans fats.
Programmes: **Eat Right India**, **Fit India** (**18 May 2026**).
The **UNGA declaration** seeks stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats** and **e-cigarettes**.

115.s:
The United Nations General Assembly declaration on non-communicable diseases and mental health includes which of the following newer areas or determinants?
1. Oral health and lung health
2. Childhood cancer
3. Air pollution and lead
4. Digital harms such as screen time
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: The declaration covers oral and lung health, childhood cancer, air pollution, lead and digital harms such as screen time. It also calls for stronger regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.
115.tq: When all listed items belong to the stated expansion of scope, select the complete combination.
xs: All four are in the **UNGA declaration on NCDs and mental health** — option **(4)** (**1, 2, 3 and 4**).
New areas: **oral health, lung health, childhood cancer**; new determinants: **air pollution, lead**.
For the **first time**: **digital harms** (screen time).
xa: Targets for **2030**.
Stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes**.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bakery products are often rich in hydrogenated fats containing trans fats.
2. Excess intake of trans fats raises the risk of non-communicable diseases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Both statements are correct (PYQ): bakery products use hydrogenated fats containing trans fats, and excess trans fats raise NCD risk, which is why FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% in fats and oils. '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement; 'Neither' rejects both.
115.tq: Trans fats: bakery + NCD risk, both true.
xs: Both are correct — option **(3)** (PYQ).
1: **Bakery products** are rich in **hydrogenated fats containing trans fats**.
2: Excess trans fats **raise the risk of NCDs**.
xa: **FSSAI** caps trans fat at **≤2%** in fats and oils.
Another PYQ: **sedentary lifestyle** + **energy-dense foods** → degenerative diseases (both correct).
**Eat Right India** promotes healthy eating.

115.s:
Which of the following are main risk factors for lifestyle (non-communicable) diseases?
1. Unhealthy diet
2. Physical inactivity
3. Tobacco use
4. Alcohol use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: All four are main NCD risk factors (UPSC), along with urbanisation and ageing. Every other option leaves out at least one listed risk factor.
115.tq: NCD risks: diet, inactivity, tobacco, alcohol.
xs: All four — **unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco, alcohol** — are main NCD risk factors (UPSC) — option **(4)**.
Each other option leaves out at least one listed factor.
xa: Also **urbanisation** and **ageing**.
NFHS-5: **24%** women, **23%** men overweight/obese.
Uddanam survey: tobacco use **38.8%**, alcohol use **23.7%**.

115.s: According to the Global Cancer Observatory projection, the number of cancer cases in India is expected to increase from approximately 1.41 million in 2022 to what number by 2045?
115.x: The projected number of cancer cases is expected to rise from 1.41 million in 2022 to 2.46 million in 2045.
115.tq: Use the precise projected figure rather than estimating from the percentage increase.
xs: Cancer cases are projected to rise from **1.41 million (2022)** to **2.46 million (2045)** — option **(2)** is correct.
That is **about 74%** more (Global Cancer Observatory).
xa: Cancer is **not notifiable nationally**; **17 states** have made it notifiable.
Registries cover only **10-16%** of people.
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for **oral, breast and cervical cancer**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cancer notification in India:
1. Cancer is not nationally notifiable in India.
2. Seventeen States have made cancer a notifiable disease.
3. Telangana was the most recent State to make cancer notifiable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: All three statements are correct: cancer is not nationally notifiable, 17 States have notified it, and Telangana was the most recent State to do so.
115.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the distinction between national and State-level notification.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
Cancer is **not notifiable nationally**; **17 states** made it notifiable; **Telangana** was the **most recent** (**4 Jul 2026**).
xa: Registries cover only **10-16%** of people.
**UNGA** declaration adds **childhood cancer** as a new area.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD):
1. It was formerly known as NPCDCS.
2. It runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and Community Health Centres.
3. It screens everyone above 40 years of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is correct: NP-NCD was formerly NPCDCS (2010). Statement 2 is correct: NCD clinics are run at district hospitals and CHCs. Statement 3 is wrong: screening covers everyone over 30, not 40. So '1 and 2 only'; '2 only' omits a true statement, and the options with 3 include the wrong age.
115.tq: NP-NCD: ex-NPCDCS, clinics at DH/CHC, screening 30+.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **NP-NCD** was **formerly NPCDCS** (**2010**) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 2 is correct: it runs **NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **everyone over 30** is screened, not 40.
xa: Funding **60:40** (**90:10** for NE and hilly states).
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for hypertension, diabetes, cancers.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

115.s:
Consider the following statements about the funding pattern of NP-NCD:
1. The usual Centre-State funding ratio is 60:40.
2. The funding ratio for North-Eastern and hilly States is 90:10.
3. The 90:10 ratio applies uniformly to all States and Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
115.x: The usual funding ratio is 60:40, while North-Eastern and hilly States receive funding in the ratio of 90:10. The latter ratio does not apply uniformly to all States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Reject the overgeneralised statement by separating the normal ratio from the special-category ratio.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: NP-NCD funding is **60:40** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
Statement 2 is correct: **90:10** for **NE and hilly states**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **90:10** is not uniform for all States/UTs.
xa: NP-NCD was formerly **NPCDCS (2010)**.
Screens everyone over **30**.
NCD clinics at **district hospitals** and **CHCs**.

115.s:
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs screen beneficiaries for which of the following conditions?
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes
3. Oral cancer
4. Breast and cervical cancers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
115.x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs screen for hypertension, diabetes, and oral, breast and cervical cancers.
115.tq: Use the inclusive option when all listed screening services belong to the same programme.
xs: **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for **hypertension, diabetes, oral, breast and cervical cancer** — all four, option **(4)**.
Options (1)-(3) each leave out a listed condition.
xa: **NP-NCD** screens everyone over **30**.
Cancer notifiable in **17 states**.
Health system must move from **curative care to screening and prevention**.

115.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the relevant SDG 3 health target?
o: Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-half
Premature NCD deaths — reduce by one-third
115.x: SDG 3 includes the target of reducing premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by one-third. It also promotes mental health and seeks to halve road-traffic deaths.
115.tq: Discriminate between the different numerical targets under the same goal.
xs: **SDG 3**: cut **premature NCD deaths by one-third** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Road-traffic deaths** are to be **halved** (not cut by one-third); NCD deaths not halved; mental health is to be **promoted**.
xa: **Tele-MANAS**: **24x7** tele-mental-health support.
**Triple burden** includes **injuries** (road accidents).
**UNGA declaration** sets **2030** targets.

115.s: Tele-MANAS, available in all 36 States and Union Territories, provides:
o: Online registration of every UIP vaccination
115.x: Tele-MANAS gives round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and UTs. Vaccination registration is U-WIN; cancer screening and trauma surgery are not its role.
115.tq: Tele-MANAS = 24x7 mental-health helpline.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** gives **24x7 tele-mental-health support** in all **36** States/UTs (**12 Jun 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
Vaccination registration is **U-WIN**; cancer screening is at **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.
xa: **SDG 3** promotes **mental health**.
**UNGA declaration on NCDs and mental health**: first time **digital harms**.
**NP-NCD** runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs.

115.s: Which initiative provides 24×7 tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and Union Territories?
115.x: Tele-MANAS provides round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and Union Territories.
115.tq: Link the service function—tele-mental health—with the correct national initiative.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** gives **24x7 tele-mental-health support** in all **36** States/UTs — option **(3)** is correct.
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for NCDs; **IDSP** is surveillance; **NP-NCD** runs NCD clinics.
xa: Reported **12 Jun 2026**.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third** + promote mental health.
UNGA declaration targets **digital harms** (screen time).

115.s: Which one of the following public-health measures was undertaken in Andhra Pradesh in relation to scrub typhus?
o: A ban on all poultry products was imposed.
A national TB prevalence survey was discontinued.
A Culex eradication mission was launched.
115.x: Andhra Pradesh set up task forces for scrub typhus under the cited state health measures.
115.tq: Identify the exact administrative response and reject measures not stated for the disease.
xs: AP **set up task forces** for **scrub typhus** — option **(2)** is correct.
No poultry ban, TB-survey halt or Culex mission is reported.
xa: AP **2025**: malaria **7,119** cases, **8** deaths; dengue **2,686**, **5** deaths.
AES/JE **146** cases, **2** deaths; chikungunya **52** cases, **0** deaths.
Source: **APSES 2025-26**.

115.s: Uddanam, located in which district of Andhra Pradesh, is associated with chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu)?
115.x: Uddanam is in Srikakulam district and is associated with CKDu. Palasa is the location of the kidney centre, while Mangalagiri is the location of AIIMS.
115.tq: Separate the geographical region from the nearby institutions associated with it.
xs: **Uddanam** is in **Srikakulam** district — known for **CKDu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vizianagaram** has the diabetic-foot clinic; **Mangalagiri** has AIIMS; **Palasa** has the kidney centre.
xa: Interim report: high kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal** (**13 Sep 2026**).
Samples tested for **pesticides/heavy metals** with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad**.
**AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs CKDu screening camps.

115.s:
With reference to the investigation into chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu) in Uddanam, consider the following statements:
1. Soil, water, blood and urine samples are being tested for viruses and protozoa.
2. The testing is being done with CSIR-IICT, Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
115.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, not viruses and protozoa. Statement 2 is correct: testing is with CSIR-IICT Hyderabad. So '2 only'; '1 only' and 'Both' accept the wrong statement, and 'Neither' rejects the true one.
115.tq: Uddanam CKDu: pesticides/heavy metals, CSIR-IICT Hyderabad.
xs: Statement 2 is correct: testing is with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad** — so **2 only**, option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: soil, water, blood and urine are tested for **pesticides/heavy metals**, not viruses and protozoa.
xa: CKDu = **chronic kidney disease of unknown cause**.
High kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal**.
Among those covered: tobacco **38.8%**, alcohol **23.7%**.

115.s: Which institution conducts CKDu screening camps in the Uddanam region?
115.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri conducts screening camps for chronic kidney disease of unknown cause in the Uddanam region.
115.tq: Distinguish the institution conducting field screening from the laboratory involved in testing.
