ABDM is **consent-based**, so sharing without consent is wrong; it does not replace doctors or make insurance compulsory.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID; **90 crore+** accounts.
ABDM is **interoperable** and built on **Digital Public Infrastructure**.
Telemedicine via **eSanjeevani** uses a Clinical Decision Support System.

120.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan — Sanitation and hygiene for disease prevention
2. Fit India Movement — Building fitness into daily life
3. Eat Right India — Safe, healthy and sustainable diets
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
120.x: All three pairs are correctly matched: Swachh Bharat focuses on sanitation, Fit India on daily fitness, and Eat Right India on safe, healthy and sustainable diets.
120.tq: Match each campaign with its precise objective before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** (**2014**) → sanitation and hygiene for disease prevention.
**Fit India** (**2019**) → fitness in daily life; **Eat Right India** (**FSSAI**, **2018**) → safe, healthy, sustainable diets.
xa: Eat Right India + Fit India together aim to **cut NCD deaths**.
FSSAI was created under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**.
Fit India fights **sedentary lifestyles**.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
120.x: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched in 2014, not 2018. Fit India is associated with 2019 and Eat Right India with 2018.
120.tq: Find the option that swaps the year of a campaign with another campaign’s year.
xs: **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan — 2018** is wrong — option **(3)**; it was launched in **2014**.
**Fit India** — **2019** and **Eat Right India** — **2018** are correct.
xa: Eat Right India is run by **FSSAI**, set up under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**.
Swachh Bharat targets **sanitation and hygiene** for disease prevention.
⚠ **2018** is also the launch year of **Anaemia Mukt Bharat**.

120.s: Eat Right India was launched by which organisation, itself established under which legislation?
o: FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
WHO under the National Health Policy, 2017
NITI Aayog under the Disaster Management Act, 2005
ICMR under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956
120.x: Eat Right India is an initiative of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
120.tq: Use the institution-and-legislation pairing to avoid swapping the responsible body with a health ministry or research body.
xs: **Eat Right India** is an **FSSAI** initiative; FSSAI was created under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006** — option **(1)**.
**ICMR** is a research body (**1911** as IRFA); **WHO** is headquartered at **Geneva**.
xa: Eat Right India aims at **safe, healthy, sustainable diets**.
With **Fit India** (**2019**), it aims to cut **NCD deaths**.
Eat Right India: **2018**.

120.s: The Eat Right India and Fit India campaigns together seek to reduce deaths due to:
120.x: Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by non-communicable diseases through healthier diets and increased physical activity.
120.tq: Infer the common public-health outcome from the two campaigns’ complementary objectives.
xs: Eat Right India and Fit India together aim to cut **non-communicable disease (NCD)** deaths — option **(1)**.
Eat Right India promotes healthy diets; **Fit India** fights **sedentary lifestyles**.
xa: Fit India: **2019**; Eat Right India: **2018** (FSSAI).
**India Hypertension Control Initiative** is an ICMR consortium.
AAMs screen for NCDs such as **hypertension** and **diabetes**.

120.s: The Indian Research Fund Association, the predecessor of the Indian Council of Medical Research, was established in:
120.x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.
120.tq: Distinguish the founding year from the later renaming year.
xs: The **Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA)** was set up in **1911** — option **(2)**.
It was renamed **ICMR** in **1949**; **1948** is the year **WHO** was founded.
xa: ICMR is among the world's **oldest medical research bodies**.
ICMR consortia: **MERA India** (malaria), **India TB Research Consortium**, **India Hypertension Control Initiative**.
The **Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat** reduces import dependence.

120.s: Which of the following is NOT a disease consortium or initiative listed in connection with the ICMR?
120.x: MERA India, the India TB Research Consortium and the India Hypertension Control Initiative are listed ICMR-related initiatives; India Food Security Consortium is not.
120.tq: Find the invented-looking member by comparing every option with the named ICMR initiatives.
xs: **India Food Security Consortium** is not an ICMR consortium — option **(4)**.
**MERA India** (malaria), the **India TB Research Consortium** and the **India Hypertension Control Initiative** are ICMR consortia.
xa: Others: **Mission Delhi**, **India Cancer Research Consortium**, **Stroke Network**.
ICMR began in **1911** as IRFA; renamed **1949**.
**Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat**: reduces import dependence.

120.s: MERA India, among the ICMR disease consortia, is associated with:
120.x: MERA India is the ICMR consortium associated with malaria.
120.tq: Test the exact disease association of a similarly structured consortium name.
xs: **MERA India** is ICMR's **malaria** consortium — option **(1)**.
Tuberculosis = **India TB Research Consortium**; hypertension = **India Hypertension Control Initiative**; cancer = **India Cancer Research Consortium**.
xa: ICMR also runs **Mission Delhi** and a **Stroke Network**.
ICMR began as **IRFA** in **1911**.
**NIKSHAY** is the TB patient management platform.

120.s: The Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat associated with ICMR seeks primarily to:
o: Increase dependence on imported medical devices
Reduce import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics
Replace all diagnostic laboratories with mobile units
120.x: The Secretariat aims to reduce India’s import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics.
120.tq: Identify the policy purpose from the stated institutional function rather than the institution’s name alone.
xs: The **Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat** aims to **reduce import dependence** — option **(3)**.
It does not regulate treaties or replace labs with mobile units.
xa: ICMR began in **1911** as **IRFA**; renamed ICMR in **1949**.
ICMR consortia: **MERA India**, **India TB Research Consortium**, **India Hypertension Control Initiative**.
PM-ABHIM builds **IPHLs** and **BSL-3 labs**.

120.s: World Health Day is observed on 7 April every year because on that date in 1948:
o: the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at Geneva
the Alma-Ata Declaration on primary health care was adopted
the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at New York
smallpox was declared eradicated by the World Health Assembly
120.x: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered at Geneva, so World Health Day falls on 7 April. WHO's headquarters is not New York; the Alma-Ata Declaration and the eradication of smallpox are later events and not linked to 7 April 1948.
120.tq: WHO: Geneva, 7 April 1948 = World Health Day.
xs: **WHO** was founded on **7 April 1948**, headquartered at **Geneva** — option **(1)**.
Hence **World Health Day is 7 April**; WHO's headquarters is not New York.
xa: ⚠ **1949** is when IRFA was renamed **ICMR**.
ICMR's origin: **IRFA**, **1911**.
**One of the oldest** medical research bodies is ICMR.

120.s: The Sanjeevani digital health programme of Andhra Pradesh, commencing in August 2026, is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Replacement of all public hospitals by private hospitals
Universal distribution of fortified food through fair-price shops
Free insurance cover of ₹5 lakh for every citizen
A digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
120.x: Sanjeevani aims to create a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Identify the defining feature of the programme rather than confusing it with an insurance scheme.
xs: AP's **Sanjeevani** (from **Aug 2026**) gives a **digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen** — option **(4)**.
It does not privatise hospitals, distribute food or give a fixed insurance cover.
xa: It links PHCs, hospitals, labs, **e-Aushadhi**, **108**, **104**, telemedicine + **AI assistance**.
The **Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App** came in **Jul 2026**.
It makes AP an **ABDM-linked**, citizen-wide digital health state.

120.s:
Which of the following facilities and services are linked through the Sanjeevani digital health programme in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Primary Health Centres and hospitals
2. Laboratories and e-Aushadhi
3. 108 emergency services and 104 mobile medical units
4. Telemedicine and AI assistance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
120.x: Sanjeevani links PHCs, hospitals, laboratories, e-Aushadhi, 108 emergency services, 104 mobile medical units, telemedicine and AI assistance.
120.tq: Use the option containing all the listed components after checking each statement independently.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are linked — option **(4)**.
Sanjeevani links **PHCs, hospitals, labs, e-Aushadhi**, **108 emergency**, **104 mobile medical units**, **telemedicine + AI assistance**.
xa: It gives every citizen a **digital health profile + ABHA ID**.
Telemedicine is available in **all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** in AP (APPSC 2024 PYQ).
AP runs a **Free Diagnostics Initiative**.

120.s: On 13 September 2026, which of the following was inaugurated in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM?
o: 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
10 Health and Wellness Centres and 12 medical colleges
12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
120.x: Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda inaugurated 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM.
120.tq: Match the two numerical components precisely instead of reversing their order.
xs: **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories** were inaugurated — option **(2)**.
Union Health Minister **J.P. Nadda** opened them from **Vijayawada** on **13 Sep 2026**, costing **₹250 crore**.
⚠ Option (4) swaps the numbers.
xa: **PM-ABHIM** was launched on **25 Oct 2021** at **Varanasi**.
It funds critical care blocks, **IPHLs in all districts** and **BSL-3 labs**.

120.s: With reference to healthcare in Andhra Pradesh, which statement was marked valid in an APPSC 2024 question?
o: Telemedicine services are available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in the State
Telemedicine is available only at AIIMS Mangalagiri
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in the State provide no teleconsultation
Telemedicine is restricted to private hospitals empanelled under PM-JAY
120.x: Telemedicine is available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in AP (APPSC 2024 statement marked valid). It is not confined to AIIMS Mangalagiri or to empanelled private hospitals, and AAMs do provide teleconsultation.
120.tq: AP: telemedicine at every AAM.
xs: **Telemedicine is available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** in AP — option **(1)** (APPSC 2024 PYQ statement marked valid).
So telemedicine is not confined to one institution or to private hospitals, and AAMs do offer teleconsultation.
xa: **eSanjeevani** now has a **Clinical Decision Support System**.
AP's **Sanjeevani** programme (from **Aug 2026**) links telemedicine with PHCs, labs, **108** and **104**.
AAMs nationally: **1.73 lakh+** converted against a target of **1,50,000**.

120.s: Which statement best expresses the criticism that an insurance-led public health policy may face?
o: It eliminates the need for public hospitals.
It increases coverage but may not ensure access.
It increases access without increasing coverage.
120.x: The criticism is that insurance-led policies can expand coverage while failing to ensure actual access to health services.
120.tq: Distinguish the related but different concepts of coverage and access.
xs: An insurance-led public health policy **increases coverage but not access** — option **(3)** (24 Jun 2026).
Option (4) reverses the criticism.
xa: NHP 2017 was **assurance-based**, with comprehensive primary care.
Primary care meets **80-90%** of health needs.
⚠ The NHP 2017 spending target of **2.5% of GDP by 2025** was missed (**1.43%** in 2022-23).

120.s: As reported in June 2026, the number of ABHA accounts had crossed:
120.x: The reported figure was more than 90 crore ABHA accounts in June 2026.
120.tq: Use the scale of the reported figure and distinguish crore-level alternatives.
xs: ABHA accounts crossed **90 crore** in **Jun 2026** — option **(4)**.
ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID under **ABDM**.
xa: Earlier (Aug 2025): **79.91 crore** accounts, **67.19 crore** linked records.
**4.19 lakh** facilities on HFR; **6.8 lakh** professionals on HPR.
**NMC (Mar 2026)**: medical colleges must link ABHA IDs for all OPD/IPD/emergency patients.

120.s: The expenditure associated with the 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories inaugurated in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM was:
120.x: The infrastructure was inaugurated with an expenditure of ₹250 crore.
120.tq: Use a direct figure-based question to distinguish the stated allocation from nearby plausible amounts.
xs: The **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs** cost **₹250 crore** — option **(3)**.
They were inaugurated under **PM-ABHIM** by **J.P. Nadda** from **Vijayawada** (13 Sep 2026).
xa: PM-ABHIM's total outlay: **₹64,180 crore** (FY 2021-22 to 2025-26).
PM-ABHIM was launched on **25 Oct 2021**.
PM-ABHIM builds **health infrastructure for pandemics**.

120.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Andhra Pradesh Sanjeevani programme?
o: It is restricted to hospitalised patients in urban areas.
It is an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health programme.
It deals exclusively with sanitation and hygiene.
It is limited to maintaining paper-based medical records.
120.x: Sanjeevani makes Andhra Pradesh an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health state through digital profiles, ABHA IDs and connected health services.
120.tq: Apply the programme’s stated scope to distinguish a citizen-wide digital system from a narrow sectoral service.
xs: **Sanjeevani** makes AP an **ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health** state — option **(2)**.
It gives every citizen a **digital health profile + ABHA ID** — not paper records, sanitation or urban inpatients only.
xa: It links PHCs, hospitals, labs, **e-Aushadhi**, **108**, **104**, telemedicine + **AI assistance**.
The **Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App** came in **Jul 2026**.
ABDM is run by the **National Health Authority** (launched **September 2021**).

120.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Indian Research Fund Association and ICMR?
o: ICMR was renamed as the Indian Research Fund Association in 1911.
The Indian Research Fund Association was renamed ICMR in 2017.
The Indian Research Fund Association was renamed ICMR in 1949.
Both were separate organisations established simultaneously in 1949.
120.x: The Indian Research Fund Association, established in 1911, was renamed the Indian Council of Medical Research in 1949.
120.tq: Discriminate between an organisation’s original name and its later institutional name.
xs: The **Indian Research Fund Association** (**1911**) was **renamed ICMR in 1949** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses the names; **2017** is the NHP year.
xa: ICMR is among the world's **oldest medical research bodies**.
ICMR consortia: **MERA India** (malaria), **India TB Research Consortium**, **India Hypertension Control Initiative**.
⚠ **WHO** was founded on **7 April 1948** — a year before the renaming.

121.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Pulse Polio programme launched
B. India became free of smallpox
C. Last wild polio case in Howrah
D. WHO South-East Asia Region certified polio-free
121.x: India became free of smallpox in 1977, Pulse Polio was launched in 1995, the last wild polio case occurred in January 2011, and the region was certified polio-free in 2014.
121.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle events.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**Smallpox-free 1977** → **Pulse Polio 1995** → **last wild polio case, Howrah, Jan 2011** → **WHO SEAR polio-free 27 Mar 2014**.
xa: **Guinea worm** certified free: **2000**.
**Maternal and neonatal tetanus** eliminated: **2015**; **Yaws** declared free: **2016**.
Switch from trivalent to **bivalent OPV**: **Apr 2016**.

121.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
121.x: Guinea worm was certified free in 2000. Pulse Polio was launched in 1995, yaws was declared free in 2016, and maternal and neonatal tetanus was eliminated in 2015.
121.tq: Check each disease–year pair against the milestone table.
xs: **Guinea worm — certified free in 2000** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Yaws** was declared free in **2016**; **Pulse Polio** launched in **1995**; **maternal and neonatal tetanus** eliminated in **2015**.
xa: India became **smallpox-free** in **1977**.
⚠ **2014** is when **WHO SEAR** was certified polio-free (**27 Mar 2014**).
Yaws freedom came under the **Yaws Eradication Programme**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about polio milestones:
1. India's last wild polio case was reported from Howrah, West Bengal, in January 2011.
2. The WHO South-East Asia Region was certified polio-free on 27 March 2014.
3. India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in April 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: last wild case, Howrah, January 2011. Statement 2 is correct: SEAR certified polio-free on 27 March 2014. Statement 3 is wrong: the tOPV-to-bOPV switch was in April 2016. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: Polio: 1995 Pulse Polio, 2011 last case, 2014 certified, 2016 bOPV switch.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: last wild polio case at **Howrah, WB**, **Jan 2011**.
Statement 2 correct: **WHO SEAR** certified polio-free on **27 Mar 2014**.
Statement 3 wrong: the switch to **bivalent OPV** was in **Apr 2016**.
xa: **Pulse Polio** was launched in **1995**.
**Yaws** was declared free in **2016**; **MNT** eliminated in **2015**.

121.s: The national target for tuberculosis elimination in India is:
121.x: India’s national target for TB elimination is 2025, five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
121.tq: Compare the national target with the later SDG target.
xs: India's national TB elimination target is **2025** — option **(2)**.
That is **five years ahead** of the SDG target of **2030**.
xa: Programme: **NTEP** — free diagnosis + treatment.
TB incidence fell **21%** and mortality **28%** (2015-2024).
⚠ **2030** is the target for **malaria**; **2027** for lymphatic filariasis; **2047** for sickle cell anaemia.

121.s: The programme associated with India’s national TB elimination target is:
121.x: The National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme, or NTEP, provides free diagnosis and treatment for TB.
121.tq: Match the disease programme with its official abbreviation.
xs: **NTEP** (National TB Elimination Programme) runs TB elimination with **free diagnosis + treatment** — option **(2)**.
**NLEP** is for leprosy; **NACP** for HIV/AIDS; **NVBDCP** for vector-borne diseases.
xa: **Ni-kshay** is the digital TB portal for notification and tracking.
**PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** (**Sept 2022**): **Ni-kshay Mitras** adopt patients.
Treatment coverage: **53% (2015) → 92% (2024)**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ni-kshay is a digital portal for TB notification and tracking.
2. Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT only to TB patients notified in the public sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ni-kshay is the digital TB notification and tracking portal. Statement 2 is wrong: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients, public and private. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: Watch 'only' - the DBT covers public and private patients.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Ni-kshay** is the **digital TB portal** for notification and tracking.
Statement 2 wrong: **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** gives nutritional **DBT to all notified TB patients — public and private**.
xa: **Ni-kshay Mitras** adopt patients under the **PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** (**Sept 2022**).
Dec 2025: **3.78 lakh+ Mitras**, **20 lakh+** patients, **45 lakh+** food baskets.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan:
1. It was launched in September 2022.
2. Ni-kshay Mitras adopt TB patients under the campaign.
3. The campaign is linked with food-basket support for patients.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: The campaign was launched in September 2022, uses Ni-kshay Mitras to adopt patients, and includes food-basket support.
121.tq: Check whether all three statements describe complementary parts of one campaign.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** began in **Sept 2022**; **Ni-kshay Mitras** adopt patients.
By **Dec 2025**: **3.78 lakh+ Mitras**, **20 lakh+ patients**, **45 lakh+ food baskets**.
xa: Campaign since **Dec 2024**: **20 crore+ screened**, **28 lakh+ diagnosed** (Aug 2026).
**Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** gives nutritional **DBT** to all notified TB patients.
National TB target: **2025**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about TB outcomes in India during 2015-2024:
1. TB incidence fell by 21%.
2. TB mortality fell by 21%.
3. Treatment coverage rose from 53% to 92%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: incidence fell 21%. Statement 2 is wrong: mortality fell 28%, not 21%. Statement 3 is correct: treatment coverage rose from 53% (2015) to 92% (2024). Hence '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: Incidence 21, mortality 28 - mortality fell more.
xs: **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: TB **incidence fell 21%** (2015-2024).
Statement 2 wrong: **mortality fell 28%**, not 21%.
Statement 3 correct: **treatment coverage 53% (2015) → 92% (2024)**.
xa: IYB gives coverage of **85%** in **2023**.
⚠ India TB Report 2022: notifications rose **19%** in 2021 over 2020.

121.s: According to the India TB Report 2022, TB notifications in 2021 compared with 2020:
121.x: The India TB Report 2022 recorded a 19% rise in notifications in 2021 over 2020 (APPSC 2022 PYQ). 'Fell by 19%' reverses the direction; 53% is the 2015 treatment-coverage figure; 28% is the fall in TB mortality during 2015-2024.
121.tq: TB Report 2022: notifications up 19%.
xs: Notifications **rose by 19%** in 2021 over 2020 — option **(1)** (**India TB Report 2022**, APPSC 2022 PYQ).
**53%** is the 2015 treatment coverage; **28%** is the fall in TB mortality (2015-2024).
xa: TB incidence fell **21%** (2015-2024).
**Himachal Pradesh** screens all indoor hospital patients for TB (intensified case finding).
**Ni-kshay** is the digital notification portal.

121.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers which period?
121.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers 2016–2030 and targets malaria elimination by 2030.
121.tq: Combine the official framework name with its exact period.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination** covers **2016-2030** — option **(3)**.
It targets **malaria elimination by 2030**.
xa: Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.
**MERA India** = Malaria Elimination Research Alliance India, led by **ICMR**.
⚠ **2021-26** is **NACP Phase V**.

121.s: Which of the following sets consists only of countries certified malaria-free by WHO among the countries listed?
121.x: Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.
121.tq: Use set comparison to eliminate a list containing an unlisted country.
xs: **Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste** are WHO-certified **malaria-free** — option **(1)**.
**Timor-Leste** is the most recent of the three (Jan 2026); **India** targets elimination only by **2030**.
xa: Only about **42%** of global malaria financing needs are met.
Malaria cases in India fell **80%** in **2015-2023**.
Vaccines: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** by GSK; **R21/Matrix-M** by Oxford, made by **Serum Institute**.

121.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the malaria vaccine with its developer or manufacturer?
o: RTS,S/AS01—GSK; R21/Matrix-M—University of Oxford and Serum Institute of India
RTS,S/AS01—Serum Institute of India; R21/Matrix-M—GSK only
121.x: RTS,S/AS01, also known as Mosquirix, is associated with GSK. R21/Matrix-M was developed by the University of Oxford and made by the Serum Institute of India.
121.tq: Start with the vaccine–organisation pair that is most distinctive.
xs: **RTS,S/AS01 — GSK**; **R21/Matrix-M — University of Oxford, made by Serum Institute of India** — option **(1)**.
RTS,S/AS01 is also called **Mosquirix**.
xa: India's National Framework for Malaria Elimination: **2016-2030**.
**MERA India** is ICMR-led.
⚠ **Cervavac** is Serum Institute's **HPV** vaccine, not a malaria vaccine.

121.s: Which of the following is NOT a tool under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for malaria control?
121.x: IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides and source reduction are listed malaria-control tools. Universal antibiotic prophylaxis is not one of them.
121.tq: Identify the non-vector-control measure among operational tools.
xs: **Universal antibiotic prophylaxis** is not an NVBDCP tool — option **(4)**.
NVBDCP tools: **IRS** (indoor residual spraying), **LLINs**, **larvivorous fish**, **bio-larvicides**, **source reduction**.
xa: NVBDCP elimination targets: **malaria, LF + kala-azar**.
NVBDCP handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue, chikungunya** (PYQ key).
Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.

121.s: MERA India is associated with which of the following?
o: National Dengue Eradication and Research Authority
Malaria Emergency Response Administration of WHO
121.x: MERA India stands for the ICMR-led Malaria Elimination Research Alliance.
121.tq: Break the acronym into its institutional and subject components.
xs: **MERA India** = **Malaria Elimination Research Alliance** India, **led by ICMR** — option **(3)**.
It is not a WHO, dengue or environment body.
xa: Malaria elimination target: **2030** (framework **2016-2030**).
Tools: **IRS, LLINs**, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides.
WHO-certified malaria-free: **Sri Lanka, China, Timor-Leste**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the National AIDS Control Programme (NACP):
1. It was launched in 1992.
2. It is led by NACO under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
3. NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at a 50% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NACP began in 1992 and is led by NACO (MoHFW). Statement 3 is wrong: Phase V (2021-26) aims at an 80% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **NACP** launched in **1992**.
Statement 2 correct: it is led by **NACO** (MoHFW).
Statement 3 wrong: **Phase V (2021-26)** aims at an **80% cut** in new infections and AIDS deaths.
xa: **HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars discrimination.

121.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.

List-I (NACP Phase)
a. Phase I
b. Phase II
c. Phase III
d. Phase IV

List-II (Period)
i. 2007–2012
ii. 1992–1999
iii. 2012–2017, extended to 2021
iv. 1999–2006
121.x: Phase I was 1992–1999, Phase II 1999–2006, Phase III 2007–2012 and Phase IV 2012–2017, later extended to 2021.
121.tq: Start from the sure chronological pair and eliminate codes.
xs: The correct code is **a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii** — option **(1)**.
xa: **Phase V**: **2021-26**, aiming at an **80% cut** in new infections and AIDS deaths.
NACP is led by **NACO** under MoHFW.
Goal: end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding HIV-related services:
1. VCTC stands for Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre.
2. Antiretroviral therapy is available free for life at ART centres.
3. ICTCs provide compulsory testing without counselling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: VCTC means Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre, and free lifelong ART is provided at ART centres. ICTC services are voluntary and include counselling, so statement 3 is false.
121.tq: Find the statement that reverses the voluntary nature of a service.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **VCTC = Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre**.
Statement 2 correct: **ART** is **free lifelong** at ART centres.
Statement 3 wrong: **ICTC = Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre**, offering **free voluntary** testing.
xa: **PEP** must be taken **within 72 hours**.
Other prevention tools: **Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PrEP**, condoms.

121.s: The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 primarily seeks to prevent which of the following?
o: Discrimination against people living with HIV
121.x: The Act of 2017 bars discrimination against people living with HIV and provides a legal framework for their protection.
121.tq: Link the legislation with its principal legal protection.
xs: The **HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars **discrimination against people living with HIV** — option **(2)**.
It does not restrict ART centres, medicines or voluntary testing.
xa: ⚠ **2017** also saw the **Mental Healthcare Act**.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Free **lifelong ART** is given at ART centres.

121.s:
With reference to the UNAIDS 95-95-95 target adopted by India, consider the following statements:
1. 95% of people living with HIV should know their status.
2. 95% of those who know their status should be on treatment.
3. 95% of those on treatment should have a suppressed viral load.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: The three 95s refer respectively to knowledge of HIV status, treatment, and viral-load suppression among those treated.
121.tq: Read each repeated numerical target separately before selecting the code.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**95-95-95** (UNAIDS, adopted by India): **95%** know their status; **95%** of them on treatment; **95%** of those treated with **suppressed viral load**.
xa: AP's minister called the national target **95-95-99** (**99%** viral suppression).
AP stands at **88% / 87% / 96.2%**; target **Dec 2026**.
AP launched the **Suraksha Dashboard** (13 Aug 2026).

121.s: The national goal associated with HIV/AIDS control in India is to end AIDS as a public health threat by:
121.x: India’s stated goal is to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
121.tq: Distinguish the national HIV goal year from programme-phase years.
xs: India aims to end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030** — option **(2)**.
This matches **SDG 3.3**: end AIDS, TB, malaria and NTD epidemics by 2030.
xa: **NACP Phase V (2021-26)**: **80% cut** in new infections and AIDS deaths.
UNAIDS 2026 report: new infections at a **30-year low**.
Funding: **$17.6 bn** available vs **$21.9 bn** needed.

121.s: Which of the following States are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States?
121.x: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States.
121.tq: Recall the exact geographical grouping rather than a single State.
xs: The highest HIV burden is in **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka** — option **(1)**.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
xa: Dominant strain in India: **HIV-1 subtype C**.
NACO's **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review was held in **Vijayawada**, Mar 2026.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about HIV/AIDS projects in India:
1. The Red Ribbon Express is an HIV/AIDS awareness train.
2. AVAHAN is a World Bank HIV prevention project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train. Statement 2 is wrong: AVAHAN is the Gates Foundation's HIV prevention initiative, not a World Bank project. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: AVAHAN = Gates Foundation.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Red Ribbon Express** is an HIV/AIDS **awareness train**.
Statement 2 wrong: **AVAHAN** is a **Gates Foundation** HIV prevention project.
xa: NACO held the **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review at **Vijayawada** (Mar 2026).
NACP was launched in **1992**, led by **NACO**.
Prevention tools: **PEP within 72 hours**, PrEP, Test and Treat.

121.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised HIV prevention tool listed for India’s response?
121.x: Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PEP within 72 hours, PrEP and condoms are recognised prevention tools. Routine antibiotic vaccination is not one of them.
121.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the prevention-tool group.
xs: **Routine antibiotic vaccination** is not an HIV prevention tool — option **(3)**.
Listed tools: **Treatment as Prevention**, **Test and Treat**, **PEP within 72 hours**, **PrEP** and condoms.
xa: **ICTCs** offer free voluntary testing; **ART** is free lifelong.
Phase V aims at an **80% cut** in new infections.
The **2017 Act** bars discrimination against people living with HIV.

121.s: Which strain of HIV is dominant in India?
121.x: HIV-1 subtype C is the dominant strain in India. HIV-2, HIV-1 subtype B and HIV-1 subtype A are other HIV types or subtypes but are not the dominant strain in India.
121.tq: India's HIV = HIV-1 subtype C.
xs: The dominant strain in India is **HIV-1 subtype C** — option **(1)**.
So HIV-2 and the other HIV-1 subtypes listed are not India's dominant strain.
xa: India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Highest burden: **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka**.
Goal: end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030**.

121.s: The principal objective of the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) is to:
o: Identify high-risk persons and link them with appropriate care
Provide only emergency surgical treatment for communicable diseases
121.x: NP-NCD focuses on finding people at high risk of non-communicable diseases and connecting them with care. It was earlier known as NPCDCS.
121.tq: Identify the programme’s core function rather than confusing it with a disease-eradication or insurance programme.
xs: **NP-NCD** (earlier **NPCDCS**) **finds high-risk people and links them to care** — option **(1)**.
It is not about communicable-disease surgery, vector-borne diseases or insurance claims.
xa: In AP, NP-NCD also covers **NMHP, elderly care, IDD, tobacco control, fluorosis + oral health**.
**NCD-CD 3.0** in AP: universal screening from **14 Nov 2024**; **53.02 lakh** screened.
**SDG 3.4**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third** by 2030.

121.s:
In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following programmes or health concerns are additionally covered under NP-NCD?
1. National Mental Health Programme
2. Elderly care
3. Iodine Deficiency Disorders
4. Tobacco control
5. Fluorosis and oral health

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
121.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the expanded NP-NCD coverage includes mental health, elderly care, iodine deficiency disorders, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.
121.tq: Use the list-completion method: check each item against the stated state-level coverage.
xs: All five — **1, 2, 3, 4 and 5** — are covered — option **(3)**.
AP's NP-NCD also covers **NMHP**, **elderly care**, **IDD**, **tobacco control**, **fluorosis + oral health**.
xa: AP's ANMs screen at home using the **ANM AP Health App**.
**NCD-CD 3.0**: universal screening from **14 Nov 2024** → **53.02 lakh** citizens screened (2024-25).
AP also runs **NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP** and rabies, leptospirosis, snake-bite programmes.

121.s: The India Hypertension Control Initiative, implemented with the involvement of ICMR, primarily seeks to reduce deaths due to:
o: Heart attack, stroke and kidney failure
121.x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from heart attack, stroke and kidney failure.
121.tq: Match the named initiative with its specific disease-outcome targets.
xs: The **India Hypertension Control Initiative (ICMR)** targets deaths from **heart attack, stroke and kidney failure** — option **(4)**.
Rabies, snake-bite and leptospirosis are separate programmes run in AP.
xa: **NP-NCD** finds high-risk people and links them to care.
**SDG 3.4**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third** by 2030.
⚠ **MERA India** is ICMR's malaria alliance.

121.s: Under Sustainable Development Goal 3.4, the target for premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by 2030 is to:
121.x: SDG 3.4 calls for reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by one-third through prevention and treatment by 2030.
121.tq: Focus on the exact target fraction and distinguish it from stronger but unsupported claims such as elimination.
xs: **SDG 3.4**: **reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third** by **2030** — option **(3)**.
It is a one-third cut, not halving, a quarter or complete elimination.
xa: ⚠ **SDG 3.3** is about ending **AIDS, TB, malaria and NTD** epidemics by 2030.
**NP-NCD** (earlier NPCDCS) links high-risk people to care.
AP screened **53.02 lakh** citizens under **NCD-CD 3.0**.

121.s: Cervavac, announced in September 2022, is best described as:
o: India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine against cervical cancer, made by the Serum Institute of India
India's first indigenous malaria vaccine, made by Bharat Biotech
An intranasal COVID-19 vaccine developed with ICMR-NIV
The world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans, made by Zydus
121.x: Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute of India against cervical cancer (Sept 2022). The intranasal COVID vaccine is iNCOVACC; the first DNA vaccine is ZyCoV-D by Zydus; and Cervavac is not a malaria vaccine (R21 is the Oxford-SII malaria vaccine).
121.tq: Cervavac = HPV, quadrivalent, SII, cervical cancer.
xs: **Cervavac** is **India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine** against **cervical cancer**, made by **Serum Institute of India** — option **(1)**.
It was announced in **Sept 2022** (two PYQs).
⚠ The malaria vaccine made by Serum Institute is **R21/Matrix-M**, developed by Oxford.
xa: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** is GSK's malaria vaccine.
AAMs screen for **oral, breast and cervical** cancers.

121.s: Which one of the following was repealed by the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017?
o: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
121.x: The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 repealed the Mental Health Act of 1987.
121.tq: Use the year-based legal distinction to identify the repealed legislation.
xs: The **Mental Healthcare Act, 2017** repealed the **Mental Health Act, 1987** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **NHP 2017** is a policy, not something this Act repealed.
xa: It gives a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
It **decriminalised suicide** and **restricted ECT**.
**National Mental Health Programme**: **1982**; **Tele-MANAS**: **2022**.

121.s: Tele-MANAS, launched in 2022, is primarily intended to provide:
o: Online certification of psychiatric hospitals only
A national database of blood donors
121.x: Tele-MANAS provides round-the-clock tele-mental-health support and services.
121.tq: Identify the service from the programme name and its stated operational feature—continuous tele-mental-health access.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** (**2022**) provides **24/7 tele-mental-health** (24-hour) services — option **(3)**.
It is not a hospital-certification, blood-donor or communicable-disease platform.
xa: **DMHP** now covers **90%+ districts**.
**1.73 lakh AAMs** include mental health.
Other initiatives: **MANODARPAN** (students); **KIRAN** helpline (**MoSJE**).

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding mental-health initiatives in India:
1. District Mental Health Programme coverage has expanded to more than 90 per cent of districts.
2. About 1.73 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs include mental-health services.
3. MANODARPAN is associated with mental-health support for students.
4. KIRAN is a helpline of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: All four statements are correct: DMHP covers more than 90% of districts, 1.73 lakh AAMs include mental health, MANODARPAN supports students, and KIRAN is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
121.tq: Group the initiatives by coverage, delivery platform, target group and ministry to avoid confusing their roles.
xs: All four — **1, 2, 3 and 4** — are correct — option **(4)**.
**DMHP** covers **90%+ districts**; **1.73 lakh AAMs** include mental health.
**MANODARPAN** is for **students**; **KIRAN** is a helpline of **MoSJE**.
xa: **Tele-MANAS** (**2022**): 24/7 tele-mental-health.
Mental health treatment gap: **84.5%**.
Psychiatrists: **0.3 per lakh**.

121.s:
Arrange the following mental-health programme developments in chronological order:
A. National Mental Health Programme was initiated
B. Mental Health Act was enacted
C. Mental Healthcare Act was enacted
D. Tele-MANAS was launched

Select the correct chronological sequence.
121.x: The National Mental Health Programme dates to 1982, the Mental Health Act to 1987, the Mental Healthcare Act to 2017 and Tele-MANAS to 2022.
121.tq: Anchor the sequence with the years 1982, 1987, 2017 and 2022.
xs: The order is **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**NMHP 1982** → **Mental Health Act 1987** → **Mental Healthcare Act 2017** → **Tele-MANAS 2022**.
xa: The 2017 Act **repealed** the 1987 Act.
It **decriminalised suicide** and gave a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
Prevalence of mental illness: about **1 in 7 Indians**.

121.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported mental-health burden and treatment-resource situation in India?
o: About one in fourteen Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 48.5%, and there are 3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in seven Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 14.5%, and there are 3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in three Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 84.5%, and there are 30 psychiatrists per lakh population.
About one in seven Indians is affected, the treatment gap is 84.5%, and there are 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
121.x: The reported figures are a burden of about one in seven Indians, an 84.5% treatment gap and 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population.
121.tq: Check the three linked figures together; the distractors reverse or inflate the percentages and ratios.
xs: About **1 in 7 Indians** affected, **84.5%** treatment gap, **0.3 psychiatrists per lakh** — option **(4)**.
The other options distort these figures (14.5%, 3 or 30 per lakh).
xa: **DMHP** covers **90%+ districts**.
**Tele-MANAS** (**2022**) offers 24/7 support.
**1.73 lakh** AAMs include mental health services.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017:
1. It gives a right to access mental healthcare from government services.
2. It decriminalised attempted suicide.
3. It removed all restrictions on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Act gives a right to access government mental healthcare and decriminalised suicide. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act restricted ECT rather than removing restrictions. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses decriminalisation and the options with 3 are wrong.
121.tq: MHA 2017: right to access, suicide decriminalised, ECT restricted.
xs: **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Mental Healthcare Act, 2017** gives a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
Statement 2 correct: it **decriminalised suicide**.
Statement 3 wrong: it **restricted ECT**.
xa: It repealed the **1987** Act.
**NMHP** dates to **1982**.

121.s: Which one of the following statements best describes Andhra Pradesh in relation to HIV/AIDS?
o: It has no state-level HIV cascade targets or indicators.
It is reported as a high-burden state with a cascade of 87/96.2/88 percent.
It is reported as a high-burden state and is tracking an HIV cascade of 88/87/96.2 percent.
It is a low-burden state with a cascade of 96.2/88/87 percent.
121.x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as a high-burden state, with the reported HIV cascade figures of 88/87/96.2 percent.
121.tq: Preserve the order of the cascade figures while rejecting reversed numerical sequences.
xs: AP is a **high-burden state** with an HIV cascade of **88/87/96.2%** — option **(3)** (Aug 2026).
Option (2) jumbles the order; option (4) wrongly calls AP low-burden.
xa: AP's target date: **Dec 2026**; national target called **95-95-99** by AP's minister.
**Suraksha Dashboard** launched on **13 Aug 2026**.
Highest burden states: **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding malaria epidemiology in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Malaria patterns are changing in tribal districts.
2. Malaria patterns are changing in non-tribal districts.
3. Sustained surveillance is therefore necessary.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: Malaria epidemiology is changing in both tribal and non-tribal districts of Andhra Pradesh, making continued surveillance necessary.
121.tq: Treat the geographical comparison as a two-part statement and connect it with the stated public-health response.
xs: All three — **1, 2 and 3** — are correct — option **(4)**.
Malaria epidemiology is **changing in AP's tribal and non-tribal districts**, so **surveillance must be sustained**.
xa: **IDSP** (**2004**, under NHM) does outbreak surveillance.
AP runs **NCVBDC** among its disease programmes.
National malaria elimination target: **2030**.

121.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2026 Andhra Pradesh HIV target and reported three-part status?
121.x: Andhra Pradesh reported 88%, 87% and 96.2% across the three indicators, with a target for December 2026.
121.tq: Preserve the order of a multi-part numerical indicator.
xs: AP targets the HIV cascade by **Dec 2026**; option (4) jumbles the order.
xa: **95-95-95** is the UNAIDS target adopted by India.
AP's minister called the national target **95-95-99**.
AP launched the **Suraksha Dashboard** (13 Aug 2026).

121.s: Which of the following sets contains only programmes reported as being run by Andhra Pradesh?
o: NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP, rabies, leptospirosis and snake-bite programmes
NTEP, WHO, IMF, NLEP and World Bank programmes
NCVBDC, UNESCO, NPCBVI, NLEP and WTO programmes
NLEP, NASA, NTEP, UNICEF and NPCBVI programmes
121.x: The state runs NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP, rabies, leptospirosis and snake-bite programmes. The other options insert international or unrelated organisations.
121.tq: Eliminate options containing bodies that are not disease-control programmes and retain the complete state programme set.
xs: AP runs **NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP, rabies, leptospirosis and snake-bite** programmes — option **(1)**.
WHO, IMF, World Bank, UNESCO, WTO, NASA and UNICEF are not AP programmes.
xa: **IDSP** (**2004**, under NHM) handles outbreak surveillance.
AP's **NCD-CD 3.0** screened **53.02 lakh** citizens.
AP's ANMs use the **ANM AP Health App** for home screening.

121.s: The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme was launched in which year under the National Health Mission?
121.x: IDSP was launched in 2004 under the National Health Mission and is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
121.tq: Separate the launch year of IDSP from the later IHIP years.
xs: **IDSP** was launched in **2004** under NHM — option **(1)**.
It handles **outbreak surveillance**.
xa: AP's malaria epidemiology is changing, so **surveillance must be sustained**.
⚠ **NVBDCP** handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue, chikungunya** (PYQ key).
AP runs **NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP**.

121.s: The national target of eliminating sickle-cell anaemia is set for:
121.x: India has set a target to eliminate sickle-cell anaemia by 2047 and to screen seven crore at-risk people.
121.tq: Separate the long-term disease mission year from 2025 and 2030 targets.
xs: India aims to **eliminate sickle cell anaemia by 2047** — option **(4)**.
It plans to **screen 7 crore** at-risk people (APPSC 2022 PYQ: A and R both true, R explains A).
xa: **Lymphatic filariasis**: **2027**; **malaria**: **2030**; **TB**: **2025**.
**Ayushman Gram** includes **sickle-cell screening**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about lymphatic filariasis elimination in India:
1. India targets elimination by 2027, three years ahead of the SDG target.
2. The triple-drug IDA regimen uses Ivermectin, DEC and Azithromycin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: the LF target is 2027, three years ahead of SDG 3.3. Statement 2 is wrong: IDA = Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole. Hence '1 only'.
121.tq: IDA = I-D-A: Ivermectin, DEC, Albendazole.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: LF elimination by **2027**, **three years ahead** of **SDG 3.3**.
Statement 2 wrong: **IDA** = **Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole**, not azithromycin.
xa: LF is eliminated through **MDA** with the triple-drug regimen.
LF is an **NVBDCP** elimination target with malaria and kala-azar.
Sickle cell anaemia target: **2047**.

121.s: Which group of diseases is targeted for elimination under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme?
121.x: Malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar are the diseases identified for elimination under NVBDCP.
121.tq: Select the complete programme-specific disease group.
xs: NVBDCP targets **malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar** — option **(1)**.
**TB** is under **NTEP**; **HIV/AIDS** under **NACP**; **leprosy** under **NLEP**.
xa: NVBDCP handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue, chikungunya** (PYQ key).
Tools: **IRS, LLINs**, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides, source reduction.
LF target: **2027**; malaria: **2030**.

121.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the leprosy-control programme?
121.x: The National Leprosy Eradication Programme provides free multidrug therapy at primary health centres. Sparsh is an awareness campaign, and Anti-Leprosy Day is observed on 30 January.
121.tq: Match the programme with its service while rejecting swapped programme names and dates.
xs: **NLEP — free multidrug therapy (MDT) at PHCs** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Anti-Leprosy Day** is **30 January**; **Sparsh** is NLEP's awareness campaign, not NTEP's.
xa: ⚠ **NACP** is the HIV/AIDS programme; **NVBDCP** covers vector-borne diseases.
AP runs **NLEP** among its disease programmes.

121.s: Which programme is associated with handling outbreaks of malaria, dengue and chikungunya?
121.x: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue and chikungunya.
121.tq: Discriminate among similarly abbreviated disease programmes by matching the vector-borne disease group.
xs: **NVBDCP** handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue and chikungunya** — option **(3)** (PYQ key).
**NLEP** = leprosy; **NTEP** = TB; **NPCBVI** = blindness and visual impairment programme run in AP.
xa: NVBDCP elimination targets: **malaria, LF + kala-azar**.
Malaria cases fell **80%** in **2015-2023**.
**IDSP** (**2004**) provides outbreak surveillance.

121.s: According to the UNAIDS report associated with the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio in 2026, which combination is correct?
o: New infections are unchanged; $21.9 billion is available against $30 billion needed.
New infections are at a 20-year low; $21.9 billion is available against $17.6 billion needed.
New infections are at a 30-year high; $17.6 billion is available against $21.9 billion needed.
New infections are at a 30-year low; $17.6 billion is available against $21.9 billion needed.
121.x: The report titled 'United to end AIDS' noted that new infections had reached a 30-year low, while available funding was $17.6 billion against a requirement of $21.9 billion.
121.tq: Pair the trend with the correct funding figures; the distractors reverse or alter one of the quantitative facts.
xs: New infections are at a **30-year low**; **$17.6 bn** available against **$21.9 bn** needed — option **(4)**.
Source: UNAIDS **'United to end AIDS'** report at the **26th International AIDS Conference**, **Rio**, **2026**.
Option (3) wrongly says "high"; option (2) swaps the funding figures.
xa: India's goal: end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030**.
**NACP Phase V (2021-26)**: **80% cut** in new infections and AIDS deaths.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV; dominant strain **HIV-1 subtype C**.

121.s: The Sustainable Development Goal 3.3 seeks, by 2030, to:
o: Reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third only
Eliminate all forms of environmental pollution
Provide universal mental-health counselling through telemedicine
End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases
121.x: SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.
121.tq: Distinguish SDG 3.3 from SDG 3.4, which concerns premature deaths from NCDs.
xs: **SDG 3.3** aims to **end the epidemics of AIDS, TB, malaria and NTDs** by **2030** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Cutting premature NCD deaths by **one-third** is **SDG 3.4**.
xa: India's TB target **2025** is five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
**Lymphatic filariasis** target **2027** is three years ahead of SDG 3.3.
Malaria elimination target: **2030** (framework **2016-2030**).

121.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: NP-NCD — Identification of high-risk persons and linkage to care
IDSP — Elimination of premature non-communicable disease deaths by one-third by 2030
IHCI — Reduction of hypertension-related heart attack, stroke and kidney-failure deaths
121.x: IDSP is concerned with outbreak surveillance. The target of reducing premature NCD deaths by one-third by 2030 belongs to SDG 3.4.
121.tq: Find the programme-target mismatch; the final option assigns an SDG target to an outbreak-surveillance programme.
xs: **IDSP — elimination of premature NCD deaths by one-third by 2030** is wrongly matched — option **(3)**.
**IDSP** (**2004**, under NHM) does **outbreak surveillance**; the one-third NCD target is **SDG 3.4**.
**Tele-MANAS** (24/7 tele-mental-health), **NP-NCD** (high-risk linkage) and **IHCI** (heart attack, stroke, kidney failure) are correct.
xa: Tele-MANAS was launched in **2022**.
NP-NCD was earlier called **NPCDCS**.
IHCI is run by **ICMR**.
